abstract: Biogeochemical cycles occur naturally in coastal regions. Estuaries, wetlands, and tidal creeks assist these cycles. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate short‐term prediction of agricultural drought is critical for sustainable crop management and climate risk mitigation in drought‐prone regions. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) as a key lagged predictor of agricultural drought in the Palakkad district of Kerala, India. title: Inter‐Comparison of Snow Depth Over Antarctic Sea Ice From Ocean Reanalyzes and Observations
abstract: Abstract Snow depth on Antarctic sea ice is a critical climate variable affecting energy and mass balance, yet its observation and modeling remain challenging. We present a systematic intercomparison of snow depth from six ocean reanalysis products, two satellite retrievals, and ship‐based and airborne observational constraints. Results indicate that reanalysis and satellite products show consistent large‐scale climatological snow depth patterns, with the highest depths in the Weddell Sea. However, substantial differences remain in magnitude, seasonal phasing, spatial variability, and trends.

title: Machine learning for climate-responsive urban design and planning: a scoping review
abstract: Urban climate researchers increasingly use machine learning (ML) to examine microclimate conditions and their effects on comfort, health, and energy. abstract: Abstract Sea surface temperature (SST) and salinity (SSS) variability in the Red Sea influences marine ecosystems, hydrologic variability, and circulation within and outside of the Red Sea. abstract: The Philippine Sea Plate (PSP) is one of the most important elements of plate tectonics in the western Pacific region. The most conspicuous feature of the PSP is that it is surrounded by subduction zones. abstract: Malaria remains a critical public health challenge in Nigeria, with Kebbi State experiencing significant transmission burdens influenced by climatic variability. Traditional statistical methods, while useful for identifying associations, often fail to capture the complex, nonlinear, and delayed effects of climatic variables on malaria transmission. abstract: Abstract Accurate forecasting of caisson tilt during construction is important for ensuring structural stability and effective construction management. abstract: Underwater electrostatic field reconstruction is a key technology for underwater target detection, equipment electric-field diagnostics, and marine engineering measurements. Conventional numerical methods require complete boundary conditions, whereas purely data-driven neural networks may generate spurious solutions that violate physical laws and exhibit marked accuracy degradation under sparse and noisy measurements. title: From social media to artificial intelligence: tactics used to lure and exploit victims of child trafficking and for curbing child trafficking in Kenya
abstract: Child trafficking is increasingly mediated through social media, artificial intelligence (AI) and other digital technologies, creating new opportunities for exploitation while strengthening digital prevention and protection. This study examines how digital platforms both facilitate and disrupt technology-enabled child trafficking in Kenya through a digital ethnography that combines social media observations, stakeholder interviews, focus group discussions and analysis of online anti-trafficking discourse. Guided by the Routine Activity and Situational Prevention (RASP) framework, the study inv

title: Remotely profiling the tropospheric absolute humidity using a single ground-based GNSS meteorological station based on an artificial neural network
abstract: Near-real-time profiling of the vertical distribution of tropospheric water vapor is important for a wide range of weather monitoring and forecasting applications. In this study, a GNSS-based Profiling Tropospheric Humidity Network (GPTHNet) was developed to retrieve tropospheric absolute humidity using observations from a single ground-based GNSS meteorological station. abstract: Artificial water bodies are becoming more numerous, and their importance at both local and global scales is growing. As a result, understanding the changes in aquatic biodiversity across various spatial and temporal dimensions requires their consideration in any analysis. title: Driving forces of contemporary wildfire severity in the American Southwest: a remote sensing and machine learning case study in Arizona, USA
abstract: As climate change continues to intensify atmospheric moisture demand across the American Southwest, predicting where wildfires cause severe vegetation mortality remains a major challenge. New thermal and optical harmonized satellite products provide emerging opportunities for evaluating how pre-fire vegetation moisture and water stress influence fire severity compared to other variables. title: Video-Based Measurement of River Surface Velocity: A Review of Methods, Measurement Workflows, and Validation
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), smartphones and computer vision are expanding the use of non-contact approaches for measuring river surface velocity and estimating discharge. This review combines bibliometric analysis with a qualitative synthesis of video-based river hydrometry, with emphasis on sensing platforms, image-processing methods, validation procedures and sources of uncertainty. title: Comparative assessment of machine learning algorithms and Ordinary Kriging for predictive mapping of soil clay content in a tropical Guinea Savanna
abstract: Abstract Clay content is an important determinant of soil physical and chemical behaviour, influencing water retention, nutrient availability, and agricultural productivity. Accurate spatial prediction of clay distribution is therefore important for digital soil mapping and sustainable land management. This study compared Random Forest (RF), Cubist, Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and Ordinary Kriging (OK) for predictive mapping of clay content in the tropical Guinea Savanna of Kaduna State, Nigeria. title: Artificial intelligence for astrobiology investigations (AI2): an open-source graphical user interface
abstract: A growing number of studies in astrobiological research have utilized and shown the potential in applied machine learning. However, the number of these studies are still quite limited. Furthermore, educators, students, and researchers often do not have the time and/or resources for developing machine learning knowledge and skills. journal: Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences

title: Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Underwater Species Detection and Classification
abstract: Underwater fish detection is challenging. Fish can be very small in images. The contrast in scenes is often weak. Turbid water can hide details. When fish overlap it becomes harder to locate each one. This study compares deeplearning object detectors using an underwater fish dataset. The focus is on both detection quality and how well the models work in video processing. The models tested are YOLO26, RF-DETR and SSD300 with a backbone. title: Mapping the plastic legacy with NIXVEGS: machine-learning enabled microplastics prediction in sediments
abstract: Abstract Aquatic sediments act as major sinks for microplastic (MP) pollution, yet accurately quantifying their MP distributions and inventories on a regional scale remains challenging, especially in hydrodynamically complex estuarine environments. Existing distribution models focus on ocean basins or simple hydrodynamic systems but lack sufficient adaptability to the spatial heterogeneity typical of estuaries. title: A composite-based analysis of the dynamical linkage of atmospheric rivers, warm conveyor belts, and extratropical cyclones
abstract: Abstract. Extratropical cyclones (ETCs), warm conveyor belts (WCBs), and atmospheric rivers (ARs) are dynamically connected features key to understand midlatitude weather and hydroclimate. However, the precise spatial and temporal coupling between the moisture transport in ARs and the ascent in ETC’s associated WCBs remains poorly understood. title: UNIQAT : An open‐source toolkit for reproducible image quality assessment in marine surveys
abstract: Abstract Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. Manual quality screening is labour‐intensive, subjective and inconsistent across observers and teams, hindering reproducible science, creating large backlogs of unprocessed imagery, and limiting real‐time algorithmic and robotic applications. title: Machine-learning-guided hydrothermal engineering of Cobalt-modified ZnFe₂O₄ for visible-light-active porous photocatalytic coating for urban infrastructure
abstract: This study presents a machine-learning-guided hydrothermal strategy for optimizing Cobalt-modified ZnFe 2 O 4 (ZF–Co) photocatalysts. Moreover, a novel scalable porous inorganic coating platform compatible with retrofit implementation on existing urban infrastructures was developed for visible-light-driven atmospheric pollutant mitigation. title: Using active acoustics from an underwater glider to investigate the relationship between acoustic target locations and coastal ocean fronts off the Pacific Northwest coast
abstract: Traditional ship-based sampling has provided valuable information about marine ecosystems. However, repeated high-resolution measurements are increasingly necessary to capture dynamic biophysical processes. In this study, we used active, multi-frequency acoustics from an autonomous underwater ocean glider to examine diel vertical migration and the relationship between zooplankton and fish aggregations to coastal fronts off the coast of Washington in the Pacific Northwest. title: Random analog prediction provides a benchmark for seasonal Arctic sea ice extent forecasting
abstract: Abstract We develop a random analog predictor (RAP) algorithm for the forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent (SIE) on seasonal timescales. This is a stochastic variant for scalar time series of the method of the analogues that only uses the historical SIE record to produce ensemble forecasts. Real-Time AI-Based Detection of Fish and Humans in Underwater Environments
abstract: Underwater visual monitoring is difficult because light attenuation, turbidity, color distortion, occlusion, and changing backgrounds can reduce the reliability of conventional object detection. This work presents an underwater human and fish detection system that combines a waterproof camera, image preprocessing, YOLO-based real-time object detection, and convolutional neural network (CNN) classification. title: In silico proof of concept for reconstruction of blood flow velocity with 4D phase contrast MRI and variational autoencoders
abstract: In this work, we investigate a new deep learning method for the reconstruction of blood velocity from 4D phase contrast MRI measurements based on variational autoencoders. The principle of this approach is to leverage lower resolution velocity measurements to train a variational autoencoder. The approach identifies optimal latent variables within the latent space and uses the generative process of the variational autoencoder to enhance reconstruction accuracy. abstract: Summary Shallow-water depth data serve as the essential foundation for marine spatial planning and coastal engineering projects. However, due to the attenuation of spectral signals, traditional retrieval of shallow-water seafloor topography struggles to maintain high accuracy in highly turbid waters and deeper areas. abstract: This research analyzes the risks that the development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) may pose to the protection of human rights. It addresses privacy, algorithmic discrimination, transparency, accountability, information manipulation, and cybersecurity. It also examines regulatory responses developed in the United States, China, and Europe, with particular attention to the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. abstract: Background: Academic library discovery systems increasingly mediate access to scholarly information through ranking, metadata matching, filtering, database coverage, availability signals, and recommender functions. These algorithmic arrangements can shape what users notice, cite, and trust. abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are powerful nonlinear function approximators that can learn complicated relationships from data. abstract: Accurate prediction of global sea surface temperature at sub-seasonal to seasonal (S2S) timescales is critical for drought and flood forecasting, as well as for improving disaster preparedness in human society. Operational physics-based numerical models are run to predict S2S sea surface temperature and corresponding climate indices, such as El Niño-Southern Oscillation. abstract: The detection of hydrothermal plumes is crucial for discovering active seafloor hydrothermal fields and exploring seafloor resources. abstract: It is too early to definitively predict how generative artificial intelligence (‘AI’) will affect the law and the legal profession. abstract: The encyclical Magnifica Humanitas of H. H. abstract: Underwater visible light communication (UVLC) offers high data rates over acoustic and radio-frequency links but is highly sensitive to bubble-induced scattering. This paper presents an RGB wavelength-division-multiplexed UVLC system simulated in OptiSystem across clear-water, intermediate, and bubble-induced turbidity conditions. abstract: This study explores the application of fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) for marine ecosystem monitoring, combining laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) with hyperspectral imaging (HSI), an approach rarely applied in marine ecology. abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) supports marine sensing, environmental monitoring, subsea inspection, and autonomous underwater operations. abstract: Accurate prediction of cumulative plastic strain (CPS) is essential for assessing the deformation stability of marine strata subjected to artificial ground freezing (AGF). abstract: The port and logistics electromechanical industry underpins port production and supply chain operation, and its level of intelligentization is directly related to the improvement of operational efficiency and industrial capacity. abstract: Rip currents pose significant threats to coastal safety and to autonomous marine vehicles operating nearshore. title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. title: Estimation of the Pitzer Parameters for 1-1, 2-1, 1-2, 3-1, and 1-3 Single Electrolytes at 25 °C
abstract: Abstract The Pitzer model is widely used in process models for determining the thermodynamic properties of concentrated aqueous electrolytes. The main drawback is the need for experimentally determined parameters for each ion pair in the system. The estimation of unknown Pitzer parameters of electrolytes is thus an attractive prospect. This paper investigates machine learning-based models for the task of predicting the Pitzer parameters of binary electrolytes based on the properties of the constituent ions. title: Intelligent Visibility Estimation Under Sea Fog Conditions Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate visibility information under sea fog or low-visibility conditions is essential for ensuring navigational safety in ports and nearshore waters. This study combines single-frame images extracted from nearshore sea fog observation videos with synchronized meteorological variables to investigate sea fog visibility estimation and develops the ConvNeXt-MS-WDFM model. title: Comparison of data-driven and numerical weather prediction models for rainfall nowcasting in major cities of Bangladesh
abstract: Flood-prone Bangladesh requires accurate short-term rainfall prediction, yet conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) models remain computationally intensive and regionally limited in skill. This study evaluates and compares four deep learning (DL) architectures — Simple Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Stacked LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) — against the physics-based Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for one-hour-ahead rainfall forecasting across six climatologically diverse stations in Bangladesh. abstract: This dossier proposes a methodological and epistemological reflection on the archive in the humanities. abstract: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. title: Seeing what students learn: assessing cognitive representations and academic outcomes via EEG image reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners' internal cognitive representations. Recent advances in brain--computer interfaces (BCIs) and deep learning have enabled image reconstruction from electroencephalography (EEG), providing a promising pathway to decode latent cognitive states. title: A practical approach to underwater depth and surface normals estimation
abstract: Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE) is crucial for tasks such as three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and underwater exploration. Current methods rely either on discriminative models, which struggle with transparent or reflective surfaces, or generative models, which, while accurate, are computationally expensive. abstract: Reliable detection of lit fishing vessels from night-time satellite observations is essential not only for monitoring fishing activity but also for investigating the distribution of fishery resources when integrated with marine environmental information. However, false detections caused by anthropogenic coastal illumination remain a major challenge for vessel detection using observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS). title: Illuminating Streptomyces : Raman Spectroscopy for Antibiotic Detection and Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Streptomyces is well known as a prolific source of many bioactive compounds. This review outlines the principles of Raman spectroscopy and its application to bacterial systems, with particular emphasis on the secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces . Streptomyces are unparalleled chemical factories, producing over two‐thirds of all naturally derived antibiotics and bioactive molecules. title: Postsecularidad y tecnociencia: la redistribución narrativa de la trascendencia en la ciencia ficción contemporánea en español
abstract: This article proposes a reinterpretation of contemporary Spanish science fiction through the lens of postsecularity, understood not as a return of religion but as its functional redistribution within technoscientific dispositifs. Against dominant readings that frame the genre as inherently secularizing, it argues that works such as Jorge Carrión’s Membrana and Elia Barceló’s El efecto Frankenstein reconfigure traditionally religious functions—memory, creation, and identity—within narrative structures mediated by technology. title: Toward interoperable bathymetric data in ocean observing systems: integrating hydrographic standards and FAIR data practices
abstract: Bathymetric data are a fundamental component of ocean observing systems, supporting applications in ocean modelling, coastal hazard assessment, marine spatial planning, and navigational safety. However, these datasets remain highly fragmented due to the diversity of acquisition platforms, including hydrographic surveys, autonomous vehicles, satellite-derived bathymetry, and legacy chart products, which often differ in spatial reference systems, vertical datums, resolution scales, and metadata quality. title: Stress corrosion cracking of 316 L stainless steel in simulated Arabian gulf seawater
abstract: Abstract Austenitic stainless steels are widely used in coastal and marine infrastructure for its corrosion resistance, yet failures associated with chloride-induced stress corrosion cracking (SCC) continue to be reported. In this work, the SCC susceptibility of 316L austenitic stainless steel was investigated using test solutions designed to simulate Arabian gulf seawater and compared with a reference standard brine. title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for sustainable development and policy integration in the shipping industry
abstract: Shipping is a critical industry for global trade but is associated with environmental externalities like air, underwater noise, and light pollution. Transitioning to a sustainable future requires optimizing propulsion systems, which currently suffer from fossil fuel reliance and energy losses. This research develops an AI-assisted evidence-synthesis framework to examine sustainable shipping and propulsion technologies and support a policy framework for a sustainable maritime agenda. abstract: Coral reefs support marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of coastal communities, yet their condition in Indonesia, including Bali, continues to decline due to coral bleaching. Bleaching monitoring still relies largely on manual surveys that are time-consuming, costly, and require trained experts. This study develops a YOLOv10-based object detection model with transfer learning to automatically detect and localize bleached areas in underwater images. abstract: Weather prediction is crucial in agriculture, transportation, and disaster management. Accurate and timely forecasts are essential for making informed decisions and minimizing risks. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning approach for weather prediction, combining Ridge Regression for feature extraction and selection and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for training and evaluation. title: Biophysical transport control in smart nanocomposite packaging under non-thermal food preservation technologies
abstract: Smart nanocomposite packaging has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing food preservation by improving barrier performance, enabling active functionality, and supporting intelligent quality monitoring. Its integration with non-thermal preservation technologies, including pulsed electric fields, cold plasma, ultraviolet irradiation, and high-pressure processing, offers new opportunities to extend shelf life while minimizing thermal damage to food products. abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo–endometrial interface. abstract: Abstract. Projections of Antarctic mass loss and its contribution to sea-level rise are highly sensitive to the applied ocean-driven melting. abstract: Earthquake Early Warning Systems (EEWS) are critical components of resilient smart cities, employing advanced digital technologies to reduce the impacts of seismic events and strengthen urban disaster preparedness. These systems integrate distributed Internet of Things (IoT) devices, wireless sensor networks, high-speed communication infrastructures, and machine learning algorithms to detect, analyze, and evaluate seismic activity in real time. abstract: Salinity is a key descriptor of transitional water bodies at the land–sea interface, and resolving its spatiotemporal dynamics is essential for understanding water-mass exchange, habitat distribution, and ecosystem functioning. However, available observations remain limited in their ability to resolve dynamic freshwater–marine interactions at relevant spatial scales. abstract: [Purpose] This article analyzes the institutional barriers constraining the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain in Ecuador's notarial system, understood as components of the digital transformation of public services dependent on telecommunications infrastructure. abstract: Strains of the picocyanobacteria genera Synechococcus and Cyanobium occur in cold-temperate zones, from coastal waters to the open ocean, spanning a range of salinities and water depths. To thrive across different salinities, picocyanobacteria strains acclimate internal turgor by expending metabolic energy to accumulate compatible solutes and extrude inorganic ions. abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing flood damage is a key challenge for both administrators and communities, particularly in the face of increasing climate‐related impacts. A fundamental prerequisite for effective damage reduction is a detailed understanding of the spatial distribution of territorial susceptibility to flood damage. abstract: Comprehending bioconvection facilitates the modelling of natural processes in aquatic environments and improves the efficacy of systems incorporating microorganism suspensions. It connects biology with fluid dynamics, providing insights into the impact of living creatures on fluid flow behaviour. The current study offers insights into the mechanisms of heat, microorganism and mass transfer in complex fluids, with potential applications in biomedical devices, chemical engineering and industrial processes involving non-Newtonian fluids under the influence of electromagnetic and thermal effects.

abstract: ABSTRACT Advancing sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with carbon reduction. This study investigates carbon emission efficiency (CEE), growth–emission decoupling, and digital–structural transformation in 35 early OECD member countries from 1995 to 2023. It combines the IGT decoupling model, a three‐stage DEA framework using the Super‐EBM model, the GML index, and truncated regression to evaluate decoupling patterns, static and dynamic CEE, and the drivers of low‐carbon transition. abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. abstract: The blue economy has emerged as a strategic framework for reconciling ocean-based economic development with marine ecosystem conservation and social well-being, particularly in maritime regions such as Southeast Asia. As one of the world’s most ocean-dependent regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) possesses extensive marine resources that support fisheries, marine tourism, shipping, offshore energy, and emerging marine biotechnology industries. abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). abstract: Communal cattle farming in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to face destabilization from non-linear climate variability, yet insurance penetration remains negligible. In Lupane District, Zimbabwe, uptake is exceptionally low at approximately 0.01%, despite recurrent droughts that threaten household livelihoods. This study aimed to develop an AI-driven framework to enhance sustainability and resilience in communal cattle insurance within the district. abstract: Abstract The international community has committed to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, and satellite monitoring can now detect industrial fishing inside marine protected areas (MPAs) at near-global scale. title: Spatial Diversity of Marine Protists Along the Northern Norway Fjords During the Sub‐Arctic Summer
abstract: Polar coastal waters are highly complex and productive ecosystems that experience increasingly higher average water temperatures, shallower and stronger stratification, and higher glacier-melting rates. Yet, the environmental complexity and high microbial diversity within fjords pose challenges to understanding the impacts of these changes and the ecological processes driving them. Here, we studied protists and prokaryote communities, their distribution, and functional ecology along the northern Norwegian coast in summer 2019 using SSU rRNA gene metabarcoding. title: The potential for habitat support structures to address habitat deficits in a declining marine ecosystem
abstract: Concurrent local and global stressors are rapidly degrading marine ecosystems. Consequences of this degradation include widespread reductions in the availability, quality, and structural complexity of habitats. For example, coral reef habitats across the Western Atlantic/Caribbean are flattening and becoming more structurally homogeneous as warming waters, severe bleaching events, unprecedented disease outbreaks, deteriorating water quality, and hurricanes continue to drive stony coral mass mortality. title: Sea Surface Temperature Influences Migratory Patterns of the Atlantic Bluefin Tuna ( Thunnus thynnus ) Between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: ABSTRACT Oceanographic variability plays a critical role in shaping the migratory behavior of the Atlantic bluefin tuna ( Thunnus thynnus ). This study investigates the thermal preferences of individuals migrating through the Strait of Gibraltar and the Gulf of Cádiz during pre‐ and post‐spawning movements. Comparing data measured from electronic tags and satellite‐derived sea surface temperature (SST) fields, we identified distinct SST preferred ranges associated with each migratory phase: 17.4°C–19.3°C inbound to the Mediterranean and 18.4°C–22°C outbound to the Atlantic. title: A pictorial key to Southeast Asian species of Collotheca (Rotifera, Collothecidae), with a new species from Thailand
abstract: A new species is described from Thailand, Collotheca laddae sp. nov ., and a pictorial key to all Collotheca species and subspecies recorded in Southeast Asia is provided. The new species was discovered during a freshwater zooplankton identification workshop. This species is characterized by a five-lobed infundibulum with very small lateral lobes and short vibratile setae. The pictorial key was developed from a review of original descriptions and illustrations of all valid species of Collotheca and is designed to facilitate species-level identification based on live specimens. title: A Two-Stage Neural Network Framework for Swimming Direction Control of an Underwater Walking Robot: Kinematic Validation via Simulation and In-Air Experiments
abstract: Each year, hundreds of thousands of tons of derelict fishing gear become entangled in ship propellers, and resolving such incidents currently requires divers to manually cut the entangled material underwater, exposing them to the risk of secondary accidents. To address this problem, we developed a radial quadruped underwater robot that walks along the hull of a ship using electromagnetic feet and swims freely using propellers mounted on the distal link of each leg. abstract: This paper presents a virtual boundary integral neural network (VBINN) for three-dimensional exterior acoustic problems. The method introduces a virtual boundary within the scatterer or vibrating body and represents the associated source density using a neural network. Based on the acoustic Green’s function, this representation satisfies the Sommerfeld radiation condition and enables direct evaluation of the acoustic pressure and its normal derivative at arbitrary field points. abstract: Mesoscale eddies play a crucial role in the ocean, and accurate detection of their three-dimensional (3D) structures is essential for understanding marine dynamics. However, 3D eddy reconstruction remains challenging: traditional methods provide limited pixel-level boundary delineation, while existing deep learning approaches suffer from insufficient physical constraints and unrealistic eddy geometries. title: Freeze-thaw model for compressive strength of flowable solidified soil based on machine learning
abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling is a critical factor triggering durability degradation of flowable solidified soil in cold-region engineering, and its damage evolution process is affected by multi-factor coupling with obvious nonlinear characteristics. Based on experimental compressive strength data of flowable solidified soil under freeze-thaw cycles, four influencing factors, namely solidifier dosage (SD), admixture dosage (AD), water-solid ratio (WS) and freeze-thaw cycle number (F-T), are selected as input variables. abstract: To investigate the impact of large-scale offshore aquaculture platform operations on the acoustic environment of local waters, this study analyzed the observed evolution of the acoustic environment around a large truss-type platform and its surrounding waters based on a continuous 46-hour synchronous multi-channel observation dataset acquired under typical calm sea conditions. abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) is a widely adopted methodology for the continuous, long-term observation of underwater marine organisms as well as various underwater noise sources using acoustic signals. However, manually identifying specific signals within long-term monitoring datasets is cumbersome and susceptible to potential biases. This study proposes a hybrid automated detection framework that simultaneously improves detection accuracy and operational efficiency for continuous 45-day underwater acoustic data on the grunt signals of Pacific cod (Gadus macrocephalus). Flag‐type triboelectric nanogenerators (F‐TENGs), which have been widely investigated for harvesting energy from low‐velocity ocean currents, generally rely on bluff body to induce vortex. This dependence limits their spatial utilization efficiency. title: A Caribbean bright spot coral reef exceeds thermal limits during the fourth global coral bleaching event
abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasing in both frequency and intensity, exposing coral reefs to prolonged periods of thermal stress and driving recurrent mass coral bleaching. Nevertheless, coral decline remains heterogeneous, with some reefs maintaining unexpectedly high coral cover despite exposure to thermal and other environmental disturbances. This study analysed benthic community change across Banco Capiro in Tela Bay and the south-side reefs of Utila, Honduras, from 2013 to 2025, spanning the 3rd and 4th Global Coral Bleaching Events. abstract: Mussaenda wallichii G. Don (Rubiaceae) is a widespread species distributed from northeastern India to Southeast Asia, but its taxonomic delimitation has remained uncertain due to overlapping morphological characters and incomplete assessment of type materials. Based on extensive herbarium examinations, including type specimens, and critical evaluation of protologues, we reassessed the taxonomic identities of M. intuspilosa Jayaw. and M. lancipetala X.F. title: Multimodal Machine Learning for Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Classification and Polarity Localization in Tropical Thunderstorm
abstract: Accurate classification and localization of Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning are essential for the development of reliable early warning systems in tropical regions and the improvement of thunderstorm monitoring. This study proposes a multimodal machine learning framework for CG lightning classification and polarity-based localization with synchronized atmospheric and electromagnetic measurements collected in Melaka, Malaysia, in 2024. title: Linking marine benthic biodiversity and ecosystem functions related to carbon cycling in a continental mud depocenter
abstract: Abstract. The importance of carbon storage in continental seafloor sediments is increasingly recognized, yet the role of benthic macrofaunal biodiversity in the regulation of these processes remains poorly understood. Benthic macrofauna contributes to organic carbon cycling through respiration and secondary production, while the sediment reworking (bioturbation) and ventilation (bioirrigation) of infauna promote the redistribution and remineralization of organic matter in sediments. title: Analytical soliton solutions, bifurcation analysis, and physics-informed neural network validation of fluid wave dynamics in the (2+1) dimensional Boussinesq equation
abstract: This study develops a hybrid analytical and computational framework for the (2+1)-dimensional Boussinesq equation, which models weakly nonlinear, weakly dispersive shallow-water gravity waves relevant to wave resonance and oblique interactions in coastal and ocean engineering. Using the unified Riccati equation expansion (UREE) method, five exact traveling-wave solutions are constructed: a bright soliton, a singular soliton, two periodic waves, and a rational solution. title: An Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Short-Range Rainfall Forecasting in Mumbai’s Monsoon Regime
abstract: Abstract Short-range rainfall forecasting in tropical coastal megacities is a formidable challenge owing to the nonlinear dynamics, strong seasonality, and pronounced interannual variability that characterise monsoon precipitation regimes. This study develops and evaluates deep learning frameworks for multi-lead-time (D+1 to D+4) daily rainfall forecasting over Mumbai (72.88°E, 19.07°N), India, a densely populated coastal metropolis where accurate precipitation prediction is directly consequential for flood early warning. title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in Singapore: a retrospective, naturalistic study
abstract: Introduction Naturalistic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) outcome data for treatment-resistant depression remain limited in Southeast Asia. This retrospective study describes such outcomes from a general hospital in Singapore. Method 28 outpatients received rTMS (10Hz high-frequency or intermittent theta-burst) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F3 scalp position) between May 2022 and May 2025. title: Explainable machine learning for predicting microplastic burden in commercially important freshwater fish and assessing dietary exposure
abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination in commercially important freshwater fish represents an emerging concern for aquatic ecosystem integrity and human food safety. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting and assessing MP accumulation in European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax), Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) and crucian carp (Carassius auratus) collected from four retail markets in Yichang City, Hubei Province, China. title: Attention-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification
abstract: Ovarian cancer histotype classification is challenging because of substantial morphological heterogeneity and subtle subtype-specific features. This work presents a controlled evaluation of high-resolution pathology representations and slide-level aggregation methods for automated classification of five ovarian cancer subtypes from whole-slide histopathology images. Precomputed CONCH patch embeddings were aggregated using mean pooling, max pooling, gated attention-based multiple-instance learning, and a max-pooling cascade. title: Deep-Learning Error Correction of Regional Significant Wave Height Forecasts
abstract: Deep-learning post-processing can correct systematic errors in numerical wave forecasts, but its reliability under high-wave conditions remains unclear. We develop an error-correction framework in which deep networks predict the full future error trajectory of operational forecasts, and compare three architectures, a pure LSTM, a pure Transformer and a hybrid LSTM–Transformer, tuned identically with Bayesian optimization, using hourly observations from six buoys in the Bohai Sea and Yellow Sea over 2023–2025. title: Multiscale pH fluctuations on a stable algal reef community (SE Sardinia, Tyrrhenian Sea)
abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is threatened by ocean acidification and warming, in combination with habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, and overexploitation. Assessing local high-frequency pH variability in the context of relevant basin-scale time series data is essential to understand ecosystem vulnerability. We report the results of the Italian national pH monitoring based on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, and the pH dynamics observed at Capo Carbonara. title: GIS-based Deep Learning for Identifying and Characterizing Small Community Lagoon Wastewater Treatment Systems
abstract: Wastewater lagoon systems remain a dominant form of secondary treatment for small communities in the United States due to their low energy requirements, operational simplicity, and affordability. Despite their widespread use, national inventories of lagoon systems are fragmented, inconsistently reported, and often outdated, with non-discharging systems particularly underrepresented. These data gaps limit effective infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and equitable allocation of resources. title: The burden of inflammatory bowel disease in Asia (1990–2023) and projections to 2050: A comprehensive analysis of the 2023 global burden of disease study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is becoming an increasingly important public health concern in Asia, with rising incidence and prevalence reported across the region. Despite progress in global burden studies, data gaps remain in Asia due to variations in healthcare and socio-demographic factors. This study aims to address these gaps by assessing the burden of IBD across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on regional trends in UC and CD. title: Projected intensification of summer upwelling along the Southeastern Coast of China
abstract: Coastal upwelling is a key dynamical process along the southeastern coast of China, regulating regional circulation, biogeochemical cycling, and marine ecosystem dynamics. While previous studies have provided valuable insights into the mechanisms and variability of this coastal upwelling, its future evolution and underlying physical drivers under climate change remain unclear. title: An attention-enhanced residual network framework for structural damage detection based on structural health monitoring data
abstract: Local damage in steel structures often produces only subtle differences in vibration responses, and measurement noise can further reduce identification robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a structural damage identification method that combines Markov transition field (MTF) encoding with a coordinate-attention-enhanced residual network. abstract: Abstract Multi‐angle polarimetric instruments (MAPs) enable the retrieval of essential aerosol properties over oceanic regions. MAPs retrieval algorithms commonly use a 1‐parameter ocean bio‐optical model (OBM), based on chlorophyll‐a concentration only to represent optical properties over open waters (case‐1), whereas the coastal water (mixture of case‐1 and case‐2 waters) representation generally requires multi‐parameter models as demonstrated for sophisticated sensors such as SPEXone. title: A Hybrid Quantum Optimization Framework for Oil Spill Detection Using Marine Radar
abstract: Oil spills at sea pose a serious threat to marine ecosystems and coastal economic development. Therefore, rapid and accurate detection of oil spills is crucial for emergency response and environmental protection. Marine radar offers unique advantages in short-range, continuous, and all-weather monitoring, making it an important supplementary tool for oil spill detection. title: Hip Fracture Registry and Audit Readiness in Southeast Asia: A Scoping Review and Public-Evidence Implementation Gap Map

title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ STEM readiness in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand: Comparative insights from teacher education programs
abstract: STEM education has become a central agenda for enhancing human resource quality and global competitiveness. This study explored pre-service teachers’ readiness to implement STEM teaching in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with particular attention to their conceptual understanding, implementation ability and experience, perceived barriers and institutional support, and attitudes toward STEM education. title: Deep learning–assisted coral morphology cover across 742 sites on the Great Barrier Reef (2022–2025): A Great Reef Census citizen science dataset
abstract: Abstract Citizen science can expand the spatial extent of coral reef surveys, but its value is often limited by inconsistent data quality and slow manual analysis. Here we combine volunteer‐collected imagery with deep learning to overcome these constraints, delivering validated coral cover data at scale. We present 46,879 benthic seascape images from 742 sites across 267 reefs on the Great Barrier Reef, collected by Great Reef Census volunteers between September 2022 and February 2025. title: Cohort-level growth modeling of ethical engagement with artificial intelligence in education
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet limited evidence explains how students’ ethical engagement develops over time. Existing research is largely cross-sectional and often treats ethical awareness, reflection, and responsible use as a unified competence. This study examined cohort-level changes in AI Ethics Awareness (AEAw), Responsible AI Use (RAIU), and AI-Driven Reflection on Decision-Making (AIRD), including relationships among their initial levels and growth rates. title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Geographic Information Systems, and Machine Learning for Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Resource Management
abstract: Environmentally sensitive coastal areas are rapidly becoming urbanised, increasing pressure on vegetation, wetlands, surface-water resources and the natural resource base. The current study combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and machine learning to evaluate changes in Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) and environmental conditions in the Lekki–Ajah axis of Lagos State, Nigeria. Built-up areas, vegetation, wetlands, surface water and bare/exposed land were mapped using multitemporal satellite imagery and spatial datasets. title: Propagation-physics-guided channel augmentation and temporal–spectral fusion for domain-robust underwater acoustic target recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Spatiotemporal Precipitation Trends and Hybrid Machine Learning Prediction in the Humid Rainforest Climatic Zone of Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the spatiotemporal trends and hybrid machine learning prediction of precipitation in Nigeria’s humid rainforest climatic zone using 45 years (1981–2025) of monthly rainfall data from Calabar, Yenagoa, Benin City, and Ikeja. Data obtained from the NASA POWER database were analyzed using statistical, spatial, and machine learning techniques. title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. title: Flood susceptibility in a coastal backwater floodplain: a spatially validated multi-event SAR framework for Alappuzha, India
abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) is dominated by studies of upland catchments. At the same time, near-sea-level coastal and backwater floodplains, where inundation is shaped by reclamation, land use, tidal influence and constrained drainage rather than relief, remain comparatively under-explored. Existing studies also commonly rely on single-event inventories and machine-learning models validated through random data partitioning, which can overestimate predictive skill in spatial data. abstract: Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain. title: Gigantes tecnológicos y poder en plataformas de inteligencia artificial: una revisión crítica
abstract: Estudios críticos, administrativos y técnicos de comunicación y de ciencias sociales suelen diagnosticar vínculos estrechos entre los gigantes tecnológicos (Big Tech) y el nuevo verano de la inteligencia artificial (IA). title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
abstract: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. title: Tornado damage prediction using machine learning
abstract: Tornadoes are the most violent of all atmospheric windstorms. Although they occur throughout the world, the highest frequency is observed in the US, where over 1,700 tornadoes were recorded in 2024 alone. Intensity measures that characterize tornado damage, such as the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale, are derived from post-event assessment on the ground. title: Predicting long-term degradation of prestressed bridge girders using a hybrid finite element and deep learning approach
abstract: Prestressed concrete girders are widely used in bridge and railway infrastructure. However, their long-term performance is highly vulnerable to environmental effects, particularly corrosion, which significantly compromises structural serviceability and durability. Accurately quantifying corrosion-induced deterioration over extended periods remains challenging due to the substantial time and computational demands of conventional finite element analyses. abstract: ABSTRACT Digital elevation models (DEMs) are widely used to characterize terrain and support applications ranging from geomorphology to environmental management. While traditional analyses rely on handcrafted geomorphometric features, advances in machine learning enable richer, data‐driven representations of topographic surfaces. abstract: Technology roadmapping is a key strategic concern for companies. The aim of this study is to propose a cluster-based technology roadmapping approach using patent documents. The proposed approach is applied to artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The proposed approach provides evidence-based decision-making in healthcare management by identifying and prioritizing artificial intelligence (AI) technology domains with high long-term success potential. title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. abstract: Desde sus primeros tiempos, la inteligencia artificial ha encontrado un campo fértil de aplicación en el dominio médico; quizá por la forma en que se modelan y abordan eventos, y por la apertura del personal sanitario. abstract: Abstract The relatively short modern observational record limits our understanding of the relationship between global tropical cyclone (TC) frequency and sea surface temperature (SST), resulting in uncertain future TC projections. Using novel deep-learning-based past-millennium simulations with the Ai2 Climate Emulator version 2 (ACE2), we provide insight into the connections between SSTs and TCs. title: Influence of intrinsic factors on at-sea behavior of late chick-rearing emperor penguins (Aptenodytes forsteri) at Cape Crozier, Antarctica
abstract: Intrinsic differences among individuals can shape how marine predators forage in heterogeneous environments. For emperor penguins at Cape Crozier, the southernmost breeding colony in the Ross Sea and a potential climate refuge, the influence of sex, size, and body condition on at-sea behavior during late chick-rearing is unknown. title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) is a fundamental parameter for ocean engineering, maritime safety, and climate studies. Although spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) wave mode observations provide global, all-weather coverage, accurate SWH retrieval remains challenging due to the complex ocean-to-SAR imaging mechanism. This paper presents an explainable machine learning algorithm for retrieving SWH from Sentinel-1 SAR wave mode data. title: Machine learning-aided groundwater level and CO2 emission estimations in Indonesian tropical peatland
abstract: ABSTRACT Tropical peatlands store a large fraction of global soil carbon and emit large amounts of CO 2 from peat decomposition and root respiration. Accurate quantification of peatland carbon emissions requires a prediction that is sensitive to environmental gradients. This study estimated biweekly total and heterotrophic peat CO 2 emissions (Rs and Rh, respectively) in the peatland hydrological unit (PHU), which represents the whole peatland ecosystem on Rupat Island, Indonesia. title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
abstract: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. abstract: Underwater Image Enhancement (UIE) is crucial for achieving better visual quality and reliability of underwater acoustic image transmission in Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV).Nevertheless, many deep learning-based UIE solutions focus only on spatial restoration, overlooking its complementary frequency-domain aspects.To address this shortcoming.This paper proposes a novel hybrid CNN-Transformer framework combining Convolution Neural Network with Transformer structure, named FACE-UIE (Frequency-Aware CNN-Transformer Framework for Underwater Image Enhancement).It includes a Frequency-Aware C

title: Subsea pipeline vibration and integrity: a review of sensing technologies, mitigation mechanisms, and physics-integrated learning
abstract: Subsea pipeline systems constantly face harsh marine environments, where complex fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear seabed responses cause severe mechanical vibrations threatening long-term structural integrity. Consequently, continuous real-time monitoring is vital. abstract: Groundwater dynamics in South Florida play an important role in shaping the hydrologic balance of the region. This study investigated long-term trends in groundwater elevation, surface water stages, and their interactions across Water Conservation Areas 3A and 3B, Everglades National Park, coastal watersheds, and Florida Bay. Time series decomposition of long-term groundwater elevation (1997 to 2022) was used to identify trends, seasonal patterns, and anomalies. abstract: Trigonium zonatulatum (Greville) A. Mann, originally described as Triceratium zonatulatum Greville, was previously known solely from the Indo-Pacific, Indian Ocean, and Bering Sea. Here, we report the first record of this diatom species from the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea), based on material collected at Boca Chica Beach, Dominican Republic. title: Artificial intelligence cooperation and domestic absorptive capacity: evidence from ASEAN economies
abstract: Cross-border artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation is expanding, but evidence on its effect on domestic technological capability in recipient economies is scarce. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we create a composite AI absorptive capacity index for 10 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, encompassing innovation foundations, application foundations and industrial support. abstract: Abstract The Himantura species complex consists of large demersal whiprays vulnerable to coastal fisheries, yet unresolved taxonomy within the genus hinders conservation efforts, making molecular assessments crucial for effective fishery management. This study clarified genetic relationships among Himantura species in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) using species delimitation techniques. abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. abstract: Rapid urbanization and the replacement of vegetated surfaces by impervious materials can substantially alter urban thermal environments, while water bodies, topography, and coastal setting may further modify these patterns. Understanding how these factors contribute to land surface temperature (LST), particularly across large and geographically heterogeneous cities, is important for spatially targeted heat mitigation. title: Storybooks and Wordwalls in Problem Based Learning to Improve Critical Thinking and Environmental Awareness
abstract: Exploration and reflection on problem-based learning building critical thinking. Implementation constrains problem-based learning in elementary schools, students' ability to understand problems is crucial. Media are needed to stimulate the ability to analyze real-world problems, express logical opinions, and implement solutions as critical thinking skills that foster an attitude of environmental concern. The purpose of this study was to analyze the influence of the use of storybooks and wordwall deep problem-based learning on critical thinking skills and environmental awareness simultaneously.

This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). abstract: Research in marine ecosystem ecology increasingly integrates biodiversity status and trends, ecosystem functioning, and human pressures. Understanding how marine biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning remains central to the field, while growing concern over ecosystem condition has shifted attention towards relationships between human pressures and ecological responses. abstract: Gastric cancer still has rather high rates of incidences around the globe and the amount of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in the tumor tissues has proved to be a reliable predictor of prognosis in patients suffering from this type of disease. abstract: Understanding the relationships between fruit morphological traits and biochemical characteristics is essential for the efficient utilization of plum (Prunus domestica L.) genetic resources in breeding programs. In this study, fifteen local European plum varieties collected from the Central and Eastern Black Sea Region of Türkiye were evaluated during [2022 and 2023 year] to characterize their morphological and biochemical diversity and to identify the key biochemical determinants of antioxidant activity. abstract: Accurately identifying whether a field of view of satellite hyperspectral infrared sounders is clear or cloudy is critical for geophysical parameter retrieval and meteorological applications. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic disturbances and climate change, despite providing ecological services, including biodiversity conservation, coastal protection, and blue carbon storage. Long-term evaluations of mangrove dynamics and associated environmental conditions remain limited, particularly in the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world. abstract: The accurate representation of tidal currents is essential for understanding coastal circulation and interpreting satellite observations of ocean surface currents. In preparation for the upcoming ODYSEA (Ocean Dynamics and Surface Exchange with the Atmosphere) satellite mission, high-resolution MITgcm (Massachusetts Institute of Technology General Circulation Model) LLC2160 outputs, generated for mission planning, were evaluated for their representation of tidal currents. abstract: Climate transition has increased investors' concerns about carbon risk, yet evidence remains limited on how firms' technological capabilities shape market responses, particularly in emerging markets. abstract: Manual visual counting remains the standard procedure for estimating Kent mango ( Mangifera indica L.) yield in northern Peru, an inconsistent practice that compromises harvest planning, transport dimensioning and commercial negotiation. abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. abstract: Recently, credit card fraud has increased a significant threat to financial institutions and consumers, thus a robust and intelligent detection system is essential to prevent fraudulent activities efficiently. abstract: La convergencia entre biotecnología, inteligencia artificial, ciencia de datos y sistemas ecológicos ha desplazado los conflictos bioéticos del ámbito clínico hacia dimensiones sociotécnicas, políticas y de gobernanza. title: Retos para la ética de la investigación clínica en el contexto de las inteligencias artificiales: hacia una inteligencia aumentada
abstract: El auge y la penetración de los modelos de inteligencia artificial en todos los ámbitos de la vida humana constituyen un fenómeno continuo y dinámico.La investigación científica igualmente se ha visto permeada por el advenimiento y la democratización cada vez mayor de dichas tecnologías.Su implementación, desde el tratamiento de datos hasta su utilización en la redacción científica, hace que el uso de estos recursos deba observarse desde una perspectiva ética que nos permita reflexionar sobre hasta qué punto su uso resulta adecuado y si constituye o no un riesgo para las personas participantes

abstract: En publicación científica se han probado distintos incentivos para optimizar el proceso de revisión por pares (RPP), sin lograr un impacto significativo en los tiempos y calidad de las revisiones. La irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) prometen revolucionar el futuro de la RPP. abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a well-known sleep disorder that can lead to major health consequences if left untreated. abstract: Against the backdrop of the deep integration of the digital economy and artificial intelligence, whether and how AI policies can enhance the intensification of industrial land use is a critical issue concerning the efficiency of land resource allocation and urban sustainable development. title: Advancing Mangrove Forest Mapping Using Super-Resolution and Semantic Segmentation of Multi-Date Multi-Sensor Satellite Imagery: Applications in East and West Africa
abstract: Remote sensing is essential for mapping mangrove forest ecosystems, yet accuracy and spatial resolution remain limited, particularly in Africa, where mangroves are fragmented, reference data and cloud-free images are scarce. The state-of-the-art of mangrove forest mapping relies on native-resolution imagery using machine learning. abstract: Reinforced concrete structures are extensively used in wastewater collection systems; however, their structural performance can progressively deteriorate under aggressive sewer environments associated with gas generation and chemical attack. abstract: This study develops an impact-acoustic framework for classifying predefined surface-damage states on steam-turbine blades, identifying one of three damage regions, and estimating class-dependent severity parameters. abstract: The corrosion behavior of weathering steels in marine atmospheric environments emerges from the synergistic interactions among alloy chemistry, exposure duration, and environmental loading, exhibiting strong nonlinearity and multiscale coupled responses. abstract: Abstract Air pollution in Africa is a critical public health issue that results in deaths of people, especially in places where urbanisation and vehicle emissions are increasing. abstract: Ecotourism promotes sustainable development, but evaluating tourists’ experiences becomes difficult because of different multi-source feedback. Traditional methods using text or rating have been inaccurate. abstract: Abstract Meteorological seasons are typically defined through fixed calendar intervals or region‐specific thresholds, yet such approaches fail to capture the actual variability of the annual cycle. Here we present a machine learning framework that objectively detects meteorological seasons and projects their future evolution. abstract: Abstract Mangroves are important coastal blue carbon ecosystems, but future sediment GHG emissions remain uncertain because global projections have largely emphasized atmospheric climate drivers, with less attention to coastal hydrology, particularly sea-surface salinity and tidal range. abstract: Abstract This study applies a grid-based, explainable machine learning framework to identify dominant flood-influencing factors under hydrologically heterogeneous conditions, using Jeju Island as a representative volcanic environment. Historical flood trace maps were integrated with multi-layer spatial datasets to classify flooded and non-flooded grid cells at a 100 m resolution using five tree-based algorithms. abstract: This study explored spatial patterns, vertical burial depths, polymer types, and ecological risk of sedimentary microplastics in sediments from five beaches on Diu Island on the Arabian Sea coast of India. title: A physics-informed and transferable machine learning workflow for basin-scale heat flow prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of heat flow is critical for geothermal resource assessment yet remains challenging in structurally complex basins because of sparse measurements and the coupled effects of multiple geological processes. We develop a physics-informed and transferable machine-learning workflow that integrates multi-source geological and geophysical parameters through a stacking ensemble model. abstract: The increasing accumulation of plastic waste has encouraged its reuse as a partial aggregate replacement in concrete, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional construction materials. abstract: Abstract. Radar mosaic data represent a critical and widely utilized resource in weather forecasting. abstract: Abstract We present a new method for developing time step controllers based on a technique from the field of machine learning. This method is applicable to stable time integrators that have an embedded scheme, i.e., that provide a local error estimate similar to Runge–Kutta pairs. abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has transformed aquatic invasive species (AIS) surveillance, yet the temporal ecology of eDNA signals remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce the concept of “eDNA phenology” to describe predictable seasonal variation in eDNA detectability arising from interactions among species life history, environmental conditions, and the ecological processes governing DNA production, transport, and persistence. abstract: Ocean-related options (OROs), including marine renewable energy and ocean-based carbon dioxide removal, are emerging as promising climate mitigation actions. This study assesses the Duero River basin (Spain), where groundwater nitrate concentrations have increased in recent decades due to intensive agriculture and livestock farming. abstract: The intersection of NANO+AI+ML is a novel approach for environmental risk governance, pollution control and disaster management. abstract: The convergence of the climate and ocean agendas has become a defining feature of contemporary global governance. abstract: Litter stranded on beaches can severely degrade local ecosystems and diminish the tourism value of coastal areas. abstract: The practice of artificial intelligence has recently expanded several social spheres, with the pharmaceutical domain leading the way. abstract: Abstract Coastal wetlands are increasingly impacted by tropical cyclones and storm surges. abstract: Environmental distortions and dataset-induced bias are challenges for underwater object detection due to the impact on model generalization. title: Push and pull factors of relocation in the coastal zone: what matters most?
abstract: Abstract Permanent relocation is increasingly proposed as an effective long-term strategy for coastal areas affected by recurrent flooding. While the literature on coastal relocation has been steadily growing—particularly on policy processes, financial mechanisms, and lived experiences—less attention has been given to understanding the reasoning behind relocation decisions. This study provides empirical evidence on the factors that drive willingness to relocate from a telephone survey administered in high-risk coastal settings on the Delmarva Peninsula in Maryland and Hampton Roads, Virginia.

abstract: Early and correct detection of cancer regions in histopathology images is important for timely diagnosis and treatment. abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent organic pollutants with widespread environmental occurrence. Their toxicity and resistance to degradation pose serious risks to ecosystems and human health. While existing separation (e.g., adsorption, filtration) and degradation (e.g., photochemical, electrochemical, thermal) technologies can achieve partial PFAS removal, limitations such as high energy demand, poor cost-efficiency, and harsh operating conditions hinder their in situ application. title: From concept to performance: A typology-based framework for designing, validating, and monitoring nature-based solutions (NbS) for coastal erosion risk in the Colombian Caribbean
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are increasingly promoted for coastal adaptation; however, ecological restoration gains and reductions in wave energy do not necessarily demonstrate sustained control of coastal erosion. This systematic review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 to examine how coastal typology, hydrodynamic forcing, sediment balance, monitoring design, and governance influence NbS performance. title: Ancient Continental Signatures Preserved in Eocene Intraplate Volcanism at the Conrad Rise, Indian Ocean
abstract: ABSTRACT Oceanic rises in the Indian Ocean are generally interpreted as products of mantle plume magmatism that developed on the oceanic lithosphere; however, evidence suggests the presence of inherited continental materials beneath select oceanic plateaus and rises. We report zircon and titanite petrochronological data from Eocene intraplate basalt dredged from the Conrad Rise in the southern Indian Ocean. title: Ocean thermal inertia sustains a tropical Pacific mean state shift under net zero
abstract: Abstract The tropical Pacific plays a pivotal role in global climate. Changes in its mean state and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) could significantly alter regional hydroclimates, causing major economic and societal impacts, yet its response to different emission pathways remains poorly constrained. Here, we assess changes in the mean state and ENSO under high-emission and net-zero scenarios using climate model simulations spanning centennial to millennial timescales. title: Spatiotemporal training‐free LiDAR denoising and hybrid pedestrian detection on airport aprons: Focus on low‐speed and stationary targets
abstract: Abstract LiDAR sensors in apron environments enable detailed monitoring of aircraft, vehicles, and pedestrians, but their clouds points often contain irregular noise from reflections, clutter, and dynamic interference. This study proposes the density and temporally aware filter (DTF‐Filter), which combines local density‐adaptive thresholding with temporal consistency across consecutive frames. title: STRATEGIC SPATIAL PLANNING FOR ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE TOURISM SECTOR IN GOA, INDIA
abstract: Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. title: A new species of sole (Pleuronectiformes, Soleidae), Soleichthys labyrinthus, from the China Sea
abstract: The genus Soleichthys (Soleidae) suffers from taxonomic confusion due to morphological similarities. In this study, a new sole species, Soleichthys labyrinthus sp. nov ., is described based on the holotype and 24 paratypes collected from the northern South China Sea and the East China Sea. This new species is readily distinguished from its congeners by a unique combination of characters: 78–86 dorsal-fin rays and 65–73 anal-fin rays; the ocular side is tawny brown, featuring a labyrinth-shaped reticulated pattern and lacking the typical transverse bands found in most congeners. title: Transformer-Based Bias Correction of ERA5 Winds over the East China Sea and Wind Resource Trend During 2016–2025
abstract: Accurate wind information is essential for offshore wind-resource assessment in the East China Sea, yet global reanalyses remain poorly constrained in this region. Using one year of multi-height (20–200 m) floating-lidar observations from the Shanghai Far-Sea Wind Demonstration Site, this study evaluates ERA5 wind performance, develops a machine-learning bias-correction model, and reconstructs a bias-corrected decadal (2016–2025) hub-height wind resource. title: An Immobilized Marine Glycosyltransferase Acts as a Stabilized Biocatalyst for the Synthesis of Mannosylated Phosphoisoprenoids
abstract: Glycosylated phosphoisoprenoids constitute valuable bioactive molecules and starting materials for complex glycosylation cascades. Herein we report the identification and the functional characterization of a newly identified polyprenyl phosphomannose synthase from the marine microorganism Rhodococcus erythropolis PR4. This enzyme, normally unstable in its free form, is significantly stabilized by immobilization and can be reused up to four times for sustainable phosphoisoprenoid derivatization.
