title: The Metamorphosis of Aesthetic Consciousness: From Paterian Sensibility to Algorithmic Modernity—A Psychological and Literary Perspective
abstract: The nineteenth-century Aesthetic Movement, which emerged as a celebration of beauty and advocated the principle of “art for art’s sake,” has undergone a significant transformation in the contemporary era. What initially emphasized individual sensibility, aesthetic experience, and the pursuit of beauty has gradually evolved into a complex synthesis of human consciousness, psychological perception, cultural hybridity, technological mediation, and algorithmic creativity. title: Toward real-time wave forecasting via data-driven reduced-order modeling with data assimilation
abstract: Reliable wave forecasts are a cornerstone of coastal risk management and offshore operations, yet operational products remain expensive to generate at high resolution and can be insufficiently calibrated for decision-making under uncertainty. We present a hybrid forecasting framework that couples data-driven reduced-order modeling with sequential data assimilation to produce flow-dependent, spatially coherent ensembles of significant wave height over the North Sea. title: Thermally Recoverable Fracto‐Mechanoluminescence in Manganese‐Based Hybrid Halides for Fatigue‐Resistant Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Fracto‐mechanoluminescence (FML) materials have recently demonstrated great potential as next‐generation interactive optoelectronic systems, while they generally suffer from irreversible fatigue degradation under long‐term cyclic stress, severely limiting their practical applications. Here we design the flexible FML composite films based on the manganese‐based hybrid halide EPB 2 MnBr 4 (EPB = ethyltriphenylphosphonium), exhibiting intense green emission under mechanical stimuli. title: La Alfabetización Digital en las Universidades, la IA y su Impacto en el Mundo del Trabajo
abstract: This research highlights the need to incorporate the teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, particularly big data, into the educational process. In addition to developing digital literacy, students must acquire knowledge of the technological tools required by companies, which may become their future sources of employment. Furthermore, this research explores the practical application of big data in the world of work.

abstract: In this work, we introduce a new thermo-fluid-structure interaction formulation for the first time to study in a systematic manner the influence of thermal stress, gyroscopic force, and fluid dynamics inside the structure on the stability of rotating pipes. title: Atomic-level design and device modeling of lead-free Cs2AgSbCl6 double perovskite solar cells through DFT, SCAPS-1D, and predictive algorithms
abstract: Lead-free double perovskite solar cells (DPSCs) have emerged as attractive alternatives to conventional lead-based perovskites because of their superior environmental compatibility, enhanced chemical stability, and reduced toxicity. In this research study, the performance of a solar cell architecture FTO/IGZO/Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 /Cu 2 O are systematically studied by the simulation software known as SCAPS-1D. DFT calculations were performed using WIEN2k package to investigate structural and optoelectronic properties of Cs 2 AgSbCl 6 material to determine its suitability for photovoltaic applications.

title: Decoupled operational transfer path analysis for vibration source identification in marine steam turbine generator sets
abstract: To address strong multi-source coupling, complex transmission paths, and reference-channel crosstalk in operational transfer path analysis (OTPA) of marine steam turbine generator sets, this study proposes a decoupled OTPA method based on vibration source coupling separation. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been progressively integrated into educational processes through smart tutors, adaptive learning platforms, virtual assistants, and generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT. These technologies can personalize instruction, provide immediate feedback, facilitate access to information, and support students with different learning paces and needs. abstract: Reliable detection of underwater objects is important for mine countermeasures, unexploded-ordnance surveys, navigational-hazard assessment, and subsea infrastructure inspection. Interpretation of side-scan sonar (SSS) imagery is still largely performed by trained human operators, making post-mission analysis time-consuming when large volumes of data are collected. title: Climate Vulnerability and Gendered Coping Strategies: Insights from Disaster-Prone Coastal Odisha
abstract: Abstract: Climate-induced disasters, including floods, cyclones, and droughts, have increased in frequency and severity in coastal Odisha over the past few decades. Recurrent crop failures, livelihood disruptions, and loss of income have heightened economic stress and reduced the resilience of vulnerable communities. These impacts are often gender-differentiated, influencing how men and women respond to and cope with disaster-related challenges. title: The impact of the Montreux convention on NATO regarding the security of the black sea region
abstract: This study examines how the Montreux Convention shapes NATO’s defense posture on the Eastern Flank within the Black Sea security environment. Building on international relations theory, maritime law, and geopolitical analysis, it evaluates regional security and international cooperation under Montreux’s legal regime. abstract: Nearshore hardbottom (NSHB) habitats occur in shallow coastal waters throughout the Florida Keys and support sessile benthic invertebrate communities dominated by sponges and octocorals. In turn, these sessile benthic invertebrates provide unique structural habitats, supporting motile invertebrate and fish communities. Design/methodology/approach: This study employs a quantitative explanatory approach using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) to examine the relationships among governance, interagency synergy, government policy, technological innovation, and trade strengthening. abstract: Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency. title: A SwiGLU enhanced ConvNeXt framework for multispectral Sentinel-2 land use and land cover classification
abstract: Land use and land cover (LCLU) classification from multispectral satellite imagery is important for applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, agriculture, and disaster management. abstract: Introduction: The growing integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has transformed the way students access, process, and produce information, creating new learning opportunities while also raising risks associated with cognitive dependence. The objective of this study was to analyze the relationship between the use of generative artificial intelligence, critical thinking, and student autonomy, identifying the conditions that foster independent judgment and those that may promote excessive delegation of reasoning. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of the drilling rate of penetration (ROP) is crucial to optimizing drilling performance, wellbore stability, enhancing operational efficiency, and reducing the overall cost of hydrocarbon exploration. This study focused on evaluating and comparing different machine learning models for ROP prediction and identifying the most influential operational drilling and gas‐derived parameters affecting ROP performance for clastic sedimentary formation. title: Forecasting compound sea level extremes: the 29–30 October 2018 Adriatic storm surge and meteotsunami extreme
abstract: On 29-30 October 2018, an extreme sea level occurred in the Adriatic Sea, driven by a combination of long-period (storm surge) and short-period (meteotsunami) oscillations. Storm surges were strongest in the northern Adriatic, while shorter-period oscillations dominated in the middle Adriatic, where a meteotsunami was observed and recorded in Vela Luka Bay (Korčula Island). title: Inferential dominance of global hierarchical neural architectures for multi-horizon univariate environmental forecasting
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate multi-horizon forecasting of atmospheric pollutants is essential for environmental decision-support systems, particularly under spatially heterogeneous and temporally dependent conditions. This study evaluates the inferential dominance of global hierarchical neural architectures for univariate forecasting of PM 2.5 , PM 10 , O 3 , and NO 2 concentrations over Paraná, southern Brazil, using CAMS-EAC4 reanalysis data from 2010 to 2024. title: Robust Peanut Size Grading via Scale-Augmented Ordinal Classification and Morphological Feature Fusion
abstract: Deep learning models classify peanut size accurately under fixed imaging conditions, but accuracy drops when apparent object scale changes, for example with camera-to-object distance. abstract: Introduction The population of Bolboschoenoplectus mariqueter has substantially declined because of habitat modification and competition. abstract: El objetivo del estudio fue analizar la relación entre el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) y el rendimiento académico percibido en estudiantes de Ingeniería de Minas mediante modelos estadísticos y machine learning. abstract: B10 Cu Ni alloy is commonly subjected to both flow and external loading during marine service, but the influence of sub-yield elastic strain on its corrosion behavior and its dependence on flow velocity remain unclear. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme rainfall events, rainfall-triggered clustered landslides have become a major concern in mountainous disaster risk management due to their sudden occurrence, regional clustering, and high destructive potential. This paper systematically reviews the current development and technological advances in early warning models for rainfall-triggered clustered landslides. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models have transformed weather forecasting, but their skill for unprecedented weather extremes is unclear. Here, we analyze GraphCast, AIFS, and FuXi forecasts of the unprecedented 2024 Dubai storm, which had twice the training set's highest rainfall in that region. abstract: Gelatinous zooplankton (GZP) comprise a highly diverse group of marine taxa that play key ecological roles throughout the world’s oceans. abstract: Energy wells underpin critical technologies in the global energy transition, including geothermal energy extraction, carbon capture and storage, and underground hydrogen storage. In recent years, digital twin (DT) concepts have been increasingly explored to support well design, monitoring, and integrity management. abstract: The white anglerfish, Lophius piscatorius Linnaeus, 1758, is a demersal species of great ecological and commercial importance in Tunisian waters. abstract: Critical transitions can irreversibly change complex systems, making anticipation a fundamental challenge. Machine learning is increasingly used for early warning, but many approaches require transition labels or control information. title: PatchRNN: A Multi-Scale Decoupled and Structure-Aware Framework for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Long-term time series forecasting is important in energy, transportation, and meteorology, yet existing methods struggle to model multi-scale features and preserve local sequence structure. We propose PatchRNN, a decomposition- and structure-aware framework for multivariate forecasting. abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral images (HSI) play a vital role in remote sensing applications such as surveillance and precision agriculture, yet they face challenges including limited labeled samples and class imbalance. This paper presents a new method for HSI classification by integrating spectral band selection with advanced deep learning techniques. title: Promoting Agricultural Green Productivity Through Geographical Indication Certification: Mechanisms and Spatial Heterogeneity
abstract: Agricultural green transformation is important for achieving economic growth and environmental sustainability. Geographical indication agricultural products (GIAPs) have become a useful tool for improving agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP). However, the mechanisms through which GIAPs affect AGTFP and their spatial differences are not yet fully understood. abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of knowledge acquisition and low information utilization efficiency in marine diesel engine fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a question answering system integrating intent recognition and named entity recognition. abstract: Abstract In near-shore shallow-water environments, continuous autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) motion causes substantial acoustic target scale variations, while seabed sediments, rocks, and clutter severely degrade sonar image quality. The economic and nutritional importance of seaweed is increasing because of its protein, vitamin, essential amino acid, and various bioactive compounds. It is a nutrient-dense “blue food” that can be grown without freshwater, fertilizers, or pesticides and has a rapid growth rate. It also provides ecosystem services including carbon sequestration and nutrient bioremediation. abstract: Stainless steel corrosion resistance is governed by an ultrathin, chemically graded passive film, whose protectiveness depends on composition, defect chemistry, electronic structure, and ion transport. abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is one of the major pollutants affecting environmental quality and human health, yet accurate surface NO2 (NO2Surface) estimation remains challenging due to complex nonlinear relationships between satellite-derived NO2 column density (NO2column) and near-surface concentrations. abstract: Fluoride contamination is a persistent public health concern, yet existing risk assessments often emphasize individual exposure pathways, most commonly drinking water, and may not fully capture the substantial variation in health outcomes observed across communities with similar drinking-water fluoride concentrations. Recent advances in offshore tsunami observation networks have made it increasingly feasible to estimate tsunami sources from observed waveforms using adjoint-based inversion methods. Updates in 2010 and 2020 provided detailed usage guidance. Numerous extensions have customized ODD for specific disciplines and model types. abstract: Abstract A rapid transition toward sustainable and clean energy is necessary for a secure energy future in today's dynamic world. title: Beyond historical catch: developing a climate-adaptive fisheries allocation framework for transboundary fish stocks under international law
abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the geographical distribution of transboundary fish stocks, challenging the legal and institutional assumptions upon which international fisheries governance has traditionally been based. Existing allocation systems, largely founded on historical catch records and relatively stable stock distributions, are becoming increasingly inconsistent with ecological realities, generating disputes among coastal States and undermining the effectiveness of Regional Fisheries Management Organisations (RFMOs). title: Geometría diferencial y topología aplicadas al aprendizaje profundo geométrico: fundamentos e implicaciones educativas para el pensamiento matemático y computacional
abstract: La geometría diferencial y la topología proporcionan fundamentos matemáticos relevantes para el análisis y la representación de datos no euclidianos dentro del aprendizaje profundo geométrico (Geometric Deep Learning). Esta revisión sistemática tuvo como objetivo analizar los aportes de la geometría diferencial y la topología que sustentan el aprendizaje profundo geométrico e identificar las implicaciones educativas que pueden derivarse para el desarrollo del pensamiento matemático y computacional. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has become a critical global threat, often described as a “silent pandemic.” Although the broad application of antibiotics across various sectors has yielded significant benefits, inadequate regulation has led to inappropriate antimicrobial use, reducing treatment effectiveness. Thus, the development of resistance genes has accelerated, leading to rising global mortality. A total of 114 first-year Tourism degree students from Complutense University of Madrid (Spain) participated. The assessed skill was oral production in English for specific purposes (ESP) in the tourism field, through two promotional videos: one created conventionally and another supported by AI. title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex.

abstract: Abstract. Data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) weather models are increasingly positioned as alternatives or complements to physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems, yet systematic model evaluation studies that compare both paradigms under controlled experimental conditions remain limited. abstract: Globally, smart technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) is proliferating quickly and reshaping political institutions, business practices, healthcare delivery systems, and civil infrastructure development. title: Quantifying SMART drumline catches in an Australian bather protection program
abstract: The global incidence of shark bites on humans has increased over time, driving the development of shark mitigation strategies to reduce the frequency of human-shark interactions. Traditional lethal shark control programs have used fishing gear aimed at reducing local shark populations. There has, however, been a shift towards more ecologically sustainable, non-lethal approaches. abstract: Many regions of India face floods and droughts in the same year, sometimes within a few hundred kilometres of each other. During a heavy monsoon spell, reservoirs in one basin release large volumes of water to protect their dams, and much of this water flows to the sea, while districts in a neighbouring basin run short of drinking and irrigation water a few months later. abstract: Salt intrusion in river-network estuaries is commonly related to upstream freshwater discharge, but the relationship may vary among channels due to flow redistribution within the estuarine network. In the Modaomen Estuary of the Pearl River Delta, salt intrusion poses a serious threat to freshwater security during the dry season. title: The Impact of AI on STEM Education and Workforce Readiness in Nigeria
abstract: This study explores the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education and workforce readiness in Nigeria. Amid rapid global technological change, Nigeria faces critical challenges in aligning its education system and labour market with AI-driven demands, including outdated curricula, infrastructural deficits, limited digital literacy, and underinvestment in teacher training. title: Image of the City in the Age of Large Language Models: ChatGPT as a New Urban Observer
abstract: This research examines how city images of Istanbul’s Historic Peninsula are evolving with artificial intelligence and expanding user-generated content. City image refers to a mental representation of urban structure, and imageability to the ease of forming it. abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. abstract: Integrated Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and Big Data Analytics (BDA) offer substantial potential to improve visibility, trust, coordination, and decision-making in maritime logistics. abstract: Continental crustal growth mechanisms remain a pivotal frontier in geoscience. The Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB), Earth’s largest accretionary orogen, provides critical insights into Phanerozoic crustal evolution. Devonian records along the southeastern CAOB are key to deciphering mid-Paleozoic crustal growth. abstract: Precision medicine increasingly relies on multimodal data and artificial intelligence, creating a need for scalable education and assessment. We developed an online diabetes precision medicine course and conducted an observational single-group pre–post evaluation of knowledge, confidence, and rubric-scored open-ended responses among 435 learners who completed the course. abstract: Salt marshes are increasingly recognized as important sources of total alkalinity (TA), contributing to coastal carbon sequestration. While hydrological drivers are well studied, plant-mediated effects on TA export remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract With the advancement of electronic manufacturing towards high density and miniaturization, PCB soldering defect detection has become a critical component of industrial quality control. abstract: Mangrove forests are ecologically and socioeconomically important ecosystems that require accurate and timely monitoring. abstract: Background Enterococcus faecalis ( E. faecalis ) is frequently associated with persistent root canal infections and treatment failure, and effective strategies for its elimination remain limited. abstract: The oil and gas industry faces substantial occupational, process, and environmental risks arising from high-pressure and high-temperature systems, hazardous hydrocarbons, complex operations, and environmentally sensitive activities. This study aims to examine how innovative technologies can be integrated with sustainable Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) practices to strengthen risk and hazard management, operational safety, environmental protection, and regulatory compliance across upstream, midstream, and downstream operations. title: AI-Assisted Image-Based Lichen Health Assessment for Environmental Sensing Using Naturally Acquired Field Images
abstract: Lichens are widely recognized as biological indicators of environmental quality because their physiological condition reflects long-term atmospheric and ecological changes. However, conventional lichen assessment relies primarily on manual visual inspection by trained specialists, limiting the scalability of environmental monitoring. This paper presents an AI-assisted image analysis framework for automated lichen health assessment using naturally acquired field images as a step toward intelligent environmental sensing. abstract: Information on heat-related health risks that is based on meteorological data and forecasts is important for outdoor workers, farm managers, and many other stakeholders, but visualization and interpretation of climate data in a user-friendly way remains a challenge. This proof-of-concept research developed Sol, an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to conveniently interpret and communicate heat stress risks through smartphones and other devices. abstract: Abstract Developing flexible electronics that integrate multimodal sensing, bias-free signal generation, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding is critical for wearable health monitoring, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction. abstract: Abstract Sustainability goals and stricter environmental protection requirements now guide a wide range of experts, from material scientists to architects, to find practical ways to incorporate byproducts and waste materials into concrete construction. title: Codon-aware multi-scale feature fusion for metagenomic sequence classification
abstract: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating among diverse sequence types remains a formidable challenge. To address this, we present CamFi (Codon-aware Multi-scale Feature Fusion), a unified framework integrating overlapping nucleotide-triplet representations with multi-scale dilated convolutions for classifying prokaryotic chromosomes, eukaryotic chromosomes, plasmids, and viruses. abstract: Rapid urban expansion in secondary cities of Sub-Saharan Africa has intensified pressure on land resources and infrastructure, exposing the limitations of conventional planning systems reliant on periodic assessments. title: A physics-guided noise-enhanced adaptive fusion dual-stream network for water level estimation using CYGNSS and Sentinel-1 observations
abstract: Abstract Accurate river water level estimation is crucial for flood prevention, disaster mitigation, water resource management, and river-network regulation. However, water level variations in complex river-network regions are characterized by strong non-stationarity and nonlinearity, posing significant challenges to accurate estimation. To address this issue, this study proposes a Physics-Guided Noise-Enhanced Adaptive Fusion Dual-Stream Network (PGNAF-DSNet) for water level estimation using the Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observation

abstract: Abstract Deep learning has been widely adopted in the field of bioacoustics, enabling behavioral and ecological research into many sound producing animals through the use of specially designed and trained models. So-called foundational models can generalize to novel species or tasks, but require larger and more diverse training datasets. title: An AI-Enabled Multi-Level Governance Framework for Consulting and Research Institutes in Saudi Public Universities
abstract: This study examines the governance of institutes of studies and consulting services in Saudi public universities, which operate as hybrid entities combining academic and contract-based consulting functions. Despite their strategic role, these institutes face governance challenges, including overlapping authorities, unclear roles, and inconsistent levels of transparency and accountability. title: Precipitation isotopes respond to contrasting moisture pathways over the Core Monsoon Zone and the Bay of Bengal
abstract: Precipitation isotopes integrate the cumulative effects of moisture transport, rainout, and land–atmosphere interactions, making them valuable tracers of monsoon hydrological processes. However, the dominant controls on isotope variability differ across the Indian Summer Monsoon region. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a comprehensive review of live‐line work on high‐voltage transmission overhead lines, with a focus on insulation performance, air‐gap breakdown and discharge physics under realistic operating conditions. This review primarily covers journal publications from approximately 2014 to 2026, with emphasis on recent developments in the field. title: Global Long-wavelength Body-wave Catalog (GLoBoCat) for Lower Mantle P and S Wave Travel Times
abstract: Long period seismic body wave travel times are a foundational source of information regarding the Earth's interior. Manual methods provide travel time catalogs with high internal consistency, but have not kept pace with the rapid growth in teleseismic waveforms. Here we use attention-based machine learning trained on prior manual datasets to develop a catalog spanning 2010-2023 which is consistent with previous catalogs and easy to update. abstract: Digitalization has been increasingly portrayed as a game-changing approach to enhancing construction safety through the adoption of technologies like Building Information Modelling (BIM), sensors, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and data analytics-based safety tools. While research interest and adoption of digital safety technologies have been increasing, the evidence of long-term improvement in safety performance is unclear. title: Exploring learning in classic African board games: a review of recent literature
abstract: Abstract A growing body of research on board games demonstrates that these games can function as learning environments and provide opportunities for learning across diverse contexts. Although learning is often conceptualized contextually within this literature, studies increasingly demonstrate that meaningful learning can occur through participation in board game environments. title: How volant seabirds benefit from sub-surface predators during multi-predator feeding aggregations
abstract: Multi-predator feeding aggregations are common in marine ecosystems and frequently involve seabirds. Often labelled opportunistic 'scroungers', volant seabirds derive diverse benefits from the association with sub-surface predators (such as cetaceans, pinnipeds, Teleosts) which can significantly enhance their hunting performance. abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) with increasing degrees of autonomy changes how tax administrations detect risk, cross-check information and prepare decisions with individual legal effects. This study designs an algorithmic governance model for tax assessment in Ecuador that combines technological efficiency, explainability and protection of taxpayers’ rights. abstract: BACKGROUND: Imported dengue remains a public health concern in non-endemic countries. Local transmission may occur when imported infections coincide with competent vectors and suitable environmental conditions. We developed a cross-national framework for predicting monthly imported dengue risk in Japan and the Republic of Korea. METHODS: We analyzed monthly data from January 2005 to June 2025. abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education requires examining how these systems represent gender. This study analyses gender attribution in the responses of five systems (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and Perplexity) to 16 controlled prompts about professional roles, organised into eight categories. The surveillance video-based rainfall measurement method has potential for high spatial and temporal resolution rainfall monitoring. Existing video-based rainfall estimation models have incorporated temporal information; however, challenges remain in improving accuracy and robustness under different environmental conditions. abstract: While machine learning (ML) weather models are emerging as promising tools for predicting weather conditions on a global scale, their coarse resolution and systematic biases limit practical applicability in regional contexts. This paper assesses the role of model output statistics (MOS) in post-processing temperature ensemble forecasts that are dynamically downscaled from the state-of-the-art ML weather model FuXi-ENS. abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly involved in travel planning and hotel choice, yet research has not fully explained how consumers move from evaluating an AI-generated recommendation to responding to the hotel brand being recommended. abstract: ABSTRACT Dimensionality reduction is essential in simulation‐based shape design, where high‐dimensional parameterizations hinder optimization, surrogate modeling, and systematic design‐space exploration. Parametric Model Embedding (PME) addresses this issue by constructing reduced variables from geometric information while preserving an explicit backmapping to the original design parameters. abstract: Abstract Marine sponges harbor diverse communities of microorganisms that are essential for the host survival and function. Omics analyses have in recent years described the functional diversity and potential of sponge symbionts, however it is unclear if and how they interacted with each other and the host to provide essential metabolites for growth. abstract: As the thermal backbone of urban energy infrastructure, transmission cables directly affect the stability and resilience of modern cities. However, high operating temperatures, driven by Joule heating and solar radiation, critically limit the ampacity of overhead transmission lines, particularly under extreme climate conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a sliding variable‐based optimal control (SVBOC) framework for canonical nonlinear systems with unknown control direction. The approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with neural network (NN) approximation to address the challenge of solving the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation in systems with unknown dynamics. abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables continuous monitoring of dynamic strain along tens of kilometres of optical fibre, generating massive datasets whose interpretation and automated analysis remain challenging. DAS data can be understood as a time-distance image array. However, the absence of standardised representation methods limits both the physical interpretability and the development of automated image-based analysis pipelines. abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive and diverse form of breast cancer characterized by the absence of progesterone and Estrogen receptors and HER2 expression, which limits conventional therapeutic options and contributes to poor prognosis. Chemotherapy remains the standard of care, but multidrug resistance, tumor heterogeneity, and systemic toxicities restrict long-term efficacy. abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom has revolutionized the production of teaching content. abstract: The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. In this context, academics who assume academic program leadership responsibilities occupy an intermediate position between teaching practice and strategic management, although the literature frequently addresses these dimensions separately. title: Tropicalisation of rocky shore gastropod communities along the Baja California Peninsula
abstract: Abstract Tropicalisation is restructuring marine communities globally. Despite extensive research in subtidal habitats, the extent of tropicalisation and its impact on rocky intertidal communities remains poorly understood. Here we integrated contemporary field surveys with genetic barcoding, historic surveys, museum collections, and fossil records to document changes in the rocky shore gastropod communities along approximately 3,120 km of the Baja California Peninsula coastline. title: Global advances in Generative AI for renewable energy and implications for sustainable energy transitions in Africa
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. abstract: Antibiotic resistance has become one of the greatest threats to global health in this century, causing many health problems in many countries. abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to climate change, land-use transformations and altered disturbance regimes. abstract: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) systems are at the core of modern cyber-physical infrastructures, powering applications in automotive, healthcare, telecommunications, industrial control, and aerospace domains. However, their resource-constrained design and deterministic execution expose them to a wide spectrum of cyber-physical attacks that can compromise both digital integrity and physical safety. abstract: Reliable long-term wind-power prediction requires linking short-term mast measurements with long-term reanalysis data. This study developed integrated methodology using measurements from five coastal and near-coastal sites, four reanalysis datasets, seven Power Law exponent methods, and seven bias-correction techniques. The proposed Day–Hour Lookup-Table Power Law produced lowest average mean absolute error, root mean square error (RMSE) and standard deviation of error of 0.23, 0.35 and 0.33 m/s, respectively, and maintained relative RMSE of 4.31–6.30% during chronological hold-out validation.

abstract: Abstract Mountain regions are experiencing rapid climate change. The SEC brought its first AI-washing enforcement actions in 2024, so regulators and researchers need a reproducible measure of AI disclosure. We provide large-sample evidence on AI disclosure in Form ADV Part 2A brochures and show how the estimate depends on measurement design. title: NAD⁺, Resveratrol, Omega-3 Fatty Acids, Vitamin D and Orthobiologics: A Critical Synthesis of the Human Evidence for a Synergistic Approach to Lifespan Extension, Tissue Repair and Wellness
abstract: Background: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) precursors, resveratrol, marine omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D and autologous orthobiologics are increasingly bundled into commercial longevity and regenerative programmes on the argument that they act on complementary hallmarks of ageing and therefore act synergistically.The argument is mechanistically attractive and, at the level of human outcomes, almost entirely untested.Objective: To assemble the randomised human evidence for each agent, to state precisely what has and has not been demonstrated, and to test the synergy hypothesis agains
journal: Journal of Clinical Practice and Medical Case Report.

title: A review of forest innovation: Technologies and sustainable practices for environmental conservation
abstract: Forests play a crucial role in climate regulation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem service provision, and sustainable socio-economic development. However, increasing deforestation, climate change, habitat fragmentation, and unsustainable resource exploitation continue to threaten forest ecosystems worldwide. title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. abstract: ABSTRACT Skin‐friendly ionogels with multi‐scenario adaptive, high‐fidelity, and self‐healing performances were critical building units in wearable signal transmission devices. Traditional ionogels doped with small‐molecule ionic liquids (SMILAs) into polymers yielding weak interchain forces, poor compatibility, and migration. title: Cross-phase partitioning of sulfur-nitrogen ratios and aerosol mixing-state evolution based on single-particle observations
abstract: Abstract. Understanding sulfur-nitrogen partitioning is essential for predicting secondary aerosol formation and mixing-state evolution, yet the mechanisms governing its cross-phase coupling remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrate single-particle mass spectrometry (SPA-MS) with air-pollutant and meteorological observations from two regional emission-control periods. title: A Control Strategy With Hybrid Compressor Modeling for Electric Vehicle CO 2 Heat Pump Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the significant range attenuation of electric vehicles in cold climates, this study proposes a simulation and optimization framework for a transcritical CO 2 heat pump system. Given the computational inaccuracies of traditional polynomial models in characterizing compressor performance under supercritical conditions, a hybrid compressor sub‐model is developed. title: Beyond production: understanding aquaculture narratives, public engagement, and visibility on TikTok and Instagram
abstract: Public acceptance and societal trust are increasingly recognized as critical challenges for sustainable aquaculture development. While previous research has examined consumer perceptions and social acceptance, limited attention has been given to how aquaculture narratives are constructed, circulated, and gain visibility within contemporary digital media environments. This study examines how thematic patterns, sentiment, audience engagement, and narrative construction shape aquaculture communication on TikTok and Instagram. title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
abstract: The lack of knowledge regarding whether a welding consumable remains suitable for the welding process or has undergone degradation that precludes its further use constitutes a significant challenge. Appropriate control procedures and effective evaluation methods may contribute to addressing this issue. This study presents the results of investigations concerning the applicability of magnetic and thermoelectric methods for such an assessment. title: Wastewater Generation and Environmental Pathways in Libya: An Evidence-Based National Accounting Framework
abstract: Reliable national wastewater accounts are difficult to construct where direct flow measurements, treatment-plant records, and discharge inventories are incomplete. This study develops an evidence-aware accounting framework to estimate domestic wastewater generation and distinguish sewer-connected from non-networked sanitation pathways across Libya’s 22 administrative areas. title: Too little too late? Nationwide carbon trading in China
abstract: China launched a nationwide, rate-based carbon market in 2021. Covering the world’s top C O 2 emitter, compliance depends on the intensity of carbon emissions rather than an absolute cap. We draw on the theoretical literature on rate-based systems to provide the first empirical evidence on an early adopter. Using plant-level data from satellite imagery and machine learning methods, we find that high-efficiency power plants increased electricity generation and C O 2 emissions by approximately 5% relative to low-efficiency plants. title: The furnace of crisis: assessing the European Union’s trajectory toward strategic independence and global actor in the shadow of the Russo-Ukrainian war
abstract: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has removed the assumptions on which the post-Cold War European security order rested and has increased pressure on the European Union to act as a provider of hard security rather than primarily as a regulatory and geo-economic power. This article examines whether that pressure is producing meaningful strategic autonomy and a more consequential global role. It applies a neoclassical realist framework in which systemic pressure is filtered through European Union decision-making rules and through member-state intervening variables: threat perception, strat

title: Silica nanoparticles antagonize while titania nanoparticles synergize silver nanoparticle toxicity in zebrafish
abstract: This study investigated the individual and combined toxicity of silver (AgNPs), titanium dioxide (TiO₂NPs), and silicon dioxide nanoparticles (SiO₂NPs) in zebrafish (Danio rerio), with emphasis on acute/chronic mortality, oxidative stress, bioaccumulation, and histopathology. In vitro stability tests showed that SiO₂NPs reduced AgNP stability more strongly than TiO₂NPs, leading to greater sedimentation and a lower silver concentration in the water. title: Integrated DNA methylation and gene expression analysis identifies CpG biomarkers in breast cancer
abstract: DNA methylation alterations are frequently associated with transcriptional dysregulation and tumor-associated molecular changes in breast cancer; however, CpG-specific methylation patterns linked to aberrant gene expression remain incompletely characterized. In this study, we performed an integrative analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic data from the TCGA breast cancer cohort to identify methylation-associated transcriptional signatures and candidate biomarkers. DNA methylation profiles generated using the Illumina HumanMethylation450K platform were integrated with RNA-se

title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
abstract: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). Instead of using SAR and optical data as independent classifiers, SAMWater transforms their

title: Isolation and characterization of human skin-derived bacteriophages with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against coagulase-negative staphylococci
abstract: Abstract Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus capitis , are significant opportunistic pathogens associated with biofilm-related infections and antimicrobial resistance. Although bacteriophage therapy is a promising alternative to antibiotics, human skin-derived phages targeting clinically important CoNS remain poorly characterized. Four bacteriophages were isolated from facial skin swabs of healthy volunteers, and two (phages Se_20 and Se_42) were selected for detailed characterization. title: Integrating Solid Waste Management into Urban Flood Risk Reduction: A Resilience Framework for Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: This study examines how solid waste management influences urban flood risk in Lagos, Nigeria, and develops an integrated resilience framework connecting waste governance, drainage management, and flood-risk reduction. An integrative evidence synthesis and comparative case-study approach was used to assess peer-reviewed studies, institutional documents, policy materials, and recent reports concerning waste disposal, drainage obstruction, flood exposure, and government and community responses. Quantitative evidence was compared descriptively, while qualitative findings were synthesized thematica
journal: International Journal of Scientific Engineering and Research

title: Multi-omics of host–gut metabolic crosstalk in Parkinson’s disease
abstract: An altered gut microbiome has been implicated in Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet its reciprocal effects on systemic metabolism remain unclear. This cross-sectional study included 67 PD patients and 64 non-PD controls and integrated untargeted serum and fecal metabolomics using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry with 16S rRNA gene sequencing of the gut microbiome. title: Measuring destination image dissonance: A compositional data analysis of cross-media representations in Sanya’s Tourism
abstract: This study examines Sanya's tourism image disparities across cognitive, spatial, and affective dimensions in Press Generated Content (PGC), Tourist Generated Content (TGC), and Official Generated Content (OGC) (2013-2022), comparing pre-pandemic (2013-2019) and COVID-19 (2020-2022) periods. Results show: cognitive consistency in "tourism/hotels" but TGC focusing on "coastal + food" vs. PGC/OGC emphasizing policy elements; spatial misalignment between policy-driven spaces and tourists' preferred spaces, revealing a systematic dissonance between institutional promotion and on-the-ground practice
institutions: Capital University of Physical Education and Sports

title: Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery for Digital Twinning of Boreal Forests
abstract: Digital twins of the Earth require Earth observation data streams that are both spatially continuous and informative about the state of the modelled system. For forests, the standard optical data source is Sentinel-2, whose 10 m multispectral imagery trades spectral detail for spatial resolution; the forthcoming operational imaging spectroscopy missions CHIME and SBG will offer the opposite trade-off with 30-m pixels and hundreds of spectral bands. title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
abstract: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accurate base temperature data limits their performance. In particular, the scarcity of high temporal resolution building energy demand data constrains regional-scale base temperature estimation through conventional methods such as the energy signature method and the performance line method. title: Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina (Sicily, Italy)
abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances. title: From Craft to Sustainable Enterprise: How Entrepreneurial Capabilities and Design–Execution Integration Drive Product Quality and Sustainable Performance in Indian Furniture Handicraft Ventures
abstract: Purpose: Handicraft furniture ventures in India are typically owner-managed micro and small enterprises that must modernise their quality systems while remaining economically, socially and environmentally viable. This study examines how entrepreneurial and strategic capabilities shape design–execution integration, product quality and sustainable entrepreneurial performance. Design/methodology/approach: An integrated resource-based view, dynamic capability, socio-technical systems and total quality management framework was tested using survey data from 384 entrepreneurs in five Indian furniture

title: Interdecadal Phase Shifts of Winter Asian‐Pacific Oscillation Modulate the Warm Arctic‐Cold Eurasia Pattern
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global warming, warm Arctic‐cold Eurasia (WACE) has garnered extensive scientific attention. However, the drivers of its interdecadal variability remain insufficiently understood. Using reanalysis data and pre‐industrial control simulations, we demonstrate that winter Asian‐Pacific Oscillation (APO), a dominant upper‐tropospheric atmospheric mode over the Asian‐North Pacific sector, modulates the WACE variability at the interdecadal timescale. title: Every Public Servant Was Once a student: Reimagining Education for Ethical Leadership, Public Service and Good Governance in Fiji and the Pacific
abstract: Not every student will become a public servant, but every public servant was once a student. This simple proposition raises a significant but insufficiently examined question about the wider purpose of education: to what extent does education contribute to forming the values, ethical judgement, critical consciousness and sense of public responsibility of those who later serve within public institutions? title: Multidirectional acoustic wave transmission via artificial periodic structures
abstract: This paper presents a unified artificial periodic structure for multidirectional acoustic wave transmission along complex pathways. The structure employs a two-dimensional, three-component unit cell—consisting of a lead core, rubber cladding, and epoxy matrix—whose resonant dynamics are captured by a double-spring model extended with nonlocal inter-cell coupling corrections. title: Predicting Fishermen's Income Based on Weather Factors and Fishing Location Using the Neuro-Fuzzy Algorithm
abstract: Fishermen's income fluctuates due to weather conditions, fishing location, and vessel characteristics. These conditions necessitate a method capable of predicting income based on various factors that have complex relationships. This study aims to predict fishermen's income using the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) algorithm. The study uses an applied quantitative approach with computational and experimental methods. title: Identification of Novel PFAS Transformation Products in AFFF-Impacted Surface and Groundwater
abstract: Abstract The widespread use of Aqueous Film-Forming Foams (AFFF) has left thousands of contaminated “hotspots” across North America. In Canada, only 25 per-/polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are regulated in drinking water at 30 ng/L. title: Feature-engineered physics-conditioned DNN with validation-selected ridge residual correction for pore water pressure prediction in clays
abstract: Introduction Accurately predicting pore water pressure is important for evaluating effective stress, deformation, and stability in clayey soils. Methods This study develops an interpretable feature-engineered physics-conditioned DNN with validation-selected ridge residual correction using 42 complete curves from kaolin clay and Mercia Mudstone clay. Complete curves were divided into training, validation, and testing subsets. title: 6PPD-quinone exposure impairs erectile function through dysregulation of the HIF-1α/eNOS/NO axis: multi-omics and in vivo evidence
abstract: Background 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire antioxidant 6PPD, has emerged as an environmental contaminant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in erectile dysfunction (ED) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and animal experiments to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to ED. title: Shifting mosquito vector ecologies pose new risks for new stakeholders
abstract: Mosquito-borne infectious disease is a major cause of mortality and a significant economic burden worldwide. Variable regional and seasonal patterns make proactive intervention challenging. Here we introduce a machine learning approach trained on satellite and mosquito observational data, improving generalizability to sparse observations while retaining similar positive performance characteristics of models used in standard practice. title: A performance-based multivariable weighting framework for WRF parameterization-scheme selection
abstract: Abstract. The selection of optimal physical parameterization schemes is a major source of uncertainty in WRF model simulations. A comprehensive evaluation of model performance requires simultaneous consideration of multiple output variables. However, existing multivariate approaches often rely on subjective or overly simplistic equal-weighting strategies and lack an objective mechanism to quantify variable importance. title: Development of an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book using tourism posters for junior high school students
abstract: Background- Poetry writing is an important productive literacy skill in the Merdeka Curriculum, yet instruction remains predominantly theoretical. Students may experience difficulties in idea generation, diction, and imagination due to limited contextual and visual support. Objectives- This study aimed to (1) identify instructional needs; (2) develop an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book integrating illustrated data cards and marine tourism posters; and (3) evaluate its effectiveness. abstract: Communities, governments, and agriculture worldwide are increasingly turning to managed aquifer recharge (MAR) as an important element of their water resources planning.A wide range of MAR approaches capture available water during wet periods, times of low demand, or water that would otherwise be lost, and move this water underground for later recovery or other benefits.MAR can address a diversity of issues, including water shortages, emergency supply, groundwater depletion, land subsidence, seawater intrusion, water-quality degradation, streamflow depletion, and endangered groundwater-depende

title: Traffic Congestion and Vehicle Emissions in a Historic Andean City: A Mesoscopic Simulation for Sustainable Urban Mobility
abstract: Traffic-related air pollution constitutes one of the primary threats to public health and environmental sustainability in urban centers worldwide.Historic centers face particular challenges because their narrow streets, irregular urban configuration, and high vehicle concentration during peak hours hinder the implementation of conventional environmental monitoring systems.This research assessed the pollutant emissions generated by vehicular traffic in the historic center of Ayacucho, Peru, an Andean city located at 2,761 meters above sea level with approximately 29,476 inhabitants in the study

title: Core–Shell Molecularly Imprinted Polymer@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 for Low‐Cost and Selective Electrochemical Sensing of Paraquat
abstract: The widespread use of the water‐soluble paraquat (PQ) herbicide has found to be linked with numerous toxic outcomes to humans as well as aquatic animals, while the on‐site and rapid measurement is still challenging due to unsuitability and lack of selectivity of the existing techniques. This study presents a selective, sensitive, and low‐cost electrochemical sensor for detecting residual PQ in water by combining a core–shell molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 material with a portable screen‐printed carbon electrode (SPCE). title: Quantification of wave–current interactions in a tide-dominated harbour: A fully coupled modelling study of Darwin Harbour, Australia
abstract: The present work investigates the effects of wave-current interactions in a tidally dominant harbour, using Darwin Harbour in Australia as a case study. Numerical experiments were performed using a two-way coupled FVCOM modelling system across five distinct configurations: a hydrodynamic model, a fully coupled wave-current interaction model, a wave model, a fully coupled model excluding wind forcing, and a fully coupled model without swell input. title: Automated fledgling call detection links adult songbird abundance to reproductive success in restored habitat
abstract: Many wildlife monitoring programs assume that adult abundance reflects habitat quality and, by extension, reproductive success, despite the possibility of these parameters decoupling. Abundance may be more likely to decouple with reproduction in human-modified landscapes such as those created through habitat restoration. However, the extent to which this occurs remains unclear due to extensive manual effort required for monitoring reproduction, especially at scale. Passive-acoustic monitoring (PAM) has recently shown promise for detecting fledgling begging calls to infer reproductive success.

title: Biofilm-host immunometabolic crosstalk in Staphylococcus aureus orthopedic implant infection: mechanisms and translational constraints
abstract: Orthopedic implant biofilms are not only antibiotic-tolerant bacterial communities but metabolically active niches that reshape host immunity. Compared with planktonic infection, mature biofilms impose spatial and metabolic constraints that can uncouple leukocyte recruitment from sterilizing activity. Neutrophils can penetrate and phagocytose portions of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, but clearance becomes incomplete as biofilms mature and may coexist with degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap-associated tissue injury. title: Industrial Paradigm of Multidimensional Poverty in Karawang Regency (Determinant Analysis and Policy Implementation)
abstract: Karawang Regency is known as one of the largest processing industry centers in West Java, with the sector's contribution of around 71 percent to GDP on a Constant Price Basis in 2024. However, the dominance of the industrial economy has not been followed by an inclusive poverty reduction: the number of absolute poor people will increase by March 2024, the open unemployment rate remains above the West Java average, and the inequality of expenditure between the poor is widening. Previous studies of the determinants of poverty have generally addressed economic, population, or environmental factor
journal: Journal of Law Politic and Humanities

title: Influencing factors and genetic model of low-resistivity shales: a case study of the Longmaxi Formation, Southern Sichuan Basin, China
abstract: Low-resistivity anomalies are widely developed in the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation marine shales of the Sichuan Basin, but their complex conductive mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering accurate reservoir evaluation. This study investigates the characteristics and formation mechanisms of low-resistivity shales in southern Sichuan Basin by integrating well logging resistivity, geochemical analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), carbon dioxide and nitrogen adsorption (CO 2 /N 2 ad

title: Optimization of waste glass, slag, and seashell usage in lime-based hybrid dsm grouts: an experimental and statistical approach
abstract: This study investigates the improvement of a low-plasticity silty soil (ML) sourced from the Gölveren region of Kastamonu province, Türkiye, using lime-based hybrid binders partially replaced with glass powder (GP), blast furnace slag (BFS), and seashell powder (SSP) within the Deep Soil Mixing (DSM) framework. The experimental program was designed using the Taguchi L18 orthogonal array method to determine the effect of control parameters and optimum mixture ratios. title: Global trends and emerging themes in GIS education: A literature review with a case study of Uzbekistan
abstract: This paper provides an overview of global GIS education and evaluates geospatial education in Uzbekistan on a regional level. An integrated approach based on combining bibliometric analysis and thematic interpretation was used to explore 325 articles listed in Scopus and Web of Science databases between 2016 and 2025. Bibliometric science mapping, thematic analysis, K-means clustering and case study evaluation were used as the methodology in order to analyze the development trends in GIS education. title: An adaptive behavioural zero-trust security framework with proactive cryptographic caching for continuous authentication in 5G non-terrestrial networks
abstract: Abstract 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are key to future global broadband and military communications, but their high latency and dynamic topologies require security approaches beyond perimeter defences and static authentication. To overcome these vulnerabilities, we propose an adaptive behavioural zero trust security framework (BZTSF) for continuous 5G NTN authentication. Our method continuously evaluates node trustworthiness using network signal information processed by an isolation forest machine learning algorithm. title: Mapping Fuel Categories in Mediterranean Regions with Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope Satellite Acquisitions
abstract: Accurate and spatially explicit mapping of forest fuel types is essential for developing integrated wildfire risk management strategies, estimating fire danger, and modeling fire propagation in fire-prone Mediterranean ecosystems. While time series of Copernicus Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery at 10 m spatial resolution have proven effective for regional fuel mapping, severe spectral and spatial ambiguities persist in distinguishing complex canopy structures, heterogeneous shrublands, and pastures. title: Integrated air quality assessment using monitoring data, emission inventory, and aermod dispersion modeling: a case study of Sohar Port and Freezone, Oman
abstract: Industrial and port areas require integrated air quality assessment methods combining monitoring observations, meteorological conditions and atmospheric dispersion modeling. In this study, we have investigated the pollution behavior and industrial source contributions in the Sohar Port and Freezone industrial area of Oman for a multi-year period of ambient air quality monitoring data and meteorological observations and AERMOD dispersion modeling results for PM 10 , NO 2 , SO 2 and CO. title: Water-rich sub-Neptunes and rocky super-Earths around different stars: Radii shaped by volatile partitioning, formation, and evolution
abstract: Despite precise characterization measurements, the nature of planets with radii between 2 and 4 Earth radii -- sub-Neptunes -- remains unknown due to degeneracies in interior models. Nevertheless, the field has compiled an impressive ensemble of small planets with measured masses and radii orbiting different stars. This dataset can be used to test the prediction of large water reservoirs on sub-Neptunes, as proposed by planet formation theory with orbital migration. title: Compact target-aware stability-based feature selection for cross-dataset wearable activity monitoring
abstract: Wearable activity-recognition models may lose reliability when transferred across participants, sensor placements, sampling rates, acquisition protocols, and activity definitions. This study evaluates a compact unsupervised target-aware feature-selection strategy for cross-dataset wearable activity monitoring under a pre-specified MHEALTH→PAMAP2 transfer protocol. title: Enabling climate action: A nexus approach for delivering co-benefits across biodiversity, water, food, and health
abstract: Climate response options rarely affect biodiversity, water, food, and health in uniform ways. This comparative analysis examines why technically viable response options generate uneven cross-nexus outcomes, and how governance and justice conditions shape whether these outcomes become durable co-benefits. Anchored in the IPBES Nexus Assessment, the analysis synthesizes evidence from fifteen response options spanning land, ocean, energy, urban, industrial, and societal transitions. title: The Struggle for Dominance in the Central Harşit Valley in the XIIIth-XVth Centuries
abstract: The Seljuks arrived in Anatolia long before establishing an official state, during Chaghri (Çağrı) Beg’s western expedition in 1018. After the establisment of the Seljuk State in 1040, the Kelkit Basin, which constitutes the eastern section of the Northern Anatolian route, emerged as one of the primary regions of initial activity during the era of Anatolian conquests. title: Insights into energy consumption and carbon emissions from freight industry in China
abstract: Against China’s commitments to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, the freight industry, a major energy consumer and emitter, demands attention. This study estimated the energy consumption and carbon emissions from the freight industry in China based on the data of 2022–2024 official turnover, energy source types and IPCC “top-down” CO 2 emission factors. abstract: The increasing demand for lactose-free dairy products, sustainable whey valorization and high-value prebiotic ingredients has intensified the need for efficient bacterial β -galactosidases capable of both lactose hydrolysis and galacto-oligosaccharide (GOS) synthesis. title: A scalable low-supervision framework for longterm land cover mapping: Automated training sample generation and independent validation
abstract: Reliable long-term land cover information is essential for environmental monitoring, yet many regions still lack dedicated datasets. Main obstacles are assembling training labels at national scale without extensive manual annotation and obtaining reference data sufficiently independent of the mapping process to support credible accuracy assessment. Here, we present a scalable, low-supervision framework for national land cover mapping addressing both limitations. Training samples are progressively identified through harmonized multi-source datasets agreement, spectral plausibility, and temporal
institutions: Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University

title: Rhein-induced free fatty acid generation cooperates with silver ions for biofilm-infected diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic foot infection (DFI) significantly increases the risks of hospitalization and amputation, with biofilm infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) being key drivers of treatment failure. Here, we analyzed MRSA/CREC biofilm-infected ulcer tissues from patients using proteomics and metabolomics. title: Bioinformatics-Driven Environmental DNA Metabarcoding and Conservation Genomics for Non-Invasive Wildlife Biodiversity Monitoring under Climate Change
abstract: Global biodiversity is declining rapidly as anthropogenic climate change interacts with habitat loss, disease emergence and overexploitation to reshape species distributions and population viability. Conventional survey methods, including live trapping, visual census and invasive tissue sampling, are frequently slow, costly and disturbing to the organisms under study, so they cannot keep pace with the scale at which ecosystems are now changing. journal: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development

title: Quantum eddy current wall thickness tomography using nitrogen-vacancy vector magnetometry for onshore crude oil pipeline integrity assessment
abstract: As core infrastructure for global energy distribution, onshore long-distance crude oil pipelines face multiple challenges, including wax deposition, structural stress concentration, and H 2 S release. Traditional non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques, such as eddy current testing and magnetic flux leakage (MFL), suffer from limitations including low spatial resolution, limited penetration depth, and directional blind spots, making high-resolution and omnidirectional defect identification difficult. title: Amine-terminated zirconium metal-organic framework as an efficient adsorbent for lanthanum removal
abstract: The current study developed an amine-terminated zirconium metal-organic framework (UiO-66-NH2) to effectively adsorb lanthanum (La3+) from water. The UiO-66-NH2 was confirmed by various analytical techniques. The optimization of La3+ removal was achieved through response surface methodology. For the adsorption of La3+, the best conditions were determined to be 10 mg of adsorbent, pH 9, and 150 min of contact time. title: Efficient zinc ion biosorption on the biomass of Ericaria selaginoides algae following response surface methodology optimization: uptake behaviors and mechanisms
abstract: Background Biosorption using marine algae biosorbents is a sustainable and effective method for removing of heavy metals from aquatic environments. Methods This study explored the biosorption of zinc ions from aqueous solutions using the biomass of the brown alga Ericaria selaginoides . The impacts of biosorbent dose, pH, and biosorbate concentration were optimized using the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and 3-D surface plots generated via Design-Expert software. title: Physics-informed parameter identification of fractional-order battery models using Nyquist-based initialization and two-stage metaheuristic refinement
abstract: Accurate parameter identification (PI) of fractional-order models (FOMs) from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data is essential for battery state estimation but is challenged by nonlinearity, parameter coupling, and local optima. This study compares ten metaheuristic (MH) algorithms for FOM PI, identifying the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) as the most robust, with a mean RMSE of 1.09×10⁻⁴ and the lowest standard deviation (1.0×10⁻⁵) over 20 trials. title: Energy Production and Economic Feasibility of a Tidal Barrage System in the Gulf of Khambhat
abstract: Rising need for clean and reliable energy has raised tidal power system interest. The large tidal range in the Gulf of Khambhat has good potential for the extraction of tidal energy. To assess the feasibility of a proposed tidal barrage using harmonic tidal reconstruction and dynamic basin modelling techniques for the purposes of estimating the hydraulic head, turbine discharges and the power production. title: Four Quality-Control Failure Modes in Public Wireline-Log Archives: Measured Effects and a Reproducible Workflow, With Examples From Wyoming and Kansas
abstract: Public wireline-log archives are widely reused in petrophysical and machine-learning studies, yet the processing steps required to make them analytically usable are rarely reported. We processed 1,210 logs from the Teapot Dome archive in Wyoming, together with a 300-well pilot drawn from 29,089 Kansas Geological Survey records, and found four processing failures, each of which produced an error larger than the signal it was supposed to resolve. title: Limits of questionnaire-based prediction of oral health-related quality of life in non-smokers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) reflects the perceived impact of oral health on daily functioning, psychosocial well-being, and social interaction. While clinical symptoms strongly influence OHRQoL, it is unclear how well OHRQoL can be estimated using only non-clinical information, particularly in non-smoking populations. This study evaluated whether sociodemographic, behavioral, and self-perceived health variables can predict OHRQoL in non-smokers. METHODS: This cross-sectional study recruited 130 adults. institutions: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland - Bahrain

title: No critical slowing down in the Atlantic Overturning Circulation in historical CMIP6 simulations
abstract: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a key component of the Earth’s climate system, and is theorized to have multiple stable states. Critical slowing down (CSD) can detect stability changes in Earth system components, and has been found in sea-surface temperature (SST) based fingerprints of the AMOC. We look for CSD in simulations from 27 models from the sixth Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6). institutions: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research

title: Catastrophe theory and AHP modelling of landslide susceptibility using multi-source geodata in southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous and structurally complex terrains, posing significant threats to lives, infrastructure, and sustainable development. Accurate Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (LSM) is therefore essential for hazard mitigation and land-use planning. This study develops a Catastrophe Theory (CT)-based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Index (LSMI) that integrates surface and subsurface conditioning factors derived from geological, geomorphological, geophysical, and climatic datasets. title: Estimating Twomey forcing sensitivity to aerosol plume spreading rates
abstract: Abstract. The amount of sunlight that reaches Earth's surface can be reduced by increasing cloud droplet number and decreasing droplet size (i.e., Twomey forcing), a central idea underpinning the Marine Cloud Brightening strategy. Cloud albedo depends nonlinearly on cloud droplet concentration, meaning the spatial extent of aerosol plumes could be an important constraint on the brightening potential. title: ACANTHUS ILICIFOLIUS L: ETHNOBOTANY, PHYTOCHEMISTRY, PHARMACOLOGYAND SYNTHESIS OF SILVER NANOPARTICLES (AGNPS)
abstract: Acanthus ilicifoliusbelongs to the family Acanthaceaeis a medicinal plant widely distributed in the coastal areas of tropical and subtropical regions. It has been traditionally used in various systems of folk medicine for managing conditions such as wounds, fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems. Phytochemical investigations have revealed the presence of several biologically active constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic compounds, and terpenoids. These constituents are associated with a range of biological effects, particularly antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immuno
journal: Magna Scientia Advanced Biology and Pharmacy

title: One health perspectives on pharmaceutical and clinical effluents driving multidrug resistance in aquatic ecosystems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the most pressing global health challenges, yet the contribution of environmental reservoirs to the spread of multidrug resistance (MDR) remains insufficiently integrated into mainstream discussions. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 167 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 to examine how pharmaceutical manufacturing effluents and clinical waste drive the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and multidrug-resistant bacteria in aquatic ecosystems. institutions: Swedish National Board of Forensic Medicine

title: Separating Environmental Modulation From Source Intermittency in Methane Leakage From a Legacy Well in British Columbia
abstract: Abstract Legacy oil and gas wells are an incompletely quantified source of greenhouse gas emissions and offer leakage pathways for subsurface gas migration if inadequately isolated. We present a high‐resolution, process‐based characterization of leakage dynamics at an integrity‐compromised legacy gas well in northeastern British Columbia using five spatial flux surveys and approximately 70 hr of continuous hotspot measurements of methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), integrated with co‐located soil and meteorological observations.
