title: Intensifying compound drought–heatwave events weaken ecosystem water-use efficiency in the Nile River Basin
abstract: Climate warming has intensified compound drought-heatwave (CDHW) events worldwide, posing growing threats to ecosystem carbon-water dynamics. However, the impacts of CDHWs on ecosystem water-use efficiency (WUE), particularly event sequencing, drought memory, and climatic heterogeneity, remain poorly understood at large river-basin scales. institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research
Florida A&M University - Florida State University College of Engineering

title: Probabilistic Digital Twin Framework for Climate-Resilient Offshore Infrastructure under Coupled Corrosion–Fatigue Degradation and Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment. Deterministic integrity assessment cannot represent that feedback or the environmental variability that drives it. institutions: Islamic Azad University, Science and Research Branch

title: Geospatial suitability of cacao in Amazonas (Peru): An ensemble predictive modeling approach (BIOMOD2) integrating multisource data, territorial management, and plant health
abstract: Identifying climatically suitable areas for cacao cultivation (Theobroma cacao L.) is essential to guide sustainable intensification, territorial planning, and compliance with emerging environmental standards in tropical regions. This study assessed the current climatic suitability of cacao in the Amazonas department (northwestern Peru) using an ensemble modeling approach implemented in biomod2, integrating bioclimatic, topographic, and edaphic predictors with spatial biophysical exclusion criteria, legal conservation constraints, regulatory eligibility associated with the European Union Defor
institutions: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza

title: Predicting environmental health-related search patterns using freely available digital and reanalysis data: A critical evaluation of Google Trends and global datasets for Morocco
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten urban public health, yet monitoring infrastructure is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning framework that predicts environmental health-related search behavior , used as a low-cost digital proxy rather than a measure of clinical burden, in Morocco using exclusively open-access global datasets. title: Stable core rhizosphere microbiota across the entire wheat growth cycle mitigates cadmium accumulation via reducing rhizosphere cadmium Bioavailiability
abstract: Reducing crop cadmium (Cd) uptake via beneficial rhizosphere microbes offers a low-cost, sustainable strategy for ensuring agricultural product safety. Most prior investigations have largely focused on mechanisms examined at single time points or individual functional strains, leaving the stable core microbial taxa that persist throughout the plant growth cycle and the synergistic potential of multi-strain consortia in alleviating Cd stress largely underexplored. title: Mental Health, Safety, and Professional Preparedness: The Role of Pre-Boarding Training for Seafarers
abstract: This study examined the role of pre-boarding training in enhancing the mental health preparedness, safety awareness, and professional preparedness of Filipino seafarers who entered maritime service after March 2020. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed involving 390 purposively selected seafarers who had completed at least one sea contract and participated in a manning agency pre-boarding training program. title: How does energy transition in China amidst climate risk shocks influence residents’ welfare?
abstract: China regards energy transition as a significant measure to handle global climate change and foster the harmonious coexistence of human beings and nature. This article matches the urban energy transition index with China Family Panel Studies data to systematically examine and evaluate the impact of energy transition on residents’ happiness. The baseline results indicate that energy transition has improved residents’ happiness. Mechanism analysis found that energy transition did not significantly change residents’ inherent energy consumption habits, while reducing their perception of wealth gap
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Efficient Harmonic Generation Toward High Power Femtosecond Blue‐Green Laser From a Thulium‐Doped Fiber Amplifier
abstract: ABSTRACT Blue‐green ultrafast lasers offer great potential for oceanic optical communication, laser fabrication, and scientific research. title: A parametric Morison-inspired model for wave-induced torque fluctuations on a vertical axis tidal turbine
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of surface waves on the hydrodynamic torque fluctuations of vertical axis tidal turbines. Wave-induced orbital velocities and accelerations are shown to generate periodic variations of the incoming flow, leading to significant unsteady torque loads. A reduced-order torque model inspired by Morison-type formulations is here developed to study wave-induced effects on vertical axis tidal turbines. title: Strategic implications of China-India geo-economic competition for Pakistan (2015-2025)
abstract: The increasing geo-economic competition between China and India has significantly reshaped South Asia’s strategic landscape, positioning Pakistan at the center of an evolving regional power contest. This study analyses the fundamental drivers of Sino-Indian geo-economic competition and its strategic ramifications for Pakistan’s economic development, security posture, and foreign policy orientation. title: Manganese-modified biochar enhances white-rot fungi-mediated lignocellulose humification: insights from molecular transformation and multi-omics analyses
abstract: Humic substance formation is essential for soil health, yet natural humification is slow, and synthetic production is often inefficient. White-rot fungi (WRF)-mediated lignocellulose humification shows potential but is limited by slow substrate degradation. Given the high biocatalytic potential of Mn(II) and its compatibility with the enzyme system of WRF, manganese-modified biochar (MBC) was utilized to enhance the degradation and conversion efficiency of lignocellulose. title: Tampa Bay observing network: a continuous data acquisition system in support of science and environmental management
abstract: The Tampa Bay estuary is a vital ecological and economic hub, whose productive, shallow-water habitats are highly vulnerable to both chronic anthropogenic stress and acute environmental disturbance events (e.g., extreme weather, human incidents). Historically, the bay's health was monitored primarily through low-frequency, monthly field sampling that has provided a foundational baseline of water quality for the last fifty years. title: Implementation Of International Maritime Organization Standards In Seaworthiness Supervision Of Indonesian-Flagged Vessels At The Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of implementing International Maritime Organization (IMO) standards in supervising the seaworthiness of Indonesian-flagged vessels at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office (KSOP), identify the inhibiting factors, and analyze the efforts undertaken by KSOP to ensure compliance with seaworthiness requirements. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office. title: ¿ Esto lo has hecho tú? Los retos de la IA en la práctica educativa: Did you do this? The challenges of AI in educational practice
abstract: Este artículo analiza los retos ético-pedagógicos de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la práctica educativa, a partir de una experiencia docente en Lengua y Filosofía con alumnado adolescente nativo digital. El texto sostiene que la integración de la IA es irreversible en la vida escolar, pero su uso indiscriminado está alterando la confianza educativa, la identidad del estudiante y el desarrollo del criterio. title: Land suitability analysis for taro (Colocasia esculenta) cultivation based on topo-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system
abstract: Taro ( Colocasia esculenta ), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species (NUCS), is regarded as a climate-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries. title: Beyond Vulnerability: Women’s Water Stewardship and Adaptive Agency in Climate-Vulnerable Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract In Bangladesh, the climate crisis manifests through acute water scarcity, which profoundly disrupts social reproduction, particularly for women. Using a Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) lens, this study explores women’s adaptive agency in daily water management practices at both household and community levels. The study was conducted in three climate-vulnerable regions of Bangladesh: Mongla (cyclone-prone coastal Bagerhat), Naogaon (drought-prone), and Cox’s Bazar (flash flood- and landslide-prone). title: Time capsules of infection: Updating the distribution of Aphanomyces astaci in Croatia using archived crayfish specimens
abstract: The crayfish plague pathogen Aphanomyces astaci Schikora, 1906 is one of the most damaging invasive pathogens affecting European freshwater ecosystems, causing declines in native crayfish populations. In Croatia, crayfish plague was first reported in the late 19 th century and was subsequently molecularly confirmed in 2016. However, its national distribution remains incompletely resolved because the initial molecular survey covered only a limited number of localities. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Can the U.S. Endangered Species Act protect biodiversity from climate change effects? Post-Weyerhaeuser unoccupied critical habitat designations
abstract: Unoccupied critical habitat designation is often highlighted as a beneficial U.S. Endangered Species Act provision for conserving biodiversity in the face of climate change. However, the effectiveness of this legal mechanism may be at risk due to the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2018 ruling in Weyerhaeuser Co. v. the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and resulting shifts in federal rules regulating unoccupied critical habitat designations. title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. title: Optimizing Logistics Ecosystems: Evaluating the Performance of Smart Port Enterprises
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the performance of smart ports remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for evaluating and improving smart port efficiency using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. title: Detection of old-growth forests using airborne laser scanning and other auxiliary data combined with National Forest Inventory field plot data
abstract: Accurate detection and mapping of old-growth forests (OGFs) are essential for biodiversity conservation and forest management, yet remain challenging due to their structural complexity, rarity and varying definitions. In this study, we developed a framework for classifying OGFs in boreal forests by integrating airborne laser scanning (ALS) data, and multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery and aerial imagery with different modelling approaches. title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug–food homologous substance target prediction
abstract: Introduction High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug–food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown. Methods Datasets related to HA illness, as well as 106 DFH substances and their corresponding chemical components, were obtained in this study. title: Second funding phase proposal: NFDI4Microbiota – National Research Data Infrastructure for Microbiota Research
abstract: Modern microbiological research generates vast quantities of data, particularly from high-throughput "omics" technologies. These datasets promise unprecedented insights into microbial diversity, function, and interactions, yet they are often deposited in unstructured formats with inadequate metadata, significantly hampering their discoverability, interoperability, and long-term reusability. Adding to this challenge is a long tail of subdomain-specific data types that typically lack a consistent structure. title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
abstract: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. title: Passive acoustic monitoring for the estimation of density of the singing lemur ( Indri indri )
abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a valuable tool for estimating animal density and abundance, particularly in challenging environments where traditional methods face limitations. In this study, we applied PAM techniques to study the indri ( Indri indri ) in the Maromizaha New Protected Area, a tropical forest in Eastern Madagascar. Leveraging advancements in acoustic monitoring methodologies, we aimed to assess the efficacy of PAM in estimating indri density and its implications for conservation efforts. title: GIS-based assessment of population and dwelling exposure to landslide-prone areas in the Valencian Community (Spain)
abstract: The spatial identification of population exposure to landslide-prone areas is essential for risk-informed territorial planning, particularly where impacts affect peri-urban and dispersed residential areas rather than consolidated urban centres. This study presents a GIS-based, multi-scale methodology to quantify and locate population and dwelling exposure beyond administrative boundaries by integrating landslide susceptibility mapping, residential cadastral data, and high-resolution population information from the 2021 census grid. title: Institutional fragmentation and rule-of-law coordination in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: a maritime soft power perspective
abstract: Introduction International assessments of maritime cities have shifted from hard infrastructure indicators toward institutional quality metrics such as maritime finance and law and attractiveness and competitiveness. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), with its distinctive “one country, two systems, and three jurisdictions” configuration, faces gaps in cross-jurisdictional rule connectivity that may limit its maritime soft power—a challenge that existing single-jurisdiction assessment frameworks do not fully capture, highlighting the need for rule-of-law coordination. title: The Impact of Virtual Dental Clinic Color and Image Modifications on Anxiety Reduction in Undergraduate Dental Students
abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. Therefore,this study investigated how color and visual imagery in dental clinics affect anxiety levels in dental students.Participants were dental students experiencing state anxiety. title: Bebas-Aktif and Pragmatic Assertiveness: Continuity and Change in Indonesia’s Foreign Policy under Prabowo Subianto
abstract: This article examines whether Indonesian foreign policy under President Prabowo Subianto (October 2024–August 2026) represents a doctrinal departure from bebas-aktif or a programmatic reconfiguration of strategic autonomy. It develops the Doctrinal Continuity–Instrumental Reconfiguration (DCIR) model, integrating foreign-policy-change theory, role theory, leader-centered Foreign Policy Analysis, and hedging. title: From the Indo-Pacific to Mexico: establishment of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775) (Acanthuriformes, Ephippidae), in the Tropical Eastern Pacific
abstract: We report 100 individuals of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775), from the Mexican Pacific. Records include first reports from the Revillagigedo Islands and Michoacán, as well as additional sightings from Baja California Sur, Jalisco, Colima, Guerrero, and Oaxaca. Individuals included juveniles, subadults, and adults documented through diving, snorkeling, and one incidental fishery capture. title: Predicting severe high-altitude de-acclimatization syndrome from pre-return exposure dose and laboratory indicators: a prospective cohort study of 475 males
abstract: Abstract High-altitude de-acclimatization syndrome (HADAs) poses significant health challenges to individuals returning from high-altitude residence, yet its de-acclimatization process of laboratory indicators and the extent to which it can be predicted before descent remain poorly characterized. We conducted a longitudinal cohort study involving 475 participants with repeated assessments at high-altitude residence (T0), 1 month after return to plain area (T1), and 3 months after return to plain area (T2). title: Mobilizing Dynamic‐Capability Microfoundations for Sustainability‐Oriented Innovation: The Role of Innovation Champions
abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. title: Improved RT-DETR-based detection and counting of shrimp in EK80 acoustic echogram images
abstract: Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object-detection models. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT-DETR. title: Hymenoptera of Galápagos: diversity and distribution of one of the most species-rich insect orders in the archipelago
abstract: Despite the importance of the Galápagos archipelago as a key site for the study of biodiversity and evolution, significant components of its invertebrate biodiversity, particularly Hymenoptera, remain insufficiently documented. Occurrence records of Hymenoptera from 1959–2025 were combined from structured surveys of non-formicid Hymenoptera, long-term ant sampling, museum collections, literature, and online sources to assess the richness, distribution, and species composition of hymenopterans across the archipelago. title: The 2 May 2025 Mw 7.4 Drake Passage Earthquake: Insights Into Tectonics at the Shackleton Fracture Zone–Chilean Trench Transition
abstract: Abstract On 2 May 2025, an Mw 7.4 earthquake occurred ∼120 km off the southern tip of Tierra del Fuego, at the transition of the Shackleton Fracture Zone and the Chile Trench. This event exhibits reverse‐faulting mechanisms with relatively steeply dipping planes and is the largest recorded along this complex plate boundary. Most aftershocks have similar mechanisms, although some show strike‐slip and normal faulting. title: SIMULATION-DRIVEN METHOD FOR WATER COVERAGE MONITORING FROM MULTI-SENSOR SATELLITE IMAGERY
abstract: Monitoring water coverage in intertidal zones is challenging due to the lack of satellite sensors that simultaneously provide both high spatial and high temporal resolution. Landsat offers detailed spatial information but is limited by its 16-day revisit cycle, whereas Himawari-8 provides frequent observations but at coarse spatial scales. Existing multi-sensor fusion approaches, such as STARFM and ESTARFM, attempt to bridge this gap but rely on the assumption of linear or abrupt land cover changes, which is inadequate for capturing the gradual and non-linear dynamics of tidal environments. title: Impact of Radio Wave Refractivity on Mobile Network Portability Threshold in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the influence of radio wave refractivity on mobile network portability thresholds in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, focusing on the effects of radio refractivity (W-unit), atmospheric temperature (K), relative humidity (%), and atmospheric pressure (hPa) on mobile network signal strength. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining field measurements and statistical analysis to assess the Quality of Service (QoS) of GSM network providers in Biogbolo and Etegwe, Yenagoa. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Colorimetría y atmósfera como constructores de percepción emocional audiovisual: una revisión sistemática.
abstract: El cine y los contenidos audiovisuales están cambiando gracias a la evolución del color y las tecnologías visuales. Actualmente, aspectos como la colorimetría, la gradación y la composición influyen de forma directa en las emociones del público. A través de una revisión sistemática basada en el método PRISMA, esta investigación examina cómo los estudios recientes aprovechan la narrativa visual, la fotografía y la teoría del color para explicar estas reacciones. title: Youth and the future of labor- and knowledge-intensive small-scale farming in West Africa under climate change and political instability
abstract: Debates on the future of smallholder farming in sub-Saharan Africa often interpret rural youth mobility and non-farm work as withdrawal from agriculture. This article examines how rural youth in coastal Guinea-Bissau engage with labour- and knowledge-intensive, climate-vulnerable mangrove swamp rice farming, and the conditions under which agriculture remains part of their imagined futures. title: Mechanical and Electrical Characterization of Hybrid Polymer Composites Reinforced with Natural and Synthetic Fibers
abstract: This study examines the effects of optimized stacking sequences and NaOH surface treatment on the mechanical and dielectric performance of hybrid polyester composites reinforced with natural fibers (flax, sisal) and synthetic fibers (carbon, glass). Twelve laminates were fabricated using hand lay-up technique to assess hybridization effects on strength, insulation, and cost efficiency. title: Confidence Based Sequential Drift Detection Under Resource Constraints
abstract: Concept Drift Detectors are the methods that are used to identify the patterns and behaviors of data that changes over time. These methods are tested separately on different datasets, which makes it difficult to compare which detector is suitable for particular situation. This paper presents the comparison of seven concept-drift detectors: ADWIN, DDM, EDDM, KSWIN, Page-Hinkley, Naive-T and a new lightweight detector called SeqConf. title: SARIMA-based forecasting of mangrove vegetation indices across India
abstract: Abstract Mangrove ecosystems are crucial to the ecological and climatic dynamics of the Asia–Pacific coastline. However, the ability to predict long-term changes is limited, hindering evidence-based resilience and adaptation strategies. The study presents a remote-sensing framework that integrates data from multiple sensors with time-series analysis to predict changes in mangrove ecosystems along India’s coastlines, aiding in conservation planning. title: Spatial spillover effects of urban forest policy on urban green production efficiency: evidence from China’s National Forest City Construction
abstract: As environmental constraints tighten and urban green transformation continues, whether National Forest City Construction (NFCC) can improve urban green production efficiency (GPE) and generate cross-regional spillovers remains an important theoretical and policy question. Using panel data for 277 cities at the prefecture level or above in China from 2006 to 2024, this study applies a spatial Durbin difference-in-differences (SDM-DID) model to estimate the effect of NFCC on GPE. journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: Leveraging word knowledge from everyday language
abstract: Within the first few years of life, children go from nonverbal infants to fluent users of hundreds of words. This feat unfolds as children are immersed in a sea of words in conversations, stories, and other language contexts. In principle, word contexts might support word learning because words with similar meanings tend to occur in similar contexts. Thus, a child who knows some fruit words and has heard them in the context of "juicy" might learn that a "juicy mango" is also a fruit even without ever seeing a mango. title: Establishment of Regional Action Plan for conservation of critically endangered crucian carp in Czechia
abstract: The crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined markedly in recent decades due to the ongoing invasion of its congeneric species complex, the gibel carp ( Carassius gibelio ) and widespread habitat degradation. In Europe, the crucian carp occurs in two highly divergent phylogenetic lineages: the northern lineage distributed across northern and central-eastern Europe and occurs in the Elbe (Labe) and Oder (Odra) River Basins and the Danubian lineage restricted to the Danube (Dunaj) River Basin. title: Quantifying the microclimatic feedback of citywide rooftop photovoltaic deployment in Sendai, Japan
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment supports urban decarbonization, but its local microclimatic effects and interactions with urban morphology remain underexplored, particularly in coastal cities such as Sendai, Japan. The current study uses the weather research and forecasting (WRF) model with PV parameterization scheme and local climate zone (LCZ) data at 400 m resolution to conduct five experiments (exp_ctrl, exp_25, exp_50, exp_75, and exp_100) representing 0–100% citywide PV roof coverage during the hottest week of 2025. title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research

title: Analysis of amplifying effect of antecedent drought on rainfall-induced shallow landslides
abstract: Abstract Rainfall-induced shallow landslides are typically attributed to short-term meteorological triggers such as rainfall intensity and duration. However, the influence of antecedent hydrological conditions, particularly prolonged dry spells, has received limited attention despite their potential to alter soil behavior significantly. This study investigates the role of antecedent dry spells on landslide occurrence in the clay-rich terrains of the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye. title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
abstract: Abstract Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. Existing research provides valuable insights into individual hazards, infrastructure components, modeling methods, and resilience metrics, but these insights remain difficult to translate into preliminary decision support because they are organized across different hazard types, sectors, analytical scales, and decision contexts. title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
abstract: Leveraging its capability for large-scale, repeated monitoring, remote sensing has increasingly supported nitrogen and phosphorus estimation in surface waters. However, the evolution of this field from proxy-based nutrient retrieval to integration with process-based models remains insufficiently synthesized. Here we review remote sensing approaches for estimating aquatic nutrients, with emphasis on their roles in supporting process-based modeling, and compare their methodologies, applications, and limitations. title: Regional Platforms for International Cooperation in Higher Education
abstract: The present overview raises questions regarding the degree of regulation of educational network cooperation between domestic and foreign universities. The current networking models within the educational space, the so-called constructors, are analysed. Special attention is given to the Network University of the Commonwealth of Independent States, the Eurasian Network University, the “Russian-African Network University” Consortium, the University Alliance of the Silk Road, the Australia Africa Universities Network, the Matariki Network of Universities, the Network of Universities of South and S

title: Safety profile and potential favorable reporting signals of liraglutide in patients with ulcerative colitis: A FAERS pharmacovigilance and network pharmacology study
abstract: Abstract: Background: Liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), has preclinical anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects, but its safety profile and potential favorable reporting associations in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain uncertain. Objectives: To characterize liraglutide-associated reports in patients with UC and explore biological pathways that may contextualize the observed pharmacovigilance signals. title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. title: Advancing operational characterisation of dwelling stock energy models: integrating climate, occupancy profiles and heating behaviour for Ireland
abstract: Extended abstract 7-265-26 Reference Dwellings (RDs) underpin Dwelling Stock Energy Models (DSEMs) used to inform national retrofit and decarbonisation strategies. In Ireland, recent work has produced statistically robust and geometrically validated RDs derived from large-scale Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) datasets. However, while these archetypes are physically representative in terms of form, envelope and systems, they remain operationally static. title: Regional tau burden tracks with lower microglial HLA class II transcription in the human brain
abstract: Background Human leukocyte antigen class II (HLA-II) genes mark several microglial states in Alzheimer’s disease, but it remains unclear how their average transcription relates to tau measured in the same brain region. Methods We used a locked 13-gene HLA-II panel selected by biological function, cross-cohort detection, and variance, without considering effect estimates. title: GIS-based spatial prioritization of natural-hazard exposure and recorded COVID-19 case counts in Lemery, Batangas, Philippines
abstract: Local governments often maintain separate natural-hazard maps and health-surveillance records but lack a transparent method for identifying areas where these concerns overlap. This study applied a Geographic Information System (GIS) sieve-mapping approach to prioritize the 46 barangays of Lemery, Batangas, Philippines using 2,505 confirmed COVID-19 cases and ten natural-hazard layers covering seismic, landslide, coastal, flood, and volcanic hazards. title: Application of near‑infrared spectroscopy for rapid detection of moisture content of ginger (Zingiber officinale Rosc.)
abstract: Background. Ginger is a horticultural commodity and a biopharmaceutical crop with many benefits and high economic value. Ginger is widely used as a raw material in the functional food, cosmetics, and herbal pharmaceutical industries. Water content is a critical parameter affecting the quality, storage stability, and activity of bioactive compounds in ginger rhizomes. Purpose. This study aims to develop a calibration model to predict ginger rhizome moisture content using near-infrared spectroscopy and chemometric modeling for fresh, dried, and fresh-dried ginger. title: Economic impacts of subsea cable deployment
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of the economic impact of submarine cable (SMC) infrastructure, which is critical for global digital connectivity and carries almost all intercontinental data traffic. Despite their fundamental role in the digital economy, robust evidence on the economic returns of SMC investments is very scarce. title: Comparing literature-guided, LLM-assisted, and data-driven models for predicting angler pressure
abstract: This study compared three models-a literature-guided, a large language model (LLM)-assisted, and a data-driven model-all developed using Bayesian networks as the framework for predicting angler pressure measured by the number of boats observed in aerial surveys. The models used meteorological data from 98 lakes in Ontario, Canada, during 2018 and 2019, as well as platform-derived variables, including angler-reported fishing trips, fishing duration, and catch rate, together with lake webpage views. title: Layer-specific microbial community structures in the meromictic lake, Lake Suigetsu, unveiled by 16S rRNA gene amplicon and metagenomic analyses
abstract: Meromictic lakes serve as natural laboratories for investigating microbially mediated biogeochemical cycling because their stable redox stratification supports diverse metabolic processes. Lake Suigetsu is a typical meromictic lake in Japan characterized by a permanent oxycline separating the oxic brackish mixolimnion from the anoxic saline sulfidogenic monimolimnion. Recently, Lake Suigetsu's vertical bacterial composition, especially of autotrophs, sulfide oxidizers, and sulfate reducers, has gained significant attention. title: New Δ246p53 isoform responds to DNA damage to enhance p53 family functions in cellular senescence
abstract: ABSTRACT p53 is with little doubt one of the most powerful genes in our genome, as it makes growth vs arrest, repair vs replacement, catabolism vs anabolism, life vs death decisions in the cell. An alteration or malfunction in p53 may lead to cancer, degeneration or premature ageing. So, it is not surprising that p53 is also one of the most complex and tightly regulated genes, encoding for at least 10 RNA variants and 12 widely accepted protein forms. title: Agente Softbot para Pruebas Automáticas de GUI: Capa de Visión Computacional
abstract: En el contexto de testing, si bien existen herramientas de testing automático para realizar pruebas, muchas de ellas dependen de interactuar con el componente a nivel lógico, realizan pruebas a un nivel elemental (probar componentes aislados), o interactúan a nivel de interfaz gráfica pero con técnicas desactualizadas a los últimos avances. title: Phased ecological responses and effectiveness assessment of subtidal oyster reef restoration: a case study from Dashentang, Bohai Bay
abstract: Subtidal oyster reef restoration presents greater challenges for implementation and monitoring than intertidal restoration, and evaluations of relatively large-scale ecological restoration projects remain limited. This study evaluated the restoration project of Dashengtang using monitoring data from five field surveys collected from 2022 to 2026, and evaluated stage-specific ecological changes in oyster populations, aquatic environments, and macrobenthic communities. title: Evolution of Research on Satellite-Based Monitoring for Algal Blooms in the African Great Lakes
abstract: Abstract Algal blooms pose significant environmental and economic challenges worldwide. As their impact increases, there is an urgent need to improve forecasting models that predict their occurrence, development, and trends. Understanding recent research developments in satellite-based monitoring of algal blooms in the African Great Lakes provides a vital foundation for creating effective early warning systems and improving both short- and long-term prediction accuracy. title: Mangrove litter mixing alters elemental composition more frequently than mass loss, with species-specific patterns across nitrogen-enrichment plots
abstract: Introduction Mangrove litter decomposition contributes to coastal carbon and nutrient cycling, yet changes in litter mass may not fully reflect changes in elemental composition. This study investigated litter decomposition and C: N stoichiometry in relation to species identity, nitrogen enrichment, and litter mixing in a subtropical mangrove wetland. Methods Two field experiments were conducted on Hailing Island, southern China. title: Projected climate extremes and health burden in Kenya to 2050: a scenario-based analysis under SSP245 and SSP585 pathways
abstract: Background Rising global temperatures and precipitation variability are intensifying extreme weather events and threatening human health worldwide. In Kenya, climate change is projected to significantly alter the distribution and severity of climate-sensitive diseases, particularly affecting vulnerable populations. This study projects climate extremes and associated health impacts in Kenya through 2050 under two emission scenarios: SSP245 (moderate mitigation) and SSP585 (high emissions). title: The Mediating Role of Fall Risk in the Relationship Between Loneliness Levels and Quality of Life Among Older Adults Living Alone
abstract: Objective: This study was conducted to determine the mediating role of fall risk in the relationship between loneliness levels and quality of life among older adults living alone.Materials and Methods: The research was a correlational descriptive study. It was carried out with older adults individuals living alone in a provincial center in the Eastern Black Sea Region. The study sample consisted of 131 older adults. title: Ulvan, carrageenan, and fucoidan: comparative immunomodulatory mechanisms and future directions in major algal sulfated polysaccharides
abstract: Sulfated polysaccharides derived from marine algae have attracted considerable interest in innate immunity research due to their structural diversity and pronounced immunomodulatory activities. Ulvan, carrageenan, and fucoidan, derived from green, red, and brown algae, respectively, represent three paradigmatic classes of algal sulfated polysaccharides. This review establishes a four-tier analytical framework, namely “structural features, receptor recognition, signaling pathways, and immune outcomes”, to systematically compare their mechanistic differences in innate immune modulation. title: Air-to-Water Condensation Farming and Fogponics for "Zero-Watering" Horticulture in India: A Review of Technologies, Crop Suitability and Readiness for El Niño-Driven Water Scarcity
abstract: India produced an estimated 369.05 million tonnes of horticultural produce from 29.48 million ha in 2024–25. Its per-capita water availability, however, has fallen to about 1,486 m³ (2021) and is projected to reach 1,367 m³ by 2031, below the 1,700 m³ water-stress threshold. Greenhouse warming is expected to strengthen the inverse El Niño–monsoon relationship. title: Geochronology and geochemistry of granitic dikes in the Xiaogushan gold deposit NE China and implications for gold mineralization
abstract: The Xiaogushan cryptoexplosive breccia-type gold deposit is located within the eastern Hebei-western Liaoning gold belt along the northern margin of the North China Craton. The mining area contains multiple episodes of subvolcanic dikes, among which the granite porphyry and granitic aplite dikes show close temporal and spatial relationship with gold mineralization. title: Optimal any-angle path planning in static and dynamic environments
abstract: Any-angle path planning extends traditional graph-based path planning by allowing movement between any pair of vertices, rather than being restricted by predefined edges. It can find straighter and shorter paths in continuous space with graphs, making it particularly suitable for navigation in open areas such as airspaces, warehouses, and oceans. Many any-angle path-planning algorithms have been proposed, but only a few can guarantee optimal solutions, especially in the presence of dynamic obstacles. abstract: Siklon tropis memiliki lead time deteksi hingga puncak dampak yang sangat singkat sebagaimana ditunjukkan oleh Siklon Tropis Seroja yang menimbulkan bencana besar di Nusa Tenggara Timur pada April 2021. title: Comparative physiological and photosynthetic responses of three mangrove species to salinity stress and exogenous melatonin
abstract: Extreme salinity is a major environmental constraint affecting plant growth and physiological performance in coastal ecosystems. Although mangroves are naturally adapted to saline environments, their tolerance and physiological responses vary among species, and the effects of exogenous melatonin (MT) under different salinity levels remain insufficiently understood. title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision. abstract: This study examines the implementation of the Indonesian Government’s policy in supervising ship seaworthiness at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master’s Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok). The study aims to analyze policy implementation based on George C. Edwards III’s four dimensions: communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure; identify supporting and inhibiting factors; and examine efforts to overcome implementation barriers. title: Species-dependent water and salt migration drives lipoprotein remodeling and quality formation during rapid curing of separated egg yolks
abstract: Rapid curing of separated egg yolks provides an efficient strategy for accelerating salted egg production; however, how species-dependent intrinsic yolk organization regulates small molecule migration and subsequent lipoprotein remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, egg yolks separated from hen, duck, and sea duck eggs were used as model systems to elucidate the relationships among water and NaCl migration, lipoprotein structural evolution and quality formation during rapid curing. title: Hydrodynamic Response of Rectangular Floating Breakwaters near Sidewalls: A Comparative SBFEM Study of Side-Plate and Stepped-Seabed Configurations
abstract: Abstract Reducing substructure clearance modifies wave–structure interaction and can increase hydrodynamic loads on the floating breakwaters. The present study therefore evaluates the resulting changes in wave-induced forces and overturning moments rather than directly quantifying wave-transmission performance. title: Microplastics as evolving particle–chemical–microbial interfaces: plastisphere ecology, ecotoxicity, and safety-informed remediation
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are not environmentally static particles; aging, fragmentation, contaminant acquisition, organic conditioning, and microbial colonization progressively convert them into dynamic particle–chemical–microbial interfaces. This transformation is central to their environmental fate and risk because plastisphere communities can alter particle transport, contaminant partitioning, nutrient cycling, antimicrobial-resistance dynamics, and polymer transformation. title: The influence of health conditions, lifestyle factors, and stress on seafarers’ self-rated health — a cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-rated health (SRH) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active-duty seafarers. A total of 22,432 international seafarers who were on board were included in the analysis of an electronic survey distributed via 52 shipping and manning companies in February-March 2024. title: Central rapidity net baryon density and baryon number carriers in high-energy collisions
abstract: This article focuses on the experimental progress of net baryon density measurements in the central rapidity region, spanning from the AGS and SPS to the RHIC and LHC energy regimes. It comparatively analyzes the interpretation capabilities of three theoretical frameworks for net baryon density distributions across different energy regions: the valence quark transport model, the hadron cascade and hydrodynamics model, and the gluon junction model. title: Enteropathy in inborn and acquired errors of immunity: histological patterns and clinical correlates
abstract: Introduction Enteropathy is a significant and under-recognised complication of inborn errors of immunity (IEI), frequently misclassified as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or coeliac disease due to overlapping and non-specific histopathological findings. Diagnostic criteria remain poorly defined, contributing to substantial diagnostic delay and associated morbidity. abstract: Modelling how mangroves disperse can help prioritize site restoration selection by identifying source populations and linking appropriate restoration efforts with potential site-specific propagule availability. Dispersal modelling approaches are particularly impactful in regions with limited empirical data, like the Middle East. title: Exploring the main determinants of green and sustainable sukuk issuance: a neo-institutional perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the main factors that influence the issuance of green and sustainable sukuk (GSS). Specifically, it investigates how institutional, environmental, and economic pressures shape GSS issuance across countries that have developed this market. Design/methodology/approach The study uses panel data from all 12 countries that issued GSS during the period 2017–2024. title: Contribution of chemical components to cloud condensation nuclei prediction across multiple continental sites
abstract: Aerosol–cloud interactions represent a major uncertainty in climate projections. Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are particles upon which cloud droplets form, yet in situ CCN measurements remain scarce. Aerosol chemical component exerts important control over CCN activity. It remains unclear how reliably aerosol chemical composition predicts CCN number concentration (N CCN ). abstract: Abstract Gnathiid isopods are common ectoparasites of fishes whose unusual life history has created challenges for characterising their biodiversity and biogeography. abstract: How does the brain transform a chaotic stream of sensory signals into a stable, shared experience of reality? abstract: Seagrass restoration increasingly relies on seed-based approaches, yet optimal seeding densities and deployment methods remain poorly resolved. abstract: Background Calculation-based dose assessment for aircraft crew is required worldwide by authorities, as cosmic radiation dose rates at aviation altitudes are substantially higher than at sea level. The accuracy of the calculated in-flight dose onboard aircraft (“route dose” hereafter) should be confirmed periodically, particularly when the flight route is significantly changed. title: Do large language models keep the hedge? Uncertainty preservation when large language models summarize aviation and maritime incident reports
abstract: Safety-incident reports are written with deliberate epistemic caution: A reporter marks what was seen, what was inferred, and what remains unsure, and a dropped hedge can turn a tentative observation into an apparent cause. As large language models take over summarizing such reports for triage, indexing, and search, whether they preserve that caution becomes a property of the safety record itself. title: Microplastic contamination in agricultural systems: impacts on plant productivity, economic losses, and supply chain resilience
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. This review synthesizes evidence to construct an integrated narrative that links the entry of MPs into farmland with declining plant productivity, quantifiable economic losses, and the erosion of agricultural supply chain resilience. title: Unsupervised graph representation learning from AIS maritime traffic
abstract: Automatic Identification System (AIS) data provide a large-scale record of maritime vessel movements, yet learning reusable port representations from these routes remains underexplored. This paper investigates whether unsupervised graph representation learning can produce meaningful and operationally useful embeddings for ports in a global maritime port network. abstract: On October 19, 2020, the Mw7.6 Sand Point earthquake occurred near the Shumagin Islands in Alaska. Moment tensor solutions suggest oblique strike-slip faulting, but the earthquake was accompanied by an uncharacteristically large tsunami. Prior models explain this with co-seismic megathrust slip release, or shallow very slow thrust slip in the overriding plate. title: Late Cenozoic Sediment Provenance in the Northern Canterbury Basin, Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Late Cenozoic strata of the northern Canterbury Basin record uplift and erosion of mountain ranges adjacent to the transition from oblique subduction to strike‐slip on the Australian–Pacific plate boundary. Using the provenance of conglomerate clasts and sandstone samples, we reconstruct sediment transport pathways and, by inference, exhumation and reverse faulting during plate boundary development in the northeastern South Island. title: Mechanism-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review
abstract: Background Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment. abstract: Precision agriculture incorporates computer vision techniques to automate image analysis and optimize monitoring tasks in production systems. This paper presents a comparison of object detection models applied to a practical precision agriculture case study, using a proprietary dataset of grape bunch images, with a methodology extensible to standard datasets such as COCO. title: From monitoring to maintenance support: a critical review of wind turbine condition monitoring systems and their integration into maintenance practice
abstract: Although condition monitoring systems (CMS) provide detailed information about the health of critical wind turbine components, their practical application in wind farm operations and maintenance (O&M) remains limited, significantly diminishing their value. The reasons for this situation are not merely technical issues, rather, a complex interplay of various factors besides the condition monitoring algorithms themselves. abstract: Diel dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics integrate biological metabolism and physical forcing and provide a powerful tool for investigating ecosystem metabolism in shallow lakes. However, whether geographically close sites exhibit similar metabolic behavior and environmental controls remains poorly understood. Here, three years (2022–2024) of high-frequency DO observations from three contrasting nearshore sites in eastern Lake Taihu were used to quantify diel and seasonal variability in net ecosystem production (NEP), gross primary production (GPP), and ecosystem respiration (R). title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. abstract: Reliable and energy-efficient wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are important for continuous monitoring in nuclear facilities, where limited battery resources, restricted maintenance access, and safety-critical operation require stable and efficient communication. abstract: Wind disturbances at low altitudes increase energy consumption and safety risks for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in densely built urban environments. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for online path planning, while threshold methods represent hazardous regions as binary no-fly zones. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a Causal‐Aware Dynamic Knowledge Graph (CA‐DKG) framework that systematically fuses FMEA domain knowledge with data‐driven causal discovery from SCADA time series. abstract: Chinese black-and-white traditional motifs are important visual records of cultural symbolism, ritual expression, and stylistic evolution, yet their small and poorly annotated image collections limit computational analysis and generation. Here, we present a chronology-aware generative framework for digital heritage representation using a curated dataset of 300 traditional pattern images from four historical periods. abstract: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. abstract: Local erosion around foundation elements, generally referred to as ’scour’, is of major concern when designing hydraulic structures. abstract: Short-term precipitation nowcasting serves as an indispensable technical support for the early warning and risk management of meteorological hazards. To improve the nowcasting accuracy by leveraging complementary information from multi-source data, this study proposes a precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention (EAA-MNFP). abstract: Abstract There is increasing attention paid to the manipulation of ships’ Automatic Identification System (AIS) signals, with implications for maritime safety, law enforcement, and security. abstract: High-severity traffic accidents impose substantial human and economic burdens, necessitating proactive and data-driven risk forecasting mechanisms within intelligent transportation systems. This study proposed TRIDENT-Risk, a temporal risk-driven imbalance-optimized ensemble framework for high-severity accident prediction using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model. abstract: Human societies depend on stable ecosystem services, which are often stabilized by the ecological portfolio effect arising from biodiversity. This study provides a social-ecological portfolio analysis of an ecosystem service by examining the provisioning service provided by commercial Pacific salmon ( Oncorhynchus ) fisheries in British Columbia, Canada. abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. abstract: Flood evacuation is an effective protective action, yet decisions to evacuate are shaped by complex interactions among risk perception, household characteristics, and contextual constraints. Empirical evidence on household evacuation during rapid-onset riverine floods in Bangladesh remains limited. Guided by the Protective Action Decision Model (PADM), this study examines determinants of household evacuation during the August 2024 flood in south-central Bangladesh. abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic optimisation algorithm based on the semi-aquatic behaviour of the red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans). abstract: This article examines conflict dynamics in the Arctic using a framework that includes the state, regional, and systemic (international) analysis levels. While public and political narratives often depict the Arctic as an emerging arena of geopolitical rivalry, these interpretations often overlook the analytical complexity of conflicts in the region. With the digital transformation movements across all sectors, the importance of cybersecurity is increasing day by day. The aim of this study is to identify the cybersecurity risks arising in the intensive use of digital technologies in logistics operations and to determine the importance of these risks. title: Tail-aware spatiotemporal diffusion for probabilistic forecasting of extreme traffic congestion
abstract: Extreme congestion occupies only a small portion of traffic records but carries disproportionate operational consequences for traffic-management systems. Conventional point and probabilistic forecasters are optimised primarily for average accuracy and therefore often underfit rare, severe speed reductions. We present Tail-Aware Spatiotemporal Diffusion (TAD-ST), a probabilistic forecasting framework that couples a temporal convolutional and graph convolutional encoder with a conditional diffusion decoder. abstract: ABSTRACT Transformer architectures have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in image restoration; however, their quadratic self‐attention complexity imposes severe computational constraints for deployment on resource‐limited platforms. We investigate an alternative pathway within the transformer family itself: replacing quadratic attention with linear attention mechanisms while preserving the architectural strengths of spatial‐wise and channel‐wise feature modelling. title: Physically constrained Mamba forecasting supports multiobjective reservoir water quality decisions
abstract: Reservoir water-quality management requires forecasts that remain dynamically plausible and scenario choices that balance water-quality objectives against the magnitude of requested trajectory change. Historical monitoring archives, however, rarely contain labelled control actions. We develop a physics-informed inverse-decision framework that combines a decomposition–interaction Mamba forecaster, observation-space oxygen-balance diagnostics, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and preference-conditioned multi-objective search. title: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths
abstract: Abstract Deep soils represent one of Earth’s largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. Despite its genome reduction (average size ~2.9 Mb), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources. title: Crystalline Admixtures for Self-Healing Cementitious Composites: A Comparative Review of Experimental Studies
abstract: Cracking remains a major durability problem in cement-based materials because it facilitates the ingress of water and aggressive agents, accelerating deterioration. Crystalline Admixtures (CAs) have gained attention as a moisture-activated self-healing approach because they promote the formation of insoluble products within pores and cracks, thereby reducing crack connectivity and improving water tightness. title: Changes in the annual cycle of shallow subarctic groundwater regimes over 50 years
abstract: Seasonal groundwater level regimes are exposed to climate change, with implications for drought and flood risks, water supply, agriculture, and ecosystems. Changes in the intra-annual groundwater fluctuations are accentuated in quickly responding shallow aquifers found worldwide, but particularly in subarctic regions, where the cold winter season attenuates infiltration and evaporation. To identify the types of subarctic groundwater regimes and their responses to the changing climate, 50-year groundwater level data from 52 monitoring stations throughout Finland were analyzed. abstract: Abstract Water quality patterns reflect spatially heterogeneous associations among topography, drainage connectivity, land use configuration, and soil hydrologic structure, whereas concentration-based assessments and global models may obscure where these relationships emerge and at which spatial scales they operate. Using monitoring data from 2020 to 2024, this study examined six water quality indicators: total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, and electrical conductivity (EC) across 67 mid-basins in South Korea. title: An AI-Enabled Predictive Procurement Model for Forecasting and Inventory Optimization
abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. title: Power demand forecasting of university buildings with Random Forest and Stacking algorithms
abstract: El pronóstico de la demanda eléctrica en entornos institucionales presenta desafíos particulares derivados de la irregularidad de los patrones de consumo, especialmente durante períodos de receso académico o ante cambios estructurales en la infraestructura eléctrica. En este trabajo se evalúa la capacidad de pronóstico de los algoritmos Random Forest y Stacking, usando datos de demanda de la Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata. abstract: Objective To explore the health status and its influencing factors among seafarers based on the Health Ecological Model, and to identify priority areas for health management. Methods A convenience sampling approach was used to administer a questionnaire survey to 106 seafarers from March to June 2026. title: STEP towards responsible GIScience: pillars, purposes, and challenges
abstract: GIScience is crucial for spatial understanding, analysis, and decision-making across multiple sectors. As GIScience demonstrates its continual impact in addressing critical societal and environmental challenges, growing concerns regarding its responsible use rise accordingly. The integration of vast and intricate datasets and the application of translucent algorithms hold the potential to infringe on privacy, perpetuate biases, exacerbate societal inequities, or undermine reliability. title: Solar Radiation Prediction using XGBoost across Topographic Zones: ENSO Variability and Implications for Chili Productivity in Yogyakarta
abstract: Chili pepper productivity in Indonesia is highly sensitive to climate variability, particularly solar radiation. This study aims to predict solar radiation to optimize chili pepper productivity across four distinct topographic zones in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. We employed the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to predict solar radiation 18 months ahead. Models were trained using monthly ERA5 data, with the solar radiation parameter specifically validated against ground-based measurements, resulting in an average Pearson correlation (r) of 0.79. title: The limits of Antarctic conservation governance
abstract: Abstract The Antarctic region exerts a profound influence on the Earth system, making its conservation fundamental to sustaining planetary health and human wellbeing. The Antarctic Treaty System (ATS) holds near-exclusive authority for environmental protection across the region, yet questions remain regarding its capacity to address a growing range of conservation threats. We investigate this by analysing over 90,000 scientific and policy documents (1961–2023) to examine how conservation threats are discussed across science and ATS policy deliberations. title: Persistent regional asymmetry with apparent late-record convergence in Eurasian-North American snowmelt trends
abstract: Abstract Northern Hemisphere snowmelt phenology has shifted earlier over the past 37 years, but Eurasia and North America have followed markedly different trajectories. Using a random forest framework fusing passive microwave brightness temperatures, ERA5-Land reanalysis, and static landscape predictors, we produce annual 6.25 km outputs of main melt onset date (MMOD), snow off date, and snowmelt duration (SMD) across the Northern Hemisphere seasonal snow domain from 1988-2025, trained on more than 13,000 in situ observations. title: HierTAC-Net: a robust and explainable hierarchical attention network for multi-configuration gastrointestinal endoscopic image classification
abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer death worldwide, even though colonoscopy is an effective screening tool. Automated analysis of endoscopic images can help doctors find more lesions and make faster decisions, but current systems usually handle just one task, are tested on clear images from a single dataset, and are rarely compared against working clinicians. abstract: Abstract Directed fluid transport is critical to diverse applications spanning water purification, atmospheric water harvesting, point-of-care diagnostics, thermal management, and energy conversion, yet conventional microfluidic systems often require external pumps and complex infrastructure, severely limiting their scalability and adaptability. Directed fluid transport enabled by milli-structured surfaces has rapidly evolved from static, one‑way capillary designs to dynamic, reconfigurable and programmable systems. abstract: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2025); after applying rigorous inclusion criteria, 38 studies were selected. abstract: Abstract The radius of maximum wind (RMW) is one of the key parameters for characterizing the structure of tropical cyclones (TCs). Although multiple methods have been developed to estimate the RMW, their estimates can sometimes differ substantially and are not always available, making it difficult to construct a comprehensive long-term RMW dataset. This study develops a Bayesian consensus method to derive a single RMW estimate from multiple RMW estimates. abstract: Surface contamination is one of the main causes of flashover on outdoor insulators, since deposits accumulated on the insulator surface reduce its resistance and can lead to failure. Monitoring techniques based on parameters such as the Equivalent Salt Deposit Density (ESDD) are widely used to estimate this contamination level and warn operators before a flashover occurs, yet reliable forecasting of ESDD remains a challenging task due to its nonlinear and noisy behavior. title: Maritime transport and policy research over the past 50 years: a review across four maritime journals
abstract: Journal focused bibliometric studies, especially those examining leading or highly relevant journals, are widely acknowledged as an effective way to capture the intellectual structure of a field. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of four important journals which have strong orientation in maritime transport and policy field using R-Bibliometrix package and VOSviewer. abstract: The Archie equation is a fundamental model for describing the relationships between formation resistivity, porosity and water saturation, and plays an important role in log-based saturation evaluation. However, in complex reservoirs, its original structure and constant-parameter assumptions are often insufficient for refined reservoir evaluation because of complex mineral compositions, diverse pore structures and other controlling factors. abstract: In regulated reservoirs, actual water-level dynamics do not always coincide with conventional hydrological periods, yet phytoplankton community variation under such conditions remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract To address the inherent challenges of localization in regions with weak or ambiguous magnetic gradients, this paper proposes a lightweight residual multilayer perceptron (MLRP) method for geomagnetic matching navigation. By establishing an accurate nonlinear mapping between geomagnetic vectors and spatial coordinates, the proposed method prevents gradient degradation and the consequent decline in accuracy and stability observed in existing geomagnetic matching methods. abstract: ABSTRACT Selective maintenance for mission‐oriented equipment systems is often simulated from fixed lifetime distributions or static initial ages, which can obscure component‐specific degradation before a mission. This paper proposes a simulation‐based selective maintenance framework that incorporates real‐time condition mapping into mission reliability evaluation. abstract: Groundwater in urban karst spring systems is increasingly impacted by coupled natural processes and anthropogenic nitrogen loading, yet the linkage between hydrochemical evolution, nitrate-related health risk, and contaminant transport remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops an integrated framework for the Baiquan spring system by combining hydrochemical analysis, entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI), probabilistic health-risk assessment, numerical transport modelling, and multivariate clustering. abstract: China Railway Express (CR Express) has become an important rail-based logistics corridor for improving Eurasian connectivity, regional openness, and sustainable freight organization. However, evaluating its node cities remains challenging because assembly-center labels are incomplete, city performance is network-dependent, and logistics development is increasingly shaped by resilience and green-sustainability requirements. abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analyses of faunal remains have demonstrated significant potential to enhance understandings of human-animal relationships during periods of European colonization. abstract: Automatic Traffic Sign Recognition is paramount in modern transportation systems. However, curating large-scale datasets for diverse traffic sign detection remains impractical. In this context, we present FUSED-Net, a novel approach that enhances Few-Shot Object Detection (FSOD) for traffic signs using limited data. abstract: The study investigates the land use and land cover (LULC) changes in Upper Bhavani River basin of the Western Ghats over the past four decades (1989–2019) using remote sensing (RS) and geographic information system (GIS) techniques. It also explores the correlation between LULC changes and population growth during this period. abstract: ABSTRACT In offshore wind power development, offshore wind farm siting (OWFS) is a crucial yet complex decision process, often compromised by expert linguistic ambiguity, multidimensional expert evaluation and conflicting criteria. To tackle these challenges, this study proposes an integrated multicriteria group decision‐making (MCGDM) framework that integrates the entropy weight method (EWM) with the cubic q‐rung orthopair fuzzy extension of TOPSIS (Cq‐ROF‐TOPSIS). title: Multi-source geospatial modelling of direct economic losses from rainstorm-related disaster events in Guangxi, South China
abstract: Rainstorm-related disasters cause substantial economic losses in Guangxi, China, but event-level loss estimates are complicated by spatially clustered events, changing socioeconomic exposure, and heterogeneous reporting. We compiled 1,811 county-event records from the official disaster archive for 2012–2021 and linked them to event-period precipitation, year-matched gridded population and GDP, and selected vulnerability-related proxies. abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. In this study, a hybrid feature-level unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework called TriAlign-UDA, which operates on frozen histopathology foundation model representations, is proposed. title: Estimation of seafood byproducts generated by freezing companies in the Souss-Massa Region, Morocco
abstract: The seafood processing industry generates substantial quantities of byproducts that remain underutilized despite their potential for recovery and further utilization. This study aimed to assess the generation and management of seafood byproducts within the freezing industry of the Souss-Massa region, Morocco. title: MSAL-YOLO: a YOLOv8-based detector for small and densely distributed object detection in UAV aerial imagery
abstract: Abstract Object detection in UAV aerial imagery is challenging because of small object scales, dense distributions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds. To address these issues, we propose MSAL-YOLO, an improved YOLOv8-based detector for aerial object detection. abstract: Abstract. Uncertainties in natural systems are pervasive, varied, and unavoidable due to inherent open system complexity and limited knowledge. Therefore, the evolution of a natural system cannot be predicted deterministically and probabilistic forecasts are commonly used to account for these uncertainties. title: Deer disturbance influences avian acoustic activity across functional groups in temperate forests
abstract: Cervid overpopulation is increasingly altering temperate forest ecosystems worldwide, when browsing pressure exceeds ecosystem resilience, with consequences that extend beyond individual species to the structure and functioning of entire communities. While the impacts of deer ( Cervidae ) on specific bird species are well studied, there remains a critical gap in understanding how deer influence avian communities across a spectrum of functional traits. abstract: Wetlands play a crucial role in regulating regional climate through their effects on surface energy balance and evapotranspiration. However, rapid wetland loss in Southeast Asia has raised concerns about its potential to intensify extreme heat exposure during heatwaves. This study investigates the impact of wetland loss on regional temperature and human heat stress during the 2023 heatwave in the Cambodia Lower Mekong Delta (CLMD). abstract: Abstract Accurate land-use and land-cover classification in hyper-arid environments is challenging because several surface types can exhibit overlapping spectral and spatial characteristics in Landsat imagery. These surfaces include water, irrigated agriculture, moist soil, barren land, and built-up areas. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid framework for classifying six land-use and land-cover classes in Najran, Saudi Arabia, using seven-band Landsat 8 imagery. abstract: Methanogenic archaea, capable of producing organic matter from hydrogen and CO 2 emanating from the mantle, constitute one of the key functional groups of microorganisms in the deep subsurface. abstract: Protection from human- induced pressures is vital to the survival of peri-urban protected areas, particularly in fast-growing urban areas.
