abstract: Niche diplomacy is a notable characteristic of the foreign policy of middle powers - states that have the capacity to play a prominent role on the international stage, but are not powerful enough to impose their will on others. Therefore, middle powers need to rely on their ability to identify and fill in “niche spaces” through diplomatic methods and skills, that is, choosing a few specific issues, institutions or areas to specialize in and orient them as important foundations in its foreign policy. abstract: Area-based and species-specific protection provide complementary benefits for biodiversity conservation. abstract: Abstract Aquaculture holds great importance as a source of sustenance for the ever-expanding global population. However, it has become increasingly apparent that this industry's growth has come at a cost, as it has been linked to a range of environmental challenges, including greenhouse gas emissions. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. abstract: Mangroves are among the most carbon-rich tropical forests, with much of their carbon stock located in underlying sediments. abstract: Apple ripeness detection in complex orchard scenarios is plagued by fruit occlusion, overlapping, intense illumination interference, and subtle maturity feature differences among similar fruits. abstract: Mission-critical applications (aerospace, automotive, and defense) have autonomous systems that must have very high reliability to allow continued operation in varied environmental structures and fault conditions. The medium of flexibility and adaptability of the computer hardware is represented by reconfigurable computing platforms and, especially, by Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Architectures (CGRAs). abstract: Abstract The meaning of targets in data-driven mineral prospectivity mapping (DD-MPM) is foremost dependent on the quality of data. The resolving power of annotated data depends on the ratio of annotated area or volume and target footprint. At sufficiently large-scales of DD-MPM, it is impossible to match annotated area and covariate resolution to the footprint of mineral deposits. Consequently, information exposed to data modelling is unrestricted to between a target and its features. title: Mapping rainfed cereals and olive groves using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data in northern Morocco
abstract: Accurate discrimination of agricultural crop categories in heterogeneous, rainfed landscapes remains challenging because crop spectral responses are strongly influenced by environmental variability and complex terrain. This study assessed the contribution of optical (Sentinel-2), radar (Sentinel-1), and topographic variables to the binary discrimination of annual rainfed cereals and perennial olive groves in the Tangier–Tétouan–Al Hoceima region of northern Morocco, a Mediterranean mountain environment characterized by fragmented agricultural systems and rainfed conditions. title: Retrieval-to-abstraction LLM-assisted literature synthesis: Case demonstrations in digital health technology-enabled randomized controlled trial outcome reporting
abstract: Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support evidence-based clinical advancement. Clinical trial reporting guidelines, including CONSORT, establish common data elements that support systematic synthesis of published trial outcomes. However, the rapid rise of digital health technologies presents new challenges for reporting guidelines, and substantial real-world reporting heterogeneity has been observed. title: Integrated adaptations of muscle structure and mitochondrial function to locomotion demands in teleost fishes
abstract: Abstract Teleost fishes display diverse swimming modes supported by functional specialization of skeletal muscle. However, the ultrastructural adaptations and molecular mechanisms regulating mitochondrial homeostasis in relation to divergent locomotion remain unclear. We compared muscle fiber composition, mitochondrial ultrastructure, and regulatory pathways in two teleosts with contrasting swimming strategies: the sustained swimmer Pseudocaranx dentex and the burst swimmer Paralichthys olivaceus. title: Spectral signatures of zenith sky radiance from surface-based sky radiometers: implications for clear- and cloudy-sky detection
abstract: Abstract. Accurate identification of clear- and cloudy-sky conditions is essential for reliable aerosol and cloud retrievals from ground-based remote sensing observations. This study investigates the spectral characteristics of zenith radiances measured by SKYNET sky radiometers and evaluates their potential for distinguishing clear- and cloudy-sky conditions based on wavelength dependence. title: Assessing the resilience of water supply infrastructure to climate variability: a current status assessment in rural India
abstract: Abstract Rural Indian communities, characterised by the decentralised and informal nature of water governance, are extremely vulnerable to climate shocks that impair local water supply infrastructures (WSIs). This study assesses WSI resilience in the face of current climate variability and examines the multidimensional elements that influence resilience results. The research uses a participatory, bottom-up, mixed-method approach to apply the “How Tough is WASH (HTIW)” framework across four rural communities—Srayikkadu (Kerala), Ahirpurwa (Bihar), Kali Nagar (West Bengal), and Kanti (Haryana),

title: Modeling and Manufacturing 3D Geometric Figures for STEM Training of Engineering Students: A Staged Methodology and Case Study
abstract: This article presents a methodology for modeling and manufacturing three-dimensional (3D) geometric figures. The need for developing the methodology is substantiated, and its significance for the STEM training of future specialists in engineering specialties is demonstrated. An advantage of the methodology is the clear structuring of all its stages, levels, and steps, which simplifies the process of implementing STEM projects. journal: International Journal of Engineering and Manufacturing

title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. title: Multi-year temporal and seasonal abundance patterns of common bottlenose dolphins near Sarasota, Florida
abstract: Long-term demographic monitoring is critical for understanding population stability and responses to environmental disturbance. Bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) inhabiting Sarasota Bay, Florida, have been studied by the Sarasota Dolphin Research Program since 1970. While most dolphins in the resident community are individually identifiable via photographic-identification (photo-ID), direct census datasets are largely unavailable elsewhere. A previous Sarasota study used capture-mark-recapture (CMR) surveys and robust-design models to estimate abundance across four seasons in 2015. Th

title: Assessment of vulnerability and economic losses of typical Chinese ports under the influence of tropical cyclones
abstract: The shipping industry is vital to global trade, with China’s ports leading in scale for years. However, the growing threat of climate change, especially tropical cyclones, poses serious risks to port operations, infrastructure, and supply chains, resulting in substantial economic losses. This study assesses the resilience and economic impacts of tropical cyclones on five key Chinese ports, using Shanghai, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Xiamen, and Qinzhou as case studies. It develops a comprehensive index system that accounts for resilience, efficiency, and importance. The study utilizes expert surveys, e

title: Generative topology inverse design of periodic ventilated acoustic metamaterials
abstract: Ventilated acoustic metamaterials can provide sound attenuation while maintaining airflow, but their inverse design remains challenging because acoustic insulation and ventilation are coupled with high-dimensional, non-unique topology-performance relationships. This study proposes a generative topology inverse design framework for periodic ventilated acoustic metamaterials. A dataset of binary pixelated unit cell topologies is generated in an axisymmetric design domain with a central ventilation channel, and the first phononic bandgap bounds are obtained using Bloch periodic theory. title: Trend Analysis and Prediction of Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) Change in General Santos City
abstract: This study analyzed land use and land cover (LULC) changes in General Santos City and predicted possible future LULC patterns for 2043 and 2063. It quantified changes in six LULC classes from 2003 to 2063 using a quantitative geospatial modeling approach. Landsat Imagery was the primary dataset, while validation points from historical imagery and spatial drivers, including aspect, elevation, slope, and distance to roads and rivers, were incorporated into the model. journal: Research Frontiers International Journal of Social Science and Technology

title: PM 2.5 air quality index in major cities. long memory analysis with fractional integration
abstract: This article presents new evidence on the persistence, seasonality, and trends of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) Air Quality Index (AQI) across twenty global megacities from January 2014 to January 2026. The research applies a fractional integration approach to model the long-memory dynamics using high-frequency daily data. Rather than relying on standard binary unit root tests, we adopt the fractional integration framework, which provides a continuous measure of the degree of persistence. title: Lightweight Artistic Style Classification via Texture Correlation and Adaptive Local–Global Fusion
abstract: Artistic style classification remains challenging because visually similar styles often exhibit subtle differences in brushstrokes, textures, colors, and global composition. To address this problem, this paper proposes a lightweight artistic style classification framework based on a MobileNet–Transformer Hybrid (MTH). First, a Lightweight Texture Correlation Module (LTCM) is introduced to capture multi-scale texture relationships from intermediate convolutional features. title: A balanced set of standardized affective environmental images for climate change research
abstract: Evocative visual imagery is central to research on affective pathways of environmental engagement, yet existing stimulus sets often overrepresent negative imagery and make it difficult to compare positive and negative affective responses under comparable conditions. We developed a balanced database of affective environmental images designed to support controlled comparisons of positive and negative environmental imagery. In total, 587 participants rated 203 images depicting consequences of unmitigated climate change and context-matched positive alternatives on pleasantness and activation. Part

title: Implementation of a New Paradigm for Hydrometeorological Support for Enterprise Leaders and the Public for Adaptation Purposes
abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of hydrometeorological support users for the population and enterprises leaders by implementing a new paradigm. The failure of enterprises to account for all climate and change-related risks, combined with the absence of systematized and formalized impact forecasts and recommendations for preventive actions, leads to increased losses. To establish a modern hydrometeorological support system, the paper proposes an implementation integrated approach of an end-to-end data processing scheme ‒ spanning from observation to decision support. title: Natural and Horizontal Visibility Graphs of EEG Power Spectra for Autism Spectrum Disorder Classification
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is primarily identified through behavioral and developmental assessment, which may require specialist expertise and considerable time. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers non-invasive neurophysiological information, but reliable ASD classification remains challenging because EEG signals are nonstationary and highly variable across individuals. This study evaluates whether visibility-graph topology derived from EEG power spectral density (PSD) curves provides complementary information beyond conventional spectral descriptors. title: PELATIHAN PERAWATAN MOTOR TEMPEL KEPADA OPERATOR DAN AWAK KAPAL SUNGAI DI DESA MUARA PADANG KABUPATEN BANYUASIN
abstract: Keandalan motor tempel merupakan salah satu faktor penting dalam mendukung keselamatan dan keberlangsungan operasional kapal sungai. Keterbatasan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal dalam melakukan perawatan preventif dapat meningkatkan risiko gangguan mesin selama pelayaran. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal sungai dalam melakukan pemeriksaan dan perawatan dasar motor tempel. title: From Demand Signals to Retail Decisions in Business Intelligence Research
abstract: Retail analytics has moved beyond improving point forecasts, yet evidence about the value of a forecast for pricing, replenishment, fulfillment, and managerial adoption remains dispersed.This structured review compares 36 journal studies published from 2023 through 2025, identified within a search window ending in January 2026, across four connected areas: demand forecasting (12), pricing and commercial levers (7), inventory and fulfillment (8), and decision systems (9).Each study is examined for its information setting, analytic approach, decision connection, and evidence boundary.The synthes

title: When the Night Stops Cooling: Modeling Extreme Warm Nights Across California Weather Stations
abstract: This paper investigates which factors influence extreme warm nights across California using NOAA GHCN-Daily station observations. We defined extreme warm nights using station-specific 95th percentile summer TMIN thresholds based on a historical baseline period. For each station-year, the percentage of valid summer nights classified as extreme warm nights was calculated. A random forest regression model was then used to explore the effect of year, latitude, longitude, elevation, and distance to coast on extreme warm-night frequency. title: Domain adaptation affects adversarial robustness in autonomous steering models
abstract: Abstract Domain adaptation is commonly used to transfer autonomous steering models across regions with different road configurations, such as from right-hand to left-hand traffic. While prior work has largely evaluated adaptation using clean target-domain steering accuracy, its effect on adversarial robustness remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates two steering architectures, PilotNet and ResNet-18, under four adaptation strategies: U.S.-trained, flipped U.S.-trained, U.S.-trained + fine-tuned, and flipped U.S.-trained + fine-tuned. title: Extracting X (formerly Twitter) information to improve relief logistics: social media analytics to the rescue
abstract: Purpose During sudden disasters, information is needed on victims’ needs and locations, resource availability, and first responders’ status to improve relief logistics; this study aims to extract this critical information from X (formerly Twitter). Design/methodology/approach Using social media analytics and the capture-understand-present approach, the authors rank users and their posts to identify relevant data to support humanitarian operations. journal: Journal of Humanitarian Logistics and Supply Chain Management

title: Technical–ethical–governance circuit–breaker framework for safe and sustainable AI governance
abstract: The growing use of large language models and autonomous AI systems in high-risk settings has created safety risks that cannot be addressed through technical safeguards alone. Existing approaches often treat technical failure control, ethical oversight, and institutional governance as separate domains, making coordinated intervention difficult when risks escalate across these boundaries. This study proposes the technical–ethical–governance (TEG) framework as an integrated circuit-breaker architecture for managing risks in high-risk AI systems. title: Latent Structure in Chess Positions
abstract: En este trabajo entrenamos autoencoders para entender representaciones latentes de posiciones de ajedrez. Utilizamos una base de datos de partidas de Lichess filtradas por nivel de juego y control de tiempo, y representamos cada posición como un tensor de múltiples canales. Entrenamos un autoencoder para reconstruir dichas posiciones y posteriormente analizamos el espacio latente mediante Análisis de Componentes Principales (PCA). title: Molecular Mechanisms of Microbial Biomineralization: Protein Molecules
abstract: Microbial biomineralization is a ubiquitous natural process involving the formation and accumulation of inorganic minerals. It plays a crucial role in biogeochemical cycles and the development of biological structures. Despite recent progress in studying this phenomenon, the underlying molecular mechanisms mediated by proteins and extracellular polymers remain insufficiently systematized. title: Thermodynamic regulation promotes in situ repair of oxide films in the damaged regions of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy and enhances corrosion resistance
abstract: This study proposes a thermodynamically regulated in situ repair strategy for scratched regions of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy. The strategy is controlled by NiCl 2 addition. It aims to enhance the corrosion resistance of the regenerated film and reduce the risk of localized corrosion failure. Pourbaix diagram analysis and potentiodynamic polarization tests identified NiCl 2 as the repair additive. A concentration of 0.1 wt% was determined to be optimal. title: Artifact-to-true seepage detection in RGB images using CLIP representations
abstract: Red-Green-Blue (RGB) vision based supervised learning is demonstrated for the purpose of identifying subsurface groundwater seepage for low-cost and accurate inspection of dams and slope embankments using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Supervised learning is constrained by the scarcity of confirmed true seepage-positive images. Our study investigates artifact-to-true seepage detection at the earliest intervention point. title: High diversity but limited expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a peatland microbial community
abstract: The in situ relevance of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remains poorly understood. We apply meta-omics to characterize BGC diversity and activity along a peatland redox gradient. From seven metagenomes, we recover 9,694 BGCs, spanning diverse taxa, most lacking close relatives in reference databases, indicating extensive novelty. Only 9-27% of this potential is expressed in situ, with Acidobacteriota, despite moderate repertoires, accounting for over half of all BGC transcription. title: Enhanced WCSPH modelling of 2-D and 3-D granular flows using μ(I) rheology with rheology-aware boundary treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH) framework for granular materials incorporating δ -SPH pressure stabilization, μ ( I ) rheology, a rheology-consistent extrapolated boundary condition (EBC), and a rheology-aware particle shifting technique (PST). title: Improving Employee Performance Through Occupational Health and Safety Compliance: A Study at the Makassar Port Authority
abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of the implementation of the occupational safety and health management system (SMK3) on employee work productivity at KSOP Utama Makassar. The results of this study indicate that, simultaneously (F-test), occupational safety and occupational health have a significant positive effect on employee work productivity, accounting for 87.6%. The remaining 12.4% is attributed to other variables not studied by the researcher. title: Reptiles in the One Health ecology of antimicrobial resistance, with insights into zoonotic pathogens: reservoirs, transmission pathways, and public health implications
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge at the interface of human, animal, and environmental health. Reptiles—including wild populations, pets, farmed species, and internationally traded animals—are increasingly recognized as participants in One Health AMR networks, occupying ecological interfaces that facilitate interactions among wildlife, domestic animals, humans, and the environment. title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. title: Modeling and optimization of battery-based energy storage systems for UAVs
abstract: The paper presents the improvement of the energy efficiency of drones used in different missions. In this paper, a model for Li-ion batteries is created, made through equivalent electrical circuits. This method facilitates the examination of the relationship between the required energy consumption and the electrical response of the battery to demands. title: UAV integrated IoT sensing platform for sustainable air quality monitoring and real time AQI estimation
abstract: Monitoring modern air pollution requires flexible but portable systems that can be used to gather real-time data in various settings. This paper describes a drone-based air quality monitoring platform with IoT-enabled sensors integrated into it. The system carries multiple gas sensors CO, NO 2 , O 3 , SO 2 , and PM 2.5 , all managed by a Raspberry Pi 4 (Model B). The platform operates at a 1 Hz sampling rate performing onboard data filtering, dynamic caching and wireless synchronization with a cloud platform (ThingSpeak®) for real-time visualization. title: Analytical Noise-Variance Assessment of Receiver-Side Optical Filtering for Background-Noise Mitigation in Free-Space Optical Communication under Atmospheric Turbulence
abstract: Receiver-side optical filtering trades useful-signal attenuation against noise suppression in free-space optical communication. We analyse a 40 Gbps, 1.54 km OptiSystem link at 1552.52 nm using six filter responses. A normalized variance metric combines received power and signal-to-noise ratio. title: Garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell equipped with an amplification system coupled with a secondary PV ‐assisted module: Utilization as eco‐sustainable electrical power supply for carbon monoxide gas sensor
abstract: Abstract Autonomous environmental telemetry requires continuous, maintenance‐free power sources capable of driving commercial sensing electronics. This study reports the development of a self‐powered bio‐electrochemical sensing platform utilizing a garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell (s‐MFC) coupled with a hybrid power management system (PMS) to drive a commercial off‐the‐shelf (COTS) carbon monoxide (CO) gas sensor. title: Instability-Aware Digital Twin Control for Grid-Constrained Low-Carbon Smart Ports
abstract: Modern smart ports combine terminal electrification, shore power, renewable generation, storage, and digital operational control under uncertain vessel traffic and time-varying grid limits. This study develops a simulation-based digital-twin control prototype that synchronizes vessel flow, berth occupancy, equipment activity, shore-power demand, renewable supply, battery state, grid import, and modelled emissions. title: Copper and zinc from slurry applications shape grassland soil microbial community structure in a long-term experiment
abstract: Soil microbes are crucial in maintaining soil and plant health, underpinning agronomic productivity. This study investigates antimicrobial copper- and zinc-laden cow and pig slurry applications on soil microbial community structures in an approximately 50-year long-term slurry experiment on a permanent grassland located in County Down, Northern Ireland. Illumina and PacBio rRNA sequencing (analysing 16S and ITS genera) were used to investigate soil samples (to 15 cm depth) from the experiment’s treatments. title: A two-stage cascaded prediction framework for urban inundation depth using a dual-branch CNN-ConvLSTM network
abstract: Study region Shenzhen, China, is a densely urbanized subtropical megacity characterized by extensive impervious surfaces, rapid runoff responses, and frequent rainfall-induced inundation. Study focus To address the underestimation of urban inundation depth driven by severe zero-inflation, this study proposes a two-stage Cascaded Multi-scale CNN-ConvLSTM Network (CMC-Net). A Random Forest classifier first identifies hazardous inundation samples using a 0.15-m threshold. title: Historical climate extremes in Europe and the connection between spring precipitation and summer heat
abstract: Abstract. Hot European summers are often preceded by dry springs such as in 2022, but also in 1473 or 1540, two well-known summers of catastrophic heat. Spring precipitation deficits deplete soil moisture levels, which can amplify extreme summer temperature anomalies in Europe through land-atmosphere feedback mechanisms and altered atmospheric circulation. However, the link is not particularly strong, and hence long time series might help to better elucidate the mechanisms. title: Mutual Adaptation and Influence: Review of Latent Dynamics Models in Human–Robot Interaction
abstract: Recent advances in robotics have enabled more dynamic and interactive roles when working with humans. This progress is enabled in part by latent state models, which allow the robot to predict human actions in a compact and tractable way. This paradigm has allowed robots not only to respond and adapt to human behavior but also to anticipate and plan proactively through the use of latent dynamics models. title: A web development method for transmission line O&M components based on multi-source data sensing and deep reinforcement learning algorithms
abstract: Transmission corridors in high-altitude and micro-topographic regions are chronically subjected to strong electromagnetic pulse interference, multi-physics field coupling, and extreme climatic stressors. This results in temporal asynchrony and spatial mismatch in multi-source monitoring data, while environmental disturbances cause confidence drift in single data sources. Furthermore, traditional O&M systems lack topological awareness and dynamic decision-making capabilities, leading to disruptions in the O&M process chain. title: Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways
abstract: Abstract. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash-flood research. title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State‐Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge‐intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision‐making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. title: Evolution of Architectural Design: A Historical Analysis of the Rivers State Government House from Independence to Present
abstract: The architectural transformation of the Rivers State Government House serves as a lens for examining the interplay between political authority, historical influence, and cultural identity in Nigeria. This study traces the evolution of its design from colonial-era structures to modern government complexes, analysing how governance, modernisation, and external architectural trends have shaped its development. title: Wind Power Scenario Generation Based on Dual‐Domain Generator and Improved Spectral Bias Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: Scene generation is a core technology for quantifying wind power uncertainty. Addressing issues such as insufficient scene realism and low spectral matching accuracy in traditional generation models, this paper proposes a frequency domain generative adversarial network (FD‐GAN) method for wind power scene generation based on a dual‐domain generator and improved spectral deviation. title: A diversified approach to the design of recombinant silk proteins for biomaterials
abstract: Silk offers a sustainable alternative to synthetic polymers, yet widespread industrial adoption has not been realised. Many current silk protein engineering efforts have focused on spider dragline silk; a pursuit made difficult by the metabolic burden of expressing high molecular weight, repetitive spidroins. This Perspective argues for a strategic redirection toward the broader sequence space of non-canonical silks for silk protein engineering. title: Real-world user interactions with large language models for explaining home electrocardiogram reports
abstract: With the development of portable electrocardiogram (ECG) devices, users can conveniently obtain physiological data in home settings, yet they still face an interpretation gap because of limited medical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) may help bridge this gap through natural-language explanations, but large-scale real-world evidence on how users interact with them in home settings remains limited. title: Conceptual analysis on synergetic retrievals of self-consistent aerosol property climate data records
abstract: The influence of aerosols on climate is determined not only by their global distribution but also by their composition. However, so far, a large fraction of the development efforts for satellite-based aerosol retrievals has focused on inverting from different single instruments the total column aerosol optical depth (AOD), as measure of the total abundance of atmospheric aerosols. title: A dual-enhanced random forest model for fatigue life prediction under multi-level variable amplitude loading
abstract: To address two limitations (hyperparameter sensitivity and black-box fitting) of random forest (RF) models in predicting fatigue life under multi-level variable amplitude loading, a dual-enhanced random forest model (Dual-ERF) is proposed. First, Q-Learning reinforcement learning is introduced to improve the Langevin Equation Evolution (LEE) model, forming the Q-LEE model. title: Analysis of the effects of different protease types on volatile compounds and oxidative properties of blackthroat seaperch ( Doederleinia berycoides ) liver oil
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of different proteases on the extraction, flavor profile, and oxidative stability of blackthroat seaperch (Doederleinia berycoides) liver oil obtained by aqueous enzymatic extraction. Trypsin-assisted extraction yielded oil with the greatest oxidative stability. Combined analysis by gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified aldehydes as the characteristic volatile compounds in the liver oil. title: Mycosphere microbiome assembly and metabolic reprogramming in Phallus rugulosus revealed by multi-omics integration
abstract: The mycosphere, defined as the soil zone influenced by fungal hyphae, hosts a distinct microbiome that plays a critical role in host development. Nevertheless, the assembly rules and metabolic functions in macrofungi remain poorly understood. This study aims to disentangle these processes in the edible fungus Phallus rugulosus . We integrated metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics to compare mycosphere soil (MS) and bulk soil (BS) of P. rugulosus . title: Dynamic Influence Based Fitness Shaping For Cooperative Coevolution
abstract: Multiagent settings are naturally characterized by coevolutionary dynamics, where agents must adapt and learn in the context of their teammates. A key challenge in such domains is determining how to credit an agent for its individual contribution to team performance. Fitness shaping approaches partially address this by identifying and isolating an agent's direct contribution to team success. title: Inclusive finance and biodiversity risk: addressing environmental challenges, improving urbanization landscape resilience and sustainable development
abstract: Introduction Biodiversity loss ranks among the most severe global risks of the coming decade, with the World Economic Forum’s 2025 Global Risks Report identifying it as the second greatest long-term threat to economic stability. Digital financial inclusion (DFI) has expanded rapidly in China and is often argued to enable green transformation, yet direct empirical evidence on its effect on emissions and biodiversity outcomes at the provincial level remains limited. title: Surgical management of reproductive disease in aquarium managed female elasmobranchs
abstract: Introduction Reproductive disease in female elasmobranchs has been increasingly reported in the literature, though there are limited descriptions of therapeutic intervention. Methods This retrospective case series details the surgical management of 20 female elasmobranchs representing nine species. Data for this study were collected from the medical records and necropsy reports of elasmobranchs at six separate zoos and aquaria. title: α-Glucosidase Inhibitory and Antibacterial Activity of Fermented Mackerel By-Product Muscle and Skin Hydrolysates: In Vitro and In Silico Peptidomics Analysis
abstract: Mackerel (Scomberomorus commerson) processing by-products represent an abundant yet underutilized protein source that can be valorized into bioactive peptides through microbial fermentation. This study investigated the α-glucosidase inhibitory and antibacterial activities of hydrolysates produced from fermented mackerel muscle, skin, and mixed by-products using Pediococcus pentosaceus IL13, with ultrafiltration applied to enrich low-molecular-weight peptides (<3 kDa). title: Reservoir-computing-based chaos synchronization and its application to medical image encryption
abstract: Abstract Chaos synchronization provides a physically interpretable route for generating common dynamical states at spatially separated terminals, but most existing schemes require an accurate model and explicitly injected actuation. This paper develops a data-driven synchronization framework based on reservoir computing (RC) that learns nonlinear state couplings directly from observed trajectories. title: H2CHAIN: Integrated web platform for energy-balance-constrained planning of green hydrogen value chains
abstract: Planning a green hydrogen project couples siting, generation, electrolysis, storage, conversion and cost decisions that are usually assessed in separate tools. This paper presents an integrated web-based decision-support platform for the planning and analysis of green hydrogen value chains. The platform combines geospatial analysis, techno-economic modeling, and system-level scenario assessment within a modular architecture that is accessible through a standard web browser. The platform enables users to investigate alternative value-chain configurations, compare technology options, and evaluat

Institut de Recherche Dupuy de Lôme

title: Learning-Based Data-Assisted Port-Hamiltonian Control for Free-Floating Space Manipulators
abstract: A generic data-assisted control architecture within the port-Hamiltonian framework is proposed, introducing a physically meaningful observable that links conservative dynamics to all actuation, dissipation, and disturbance channels. A robust, model-based controller combined with a high-gain decentralized integrator establishes large robustness margins and strict time-scale separation, ensuring that subsequent learning cannot destabilize the primary dynamics. title: Seismic resilience of high-rise buildings: optimizing active tuned mass dampers with advanced control strategies considering soil-structure interaction
abstract: This paper investigates the seismic control of a 40-story high-rise building equipped with a Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) and an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) while considering Soil–Structure Interaction (SSI) effects. The structure is evaluated under four foundation conditions, including fixed-base, soft-soil, medium-soil, and dense-soil cases. title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
abstract: Abstract. The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for identifying and quantifying precipitation. Hence, SMLs can serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementary to conventional instruments. However, a significant challenge for opportunistic sensors, such as SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart, i.e., commercial microwave links (CMLs), stems from potential ownership issues, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. title: Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI-enabled phenotyping
abstract: Abstract Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. title: Zero-shot snow depth extraction from time-lapse imagery using vision foundation models
abstract: Automated snow depth retrieval from time-lapse cameras is constrained by site-specific annotation and manual image quality screening, thus limiting scalability across deployments. We present a fully automated, zero-annotation pipeline that integrates text-prompted segmentation for snow pole detection with a vision language model for image quality control. title: Bioash amendments from biomass energy systems reshape rhizosphere bacterial communities and reduce metal bioavailability in contaminated soils
abstract: Biomass-derived ashes (bioash) from energy production are increasingly promoted within circular bioeconomy frameworks as soil amendments that recycle nutrients and mitigate soil acidity. However, their impacts on rhizosphere bacterial communities in metal-contaminated soils (MCS) remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how four bioash types applied at three rates influence rhizosphere biogeochemistry and bacterial community dynamics of lettuce ( Lactuca sativa L.) grown in MCS. title: Environmental Sustainability and Climate Challenges in Local Urban Indonesia
abstract: This paper studies the partial relationship between environmental sustainability and climate challenges in local urban Indonesia, with an attempt to explain cross-level interaction among ecological stress, climate vulnerability as well as governance capacity taking place within medium cities of a developing country. This study attempts to provide a more integrated approach of local urban sustainability beyond the usual concerted focus on large metropolitan areas. title: Microplastics at the ‘roof of the Americas’: widespread presence in snow on Mount Aconcagua, Central Andes, Argentina
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. title: Pan-genomics in One Health: linking pathogens, hosts, and environments
abstract: The One Health approach recognizes the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health for managing global health challenges. The increasing incidence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and environmental degradation underscores the relevance of integrated surveillance strategies. In this context, pan-genomics has emerged as a valuable tool for characterizing the genetic diversity of bacterial pathogens across hosts, geographic regions, and ecological niches. title: Distribution of Microplastics in Freshwater Mussels across a Watershed
abstract: Microplastic research is an emerging field of study, and we do not yet fully understand the scope or effects of microplastic pollution. Microplastics are ubiquitous in the environment, but the field suffers from a lack of unified, accessible protocols and an ecosystems approach to evaluating microplastic contamination. During autumn 2020, we collected water, mussel, and sediment samples from five sites along the Yadkin–Pee Dee River Basin, North Carolina. title: First record of Chaetophiloscia elongata (Dollfus, 1884) from Belgium (Isopoda, Oniscidea, Philosciidae)
abstract: The Belgian terrestrial isopod fauna currently comprises 38 species, with only two from the family Philosciidae recorded until now. We report the first occurrence of Chaetophiloscia elongata (Dollfus, 1884) in Belgium, discovered in 2025 in a managed but microhabitat-rich garden in Brussels. This finding adds both a new species and genus to the Belgian fauna and represents a northward extension of the species’ known range in continental Europe, further supporting the ongoing expansion of Mediterranean isopods in anthropogenic environments outside their native range. title: Fostering Transnational Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics Education: An Exploration of Climate-Smart Practices
abstract: This paper discusses the pressing need for a transboundary approach to tackle climate change through STEM education, which is currently limited by traditional education methods. It introduces the Climate-Smart Transnational STEM Framework, encompassing seven dimensions: Cross-border Collaboration, Localised Climate Context, Innovation for Mitigation and Adaptation, Measurement and Data, Awareness and Action, Teacher Capacity, and Equity and Access. title: The roof grouting and active support technology of roadways based on stratified mining
abstract: Abstract This study aims to enhance roadway support effectiveness and construction efficiency. The study proposes a synergistic technology integrating roof grouting with active support techniques in stratified mining environments, enhanced by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms that adaptively optimize grouting parameters in real time. title: Post-use evaluation of Beijing's Second Green Belt country parks based on LSTM model analysis
abstract: The country parks in Beijing’s Second Green Belt are important to urban green space expansion and recreation. Therefore, exploring park visitors’ real needs and expectations has practical significance. Online review data and the LSTM model were used to analyze and systemically study four aspects of the country park – location layout, landscape environment, functional service, and physical and mental perception. abstract: Electrified container ports are coupled logistics–energy systems in which uncertain vessel arrivals determine berth occupancy, shore-power activation, cargo-handling intensity, and the residual demand balanced by renewable generation, battery storage, and the utility grid. This study develops a scenario-based stochastic framework linking a non-homogeneous vessel-arrival process to queue-consistent berth occupancy, congestion-responsive demand, photovoltaic and wind uncertainty, battery dispatch, and grid exchange. title: Optimal dietary glycerol monolaurate supplementation improves growth performance, antioxidant capacity, immune responses and intestinal microbiota in juvenile largemouth bass
abstract: Introduction Plant-derived functional additives have gained increasing attention as sustainable alternatives in aquafeed. This study aims to investigate the effects of dietary monolaurin on productive performance, innate immune indicators, antioxidative effects, and gut flora in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). Methods Fish were fed diets containing 0, 500, 800, 1100, and 1400 mg/kg GML for 56 days, with three replicates per treatment. abstract: The modulation of rainfall extremes by the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) over Indonesia and the Maritime Continent is well established, but less is known about how consistently this relationship is represented in documented large-scale flood-impact records. This study provides an event-based assessment of active MJO phases 3–5 on high–very high (HVH) rainfall associated with large-scale flood events across seasonal rainfall zones (ZOMs). title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
abstract: Abstract Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. title: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
abstract: Decentralized diagnostics are vital for infectious disease control, yet current point-of-care tools remain largely one-dimensional, failing to capture the multidimensional profiles required for precision management. Here, we show SID-WAVES (Smartphone-Integrated Diagnostics with Wax-encoded Amplified and Versatile Evaluation System), an intelligent, multimodal microfluidic platform. abstract: Optimization of drying parameters of periwinkles (Turritella communis) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain high quality product, it is very vital as improper drying conditions can affect the composition of the dried Periwinkles and thereby increases the risk of it running into deterioration of the nutrient contents of the product and post-harvest loss. abstract: ABSTRACT This article proposes a novel and practical prescribed time control (PPTC) method for strict feedback nonlinear systems (SFNSs) subject to input saturation and sensor faults. This method fills the research gap in existing literature, which only addresses a single constraint (either input saturation or sensor faults) rather than their simultaneous occurrence. title: Predictive Modeling Techniques for Forecasting Emergency Department Overcrowding and Resource Needs in United States Public Hospitals
abstract: In the United States, emergency department congestion stealthily undermines the safety net of public hospitals for uninsured, underinsured, and medically complex populations, and the use of forecasting tools is limited where it is desired most. title: Scale‐space image analysis for mapping spotted knapweed in grassland ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Premise This study investigates the value of scale‐space representations of spatial features for the identification and mapping of invasive plants using high‐resolution multispectral imagery. Scale‐space representations combine the two‐dimensional spatial domain with a third dimension representing spatial scale, such that features can be represented across both space and image spatial resolution. abstract: Introduction Improving livelihood adaptation outcomes are crucial for relocated households to achieve sustainable development and consolidate poverty alleviation gains. Methods Using survey data from relocated households in karst mountainous areas, this study constructs a multidimensional livelihood adaptation outcomes index via the CRITIC method and combines OPGD and fsQCA to examine associated factors and configurational patterns. title: Hydrodynamic and ecological modeling for water quality assessment in Lake Qaroun, Egypt
abstract: Abstract Qaroun Lake, a closed salty lake in the Fayoum depression of Egypt, is an important natural resource that supports fishing, wildlife, and local communities. It mainly receives water from a dense drainage network, with some possible small contribution from groundwater. Since it has no outlet and loses water only through evaporation, its salinity keeps increasing. Any change in the amount or quality of incoming water strongly affects the lake’s environment. title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
abstract: Streams and rivers are major contributors to global emissions of carbon dioxide and methane, yet seasonal hydrological variability in discharge and river surface area is often not fully represented in large-scale emission estimates. Here, we integrate riverine and dry riverbed carbon dioxide and methane data with geospatial data of the Australian drainage network to predict emissions at a monthly time-step. title: A meteorological big data-driven method for generating chaotic time-series curves of power supply loads for wind-solar-storage hybrid systems
abstract: The wind-solar-storage hybrid system represents an efficient and clean energy supply mode. However, its power supply load is influenced by multiple factors and exhibits complex chaotic time-series characteristics, which pose significant challenges to system operation scheduling and load forecasting. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method for generating chaotic time-series curves of the power supply load in such hybrid systems based on meteorological big data. title: Identification of optimal ERA5 model level for wind resource assessments in mountainous terrain
abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of hub-height wind speed is crucial for wind resources assessment at prospective sites. Traditionally, long-term wind speed series are derived from short-term site observations combined with reanalysis products, most commonly the ERA5 single-level data at 10 m and 100 m heights. However, the coarse spatial resolution of ERA5 limits their reliability in complex mountainous regions, leading to weak correlations with local wind measurements due to not adequately resolved near-surface flow. title: The System Hallucination Scale (SHS): A Human-Centered Instrument for Assessing Perceived Reliability of Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models routinely produce factually incorrect or misleading outputs, yet conventional automated benchmarks overlook how users perceive reliability during interaction. We introduce the System Hallucination Scale (SHS), a lightweight instrument modeling the famous System Usability Scale (SUS) and System Causability Scales (SCS). abstract: Abstract. This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. title: A 256-year daily rainfall record reveals multiscale rainy-season variability and emerging hydroclimatic hazard over northern East Asia
abstract: Monsoon rainy seasons shape water supply and flood hazard across northern East Asia, but their long-term variability remains poorly understood because few daily rainfall records extend beyond the instrumental era. Here, we reconstruct rainy-season onset, retreat, and duration from a 256-year daily precipitation record for Seoul (1770-2025), providing an unusually long view of seasonal monsoon behavior. abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces a standard specification that defines how Foundation Model (FM)-based agents should interact with external systems by invoking tools. However, to understand a tool’s purpose and features, FMs rely on natural-language tool descriptions, making these descriptions a critical component in guiding FMs to select the optimal tool for a given (sub)task and to pass the right arguments to the tool. title: A Gateway-Based Approach for Integrating Digital Compass Data into Controller Area Network (CAN) in Precision Farming Systems
abstract: The integration of high precision orientation sensors into resilient communication infrastructures is a key requirement for next-generation autonomous systems. Digital compass sensors typically generate data in the NMEA format, whereas distributed control architectures in mobile robotics predominantly utilize the CAN 2.0B protocol. This study presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based hardware-software gateway that enables seamless interoperability between these heterogeneous communication standards within autonomous agricultural platforms. title: Sampling-based integrated design optimization of floating wind turbine substructures with Pywind
abstract: Abstract Design optimization of floating wind turbine (FWT) substructures remains computationally demanding due to the extensive time-domain simulations required to explore high-dimensional design spaces. This study builds upon the previously developed Pywind-based integrated design optimization (IDO) framework, extending it by comparing two sampling strategies: Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Maximin LHS. abstract: Abstract. Heat has emerged as a major public health concern. Over 62,000 heat-related deaths were estimated to have occurred during the European summer of 2024, exemplifying the pressing need to develop effective early warning systems. Such systems depend critically on the quality of the underlying forecasts, and recent work has focused on developing impact-based forecasts for heat-related mortality, which provide impact-oriented information. title: Fault detection filter design for unmanned surface vehicle systems via an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol under deception attacks
abstract: This paper focuses on the fault detection filter problem for unmanned surface vehicle systems via an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol under deception attacks. Taking into account factors such as external disturbances and potential system faults, a motion model for the unmanned surface vehicle system in a complex environment is constructed. abstract: This study aimed to investigate the seafood consumption behaviors of university students and the factors influencing these behaviors. The study was conducted with 118 students, and the relationships between consumption frequency, reasons for consumption, reasons for non-consumption, purchasing preferences, and demographic variables were analyzed. title: Evaluating alternative trade network configurations under geopolitical risk: a multi-scale systems approach
abstract: Rising geopolitical risks and supply-chain disruptions have increased interest in transport-network diversification and alternative connectivity systems. This article presents a scenario-based comparison between a traditional maritime chokepoint configuration centered on the Strait of Hormuz and a prospective diversified multimodal corridor connecting the Middle East and Europe. abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimation from satellite-derived Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is often biased in humid tropical environments because aerosol water uptake enhances optical extinction without a corresponding increase in dry particulate mass. This study develops a physics-informed, non-linear AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion framework that explicitly accounts for hygroscopic growth. journal: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability

title: Manta ray foraging optimization algorithm with dynamic penalty function and chaos switching factor to solve combined economic emission dispatch problem
abstract: The Combined Economic and Emission Dispatch (CEED) problem plays a vital role in balancing energy efficiency and environmental protection. To address its multi-objective characteristics, this paper proposes an improved Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MRFO) algorithm. It introduces a chaotic switching factor to dynamically regulate the transition between exploration and exploitation phases, thereby enhancing global search capability. In addition, a dynamic penalty function is developed to adaptively handle constraint violations, offering greater flexibility and robustness compared with convent
institutions: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

title: IMU- and LSTM-CNN-based multi-gait recognition for a lower limb exoskeleton
abstract: This study presents a platform-specific and subject-independent validation of an IMU-based LSTM-CNN gait-recognition pipeline on a self-developed lower-limb exoskeleton. Ten healthy participants performed five locomotion modes, including level walking, stair ascent, stair descent, standing up, and sitting down. Each participant completed five level-walking trials and ten trials for each of the remaining four locomotion modes, resulting in 450 original recording trials. IMU signals collected from the thigh, shank, and foot were segmented using a 128-sample sliding window with a 64-sample step.

title: Management of headwater catchments: cultural background, science and policy
abstract: Headwater catchments serve as water towers and initial regulatory buffers against hydrometeorological hazards, yet they face several forms of degradation from unsustainable land use and accelerating climate change. We argue that effective headwater control requires an integrated approach combining watershed governance, science, policy, and cultural background. Old societies showed considerable capacity to solve hydraulic problems but did not fully understand watershed runoff formation and downstream impacts. title: Toponymic knowledge infrastructures in five-state Middle Asia: linguistic transformation, manuscript cartography, and historical-geographical reconstruction
abstract: Toponymic records embedded in Arabic, Persian, and Chinese manuscript traditions provide evidence for reconstructing the historical geographies of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. This review uses a structured narrative and conceptual-synthesis methodology to compare place-name transmission across languages, scripts, manuscript genres, and political regimes. title: Emerging Hydroclimatic Signals of Global Climate Change in Equatorial Indonesia: Evidence from Borneo Island
abstract: Global climate change has become an increasingly pressing environmental issue, with significant impacts on atmospheric, hydrological, and ecological systems across the globe. Borneo Island is a strategic region for climate change studies, given its extensive tropical forest cover, peatland presence, and rapid land-use changes due to human activities such as deforestation and oil palm plantation expansion. These changes not only affect local conditions but can also amplify feedbacks to the regional climate system through changes in evapotranspiration, albedo, and the hydrological cycle. This st

title: A generative diffusion framework for physically consistent 3D turbulence
abstract: Abstract Synthesizing fully developed three-dimensional turbulence remains a long-standing problem in fluid mechanics and an open challenge for generative modeling. This difficulty arises from extreme dimensionality, multiscale fluctuations, strong intermittency, and the need to satisfy exact physical constraints, including incompressibility and prescribed mass and momentum fluxes under given boundary conditions. title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. title: From resource orchestration to robustness and resilience: the role of data analytics capability in bulk commodity maritime supply chains
abstract: Introduction Bulk commodity maritime supply chains are increasingly exposed to climate-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions, port congestion, transportation uncertainty, and other external shocks. However, limited attention has been paid to how firms transform dispersed supply chain resources into capabilities that support both disruption resistance and recovery. title: Investigation of the effect of albatross bill impact on CFRP and GFRP wind turbine blades using Diomedea exulans collision scenarios
abstract: Wind turbine blades are highly vulnerable to damage from transverse loads such as bird collisions, which can compromise structural integrity, reduce aerodynamic efficiency, and raise ecological concerns. This study employed finite element simulations in Abaqus Explicit to examine the collision of a Diomedea exulans (wandering albatross) bill with Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) and Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) blades. The albatross bill was modelled in two configurations: a shell model representing the realistic hollow, lightweight anatomy based on β-keratin properties, and a s

title: A comprehensive comparison of single- and composite-seaweed feeds on growth performance, lipid metabolism, and immune function of large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea)
abstract: Introduction The large yellow croaker ( Larimichthys crocea ) is an economically important fish species in China, yet its quality and value are compromised by excessive fat deposition induced by high-fat diets under high-density aquaculture. Our previous study noted the lipid-regulating potential of individual seaweed components like fucoidan and kelp ( Saccharina japonica ) powder, the synergistic effects of composite seaweed feeds remain underexplored. title: Contributing to SDGs 9, 16, and 17: Unveiling the Role of Supply Chain Analytics, Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management and Trust
abstract: ABSTRACT The primary objective of this study is to explore the relationships between supply chain (SC) analytics, cybersecurity supply chain risk management (C‐SCRM), SC trust, and Sustainable Development goals (SDGs) in a sample of Jordanian pharmaceutical SCs, considered an emerging country. To test the aforementioned relationships, a conceptual research model was designed to frame these relationships based on both information processing theory (IPT) and dynamic capabilities view (DCV). title: Antioxidant, Cholinesterase-Inhibitory, and Antiproliferative Potential of Sparganium erectum Extracts
abstract: In the present study, the antioxidant capacity, cholinesterase-inhibitory activity, and antiproliferative effects of Sparganium erectum extracts were investigated. Antioxidant analyses showed that the ethanol extract had a total antioxidant status (TAS) of 2.925±0.023 mmol/L, a total oxidant status (TOS) of 10.116±0.042 µmol/L, and an oxidative stress index (OSI) of 0.346±0.003. For the methanol extract, these values were recorded as 2.491±0.039 mmol/L, 12.889±0.056 µmol/L, and 0.517±0.006, respectively. journal: International Journal of Chemistry and Technology

title: Spatial differentiation and potential influencing factors of land-surface heat exposure based on street-view imagery: a case study of Luolong District, Luoyang
abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent extreme heat events, mitigating land-surface heat exposure on urban streets is crucial for safeguarding public health. Existing studies have often overlooked the spatially differentiated effects of complex street environments on land-surface heat exposure and the associated cooling thresholds. Therefore, this study takes Luolong District, Luoyang, as a case study to investigate the spatially heterogeneous effects and nonlinear threshold characteristics of street-view metrics on land-surface heat exposure. title: Modeling Hydrogen Fuel Cell of High-Speed Passenger Ship by Using Simulink
abstract: The maritime industry is under increasing pressure from environmental regulations, and therefore, it is required to provide energy solutions that comply with sustainable practices immediately. The study conducted by the researchers indicates the creation of a hydrogen fuel cell model that is designed specifically for the MATLAB Simulink high-speed passenger vessels. A detailed analysis sketch is laid out, which shows the design and simulation of the Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) system, displaying the emission reduction effect of this technology. title: Physicochemical and microbiological qualities of shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) coated with pectin incorporated with green tea spent extract during refrigerated storage
abstract: This study developed and characterized a pectin (PEC) based coating incorporated with green tea spent extract (GTSE) and/or nisin. Further, Pacific white shrimp were treated with the developed coating and investigated for physicochemical, textural, microbial, and melanosis formation during refrigerated storage for 12 days. Among the four coating solutions, PEC-2 had higher homogeneity (583.6 nm) and antioxidant activity (DPPH: 76.73% and ABTS: 70.95%). Shrimp coated with PEC-4 showed higher quality parameters, maintaining pH (7.12), minimizing weight loss (5.07%), preserving textural integrity
journal: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis

title: Development and physico-mechanical characterization of epoxy matrix biocomposite reinforced with multi-short Cynara scolymus fibers
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the development and physico-mechanical evaluation of an epoxy matrix biocomposite reinforced with multi-short Cynara Scolymus fibers of lengths 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 cm, in a bid to bridge the gap in studies conducted in the millimeter scale and to statistically validate the results obtained. title: Advancements in Applied Food Biotechnology: Integrated Approaches in Biopreservatives, and Probiotic Delivery Systems, Two Years of Journal Experience
abstract: Background and Aim: Faced with rising antimicrobial resistance, environmental concerns, and growing consumer demand for clean-label food products, applied food biotechnology plays a pivotal role in establishing sustainable, resilient, and health-oriented food networks. This manuscript synthesizes recent advancements across three interconnected domains: natural antimicrobials, industrial fermentation, and probiotic delivery systems. title: Antibiotics in aquatic environments: A review of occurrence, fate, ecotoxicity and advanced removal technologies
abstract: Antibiotics are among the most widely distributed contaminants of emerging concern in aquatic systems, entering water from hospital effluent, pharmaceutical manufacturing, livestock production, aquaculture and municipal sewage. Their principal hazard is not acute toxicity but sub-inhibitory selective pressure, which enriches antibiotic resistance genes and drives their horizontal transfer at concentrations of nanograms per litre. title: Microplastics and nanoplastics as potential ecological oncogenic co-drivers: rewiring host–microbe interactions in cancer
abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are increasingly recognized as biologically active interfaces that may reshape host–microbe interactions in carcinogenesis. This review proposes a hypothesis-generating mechanistic framework in which MPs/NPs may influence cancer-related processes through the integration of environmental exposure, epithelial barrier disruption, immune dysregulation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling. title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in the Utilization and Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation and Flutter: a State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Catheter ablation (CA) has become a first-line option for rhythm control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL). We synthesize recent evidence regarding racial and ethnic disparities in CA utilization in the United States and examine the structural mechanism driving them. title: MilsPD: a lightweight multiphysics-integrated peridynamics solver
abstract: Abstract This paper presents MilsPD, a highly efficient multiphysics-integrated peridynamics (PD) solver designed for fracture mechanics applications. It addresses a key computational challenge in the field: the expensive simulation of large-scale multiphysics problems involving evolving fractures and fluid–solid interactions. Central to its performance is a set of fused multiphysics algorithms that update both coupled thermo-mechanical and thermo-hydrodynamic governing equations in optimized passes over material points. title: A unified pipeline for traffic sign detection using resolution aware dataset reduction
abstract: Abstract Robust traffic sign detection is an important factor of safe autonomous driving, allowing vehicles to accurately interpret and comply with dynamic road regulations. However, real world deployment remains heavily challenged by distant, extra-small signs, as well as partial occlusions from trees, structures, or other vehicles. While optimizing training datasets through size reduction can dramatically lower computational overhead and storage footprints, conventional pruning methods often discard critical spatial features, severely degrading model accuracy. title: Global emergence of begomoviruses in cucurbits: diversity, epidemiology, and management strategies
abstract: The rapid spread of begomoviruses (family Geminiviridae) threatens global cucurbit production, yet the drivers of their emergence and the readiness of management strategies remain poorly integrated. This review synthesizes current understanding of cucurbit-infecting begomoviruses, contrasting the intercontinental spread of key Old World viruses, particularly Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV), with persistent New World complexes such as Squash leaf curl virus (SLCV) and Cucurbit leaf crumple virus (CuLCrV). title: Beyond single-element toxicity: chromium-salinity interactions, food-chain transfer and mitigation in sugarcane agroecosystems
abstract: Chromium contamination in sugarcane soils is often combined with co-metals and salinity caused by tannery effluent, electroplating effluent, paper mill wastewater, vinasse fertigation and filter cake. Hence, single element toxicity assessment does not provide realistic assessment of its exposure. The present review summarizes research on chromium behaviour along the soil, root, stalk and cane juice in sugarcane. title: Rediscovery of a type specimen of Plehnia arctica (Plehn, 1896) (Polycladida, Plehniidae) described by Marianne Plehn, a pioneering woman in German zoology
abstract: The rediscovered type specimen of the polyclad flatworm Plehnia arctica (Plehn, 1896), collected during Kükenthal’s 1889 Spitzbergen expedition and presumed lost for more than a century, was rediscovered in the collection of the Phyletisches Museum Jena (PMJ). The specimen was reexamined and compared with Plehn’s original description. High-resolution images of the type specimen were taken for the first time, and a short historical overview of Marianne Plehn, the first female professor in Bavaria, as well as of the expedition of Kükenthal and Walter to Spitzbergen (Norway), is provided. title: Aplicación móvil basada en visión artificial y regresión lineal para el reconocimiento del estado de madurez y el pronóstico de rendimiento en cultivos de cacao (Theobroma cacao L): estudio de caso en la Finca Mendoza, Ecuador
abstract: Introducción: La determinación del grado de madurez del fruto y la estimación del rendimiento en fincas cacaoteras de Ecuador suele realizarse mediante observación empírica y registros manuales, lo que genera apreciaciones subjetivas, errores operativos y ausencia de información histórica sistematizada. Frente a esta problemática, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo desarrollar y evaluar funcionalmente una aplicación móvil que integrara visión artificial y un modelo predictivo para el reconocimiento del estado de madurez del cacao y el pronóstico de rendimiento en la Finca Mendoza, Ecuador.
journal: Journal of Multidisciplinary Novel Journeys & Explorations

title: Hydration, mechanical, and environmental performance of blended cements incorporating ground granulated blast furnace slag, ground waste bottle glass, and metakaolin
abstract: This study investigates the effect of incorporating 20 wt% ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), ground waste bottle glass (GWBG) and metakaolin (MK) on the hydration behavior, mechanical and environmental performance of blended cements cured at 23 °C ± 2 °C for 7, 28, and 90 days. title: The neglected role of knowledge organization in disaster risk management: A scoping review
abstract: Knowledge plays an important role in Disaster Risk Management (DRM). However, although processes of organization, representation, classification, retrieval, and sharing are widely mobilized in this field, their relationship with Knowledge Organization (KO) remains insufficiently explicit and is frequently addressed from the perspectives of Knowledge Management (KM), Information Management (IM), and technological solutions. title: Integrating images, sounds, citizen science and AI to assess the biodiversity of the Atlantic Forest of Brazil
abstract: The Atlantic Forest is an endangered biome in Brazil with only 15% of its area remaining. Although it is reported that it has a high biodiversity and many endemic species, the biological composition of its territory remains largely unknown. Citizen science can speed up the description of the living organisms present in this biome and at the same time increase citizens' perception of the importance of the conservation of this endangered tropical ecosystem. title: Halal Tourism Development Strategy in Pontianak City: Potentials, Disparities, and Urban Islamic Tourism
abstract: Halal tourism studies in Indonesia have largely focused on Sharia-compliant services, such as halal food, worship facilities, and religious tourism, while the development of urban Islamic tourism remains relatively limited. This study analyzes the development of halal tourism through an urban Islamic tourism approach in Pontianak City. title: UAV close-range photogrammetry combined with adaptive octree-based point cloud filtering for rock joint extraction of open-pit mine slopes
abstract: Abstract Manual joint surveys on open-pit mine slopes are high-risk and inefficient, whereas conventional remote sensing and laser scanning are costly and limited in fine-crack detection. title: Nutritional, Physicochemical and Sensory Evaluation of Geblek, a Traditional Food from Kulon Progo Regency Enriched with Ulva sp. from Gunungkidul Coast
abstract: Geblek is a traditional cassava-based snack from Kulon Progo, Yogyakarta, that generally has limited nutritional value because of its relatively simple ingredient composition. Ulva sp., a green seaweed, contains macro- and micronutrients, antioxidants, and other bioactive compounds, making it a potential functional food ingredient. title: Ecosystem health and its constraint transitions in Plateau cities: insights from Lhasa, China
abstract: Abstract High-altitude urban ecosystems are exposed to pronounced ecological vulnerability and increasing human pressures. Existing assessments have primarily characterized overall health status and its spatiotemporal variation, whereas temporal changes in the configuration of underlying constraints have received less attention. As the capital of the Xizang Autonomous Region of China, Lhasa’s unique geographic and climatic setting on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau poses distinctive challenges for ecosystem health assessment. abstract: The replacement of internal combustion engine (ICE) with electric motor by electric vehicles (EVs) technology is one of the most comprehensive transition in the automotive industry for recent decades. EVs technology causes fundamental changes in vehicle architecture and dynamics including increased overall weight due to battery packs, altered torque delivery, and regenerative braking systems.
