title: A multi-measure adaptation method for temporal coordination under drought–flood transition risks
abstract: Rapid drought–flood transitions create short-term conflicts between drought mitigation and flood-control measures, while fixed decision modes may not adapt as risk evolves. This study develops a prediction–decision coupling framework that integrates Transformer-based precipitation forecasting with the NK model to evaluate the synergistic performance of DRR measure portfolios under evolving risks. title: Low cost energy harvesting systems for smart sensing and Internet of Things applications
abstract: The increasing proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor networks (WSN), wearable electronics, and smart sensing platforms have intensified the demand for sustainable and maintenance-free power sources. Energy harvesting has emerged as a promising solution to replace or complement traditional batteries by converting ambient energy into usable electrical power. title: Climate risk, uneven development, and threshold-dependent tourism resilience in selected cities of western China
abstract: Abstract Climate risk and socioeconomic development are increasingly reshaping tourism resilience, particularly in climate-sensitive and unevenly developed regions. Yet how climate risk and economic development jointly influence tourism, and how these effects vary across regions, remains insufficiently understood. abstract: This study presents a synthetic proof-of-concept surrogate-assisted simulation–optimisation framework for identifying potentially mineralised locations using groundwater copper-isotope observations. The methodology adapts established groundwater contaminant-source characterisation principles, in which unknown source release histories are reconstructed from down gradient concentration measurements, to the investigation of concealed copper mineralisation. abstract: The olive tree is one of the most important crops in the world, but even more, one of the most identitarian plant for the countries of the Mediterranean basin. In this article, the vast consultation of scientific literature, archaeological, historical and anecdotal sources, allowed to outline a global reasoned vision on the olive origin, its spread during early history and how olive fruit fly may represent as proxy for tracing its early diffusion. title: Q-rung orthopair fuzzy framework for multimodal MRI image fusion and U-Net-based segmentation for brain tumor detection
abstract: Introduction Medical image analysis is a significant research domain in contemporary healthcare systems, which helps to accurately diagnose diseases and support clinical decision-making. This domain consists of important operations, including image enhancement, fusion, segmentation, morphological processing, and denoising, which assist in the effective understanding of complex biomedical information. title: The EU's Indo‐Pacific Strategy and South Korea: Convergence, Perceptions, and Prospects for Strategic Cooperation
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the evolving European Union–South Korea relationship through the framework of the EU's Indo‐Pacific Strategy (IPS). Drawing on interviews with policymakers, officials, and influencers, it traces six decades of bilateral ties, highlighting Korea's 2022 IPS and its convergence with EU priorities in digital governance, green transition, and sustainability. title: Coupling of VIIRS and Sentinel-2 observations to generate Landsat-scale TIR imagery for estimating landscape evapotranspiration using the Simplified Surface Energy Balance (SSEB) model
abstract: : Satellite thermal infrared (TIR) data are essential for remote sensing of energy exchange processes at the Earth-atmosphere interface. Current satellite sensors are subject to a trade-off between spatial resolution and temporal coverage. Daily TIR observations from MODIS and VIIRS are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of ∼400–1000 m, whereas higher-resolution Landsat TIRS observations (∼100 m) provide infrequent temporal coverage (∼8 days). Downscaling methods that correlate TIR imagery with higher-resolution multispectral data can improve the availability of fine-scale TIR observations.

title: Linearised metamodel for two-dimensional sloshing effects in partially-filled rectangular tanks under horizontal excitation
abstract: Sloshing dynamics in partially-filled rectangular tanks remains a computationally demanding phenomenon in applications such as tuned liquid dampers, largely due to high computational costs of using high-fidelity sloshing models. Additionally, the effective damping of coupled dynamic systems is challenging to describe with existent equivalent or reduced-order sloshing models. abstract: Abstract Quantifying the structure and heterogeneity of complex spatial patterns remains a key challenge in spatial data analysis. Recurrence plots (RPs) offer a powerful method for visualizing the recurrent spatial patterns in such data. abstract: Interdisciplinary approaches can create opportunities for connecting scientific observation with artistic interpretation and environmental communication. abstract: Abstract Diffusion models and flow-based models have recently become the dominant paradigms in generative modeling, largely due to their ability to learn rich, multi-level visual representations through large-scale training. This creates a bidirectional relationship between generative models and representation learning: improving representation learning enhances generation quality, while the learned representations can be leveraged for broader understanding tasks. abstract: The use of biomass has the potential to improve the mechanical characteristics of cement-based composites. abstract: Real time observation of students' exercise load is very important for scientific sports teaching and injury prevention. abstract: Most of the sand and aggregate used for construction in mid-western Nepal comes from the rivers of the Bheri basin in Surkhet District. title: Evaluation of sheep and goat farming systems in Fiji and Samoa through farm typology analysis
abstract: Small ruminant production supports rural livelihoods in Pacific Island countries, yet limited information exists on the production-system diversity and reported production constraints. This study aimed to characterize small ruminant production systems in Fiji and Samoa, identify constraints to production, and develop a classification tool to support targeted interventions. abstract: In recent years environmental management has been raised to a new level in the context of cultural heritage sites. Climate change, urbanization, mass tourism, and limited institutional resources and management capacities are the most pressing challenges facing cultural heritage today. abstract: Abstract In mining metal deposits, blasting fragmentation is a key indicator that directly affects production efficiency and economic costs. To address the limitations of current post-blast assessment, which overlooks the intrinsic relationship between in-situ fragmentation (geological characterization of in-situ rock mass discontinuities) and the resulting blasting fragmentation, this paper proposes a quantitative prediction model and methodology for blasting fragmentation. abstract: For decades, plant biology has relied on a narrow set of classical model organisms—such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays —to uncover core physiological, developmental, and molecular pathways. abstract: ABSTRACT Agricultural mechanization (AM) plays a critical role in agricultural modernization, influencing productivity, resource use, and environmental sustainability; however, its overall contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Understanding the effects of temperature variations on pollutant dynamics is crucial for enhancing the accuracy of simulations of contaminant transport under climate change scenarios and groundwater protection. abstract: Oral ulcer healing is hindered by the slow formation, weak adhesion, and limited protection of the native pseudomembrane. abstract: Reliable rock-mass characterization in structurally complex terrain requires spatial information beyond conventional drilling and surface mapping. abstract: Satellite data is increasingly being used as a basis for operational crop monitoring. However, satellite technologies for monitoring perennial crops remain underdeveloped. abstract: Health tourism (HT) is an umbrella domain encompassing medical tourism and wellness tourism. title: Innovative fat modification technologies in meat products for improved nutritional quality and sensory performance
abstract: A strategic research focus on fat modification in meat products aims to improve nutritional quality and lower health hazards related to consumption of cholesterol and saturated fat. The high percentage of animal fat found in conventional meat products is linked to a higher risk of metabolic disorders such as obesity, atherosclerosis, and cardiometabolic syndrome. title: An atlas of alien-dominated vegetation in Italy
abstract: In this study, we reviewed the distribution of alien-dominated and co-dominated plant communities in Italy. abstract: Abstract Intermodal freight transport represents a critical strategy in the hub location problem (HLP) to reduce operational costs. Although the integration of container consolidation strategies and additional operational modules within intermodal networks presents novel operational challenges that increase vulnerability to disruptions, it has not been thoroughly examined in the literature. title: Polarization‐Multiplexed Double‐Helix/Airy Metalens for Depth‐Resolved Texture Imaging With Extended Depth‐of‐Field
abstract: Simultaneously acquiring high-fidelity texture and reliable depth cues over an extended working range remains a central challenge for compact passive imaging systems. Conventional point-spread-function (PSF)-engineered optics usually rely on a single optical response to perform both axial encoding and image formation, creating an inherent trade-off between depth discriminability and lateral image quality. title: Wettability alteration of CO2-water-shale system: state of the art and future directions
abstract: Wettability serves as a fundamental petrophysical property governing hydrocarbon recovery efficiency and determining the geological storage security of injected CO 2 within shale formations. This work systematically reviews the recent advances in wettability alteration (WA) of shale induced by CO 2 flooding. title: Enhancing resilience in complex systems through transdisciplinary approaches to sustainable infrastructure and urban development
abstract: Abstract Urban resilience is a critical challenge amidst escalating risks of climate change, rapid urbanization, and systemic disruption, particularly in the Global South. This research seeks to fill a gap in the literature that often overlooks the institutional and relational mechanisms that generate adaptive capacity. Using an exploratory qualitative case study design, this research compares resilience dynamics in Shenzhen (high resilience), Bandung (medium resilience), and Dhaka (low resilience). title: Prediction of HIV incidence in Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, China: a time series study
abstract: Objective In China, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region has a high incidence of HIV, and the situation regarding its prevention and control remains challenging. This study aimed to compare the predictive performance of three time series models, SARIMAX (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors), Prophet with exogenous variables, and random forest, using rolling validation, and to provide references for HIV prevention and control in Xinjiang. abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a kinetically demanding anodic process in water electrolysis and related electrochemical energy-conversion systems. Its multistep proton-coupled electron-transfer kinetics and catalyst degradation under strongly oxidizing conditions limit overall efficiency and durability. title: Nanoparticle Fabrication and Optimization: From Green Chemistry to Transformative Applications in Life Sciences, Medicine, and Public Health
abstract: Nanotechnology has changed many fields by allowing scientists to work with matter at the atomic and molecular levels. NPs including metal (e.g., Ag, Au), metal oxide (e.g., ZnO, FeO), polymeric (e.g., PLGA), and carbon-based (e.g., carbon nanotubes), have special chemical, biological, and physical properties. This review paper discusses a lot of detail about making and improving nanoparticles, guided by the 12 principles of green chemistry ideas to make sure they are safe for living things and last for a long time. Traditional synthesis methods, employ toxic chemicals and use a lot of energy.

abstract: La escasez de documentos etiquetados limita la clasificación automática de documentos y eleva los costos de etiquetado. En este contexto, el aprendizaje semi-supervisado (SSL) constituye una alternativa viable; sin embargo, la selección de modelos adecuados se dificulta por la ausencia de análisis comparativos que evidencien sus fortalezas y limitaciones. Este trabajo presenta dos aportes principales. title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial en la detección automática de errores en el código fuente
abstract: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar cómo la IA ha mejorado los procesos de desarrollo de software, resaltando sus beneficios, limitaciones y herramientas utilizadas. Metodológicamente se empleó un enfoque cualitativo basado en la revisión de literatura académica publicada en los últimos cinco años, considerando fuentes reconocidas en el ámbito tecnológico. Los resultados indican que la IA ha optimizado la detección de errores mediante técnicas de aprendizaje automático y análisis estático, reduciendo falsos positivos y mejorando la calidad del código. title: Gas Turbine Propulsion Systems for Naval Vessels: Energy Flow Calculation Methodology and HighPressure Rotor CFD Simulation
abstract: This paper addresses the modernization of naval propulsion systems through the adoption of gas turbine technology, with emphasis on thermodynamic calculation methodology and rotor flow simulation. The study is centred on the Rolls Royce gas turbine, employed in naval propulsion applications and covers all thermodynamic states from atmospheric air intake through the two-stage compression process, combustion chamber, high-pressure and lowpressure turbine stages, to the power turbine exhaust. title: Topology-aware and constraint-guided deep reinforcement learning for climate-resilient control of urban stormwater systems
abstract: Introduction Urban stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by extreme precipitation events, leading to hydraulic surcharge when system capacity is exceeded. Traditional rule-based control (RBC) is reactive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) does not explicitly exploit drainage‐network topology or ensure physically consistent control. This study introduces Constraint-guided Graph-PPO (PIG‐PPO), a topology‐aware reinforcement learning framework designed to improve stormwater control under extreme precipitation conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfur leaching from metal sulfide electrocatalysts undermines formate intermediate stability during CO 2 reduction, yet existing protection strategies remain static. abstract: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. abstract: Exploring strain-specific differences in bacterial vaterite biomineralization can supplement the basic theoretical research of biomineralization and reveal the biogeochemical linkages between microbially induced carbonate formation and in-situ pollutant sequestration in soil environments. In this study, Bacillus velezensis LB002 and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 were used as representative bacterial strains to compare strain-dependent vaterite formation and pollutant sequestration behavior. title: A chronological framework for atherosclerosis: from environmental pressure to clinical disease, with vascular aging as a cross-cutting dimension
abstract: Atherosclerosis is a multiphase disease, yet contemporary cardiovascular risk stratification relies predominantly on calculators that estimate event probability within a limited pathophysiological window. Framingham, SCORE2, GLOBORISK and PREVENT capture lipid burden, metabolic parameters, and renal function, but they do not organize the chronological sequence of atherogenesis, assign measurable biomarkers to each stage, or integrate vascular aging. title: Thailand Land Surface Temperature Variation and Forecasting
abstract: Climate change has emerged as a global challenge, influenced by human activities, industrial operations and energy systems that depend on non-renewable energy such as carbon, gas, and petroleum. These activities have contributed to long-term shifts in temperature and broader climatic conditions. Land Surface Temperature (LST) has become an important standard for informing weather-related strategies at regional scales. title: Forest green-up in the Pearl River Basin: trends, driving factors, and relationships with net primary productivity
abstract: The spring green-up date (GUD), a critical indicator of ecosystem response to climate change, profoundly influences terrestrial productivity. However, the complex drivers of GUD remain elusive, while the contentious relationship between GUD and net primary productivity (NPP) challenges the universal validity of the hypothesis that earlier green-up enhances productivity. abstract: Wind farm maintenance scheduling is a challenging sequential decision-making problem due to the dynamic operational environment, multi-objective optimization requirements, and complex dependencies among turbine states, maintenance resources, and future power generation dynamics. Existing optimization and deep reinforcement learning methods often suffer from limited interpretability and insufficient capability in proactively balancing energy production efficiency and output stability. abstract: Abstract The biodegradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), a major commodity polymer, has become a core focus of multidisciplinary research. title: Toward Mechanical Intelligence in Robotics
abstract: Conventional robotic systems concentrate sensing, control, and actuation in electronic hardware, creating constraints in harsh environments, energy efficiency, and miniaturization. The physical body of a robot is more than a passive executor of control commands; it is an active substrate that transforms inputs into functional operations through its intrinsic mechanical dynamics. abstract: Abstract. Geosciences are often described as interdisciplinary, yet research and training remain fragmented across sub-disciplines and institutions. To understand how early career scientists (ECS) experience and practice interdisciplinarity, and which support structures actually help, we conducted an online survey within the German Geo.X research network. abstract: Atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) remains a major global health risk, with its associated health burden continuing to rise despite decades of pollution control efforts. Air pollution studies often focus on particle levels and known toxins, missing hidden organics that may drive serious health risks. title: Realising the potential of ecological digital twins as decision support tools
abstract: Ecological digital twins are continually updating models used for decision-making. Current progress in ecological digital twinning has focused on overcoming the technological and modelling challenges to create a continually updating system. We argue that attention should now also focus on effectively integrating digital twins into decision-making systems to inform timely action. abstract: Mediterranean maquis ecosystems of North Africa harbor unique fauna, but their herpetofaunal diversity remains poorly documented despite increasing anthropogenic pressures and habitat fragmentation. In this study, we conducted field surveys across nine one-kilometer transects spanning natural, rural, and urban landscapes along an elevational gradient (175-1245 m) in the Chréa National Park, Tell Atlas, Algeria. abstract: El objetivo de la investigación fue diseñar una solución basada en aprendizaje automático para optimizar rutas logísticas y mejorar la predicción de demanda de transporte. Se analizaron los requerimientos de cinco empresas comerciales y se estudiaron sus datos históricos de 12 meses para el diseño de la solución. abstract: Abstract Background Liver biopsy has traditionally been regarded as the reference standard for evaluating chronic liver disease because it provides direct tissue-level assessment of necroinflammatory activity, fibrosis, architectural remodeling, and disease-specific patterns of injury. abstract: Transcriptomics is moving beyond gene-level quantification toward isoform-resolved interrogation of alternative splicing, transcript structural variation, and repeat-derived transcription. abstract: Understanding soil water content dynamics under saline conditions remains a major challenge for effective soil and water management in agricultural systems. This study aimed to optimize the correction of soil water content measurements obtained from gypsum blocks under the combined effects of salinity and matric suction using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). abstract: This study empirically investigates how safety culture, customer relationship management (CRM), and quality management jointly drive organizational effectiveness within Thailand’s maritime transport sector. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) theoretical framework, the research examines these vital intangible capabilities as synergistic drivers of sustained competitive advantage. abstract: Surface water governance depends not only on monitoring capacity but also on whether residents can access relevant information, navigate institutional responsibilities, and recognize opportunities to participate. This study examined these dimensions in Jalisco, Mexico, through a statewide, face-to-face household survey assessing exposure to and perceptions of surface water quality communication, information-seeking practices, awareness of inquiry and feedback mechanisms, and interest in public hearings and participatory monitoring, including perceived motivations and barriers. title: Quinoa as an alternative dry season climate resilient crop in the Mekong Delta Vietnam
abstract: Saline intrusion, drought, and water shortages are causing rice production losses in the Mekong River Delta dry season. Quinoa is a drought tolerant halophyte that could be an alternative crop option to rice or fallow in the dry season. The novelty of growing quinoa in the delta requires an understanding of variety selection and crop optimisation in conditions experienced in the dry season. title: Spatial variation shapes gut microbiome composition and functional potential in an Afrotropical fish
abstract: Abstract Host-associated microbiomes are shaped by environmental heterogeneity across spatial gradients. However, the extent to which site-level variation structures gut microbial communities in Afrotropical fishes remains poorly resolved. In this study, we employed high-throughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize the gut microbiome of the African forktail catfish ( Chrysichthys nigrodigitatus ) encompassing two contrasting habitat types, with the aim of assessing spatial patterns in microbial composition and predicted functional potential. title: Names of Chinese Places of Worship in The City of Medan
abstract: Place names represent more than geographical identifiers; they function as cultural symbols that preserve historical memory, religious values, and community identity. The names of Chinese places of worship in Medan reflect complex interactions between language, religion, and cultural adaptation within the Chinese community in Indonesia. abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa ha llegado a cambiar las reglas en la creación de imágenes, transformando los flujos de trabajo tradicionales y redefiniendo la ontología del artista. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el impacto de las herramientas algorítmicas en los procesos de creación de la animación digital y la ilustración desde un enfoque teórico-conceptual. abstract: Abstract Flood extent, depth, duration, and connectivity are key attributes of the seasonal flood pulse in Amazon floodplains, but characterizing them consistently remains difficult in forested, low-relief terrain. abstract: Seismic assessment of reinforced-concrete (RC) buildings requires understanding behavior beyond the elastic range. abstract: Polymer retention is a critical parameter in polymer flooding and requires accurate measurement for successful field implementation. abstract: Abstract Urban rivers receive substantial organic matter and nutrients, but seasonal changes in their microbial communities remain poorly understood. In this study, water and sediment samples were collected from four urban rivers in Changzhou during winter and summer. 16S rDNA, ITS amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to characterize microbial composition and its functional potential. abstract: Abstract 实时微型物体探测是低空无人飞行器(UAV)感知的关键任务。然而,由于成像高度、视角和复杂背景的变化,空中目标通常体积小、分布密集且视觉模糊,从而对检测精度和推理效率构成了巨大挑战。尽管RT-DETR框架提供了端到端的检测模式,但它对微小物体的反应较弱,特征融合过程中细微细节的退化,以及无人机场景中不稳定的边界箱回归。为应对这些限制,我们的FAMO-DETR被引入为一种频率感知的端到端探测器,专为通过无人机探测微小物体而设计。具体而言,通过离散的小波变换,将频率感知的Mamba编码器(FAME)设计用于将低频语义信息与高频边缘细节分离,从而通过Mamba序列建模,增强深度特征中的全局情境表示。随后开发出一种高频CARAFE模块(HF-CARAFE),将高频边缘引导和动态内核重新组装为特征融合,从而缓解传统升级操作引起的语义错位和边界模糊。最后,开发了NWD-CIoU损耗(NC-Loss),将归一化的Wasserstein距离的平滑距离约束与CIOU的几何重叠约束相结合,为微小物体定位提供了更稳定的优化信号。对VisDrone2019-DET和AI-TOD数据集的全面实验表明,FAMO-DETR实现了 $$AP_s$$ 在VisDrone2019-DET上,数值为22.1%,在AI-TOD上为AP值为23.5%,使基准配置分别提高了1.7%和2.3%,同时保持了134

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of cultural ecosystem service supply, demand and service flows along the Jiangsu music–cultural corridor: a grid-based framework across 13 prefecture-level cities
abstract: This study evaluates potential cultural ecosystem service (CES) supply, potential demand and modelled least-cost accessibility pathways across Jiangsu Province on a common 1 km grid for 2014, 2019 and 2020. Nine indicators are organised into a six-indicator supply block and a three-indicator demand block. After direction adjustment and min-max standardisation on the common valid-cell mask, entropy-derived within-dimension weights are normalised to sum to one and the supply and demand blocks are each assigned an equal block weight of 0.5 before the relative supply-demand balance is calculated.

title: AI-based task-scheduling advice: the associations between adoption intent, AI anthropomorphism, and perceived competence fit
abstract: Recent studies have suggested that user adoption of AI-based outputs may be positively related to AI agent anthropomorphism, with perceived agent competence serving as a mediator. This paper examines those relationships in the novel, general-purpose context of AI-based task-scheduling advice, which guides users in their daily activities. Path analyses were conducted across two scenario-based studies (Study 1, N = 258; Study 2, N = 194), which presented AI-based apps. title: Adaptive multi-agent optimization in intelligent-connected vehicles based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In order to provide offloading services for computationally demanding and time-sensitive operations on vehicles, multi-access edge computing has emerged as a successful paradigm. However, there are typically spatiotemporal load mismatches across edge servers due to significant vehicle mobility. As a result, task migration is used to transfer excessive tasks from overloaded to underloaded servers in order to maintain dynamic workload balance. abstract: Smile Chicken MSME faces challenges such as manual transaction recording, raw material inventory tracking, report preparation, and purchasing decisions that still rely on estimation. This study aims to build a web-based Point of Sales system that integrates sales transactions, inventory management, automated reports, and raw material purchase recommendations. title: Gut virome orchestrates nitrogen partitioning between the host and microbiome
abstract: Dietary protein is essential for host growth and nitrogen homeostasis. How dietary protein shapes intestinal phage-bacteria interactions and influences the translation of dietary cues into host physiological outcomes remains poorly understood. We show that low-protein diet (LPD) substantially remodels the murine gut virome by altering phage-bacteria dynamics. title: Exploiting Input Redundancy for High‐Performance Discrete‐Time LQR Control
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem for discrete‐time linear systems with redundant inputs. Under stabilizability and detectability assumptions, two monotonically decreasing sequences of upper bounds are derived for the stabilizing positive semidefinite solution of the discrete‐time algebraic Riccati equation. title: Field‐Aligned Photovoltaic‐Photothermoelectric Coupling in SnSe/ZnO/Si Heterojunctions for Stable Self‐Powered Broadband Photodetection
abstract: ABSTRACT Broadband self‐powered photodetectors that combine photovoltaic (PV) and photothermoelectric (PTE) effects are attractive for low‐power optoelectronic sensing. However, in many heterojunction devices, the PV built‐in field and the PTE‐induced field point in opposite directions, causing wavelength‐dependent polarity reversal and unstable signal readout. Here, we report a field‐aligned p‐SnSe/n‐ZnO/p‐Si heterojunction that converts the conventional competition between PV and PTE effects into constructive coupling. title: Integrating MaxEnt and MaxNet for climate-resilient habitat restoration: Predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in semi-arid landscapes
abstract: Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. title: Localized impact-resistant battery enclosures for electric vehicles: crashworthy lightweight design, mechanical–thermal safety, and validation pathways
abstract: Electric-vehicle battery enclosures must reduce structural mass while preserving deformation clearance, sealing integrity, electrical isolation, and post-impact safety. These requirements are difficult under bottom strike and side-pole collision because both load cases create localized intrusion near cells and modules, where only limited deformation space is available. title: Agroecological zoning of mezcal and tequila agaves in Mexico through MaxEnt ecological niche modeling: Sustainability and climate resilience implications
abstract: Agave‑based distilled‑beverage production in Mexico, particularly mezcal and tequila, is facing intensifying sustainability challenges driven by climate change, monocropping expansion, and degradation of socio‑ecological systems. In this context, agroecological zoning represents a strategic tool for improving territorial planning and strengthening climate resilience. institutions: Autonomous University of San Luis Potosí

title: Bio‐Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra‐Fast and Context‐Aware Human‐Robot Interaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. However, existing proprioceptive or vision‐based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions. Effects of pre-harvest salicylic acid and irrigation interval on rhizome yield and phytochemical accumulation in Curcuma aromatica Salisb.
abstract: Curcuma aromatica Salisb. is a medicinal plant valued for its rhizomes rich in essential oils and phenolic compounds. This study aimed to determine (i) an optimal concentration of salicylic acid (SA) to improve plant performance and secondary metabolite accumulation, and (ii) the effects of different pre-harvest irrigation intervals on plants pre-treated with the selected SA concentration. Salicylic acid was applied as a foliar spray at 50, 100, 150 and 200 ppm at 18, 24 and 30 weeks after planting. title: Inteligencia Artificial en la Animación Digital: Impacto en el Mercado Laboral y la Toma de Decisiones Creativas
abstract: Este estudio analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la toma de decisiones estratégicas de la animación digital y sus consecuencias laborales. Mediante una revisión sistemática documental PRISMA de 50 artículos (2021–2026), se evalúa cómo la IA genera eficiencia operativa (reducción de tiempos de renderizado, automatización de tareas repetitivas) pero también desplaza empleos tradicionales, especialmente en México y América Latina, donde más de 200,000 animadores enfrentan riesgo de disrupción en cinco años. abstract: Allometric relationships represent common laws of relative growth between size and weight of different organisms, including mollusks. Although allometries between shell size and weight of highly invasive apple snails ( Pomacea spp.) vary globally, food‐source effects on these relationships remain unclear, challenging local conservation for freshwater biodiversity. title: Measurement-informed finite element damage identification under modal uncertainty using hybrid QPSO–SA
abstract: Vibration-based damage estimates depend not only on the inverse algorithm but also on the quality, completeness, and modal reliability of the measured data. This study presents a measurement-informed finite element model updating framework that combines quantum-behaved particle swarm optimization with conditionally activated simulated annealing. Field acceleration measurements from a steel truss span of the Chuong Duong Bridge in Hanoi were processed by covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification and used to calibrate the healthy-state model. title: In silico evaluation of potential penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2) inhibitors from Borassus flabellifer haustorium against cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae
abstract: Background The emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, encoding altered Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 (PBP2), has become a major global public health concern. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents. In the present study, phytocompounds derived from the haustorium of Borassus flabellifer L. were investigated as potential inhibitors of PBP2 using an integrated in silico approach. abstract: Pantai Teluk Sepang merupakan kawasan pesisir yang dinamis dan berhadapan langsung dengan Samudera Hindia. Perubahan garis pantai dapat memengaruhi keberlanjutan infrastruktur, permukiman, dan ekosistem pesisir sehingga diperlukan pemantauan yang konsisten. abstract: Aquaculture is a fish-producing subsector of agriculture that has a significant role in India’s economy and livelihood. The major threat to fish production is the outbreak of bacterial infections that creates severe losses every year. Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic invader of human and aquatic animals, ubiquitously present in the aquatic environment. Antibiotics are the common control measure, but their indiscriminate use has resulted in the development of resistance by the pathogen. title: Evolutionary game analysis of scientific research data sharing under the open science context
abstract: Scientific data sharing is central to open science, yet its development is constrained by fragmented data resources, heterogeneous stakeholder incentives, privacy risks, and limited regulatory capacity. This study develops a bounded-rationality, four-population evolutionary game framework involving data providers, data users, government agencies, and sharing platforms. title: Advancing Micro-Ecotone Mapping Using UAV Photogrammetry and GIS
abstract: Ecotones are transitional boundaries between ecosystems and essential to regulating biodiversity and ecological processes. Although ecotones are often wider transition zones like aquatic-terrestrial boundaries, they can happen at fine spatial scales (micro-ecotones) and occur over only a few meters or even centimeters. In the past, ecotones have been examined using one-dimensional transects or coarsely resolved remote sensing data for analysis. title: Integrated assessment of meteorological drought impacts on terrestrial water storage and vegetation dynamics in East Africa
abstract: Abstract Water is essential for life, and effective hydrological management is crucial for economic stability and quality of life. Poor water resource governance can lead to scarcity, displacement, or even fatal consequences. Hydrological conditions in East Africa are influenced by drivers such as demographic expansion, industrialization, droughts, and vegetation dynamics. abstract: Este artículo se enmarca en una investigación sobre el uso de Inteligencia Artificial en la escritura académica en carreras humanísticas de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario, Argentina. The problem involves the combined influences of porous medium permeability, uniform suction/injection, rotation of the system, thermal radiation, and coupled heat and mass transfer. abstract: This study aims to develop a practical module for ship machinery based on the operation of the ICE 1–SBR 18 incinerator that is suitable for use as instructional material for cadets of the Nautical Technology Study Program at the Politeknik Pelayaran Sumatera Barat. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE development model, which consists of five stages: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
abstract: Abstract Accurate counting and morphological analysis of welding electrodes and wire stubs are essential for warehouse data management in welding factories. However, the visual recognition of welding material stubs in real-world industrial applications is frequently hindered by issues such as missed detections, false detections, and imprecise boundary localization. abstract: This work presents a prescribed-performance attitude tracking control strategy for under-actuated quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles subject to external disturbances and actuator saturation. A novel four-stage cascaded dynamic representation is first developed by incorporating atmospheric disturbances and actuator saturation effects. title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. abstract: High strength and lightweight alloys like AA7075-T6 Aluminium alloy pose great challenge in drilling, particularly in achieving high surface quality and productivity. The existing work is a systematic investigation of the effect of the cutting speed, feed rate and drill depth on surface roughness and material removal rate (MRR) in conventional drilling. abstract: Earthquake prediction has long been considered one of the greatest challenges in the global scientific community due to the complex and uncertain nature of seismogenic processes, along with the prevailing consensus that earthquakes are inherently unpredictable. Here, we present a novel and potentially transformative concept—seismo-ripples—resonance signals consistently observed in seismic, magnetic, and ionospheric data prior to major earthquakes. abstract: Abstract This study presents a vertically integrated terahertz metasurface biosensor that combines graphene with transition metal dichalcogenides for breast and colorectal cancer detection based on refractive index sensing. The resonant region uses a clustered cross geometry composed of four hollow circular rings and four solid circular resonators linked by orthogonal MoS2-coated rectangular strips on a graphene layer. title: Auditoría tributaria digital del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas mediante el Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos en el Perú: revisión sistemática y propuesta preliminar de indicadores de riesgo
abstract: La digitalización de la administración tributaria peruana ha trasladado una parte creciente del control del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas hacia registros electrónicos y cruces automatizados. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia científica, normativa e institucional sobre auditoría tributaria digital, facturación electrónica y crédito fiscal, y derivar una propuesta preliminar de indicadores de priorización aplicables al Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos. title: Seasonal flood inundation area and repetitive flood exposure shape the fundamental patterns of flood exposure in China from 2000 to 2020
abstract: Remote sensing of floods and associated exposure is essential for understanding and managing flood risks, yet exposure differences among floods with varying frequencies remain underexplored. Using MODIS time-series data, this study mapped infrequent flood inundation area (IFIA) and seasonal flood inundation area (SFIA) across China during 2000–2020. abstract: Benzimidazole is a privileged nitrogen-containing fused heterocyclic scaffold that has attracted considerable interest in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry because of its structural versatility, favorable physicochemical properties and broad biological profile. title: Assembly processes and network structure of rhizosphere fungal communities in healthy and Ralstonia solanacearum-infected tomato plants
abstract: Introduction Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum is a major constraint to tomato production worldwide. Rhizosphere microbial community is closely linked to plant health. However, how R. solanacearum invasion alters the assembly processes and co-occurrence network in tomato rhizosphere fungal communities remains largely unclear. abstract: ABSTRACT Pipelines, valves, and pressure vessels (PVs) are vital components in nuclear, thermal power, and chemical systems, operating under high temperature and pressure over extended periods, leading to safety risks. Ensuring their safe operation requires regular inspections, which current robotic systems cannot fully address due to the diverse and challenging environments. abstract: Plant fungal diseases impose significant annual reductions of global crop yield and quality. Despite advances in our understanding of the etiology and molecular mechanisms of plant-fungus interactions, effective management of fungal diseases remains challenging due to climate-driven shifts in pathogen populations, the emergence of fungicide-resistant strains, globalization in agricultural supply chains, and postharvest vulnerabilities. abstract: Asian weatherloaches have expanded their range across Europe, potentially increasing competitive pressure on the conservation-dependent native European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis . Because interspecific interactions are potentially mediated by benthic habitat use, we quantified substrate choice of native European and invasive Asian weatherloaches in a replicated laboratory two-way choice experiment. Vía a la Costa and Posorja sectors have become contrasting but complementary scenarios of the same phenomenon: the progressive loss of rural habitat in the face of the dynamics of accelerated urbanization. abstract: The seafood processing industry faces critical operational challenges in maintaining mass-balance integrity because manual, paper-based recording causes data lag and human input errors. abstract: The transition from conchocelis to conchosporangial branches is not only a key stage in the life cycle of Pyropia/Porphyra but also directly affects the yield and quality of economically important species such as Pyropia haitanensis . title: Airborne measurements of turbulence and cloud microphysics during PaCE 2022 using the Advanced Max Planck CloudKite Instrument (MPCK + )
abstract: Abstract. This paper presents the data set collected with the Advanced Max Planck CloudKite instrument (MPCK+) during the Pallas Cloud Experiment (PaCE), conducted at Pallas, Finland, between September 19 and September 26, 2022. abstract: Este estudio formaliza la receta técnica de un cheesecake semifrío mediante el uso de herramientas de modelación lineal para optimizar su escalado industrial. title: Effectiveness of Ballast Water Management Convention Implementation at Samarinda Port
abstract: The implementation of the Ballast Water Management Convention (BWMC) is an important instrument in controlling ecological risks due to the movement of aquatic organisms through ship ballast water. abstract: Advances in multi-omic sequencing have revolutionized our understanding of the composition and potential function of genetic sequences across human, natural, and engineered systems. abstract: The electrification of port operations is reshaping the technical relationship between logistics performance, energy demand, infrastructure condition and data reliability. abstract: Abstract Sustainability and resilience expectations for infrastructure are escalating faster than the regulatory frameworks meant to deliver them. This mismatch is most acute for ageing critical infrastructure. Yet, adaptation decisions remain fragmented because resilience and sustainability operate on fundamentally different temporal domains: resilience captures short-term recovery dynamics and service continuity. abstract: ABSTRACT Ongoing climate change poses a major threat to biodiversity, with current extinction rates highlighting the urgent need to identify species that are most vulnerable. abstract: Maritime simulators play a key role in training and assessing cadets’ operational competencies, especially within the framework of the STCW Convention. abstract: El fútbol siempre ha sido mucho más que un deporte. Es lenguaje universal, emoción colectiva, identidad cultural. Es infancia, es barrio, es gloria y derrota, es historia compartida. abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic pathogen of fish, humans, and livestock, and has a severe negative impact on aquaculture development. abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) varies with climate and soil resources, but whether species-level plant traits provide information beyond these environmental controls remains unclear. abstract: This study discusses the process of becoming undergone by the mythical female figure, Medusa, in Natalie Haynes’ Stone Blind. title: Multi-response optimization of flexural performance in additively manufactured carbon fiber-reinforced PLA composites
abstract: Abstract Additively manufactured carbon fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (CF-PLA) composites are increasingly used for lightweight components that require improved flexural performance. However, their mechanical response is strongly governed by the combined effects of printing parameters, making systematic modeling and multi-response optimization essential. abstract: Perkembangan drone berbasis IoT meningkatkan kebutuhan sistem telemetry real-time yang stabil dan efisien. title: MCATNet: Multiscale Context-Aware Transformer Network for infrared small target detection
abstract: Infrared small target detection is a crucial task for IR image processing, aiming at identifying and localizing targets which typically occupy only a few pixels. title: Morphotectonic and topographic correlates of spring occurrence and perennial spring discharge in a forested catchment of the Garhwal Himalaya
abstract: Springs sustain domestic water supply across the Indian Himalaya, yet many are declining, and the landscape factors associated with their occurrence and discharge remain poorly quantified at the sub-catchment scale. This study examines the association of spring occurrence and dry-season discharge with elevation, morphotectonic indices and land cover in the Henval River Catchment (252.71 km 2 ), Garhwal Himalaya, India. abstract: Accurate estimation of Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is crucial for understanding climate change and its impacts on public health, as aerosols are a measure of air quality conditions. AOD is usually retrieved from satellite imagery at coarse spatial and temporal resolutions. However, producing high-resolution AOD estimates in both space and time can better support evidence-based policies and interventions. abstract: Abstract This article examines two tendencies in contemporary Latin American science fiction, drawing on Mark Fisher’s terms Terminator and Avatar . Derived from the eponymous movies, Terminator narratives depict capitalist destruction as inevitable, while Avatar narratives imagine that global collapse can be averted by returning to premodern forms of social organization. abstract: The article examines the problem of the justification of preliminary sizing and interconnection scheme for a distributed generation unit serving an area with abnormal power demand relative to the normative level. The research extends the previously completed stage of interval estimation of the technocenosis of municipal entities within the Prokopyevsky district of the Kemerovo Region (Kuzbass). abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella is a key One Health issue because resistant lineages and AMR determinants occur across human, animal, food and environmental compartments.This important review article summarizes recent knowledge regarding the epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, integrated control and genomic surveillance of antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella at the humananimal-environment interface.There are significant differences in resistance patterns among serovars, geographic regions, host populations and surveillance systems.The epidemiology of several non-typhoidal Salmonella lin

title: Increasing exposure to potential flooding in high-mountain catchments
abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. Validation against a manually derived reference dataset revealed considerable differences in accuracy and completeness across five building footprint products. title: The potential global distribution of Drosophila suzukii , including consideration of irrigation and Australian host cropping areas
abstract: BACKGROUND: Spotted wing drosophila, Drosophila suzukii (Matsumura), is a major fruit fly pest of cherries and berries across Eurasia and North America, with a restricted distribution in the southern hemisphere. It is currently ranked the third greatest threat to Australia on the National Priority Plant Pest (NPPP) list (2024). Various CLIMEX, MaxEnt and mechanistic models of the potential global distribution of D. suzukii have not included irrigation effects. Here, we model the potential global distribution of D. suzukii using CLIMEX, mapped as a composite of natural rainfall and irrigation.

abstract: ABSTRACT Fuel cells represent the core components of next‐generation high‐efficiency electrochemical energy conversion technologies. The performance of the cathode oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalyst determines battery efficiency and lifespan. Thus, developing efficient, cost‐effective ORR single‐atom catalysts is essential for fuel cell commercialization. title: A three-year study reveals a strong association between NO2 and COVID-19 in the state of Oklahoma, United States
abstract: Background Air pollution has been linked to adverse COVID-19 outcomes. However, studies of the US to-date have generally focused on the US as a whole or large cities on the east and west coasts. Few studies have considered the Midwest, and no comprehensive study of the four most common gaseous pollutants has considered Oklahoma. Oklahoma, a fossil fuel-dependent state with a relatively high respiratory disease burden, provides a unique context to evaluate pollutant impacts on COVID-19 case numbers. title: Dynamical and thermodynamic mechanisms driving the April 2025 severe thunderstorm over eastern India
abstract: On 10 April 2025, a severe thunderstorm impacted eastern India, causing disastrous impacts across 19 of Bihar's 38 districts. Survey-estimated peak surface winds of 120 km/h (based on structural damage assessment) contributed to 63 deaths—40 from wind-related hazards and 23 from lightning strikes—with the district of Nalanda experiencing the most extensive devastation. abstract: Background The coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic demonstrates the importance of organizational sustainability across all sectors, and universities are no exception. It revealed deep-seated fragilities in institutional supply chains, revealing that the ability to sustain core educational and research missions is inherently connected to the robustness of supply chain capabilities, thus underscoring the need to shift from a reactive to a proactive stance in university operations. abstract: Wind turbine vibration monitoring under variable speed operation requires separating nonstationary rotor-order components whose frequencies and operating intervals depend on operating state. These components can occupy local support regions in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) plane rather than fixed spectral bands or continuous ridges. abstract: Purpose – This study aims to implement Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for analyzing election logistics distribution monitoring reports at Bawaslu RI and to develop an interactive dashboard to support topic exploration. The study addresses the difficulty of manually interpreting large collections of institutional reports containing operational, administrative, geographical, procurement, and legal information related to election logistics distribution. title: Addressing the Interconnected Crises: Policy Integration for Climate and Biodiversity in Norway
abstract: ABSTRACT The biodiversity and climate crises are interconnected through land use and land use change, posing significant threats to ecosystem integrity, human well‐being, food and water supply and climate resilience. To effectively address these challenges, policies for climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation and biodiversity protection must be considered jointly. abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess flood-prone areas in Auckland, New Zealand, using stream order analysis as a geospatial tool to delineate flood risk zones. The research addresses the growing need for efficient flood risk mapping in urban settings by providing a simplified, yet effective, method for identifying high-risk zones. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. title: Analysis of Barriers within the Decision-making Chain for German and Danish SMEs Supplying Climate Adaptation Solutions
abstract: Climate adaptation has become a central policy priority across Europe, yet the uptake of new adaptation solutions remains slow, particularly within public-sector markets. Small and medium-sized enterprises play an important role in developing innovative climate adaptation technologies, but often struggle to gain access to planning, procurement and implementation processes shaped by established routines, regulatory complexity and risk aversion. title: SMART TOURISM GOVERNANCE: A SCIENTOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF GOVERNMENT ROLES
abstract: Smart tourism governance has become increasingly important as digital technologies reshape tourism management, public services, and destination development. However, existing studies have predominantly emphasized technological innovation, destination competitiveness, and tourist experiences, while the evolving administrative roles of government remain fragmented. This study aims to examine the intellectual development of smart tourism governance and map the evolving roles of government through a scientometric analysis. abstract: Abstract While extreme precipitation is expected to intensify globally in a warming climate, changes in extreme precipitation on regional scales remain uncertain. To understand how well Earth system models (ESMs) capture recent changes in regional extreme precipitation, we compare trends in daily and monthly extreme precipitation across multiple observational data sets and three ESM ensembles. abstract: Introduction Equalizing basic older adult care services is a core objective of China’s response to population aging, yet whether the provision of older adult care bed supply has become more equal across provinces, and how its spatial structure has evolved, remains unclear. We ask how large provincial disparities in bed supply are and where they originate, whether supply is spatially clustered, how the distribution has evolved, and whether gaps converge. abstract: Industrial control systems would increasingly depend on remote operation, online monitoring, and potentially autonomous control. This creates new requirements for secure, low-latency communications, and introduces new operational constraints on secret key availability, communication autonomy, and resilience under normal and abnormal conditions. abstract: The availability of communication signals for dense wireless local area networks (WLANs) is being increasingly hindered by spectrum contention, interference, and traffic dynamics. Side effects of coverage can also be captured by higher layers, such as the transport or application layer; however, their sensing capabilities are limited, and their information may be strongly biased by the network conditions or the user traffic. title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. abstract: En un mundo marcado por la omnipresencia algorítmica y la rápida integración de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) en la educación, la pregunta fundamental trasciende la capacidad tecnológica para centrarse en la esencia del desarrollo humano. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la justicia penal desafía el debido proceso y la igualdad ante la ley, afectando de forma especial a poblaciones vulnerables como los migrantes irregulares. Mediante la revisión sistemática de la literatura y de los marcos normativos, incluido el Reglamento (UE) 2024/1689, este artículo analiza el impacto de la IA en las decisiones judiciales, la policía predictiva y la gestión penitenciaria. abstract: Abstract Rapid and reliable localization of survivors is critical in post-disaster search and rescue operations. However, conventional sensing methods such as visual imaging are often ineffective due to smoke, dust, or debris, and traditional RSSI-based localization suffers from severe multipath interference and noise. abstract: Natural products have played a central role in the development of medicines and continue to provide structurally diverse molecules, pharmacological leads, and molecular frameworks for contemporary drug discovery. Chemical pharmacognosy has traditionally focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of constituents obtained from medicinal plants and other natural sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Reconstructive spectroscopy offers a promising route toward miniaturization by replacing dispersive optics with computational recovery from encoded measurements, but existing implementations typically rely on complex nanofabrication and highly decorrelated encoding elements, limiting manufacturability and robustness. abstract: Nori merupakan produk pangan berbasis rumput laut yang semakin banyak dikonsumsi di Indonesia dan berpotensi mengakumulasi kontaminan dari lingkungan, termasuk arsen. abstract: La animación digital y la inteligencia artificial están transformando y ofreciendo herramientas innovadoras en la producción de películas animadas, reducción de producción y automatización de tareas. abstract: The interdependence of water, energy, and food (WEF) systems requires governance approaches that address cross-sectoral interactions rather than separate policy regimes. abstract: Drought is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that includes meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, and socio-economic components. Both single and composite drought indices were used in this study to assess agricultural drought in the East Shewa Zone of Central Ethiopia. The Precipitation Condition Index (PCI), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), and Soil Moisture Condition Index (SMCI) were used as single indices. abstract: Abstract Distributed Earth Observation (EO) workflows require cluster configurations that balance competing objectives (execution time, computational cost, energy consumption, and resource-use efficiency), yet practitioners typically provision resources using fixed heuristics that ignore most of these dimensions. This paper presents an outcome-as-a-service framework for Dask-based EO processing that jointly optimises all four objectives. title: Innovative performance indicators for effective Quality, Safety, and Environment management in oil drilling operations
abstract: Abstract Effective management of Quality, Safety, and Environment (QSE) performance is critical in high-risk oil drilling operations. Despite extensive research on generic Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) frameworks, there remains limited guidance on context-specific, operationally validated methodologies that integrate leading and lagging indicators within unified QSE systems for drilling operations. title: Laboratory-based nutritional risk assessment including GDF15 in cirrhosis: a multicenter retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Malnutrition is a common complication of cirrhosis and is associated with adverse outcomes. However, current nutritional risk assessment tools may not fully incorporate objective laboratory biomarkers. This study aimed to develop a biomarker-based prediction model for nutritional risk assessment in patients with cirrhosis. We retrospectively collected the clinical data of 551 patients with liver cirrhosis from two centers between April 2023 and April 2026. title: Toward human-centered AI-assisted terminology work
abstract: Abstract Generative AI is likely to transform terminology work by creating new opportunities for automation. At the same time, it raises concerns about the future of terminologists and terminological resources, as efficiency pressures may encourage excessive automation based on the perception that human expertise can be replaced by AI. title: Crop improvement of Bambara groundnut through mutation breeding
abstract: Bambara groundnut is an important indigenous African grain legume cultivated primarily by smallholder farmers across sub-Saharan Africa. The crop is valued for its nutritional richness, adaptability to marginal environments, and contribution to household food security and soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation. title: Curvularia lunata as a versatile pathogen causing leaf spot diseases in diverse plant species and its management strategies
abstract: Curvularia lunata poses a significant threat to agricultural ecosystems worldwide, causing substantial yield losses and economic consequences across a variety of crops. As a prominent phytopathogenic fungus known for its affinity for leaf spot diseases, its proliferation warrants attention due to its remarkable adaptability and expanding influence. It can serve as a beneficial endophyte for certain plants; however, its pathogenic nature underscores its potential to affect both plant and human health. title: Musa dulongjiangensis (Musaceae), a new species from Yunnan, southwest China
abstract: Musa dulongjiangensis (Musaceae), a new species of the genus Musa endemic to Yunnan, southwestern China, is described and illustrated in this study. This new species is morphologically similar to M. puspanjaliae , but can be clearly distinguished by a combination of morphological characters. Its female bud bracts are dark purple externally and purple internally, with 6–7 basal female flowers arranged in two rows; the base of the compound tepal bears distinct and dense red stripes, the ovary is pale green and glabrous. title: Development and application of a smartphone-based thermal contrast amplification reader for photothermal lateral flow immunoassays
abstract: The high cost and poor portability of external infrared thermal imagers have limited the widespread adoption of photothermal lateral flow immunoassays (PT-LFIAs) in on-site testing. To address this, we developed a smartphone-based handheld Thermal Contrast Amplification (TCA) Reader, eliminating the need for costly external hardware. Compared with existing recent external thermal imager-based PT-LFIA readout, this reader integrates a selected thermal-sensor-equipped smartphone, a motorized laser module, Bluetooth-enabled control, and a fixed 3D-printed holder into a compact device. title: Declared Unauthorised Construction in Greece: An Indicator-Based Spatial Analysis
abstract: Unauthorised construction has been a persistent feature of spatial development in Greece, yet its geographical variation cannot be adequately captured by counts of recorded cases or total unauthorised building area alone. This study examines the officially recorded and legally regularised component of the phenomenon using administrative data from the Technical Chamber of Greece, comprising approximately 1.2 million declarations and more than 4.1 million violation records. abstract: Abstract Scale invariance (fractality) is a prominent feature of the large-scale behavior of many stochastic systems. In this work, we construct a provably convergent and easily interpretable algorithm for the statistical identification of the Hurst distribution (in particular, the scaling exponents) undergirding a high-dimensional fractal system. title: Plant Crude Polysaccharide‐Enabled Hydrogel Electrodes for Long‐Term Stable EMG Recording
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels with high conductivity, flexibility, skin compatibility, and long‐term stability are essential for reliable bioelectrical signal recording in flexible bioelectronic interfaces for wearable health monitoring and human‐machine interaction. abstract: ABSTRACT Attributing regional evapotranspiration (ET) and assessing its impacts are critical for understanding land‐atmosphere interactions in climate‐sensitive regions such as northern China. This study fuses six gridded ET products with in situ measurements using Random Forest after excluding poorly representative flux sites. abstract: We present Seg-TTO, a novel framework for zero-shot, open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS), designed to excel in specialized domain tasks. While current open-vocabulary approaches show impressive performance on standard segmentation benchmarks under zero-shot settings, they fall short of supervised counterparts on highly domain-specific datasets. abstract: ABSTRACT The quest for better and advanced materials that comply with economic and environmental sustainability principles has led to the development of several materials, including geopolymers. Derived from aluminosilicates and acid/alkali activators, geopolymers have proven to be a good alternative to several materials, to be environmentally benign and cheap to produce as they can be produced from valorizing waste. abstract: The cultivation of Stropharia rugosoannulata involves substantial organic substrate input and fungal mycelial activity, which may influence soil nutrient transformation, microbial communities and functional gene profiles. However, whether these responses differ between protected and open-field cultivation settings remains unclear at the metagenomic level. title: Aeroallergen Sensitization Patterns Among Adults with Allergic Rhinitis at a Tertiary Center in Erzurum, Turkiye
abstract: Allergic Rhinitis has evolved beyond the conventional definition of nasal mucosal inflammation, becoming a complex ecosystem problem shaped by climate change and shifts in regional biodiversity. This study aimed to characterize aeroallergen sensitization patterns among adults with allergic rhinitis at a tertiary care center in Erzurum, Türkiye. This study was conducted as a single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study at a tertiary allergy clinic in Erzurum, Türkiye. abstract: У статті досліджується фундаментальна природа та еволюція характеру конфліктів між великими державами у період з 1914 року до наших днів. title: Climate policy uncertainty and agricultural digital-intelligent transformation in China: evidence from provincial panel data
abstract: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive research initiative focused on the intelligent management and control of urban drainage systems, specifically applied to Pinggu District in Beijing. Utilizing the Storm Water Management Model (SWMM), the research integrates extensive literature reviews, comparative case studies of water utility management in major global cities, and rigorous on-site field investigations. abstract: Tectonic ground movements in the form ot earthquakes can devastate infrastructure and cause significant casualties once their magnitude is 6 and above. This study investigated early indications of such seismic activity through the correlations with temporal variations in groundwater properties. abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) pose a growing risk in high mountain regions as climate-driven glacier retreat accelerates lake expansion and new lake formation. In the Hindu Kush Himalaya, particularly in Afghanistan, triggering processes and GLOF propagation downstream are largely unstudied. title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.

abstract: Urban pluvial flooding represents a growing threat to contemporary cities, driven by the compounding effects of climate change, rapid urbanization, and inadequate stormwater infrastructure, prompting the study of nature-based solutions (NBS) as potential interventions for mitigating the detrimental effects of urban flooding. abstract: Flood peak timing (FloPT) is a key indicator of hydrological responses to climate change. Yet global FloPT assessments is limited by sparse and uneven in-situ discharge observations. Here, we demonstrated the capability of satellite altimetry to estimate FloPT worldwide and presented the global map of observed FloPT, with a dramatic improvement in spatial coverage, especially in Global South countries. abstract: Variable importance derived from species distribution modelling (SDM) is widely used to identify key environmental drivers of species distributions. However, the reliability of these inferences has rarely been systematically evaluated, particularly with respect to their sensitivity to individual occurrences. abstract: This study examined the relationship between Computational Thinking Skills (CTS) and Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) among high school students majoring in biology in Jakarta, Indonesia, using a quantitative, correlational, and cross-sectional research design. abstract: The fast increase in population and rapid urbanization necessarily heighten the production of (MSW), thereby raising waste management to a significant environmental and policy issue. abstract: Abstract Higher-education campuses are well suited to staged decarbonization because they combine concentrated electrical demand, substantial rooftop area, diverse load flexibility, and long-term institutional ownership of energy assets. abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. abstract: Cancer patients arrive for psilocybin therapy with bodies altered by illness and treatment — bodies that they have learned to brace against, dissociate from, or scan for threat. Research on psilocybin-assisted therapy for cancer-related depression and anxiety consistently identifies the quality of the acute subjective experience — reflected in constructs such as acceptance, surrender, boundlessness, and emotional breakthrough — as a key predictor of therapeutic benefit. title: Macrophage reprogramming by the ultraviolet filter benzophenone-1 promotes malignant phenotypes in breast cancer cells: integrated computational and experimental evidence
abstract: Background Benzophenone-1 (BP-1) is a benzophenone ultraviolet absorber used in cosmetic and personal care products. Although BP-1 exhibits estrogenic activity, its broader effects in breast cancer remain unclear. This study investigated the molecular and cellular responses associated with BP-1 exposure. abstract: Global sustainability education has expanded rapidly since UNESCO adopted its 2030 framework. Informal sustainability knowledge has eroded across the same decade. abstract: This paper forecasts United States (US) oil and gas production to 2100 based on historical production data from the US EIA. abstract: Deuterium is a natural heavy isotope of hydrogen, containing a neutron as well as a proton, making it twice as heavy. title: Living on the edge: climate-induced displacement and livelihood adaptation among char communities in Bangladesh
abstract: Every year, a large number of people in Bangladesh are displaced in char land (riverine island) areas due to climate change. These internally displaced people suffer from socio-economic crises and struggle persistently for a livelihood. This paper investigates the impact of climate change on the livelihoods of displaced char land dwellers, their coping mechanisms, and the obstacles they face. abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the crucial need for fully quantitative risk assessment of large‐scale structures, their performance is typically assessed through deterministic or semi‐quantitative approaches. abstract: Determining the breeding frequencies and breeding periods of species that spend part or all of their lives underground is challenging because of limited population surveys. abstract: Abstract Seasonal water scarcity in western Bahia, Brazil, has led to increased dependence on groundwater resources; however, basin-scale hydrogeological measurements remain insufficient for preliminary assessments. This study presents a geographic information system-based groundwater potential map for the Grande River Hydrographic Basin (GRHB), where groundwater potential is defined as a relative index reflecting conditions favorable for recharge and subsurface storage, rather than a direct measure of aquifer productivity. abstract: Groundwater quality in the Zabzugu District, Northern Ghana, is increasingly affected by geogenic processes and anthropogenic activities, particularly agriculture. This study examined the hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling mechanisms, and health implications of groundwater in the district. abstract: Background Parks are promoted as a public health resource, and neighborhoods with limited park access often face co-occurring air pollution and socioeconomic disadvantage. title: Modern human δ¹³C isoscapes in Brazil reveal spatial structure in a C₄-dominated diet landscape
abstract: This study presents δ¹³C isoscapes for modern human tissues in Brazil, based on paired analyses of dentine collagen and fingernail keratin. Using a random forest modeling approach combined with climatic and socio-economic covariates, we reveal spatial patterns in dietary carbon source assimilation across the Northeast and Southeast regions. While δ¹³C values in dentine correlated mainly with environmental variables, those in fingernails were more closely tied to socio-economic indicators such as municipal GDP and income inequality. Partial dependence plots illustrated contrasting relationships

title: Land Use Land Cover (LULC) Change Detection in Delhi NCT Using Multi-Sensor Satellite Data and Google Earth Engine
abstract: Land Use Land Cover (LULC) change detection is essential for understanding the dynamics of human modified landscapes and for supporting effective land management and urban planning. This study analyses LULC change across the Delhi National Capital Territory over a fifteen-year period, from 2010 to 2025, to assess urban sprawl and its environmental impact in one of India's fastest growing metropolitan regions.
