title: The impact of leachate from waste rubber particles on duckweed: growth, oxidative stress, and cell structure
abstract: Waste rubber particles, especially tire wear particles (TWPs), have become major contributors to microplastic pollution. Through rainwater and road runoff, TWPs can enter the water environment, posing potential threats to aquatic organisms. However, systematic research on the effects of waste rubber particles on duckweed remains limited. Thus, Spirodela polyrhiza was exposed to rubber leachate at 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25% levels, aiming to evaluate the effects of rubber leachates on duckweed at the individual, physiological, and cellular levels. title: Black soldier fly algorithm based on swarm intelligence method for solving optimization problems
abstract: Meta-heuristic swarm algorithms are vital for resolving complex, non-convex optimization problems. However, contemporary optimizers increasingly suffer from structural stagnation and slow convergence rates when tracking highly rugged engineering surfaces; this limitation stems from their strict reliance on standard linear vector updates or basic random walks that cause search agents to blindly bypass narrow global valleys. title: Prospects for overcoming the systemic crisis in agriculture: Focus on Ukraine
abstract: The current state of Ukraine’s agricultural sector is characterized by the deepening of a systemic crisis driven by the cumulative impact of military, economic, environmental, and social factors, as well as climate change. War-related destabilizing factors, including the temporary occupation of territories, landmine contamination of agricultural lands, destruction of infrastructure and irrigation systems, chemical and mechanical soil contamination, disruption of logistics chains, and shortages of financial, human, and material resources, have significantly intensified environmental challenges.

title: Characterization of a Magdalenian Composite Adhesive Lump From the Ćmielów 95 Site, Poland: Implications for Late Pleistocene Resin‐Curing Technology
abstract: ABSTRACT A unique, black, plastic object recovered from a Magdalenian dwelling structure at the site of Ćmielów 95 using a multi‐instrumental approach to assess Upper/Late Paleolithic adhesive technology. Multimethodological analyses reveal that the object is a sophisticated, artificially synthesized composite binder comprising an organic matrix and inorganic mineral fillers. title: Optimising the bifurcation analysis, phase portrait, chaotic behaviour, and optical soliton solutions of the Biswas–Milovic model in fibre optic communication
abstract: This work presents an exclusive study on the (1 + 1)-dimensional Biswas-Milovic model with power-law nonlinearity, focusing on bifurcation analysis, phase portrait, and dynamic behaviour of optical wave propagation. This model is a momentous nonlinear evolution equation to describe optical pulses in optical fibre communication and nonlinear wave dynamics. The bifurcation analysis provides insights into the qualitative behaviour of the system, revealing critical parameter thresholds at which solution structure changes. title: Catalyzing sustainable development through digitalization: the nexus between government digital transition and green total factor productivity
abstract: Green total factor productivity (GTFP) represents a cornerstone for sustainable development; however, previous scholarship has primarily concentrated on market-based or technological determinants, frequently ignoring the impact of institutional governance. Comprehending the mechanisms through which digital public administration drives GTFP is vital for facilitating a profound ecological shift in both society and the broader economy. title: Ecosystem complexity and climate adaptation in Oman: Climate-water-ecosystem nexus
abstract: This study examines the relationships among climate variability, water-related variables, and vegetation dynamics across the Sultanate of Oman. Using six decades of climatic and hydrological data, the study evaluates long-term climate variability patterns, identifies the main climatic and ecohydrological factors associated with native vegetation dynamics, and proposes a Climate–Water–Ecosystem framework to explore interactions, trade-offs, and synergies within arid environments. title: Association between infertility prevalence and exposure to heat stress: an ecological study based on the Universal Thermal Climate Index
abstract: Background Repeated exposure to heat stress may adversely affect reproductive health, yet the population-level relationship between heat stress and infertility has not been well characterized. Methods We conducted a global ecological analysis across 174 countries and regions from 1990 to 2021. Heat exposure was quantified as the annual number of days falling into four Universal Thermal Climate Index categories: moderate, strong, very strong, and extreme heat stress. title: Warming and photoperiod differentially mediate native and invasive alien predator effects on damselfly fitness traits
abstract: Invasive alien (IA) predators can disrupt predator-prey interactions and alter prey phenotypes. However, how their effects differ from those of native predators remains poorly understood. Additionally, it is unclear to what extent these impacts interact with environmental factors such as warming and photoperiod. title: Analysis of the Effect of Inlet Pressure and Feed pH on Permeate Conductivity Stability in a Reverse Osmosis Unit at a Coal-Fired Power Plant
abstract: The Reverse Osmosis (RO) unit in the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) of a coal-fired power plant plays a vital role in producing low-conductivity demineralized water for boiler feed. Permeate quality stability is strongly influenced by operating conditions, particularly inlet pressure and feed pH. This study evaluates the effects of inlet pressure and feed pH, both partially and simultaneously, on permeate conductivity as an indicator of RO performance stability. title: Testing a recently proposed framework for assessing the success of conservation translocations: the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri) programme in Hungary
abstract: Advancing conservation translocation science requires the synthesis and comparative analysis of individual case studies to generate broader evidence-based insights. However, no widely adopted framework currently standardises outcome assessment across diverse translocation programmes. Birot et al. (2025) recently proposed a candidate framework that could potentially provide such a standard. Being one of the main factors influencing the process of industrial relocation, labor migration will undergo significant change in the patterns and determinants of migration. title: What we need to know to study contemporary resistance: the changing role of the corporeal body
abstract: This paper suggests that recent developments have transformed the role of the corporeal body in practices of resistance. While the significance of the resisting body has increased in some forms of resistance, in others the corporeal body matters less. In digital and juridical forms of dissent, concrete bodies, once the primary vehicles of resistance, take a back seat to digital cyborgs or interpassively outsource resistance to proxy legal subjects, documents, and institutional processes. abstract: This study aims to examine the traces of the Medusa depiction—one of the most characteristic figures of Greek iconography—within the city of Tokat, located in the ancient Pontus region, through archaeological and numismatic data. Known as one of the Gorgon sisters in Greek mythology and believed to possess the power to turn any living being into stone with her gaze, Medusa was widely utilized as an apotropaic (protective) symbol in the ancient world. title: Becoming climate sentinels
abstract: Abstract In South Korea, forest scientists refashion themselves as “climate sentinels” as they confront subtle yet disquieting shifts in plant seasonality brought about by climate change. Unlike traditional sentinels, who watch for external threats from a frontier, climate sentinels face ecological anomalies and surprises—such as untimely flowering—that have permeated everyday spaces. title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. title: Defining and resolving seismic complexity through a unified source–path–site framework: the Vrancea intermediate-depth ground motions
abstract: Abstract Ground motions generated by the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismic source exhibit long-recognized intricate characteristics that challenge standard seismological interpretations. As a result, Vrancea earthquakes are frequently excluded from global comparative studies, being treated as exceptions for which conventional source, path, and site models fail to provide consistency. title: The Potential of Self‐Maintainable Living Materials
abstract: Engineered living materials (ELMs) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self-maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self-repair, adaptive response, and long-term functional persistence. abstract: Cryptography is essential in many digital fields to provide information security and confidentiality. Thus, many digital services, such as those that transfer sensitive data, require encryption using a lightweight block cipher such as PRESENT, which is an ultra-lightweight encryption algorithm. However, this algorithm has weaknesses; for this reason, we propose in this paper an extended version of the PRESENT algorithm based on a substitution-permutation network and the Alfa function. abstract: Abstract To address severe wear of tunnel boring machines cutter rings under complex service conditions, a Ni-WC coating (60 wt% WC) was prepared on cutter rings by laser cladding. The results indicated that the formation of WC, W 2 C, and M 23 C 6 hard phases in the coating increased its microhardness by 2.90 times that of the substrate. abstract: In the context of power market development, the power demand of computing power enterprises is on the rise. As an important link, the operation mode of virtual power plants (VPP) affects the power market and the growth of new energy power generation, and is restricted by many factors, such as thermal power costs. Red mud-metakaolin based geopolymer microspheres (RM-MGMs) with good sphericity and high mechanical strength are prepared via dispersion-suspension-solidification method. title: Urban accidents and safety governance in China (2015–2024): evolution, achievements, and future pathways
abstract: Urban safety governance is critical for China’s sustainable urbanization. This study evaluates the evolution of urban safety governance in China (2015–2024) through a five-dimensional analytical framework—resilience, risk governance, collaborative governance, spatial justice, and system modeling. title: Source evolution controls the molybdenum isotope composition of Archean continental crust
abstract: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. title: Water and carbon fluxes in vineyards under climate change – A review of Eddy-Covariance studies currently dominated by irrigated Mediterranean systems
abstract: Viticulture faces a double challenge under climate change: optimizing water use and contributing to the sequestration of atmospheric CO2. This review synthesizes 25 years of advances in flux stations’ measurements of water vapour and carbon fluxes in vineyards using the eddy-covariance (EC) method, based on a corpus of 92 articles focused on evapotranspiration (ET) and Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE). abstract: Abstract The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) includes fast emerging member states with their trade, investment and industrial policies affecting trans boundary ecosystem. The study examines how tariff laws, tourism, direct foreign investment, industrialization, and inflation affect CO 2 emissions in the transport sector in the SCO members from 1994 to 2024. abstract: Abstract. Agriculture is the largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N2O), primarily due to nitrogen (N) fertilization. Understanding how the influence of key drivers and the relative contribution of source processes change throughout the cropping season is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate N2O emissions. title: Multi-scale Feature Enhanced Network for Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: The task of remote sensing image target detection still faces many challenges: the target scale, orientation and spatial distribution are very different. In particular, small targets are difficult to identify in complex backgrounds, and the change of target geometry will affect feature extraction and positioning accuracy. In view of the above problems, this paper builds an improved detection network MSTD-Net based on YOLO26 m. abstract: Abstract Layer melt crystallization (LMC) is a promising green separation technology for ultrahigh‐purity chemical production, particularly for challenging isomeric mixtures. abstract: ABSTRACT Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) represents a major hydro‐meteorological hazard in Algeria, with its frequency and intensity increasing under the effects of climate change, thereby heightening threats to populations, infrastructure, and ecosystems. Yet existing PMP projections rarely employ multi‐variable bias correction or systematically compare correction methods, which is a critical gap given PMP's dependence on multiple correlated variables. title: Glacier change at the ISM-MLW transition: multi-decadal evidence of spatial heterogeneity from the Sara Umga watershed, western Himalaya
abstract: This study presents a multi-decadal assessment of glacier change in the Sara Umga Watershed (SUW), between the Parvati and Chandra basins. The region receives a majority of its annual precipitation from Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) and a comparatively lower share contributed by winter Mid Latitude Westerlies (MLW). title: Joint optimization of detection, task allocation, and path planning for multi-agent cooperative interception under partial observability
abstract: Safety-critical autonomous systems often require multiple agents to detect, assign, and intercept non-cooperative mobile targets using only partial observations. These subtasks are tightly coupled because the same agents must balance spatial exploration for detection with goal-directed motion for interception, while target maneuvers remain uncertain. abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum–sulfur (Al–S) batteries are promising next‐generation energy storage systems owing to the high abundance, low cost, and multi‐electron redox capability of Al, combined with the high theoretical capacity and environmental friendliness of S. This review systematically compares the dual electrochemical mechanisms based on S reduction (S 0 /S 2− ) and S oxidation (S 0 /S 4+ ), highlighting their distinct advantages in energy density and safety. title: Dynamic interactions between multidimensional civilization development and urban–rural land use behaviors in China
abstract: Understanding how civilization development interacts with land use transformation is critical for advancing sustainable human–land governance. However, existing studies have largely examined land use transitions from socioeconomic or ecological perspectives, while the dynamic feedback mechanisms between multidimensional civilization development and land use behaviors remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Understanding energy accounting is increasingly important because it directly influences our understanding of the energy system and what energy policies make sense. Yet, the confusion has never been more obvious, particularly in the media, consulting arenas and also in some academic work. title: Civil Aviation Cybersecurity in Indonesia: Legal Compliance, Regulatory Gaps, and Reform in Light of ICAO Standards
abstract: Cybersecurity has become an important component of international aviation safety and security as the increasing digitalization of aircraft systems and air traffic management creates new risks for civil aviation. In Indonesia, the expansion of digital infrastructure in the aviation sector requires a coherent legal and institutional response to these risks. abstract: Abstract. Lightning is a spatio-temporal phenomenon comprised of individual strikes with specific occurrence times and spatial coordinates. abstract: La inteligencia artificial tiene cada vez una mayor presencia en las producciones de animación y diseño digital, siendo una herramienta para dirigir las producciones digitales con mayor eficiencia y mostrando resultados competentes. abstract: Precipitation seasonality is a fundamental characteristic of monsoon climates, with direct implications for regional water resources and ecosystem stability. Here, we investigate changes in precipitation seasonality over the Indochina Peninsula and assess the responses to different external forcings. abstract: Using novel technology and dedicated algorithms, the FLuorescence EXplorer (FLEX) will yield information about the health of the world’s plants. This study compared ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) and shaking extraction (SKE) of cucumber and developed an antioxidant-oriented under-eye hydrogel mask. Total phenolic, flavonoid, and polysaccharide contents were determined, and antioxidant activity was assessed using DPPH and FRAP assays. title: Improving the reliability of ultrasonic welding: a hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-EC framework for cost and risk prioritization in mass production
abstract: Our research addresses the limited applicability of traditional reliability assessment methods by implementing a hybrid framework for the Branson 2000X AED ultrasonic welding system in mass production. We aimed to align the quantitative technical framework with the causality and financial impacts of identified failures. This approach created a tool that directly links failure frequency to its systemic causes and economic consequences. title: Forest bathing as a pathway toward ecological identity: a community case study
abstract: Climate and ecological disruption can affect wellbeing, social relationships, and connection to place; when experienced across generations, these widespread disruptions can lead to collective trauma, becoming culturally embedded in identities shared at a community-level. This paper proposes a theoretical model demonstrating the reciprocal relationship between collective trauma and ecological dissociation, defined as diminished capacity for relational connection with the more-than-human world. title: OCE: an optimization convergence metric for LiDAR SLAM degeneracy detection
abstract: Abstract LiDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems suffer from environment-induced degeneracy in geometrically self-similar scenes such as tunnels and cylindrical structures, where the point cloud registration problem becomes ill-conditioned. Existing degeneracy detection methods predominantly rely on eigenvalue analysis of the Hessian matrix, which assesses geometric conditioning at a fixed linearization point. title: Complementary root and mycorrhizal foraging strategies for phosphorus acquisition among arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal trees in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) availability is widely recognized as an important constraint on plant growth in many subtropical forest ecosystems, yet how contrasting mycorrhizal strategies mediate the use of inorganic and organic P forms remains unclear. In a subtropical forest, we integrated a 50‐ha survey of adult tree dominance, a seedling growth survey across six 1‐ha plots and a shade‐house experiment to examine how arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (ECM) trees adjust root‐fungal foraging strategies across gradients of inorganic and organic P availability. title: Piceatannol enhances polymyxin B efficacy against Escherichia coli O157:H7 via inhibition of biofilm formation
abstract: Introduction Escherichia coli O157:H7 ( E. coli O157 ) poses a severe global health threat, particularly due to its ability to form recalcitrant biofilms and the paradoxical exacerbation of life‑threatening haemolytic uraemic syndrome by conventional antibiotics. This study identifies piceatannol as an effective agent that suppresses E. coli O157 biofilm formation in vitro and acts as an adjuvant to enhance antimicrobial efficacy. title: Spatio-Temporal Transformation of Cropping Patterns in the Western Haryana Plains, India: A Five-Decade Analysis (1974-2022)
abstract: The increase in crop productivity resulting from the Green Revolution has had both positive and negative consequences for the natural environment, particularly with respect to water resources. Changes in cropping patterns have also increased the environmental risks associated with agricultural activities. The present study examines the long-term spatio-temporal changes in cropping patterns in the Western Haryana Plains of northern India during 1974 to 2022, with special emphasis on the expansion of wheat and paddy cultivation using geospatial data. title: Personality traits, coping styles, and perceived stress across polish military formations and a civilian comparison group
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined differences in personality traits, coping styles, and perceived stress across three Polish military formations and a civilian comparison group, and associations of personality traits and coping styles with perceived stress. The sample comprised 193 men: 37 Special Forces soldiers, 54 Regular Army soldiers, 48 Territorial Defence Forces (WOT) soldiers, and 54 civilIians without military service experience. Space-based military technologies are re-emerging as central elements of contemporary strategic competition. The weaponisation of outer space is no longer a hypothetical concern but an increasingly evident reality shaping the global security environment. title: Sesgo de automatización: impactos psicológicos en el candidato y el empleado.
abstract: La transición hacia una gestión del talento basada en algoritmos predictivos ha transformado radicalmente el reclutamiento y la evaluación del desempeño. Aunque estas herramientas prometen una precisión matemática y eficiencia operativa, su implementación genera tensiones psicológicas profundas tanto en candidatos como en empleados. Uno de los principales desafíos es el sesgo de automatización, definido como la confianza desproporcionada que los reclutadores otorgan a los sistemas tecnológicos, llegando a delegar su responsabilidad ética en algoritmos cuya lógica suele ser opaca. title: Alfabetización en inteligencia artificial para la transformación de la práctica docente en la Educación Superior
abstract: La rápida incorporación de herramientas de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (IAG) en Instituciones de Educación Superior (IES), ha transformado e impulsado significativamente nuevos procesos de enseñanza, aprendizaje, transmisión y gestión del conocimiento, este escenario ha puesto de manifiesto la alfabetización en Inteligencia Artificial (IA) derivada del uso de estas tecnologías en los contextos educativos. title: ARISE: an urban political economy-informed resilience indicator framework for south asian metropolitan cities
abstract: Introduction Existing urban resilience indicator frameworks combine literature-derived pooling, expert validation, and multi-criteria weighting independently of any explicit theory of why some urban conditions, rather than others, are politically constituted as resilience priorities. Methods This paper’s contribution is methodological: it demonstrates how Urban Political Economy (UPE) theory can condition an indicator-development pipeline, from category structure through to how weighting outcomes are interpreted against theoretical commitments. title: Performance of the water cycle algorithm in optimal economic design of passive power filter
abstract: Abstract Harmonic distortion in power systems, caused mostly by nonlinear loads, results in significant power quality (PQ) issues such as higher losses, lower power factor (PF), and equipment malfunctions. Passive power filters (PPFs), which use tuned combinations of inductors and capacitors to attenuate specific harmonic frequencies, are widely used because of their lower cost and simpler design compared to active filtering systems. title: Sustainable Agriculture Development Based on Green Economy to Improve Work Ethic and Economy of the Community in Indonesia
abstract: This study explores the development of sustainable agriculture based on the principles of green economics and Islamic ethics to strengthen work ethic and improve the welfare of the community in Gisting Regency, Tanggamus Regency, Lampung, Indonesia. Based on the Islamic Green Economics and Ethical Sustainability Framework (IGEESF), this research integrates environmental responsibility, ethical awareness, and socio-economic transformation in a rural context. title: A new delta-headed branchiosaurid temnospondyl from the early Permian Meisenheim Formation of Germany
abstract: Two temnospondyl specimens from the Ruthweiler deposit (M8) in the early Permian Meisenheim Formation of the Saar-Nahe Basin are identified as pertaining to a new branchiosaurid taxon, Schoenfelderpeton brevifrons . They are distinct from all other temnospondyls in the region by the delta-shaped skull, small orbits, and short frontals. The maxilla fails to contact the cheek and has tiny, pin-shaped teeth, a feature that persists in the mature specimen. title: “Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany (Italy): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling
abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany (Italy) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi-source geospatial datasets.

title: Development and multi-response optimization of sustainable hemp fibre/cassia gum reinforced polyester hybrid composites for structural and insulation applications
abstract: Abstract The growing demand for lightweight and sustainable materials has prompted the development of natural fibre-reinforced polymer composites with multi-functional properties. In this study, hemp fiber/Cassia gum reinforced polyester hybrid composites (HC0–HC5) were prepared by hand lay-up and then compression molding. The effect of Cassia gum loading on mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, morphological, and water absorption properties was systematically investigated. title: Analysis of Landslide Susceptibility Toward the Presence of Accommodation Areas (Glamping and Villas) in Kejajar District, Wonosobo Regency, 2025
abstract: This study aims to analyze and map the level of landslide susceptibility in accommodation areas in Kejajar District, Wonosobo Regency, using a Geographic Information System (GIS) approach. Scoring, weighting, and overlay methods were applied to integrate rainfall, slope gradient, soil type, geology, and land-use parameters. The results indicate that Kejajar District is divided into three landslide susceptibility classes: high susceptibility covering 4,936 ha (76%), moderate susceptibility covering 1,515 ha (23%), and low susceptibility covering 37 ha (<1%). title: Autoría académica y continuidad de la agencia ante la inteligencia artificial generativa: una aproximación filosófico-educativa para la evaluación universitaria
abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) invita a revisar la relación entre la calidad de un trabajo universitario, el estudiante que lo firma y el aprendizaje que la institución pretende reconocer. Este ensayo analiza en qué condiciones un producto mediado por IAG puede atribuirse responsablemente al estudiante y constituirse como evidencia válida de aprendizaje. title: Meta-bird mating optimizer for combinatorial optimization problems
abstract: Combinatorial optimization problems, such as the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and the Berth Allocation Problem (BAP), are challenging problems due to their complex search spaces. These challenges require an effective optimization with an efficient balance between exploration (searching through new areas of the solution space) and exploitation (refining existing solutions). title: Culinary Chemistry as a Platform for Interfacial Materials Design
abstract: ABSTRACT This Review examines culinary systems as experimentally accessible models of interfacial materials design. Culinary operations, including emulsification, foaming, gelation, spherification, controlled heating, smoking, and dehydration, govern gas‐liquid, oil‐water, solid‐liquid, polymer‐nanoparticle, and hydrogel‐analyte interfaces, thereby coupling microstructure to transport, mechanics, optical response, and sensory performance. title: Farmers’ knowledge, attitudes and perceptions of green hydrogen in Oshikoto Region, Namibia
abstract: Introduction: Commercial farmers in Namibia’s Oshikoto Region operate under drought, water scarcity, high agricultural input costs and uneven rural energy access. Although Namibia has prioritised green hydrogen within its industrial and energy strategies, limited farmer-level evidence explains how potential agricultural applications are understood and evaluated. title: Non-destructive Evaluation of the Properties of Self-compacting Concrete Using Ultrasonic Testing and a Rebound Hammer
abstract: This study aims to improve the estimation of concrete compressive strength by combining destructive and non-destructive testing (ultrasound and sclerometer) to obtain a more precise and reliable assessment for quality control and the diagnosis of concrete structures. The experimental data were analyzed using a program linked to the Pundit Lab measurement tool to establish a regression model linking the ultrasonic propagation velocity (UPV) to the compressive strength of self-compacting concrete (SCC). title: Life Under the Snow: Camera Trap Videos Capture Year‐Round Lemming Activity and Behavior
abstract: Studying Arctic animals in winter is challenging, particularly for cryptic species like lemmings, which live within the snowpack for protection from the cold. Winter reproduction is thought to be a crucial component of their cyclic fluctuations, yet little is known about their winter behavior and demography. Camera traps are widely used to study animal ecology, but none are specifically designed for animal life beneath the snow under harsh conditions. title: Shaped by humans but increasingly threatened: pathways for the conservation of Palaearctic grasslands
abstract: Palaearctic grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems of the Northern Hemisphere, but their conservation depends on continued management that must be reconciled with agricultural production, rural livelihoods and other socio-economic demands. Introducing a special issue that brings together 18 contributions from across Eurasia, we synthesize the interacting pressures shaping these grasslands and identify pathways towards their effective conservation. title: Assessment of multiple ecosystem services and interrelation-ships in Forest-rich regions: a case study of Guilin, China
abstract: Ecosystem services (ES) are fundamental to achieving human well-being. To systematically evaluate ES and their interrelationships in forest-enriched regions, this study takes Guilin, a representative forest-rich area in China, as the study area and develops an integrated coupling model for the comprehensive measurement and interaction analysis of provisioning, regulating, and cultural ES. The InVEST model was used to quantify provisioning and regulating ES. title: Habitat Suitability Modeling of Bombus affinis under Climate Change
abstract: The North American bumble bee Bombus affinis (B. affinis) is an important wild pollinator that has experienced severe population declines since the late 20th century. However, spatially explicit assessments of how climate change and human activities jointly shape its distribution remain limited, constraining forward-looking conservation planning. title: Land Cover Change, Ecosystem Service Implications, and Economy–Land Use Decoupling:
abstract: Land cover change plays a critical role in shaping watershed ecological conditions and supporting regional economic activities. This study analyzes land cover dynamics in the Tiworo Watershed, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, for 2014, 2019, and 2024, and examines their relationship with sectoral economic growth. Remote sensing and GIS were used to map and quantify land cover changes, while sectoral Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP) data for agriculture, forestry, and fisheries represented economic performance. journal: International Review for Spatial Planning and Sustainable Development

title: Neotypification of Three Names in Myristica (Myristicaceae)
abstract: ABSTRACT In absence of the original materials, neotypes are proposed for three names. These are Myristica cagayanensis, Myristica hellwigii , and Myristica sulcata. These neotypifcations will be helpful in correct application of these three names.

title: Does higher-resolution climate forcing improve impact model performance?
abstract: Abstract Climate-impact assessments increasingly use high-resolution climate forcing, often assuming that finer spatial detail improves impact projections. Yet this assumption has rarely been tested systematically across impact sectors, regions, and forcing variables. Here we use coordinated simulations from 16 impact models participating in the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISIMIP) to evaluate how increasing forcing resolution from 60 km to 10 km, 3 km, and 1 km affects both climate-input accuracy and impact-model performance. title: Spatially explicit modeling of future land use and land cover dynamics in the São Francisco River Basin, Brazil
abstract: Future land use and land cover (LULC) changes in major Brazilian river basins may pose substantial challenges for water resource management by altering streamflow regimes, reducing water availability, affecting ecosystem services, and increasing pressure on vulnerable hydrological systems. This study projected LULC scenarios for 2050 in the São Francisco River Basin, Brazil, to identify potential spatial changes in LULC. title: Sheer-Dam: A structural-health and energy-efficient routing protocol for wireless sensor networks in dam monitoring
abstract: Large dam vibrations will be assessed by using a sensor network as part of the proposed protocol. The other main components of the proposed protocol are dual-threshold selective reporting and structurally-based clustering methods which provide for nodes to report only vibration readings that have deviated from what is normal operationally; all vibration readings need not be reported. The communication overhead associated with this protocol is reduced through local filtering. title: Profiles of cybervictimization among college students and associated psychosocial patterns: a latent profile and network analysis
abstract: Introduction Cybervictimization has become a prevalent global public concern as it threatens the wellbeing of young people. Understanding the distinct patterns of cybervictimization, along with their associated factors is crucial for developing effective interventions. Methods A total of 1,009 college students were selected from three comprehensive universities in Shandong Province, China, via convenience sampling. title: Capillary-driven Water Transport in Microfiber Textiles: Experimental Characterization and Application in a High-efficiency Multi-stage Passive Solar Desalination
abstract: Given the escalating water and energy crises worldwide, the development of passive desalination systems has become inevitable. Among various approaches, particular attention has been directed toward capillary-driven systems, yet despite numerous studies in this field, selecting textiles with optimal capillary and evaporative properties remains a key research challenge. title: Recurrent hotspot zones of projected heat and dry-spell persistence across MENA
abstract: Persistent heat and dryness increasingly shape climate risk by extending exposure time, yet future projections are often communicated as pixel-wise changes that obscure recurrent spatial organisation. Here we identify recurrent hotspot zones of projected heat and dry-spell persistence across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Using an ERA5-anchored Stacking-EML product integrating six CMIP6 simulations under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, we quantify changes in the Warm Spell Duration Index (WSDI) and Consecutive Dry Days (CDD) across three future horizons. title: Estudio de modelos de lenguaje (LLMs) para la deteccion de riesgo de psicosis
abstract: La identificación temprana de riesgo de psicosis representa un desafío importante para la psiquiatría computacional. Investigaciones previas han demostrado que el análisis automatizado del discurso, mediante técnicas como el Análisis Semántico Latente (LSA) y el etiquetado de partes del discurso (POS-tagging), puede predecir la transición a la psicosis con notable precisión. title: Global grassland productivity and carbon storage benefit from functional diversity under climate change
abstract: Functional diversity plays an important role for ecosystem services of managed grasslands such as their gross primary productivity (GPP) and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. Yet vegetation models assessing functional diversity have been limited to small spatial scales. We used the Lund-Potsdam-Jena managed land (LPJmL) competitor stress-tolerant ruderal (CSR) model to assess the role of functional diversity for managed grassland GPP and SOC under climate change at the global scale. title: Elastic–Plastic Modeling and Experimental Characterization of Granular Jamming Actuators
abstract: Granular jamming enables soft actuators to transition rapidly between compliant and rigid states, yet the disordered microstructure of jammed particles has long precluded rapid predictive modeling. Here, we develop and validate a pressure‐dependent moment–curvature constitutive framework based on elastic‐perfectly‐plastic mechanics, describing the evolution of internal stress distributions during loading and unloading for granular jammed beams spanning vacuum pressures from 0 to 101 kPa and a broad geometric design space. title: THE INTERNAL LOGIC AND PRACTICAL PATHS OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY EMPOWERING THE HIGH-QUALITY DEVELOPMENT OF CHINA'S TOURISM ECONOMY
abstract: Tourism is a people's livelihood and well-being industry with strong comprehensiveness and driving force, and a key lever for expanding domestic demand, boosting consumption, and stabilizing employment. In 2025, China's tourism economy got off to a strong start and continued to rise: domestic tourist trips reached 6.522 billion and total tourism spending reached 6.30 trillion yuan, up 16.2% and 9.5% year on year respectively, both setting new historical records; inbound visits by foreign nationals reached 82.035 million, up 26.4% year on year, and the tourism economy as a whole entered a new c

title: Sub-minute fatigue monitoring for enhanced lifetime assessment of wind turbines
abstract: Abstract. Accurate fatigue damage estimation is a critical step for managing and extending the life of wind turbine fleets, and the basis on which operators decide whether an ageing asset can be kept in service beyond the end of design life. The most accurate estimation relies on continuous high-frequency strain measurements processed with rainflow cycle counting. title: Parallel science and technology for C2 in the agentic age: from military operations to peaceful sustainability and resiliency
abstract: Abstract Command and control (C2) has traditionally been framed as a military problem of sensing, deciding, coordinating, and acting under uncertainty, conflict, and time pressure. In the agentic age, however, this problem is being extended far beyond the battlefield, as human organizations become increasingly embedded in hybrid environments composed of artificial agents, digital twins, social sensing networks, foundation models, autonomous platforms, and cyber–physical–social institutions. title: Development and evaluation of the ECHAM6-iMAPLE v1.0 coupled atmosphere–ecosystem model
abstract: Abstract. Land-atmosphere interactions play a fundamental role in regulating climate variability, ecosystem productivity, and air quality through coupled exchanges of energy, water, carbon, and reactive trace gases. However, many Earth system models adopt simplified representations of vegetation physiological processes, leading to biases in terrestrial carbon and water fluxes and increased uncertainties in climate simulations. title: Distribution, habitat, and population dynamics of the European weatherfish (Misgurnus fossilis L., 1758) in the north-easternmost part of Germany
abstract: This study analyses a distribution database of fishes and cyclostomes from the German federal state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and evaluates a monitoring programme initiated in 2008, with a focus on the ecology of the European weatherfish. Over 35 years, the species was recorded across nearly the entire state, but it was rarely found in high abundances. title: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact
abstract: Abstract The U.S. federal government undertook a flurry of new actions to monitor and regulate methane emissions beginning in years 2021 and 2022, including the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). The IRA and Waste Emissions Charge (WEC) represent a historic legislative effort to regulate U.S. methane emissions, yet its early effectiveness remains empirically unverified. Here we estimate changes in U.S. oil and gas methane emissions during 2019--2024 using an inverse model constrained by satellite observations. title: Can Beauty Save the World? A Multimethod Analysis of Regulatory Focus Appeals in Climate Change Advertising
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates how organizations can strategically design climate change advertising to foster greater consumer involvement by comparing the effectiveness of promotion‐ and prevention‐focused advertising appeals. Using a sequential explanatory mixed‐methods design, a facial coding experiment revealed that promotion appeals reduced sadness, which in turn positively influenced attitudes toward the ad and increased climate change involvement. title: Organizational and administrative requirements of NGOs for environmental crisis response: a field study of civil associations
abstract: Environmental crises are increasing in frequency and severity across Egypt, yet the organizational requirements of civil society organizations for effective response to these events remain insufficiently documented. This cross-sectional census survey assessed the administrative, human resource, financial, and legislative requirements necessary for effective environmental crisis response among non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in Aswan, Egypt. title: Reevaluating how tree canopy cools the air and surfaces in cities at very high resolution
abstract: Abstract Tree canopy mitigates urban heat, yet the magnitude and spatial distribution of the cooling effect, particularly for air temperature, remain poorly understood. While land surface temperature (LST) is frequently used in urban heat studies, it is neither a good proxy for metrics of human thermal comfort nor does it adequately predict air temperature. title: TSI-AsphaLab: an Open-source Software for Calibrating and Simulating the Thermo-Stiffness Integration (TSI) Model
abstract: Abstract This study presents TSI-AsphaLab , an open-source software developed to calibrate and simulate the Thermo-Stiffness Integration (TSI) model. Based on thermodynamics concepts and the time-temperature superposition principle, the TSI model accurately represents the stiffness modulus of asphalt mixtures along a wide range of loading conditions (i.e., frequency and temperature) without requiring shift factors. title: Bridging design disciplines: a literature review of biologically-inspired design, human-centered design, and human-robot interaction
abstract: Abstract As robotic technologies become more integrated into society, there is a growing demand for systems that are not only technically robust, but also socially accepted, safe, and designed for long-term use. Biologically-Inspired Design (BID), Human-Centered Design (HCD), and Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) each offer valuable theories, methodologies, and tools to support the design and evaluation of such systems. abstract: Background Complex diabetes-related foot infections (DFIs) frequently involve tissue necrosis, impaired perfusion, bacterial persistence, and residual dead space, which may complicate infection control despite surgical and systemic antimicrobial treatment. Bioabsorbable calcium sulfate provides a potential means of delivering high local antibiotic concentrations after surgical source control. abstract: Wireless rechargeable sensor network (WRSN) employs a Mobile Charger that mitigates sensor's energy depletion helps to maximize active node counts (operational size) and minimizing node downtime (disconnection time). abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic yield of ancillary investigations in children presenting with new-onset seizure-like events (SLEs) at a tertiary first seizure clinic (FSC). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 1213 children evaluated for new-onset SLEs at a tertiary FSC. title: Assessing the impact of sand mining on economic growth and environmental degradation across countries
abstract: Changes in land use, carbon emissions, biodiversity loss, natural resource scarcity, and ecosystem degradation pose significant threats to global sustainability. While previous research has examined various environmental challenges, the role of sand extraction remains comparatively unexplored. This study investigates the impact of sand mining, economic growth, income inequality, democracy, environmental policy stringency, and biodiversity loss on environmental quality, measured by ecological footprint, land-use change, and carbon emissions in the BRICS, G7, and MENA countries during 1990–2022.

abstract: By 2030, pluvial flooding is estimated to cause nearly $500 billion in global damage, affecting 54 million people (UNDRR, 2015) each year. This rising risk has sparked an increased interest in nature-based solutions (NbS), as traditional hydraulic infrastructure may lack the flexibility required to manage more complex flood hazards. title: Estacionalidad y variabilidad espacial de las lluvias en la Patagonia Austral Continental
abstract: La precipitación es uno de los fenómenos meteorológicos con mayor variabilidad espacial y temporal, y su estacionalidad influye de manera directa en la provisión de servicios ecosistémicos y en la productividad primaria neta de pastizales y cultivos, especialmente en ambientes áridos y semiáridos. En este estudio se analizó la estacionalidad de la precipitación para el período 1995-2014 y su variabilidad espacial y temporal en la Patagonia Austral Continental. Se utilizaron datos mensuales normalizados y reticulados, disponibles en el Banco de Datos Hidrometeorológicos de INTA EEA Santa Cruz.

abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of COVID-19 cases and mortality is important for identifying high-risk areas and strengthening global public health preparedness. Although many COVID-19 spatial studies have been conducted at national or regional scales, fewer have applied a consistent global spatial framework to compare the clustering of both reported cases and deaths. title: Rapid Quantification of Fatty Acids in Fish Eggs Through Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT In aquaculture, omega‐3 fatty acids (FAs) are essential for fish health and growth during early development, making them important indicators of egg quality. The current standard for measuring FAs relies on analytical instruments that require complex sample preparation and long analysis times. In contrast, Raman spectroscopy can obtain the chemical fingerprint of an egg sample within seconds. abstract: Trash screens are essential components in open channels for debris capture and the protection of downstream hydraulic structures. However, debris accumulation can significantly alter flow conditions and reduce conveyance efficiency. While previous research has primarily quantified blockage based on the cross-sectional area, the longitudinal length of accumulation a common real-world phenomenon has received limited attention and has not been investigated independently. abstract: This study examines how communication technology shapes contemporary globalization and why the same technologies can simultaneously integrate and divide the world. Earlier scholarship has documented either the integrative or the exclusionary effects of digital media, but few studies explain the conditions under which each outcome prevails. abstract: The equine sector provides employment opportunities and leisure activities for a substantial number of people in Sweden. Although these activities are closely connected to nature and dependent on ecosystem services, the sector faces significant ecological challenges. This article explores how representatives of the equine sector—particularly riding schools—conceptualize and articulate their work with environmental sustainability in policy documents and “talk about” everyday practice. abstract: La disponibilidad de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) contrasta con las dificultades de las empresas de menor tamaño para integrarlas en sus operaciones. abstract: Scholarship on Islamic legal pluralism has largely taken the Sharia court as its measure of institutional significance, asking how Islamic norms are incorporated, accommodated, or made enforceable by the state. abstract: Amidst technological changes and escalating data consumption, this article addresses the necessity to evaluate and measure the impact of administrative process digitization and systematization on the healthcare sector. abstract: El grafiti se consolidó como un medio de expresión artística dentro del espacio urbano y atravesó diversos contextos sociales. Surgió como una manifestación visual asociada a la protesta, la identidad y la apropiación del espacio público. abstract: This article assesses the impact of the digital economy on industry and the environment by comparing 15 countries (7 developed and 8 developing) over the period 2000–2021. abstract: Drawing on Türkiye’s illegal military invasion of the independent island Republic of Cyprus and occupation of Cypriot territory, classic strategic theory, and empirical war studies, this article delineates a pattern of revisionist strategy. abstract: Abstract The study examines three Chinese art districts—Beijing 798, Hangzhou Xiangshan, and Jingdezhen Taoxichuan—using 28,661 social media posts. abstract: Background To determine whether a biomarker-derived injury score integrating exercise-induced cytokine responses with mitochondrial and bioenergetic readouts improves short-term injury risk stratification in professional football players compared with normalized TPL and high-intensity running distance (HIRD). abstract: Abstract Intermediate wheatgrass (IWG; Thinopyrum intermedium ) is a perennial grain crop that offers many environmental benefits through extensive root systems in addition to food production. abstract: This study investigated personality traits as predictors of psychological well-being among health workers in Gboko Local Government Area of Benue state, Nigeria. abstract: La presente investigación analiza la incidencia de Palantir Foundry en el comercio exterior ecuatoriano a partir de su incorporación al sistema aduanero nacional en mayo de 2025. abstract: New Quality Productive Forces (NQPF) have become China’s primary policy imperative to drive high-quality development of its economy. abstract: La incorporación de sistemas de inteligencia artificial generativa a los procesos evaluativos de la educación superior ha desplazado el debate desde la factibilidad técnica hacia la definición del lugar que ocupa el juicio profesional docente en el ciclo de retroalimentación. abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines have reshaped modern vaccinology by enabling rapid antigen design, scalable manufacturing, and coordinated induction of humoral and cellular immunity. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an escalating global health crisis, yet patterns of public understanding and antibiotic consumption in the Middle East and North Africa remain under-researched. This study aimed to evaluate the current landscape of AMR awareness, knowledge gaps, and self-medication practices among the general populations of seven Middle Eastern and North African nations. abstract: La transformación digital de la profesión contable plantea la necesidad de revisar cómo los profesores de educación superior seleccionan, utilizan y evalúan las tecnologías en sus asignaturas. abstract: Abstract Ciprofloxacin is widely used as a drug for broad-spectrum treatment of infections. However, it is classified as class IV by the Biopharmaceutics Classification System, being characterized by low solubility and permeability. Aiming to contribute to the rational design that may improve the biopharmaceutical properties to increase drug efficacy, two series of prototypical compounds were designed: (1) ciprofloxacin prodrugs and (2) ciprofloxacin dendrimer prodrugs. title: A Living Multi‐Omics PDX Biobank of High‐Risk Sarcomas Reveals ecDNA‐Driven Oncogene Amplification in Osteosarcoma and Enables Preclinical Precision Oncology
abstract: Sarcomas are rare, genomically heterogeneous malignancies for which prognosis has remained poor and largely unchanged over recent decades. Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models are an important tool for cancer research, but their availability and utility remain limited in sarcoma. Here, we establish the SGH sarcoma PDX biobank, a living multi-omics resource comprising 155 xenografts from 132 patients across 11 sarcoma histotypes, with osteosarcoma as the predominant subtype. This cohort is enriched for high-risk sarcomas characterized by poor prognosis and widespread copy-number alterations.

abstract: Introduction Marburg virus (MARV) is a hemorrhagic fever virus, and its glycoprotein (GP) represents an important target for vaccine research. MHC class I (MHC-I)-restricted T cell epitopes are critical for inducing cytotoxic CD8 + T cell responses. In this study, we aimed to identify MHC-I-restricted T cell epitopes derived from the MARV Angola strain GP through an integrated bioinformatics and experimental approach. Ayurvedic classics describe various Doṣaja variants of Mūtrakṛcchra, each exhibiting distinct clinical manifestations. abstract: Urban dredged silt has a weak structure and poor water stability, which limit its direct infrastructure reuse. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior plantea nuevas oportunidades y desafíos para el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes universitarios. abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. This study provides a comprehensive review of the historical evolution and current status of R-factor estimation, ranging from simplified empirical equations to complex process-based models. Special emphasis is placed on data requirements, model assumptions, and method transferability. title: Balancing Profit and Planet: Introducing the CARE Framework for Firms' Ethical Climate Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change presents an urgent ethical and strategic challenge for contemporary business, demanding responses that are both morally grounded and competitively viable. This paper proposes the CARE framework, Comprehend , Align , Refine , and Evaluate , a structured model for ethical climate strategy rooted in resource‐advantage ( R‐A ) theory and foundational ethical principles. abstract: Background Severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with increased morbidity and mortality, particularly among patients with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity. abstract: Thailand is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change, ranked 8th by the Global Climate Risk Index (CRI) for the period 1999–2018. abstract: Introduction: Herbal medicine is among the oldest therapeutic traditions and is deeply rooted in European spa culture, most fully expressed in the system of Sebastian Kneipp. In Polish spas, however, phytotherapy is used only marginally, and public knowledge of medicinal plants is fading. Aim: To assess the knowledge of phytotherapy and attitudes towards its use in spa treatment and in self-treatment among spa patients, visitors and residents of the Polish spa town of Inowrocław, answering five research questions with five research and five statistical hypotheses. abstract: ABSTRACT Tectonic fractures and bedding‐parallel fractures jointly develop in continental shale reservoirs, providing critical storage space and efficient flow pathways for hydrocarbons. abstract: Data cubes are p-dimensional data structures (p ≥ 3). abstract: La gamificación digital se ha situado como una estrategia para fomentar experiencias de aprendizaje más motivadoras, participativas e inclusivas, si bien sus efectos son influenciados por el diseño pedagógico y las condiciones de aplicación. abstract: This study provides a systematic exploration of whether neighbourhood-level built environment factors are associated with mental health service (MHS) utilisation by Indigenous peoples in South-East Queensland, Australia, while controlling for individual socio-demographic factors. abstract: One of the biggest misconceptions about clonal bacterial populations is that all members act identically. In fact, microbiologists have known for decades that genetically identical populations of bacteria are capable of reproducibly generating subgroups with differential gene expression. abstract: Arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis and gout, imposes increasing clinical and economic burdens. Current diagnostic tools such as serology, imaging, and clinical assessments are episodic, resource-intensive, and insufficient for capturing the daily dynamics of disease activity. Epidermal sweat sensing has emerged as a promising non-invasive technique for at-home physiological tracking. abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used as operational interfaces that connect physical assets, engineering models, and instantaneous data. This review develops an integrative framework for Saudi Arabian facilities and projects, where rapid infrastructure delivery, challenging climate, and high-risk operations require proactive risk management. Accelerated by urbanization, land-use changes have significantly exacerbated climate change and disrupted carbon dynamics. title: DESAFÍOS EDUCATIVOS FRENTE A LOS RESULTADOS DE PISA EN ESTUDIANTES DE EDUCACIÓN MEDIA DE PARAGUAY: PERSPECTIVAS DE DOCENTES, FAMILIAS Y ESTADO
abstract: Los resultados de Paraguay en el Programa para la Evaluación Internacional de los Estudiantes (PISA) 2022 evidencian importantes desafíos en los aprendizajes de los estudiantes de 15 años. Solo el 15 % alcanzó al menos el nivel 2 de competencia en Matemática, frente al 34 % en Lectura y el 29 % en Ciencias (OECD, 2023). Estos resultados constituyen un punto de partida para analizar las condiciones que intervienen en el proceso educativo y los aspectos que requieren fortalecimiento. title: Contrasting species composition between common and rare woody species in the intake area of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project
abstract: Understanding the species composition and structural dynamics of both common and rare species in forest communities is fundamental to comprehending forest ecosystem functioning. The intake area of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, recognized as an ecologically sensitive region, harbors forest communities that play a pivotal role in water resource conservation and regional environmental stability. title: Sustainable water management in urban areas of Pakistan: challenges and future policy directions
abstract: Urban water management challenges in Pakistan are intensifying due to the rapid urbanization, increasing population, rising demand for limited water resources, climate change and inadequate infrastructure. The issues of water insecurity and unsustainable urban development are growing because of water scarcity, depleting groundwater reserves, poor water quality, urban flooding and lack of water governance. title: From Moralizing to Textual Mechanization: The Trajectory of Efferent Reduction and Aesthetic Erosion in Teaching Folkloric Texts
abstract: This study investigates how 48 folktales from the official textbooks of Indonesian subjects at the elementary through high school levels are presented, as well as the reductions that occur as a result of pedagogical processes. Focusing on text reduction and its evaluation, the main objective of this study is to test the application of Bloom’s cognition taxonomy and pedagogical reduction through the framework of transactional reading theory. title: Pre-mining baseline characterization of groundwater quality using integrated water quality indices around metalliferous deposits, northeastern Algeria

abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) provides a sustainable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis; however, achieving concurrent high activity, high selectivity and appropriate stability of catalysts remains a substantial challenge. title: Implementation of universal welfare policies in the Global South: a case study of Indonesia’s free nutritious meal program
abstract: Introduction Universal welfare policies are increasingly adopted by countries in the Global South as instruments for human development and state legitimacy. However, uniform policy designs often encounter diverse social, economic, institutional, and geographical conditions. This study examines the implementation of Indonesia’s Free Nutritious Meal Program (Program Makan Bergizi Gratis, MBG) in North Sulawesi Province, focusing on the interaction between national policy content and local implementation contexts. title: Economic Development and Human Security: Evidence from Muhanga District, Rwanda
abstract: Economic development is widely recognized as a key engine of human security by improving livelihoods, access to essential services, and resilience to socio-economic vulnerabilities. However, limited empirical evidence exists at the district level in Rwanda on this relationship. This research explored the relationship between economic development and human security in Muhanga District, Rwanda. A cross-sectional survey design was used with 402 household respondents. journal: International Journal Of Humanities Education and Social Sciences (IJHESS)

title: Long-term exposure to ambient air pollution and lipid profiles: a longitudinal study in a heavily industrialized region of northern China
abstract: Background Dyslipidemia is an important modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and growing evidence suggests that long-term ambient air pollution exposure may adversely affect lipid metabolism. However, longitudinal evidence from heavily industrialized regions with complex multipollutant exposure remains limited. Methods We conducted a repeated-measures study of 9,040 adults with 19,113 lipid measurements from a health-screening program in Shanxi Province, China, between October 2019 and September 2023. title: Methane bursts during spring thaw in the permafrost region of Northeast China
abstract: Spring thaw in permafrost regions is associated with episodic bursts in atmospheric methane concentration. In this study, these methane bursts were investigated across different permafrost types in Northeast China. MODIS data and Sentinel-5P methane observations were used to derive the thaw onset date and methane burst timing, respectively. Results showed that methane bursts exhibited distinct spatial and interannual variability. title: Effect of Waste Engine Oil Treatment on Moisture Absorption and Hygroscopic Performance of Selected Tropical Hardwoods

title: Structural Evolution of the International Migration Network (1990 – 2024)
abstract: Las migraciones internacionales configuran una red compleja de relaciones entre países que evoluciona a lo largo del tiempo. En este trabajo analizamos la estructura y evolución del sistema migratorio mundial entre 1990 y 2024 modelando los stocks del dataset UN International Migrant Stock como un grafo dirigido y ponderado, donde los nodos son países y las aristas representan volúmenes de migrantes entre pares origen-destino. title: Exploraciones digestivas. La relación estética y conceptual entre cine y performance en la película Crímenes del futuro de David Cronenberg
abstract: The paper argues that the film Crimes of the Future opens up a critical dialogue on the relationship between the body and technology through two controversial figures in the world of performance art: Orlan and Stelarc. The tensions arising from this relationship are framed by the premise that the evolution of bodies is not to be found in the body-machine hybridisation and prosthetics; rather, it lies in the mysterious rebellion of the organs: the organ in question—or rather, the system in conflict—is here the digestive system. title: A comprehensive analysis of pyrimidine, pyrazine, pyridazine, and piperazine derivatives as effective organic corrosion inhibitors within corrosive aqueous environments
abstract: Corrosion represents a substantial challenge across various industries, frequently resulting in the pronounced degradation of metallic structures. Organic corrosion inhibitors contribute to alleviating this challenge by establishing a protective film over metallic surfaces, thus diminishing or preventing corrosion. Among these inhibitors, nitrogen-based heterocyclic compounds are widely employed due to their ability to form robust coordination bonds with metal atoms. title: The Production, Characterization, and Biodegradation Kinetics of Bioplastics From Starch Extracted From Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta Tubers
abstract: ABSTRACT The accumulation of non‐biodegradable plastics is driving the search for environmentally friendly, low‐cost alternatives. This study investigated the production of biodegradable bioplastics using starch extracted from Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta tubers. The tubers were pulverized, and starch was extracted. Bioplastic was produced by reacting the starch with ethanoic, methanoic, and propanoic acids in the presence of glycerol and water at 80°C for 25 min. title: A Self‐Sustained System for Producing Green Hydrogen via Moisture Power
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a self‐sustaining system that directly converts atmospheric moisture into green hydrogen, eliminating reliance on intermittent renewables and liquid water sources. The core of the system is a multifunctional hydrogel device that integrates moisture‐enabled electricity generation, atmospheric water harvesting, and electrolysis into a seamless operation. Concerted ion diffusion and active electrode chemistry in the gel yield a stable power output of 1.87 V and 450 μA cm −2 , while its hygroscopic components capture water at 1.318 g g −1 . title: Debt of gratitude: The pilgrim teen caught in a vicious cycle in Karen Tei Yamashita’s Through the Arc of the Rain Forest
abstract: Debt comes in all shapes and sizes: from minuscule economic baggage to downright bankruptcy, whether financial or psychological. In Through the Arc of the Rain Forest by Karen Tei Yamashita, one of the chief characters, Chico Paco, turns his life around when encountering the metaphorical rainbow of Brazilian culture, falling into an intriguing form of debt. Carrying on the will of his aged neighbor, the so-called angel becomes entangled in a seemingly mystical whirlpool of performing pilgrimage on behalf of others unable or less able to do so. title: The Papua New Guinea snakebite partnership: a retrospective study of snakebite epidemiology and management, 2018-2023
abstract: Background Snakebite envenoming is a major public health challenge across Papua New Guinea (PNG). Since 2018, the PNG Snakebite Partnership has distributed life-saving Australian antivenoms to health centres across PNG, trained healthcare workers in appropriate snakebite patient management, and collected snakebite patient data to map the impact of snakebite at participating health centres. Here, we report on the snakebite patient data collected through the PNG Snakebite Partnership between 2018 and 2023. title: Innovación en las elecciones: Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial para el fortalecimiento de la democracia
abstract: México es una República federal, ubicada en América del Norte, donde se realizan elecciones federales, estatales y municipales para renovar diversos cargos públicos. La incorporación de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y del voto electrónico ha sido propuesta como una alternativa para modernizar los procesos. El problema de investigación consistió en determinar si el uso de estas tecnologías puede contribuir al fortalecimiento de la democracia. La hipótesis plantea que su incorporación puede contribuir a dicho fortalecimiento, siempre que su implementación esté sujeta a regulación y supervisión

title: Histopathological lung damage associated with Sebekia sp. in farmed Crocodylus moreletii from Campeche, Mexico
abstract: Abstract Pentastomids are parasitic arthropods that infect the respiratory tract of vertebrates, with the genus Sebekia being particularly associated with crocodilians. In October 2023, a postmortem examination was performed on a farmed Crocodylus moreletii in Campeche, Mexico. title: Fundamentals of ion transport in polyethylene oxide- and polyvinylidene fluoride-based battery polymer solid electrolytes
abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are promising candidates for next-generation solid-state lithium batteries, but their practical application is limited by insufficient room-temperature ionic conductivity and incomplete mechanistic understanding of ion transport. Previous reviews have largely discussed polyethylene oxide (PEO)- and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based electrolytes separately or have focused primarily on material modification and electrochemical performance. title: Crop-associated differentiation of rhizosphere microbial communities and soil functional traits in saline-alkaline farmland
abstract: Introduction Saline-alkaline soils constrain crop production, yet it remains unclear how different crops shape rhizosphere conditions, plant ion allocation and microbial communities when grown under the same field background. Methods We compared eight crops under uniform saline-alkaline field and management conditions and integrated rhizosphere physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, plant nutrient and ion traits, and bacterial and fungal community characteristics using a multivariate framework. title: Impact of disturbance on spatio-temporal dynamics of carbon dioxide efflux on forest floor in tropical sal forests of the Eastern Ghats
abstract: Understanding soil carbon dynamics in tropical forests is essential for developing sustainable forest management strategies and strengthening climate change mitigation efforts. This study examined soil respiration and carbon turnover across three moist deciduous sal forest types of the Eastern Ghats, India: pure sal forest (PSF), sal-dominated moist mixed forest (SDMDF), and mixed forest without sal (MDFWS). title: Selective Fuzzy Bytetrack: An Association-Level Fuzzy Enhancement For Multi-Object Pedestrian Tracking
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to improve pedestrian identity preservation in crowded multi-object tracking by enhancing ByteTrack's association stage without modifying the detector. The focus is on reducing incorrect detection-to-track assignments under occlusion, overlap, and trajectory crossing. Design/Methodology/Approach: Selective Fuzzy ByteTrack with a fixed YOLOX detector was employed. title: Nomenclatural Notes on the Genus Meyna (Rubiaceae, Vanguerieae) With Lectotypification of Five Names
abstract: ABSTRACT The lectotypification of five names in the genus Meyna ( M. spinosa , M. tetraphylla , M. velutina , M. grisea , and M. pubescens ) is presented. Further, we clarified the nomenclature of the genus name, originally published by Robyns in his monograph Tentamen Monographiae Vangueriae Generumque Affinium . A comprehensive taxonomic treatment of the genus Meyna , along with a diagnostic key at species rank, is also provided.

title: Probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus provides an adjuvant effect to an orally administered chitosan nanoparticle-based Salmonella subunit vaccine in broilers against Salmonella Enteritidis infection
abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis (SE) is a prominent zoonotic pathogen that contaminates poultry meat and eggs, leading to widespread foodborne illness in humans. Despite better biosecurity measures and available commercial vaccines, SE foodborne illness from broiler meat remains a challenge, necessitating a novel vaccination strategy. This study investigated the adjuvant efficacy of probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus to a mannose-conjugated chitosan nanoparticle-based Salmonella subunit nanovaccine encapsulated with outer membrane proteins (OMP) and flagella antigens (FLA) of SE. title: Predicted spatial distribution of the primary Lassa virus reservoir, the multimammate mouse, in Africa
abstract: Objective This study predicts the potential spatial distribution of the multimammate mouse ( Mastomys natalensis ), the primary host of Lassa virus, a major public health concern across West Africa. Methods Correlative maximum entropy models were constructed with occurrence records of M. natalensis from Global Biodiversity Information Facility, using long-term bioclimatic variables at ~1 km resolution as predictors. title: Comparison of Building Energy Performance Policies in the European Union and Türkiye in the Context of Climate Risk Management
abstract: Due to its significant contribution to global energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, the building sector plays an important role in reducing carbon footprints, supporting climate adaptation, and strengthening risk management. This study compares building energy performance policies in the European Union (EU) and Türkiye from the perspective of climate risk management. title: Usar no es aprender: una lectura crítica de PISA 2025 y de la evidencia internacional sobre IAGen
abstract: La discusión educativa sobre inteligencia artificial generativa suele tratar el “uso de IA” como una exposición homogénea cuyos efectos podrían establecerse mediante una respuesta única. Este ensayo cuestiona esa premisa mediante un análisis documental comparado de un corpus principal de fuentes institucionales y académicas de alta influencia publicadas entre 2023 y 2026, complementado por antecedentes teóricos sobre instrumentación, descarga cognitiva y autorregulación. abstract: Abstract The audit expectation gap exists and persists due to changing “…social, economic, and political developments of the time.” (Sikka, et al., 1998) Like stakeholders’ demands for and the profession’s response to fraud detection in the 2000s, investors are increasingly interested in C-suite employees’ and entity’s illegal acts, finding them both relevant and material (Cline, Walkling & Yore, 2018). title: Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) Integrating Cold Chain Management, Digital Traceability, and Nutritional Profiling of Cow, Goat, Sheep, Mare, and Buffalo Milk
abstract: The Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) is proposed as an integrated digital platform to improve milk supply chain management through cold chain management, digital traceability, and nutritional profiling. This study adopts a qualitative approach involving literature review, observation of milk handling processes, and stakeholder discussions to identify operational challenges and develop a conceptual framework for managing cow, goat, sheep, mare, and buffalo milk. title: Biodiversity Disclosure and Analyst Forecast Accuracy: Evidence From Chinese A‐Share Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether biodiversity‐related disclosure in annual reports is associated with analyst forecast accuracy among Chinese A‐share firms. Using 20,038 firm‐year observations from 2011 to 2023 and a dictionary‐based measure validated against independent manual coding, we find that greater disclosure intensity is associated with lower subsequent forecast error after accounting for firms' broader ESG and textual‐reporting characteristics. title: Polyethylene Glycol‐Regulated Finger‐Sponge Substrate Enabling High‐Performance Nanofiltration Membranes for Efficient Mg 2+ /Li + Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient lithium recovery from salt‐lake brines relies on the precise discrimination and lithium ions separation from magnesium ions. In this study, polyethersulfone (PES) ultrafiltration (UF) substrate layer featuring finger‐like and optimized finger‐sponge transitional structures were fabricated by varying polyethylene glycol (PEG) concentrations via phase inversion.
