title: Evaluating Passive Envelope Strategies and Lighting Efficiency for One-Story Residential Buildings in Amman’s Suburban Neighborhoods
abstract: Residential buildings contribute to the maximum percentage of total energy consumption in Jordan. This current study attempts to investigate the energy-saving potential associated with passive envelope design interventions along with the use of efficient lighting units. The study seeks to reduce energy consumption in a one-story residential building located in the Amman suburbs. In this regard, a model house of an area of 133 m² was constructed using DesignBuilder simulation software in order to estimate the total baseline energy consumption. title: Global distributions and environmental correlates of community leaf length and width in forests
abstract: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integrating tree leaf traits and community data, we mapped community leaf length and width and identified their environmental correlates in global forests. title: Value Co-creation in Service Ecosystems—Investigating the Role of Mediating Modalities Between Structure and Agency in Business-to-business Relations
abstract: Abstract Research in the field of service ecosystems (SE) in the business-to-business (B2B) context is still in its infancy, especially lacking consideration of social dynamics that shape collaboration among firms. This study focuses on this topic and investigates how companies interact, coordinate, and co-create value within in an industrial SE. title: Criminal infiltration in the legal economy: An empirical analysis of firms linked to organized crime
abstract: Organized crime increasingly exploits legitimate businesses to infiltrate the legal economy. While previous empirical research has mainly relied on confiscated firms and judicially identified cases, considerably less is known about firms identified through preventive administrative measures. This study investigates whether firms subject to anti-mafia injunctions differ systematically from comparable firms in terms of territorial, ownership, and governance characteristics. title: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations
abstract: Abstract Background Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. title: Motivational climate, basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivation, and engagement in Chinese students during physical education classes
abstract: Introduction Although policy initiatives emphasize improving students’ physical health, physical education (PE) classes continue to rely predominantly on traditional teacher-centered approaches, often resulting in insufficient class engagement. Existing research has examined motivational climates, basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivation, and class engagement, yet most studies adopt a single theoretical perspective, offer limited exploration of mediating mechanisms, and provide scarce empirical evidence within the Chinese educational context. title: TOURIST ACCOMMODATION FACILITIES, COMFORT AND SATISFACTION: EVIDENCE FROM TAHIR GUEST PALACE, KANO, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined how tourist accommodation facilities enhance guest comfort and satisfaction at Tahir Guest Palace, Kano. A quantitative survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 30 tourists using a structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, mean scores, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, and linear regression analysis at the 0.05 level of significance. title: Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterojunctions Regulation in Ni‐MnO/C Microspheres With Tunable Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
abstract: Heterojunctions engineering is crucial for optimizing dielectric polarization and electromagnetic (EM) wave absorption, yet precise spatial control over semiconductor components in magnetic-dielectric microspheres remains challenging. Herein, super-dispersed MnO protrusions and Ni particles were confined within a carbon matrix, constructing unique Ni-MnO/C microspheres via a pyrolysis-controlled strategy. title: Can AI Solve Eco-Economic Challenges? Simulating the Impact of AI Systems on Seasonality Using Agent-Based Modelling
abstract: Abstract As visitors increasingly rely on AI-enabled apps and recommender systems, AI is becoming an important mediator of tourism choice. Tourism decision-making is cognitively demanding, and visitors rarely evaluate all available destinations, attractions, travel periods, and services equally. Consistent with bounded rationality, they simplify complex choice environments through limited information, heuristics, and platform-mediated evaluation. title: From salinity, alkalinity, and sodicity to vegetation recovery: a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping of plant responses and restoration strategies
abstract: Introduction Saline, alkaline, and sodic soils constrain plant establishment, but research on vegetation restoration is spread across plant physiology, soil reclamation, and restoration ecology. Methods We searched Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, obtaining 554 English-language articles and reviews published through 2025, and used bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping to examine research patterns and thematic development. Publication, country, and text analyses used all 554 records; keyword networks, thematic trends, and cited-reference analyses used 386 Web of Science records.

title: From life cycle assessment to life cycle thinking in agri-food systems: lessons from the avocado supply chain
abstract: Agri-food systems face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental performance and support sustainability transitions. In this context, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) generates evidence on environmental impacts, while Life Cycle Thinking (LCT) helps integrate that information into decision-making across supply chains. title: Spatially Programmable S‐Scheme Heterojunction Photoanodes via Aerosol‐Jet Printing for Efficient Solar Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT S‐scheme heterojunctions enable efficient charge separation while preserving the strong redox ability of photogenerated carriers, offering a powerful platform for advanced photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. However, translating such rationally designed heterostructures into scalable, high‐performance photoanodes remains a critical bottleneck for conventional fabrication methods. title: EVALUASI USABILITY PADA APLIKASI PELAYANAN ADMINISTRASI DESA WARGASARA MENGGUNAKAN TEKNIK SISTEM USABILITY SCALE (SUS)
abstract: Pelayanan administrasi desa yang masih dilakukan secara manual sering menimbulkan berbagai permasalahan seperti keterlambatan pelayanan, antrean masyarakat, dan kesulitan pengelolaan data administrasi. Untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, dikembangkan aplikasi pelayanan administrasi Desa Wargasara berbasis mobile menggunakan Flutter dan Laravel 12. title: Mapping the Evolution of Crisis Management in Tourism: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scopus-Indexed Literature Using RStudio
abstract: Crisis and disaster events, from terrorism and natural hazards to the COVID-19 pandemic, have become a defining concern of tourism research over the past two decades. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the crisis-management-and-tourism literature indexed in Scopus, using a bibliometrix/R science-mapping workflow together with document-level evidence reconstructed from the underlying export. title: An update on freshwater gastropods serving as intermediate hosts of amphistomes infecting livestock in South Africa
abstract: Improved surveillance of amphistome parasites and their intermediate hosts is crucial for comprehending their epidemiology and developing effective prevention and control measures, since amphistomosis is among the neglected parasitic diseases of ruminants, alongside schistosomiasis and fasciolosis. This study characterized the diversity of freshwater gastropods collected from six South African provinces and assessed their potential in the transmission of amphistomes infecting livestock. abstract: This article explores how the tradwife, an Alt-Right version of femininity, is becoming increasingly popularised throughout contemporary media texts. abstract: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are central to assessing the benefits and harms of interventions, but incomplete reporting undermines their verifiability and usefulness. Although SPIRIT and CONSORT reporting guidelines promote complete reporting of RCT protocols and results publications, many RCTs remain incompletely reported. En este contexto, se desarrolló un sistema basado en TinyML e IoT para monitorear y clasificar alteraciones motoras mediante un sensor MPU6050 y un sensor EMG, utilizando un microcontrolador ESP32. abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. abstract: This study aimed to identify sustainability strategies for the Bali cattle purification program in South Sulawesi. abstract: La línea de investigación presentada en este trabajo tiene como objetivo formular e implementar una metodología para la creación de traductores de lenguas con bajos recursos en América del Sur. title: Workplace Welfare Services in Promoting Employee’s Work-Life Balance; Ecological System Perspective at PT. USSI Pinbuk Prima Software

abstract: Abstract. title: High-resolution soil moisture forecasts for drought early warning in Germany
abstract: Abstract Drought early warning increasingly relies on high-resolution monitoring, but the skill of daily soil moisture forecasts at lead times of 1–2 weeks driven by real-time meteorological ensembles has rarely been evaluated. The Hydrological Sub-seasonal Forecasting System (HS2S) extends an established national drought-monitoring framework into high-resolution probabilistic soil moisture forecasts up to two weeks ahead for Germany at 0.015625° resolution. title: Mechanical and numerical evaluation of expansive soils for flexible road pavement stabilization using sugarcane bagasse ash and lime
abstract: Abstract The expansive, highly swelling clay soils, which have low bearing capacity, result in damage to flexible pavements. Utilizing locally available waste materials to develop low-cost, sustainable stabilizers improves the engineering properties of the subgrade. Laboratory-strength enhancement, establishing links between material-level stabilization and structural response via numerical modeling, has become a landmark. abstract: Abstract Catchment hydrologic function describes how meteorological conditions are transformed into streamflow. Here, we analyze about 1.7 million runoff-producing events across 4838 catchments on six continents. abstract: Balloon-assisted enteroscopy (BAE) has substantially advanced small bowel disease management. abstract: This study investigates the use of visual metonymy in social app icons within a highly competitive global app market. abstract: Background: The hospital environment represents a dynamic microbial ecosystem where diverse bacterial populations can establish and persist in various environmental compartments such as soil, water, air, and surfaces. abstract: Contemporary risk landscapes are shaped by systemic phenomena-compound disasters, cascading failures, non-stationarity, and cross-domain crises-that challenge conventional frameworks. abstract: Despite advances in resident–tourism discourse and overtourism research, it remains unclear how place-based emotions and perceptions of injustice become collectively articulated and connected to resistance. abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced imaging techniques, particularly computed tomography (CT), are revolutionising veterinary diagnostics by providing detailed structural insights essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. abstract: Islamic financial institutions (IFIs) face growing demands to disclose environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. abstract: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigates the determinants of consumer FW by integrating individual plate-waste measurements with behavioral and dining-related factors in a university dining hall setting. abstract: Abstract The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. abstract: This study examined the relationship between life insurance development and economic growth in Nigeria over the period 2000–2024. abstract: Transporting large saltwater crocodiles over remote, uneven terrain is a specialised wildlife-management operation in which road-induced vibration may contribute to animal stress, fatigue, and injury. abstract: The monoglossic ideological space that dominates United States teacher preparation policy sits increasingly at odds with a growing push for heteroglossic stances in the praxis of the teacher preparation professional community. abstract: Science-policy interfaces in the field of biodiversity have undergone significant progress in the recent years, becoming important spaces for communication and consultation. abstract: Dual‐network (DN) hydrogels possess tunable polymer network architectures, exceptional mechanical robustness, and superior water retention capability. En este contexto, los recuperadores urbanos (organizados en cooperativas) recuperan en promedio 5 toneladas mensuales por grupo, trabajando en condiciones precarias y sin integración efectiva al sistema formal. Esta problemática se agrava por la escasa concientización ambiental, la falta de políticas públicas consistentes, la ausencia de incentivos ciudadanos y la débil aplicación de principios de comercio justo hacia los recicladores. Objetivos Promover la revalorización de residuos

title: Nitrogen addition alters soil microbial community structure and decrease nitrogen cycling gene abundance in acidic macadamia orchard soils
abstract: Nitrogen addition can alter soil microbial communities and regulate nitrogen cycling processes. However, the role of nitrogen-induced soil acidification in modulating nitrogen cycling in macadamia orchard soils remains poorly understood. Based on a 3-year field fertilization experiment, this study established three treatments: no-nitrogen (N0), medium-nitrogen (N1), and high-nitrogen (N2). abstract: Introducción El programa con enfoque de “Una Sola Salud” para prevenir, detectar y responder eficazmente a los desafíos de salud que surgen de la relación entre humanos y medio ambiente debe ser tarea de todos con la disposición de herramientas y mejores prácticas, a través de un enfoque integrado y unificador para equilibrar y optimizar de manera sostenible la salud de las personas y el ecosistema. Norway has seen a rise in mental health challenges among young individuals in recent decades, including both Sámi and non-Sámi youth. Culturally responsive and accessible mental health interventions are needed. The NEON Young Norway Study investigates the use of mental health recovery narratives as a low threshold intervention. abstract: Introducción La donación de sangre altruista contribuye a la disminución de la escasez de hemoderivados. Objetivos Promover la donación de sangre altruista entre los estudiantes y personal de la Facultad de Biología de la Universidad Autónoma de Sinaloa, con el fin de contribuir a la disminución de la escasez de hemoderivados y la donación principalmente altruista en la comunidad académica mediante la divulgación de la importancia y las ventajas de la donación altruista. title: Revealing novel findings on ant distribution and natural history in Ecuador (Hymenoptera, Formicidae)
abstract: Ecuador is known for breaking world records for species concentration per area. Ants are an important component of that biodiversity. In the framework of The Ants of Ecuador initiative, we identified fifteen new species of ants for the first time recorded from the country. These species belong to four subfamilies and eight genera. The genus Cryptomyrmex Fernández, 2004 is reported for the first time in Ecuador. We provide concise taxonomic diagnoses of the species, with notes on their natural history and distribution. title: Through the Eyes of Women Writers Women in the Context of Family Problems
abstract: In recent Turkish short stories, female authors’ awareness of women’s issues is particularly noteworthy. Authors who examine women through the lens of social life, family life, and professional life address the challenges women face in these areas and explore women’s attitudes toward these challenges. The visibility of women’s experiences in social life within literary works fosters significant awareness regarding women’s issues. title: Sulfur‐ and Selenium‐Decorated Coumarins: Synthetic Strategies Involving Cyclization and Late‐Stage Functionalization
abstract: Chalcogen-containing coumarins have attracted considerable attention as a versatile class of heterocyclic compounds because sulfur- and selenium-substituted derivatives can significantly influence molecular reactivity, electronic characteristics, and biological activity. Over the past decades, synthetic approaches toward these compounds have advanced through two main strategies: direct construction of the coumarin framework through cyclization processes and late-stage functionalization of preformed coumarin scaffolds. abstract: Introducción Las alteraciones neurológicas infantiles son una prioridad en salud pública por su impacto en el desarrollo funcional, emocional y social de los niños, especialmente en contextos vulnerables con acceso limitado a servicios especializados. Según la OMS, la parálisis cerebral infantil afecta entre 2 y 3 de cada 1.000 nacidos vivos, siendo una de las principales causas de discapacidad física en la infancia. title: The Protective Action Decision‐Making Process in Emergency Responses During and After Earthquake Tremors: Qualitative Findings From the Elazığ and İzmir Earthquakes
abstract: Understanding behavioral responses during and immediately after an earthquake is critical to reducing injuries and developing preparedness strategies. This study identifies response patterns under seismic threat using qualitative evidence from the 2020 Elazığ and İzmir earthquakes in Türkiye. Data were collected from 63 participants through semistructured individual interviews and family‐based focus group discussions. title: Technical note: T c 1D – a 1D thermal and thermochronometer age prediction model
abstract: Abstract. Thermochronological data are commonly used to study the activity of geological processes over timescales of millions of years. Ages produced by thermochronological measurements, however, are non-unique and do not directly record rates of processes, which has led to the development of a variety of software tools for interpreting age data in the context of geological processes. Most of the widely used software packages focus on determining thermal histories, which are easy to use but do not provide direct quantitative estimates of geological process rates. title: Mapping groundwater-dependent vegetation in temperate climates on the example of Central Germany
abstract: Abstract Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. institutions: German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research

title: Gut-liver axis in liver pre-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities
abstract: The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis. The formation of pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive “soil” for disseminated tumor cells. However, how the gut-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood. institutions: Wangjing Hospital of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

title: The mediating role of social distance on the association between audience-protagonist similarity and fear: a case of fear of COVID-19
abstract: Objective This study examined the effects of news content on fear of COVID-19 by examining perceived social distance and audience-protagonist similarity. Method Participants ( N = 78) read a fictitious news story about a COVID-19 patient (similar/dissimilar protagonist) and then rated social distance regarding this protagonist and their fear of COVID-19. title: Comprehensive patient education in cardiac rehabilitation: A Mexican perspective
abstract: Background Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR), yet it is frequently delivered as a standardized transfer of information rather than as a structured intervention aimed at promoting behavioral change and long-term self-management. This limitation may be particularly relevant in culturally, geographically, linguistically, and socioeconomically diverse populations, such as Mexico. title: A Bivariate Generalized Inverse Weibull Distribution for Advanced Modeling in Economics and Environmental Science
abstract: Introduction: Modeling economic and environmental phenomena is a great importance due to the complex, uncertain and independent nature of real-world data arising in these fields. This paper introduces a new bivariate distribution known as FGM bivariate Generalized Inverse Weibull distribution. The proposed model is constructed by combining Generalized Inverse Weibull marginals through FGM copula framework, allowing for flexible modelling of dependence in economic and environmental data. title: Determining strategic locations for rental housing development with GIS and expert systems around the educational area of Universitas Sulawesi Barat
abstract: Agglomeration is no longer confined to the economic sector but has also expanded into education, generating concentration effects around higher-education institutions. A similar phenomenon is evident around the campus of Universitas Sulawesi Barat in Majene Regency, where the rapid growth of rental housing risks triggering uncontrolled urban sprawl. This study aims to (1) identify the key factors influencing the selection of potential locations for rental housing and (2) determine the most suitable locations based on these factors. title: Clasificación de Estados de Actividad Física Mediante la Dinámica Temporal del Tiempo de Llegada del Pulso
abstract: El reconocimiento de la actividad humana (HAR, por sus siglas en inglés) basado en señales fisiológicas ofrece una visión directa de la respuesta metabólica y autonómica del cuerpo. Este trabajo propone una red neuronal recurrente de memoria a corto y largo plazo (LSTM, por sus siglas en inglés) para clasificar los estados de actividad (reposo, caminar, correr) basándose exclusivamente en la dinámica temporal del tiempo de llegada del pulso (PAT, por sus siglas en inglés). title: Determinants of continuance intention toward eLearning usage in higher education institutions
abstract: Abstract This study aims to examine the key determinants influencing students’ continuance intention towards eLearning usage in higher education institutions in Iraq. It proposes an integrated model combining the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), extended with the construct of digital literacy. title: AN INSTITUTIONAL PERSPECTIVE ON DIGITAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN INDONESIA: CHALLENGES AND SUPPORT MECHANISMS
abstract: Digital entrepreneurship has increasingly been recognized as a key driver of economic transformation in emerging economies, including Indonesia. The rapid diffusion of digital technologies creates opportunities for innovation, market expansion, and economic inclusion, while simultaneously generating complex institutional challenges. This article aims to analyze the role of institutional challenges and institutional support in shaping the dynamics of digital entrepreneurship in emerging economies, with a particular focus on the Indonesian context. title: Beyond traditional anticoagulants: exploring the future of thromboembolism treatment with FXI inhibitors
abstract: Thromboembolic diseases impose a significant burden on global health. However, the currently approved anticoagulant drugs, including heparin, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), all carry certain bleeding risks. The proteases inhibited by these drugs play crucial roles in both pathological thrombosis formation and normal hemostasis. Therefore, how to effectively anticoagulate without increasing bleeding has become the core direction of clinical research. title: Piloting Digital Leadership, Technology Acceptance, and Literacy–Numeracy Instruments in Early Childhood Education
abstract: Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy in early childhood education (ECE) may depend partly on how principals lead digital change and how educators perceive technology, but, to our knowledge, no published instrument set measures these constructs together for Indonesian ECE. title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. title: Design challenges and enabling technologies for ultra-high-speed electric drive systems
abstract: Ultra-high-speed electric drive systems are a key route toward higher power density in electric vehicles, aerospace propulsion, and industrial applications, with series-production traction machines now exceeding 20,000 r/min and laboratory prototypes approaching or exceeding 100,000 r/min. title: A systematic assessment of environmental impacts and techno-economic benefits of solid digestate conversion to biochar: a case study of pig farm digestate in Taiwan
abstract: Abstract Digestate, the solid by‑product of anaerobic digestion, can cause nutrient leaching, greenhouse‑gas release and heavy‑metal accumulation. Slow pyrolysis offers a promising route for upgrading digestate into biochar, yet its high energy demand and uncertain economics must be carefully weighed. This study evaluates the functional unit of 1 t solid digestate, the conversion of digestate to biochar at a pig farm in Pingtung, Taiwan, and compares the results with composting and incineration. title: Biogenic fabrication of zinc oxide nanoparticles for enhanced germination and early seedling establishment of rice under salinity stress
abstract: Introduction Salinity stress restricts rice ( Oryza sativa L. ) germination and early establishment through osmotic stress, ionic toxicity, and excessive reactive oxygen species production. Although ZnO nanoparticles (ZnONPs) can enhance salinity tolerance, the influence of their biological synthesis source on nanoparticle properties and efficacy remains poorly understood. title: Design and experimental evaluation of an internally illuminated hybrid mixing photobioreactor for intensified microalgal biodiesel production with techno-economic and scale-up assessment
abstract: The technical and financial limitations associated with the production of microalgal biodiesel are significantly influenced by reactor structure, biomass productivity, lipid accumulation, and energy consumption. This study designed and experimentally evaluated a 50-L nominal-volume (42-L working-volume) cylindrical stainless-steel photobioreactor that combined internal LED illumination with low-shear mechanical agitation and fine-pore gas diffusion to enable culture circulation, illumination, and gas–liquid transfer. title: GTPase GBP7 promotes HSV-1 infection by interacting with and activating eEF1A1 to accelerate the protein translation process
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are immune GTPases induced by interferons (IFNs) and comprise GBPs1-7. In this study, GBP7, a less studied member of the GBPs, was identified to possess Herpes simplex virus I (HSV-1) promoting effects on replication both in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of GBP7 or loss of its GTPase activity demonstrated significant antiviral effects. Consistently, GBP7-/- mice infected with HSV-1 showed higher survival and milder symptoms. title: Sustainable active packaging via bio-functionalized cloth bags containing peppermint oil-chitosan biocomposites for sesame seed preservation
abstract: Meeting international consumer demand now requires a dual approach of adopting eco-friendly farming practices while keeping chemical residues strictly below target MRL values. The increasing demand for produce that limits residues to below maximum acceptable levels and concerns over the environmental impacts of conventional pesticides necessitate the development of safe, sustainable, and cost-effective storage technologies. title: Integration of IoT-based healthcare devices within the smart grid architecture model: a conceptual framework with economic and energy assessment for elderly care in Europe
abstract: Introduction This study investigates the integration of IoT-enabled medical devices within the Smart Grid Architecture Model (SGAM) to support elderly home-based care in Europe. The study develops a conceptual SGAM–IoT framework that maps healthcare devices, actors, communication pathways, and functions across the SGAM interoperability layers, domains, and zones, with particular attention to interoperability, data exchange and integration between the home environment, healthcare services, and energy-aware infrastructure. title: Parametric Optimization of Shading Devices to Improve Classroom Daylighting Performance
abstract: Inadequate visual comfort in classrooms can impair the physical and mental well-being of teachers and students, making sufficient daylight essential in academic environments, particularly in hot, arid climates. This study investigates shading devices (SDs) for improving daylight performance in an existing university classroom. Parametric analysis and optimization used Autodesk Revit (BIM) with Insight plugins. abstract: Egg parasitoids of the genus Trichogramma Westwood, 1833 are widely used in integrated pest management, but their minute size and reduced morphology complicate identification. Using integrative taxonomy, we describe Trichogramma vitessoides Hu & Yang, sp. nov . from Guangdong, China, based on a laboratory colony established from parasitoids reared from naturally parasitised egg masses of Heortia vitessoides (Moore, 1885) (Lepidoptera, Crambidae), a defoliator of Aquilaria sinensis (Lour.) abstract: Introducción: El perfil blando es importante en ortodoncia porque influye en la apariencia y función del rostro, y conocerlo ayuda a planificar mejor los tratamientos. Objetivo: determinar la relación del perfil blando facial con las diferentes maloclusiones esqueletales según el índice de maduración cervical en una base de datos radiológica en pacientes de 8 a 20 años de la ciudad de Cuenca en el periodo 2022-2023. title: Repurposing farnesyltransferase inhibitors tipifarnib and lonafarnib as antibacterial agents: proteomic and functional analyses
abstract: Farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) like tipifarnib and lonafarnib, originally developed as anticancer agents, show antibacterial activity against Gram-positive pathogens through an unknown mechanism of action. Here, we investigated the proteomic response of Bacillus subtilis 168 (Gram-positive) and an efflux-deficient Escherichia coli Δ tolC mutant (Gram-negative) to sublethal concentrations of FTIs. title: The effect of air pollution exposure on mortality: a time series study in Sivas, Türkiye
abstract: Using a generalized linear model (GLM), the relationships between daily changes in air pollutants and mortality rates in Sivas Central District (Türkiye) were examined over five years (2017–2021), controlling for long–term time trends, seasonal effects, and meteorological factors in this study. The impacts of major pollutants (PM₁₀, PM 2.5 , and NO₂) on daily mortality were analyzed at different time lags (0–10 days). title: Length of the growing season as a key determinant of spatial variation in forest surface litter quantity
abstract: Forest surface litter is an integral component of forest ecology, it acts as bridge between biotic and abiotic components of any forest ecosystem. Comprehensive, wall-to-wall mapping of forest litter distribution can enhance our understanding of ecosystem processes and nutrient dynamics, and improve management interventions and strategies for forest fire prevention and control. Forest phenology refers to start of season (SOS), peak of season (POS), end of season (EOS) and length of season (LOS). Thereby can be a potential indicator of accumulated surface litter quantity. title: Olaparib plus tremelimumab in women with recurrent ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation: a phase I/II study
abstract: Response rates to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in ovarian cancer are low. In preclinical studies, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition (PARPi) synergized with CTLA4 ICB to achieve long-term survival in Brca1-deficient ovarian cancer models. Here we evaluated the safety and efficacy of combined treatment with the PARPi olaparib and the CTLA4 ICB tremelimumab for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer in a multi-site single-arm phase I/II study enrolling 50 women with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (NCT02571725). title: Comparative Morphology and SEM –Based Micromorphology of 11 Galium L. Taxa From Eskişehir, Türkiye
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the morphological and SEM‐based micromorphological characteristics of 11 Galium L. taxa representing eight sections occurring in Eskişehir Province, Türkiye, to identify taxonomically informative characters. Morphological and micromorphological assessments were conducted on stems, leaves, flowers, and mericarps, with particular emphasis on epidermal cell morphology, stomatal distribution, trichome characteristics, and surface ornamentation. title: Flood susceptibility assessment using GIS and an analytical hierarchy process in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding remains a major environmental challenge in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria. In this study, flood susceptibility across the metropolis was assessed using geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). title: A unified pressure-temperature stability diagram for assessing injection-induced fault reactivation potential
abstract: Cold fluid injections into hot geological formations drive coupled pore pressure and temperature perturbations that alter in-situ stress states and can trigger fault reactivation, a critical risk for geoenergy and geostorage operations such as CO 2 storage. Existing analytical approaches often treat pressure and temperature perturbations independently, rely on two-dimensional Mohr circle analysis under a fixed stress regime, and therefore cannot directly constrain coupled operational thresholds for fault reactivation. title: Hierarchical Interfacial Engineering Enables Durable Superamphiphobic Cotton Fabrics With Integrated Fire Safety and Photocatalytic Air Purification
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable cellulose textiles are promising for wearable protection, yet integrating durable superamphiphobicity, fire safety, and environmental remediation within a single cellulose substrate remains challenging. Herein, a silane‐mediated stabilized organic–inorganic interface was constructed on cotton fabric through hierarchical interfacial engineering. abstract: Forensic entomology is an essential discipline for determining the Postmortem Interval; however, the description of color in species of the Piophilidae family remains a subjective process that depends on the expert's perception and lighting conditions. This study addresses this issue throught chromatic analysis to standardize the characterizing of forensic-interest Piophilidae entomological samples in Ecuador. abstract: Background Long-read sequencing has revealed complex variations, such as gene conversions in immunologically critical PE/PPE gene families, yet their role in Mycobacterium tuberculosis host adaptation remains unclear. Methods We performed a comparative genomic analysis across a gradient of host-imposed selective pressure: chronic within-host infection, latent household transmission, and a 21-year clonal outbreak in Bern, Switzerland. title: Transformation of the media systems of the South Caucasus countries under digital globalisation
abstract: This paper aimed to study changes in the media systems of South Caucasus countries (Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan) against the background of digital globalisation. Methods of the study included document and content analysis of academic publications, materials of international organisations, information on monitoring and civil society platforms, regulatory and legal acts, information from analytical agencies, and comparative analysis of indicators of the level of digitalisation and freedom of the media in each of the three countries. title: Laminarin suppresses PD-L1 translation by targeting YTHDF1 to exert antitumor immunity in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by low response rates and rapid acquired resistance to current immunotherapies, highlighting an urgent unmet clinical need for novel therapeutic strategies. Herein, we demonstrated that laminarin, a biocompatible β-1,3-glucan extracted from brown algae, exerts significant antitumor immune effects against TNBC with no evident toxicity under the tested conditions. title: Biomodelos como sistemas centinela en ecotoxicología reproductiva
abstract: La contaminación ambiental es un tema de índole mundial que repercute directamente en la salud de los seres vivos, siendo un tema importante de estudio e investigación. Dentro de estos procesos de contaminación tenemos las aguas residuales, las cuales contienen mezclas complejas de sustancias químicas disruptoras endocrinas, metales pesados y fármacos que representan riesgos para la salud reproductiva. title: Effect of the C = C double bond in biodiesel compounds on copper corrosion
abstract: Abstract Biodiesel is a mixture of fatty acid methyl esters in which the chemical structure, hydrocarbon chain length, saturation or unsaturation, and position of the C = C double bond in each methyl ester influence the biodiesel’s properties. In this study, pure mixtures of short-chain methyl esters (methyl acrylate and methyl propionate, methyl 3-butenoate and methyl butyrate) were selected as model systems to evaluate the effect of the C = C bond on copper corrosion behavior. title: Three-dimensional geostatistical inverse modeling of coupled heat and salt tracer tests based on mildly and highly heterogeneous synthetic fields
abstract: Accurate characterization of subsurface heterogeneity is essential for understanding groundwater flow and contaminant transport. abstract: Since the 1990s, Bangalore has undergone rapid urbanisation, largely driven by the growth of IT parks, attracting multinational corporations and a significant population influx. abstract: Introduction Numerous studies have used the Assessing Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA) battery to evaluate physical fitness (PF) and its positive impact on the health of school-age children, assessing various components of fitness. abstract: As global warming intensifies urban heatwave risk, blue-green spaces have become critical regulators of urban thermal environments. abstract: Padang, West Sumatra, has high seismic activity due to the subduction zone beneath western Sumatra. abstract: Saudi women Novel has gone through distinctive literary trends until it reaches its present form. Fictions have experienced variety of topics from the past through the present to the future. The present study aims to investigate the new trends in the development in Modern Saudi Woman fiction by presenting models of Saudi women's writing within the horizon of the vision of 2030. abstract: This study assesses the integrated impacts of land use/land cover (LULC) change and climate change on hydrological responses in the Hare watershed, Southern Ethiopia, using the SWAT model. abstract: La formación docente en educación musical enfrenta el reto de integrar la tecnología digital de manera crítica, creativa y pedagógicamente significativa. abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. abstract: Conventional adenomas and serrated lesions are two major precursor lesions of colorectal cancer. abstract: The origins of initial domestication of crops have long intrigued researchers across disciplines, with implications for genetic resource utilization and conservation. title: Naiveté or Strategic Ambiguity? Examining Economic, Demographic and Security Narratives in India's Refugee Policy
abstract: ABSTRACT The decadal transition in the Indian politico‐legal stance on refugees, from a human rights tilt to national security concerns, invites a close examination. India maintains a theoretical safe distance from the international legal framework on refugees by not acceding to the 1951 Refugee Convention, while on the ground, it extensively engages—politically and judicially—with refugee‐related domestic legal issues. In the absence of a dedicated legal framework, the refugees, categorised based on temporalities and spatialities, face a highly unpredictable executive and judicial discretion.

abstract: Non-Hispanic Black adults have poorer sleep quality than non-Hispanic White adults (hereafter, Black, White), which may underlie disparities in cognition. abstract: Crop rotation analysis is fundamental to understanding agricultural landscape dynamics, yet the complexity of multi-annual, spatially explicit agricultural data presents significant analytical challenges. Media reports provide insights into demographic characteristics, suicide methods, homicide–suicide incidents, and the social contexts associated with these events. abstract: Boswellia species and the resins like frankincense derived from them have long been used in traditional medical systems for the treatment of inflammatory and skin disorders owing to their diverse bioactive constituents. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the dermatological potential of Boswellia species and their metabolites in inflammatory and non-inflammatory skin diseases, with particular emphasis on boswellic acids. abstract: Abstract Global Justice Index, whose most results are presented here, is an ongoing, multiyear research project based at the Fudan Institute for Advanced Study in Social Sciences to assess countries’ contributions to and performance in the advancement of global justice. abstract: This study examines the transformative role of equity-based and donation-based crowdfunding in fostering innovation, promoting financial inclusion, and creating employment opportunities in the United States. Through a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative analysis of crowdfunding platform data and qualitative interviews with entrepreneurs and investors, we investigate how these alternative financing mechanisms address traditional capital market gaps. abstract: Today, integrating technology into the instructional process has become an essential component of students’ learning experiences. However, research examining the pedagogical effects of Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy in education remains limited. This study aims to investigate the effect of mathematics instruction based on Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy on students’ academic achievement and to explore students’ views regarding the instructional process. abstract: Understanding musical solitude in vocal performance requires tracing how musical and poetic observations inform embodied interpretive decisions across contrasting repertoires. abstract: ABSTRACT This article presents the results of a research project aimed at identifying the Social Representations of a group of preservice teachers who participated in a museum internship and inferring the influence of these representations on educational practice in this context. abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. abstract: Introduction The question of how individuals make meaning of, and cope with, the threat of war remains underexplored, particularly in highly secular societies and in contexts of anticipated rather than directly experienced conflict. Methods This article reports findings from a qualitative study of meaning-making coping among people in Sweden, a country that has not experienced war within its borders for more than two hundred years but that now faces heightened geopolitical tension. abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) is critical for severe weather forecasting, yet existing GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) retrieval methods are limited by neglecting tropospheric horizontal gradients and lacking regional coverage. abstract: Though integrated farming is believed as an adaptation strategy to climate change and variability, information about the extent of adaptation benefits due to drought remains limited. abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that predominantly affects elderly people and is characterized by cognitive decline and dementia. abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a growing clinical burden through recurrent intestinal inflammation, malnutrition, treatment-related toxicity, and incomplete mucosal healing. abstract: Tissue survival depends on adequate oxygen delivery, yet when red blood cell (RBC) transfusions are unavailable or contraindicated, restoring oxygen delivery remains an urgent clinical need. To meet this need, researchers have developed hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers (HBOCs) that transport oxygen via cell-free hemoglobin circulating in plasma. However, the intrinsic toxicity of cell-free hemoglobin (Hb) has slowed its clinical translation. title: Multidimensional molecular strategies for crop photoperiod adaptation and latitudinal expansion
abstract: The traditional regional distribution of agriculture was historically constrained by crops’ inherent dependence on local environmental cues, particularly photoperiod and temperature. Natural domestication and artificial selection have progressively reduced this dependence on native ecosystems, resulting in a profound restructuring of global agricultural patterns. abstract: Colonial legal historiography in Minangkabau has long portrayed matrilineal adat and Islamic law as antagonistic systems, casting adat as static custom and Islam as an external imposition. This article repositions the formula Syarak Mangato, Adaik Mamakai (SMAM), rendered here as “Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies,” as an analytical method for dismantling this binary, rather than treating the formula merely as a cultural description, as much of the existing scholarship has done. title: From There and Back Again: A Commentary on the Future of Animal Transfers in Zoos and Aquariums
abstract: Animal transfers among zoos and aquariums are essential for sustaining genetically diverse and demographically stable populations. However, they mark substantially disruptive events in an animal's life under human care. Current transfer practices-spanning population recommendations, health evaluation, transport, quarantine, and subsequent introduction-are shaped by decades of experience and now face growing impacts of climate change, regulatory complexity, and evolving welfare standards. abstract: This article examines how the Danu Son See Yar Day (DSSYD) festival functions as a religious-cultural medium for strengthening ethnic visibility and identity among the Danu community in Myanmar, addressing the limited scholarly attention to festival-based minority identity formation. abstract: Abstract Gesture has emerged as a powerful multimodal tool in vocabulary acquisition, with converging behavioral and neuroscientific evidence for its facilitative role in second language (L2) vocabulary learning. abstract: El repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara nos ha llegado casi en su totalidad tras las correspondientes adaptaciones escénicas e impresas y sin control de la transmisión por parte del poeta. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) show immense potential in next‐generation display technologies due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties. abstract: The tropical rat mite, Ornithonyssus bacoti (Hirst, 1913), is an obligate hematophagous gamasid mite of global veterinary, animal, and public health importance. While traditionally recognized as a cause of rodent mite dermatitis in humans, its potential involvement in zoonotic pathogen transmission requires rigorous critical evaluation. abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), encompassing coronary artery disease (CAD), cerebrovascular disease (ischemic stroke, IS; and transient ischemic attack, TIA), and peripheral artery disease (PAD) of atherosclerotic origin, remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in prevention and treatment. title: Seed weight grading improves germination and seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
abstract: Abstract Seed weight is a critical factor influencing germination, seedling establishment, and subsequent crop development. Khasi Mandarin exhibits considerable variation in seed weight, and limited information is available on the effect of seed weight on germination and seedling performance. This study assesses the effects of seed grades on seed germination, seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin. title: NeuPlume: generative inversion of atmospheric point-source emissions from sparse observations
abstract: Abstract. title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives
abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. abstract: La mastitis bovina es una enfermedad de gran relevancia en la industria lechera debido a su impacto en la salud animal, la calidad de la leche y las pérdidas económicas que genera. El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre el método de ordeño y la presencia de mastitis, así como su efecto sobre la producción de leche. title: A CFD-GIS-QMRA framework for post‑release urban bioaerosol risk and healthcare demand assessment
abstract: Urban bioaerosol releases pose increasing challenges to urban biosecurity resilience, yet their public health impacts remain insufficiently assessed. Here, we developed an integrated CFD–GIS–QMRA framework to simulate bioaerosol dispersion, quantify infection risk, and estimate associated health outcomes and healthcare demand. title: Recent advances in hybrid treatment technologies for pharmaceutical removal from complex water matrices
abstract: The widespread occurrence of pharmaceuticals in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and health concerns, largely due to their persistence and the limited removal efficiency of conventional wastewater treatment systems. This review critically examines advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and their hybrid configurations for the removal of pharmaceuticals from complex water matrices, including municipal, hospital, and pharmaceutical industry effluents. abstract: Abstract Key message Alpine or mountainous forest genomics research is rapidly moving from classic population genetic studies toward exploring population environmental adaptation to address climate vulnerabilities. For alpine conifers in particular, future progress in sustainable management relies heavily on overcoming the current bottleneck in the availability of genomic and experimental resources through targeted, interdisciplinary research efforts. abstract: Accumulation of ∼200 h of hypoxia exposure (pre-acclimatization) has been suggested to prevent the development of acute mountain sickness when a person is subsequently exposed to high altitude. These pre-exposures are typically undertaken intermittently at or near the place of residence, primarily during sleep in hypoxic tents, and are likely to induce effective ventilatory acclimatization. abstract: Background Recovery-oriented approaches in forensic psychiatry increasingly emphasize the importance of social relationships. However, research and practice have primarily approached significant relationships through a family-caregiver lens leaving less knowledge about the broader range of relationships that may be meaningful to patients. abstract: This paper presents the development of a three-dimensional model of a historic townhouse located at the Market Square (Rynek 11) in Przemyśl using data acquired by terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and terrestrial and aerial photogrammetry. The study aimed to assess the usefulness of an integrated measurement approach for preparing detailed architectural documentation of a heritage building and to evaluate the quality of the final products, including the point cloud, mesh model, vector 3D model, and orthophotos. title: Dominant crack selection in multi-crack stress corrosion cracking of AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained loading in flowing HCl
abstract: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in structural components often involves the simultaneous development of multiple cracks; however, the mechanism by which a dominant crack emerges under sustained loading remains insufficiently resolved. This exploratory study investigates competitive multi-crack SCC behavior in AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained tensile loading in flowing 1 M HCl. abstract: Animal welfare assessment draws on evidence about both the animal’s observed state and the husbandry conditions in which it lives, but these sources of evidence are related rather than equivalent. abstract: The ectoparasitic mite Varroa destructor is one of the main sanitary threats to Apis mellifera colonies worldwide, prompting the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic acaricides. This study evaluated the effects of hydroethanolic extracts from Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis on phoretic V. destructor infestation and mite fall under field conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite nanocrystals hold great promise for low‐cost optoelectronic and lasing applications, yet their integration into composite films is limited by poor stability under high excitation. abstract: This study investigated follicular growth patterns, corpus luteum dynamics and endocrine profiles during natural and hormonally induced estrous cycles in Arunachali yak maintained at the ICAR–NRC on Yak, Nyukmadung, Arunachal Pradesh, India. abstract: This study evaluates the operational performance of three configurations of an Integrated Resource and Recovery Centre (IRRC) as a decentralised rural waste-to-energy (WtE) system using Monte Carlo simulation. abstract: Situada em uma região de grande biodiversidade, a bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires vem sofrendo sucessivas e intensas mudanças no uso e cobertura da terra, trazendo impactos ambientais provocadas pelas atividades econômicas da região. abstract: Maintaining sustainable animal populations is fundamental to zoo and aquarium missions in education, visitor engagement, entertainment, scientific advancement, public health and wellbeing, advocacy, and conservation impact. abstract: Abstract In regions facing water scarcity, optimising existing treatment infrastructure is increasingly important. abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Intercropping of legumes with cereals enhances resilience, resource efficiency, and nutritional quality in food systems, yet few studies have integrated yield stability with grain quantity and post‐harvest processability. abstract: Tourism is an important driver of socio-economic development. However, its rapid growth has increased pressure on the environment and host communities. title: Socioeconomic determinants of maternal and neonatal healthcare utilization among recently delivered women in Sudan
abstract: Armed conflict and economic instability can exacerbate socioeconomic inequalities in maternal and neonatal healthcare access and utilization. This study assessed the association between household income, healthcare costs, and maternal and neonatal healthcare utilization among women who had recently delivered and were reachable through functioning health facilities in Sudan. A facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 468 recently delivered women recruited from 19 public and private health facilities across nine Sudanese states. abstract: Este artigo mapeia e analisa a evolução da produção científica que relaciona a Indústria 4.0 à competitividade por meio de um estudo bibliométrico longitudinal. title: Steel mill scale in concrete and mortar: a critical review of the evidence base and a proposed framework for future quantitative synthesis
abstract: Steel mill scale is an iron-oxide-rich by-product of hot rolling that is generated at roughly 1%–3% of the mass of steel processed and is still largely landfilled or downcycled. Its high iron content, high specific gravity and fine flake morphology have prompted a growing number of laboratory investigations into its use in concrete and mortar, principally as a partial replacement for fine aggregate and, far more rarely, for cement. abstract: Introduction In this study, we examine how documented cockpit equipment differentiates selected Chinese-brand battery electric vehicles (BEVs). We compare configuration richness with and without a price criterion and identify recurring equipment arrangements, rather than using specifications as a proxy for tested cockpit performance. Methods The dataset comprises 36 purposively selected model–trim combinations from 13 brands. title: Examining West African Regional Integration on the Scale of Anglophone-Francophone Linguistic Strain
abstract: The hope of the eventual transformation of the Economic Community of West African States into a cohesive regional union, accentuated with the dynamism and transformation of the institution from 1975 to the present, reflects evolving exigencies. However, five decades down the line, the dream of a fully integrated West African community remains a pipe dream. The nascent nationalism manifesting as a military uprising in the sub-region further obfuscates attempts at characterising the milieu within globalisation and regionalism contexts. title: Taxonomic novelties in Triolena (Melastomataceae, Trioleneae): a new species from Colombia, new synonyms, and an updated key
abstract: Background and Aims: Triolena (Melastomataceae) consists of about 30 species of terrestrial or epiphytic herbs distributed from Mexico to Bolivia and the western Amazon. This study describes a new species from Colombia, proposes new synonyms, reinstates one taxon, and presents a taxonomic key for the genus. Methods: The description of the new species was based on material from the herbarium COAH, and its threat status was assessed using IUCN Red List criteria. abstract: Purpose This study examines the mediating role of restorative experience in the associations between therapeutic landscape perception, visitor satisfaction, and revisit intention in Palandöken Urban Forest. Methodology A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 413 visitors through face-to-face questionnaires and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. title: Radiological assessment of natural radionuclides (238U, 232Th, and 40K) in soil and sugar samples from the Arjo-Didessa Sugar Factory, Ethiopia
abstract: This study presents the first baseline assessment of natural radionuclide activity concentrations ( 238 U, 232 Th, and 40 K) in five refined sugar samples and five corresponding agricultural soil samples from the Arjo-Didessa Sugar Factory in Ethiopia. Using high-purity germanium (HPGe) gamma-ray spectrometry, the average activity concentrations in sugar samples were measured at 4.78 ± 0.60 Bq/kg for 238 U, 23.23 ± 1.56 Bq/kg for 232 Th, and 274.93 ± 14.53 Bq/kg for 40 K. title: Reality stabilization: a unified framework for psychosis and post-psychotic depression
abstract: Both quantum mechanics and cognitive neuroscience challenge the classical view of a passively perceived reality. Instead, they suggest that reality arises through a process of selection and stabilization from a field of possibilities. This article proposes that this “reality stabilization” framework can unify our understanding of psychosis and post-psychotic depression—two conditions that are currently studied as distinct phenomena, and which existing models of predictive coding, dopaminergic dysregulation, and network neuroscience rarely integrate into a single account. title: Translation at a distance: United Nations visiting missions and the making of international decolonization
abstract: How did the United Nations, in their early years become an actor in the process of decolonization? This article shifts attention away from the diplomatic negotiations conventionally associated with international decolonization and toward the United Nations visiting missions, a largely overlooked instrument of the Trusteeship System entrusted with an epistemic mandate to investigate, inspect, and report on conditions in dependent territories. title: Uncovering Soil Health Responses to Short-Term Crop Rotation under Deficit Irrigation in Cold and Semi-Arid Agroecosystems
abstract: Crop rotation (CR) is a fundamental sustainable management practice, yet the temporal dynamics of soil recovery, particularly the synchronization between physical and chemical properties, remain poorly understood, especially in the fragile soil of semi-arid agroecosystems. This field study evaluated the impact of 0, 1, and 2 years of CR (0CR, 1CR, and 2CR) on soil organic carbon (SOC), soil total carbon (STC), soil total nitrogen (STN), macroaggregate formation, and soil water holding capacity (SWHC) under limited (75%) irrigation regime in a barley-bean- sugar beets cropping system in northwe

abstract: Los patrones de actividad vocal de las aves están determinados por factores tanto bióticos como abióticos, lo que da lugar a variaciones estacionales que típicamente alcanzan su pico durante la temporada reproductiva. title: Adjoint-based corrective approach for nodal indoor air quality predictions
abstract: Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) modelling in building simulations often relies on the nodal approach to evaluate exposure to airborne pollutants. This approach assumes perfect mixing within each zone, which can lead to significant discrepancies compared to CFD predictions, especially under complex airflow configurations. To address this limitation, this study proposes a correction model that modifies the nodal scalar mass balance using a correction factor derived from CFD results. title: Immunometabolic crosstalk between dysfunctional adipose tissue and the brain: implications for postoperative cognitive dysfunction in obesity
abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is an important complication after surgery, particularly in patients with pre-existing metabolic and inflammatory vulnerability. Obesity may increase susceptibility to postoperative cognitive decline, but its independent association with POCD and the underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. This review critically examines a proposed adipose–immune–brain pathway linking obesity-associated adipose dysfunction to perioperative neurocognitive outcomes. title: The Effect of Teaching Materials Produced Using 3D Printing in Social Studies Education on the Motivation, Attitudes, and Achievement of Fifth-Grade Students
abstract: This investigation primarily explores the pedagogical implications of integrating instructional artifacts manufactured via three-dimensional (3D) printing technologies within fifth-grade social studies education, specifically monitoring shifts in student motivation, subject-directed attitudes, and academic outcomes. Using a quasi-experimental approach, the study employed pre-test and post-test non-equivalent control group design. abstract: Written by Muzaffereddin Galib, Bir Bakış (“A Glance”) 1892) is examined as the earliest known Turkish serialized novel published in Cyprus, where “first” functions not as an aesthetic judgment but as an indicator of earliness grounded in publication context and supported by archival materials. title: The future of scholarly blogs: Scholarly bloggers' perspectives on long‐term preservation
abstract: Abstract Scholarly blogs are an important venue for scholarly communication; however, they are not yet integrated into the preservation workflows of digital research and information infrastructures, which places their long‐term access at risk. By using Star and Ruhleder's (1996) dimensions of information infrastructure as a theoretical framework, in this study we investigate social and organizational factors that impact blog preservation and derive implications for the implementation of blogs into an information infrastructure. title: Increased water requirements for avocado, chayote and coffee due to climate change in central Mexico
abstract: Efficient water management in agriculture is essential for crops that are sensitive to water stress. Poor water management and climate change will increase the water demands of crops, making irrigation indispensable for maintaining productivity. In this study, the water requirements (CWR) and irrigation water requirements (IWR) of chayote (Sechium edule var. Virens levis), avocado (Persea americana var. title: Performance gap between archived real-time and post-processed precise products for multi-GNSS and multi-frequency PPP-AR
abstract: Abstract Real-time Precise Point Positioning (PPP) with Ambiguity Resolution (PPP-AR) is an increasingly important Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) technique for high-precision positioning, navigation, and other time-critical applications. Its performance depends strongly on the availability and accuracy of real-time satellite orbit and clock products. title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities is crucial for achieving coordinated development between socioeconomic progress and the ecological environment. This paper assesses the ecological efficiency level of 279 prefecture-level cities in China by adopting the super-efficient EBM model. title: Inverse CeO 2 /Cu Catalysts with Engineered Cu + ‐O V ‐Ce 3+ Interfacial Sites for Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT The reverse water‐gas shift (RWGS) reaction can serve as a pivotal hub for converting CO 2 into value‐added chemicals. However, conventional Cu/CeO 2 catalysts are constrained by a limited metal‐oxide interfacial perimeter, suffering from both inadequate low‐temperature activity and poor stability. Herein, a series of CeO 2 /Cu‐x catalysts (where x is the Ce/Cu molar ratio) were synthesized via an oxalic acid‐assisted sol‐gel coprecipitation method, and tested for RWGS at 400°C and atmospheric pressure. title: Settler-colonial entanglements: Using Par/Des(i) to understand Black and Racialized international student experiences in Canada
abstract: This scholarly paper discusses the complex positioning of Black and Racialized international students (BRIS) in Canada, both as marginalized bodies and complicit in perpetuating settler colonialism. It delves into the paradoxical role these students play within the framework of Canadian higher education, which is deeply entwined with the country's colonial history and contemporary policy shifts aimed at managing the influx of international students. title: Urban energy peaking in China: timing, persistence, rebound risk, and regional heterogeneity
abstract: Introduction Determining whether urban energy demand has entered a persistent post-peak phase is important for assessing China’s energy transition. A historical maximum alone, however, does not establish a durable turning point because energy consumption may subsequently rebound or remain close to its previous peak. abstract: Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini-publics. These forums' participants are selected randomly from the general public (sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors). After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations. title: Organisational and economic conditions for implementing unmanned aerial systems in the production processes of agricultural enterprises
abstract: The article substantiated the organisational-economic conditions and engineering prerequisites for implementing agricultural drones in the production processes of agricultural enterprises of Poltava region. The aim of the research was to determine the minimum land area at which purchasing or contracting drone services becomes economically viable, and to establish the technical parameters of spray application quality and the priority operations for unmanned aerial equipment. title: Is physical climate risk priced in India’s financial sector? A monthly index approach, 2014–2024
abstract: Floods, cyclones and heatwaves are no longer viewed as humanitarian crises; they also have significant financial implications by affecting borrowers’ ability to repay loans, increasing potential liabilities of insurers and influencing how investors assess and price financial risks. Whether financial markets actually respond to this physical climate risk remains an open question, particularly in emerging economies like India, where climate exposure is high but market-based evidence is scarce. title: Integrating cortical microtubules into plant gravity signaling: dynamics, tubulin phosphorylation, and growth regulation
abstract: Plant gravity responses depend on coordinated signaling and growth-control mechanisms that convert directional and mechanical stimuli into differential cell expansion. Cortical microtubules are central to the conversion: they pattern cellulose synthase trajectories, set cell-wall anisotropy, and are remodeled in altered-gravity and tubulin-mutant systems. Yet the cytoskeletal regulatory pathway remains only loosely connected to the canonical, auxin-centered picture of how plants perceive and respond to gravity. title: Del residuo agroindustrial al biochar diseñado: composición, estructura molecular y aplicaciones de alto valor agregado
abstract: En este artículo se examina cómo la composición de la biomasa agroindustrial y las condiciones de pirólisis determinan la estructura molecular y el desempeño funcional del biochar desde una perspectiva de ingeniería de materiales. En el contexto colombiano y latinoamericano, la valorización descentralizada de residuos agrícolas y forestales (cascarilla de arroz, bagazo de caña, podas urbanas, residuos de palma y pulpa de café) representa una vía estratégica para la transición energética y la economía circular, en línea con los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y el enfoque One Health. title: The Good Daughter?
abstract: Abstract We study the impact of Federal alcohol Prohibition in 1919 on workers in the alcohol industry and their families, using newly linked census records following spouses, sons, and daughters 1910-1940. Through 1930, affected men were less likely to work and worked in lower-skilled jobs when employed. By 1940, they were more likely to be employed, suggesting delayed retirement. title: Fire return intervals are very short at Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, especially in dry miombo woodlands—a survival analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Fire shapes savanna and woodland landscapes, but the temporal spacing of recurrent fires remains poorly quantified in African miombo ecosystems. Understanding how fire-return intervals vary across vegetation and landscape settings is important for interpreting fire-regime heterogeneity, vegetation recovery, and fire-management needs. We assessed Fire-return intervals across the Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, and evaluated whether fire recurrence differed among major vegetation types. title: Organ-dependent phytochemical and pharmacological specialization in the endemic Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss.
abstract: Introduction Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss. is a western Mediterranean shrub restricted to Morocco and Spain, whose phytochemistry and pharmacology remain unexplored despite ethnomedicinal records reported for other species of the genus. This study reports the first organ-resolved characterisation of the species. Although consistent behavioral differences have been linked to variation in behaviors that create or modify extended phenotypes, their role in shaping the deployment of chemical effectors that induce phenotypic changes in other organisms remains largely unexplored. abstract: The nomenclatural history and taxonomic problems associated with two poorly known Vietnamese potamid freshwater crab species assigned initially to Hainanpotamon Dai, 1995, and later to Vietorientalia Đặng, 2012, viz., V. glabra (Đặng, 1967) and V. rubra (Đặng & Trần, 1992), are addressed. title: Precision-weighted mixed models identify high-yielding and temporally stable cowpea germplasm across three growing seasons
abstract: Introduction Cowpea is an important multipurpose legume that contributes to food and nutritional security, particularly in regions affected by environmental stress. Identifying high-yielding and stable germplasm is essential for improving breeding efficiency and developing resilient cultivars. However, distinguishing persistent genetic merit from seasonal environmental noise remains challenging when trial precision varies among years. title: Performance of smooth cayenne pineapple under tropical conditions: unravelling effects of postharvest duration and ripening stage
abstract: Introduction Optimizing harvest maturity and postharvest handling is important for maintaining pineapple quality and reducing losses under tropical storage conditions. However, limited information is available on how ripening stage at harvest interacts with postharvest storage duration to influence physical and quality characteristics of Smooth Cayenne pineapple under ambient conditions in Fiji. title: Biomass conversion in thermo‐catalytic reforming reactor: process modeling and kinetic insights for integrated intermediate pyrolysis
abstract: Abstract A sustainable energy transition in the 21st century necessitates efficient biomass‐to‐energy conversion technologies, with pyrolysis playing a crucial role. Thermo‐catalytic reforming (TCR) combines intermediate pyrolysis with a catalytic post‐reforming stage, producing higher‐quality bio‐oil, char, and syngas than conventional pyrolysis. However, process models capable of predicting TCR performance across different feedstocks remain limited. title: Merging molecular dynamics with homogenisation: a novel strategy for the modelling of nano-filtration phenomena
abstract: Filtration flows through nanoporous membranes play a crucial role in a range of cutting-edge technologies, including water purification, osmotic power generation and targeted drug delivery. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are currently considered the state-of-the-art approach for modelling nano-filtration processes. abstract: Este trabajo constituye un aporte al estudio de la Transformación Digital (TD) en pequeñas y medianas empresas de economías menos desarrolladas, al analizar la TD en empresas industriales del Partido de General Pueyrredon (PGP), uno de los principales entramados productivos de Argentina. title: Functional nanocomposite PVA hydrogels for tissue engineering: Mechanisms and applications
abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels have attracted extensive interest in tissue engineering due to their excellent biocompatibility, hydrophilicity, and tunable physicochemical properties. However, pristine PVA hydrogels often suffer from limited mechanical strength, biological activity, and functional performance, restricting their application in complex tissue regeneration. title: Digital solidarity as a process: Developing the Digital Solidarity Escalation Model (DSEM) through a netnographic study of disaster response
abstract: This study investigates the development of digital solidarity within disaster-related online communities by conducting a netnographic analysis of the 2025 Aceh–Sumatra flood response campaign on Ferry Irwandi's YouTube channel. Although previous research has investigated the interconnections between mobilization, collective identification, trust, accountability, and sustained civic engagement during disaster response, it has given less attention to the topics of crowdfunding, trust, and digital donations.
