title: From Avocado Seed Waste to Green Synthesis Laser-Induced Graphene: A Rapid, Direct, Low Cost and Flame-Retardant-Free Route
abstract: Laser-induced graphene (LIG) offers a rapid and versatile route for converting carbon-rich precursors into conductive graphitic materials. However, the direct conversion of lignocellulosic biomass remains challenging because of its heterogeneous composition and thermal degradation behavior. In this work, Fuerte avocado seed ( Persea americana Mill.) waste was investigated as a lignocellulosic precursor for the direct synthesis of LIG using CO₂ laser irradiation without flame retardants or chemical pretreatment. title: Spatial associations between urbanization, watershed runoff potential, and groundwater-depth change in a Semi-Arid Alluvial Plain, Multan, Pakistan
abstract: Groundwater decline in irrigated semi-arid alluvial plains reflects interacting land-surface, climatic, pumping, and hydrogeological controls. This study evaluates spatial associations among urbanization, Curve Number-based event-runoff potential, regional climate variability, and groundwater-depth change in Multan, Pakistan. title: AccES: A Framework for Predicting Building‐Level Loss of Accessibility to Essential Services Post‐Disasters Based on Publicly Available Information
abstract: Natural hazards significantly disrupt access to essential services, affecting individuals' capacity to withstand and recover from such events. However, existing hazard resilience models often fail to account for the interdependencies among essential services and lack the spatial resolution needed to assess accessibility loss at the building level. abstract: Objective: This study aims to provide recommendations for improving healthcare services in a private hospital and to demonstrate the potential use of multicriteria decision-making (MCDM) methods that are not commonly used in the context of quality function deployment. Methods: The research was carried out in two private hospitals. title: THE CONCEPT OF ‘BÖRİK’ (BÖRK) IN KAZAKH: AN ETYMOLOGICAL, LEXICAL AND CULTURAL STUDY
abstract: The concept of börik (börk) in Kazakh possesses a deeply rooted history in terms of its etymological, lexicological, dialectological, and cultural dimensions. Preserved continuously from Old Turkic to modern Turkic dialects, this term initially referred merely to a type of headgear; however, over time it underwent a semantic expansion and acquired powerful symbolic meanings associated with identity, status, protection, and social belonging. abstract: ABSTRACT Indus Waters Treaty (IWT, 1960) survived four major wars, decades of cross‐border militancy, and 56 years of parliamentary skepticism in India. title: Analyzing Bunyaviruses from a One Health Perspective
abstract: Zoonotic viral diseases continue to pose major challenges to global health, particularly as environmental, social and economic changes increasingly influence interactions among humans, animals, vectors, and ecosystems. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. abstract: Introduction Late sowing constrains grain yield formation in wheat by shortening the duration of post-anthesis assimilate accumulation and limiting the effective utilization of source-derived assimilates during grain filling. Optimizing nitrogen nutrition and growth regulation could help maintain physiological activity, sink development and grain productivity under late-sown conditions. abstract: Sports tourism destination competitiveness has been theorized predominantly through static, asset-based frameworks that privilege physical infrastructure and promotional capacity, yet these accounts offer limited purchase in knowledge-intensive, innovation-driven tourism systems. This study advances a dynamic alternative, drawing on the Knowledge-Based View to reconceptualize competitiveness as an ecosystem-level process rooted in the collective mobilization and transformation of knowledge. title: Plant-derived extracellular nanovesicles in musculoskeletal repair and functional rehabilitation: mitochondrial–immune–metabolic regulation
abstract: Musculoskeletal injuries and degenerative disorders caused by trauma, aging, chronic inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction frequently result in impaired functional recovery, including skeletal muscle atrophy, bone loss, cartilage degeneration, and neuromuscular dysfunction. abstract: The escalating occurrence of extreme high temperature weather exposes individuals to passive heat stress more frequently, resulting in strain on the vascular system. One example of this strain is the doubling of cardiac output during heat stress, achieved through an increase in heart rate and the redirection of blood flow from non-cutaneous tissues. These combined stressors can present substantial risks, potentially leading to syncope and cardiovascular collapse. title: Plant mediated nanoparticles from Cissus quadrangularis L.: a comprehensive review on antimicrobial resistance, biological activities and therapeutic applications
abstract: Cissus quadrangularis L. (CQ) is one of the most promising medicinal plants owing to its prominent phytochemical composition and pharmacological potentiality. The current review provides an insight into the recent progress of CQ based nanoparticles. The biosynthesis of plant-based nanoparticles using CQ extract was found to be an efficient, cost effective, and eco-friendly approach to conventional chemical methods due to presence of phenolics, flavonoids, and other phytochemicals. title: Perceived cross-cultural competency and purchase intention in foreign-influencer live streaming commerce: an extended theory of planned behavior perspective
abstract: Foreign influencers are playing a growing role in China's live-streaming commerce industry. Yet, little is known about how consumers respond to foreign influencers’ ability to communicate and adjust across cultures. To address this gap, the present study draws on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and distinguishes between two consumer perceptions: Intercultural Communication Competency (ICC) and Intercultural Adaptability (ICA). title: Microfungi associated with Azadirachta (Meliaceae, Sapindales): New species, new records, and a global checklist
abstract: Azadirachta (Meliaceae) is a small genus comprising economically and ecologically important plants, including A. indica , which is widely used in traditional medicine and other applications such as natural pest control and cosmetics. Several studies have previously been conducted on Azadirachta , including its phytochemistry and associated microfungi, particularly endophytic species inhabiting the A. indica host. title: Vector-borne zoonotic bacteria in Tunisia: from fragmented data to an integrated One Health surveillance framework
abstract: Vector-borne and vector-associated bacterial zoonoses represent an important component of infectious disease epidemiology in Tunisia. This review synthesizes available evidence on major bacterial groups, including Rickettsia , Bartonella , Anaplasma , Ehrlichia , Borrelia , Coxiella burnetii , and other arthropod-associated bacteria, using a One Health framework integrating human, animal, vector, wildlife, and environmental compartments. abstract: Tujuan: menganalisis peran manajemen inovasi dalam hilirisasi riset kimia bahan alam. title: High-density SNP mapping reveals genomic hotspots for photosynthetic traits under Huanglongbing disease in citrus
abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a major constraint to citrus production, but the genetic basis of physiological responses to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus ( C Las) infection remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized photosynthetic and gas-exchange responses and investigated their genetic architecture in 120 F₁ hybrids derived from ‘Daisy’ tangerine × Carrizo citrange. title: Chinese herbal medicine for ulcerative colitis: product-level clinical evidence, mechanistic appraisal, and a roadmap to precision translation
abstract: Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) is widely used for ulcerative colitis (UC), but product heterogeneity, variable trial quality, and limited long-term safety data preclude class-level efficacy claims. This critical narrative review therefore evaluates evidence at the level of the defined botanical drug product, formulation, route, dose, and manufacturing process. The review focuses on traditional formulas, processed botanical drugs, and proprietary preparations with documented use in Chinese medical practice. institutions: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine

title: Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles
abstract: To date, the circular economy (CE) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate. title: Development of a family functioning measure for Hispanic lesbian, gay, and bisexual adolescents
abstract: Introduction Hispanic lesbian, gay, and bisexual (LGB) adolescents experience elevated risks for HIV-related risk behaviors, drug use, and mental-health problems. These problems may be impacted by various family functioning behaviors (e.g., communication, parental involvement). However, existing family functioning measures may not adequately capture the culturally shaped, identity-specific family processes relevant to this population. abstract: Introduction Recent work has shown that Eubacterium limosum suppresses colorectal cancer (CRC), but the contribution and cellular actions of its short-chain fatty acids remain incompletely defined. Methods We characterized E. limosum KGMB01548, a human gut isolate, and examined the antitumor activity of its cell-free culture supernatant (ElCFS). title: Political discourse and crimmigration in South America: a comparative study
abstract: This article analyzes the dynamics of crimmigration in South America, examining how contemporary political discourses in Argentina, Ecuador, and Chile (2023–2025) instrumentalize penal populism as a propaganda tool that subsequently translates into regulatory changes restricting the rights of the migrants. The research argues that the approach to migration management has turned from a human rights paradigm toward a securitization logic that identifies migrants as a “useful enemy” to legitimize promises of order and punitive control. abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the key determinants of humanitarian logistics effectiveness in Malaysia’s flood disaster management and develop the good humanitarian logistics practices model (GHLPM) as an integrated framework to enhance coordination, quality assurance and operational readiness. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative approach using five focus group discussions (FGDs) involving government agencies, non-governmental organisations and community representatives directly engaged in flood response operations. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving mechanisms of cultivated land multifunctionality evolution: evidence from county-level data in Sichuan Province, China
abstract: The pursuit of socioeconomic development, food security, and ecological sustainability has driven the multifunctional evolution of cultivated land. Under the constraint of limited cultivated land resources, achieving synergy among the economic, food security, and ecological functions of cultivated land has become a major challenge for agricultural modernization in Sichuan Province. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal evolution of cultivated land multifunctionality (CLM) and investigates the driving mechanisms underlying the CLM synergy level. title: Co-application of biochar and inorganic fertilizer improves soil chemical properties without increasing carbon dioxide efflux in Alfisols of Morogoro, Tanzania
abstract: Combining biochar with inorganic fertilizers has gained global significance as a strategy for improving soil fertility; however, the agronomic and biogeochemical responses of soil remain inconsistent across environments and are further underexplored in Sub-Saharan Africa. This study evaluated the interactive effects of biochar and inorganic fertilizer on soil chemical properties and soil CO₂ efflux in Alfisols of Morogoro, Tanzania. title: PP2A targeting: balancing anticancer potential and neurological risk
abstract: Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a multifunctional serine/threonine phosphatase that regulates cell-cycle progression, oncogenic signaling, neuronal development, synaptic homeostasis, and protein proteostasis. Its dysregulation contributes to cancer, whereas impaired PP2A activity in the nervous system is linked to neurodevelopmental disorders and neurodegenerative proteinopathies, including tau and α-synuclein pathology. title: Population Dynamics of (Asplenium nidus) as a Bed Bioindicator (Paradisaea minor jobiensis Rothschild, 1897) in the Period 2018-2024 in Barawai, Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia
abstract: Asplenium nidus is an epiphytic fern recognized as an ecological bioindicator associated with the nesting habitat of the lesser bird-of-paradise (Paradisaea minor jobiensis Rothschild, 1897). This study analyzed population dynamics of A. nidus between 2018 and 2024 and examined its relationship with host tree species as an indicator of forest ecosystem health in the Imbowiari Barawai Forest, Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia. abstract: ABSTRACT Montane forest birds are highly vulnerable to climate warming because their habitats are often fragmented, topographically constrained, and difficult to track through dispersal. For Lady Amherst's Pheasant ( Chrysolophus amherstiae ), future climate risks remain poorly understood, especially the mismatch between habitat suitability and habitat accessibility. abstract: The relationship between SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses and COVID-19 risk is incompletely understood, particularly after variant-adapted booster receipt. abstract: Abstract Urban areas are increasingly exposed to mudflow hazards as unplanned urban expansion intersects with steep drainage basins and extreme rainfall events intensify under climate change. Physics-based models offer powerful tools for hazard assessment, yet their performance in densely built environments remains insufficiently explored. title: Obstáculos a la contratación pública estratégica en España: análisis factorial comparado entre sector público y sector privado
abstract: Este estudio analiza los determinantes internos y externos que condicionan la aplicación estratégica de la Directiva 2014/24/UE en España, comparando las percepciones del sector público y el privado. Objetivos: identificar las dimensiones latentes que influyen en la capacidad de ambos sectores para incorporar principios estratégicos en los procesos de contratación pública. title: Experiences, Challenges, and Coping Mechanisms of Elementary Teachers in New Normal Education In Cotabato City
abstract: The sudden shift to new normal education changed the work of elementary teachers in Cotabato City, but local evidence on their lived experiences, challenges, and ways of coping remained limited. This study explored the experiences, challenges, and coping mechanisms of elementary school teachers in the Cotabato City Division during School Year 2020–2021. abstract: Abstract Non-invasive recordings using brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. title: Phthalates: the interplay between diet, obesity, diabetes, and gut microbiota
abstract: Millions of tons of plastic are produced worldwide each year. Currently, it is almost impossible to avoid plastic and exposure to its effects. There are many chemical compounds that are used in its production. Some of them, classified as plasticizers, are phthalates, which are found in food packaging, toys, and many cosmetics. title: Between institutional strategy and disciplinary differences: The speculative redesign of university courses for preferable futures
abstract: This paper explores the challenges of curriculum design in Higher Education, focusing on the difficulty of balancing disciplinary and institutional priorities. During the pandemic, the ‘pivot’ to online teaching kept universities open, but created new problems for marginalised students and for teachers. When campuses re-opened, the rush to return to ‘normal’ also reintroducing long-established forms of prejudice and exclusion, locking in economic logics and the commodification of academic work in place of pedagogies of care. abstract: Against intensifying climate risks, this study compares the associations of sectoral, cross-sectoral, and international climate policies with annual changes in adaptation readiness. Using an unbalanced panel of 59 countries from 2002 to 2022, it estimates OLS and SUR models with policy–income interactions and assesses robustness through Mundlak and dynamic GMM specifications. abstract: Integrating seismological, gravimetric, and geodetic observations provides a complementary framework for investigating spatiotemporal relationships among seismic activity, mass redistribution, and surface deformation in active fault systems. abstract: Urban decarbonization is essential for meeting global climate goals; however, progress toward integrated low-carbon urban energy systems remains inadequately slow. The SolarEV City Concept integrates rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation with electric vehicles (EVs) as city-scale distributed mobile energy storage, using EV batteries to increase the value and flexibility of urban rooftop PV. title: A numerical forecast for birch and grasses pollen concentration in Germany
abstract: Prevention of pollen exposure is a way to assist allergic individuals to better cope with their disease. To enable this prevention, a prediction of next day(s) pollen flight is needed. The most accurate predictions are from numerical models which calculate the expected airborne pollen concentrations using simulation of emission combined with atmospheric dispersal processes (as in the SILAM model). title: Frontline perceptions of middle management as a bottleneck in cybersecurity escalation and risk communication
abstract: Purpose This study examines how frontline cybersecurity professionals perceive middle management's role in the escalation and communication of cyber risk within large organizations, and identifies the communication failures they associate with delayed or incomplete reporting of critical security issues to senior leadership. abstract: Congenital transmission of Zika virus (ZIKV) and Trypanosoma cruzi ( T. cruzi ) remains a major public health concern in the Americas. Both pathogens cross the placental barrier and cause severe neonatal outcomes, yet no confirmed congenital co-infections have been reported, and their combined effects on maternal–fetal health are unknown. abstract: The periocular region shows early visible ageing because thin skin, repetitive orbicularis oculi activity, retaining ligaments, orbital fat, and the bony framework change together. Clinical manifestations include rhytids, dermatochalasis, eyelid laxity, tear trough deformity, edema, and dark circles, with potential cosmetic, ocular-surface, and functional consequences. abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate multiple mechanisms associated with glioblastoma (GBM) therapy resistance, which remains a major challenge in GBM treatment. Some resistance mechanisms involve genetic heterogeneity, glioblastoma stem cells, the tumor microenvironment, autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, vascular adaptation, and altered transcriptional regulation. title: From measurement to mitigation: a historical review of livestock emission research in the U.S. Southern and Central Great Plains
abstract: As airborne emissions from agricultural operations began to receive more concentrated scrutiny, the federal Task Force on Agricultural Air Quality was established in the 1996 Farm Bill and began operations in 1997 to advance research and provide solutions for sustainable agricultural operations with primary focus on particulate matter, ozone, and odors. title: Wind energy in european balancing markets: policy challenges, market design, and a multi-criteria feasibility index
abstract: The transformation of the European electricity market under the Clean Energy Package (CEP) has positioned wind power as a cornerstone of the EU’s renewable energy transition. Balancing markets have consequently become strategically important, requiring wind power to assume a more active and technically capable role. abstract: Los convertidores DC-DC tipo Buck-Boost desempeñan un papel fundamental en los sistemas electrónicos de potencia modernos, ya que permiten la conversión tanto reductora como elevadora de tensión en un amplio rango de niveles de potencia, desde aplicaciones de baja tensión hasta sistemas industriales de escala megavatio. title: With whom and how: policy learning during critical junctures in Euro-Mediterranean relations
abstract: Structural power asymmetries and policy-learning dynamics shape the European Union’s choices of partners and cooperation formats in Euro-Mediterranean relations. The article traces these dynamics across five critical junctures, moments when accumulated experience and actor constellations may enable foreign policy change: the post–Cold War period, 9/11, the 2004 enlargement, the Arab uprisings and the post-2020 “permacrisis”. abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate the relationship between environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and corporate financial performance (CFP), focusing on the moderating role of board gender diversity and the influence of national cultural orientation. title: From the Euro-Mediterranean partnership to DG MENA: examining three decades of Euro-Mediterranean relations through the lenses of policy learning
abstract: Abstract This Special Issue examines the thirty-year trajectory of Euro-Mediterranean relations, through the lenses of policy learning. By analyzing what is learned, how learning occurs, and what outcomes emerge from the learning process, this Special Issue highlights how and to what extent EU policymakers acquire knowledge and interact with different actors. abstract: ABSTRACT Setting urban water connection fees is a complex policy problem: Fees must balance affordability, equity, and adequate cost recovery. This study develops a two‐stage framework for setting urban water connection charges in Iran. abstract: Public schools provide continued professional development, but there are still gaps between policy goals and classroom practice. This study determined the implementation of Development Education programs along objectives and content integration, teaching strategies, instructional materials and monitoring evaluation and mechanisms in selected public schools in Lapu-Lapu City. The study used a mixed-methods approach, obtaining quantitative survey data and qualitative interview data. abstract: Part I of this two-part series advanced the CHORA Hypothesis as a candidate account of biological coherence: how organised biological function is sustained, transformed, and lost within the organism and across the lineage over deep time. abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the relation between digitalization and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting using a sample of listed US banks from 2010 to 2022. Our study is based on a two‐step theoretical framework, building on voluntary disclosure and signaling theory: First, we expect and find technological progress to enhance internal information quality. abstract: Introduction Territorial health equity depends not only on expanding health resources but also on aligning local capacity with territorial planning contexts. We examined whether changes in hospital and health-center bed allocation were associated more strongly with territorial planning context or local fiscal-economic capacity. abstract: Outdoor spaces in hot-arid environments are frequently exposed to severe thermal stress, limiting their thermal usability and comfort. Urban vegetation can provide an important passive strategy for improving outdoor microclimatic conditions; however, its performance depends on the characteristics of the vegetation and the surrounding spatial context, including courtyard orientation. abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. abstract: Medium- to low-temperature geothermal resources hosted in sedimentary basins are important for regional heating and direct utilization. This study investigates the geothermal reservoir characteristics, fluid origin, genesis, and development potential of the Sanjiaochenggou area in the Jinchang Depression, a poorly explored inland sedimentary basin in the eastern Hexi Corridor. abstract: Introduction Complementary and integrative healthcare (CIH) approaches play an increasingly important role in oncology care, involving a wide range of healthcare professionals and therapeutic methods. While patient demand for CIH and the evidence base for individual interventions have grown considerably, the implementation of structured counseling services for the effective and safe use of CIH remains limited. To address this gap, a controlled, multicenter implementation study was conducted at four Comprehensive Cancer Centers (CCC) in Germany to establish an outpatient, interprofessional, evi

title: The Dynamics of the Racial Wealth Gap
abstract: ABSTRACT We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap (the wealth of Black households relative to white ones) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations. We match the model to the cross‐sectional distributions of wealth and earnings by race. We find that equalizing earnings is critical for permanent reductions in racial wealth inequality, and that one‐time transfers will have only transitory effects unless earnings are also equalized. title: Biofortified feed crops: bridging plant biotechnology and animal-derived functional foods
abstract: Micronutrient deficiency continues to be a significant global nutritional problem, especially in populations relying on staple diets with limited micronutrient diversity. Biofortification presents a sustainable way to enhance crop nutritional quality through methods like agronomic practices, traditional breeding, microbial interventions, nanotechnology, transgenic techniques, and genome editing. This review critically explores these strategies, focusing on their application to feed and forage crops, which are often neglected in biofortification discussions. It examines factors affecting micron

title: Supply Chain Management and Business Performance of Agri-Farm Businesses in the Province of Rizal
abstract: Agricultural enterprises in the Province of Rizal face persistent supply chain challenges, including fragmented supplier networks, inadequate post-harvest infrastructure, and limited coordination across production and distribution stages. This study assessed supply chain management (SCM) practices and their relationship with the non-financial business performance of agri-farm businesses in Rizal. Specifically, it examined SCM implementation using the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Model dimensions of Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, and Return, alongside business performance indicators c

title: The cingulate–mitochondrial–resonome axis: a conceptual framework integrating rehabilitation, interoception, and affective–motor processing in canine chronic pain
abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal disease in Canis lupus familiaris (dogs) is associated not only with biomechanical dysfunction but also with alterations in autonomic regulation, affective processing, movement behavior, and chronic pain adaptation. Current rehabilitation models primarily emphasize peripheral tissue healing and biomechanics while placing less emphasis on interactions among interoception, nociception, autonomic regulation, and affective-motor processing. title: Playing together, living together: Community-based music learning as a catalyst for rural wellbeing
abstract: This article explores how participatory instrumental music tuition can strengthen wellbeing, confidence, and social cohesion for adults living in rural Scotland. Focusing on the town of Millport, Isle of Cumbrae, the study was conducted as part of the Community Instrumental Music Service for Rural Scotland (CIMSRS), an initiative designed to address barriers to adult music learning caused by isolation, limited provision, and economic constraints. Nineteen adults aged between 25 and 75 took part in weekly group violin and viola sessions, culminating in a community performance. Through individua

title: The immune phenotype of circulating tumor cells: from escape mechanisms to immunotherapy navigation
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) must survive immune attack in the bloodstream before they can contribute to distant metastasis. Their immune phenotype, including checkpoint ligands, antigen-presentation molecules, and immunomodulatory features, can be assessed through serial blood sampling and may provide information complementary to established immunotherapy biomarkers. title: Faker Island: Profiling misinformation sharers on the French Twittersphere
abstract: What are the distinctive characteristics of misinformation sharers? So far, most studies have focused on the U.S., a two-party system with a highly polarized media landscape, leaving open the question of what misinformation sharers look like in other socio-political contexts. Research has also prioritized testing causal links between cognitive or political variables and misinformation sharing, while paying less attention to fine-grained descriptions of who these users are. To address this gap, we analyze the French Twittersphere using ideological inference methods and a matching procedure. Dra

title: Mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine interventions in the gastric ‘inflammation-to-carcinoma’ cascade: advances in in vitro models from monolayer cells to organoids
abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The Correa cascade, progressing from chronic gastritis through precancerous lesions to adenocarcinoma, provides the framework for understanding gastric mucosal stepwise malignant transformation. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas, such as Zuojin Pills and Wuji Pills, have been historically used to treat gastric disorders including epigastric pain and acid regurgitation, yet their mechanisms of action in blocking the inflammation-to-carcinoma transition remain incompletely understood. title: Identifying Arctic states vulnerable to rapid ice loss with a convolutional neural network
abstract: This work investigates the incidence of rapid ice-loss events in the Arctic, in which a substantial fraction of September sea-ice is lost in only a few years. Such events are seen to occur in climate model simulations forced with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations, but not as yet in the relatively short observational record. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using six large climate model ensembles to diagnose vulnerability to rapid ice-loss events. The trained model is shown to separate higher and lower risk states in out-of-sample climate models via a leave-one-out cross-val

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers

title: Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1)
abstract: Infrared small target detection is often used in different civilian and military applications to detect static or moving targets in scenes like in ground, air and sea surveillance. First valuable research has emerged since 30 years ago and the two last decades witnessed very significant publications in this field following the rise of low-rank and sparse decomposition (model-based methods) and deep learning models (data-based methods). title: Competition-Aware CPC Forecasting with Near-Market Coverage
abstract: Cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search is an auction-generated outcome shaped by a competitive landscape that is only partially observable from any single advertiser’s history. From 1.66 billion Google Ads log records for a concentrated car-rental market (2021–2023), we construct a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks (218,924 keyword–week observations) and build competition-aware proxies from keyword text, CPC trajectories, and geographic market structure. title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
abstract: Air pollution poses a significant threat to public health, exacerbated by the rapid industrialization and urbanization of modern society. While traditional deep learning offers predictive capabilities, recent advancements in quantum machine learning (QML) present a compelling alternative. Here, we introduce a scalable hybrid framework that integrates variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing. title: Kriging and Gaussian processes: interconnected frameworks for spatial modelling and prediction
abstract: Spatial modelling and inference arise across many areas of science and engineering, with Kriging and Gaussian process (GP) regression serving as two widely used predictive models. Although grounded in the same random field theory, these approaches are often treated in isolation. As a result, their connection has been obscured by differences in terminology, notation, and practical implementation. This separation largely reflects their independent development within geostatistics and machine learning, respectively. title: Sea-Net: A Small and Inherently Interpretable Neural Network for Time Series Classification
abstract: Traditional time-series classification methods often operate as black boxes, providing a class prediction without indicating which time point or time interval within the series led to that prediction. To improve temporal interpretability, MILLET (Multiple Instance Learning with Temporal Explanation), which combines an InceptionTime encoder with Conjunctive Pooling, provides both classification and temporal explanations. title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning in Oncology
abstract: Deep learning has enabled substantial advances in oncology, including cancer detection and diagnosis, medical image analysis, tumor characterization, treatment planning, response assessment, and outcome prediction. However, conventional data-driven models often require large annotated datasets, exhibit limited generalization across heterogeneous clinical settings, and lack explicit mechanisms for incorporating the physical, physiological, and biological principles underlying cancer development and treatment. Physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) integrates governing physical laws, mechanistic

title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
abstract: Learning constitutive laws of complex fluids from velocity data (i.e. indirect observations) is a PDE-constrained inverse problem in which expressive neural parameterizations risk breaking the well-posedness of the forward physics model. We address this tension by learning, rather than the constitutive law itself, the dissipation potential: a scalar function whose convexity, frame-indifference, and dissipativity propagate into the underlying continuum mechanics and guarantee the structural properties needed for a well-posed and generalizable forward PDE. title: Image-Space Refraction Correction for Underwater 3D Reconstruction: Warping Flat-Port Views into Pinhole Perspective
abstract: Consumer-grade cameras in flat-port housings are widely used for underwater exploration and mapping of coral reefs and seafloor habitats due to their low cost and accessibility. However, refraction at flat-port interfaces causes bowl-shaped deformation in reconstructed scenes and camera trajectories, compromising the metric accuracy required for mapping and navigation. To remove the dominant refractive distortion before reconstruction, we introduce a physics-based refraction correction in image space. title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph
institutions: Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (Switzerland)

title: Onboard Marine Anomaly Detection on Φsat-2: From Simulation-Based Development to In-Orbit Demonstration
abstract: Onboard Artificial Intelligence can improve responsiveness and bandwidth efficiency of Earth Observation systems by processing data directly on the satellite. This paper presents the experience gained from the development, onboard integration, and post-launch adaptation of a lightweight marine anomaly detection pipeline deployed on the European Space Agency’s Φsat-2 mission. The application combines sea segmentation, self-supervised feature encoding of marine regions, generic anomaly detection based on deviations from a normal sea state, and optional characterization of selected anomaly types.

title: Fluorescence-enhanced Whisker Array with Vision-based Deformation Analysis for Underwater Source Localization
abstract: Deep-water biological observation is essential for understanding marine organisms and their interactions with the environment. However, conventional optical and acoustic approaches can introduce stimuli that alter animal behavior and bias biological observations. This paper proposes a fluorescence-enhanced whisker array sensing system that pinpoints underwater hydrodynamic sources through local optical readout rather than direct source imaging. Five spatially oriented whiskers, fabricated with nitinol cores and fluorescent urethane shells, are integrated with ultraviolet excitation and a monoc

title: Real-world application of deep learning in large-scale seismic interference attenuation: A case study in the Camie field of Angola
abstract: In marine seismic acquisition, seismic interference (SI) occurs when energy from nearby external seismic source(s) is captured. It typically appears as coherent noise with linear or non-linear movement and varying amplitudes across different sail lines. SI is commonly observed and poses a challenge for seismic data processing. We present a case history of a previously proposed deep neural network (DNN)-based workflow applied for SI attenuation across a marine seismic block in the Camie Field of Angola. This field survey covers over 345 km2 and is marked by the challenge of multiple SI types. T

title: A Physics-Constrained Implicit Profile Network for Continuous Reconstruction of Tropical Cyclone Near-Surface Wind Profiles
abstract: Near the ocean surface, tropical cyclone winds change rapidly with height, but direct measurements are limited because aircraft dropsondes provide only sparse and irregular observations. Continuous wind profiles are important for understanding hurricane boundary-layer processes, improving storm-surge prediction, supporting offshore engineering, and assessing coastal hazards. In this study, we developed an artificial intelligence model that combines machine learning with physical principles to reconstruct continuous wind profiles from sparse observations. title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Quantum machine learning, and quantum neural networks (QNNs) in particular, are advancing fields with growing potential. Although systematic comparisons of QNN configurations have been explored primarily for classification tasks, comparatively little attention has been given to regression problems, particularly financial time series forecasting. This study presents a large-scale systematic comparative evaluation of QNN component configurations for financial time series forecasting, using the GBP/USD spot exchange rate as a case study. A grid search across encoding methods, ansatz designs, qubi

title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part I: Framework and Recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target detection and recognition are essential to marine surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Despite substantial advances in deep learning, existing systems typically produce binary detection decisions, categorical labels, or scalar confidence scores, offering limited insight into the physical evidence underlying their outputs. title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
abstract: Day-ahead electricity forecasts can help building operators schedule heating, ventilation, and other services around anticipated demand. Choosing a forecasting model also requires balancing accuracy with its forecast-time inputs, local training, and computational requirements. We benchmark statistical, machine-learning, recurrent neural-network, and pretrained TimesFM models for a university building. We use chronological validation and evaluate all configurations on the same 57 test days, comparing accuracy across workdays, weekends, and holidays alongside local fitting and forecasting time.

title: Robust Prediction of Internal Wave-Affected Multi-Scale Sound Speed Distribution Using Lightweight Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Hybrid Basis Functions
abstract: The underwater sound speed distribution directly governs acoustic propagation paths, rendering it critically important for underwater acoustic communication and target localization. Conventional sound speed profile (SSP) prediction methods provide a good way to estimate the underwater sound speed distribution without on-site data measurement, thus breaking through the coverage area constraints of sonar observation equipment and making the model universal in most marine areas. title: Physics-based deep learning for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression
abstract: Surface-related multiple elimination (SRME) is an indispensable processing step in marine seismic exploration, comprising two main components: multiple prediction and adaptive subtraction. While the multiple prediction is theoretically data-driven and relies on the data itself, the adaptive subtraction step requires a fairly subjective manual control. Our approach introduces a purely data-driven and physics-based deep learning (PDL) algorithm for improving the adaptive multiple subtraction to significantly enhanced performance. There are two main innovations in the proposed deep-learning (DL)

title: Sequential Conditional Independence Testing with Machine Learning Models
abstract: Conditional independence testing is a ubiquitous problem in scientific discovery. The widely employed model-X assumption shifts the modelling burden from the dependence of the output on the inputs to the dependencies within the inputs. Log-optimal e-variables have been studied in this setting, but it remains unclear how to incorporate machine learning models into their design. Other approaches test exchangeability directly, yielding an e-variable with lower power in theory but, surprisingly, higher power in practice. title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions
abstract: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is computationally expensive for iterative building design. Deep learning surrogates offer faster predictions, but generalization across varying room dimensions remains challenging. This study compares two geometry-conditioned neural network surrogate models for rapid indoor airflow and temperature field prediction under varying room sizes. During the architectural design stage, this method is relevant for real-time assessment of whether conditioned supply air will effectively provide fresh and cool air throughout rooms with varying heights and lengths. title: Learning native eddy-resolving ocean dynamics outperforms coarse emulation and downscaling
abstract: Eddy-resolving ocean simulations are essential for representing mesoscale dynamics that regulate ocean circulation, energy transport, and climate variability. However, they are costly to generate, store, and share. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help, but it remains unclear whether high-resolution ocean fields can be faithfully represented by evolving ocean states at coarse resolution followed by spatial downscaling, or whether dynamical evolution needs to be learned directly from native high-resolution simulations. title: Is this machine playing?
abstract: We placed a modern AI coding assistant in an unintended role: as the mind of a body on an unknown digital island. With only a minimal instruction mentioning no specific task, reward, or activity, the machine started animating its virtual body. Across thirty-hour runs, the embodied AI agent climbed hills, stacked blocks into towers, drew mandalas, reinterpreted sports, ran experiments on the physics of its world, and learned techniques that later expanded what it could accomplish. title: Unsupervised and Supervised Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 2)
abstract: Since the rise of supervised deep learning modelet dets, researchers has attempt to solve infrared small targection using various models like conventional neural networks, GANS, Transformers, Mixture of Experts and recent graph/hypergraph neural networks. Moreover, these deep neural networks methods surpassed the traditional unsupervised models and the low-rank and sparse decomposition unsupervised models reviewed in "Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1). title: EM-SNN: Efficiently Modulated Spiking Neural Network for Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
abstract: Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient alternative to artificial neural networks (ANNs), their application to remote sensing image dehazing remains limited. A key challenge arises from the coupling between haze-induced high-frequency attenuation and discrete spike thresholding. This interaction suppresses weak responses and fundamentally limits the recovery of edges, textures, and fine details in spiking dehazing models. title: A Robust Learning Framework for Deep-Learning-Based Radar Target Detection With Partially Mislabeled Training Data
abstract: Deep-learning-based radar target detection has substantially improved detection performance, but its effectiveness depends critically on the correctness of the training labels assigned to radar echo samples. In practical applications, training data may contain partially mislabeled samples, which can cause detection models to learn biased supervisory information and thereby degrade detection performance. title: Explainable Failure Prediction and Prevention in Maritime
abstract: Maritime systems operate in highly dynamic environments where unexpected equipment failures can compromise safety, reliability, and operational efficiency. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, digital twins, and predictive maintenance enable proactive failure prediction and prevention. However, ensuring trustworthy and explainable decision-making remains a major challenge in safety-critical maritime applications. title: Textual Environmental Context and Spatial Graphs for LLM-Based Regional SST Forecasting
abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) forecasting depends on local temporal persistence, regional spatial dependence, and environmental conditions that evolve with the forecast date. We study how these heterogeneous conditions can be presented to a large language model (LLM) for regional multi-step forecasting without serializing the full SST grid as text. title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. title: Parameter Estimation in Machining Dynamics with Regenerative Delay and Nonsmooth Friction using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: A multi-domain eXtended Physics-Informed Neural Network (XPINN) framework is developed for nonsmooth Delay Differential Equations (DDEs). This is the first implementation to demonstrate the efficacy of partitioning the temporal domain into subdomains of integer multiples of the characteristic time delay and progressively training the associated subnetworks while freezing previously learned parameters. title: TailWeather: from tail to extremes, a global climatological dataset for machine-learning weather forecasting
abstract: Abstract. Weather forecasting models are usually judged by their average skill, yet average skill says little about the rare conditions that matter most. Testing forecasts on those conditions requires a target defined consistently everywhere. Disaster catalogs record harm, but they are sparse and shaped by reporting; climatological tails can be defined everywhere, but rarity does not imply harm. We present TailWeather, a global, land-only, 0.25° dataset of climatological tail events derived from ERA5, covering 1981–2022 and early January 2023. title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels
abstract: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. title: Generative and deterministic deep learning models comparison for fine-scale precipitation retrievals from infrared brightness temperature
abstract: Accurate precipitation estimation at fine spatial scales is critical for hydrology, agriculture, and climate studies. Infrared brightness temperatures from geostationary satellites offer excellent temporal coverage over continental-scale domains. However, because these measurements primarily characterize cloud-top properties rather than precipitation processes near the surface, their correlation with rainfall intensity remains limited, making quantitative precipitation estimation challenging. title: PolUR: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration
abstract: Recovering high-quality images from degraded underwater observations is crucial for underwater exploration. Polarization observations show promise as an effective source of complementary physical cues for recovering target radiance under clear-water conditions. However, existing methods have yet to jointly model raw intensity information and polarization cues to enable image restoration driven by an understanding of mixed degradations (color casts, haze, and low light). title: On the Comparison of Optimizers for Imbalanced Learning
abstract: Data imbalance is pervasive in machine learning, from rare words and anomalies to underrepresented patterns in heterogeneous or cross-tabulated data. We study idealized optimizers geometries in continuous time to model small-step training in deep learning. We assume that the source of imbalance is unobserved: the optimizer has only access to the aggregate training loss ignoring the exact contributions of the majority and minority groups. title: CORAL: Cross-modal Vector Retrieval via Incremental Graph Construction at Scale
abstract: Cross-modal vector retrieval is widely used in multimodal systems, such as search engines and vector databases. It typically operates in out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, where query vectors follow a distribution that differs from that of the vectors stored in the database. In such cases, conventional indexes suffer significant performance degradation, and even methods specially designed for OOD remain limited by inefficient use of query modal characteristics, restricted GPU parallelism, and inadequate support for dynamic updates. title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
abstract: Koopman operator theory provides a linear framework for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems and has become a major tool for data-driven modeling. A central challenge, however, is that finite-dimensional approximations computed by methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) require the dictionary to be specified a priori. title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
abstract: Poly(1,3-dioxolane) (pDXL) is a chemically recyclable polyether that can be synthesized by living cationic ring-opening polymerization with precise control of chain length into the ultra-high-molecular-weight (UHMW) regime, where it acquires enhanced mechanical properties. Like most polymers, however, it has amorphous condensed-phase structure, and diffraction measurements alone cannot resolve the atomistic microstructure that underlies them. title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery
abstract: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. title: Statistical Oceanography of Profiling Floats and Surface Drifters
abstract: The Global Ocean Observing System is key to understanding oceanic variability and climate change. The ocean is vast and often sparsely and irregularly sampled in time and space by various instruments and systems. Statistical models, especially spatio-temporal ones, are useful for enabling inferences, forecasts and decisions from sparse oceanic observations. This article focuses on the statistical treatment of two types of in situ observations in the Global Ocean Observing System: from profiling floats and surface drifters, focusing on the Argo and Global Drifter Programs. title: Detecting Nighttime Anomalies from NASA Black Marble Using a Generalized Spatio-Temporally Robust Framework of Machine Leaning Ensembles
abstract: Nighttime lights from NASA's Black Marble product suite capture thermal and light emission signals from anomalous events including fires, volcanic eruptions, and gas flaring. Existing detection approaches rely primarily on thermal bands, limiting sensitivity to weaker signals. We propose a novel machine learning framework that jointly models Black Marble M-band and Day/Night Band (DNB) signals to derive a generalized, spatio-temporally robust ensemble of anomaly detectors. title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data
abstract: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. title: SEA-LM: Egocentric Spatial Audio Understanding for Wearable Microphone Arrays
abstract: Embodied, ego-centric intelligence fundamentally requires the ability to comprehend spatial audio within complex environments. While large audio-language models excel at mono-channel reasoning, they lack spatial awareness, discarding critical spatial cues that enable sound localization and that can improve the disentanglement of overlapping sound sources. title: Scalable AI Uncertainty Quantification via Generalized Laplace Active Subspaces
abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for deploying neural networks in scientific and high-stakes applications, but full Bayesian inference over the network parameters is computationally infeasible. We propose a low-rank generalized Laplace approximation for neural-network UQ based on a small number of data-informed curvature directions. title: Input-Constrained Active Disturbance Rejection Control for AUVs
abstract: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. However, existing stability analyses typically assume bounded control inputs and derivatives, which are difficult to guarantee under unknown disturbances and measurement noise. title: When Can You Prune Your Network? A Study of Intermediate Neurons in Multilingual Speech Parsing
abstract: End-to-end speech parsing, a task recently proposed, consists in predicting both the transcription and the syntactic tree for a spoken utterance. Existing architectures for speech parsing often utilise intermediate neural networks. In this work, we examine the effectiveness of intermediate neural networks (NN) for parsing, and, specifically, what role do they play. We introduce a simpler end-to-end architecture for speech parsing, where we remove these intermediate NN units, reducing the parameters by 12%, while achieving comparable or better performance than prior method on both automatic spe
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: A Unified Dynamics Framework for Reinforcement Learning and Classical Control of a Six-DOF Pipeline-Tracking ROV in NVIDIA Isaac Sim
abstract: Reinforcement learning controllers for underwater vehicles are usually trained against one physics representation and deployed against another, so reported performance does not always describe behavior outside training. This paper presents a pipeline-tracking architecture for a six-degree-of-freedom remotely operated vehicle (ROV) in which one Universal Scene Description (USD) scene supplies the real BlueROV2-Heavy mass, added-mass, damping, buoyancy, and thruster parameters to both halves of the system: a vectorized NumPy implementation of Fossen's marine-craft equations, and an interactive N

title: Learning minimum-time navigation policies in two-dimensional flows with a genetic algorithm
abstract: We study minimum-time navigation between two points in a known two-dimensional fluid flow for a vessel with fixed-magnitude slip velocity and controllable direction. The navigation policy is parameterized by a neural network and optimized using a genetic algorithm that evolves an ensemble of candidate strategies through Darwinian selection and parameter mutation, without crossover. The method recovers analytical and numerical optimal-control solutions in several benchmark cases, including two-dimensional turbulence, and outperforms Q-learning and one-step actor-critic method. institutions: National Research University Higher School of Economics

title: Co-Designing Community-Centered AI Education for Adults: A Midwestern Case Study
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) education is increasingly important, yet adults outside higher education receive less attention. We report a case study of an AI education session with 54 adults (48 in-person and 6 virtual) in a predominantly African American community on the east side of a major Midwestern city. We ask: "What does AI education for adults outside formal educational systems look like in practice?" and "What does this AI education session reveal about AI literacy at the community level?" Through a co-designed session developed with community partners, we found that concerns about AI

title: Generative AI translations in high-stakes emergency messaging
abstract: Emergency messaging such as extreme-weather reports and earthquake instructions can involve high stakes, to the extent that translation errors can lead to tragic consequences. The use of machine translation or generative artificial intelligence might therefore not be recommended. On the other hand, time savings in the initial translation can allow greater investments of resources in revision and authorization processes, as well as a wider range of target languages. An experiment with generative AI translations of an earthquake instruction text from English into Chinese and Spanish shows that u

title: Choosing an energy-efficient software architecture for building system diagnostic support
abstract: Around 30\% of global energy expenditure can be attributed to the building sector, where a large portion of energy-consumption could be avoided by repairing existing faults. Fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) software addresses this issue; however, its creation and operation also have an environmental impact. The magnitude of this impact is influenced by the diagnosis architecture, as different architectures and methods have different energy demands. Yet, simply considering the energy consumed by the software itself is not sufficient to assess its overall environmental impact, since the diagn

title: Physics-Guided Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Modeling for Natural Supercavity Geometry of an Axisymmetric Conical Cavitator
abstract: Natural supercavitation behind conical cavitators generates a vapor-filled envelope that, when sustained over the full body of a high-speed underwater vehicles, reduces hydrodynamic skin-friction drag and enables performance levels unattainable in fully wetted flow. Accurate prediction of maximum cavity length and maximum cavity radius and local cavity profile as functions of cavitation number and cone half-angle is essential for both the static design and the real-time shape management of super-cavitating torpedo cavitators. Classical analytical models provide computationally inexpensive pred

title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
abstract: While deep learning models for tabular data have recently received significant research attention, the choice of objective functions for regression tasks remains an understudied degree of freedom. Several lines of research offer alternatives to the standard Mean Squared Error (MSE), but differences in datasets, backbones, and evaluation protocols make their practical benefits difficult to compare. In this work, we address this gap by performing a systematic re-evaluation of regression objectives across a broad collection of established tabular datasets and multiple neural backbones. Our compar
institutions: National Research University Higher School of Economics

title: Dataset-Specific Encoding of Image Content Underlies Cross-Dataset Failure in Brain MRI Foundation Models
abstract: Frozen features of brain MRI foundation models lose accuracy on new datasets, a failure usually blamed on the features encoding where each scan came from. We show that the failure lies elsewhere. Across 17 public datasets and eight frozen representations, every representation recognizes the MRI sequence within each dataset, yet most fail on an unseen one. The cause is neither dataset encoding nor a shift of each dataset: the content itself is encoded along different directions in each dataset. This explains which datasets fail, for the sequence and for sex, and why removing the dataset signal

title: Sim-to-Real RL for ASVs using SysID
abstract: Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) operating in dynamic marine environments require robust control policies for tasks such as path following and station keeping, making reinforcement learning (RL) a promising alternative to classical controllers. However, existing ASV simulators rarely support parallel environments for RL training. Such existing simulators require accurate hydrodynamic modeling from computational fluid dynamics solvers or towing tank tests for setting hydrodynamic parameters to address the sim-to-real gap. To address these challenges, we present an ASV simulator and accompanyi

title: The Evolution of In-Premise Networks In the Era of Immersive Services: From Copper to Fiber-to-The Room [Invited Tutorial]
abstract: The telecommunications industry is shifting toward an experience-driven era defined by immersive applications that impose stringent network demands. While passive optical network (PON)-based Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) architectures have historically delivered high-capacity broadband, a growing performance gap between access and indoor networks necessitates driving fiber deeper into premises. Complementing existing copper and WiFi technologies, Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) is emerging as a critical enabler. This article examines the drivers of this architectural shift, specifically focusing on collab

title: Understanding Interfirm AI Talent Flow Networks through Online Professional Profiles
abstract: Artificial intelligence capabilities are often measured as resources accumulated within firms, yet they also circulate across organizational boundaries through worker mobility. Drawing on a database of approximately 535 million employment records across 58 countries, we reconstruct the inter-firm network of AI talent flows over 2010--2022. We find that AI talent inflows are becoming increasingly concentrated among a small set of leading firms, with stronger preferential attachment than in general labor mobility. Yet the network core remains contestable: central positions in AI networks change
institutions: Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology

title: Generalized Matheron Variational Implicit Processes
abstract: Implicit-process priors specify distributions over functions through sample-forward mechanisms such as Bayesian neural networks and stochastic simulators, but their function-space densities are typically unavailable. We introduce Generalized Matheron Variational Implicit Processes (GMVIP), a pathwise variational family for posterior inference with such priors. For Gaussian-process priors, GMVIP recovers the standard inducing-variable variational GP construction; for general implicit priors, its empirical covariance construction preserves the prior mean and covariance in the population limit. title: Coarse-Grained Predictive Resource Allocation Framework enabling In-Premise XR Collaborations
abstract: Immersive extended reality (XR) applications are key enablers of human-centric connectivity in next-generation networks. However, meeting their high-throughput, ultra-low-latency, and high-reliability demands while preventing cyber-sickness remains a critical challenge, especially in environments with non-deterministic wireless connectivity. Fiber-To-The-Room (FTTR), extending widely deployed Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) infrastructure, offers a promising solution. Yet, satisfying the stringent Quality-of-Experience (QoE) requirements of XR collaborators demands robust resource allocation across t

title: Know Yourself and Know Your Neighbour: A Syntactically Informed Self-Supervised Compositional Sentence Representation Learning Framework using a Recursive Hypernetwork
abstract: Sentence representation learning is still an open challenge in Natural Language Processing. In this work, we propose a new self-supervised framework for learning sentence representations, using a special type of neural network called a recursive hypernetwork. Our proposed model composes the representation of a sentence from representations of words by applying a recursive composition through the parse tree. institutions: ADAPT - Centre for Digital Content Technology

title: Spatial Prediction with Guided Diffusion
abstract: Spatial prediction is a critically important task in data analyses that involve spatially or spatio-temporally-referenced data. It is commonly carried out using hierarchical models, which comprise a process model describing the latent process of interest, and a data model describing how the process is observed. The target quantity is the predictive distribution, which is the conditional distribution of the latent spatial process given the observed data. title: FlexCast: Adaptive Weather Forecasting from Arbitrary Field Sets
abstract: Most deep learning weather models assign a fixed set of variables and pressure levels to predefined channels, limiting transfer across atmospheric field configurations. This dependence on a fixed field set limits the transferability of trained models across atmospheric field configurations. We propose FlexCast, a field-adaptive weather forecasting model that uses a single set of parameters to produce identity-aligned forecasts for variable-cardinality subsets drawn from a 69-field ERA5 registry. institutions: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning has gained significant attention in recent years. In regimes of limited data, parametrized Gaussian processes have become popular. Existing approaches, however, often face limitations, such as requiring parametrizable (also called controllable) systems or a large number of output tasks. In this work, we introduce a systematic procedure we call "ghost tasking", using auxiliary tasks to circumvent these limitations. title: Rethinking Tabular Foundation Models On Data Streams
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) outperform established machine learning models on tabular benchmarks through in-context learning. Building on this success, interest is growing in applying them to data streams, where data arrive continuously and evolve over time. On a stream, a TFM adapts by updating its context rather than its parameters, so its accuracy and cost depend on which examples it keeps and how often it rebuilds its context. We therefore present a systematic study of TFMs on data streams, covering memory management, computational cost, and stream-specific challenges such as concept
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: An AI-assisted conditioning and geological interpretation workflow for usage in implicit geological modeling
abstract: Implicit modeling and Relative Geologic Time are geological modeling techniques that enable more efficient, faster, less biased and more reproducible modeling results. For optimal operation, these techniques require many well-constrained input data. In the framework of the Horizon Europe GO-Forward and MOOI WarmingUP GOO projects and to accelerate Implicit modeling, Machine Learning (ML) methods have been tested and implemented in a toolkit for the interpretation of (onshore) seismic data from the shallow to deep range (+- 300 - 3500 m). institutions: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research
Fraunhofer Research Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies IEG

title: Radar Intelligent Detection with Coarse-Grained Labels
abstract: Many deep learning based radar target detectors rely on range-cell level labels for training, which are expensive to obtain. To reduce the labeling burden, this paper presents a training strategy that uses only range-window level labels. Specifically, two sub-echoes are randomly cropped from the same window echo, resulting in a known relative shift between them. A siamese Transformer is then used to identify target-salient responses from one sub-echo and form pseudo labels, which are mapped to the paired sub-echo according to the known shift. institutions: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: A Stateful Research Information Infrastructure for Scientific Discovery
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied to an expanding range of scientific activities, including literature analysis, hypothesis generation, software development and automated experimentation. Yet these capabilities rely on a more fundamental condition: scientific information must remain identifiable and traceable across systems and over time. In practice, different versions of a work and their associated records and files are often scattered across services and local directories. This fragmentation forces researchers to identify and contextualize the same work repeatedly, disrupting co

title: Feature Space Adaptation for Effortless Gaussian Process Flows
abstract: Outside the linear-Gaussian regime, conditional sampling from Gaussian processes (GPs) is challenging. Recent methods such as FlowGP (Moss et al., (2026)) can condition on arbitrary non-linear and non-Gaussian statements, but at considerable cost: an expensive iterative and high-dimensional diffusion that requires hand-specified kernel hyperparameters. title: Automated Disinformation and Malicious AI Swarms: Risks for Democracy and Development in Africa
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping how information is produced, accessed, and circulated, while enabling disinformation campaigns of increasing scale and sophistication. There is currently no clear evidence that fully autonomous AI swarms conduct influence operations at scale, but their enabling capabilities are advancing. We define malicious AI swarms as coordinated, persistent, and adaptive multi-agent systems designed for influence operations, distinguishing them from AI-assisted content production and centrally managed synthetic personas. institutions: Bavarian Research Institute for Digital Transformation

title: Accounting for model error in ensemble variational data assimilation through learned generative dynamics
abstract: Many approaches have recently been proposed to combine data assimilation with machine learning for improved forecasts with geophysical models. Here, we focus on combining advanced sequential data assimilation schemes with a generative forecasting model which accounts for complex model errors. This generative model provides a stochastic approximation of the conditional distribution of the successor state given the current state. Centre d'Enseignement et de Recherche en Environnement Atmosphérique

title: AI-Based On-Board Maritime Object Detection for Earth Observation Payload Data Reduction on Versal Embedded Hardware
abstract: Very-high-resolution Earth-observation satellites acquire more data than they can store and downlink, while in maritime surveillance the vessels cover a tiny fraction of each scene. We study onboard vessel detection as a way to select what is downlinked, which reduces the data according to its content rather than coding every pixel; it is complementary to conventional onboard compression. The work follows three axes. (i) Data and algorithm: a controlled dataset is generated from 68 annotated Maxar scenes with 43 vessel classes, and a YOLOX-S detector is trained on it.
