institutions: Tianjin University of Finance and Economics
Tianjin University of Science and Technology

title: Synthetic Sources?: Auditing Generative Search Engine Citations for Evidence of AI-Generated Sources
abstract: The growing accessibility of Large Language Models via conversational interfaces capable of responding to users’ questions by drawing on, synthesizing, and citing information from the web (i.e., Generative Search Engines) has simpli- fied the information-seeking process for users. However, with the proliferation of AI-generated content on the web, it is un- clear whether these engines can reliably omit citing synthetic sources (i.e., AI-generated sources). Should these engines be unable to do so, this puts users at risk of harm by treat- ing information from AI-generated sources synthesized in

title: A theory for detecting the Turing instability on static and temporal multiplex networks
abstract: The purpose of this work is to introduce and discuss a general framework for performing a linear instability analysis on multiplex networks, in the absence of inter-layer diffusion, with the specific motivation of detecting the Turing instability. The formalism itself is presented in full generality for $m$-unknowns, each of which arise as solutions of non-autonomous reaction-diffusion equations, on $n$-node temporal multiplex networks. In addition, we identify a class of multiplex networks for which the Laplacian matrices commute. In this setting analytical progress can be made and the explic

title: On Collusion-Free Teaching in Planar Graphs
abstract: Non-clashing teaching minimizes teaching complexity among models satisfying the Goldman--Mathias collusion-avoidance criterion. While the Vapnik--Chervonenkis dimension (VCdim) measures the complexity of learning from samples, non-clashing teaching dimension (NCTD) measures the number of examples required when a teacher can select them. Whether NCTD is always bounded above by VCdim remains a fundamental open question in learning theory. In this paper, we investigate this question for the concept classes of closed neighborhoods in planar graphs. We prove a tight upper bound of two on their NCTD

title: Behavior-Conditioned Animal Vocalization Generation: Event-Aware Modeling and Multidimensional Evaluation
abstract: Behavior-conditioned animal vocalization generation aims to synthesize vocalizations from natural-language descriptions of animal behaviors, social interactions, and contexts. This task remains largely unexplored, with limited behavioral text supervision and substantial variation in vocalization duration. We construct the Behavior-Vocalization Dataset (BeVo) by integrating public bioacoustic data from six species with natural-language behavioral conditions derived from species-specific ethological and bioacoustic literature, totaling 31,191 events. We then adapt a rectified-flow-based generato

title: TeV Gamma-Ray Emission in the DA 495 Region from HAWC Observations of J1952+2924, J1954+2837, and J1958+2848
abstract: Previous observations of the DA 495 region, which contains the pulsar wind nebula (PWN) DA 495 and other very-high-energy (VHE; $>100~\textrm{GeV}$) gamma-ray emitters, showed inconsistent results across different VHE experiments, including differences in the measured flux of DA 495 and in the number of reported sources. Our new dedicated analysis using 3071 days of HAWC data resolves these discrepancies. We identify three extended sources, HAWC J1952+2924 (DA 495), HAWC J1954+2837, and HAWC J1958+2848, all with curved spectra, and find a hint of a fourth source. For DA 495, a multi-wavelength

title: Deep Prior Learning for Embodied Perception
abstract: Embodied systems need geometric perception that exploits available observations beyond images alone. Recent feed-forward 3D models incorporate geometric priors, including camera poses, intrinsics, and depth. However, handling noisy poses, preserving accurate priors, and recovering physical scale require more than simply accepting these inputs. We introduce \emph{Vision-Prior Geometry Grounded Transformer} (VPGGT), a VGGT-based framework that extends OmniVGGT for prior-aware embodied perception. We formulate sensor-motivated pose corruptions from ground-truth trajectories for training and intro

title: CXDVirt: Low Latency Kernel Module Based CXL-SSD Emulation
abstract: CXL-SSDs promise memory-semantic access to NAND-scale capacity through a small in-device DRAM cache, but scarce hardware makes emulation central to CXL-SSD research. Cylon, a state-of-the-art emulator, runs workloads in a VM, intercepting DRAM misses to inject NAND latency. We show this VM machinery adds over 3$μs$ per miss, exceeding high-performance NAND read latency, while repeated VM exits inflate tail miss latencies several-fold. We present CXDVirt, a kernel-module-based CXL-SSD emulator that removes the VM entirely: the device is exposed through host devdax, hits run natively via the MMU

title: BACAM: Behavior-Aware Continual Agent Merging for Multi-Turn Interaction
abstract: Model merging offers a way to integrate the capabilities of specialized experts, but existing agent merging methods typically require all of them to be available at once. We study continual agent merging, which integrates incoming experts sequentially without retaining previously merged experts. Yet merging in parameter space or feature subspaces does not ensure that the merged model acquires an incoming expert's behavior on interaction trajectories. Moreover, updates toward a new expert can disrupt the merged model's previously integrated interactive behavior. Therefore, we propose Behavior-A
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Harness Compilation: Which Decisions Should a Small Vision-Language Model Keep?
abstract: Small vision-language models may be able to read external evidence yet struggle to obtain it. We introduce Harness Compilation (HC), an offline procedure that adapts the division of work between a frozen small VLM and its external harness. A large teacher uses student execution traces to revise reusable content and control, while a separate validation set selects the deployed harness. Deployment requires neither weight updates nor teacher calls. Across seven visual question-answering settings with students of at most 9B parameters, HC improves scores over bare students by 9.9-23.9 points, aver
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: FissionGuard: Testing Local Watermark Proportions with FDR Control
abstract: A watermark detector can flag a text even when only a small fraction of its tokens are watermarked. We study sequential auditing to identify local passages whose watermark proportions exceed a prespecified threshold. Each alarm fixes a candidate passage's endpoint, while its start is chosen from earlier tokens. Reusing the same evidence to locate and test a passage can invalidate inference. We propose FissionGuard, which uses data fission to construct an alarm value and a validation value from each token-level $p$-value. The alarm values guide alarms and localization. The validation values yie

title: Beyond the Doppler Dilemma: Improved Fast Weather Radar Unambiguous Doppler Velocity Spectrum Reconstruction from Sparse Aperiodic Sweeps
abstract: The problem of fast Doppler counter-aliasing for short-dwell weather-radar measurements is addressed. The proposed approach realizes a log-periodic slow-time design by changing only the waiting time between otherwise unchanged frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) chirps. The fast-time waveform, bandwidth, and range-processing chain are preserved while the acquisition changes the Doppler ambiguity structure. We formulate a novel moment-space ambiguity function for distributed weather spectra. It measures statistical ambiguity jointly in mean Doppler velocity and spectral width and express

title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
abstract: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
abstract: Let $V_i(n)$ denote the minimum worst-case number of comparisons needed to find the $i$-th smallest of $n$ distinct elements. We construct algorithms showing $V_7(16)\le28$ and $V_8(16)\le29$, improving the previously reported upper bounds of 30 and 31. Together with known lower bounds, these results establish $V_7(16)=28$ and leave $V_8(16)\in\{28,29\}$. For 17 elements, we establish $V_5(17)=27$ and improve the upper bounds for ranks 6 through 9 to 29, 30, 31, and 31, respectively. Every new upper bound has an explicit decision-graph certificate verified by a static checker developed indepen

title: Doc2Feat-Bench: Evaluating Documentation-Driven Feature Addition
abstract: Documentation changes in mature software projects often describe newly introduced or modified behavior. This makes them a natural basis for documentation-driven feature addition, where software engineering agents implement features from public-facing documentation updates. However, existing benchmarks for agentic software development primarily rely on issue reports written for maintainer coordination and often contain implementation-level details. Motivated by this observation, this work introduces Doc2Feat-bench, a benchmark for documentation-driven feature addition. Doc2Feat-bench consists o
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Reliable Risk Estimation with Kernel Mean Matching under Dependent Sampling
abstract: Kernel Mean Matching (KMM) estimates risk under covariate shift by reweighting labelled source samples so that their kernel mean embedding matches that of unlabeled target samples. Existing finite-sample guarantees are usually stated for independent samples, although many applications involve temporal, spatial, or clustered dependence. We give a finite-sample KMM analysis under dependent sampling by replacing nominal sample sizes with effective sample sizes in the concentration steps used by the classical proof. The approach uses Bernstein inequalities for geometrically strongly mixing process

title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation
abstract: Video diffusion models increasingly serve as priors for 4D generation, but the generated videos often lack geometric consistency. Recent approaches address this through post-training by designing geometric rewards, yet this can degrade texture and fine detail, requiring auxiliary appearance rewards and careful reward balancing. To address this challenge, we propose GeoFix, a unified framework that improves geometric consistency and visual quality with a single geometric reward, applicable to both training and inference-time reward alignment. Our reward measures cross-view depth consistency in

title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
abstract: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. We score validity, alignment, and design across three settings that vary in scale and part availability. We provide BrickAgent, an environment for coding agents to construct, inspect, and validate their designs. We find that leading agents largely satisf
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
Institut national de recherche en sciences et technologies du numérique

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Evil Vectors Is Directionally Asymmetric
abstract: Persona vectors are linear directions in the residual-stream activations of LLMs that encode behavioral traits and enable fine-grained control over model behavior. Among them, the evil persona vector is particularly relevant to understanding harmful behavior, jailbreak vulnerabilities, and the unlearning of harmful knowledge. Yet whether this vector reflects a genuinely cross-lingual concept, rather than an artifact of its extraction language, remains untested. We conduct a systematic evil-vector transfer study across two high-resource languages (English, Spanish) and two low-resource language
institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: Fisher Information and Differentiability for $r$-Largest Generalized Extreme-Value Models
abstract: The $r$ largest observations of a block form a dependent random vector whose support moves with all three parameters of the $r$-largest generalized extreme-value ($r$GEV) model. For a fixed number $r$ of order statistics, we show that the model is differentiable in quadratic mean if and only if $k_0<1/2$, where $k=-γ$ is the shape parameter; the threshold is thus the same as for block maxima, because only the largest or the smallest retained order statistic can reach the moving boundary. In this range the Fisher information is positive definite and decomposes into the block-maximum information

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
abstract: We introduce Timer-M1, a pretrained multivariate time series foundation model that learns with primitives for zero-shot forecasting. Across domains, time series share elementary temporal and relational patterns, termed primitives, yet differ in how these primitives manifest and evolve across different contexts. Despite progress in zero-shot and task-general forecasting, existing foundation models may still struggle to generalize to complex real-world scenarios. To this end, we develop a primitive-based data synthesis and pretraining pipeline. The synthesis pipeline generates series with tempor

title: Technology-Supported Moderation in Online Deliberation
abstract: Mini-publics are an increasingly popular family of democratic innovation to broaden citizen engagement. However, convening a representative sample in person is resource-intensive, and requires significant organizational efforts to coordinate travel, venue logistics, and facilitator training. This chapter outlines the design and development of the Stanford Online Deliberation Platform, initially tailored for Deliberative Polling, building upon insights from in-person moderation in that setting, but supporting a broader range of methods and approaches in the deliberative space. The platform supp
institutions: Center for the Study of Democracy

title: Language Unalignability: Why Some Concepts Resist Cross-Cultural Benchmark Evaluation
abstract: Current evaluation of multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) rests on an implicit Translation-Isomorphism Assumption (TIA): that semantic structures across languages are congruent and mutually mappable without loss of information. We argue that this assumption is not merely violated in practice, but ill-posed in principle for a typologically identifiable class of concepts, including pragmatic markers, honorifics, and diachronically stratified terms. We formalize this failure using a usage-cloud framework, representing concepts as point sets of contextualized embeddings. We define $α$-unalig

title: AccentCL: Robust Accent Classification with Incremental Expansion
abstract: Accent classifiers are typically trained with a fixed label inventory and cannot accommodate new accent categories as new data becomes available. Moreover, accented speech corpora often exhibit substantial class imbalance and/or domain shift due to differences in recording conditions across corpora. We present AccentCL, a class-incremental learning framework for English accent classification that is robust to class imbalance and cross-corpus domain shift. AccentCL extracts multi-layer representations from a frozen Whisper-Large-v3 encoder, optimized with an imbalance-aware cross-entropy loss t

title: Improved Lower Bounds and Output Augmentation for Facility Location Mechanisms
SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking
abstract: Typed decision models answer a declared question without generating text: a decision head returns a probability for each of the declared options in a single forward pass. A single pass is fast, intuitive System 1 thinking. We study what lies between one pass and generated reasoning: looping, in which the same layers are recursively applied several times before one typed readout. Each loop lets the model revise its hidden state before it commits to an answer, without generating a token; we call this System 1.5 thinking. We propose SanSi, which turns a pre-trained looped language model into a ty

title: Local Citation Recommendation Without Graph Signals
abstract: Resolving correct citations can be a time-consuming task for research writers. We address local citation recommendation (LCR), where the goal is to retrieve appropriate references for a given sentence. Web tools generally depend on the existing citation graph, which may bias results toward citation count or more recent publications. LCR research using full paper texts has been limited by the lack of publicly available data. We present a new dataset, the Local Citation Recommendation Corpus (LCRC), containing 14,735 scientific statements derived from astrophysics review papers, each with one or

title: Dimensional uplifts of thermal two-point functions and higher-derivative CFTs
abstract: We explore the idea that the mass parameter $m$ can be used as a diagnostic tool for identifying the critical points of thermal two-point functions of massive free scalar fields in odd $d$ dimensions. For general values of $m$ these correlators admit an expansion in thermal conformal blocks associated with symmetric traceless operators of definite scaling dimension. For each spin the higher-twist contributions can be resummed into a closed-form dressing factor of the leading-twist coefficient. title: Improving Diversity in LLM Short Story Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate accurate responses, but these are void of diversity. We attempt to address this for the task of creative short story generation. Drawing on established writing conventions and known LLM limitations, we target variation in genre, tone, style, and named entities. To promote diversity across these dimensions, we introduce DivLM, an LLM post-training framework consisting of two phases. First, we perform continued pre-training on a creative writing corpus and restore instruction-following capabilities using weight residuals. We then apply reinforcement lear

title: Tight bounds and output sensitive algorithms for maximal clique enumeration in link streams
abstract: A link stream is a set of interactions between pairs of vertices, each one lasting during some time interval, and a clique of a link stream is a set of vertices together with a time interval during which all of them interact. A clique is maximal if neither its vertex set nor its interval can be enlarged. All known algorithms listing the maximal cliques of a link stream may spend time exponential in the size of a clique for each clique they output. title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
abstract: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. Despite substantial research on continual learning, existing work remains largely confined to non-embodied settings, without extending to embodied environments. To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench, the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. With compositional generalization as the core evaluation principle, our benchmark evaluates whether agents can first learn from basic tasks and then recombine the acquired skil
institutions: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence

title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from multi-turn interactions with verifiable outcomes. Textual skills can improve exploration by distilling prior interactions into reusable guidance. However, existing skill-based RL approaches often either assume skill injection is beneficial or rely on indirect feedback or rollout-intensive evaluation to assess its utility. Our pilot studies show that rollout-based utility estimation for skill credit assignment is costly and unstable under limited sampling, while skill benefits vary across candidates and depen
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: IMPPAT 3.0: An updated FAIR database of phytochemicals and formulations of Indian Medicinal plants
abstract: Ayurvedic formulations represent a rich source of traditional knowledge, encompassing distinct therapeutic approaches, medicinal ingredients, and underlying principles of drug action. However, systematic integration of this knowledge with standardized modern biomedical terminology and resources remains limited. Here, we present IMPPAT 3.0, an updated version of the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry And Therapeutics (IMPPAT: https://cb.imsc.res.in/imppat/) database that extends its scope by incorporating curated and harmonized information on Ayurvedic formulations from authoritative sourc

title: PersonaFactor: Preference Factors with Dynamic Selection for LLM Personalization
abstract: Although users may express different personalization needs across tasks, these task-specific behaviors can reflect shared underlying preference mechanisms. Existing LLM personalization methods often focus on surface-level interactions or undifferentiated histories, overlooking the shared mechanisms underlying these behaviors. We introduce PersonaFactors, a framework that distills reusable and interpretable personalization factors from heterogeneous user interactions. We construct a library of thirteen PersonaFactors by extracting evidence-grounded rationales and clustering recurring patterns a

title: STcubeOperator: A Framework for Analyzing Spatiotemporal Event Data
abstract: The analysis of spatiotemporal event data is essential for informed decision-making in domains such as disaster response, conflict analysis, or intelligence investigations. However, the complexity and interdependence of spatial, temporal, and multiple thematic attributes pose significant challenges for both analysis and visualization. While space-time cubes (STCs) present a powerful integrated visualization technique to analyze this kind of data, existing approaches often lack support for complex exploratory workflows, thus limiting the ability to derive meaningful insights. We address this ga

title: Transforming Image Editors into Video Editors
abstract: Recent image editing systems have achieved impressive semantic understanding, visual fidelity, and instruction-following ability, while video editing remains substantially more difficult and costly. In this paper, we present a simple alternative to end-to-end video editing: instead of training a monolithic video editor, we transform a strong image editor into a video editor through anchor-based generation. Our key insight is that video editing can be decomposed into two subproblems: editing a sparse set of keyframes and propagating those edits across time. Based on this observation, we propose

title: What powers the most energetic flares in the Kepler field? Revisiting the superflaring star KIC 2852961
abstract: Flare activity in red giants is quite common when continuously monitored with high-precision space photometry. In fact, the most powerful flares, also known as "superflares" have been observed on red giant stars. KIC 2852961 is a red giant star producing the highest-energy flares in the Kepler field, and is also known for its large-amplitude starspot-induced light variations. Our goal is to find out what causes the extreme flare activity and flare energies in this star. For our investigations, we use ground-based spectroscopic measurements and space photometric data, which we process using sta
institutions: HUN-REN Research Centre for Astronomy and Earth Sciences

title: Recovering Software Architecture Intent from Historical Work Items using Generative AI: A Mixed-Methods Industry Case Study
abstract: Software architecture is often only partially captured in code, while much of the design intent lives in evolving project artifacts. In agile projects, work items, user stories, and related tracking documents preserve valuable traces of that intent, but they rarely support direct architectural analysis. This work investigates the recovery of C4 architecture diagrams from historical agile work items using an LLM-based pipeline. The semi-automatic five-step workflow employs a prompt chain, bidirectional traceability, and Chain-of-Thought reasoning to transform unstructured Azure DevOps work item

title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
abstract: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. institutions: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences
Laboratoire de Physique Subatomique et de Cosmologie

title: Altruism as Infrastructure: Volunteer Moderation in a Bangladeshi Higher Education Facebook Group
abstract: Aspiring international students across Asian countries increasingly depend on commercial education agents to navigate scholarships, documentation, and visas. Alongside this commercial infrastructure, volunteer-run Facebook groups have emerged. Unpaid admins and moderators, often under their real identities, vet information, screen scams, and guide members through scholarships, visas, and departure logistics. We study one such Bangladeshi group, \textit{HigherStudyAbroad: Global Hub of Bangladeshis}, founded in 2010. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 17 volunteer admins and moderators,

title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly advancing scientific and engineering problem solving, with physics simulation emerging as a challenging yet practical testbed for reproducing complex physical phenomena with application in embodied AI, games and films. As the workhorse of such simulation, a solver computes how the state of a dynamic system evolves over time. title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
abstract: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Fast Analytical Method for Resource Adequacy Assessment in Renewable-Rich Power Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel analytical method for resource adequacy assessment in renewable rich power systems. The approach begins by applying the stress strength method to estimate two key resource adequacy indices: loss of load expectation (LOLE) and expected energy not supplied (EENS). This method requires defining the probability distribution functions (PDFs) for both the generation side and the load side. title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. title: Goldsmith: Gold-Loss-Guided Definition Optimization with an Agentic Annotation Harness
abstract: Many annotation projects begin before experts have a stable guideline or enough labels to train a task-specific model. We present Goldsmith, an agentic pipeline that turns a small gold set---expert-annotated calibration examples representing the intended task boundaries---into a reusable structured annotation definition. Goldsmith treats this definition as a trainable textual object. title: Landau Theory for Non-relativistic Magnetism Beyond Altermagnetism
abstract: In this work we study phenomenological Landau theories of non-relativistic magnetic systems, generalizing work on the collinear case to coplanar and non-coplanar orders. Focusing on zero-wavevector ($\boldsymbol{k}=0$) magnetic orders described by a single irreducible representation of the crystallographic point group, we construct the symmetry-allowed free energies to quartic order for all possible multi-dimensional irreducible ordering channels. Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

title: Beyond Anonymous Captions: Grounding Character Identity in Video Captioning and Question Answering
abstract: Linking people's appearance and actions to character identities is essential for understanding video narratives. We present a framework for identity-aware video captioning and person-centric question answering that combines automatic character identification, explicit spatial grounding, and task-specific adaptation. Starting from LSMDC v2 movie clips, our pipeline matches detected faces to actor reference images, tracks characters across frames, and builds inputs with identity-linked bounding boxes. title: Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation
abstract: Google Earth AI is a family of geospatial AI models, together with an agent that orchestrates them. We present this agent, Google Earth AI's Geospatial Reasoning agent (GRA), a Gemini-powered research system that combines geospatial data sources, foundation models, and tools to answer questions about our planet. GRA organizes these into modular domain skills and pairs them with upfront geospatial planning to decompose complex queries into multi-stage workflows. title: Hallucination Across the Reasoning Lifecycle: Interface Visibility, Causal Evidence, and Release Control in Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Reasoning errors can propagate into later decisions and memory. This survey synthesizes 312 papers and first-party reports on text-based reasoning hallucinations around three questions: what evidence is observable, what study designs establish, and which corrective actions the evidence supports. UIPCA records unsupported premises (U), invalid inferences (I), dependent reuse (P), visible answer-trace consistency (C), and action-policy failures (A). title: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for automating complex digital workflows across diverse applications. However, training highly capable and generalizable agents fundamentally relies on massive, high-fidelity visual-action trajectories, which are notoriously difficult to acquire. While human demonstrations are unscalable, existing GUI world models rely on text descriptions or HTML rendering, discarding crucial pixel-level visual details like icons and layout styles. To address this issue, we introduce Infinite-Dreamer, a simulation-free data synthesis m
institutions: Jilin Agricultural Science and Technology University

title: The Geographic Moran Effect: Theory, Methods, and Interpretation
abstract: The Moran effect traditionally refers to the synchronization of population dynamics driven by shared environmental forcing rather than direct interactions among populations. Although extensively studied in ecology, the Moran effect has received limited attention in geography, and its applicability has yet to be fully explored. In this study, we build upon the classical Moran effect in population ecology as a conceptual foundation, developing a more comprehensive conceptual framework in a geographic context. institutions: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

title: Making COMET Comparable Across Scripts: Diagnosis and Correction of Tokeniser-Induced Script Bias in Indic MT Evaluation
abstract: COMET reports translation quality as a single number, and that number is routinely compared across target languages written in different scripts. Such a comparison assumes Script Invariance: the score should not depend on the writing system that carries the target. We test it on IndicMT Eval by re-encoding the target into Latin script, which changes orthographic form while holding content and human ratings fixed. title: IsoVRBench: Video Reward Modeling Without Human Feedback
abstract: Video reward models are trained and evaluated on human preferences between videos that often differ simultaneously on properties such as prompt alignment, visual fidelity, motion, and generator identity. As a result, aggregate accuracy does not reveal which video properties a reward model can reliably distinguish. We construct preference pairs by controlled interventions that change one property of a generated video while holding the rest fixed. The resulting pairs, by construction, provide preferences for how the videos differ along a specific dimension, without requiring any human annotation

title: Thinking Outside the Bots: Human Ideas in AI's Semantic Blind Spots Are Not Inferior
abstract: AI-generated outputs are frequently perceived as highly creative, but also tend to be more similar to each other (homogenized) than human ideas. Does the human heterogeneity that extends beyond AI reflect valuable thinking that AI misses? Alternatively, is greater human heterogeneity driven by lower-quality ideas and less effective thinking that AI avoids? We developed Expansion of Divergent Generative Expression (EDGE) to map AI's semantic "blind spots" by assessing how strongly/weakly individual human ideas were represented in a task-matched AI semantic comparison set. title: Sharper bounds on the thresholds for sensitive and Blackwell optimality
abstract: In perfect-information two-player stochastic games, the notions of Blackwell and sensitive optimality provide generalizations of the classical mean-payoff optimality and discount optimality criteria to account for more farsighted preferences. We provide bounds on the Blackwell threshold $α_{\sf bw}$ and the $d$-sensitive thresholds $α_{\sf d}$, defined as the smallest discount factors above which discount optimal policies coincide with Blackwell optimal policies and $d$-sensitive optimal policies respectively. title: EPOCH: Reliable Discovery through Evidence-Governed Search
abstract: AI research agents are increasingly used to search over programs, mathematical constructions, and proofs. However, existing systems typically optimize evaluator feedback without adequately governing how that feedback is interpreted, challenged, and reused. As a result, promising but fragile candidates can be promoted as discoveries, while benchmark improvements, finite certificates, and theorem-level claims are too easily conflated. title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: Hallucinated information can propagate through multi-stage LLM systems and become part of the context for subsequent reasoning. Existing studies of post-hallucination reasoning (PHR) mainly characterize changes in final outcomes and aggregate reasoning dynamics, leaving how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce PHRBench, a controlled benchmark for behaviorally structured PHR across four domains and 18 large language models. title: Nuclear structure functions and EMC effect in a relativistic deuteron
abstract: We investigate the longitudinal momentum distributions (LMDs) of the deuteron using a relativistic deuteron wave function derived from a realistic nucleon-nucleon (NN) interaction within the light-front framework. By convoluting the deuteron LMDs with the nucleon parton distribution functions (PDFs), we analyze the unpolarized, longitudinally polarized, and tensor-polarized structure functions of the deuteron. title: The Multilingual Artificial Hivemind: Do All LLMs Think Alike in Every Language?
abstract: Text generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) often remains limited in diversity compared to that produced by humans. Recent advances demonstrate the presence of inter- and intra-model collapse in open-ended generation of English text, raising concerns about the long-term homogenization of LLM, and more importantly, human thought. However, our understanding of whether this homogenization extends to languages beyond English is limited. In this work, we investigate the role of language on output diversity. title: Poor Privacy Practices Of The Apple App Store: Cookies, Advertising and Tracking Of Users
abstract: We analyse the data that the Apple App Store sends to and receives from Apple servers. We find that multiple cookies are sent by Apple servers and stored on the handset. Adverts with tracking identifiers are also stored on the handset, and we observe that adverts are selected by Apple servers using GDPR special category personal data such as sexuality, religious beliefs and health. User interactions with the Apple App Store (apps and adverts viewed, buttons clicked, searches made etc) are transmitted to Apple servers alongside identifiers linking this data to the individual user and device. title: Tracking High-Impact Researchers Through Highly Cited Tails
abstract: It is well recognised that field weighted citations are approximately lognormally distributed. This skewness reflects competition for attention, whereby most publications are gradually forgotten and only a minority continue to be recalled years later. Exploiting this observation, we construct a researcher-level indicator based on authorship of top 10% cited papers in All Science Journal Code (ASJC) bins and apply it to publications affiliated with Irish institutions over a typical funding cycle. title: CorleoneGame: A library of biological dynamic games with a companion Julia solver
abstract: Biological agents, from regulatory modules and microbial strains to organisms and populations, act on a common environment while each responds to its own costs, benefits, and limits. A dynamic game makes such interactions explicit by assigning who controls which decision, what each participant values, and which restrictions constrain unilateral deviations. We present a library of 25 biological dynamic games with 2 to 10 players spanning molecular, cellular, organismal, and population scales and competitive, antagonistic, mutualistic, and regulatory interactions. title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as agents with little human oversight, so potential mistakes they make can go unnoticed. Users then depend on the model to report what went wrong. An honest model discloses its mistakes, while a deceptive one conceals them. However, it is unclear how current LLMs behave in such situations. In this study, we prefill LLM trajectories with synthetic mistakes. title: SurvICL: a Foundation Model for in-context Survival Analysis
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) now outperform gradient-boosted trees in classification and regression. Yet in survival analysis, which predicts when an event occurs from censored data, often on small clinical cohorts, we find that no existing TFM beats the half-century-old Cox model. We address this issue by introducing SurvICL, a TFM that predicts survival curves in-context. SurvICL is pretrained on purely synthetic datasets generated from a novel flexible proportional-odds prior that outperforms other prior types in our ablation study. title: OceanFlow: Coherent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Ocean Modeling
abstract: Probabilistic ocean modeling is essential for risk-aware marine operations, climate analysis, and scientific decision-making, where downstream decisions depend on the conditional distribution of future ocean states rather than a single deterministic trajectory. Recent data-driven ocean models have made deterministic global ocean modeling increasingly accurate and efficient, but probabilistic ocean modeling remains underdeveloped. title: Prediction-Informed Landing Window Planning for UAV Landing on USV in High Sea States
abstract: Autonomous landing of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) on unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is difficult in high sea states. Existing hierarchical landing methods often infer future USV motion only implicitly from short observation histories, which limits their ability to adapt to severe and rapidly changing sea conditions. This paper presents a prediction-informed hierarchical control framework. A pretrained model is developed to explicitly predict the USV attitude during high-level landing decisions. title: NAViLoss: An Underwater Navigation-Aware Dual-Residual Objective for Physics-Consistent Learning
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) commonly rely on inertial navigation systems (INS) aided by Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) for reliable underwater navigation. Accurate DVL velocity estimation is therefore essential for successful operation. Recent learning-based methods have demonstrated improved DVL velocity estimation, particularly under degraded measurement conditions. title: Subseasonal forecast improvements from sea ice concentration data assimilation in the Antarctic
abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates the impact of sea ice concentration (SIC) data assimilation (DA) on subseasonal forecasts of Antarctic sea ice by comparing reforecast experiment suites initialized from two sets of initial conditions (ICs): one with SIC DA and the other without. The two ICs are evaluated against NSIDC SIC observations. Results show that the SIC DA significantly improves the climatology and interannual variability of the SIC IC. title: Can Cybernetic Twins Function as Regulators for Sustainable (Sea)Food Systems?
abstract: Feeding the growing global population without permanently overshooting local-to-planetary boundaries demands a transition from conventional resource extraction to holistic models. Current digital twin applications in (sea)food systems primarily emphasize predictive monitoring and decision support, whereas their integration with heterogeneous socio-economic-ecological systems (SEES) remains incomplete. title: Leveraging Digital Twins for Bridge Maintenance Prioritization following Coastal Flood Events
abstract: Abstract Bridges are critical to the US transportation network and are essential components of our infrastructure systems. Coastal floods can disrupt these structures, isolating communities and highlighting the urgent need for effective maintenance and prioritization strategies. This study introduces a digital twin framework that evaluates the impacts of coastal floods on bridge substructures by integrating multisource data and employing spatial algorithms like inverse distance weighting and k - d tree methods to model flood severity. title: A Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring and Fault Identification of Marine Internal Combustion Engines
abstract: Monitoring the current technical condition of a marine internal combustion engine and diagnosing the causes of deviations of its operating parameters from reference values are important tasks for ensuring the efficient and safe operation of marine power plants and vessels in general. This study develops a digital twin framework for marine engine diagnostics and demonstrates its integration with the DEPAS 5.0W diagnostic system. title: Uncertainty-aware digital twin-driven fault-tolerant control for autonomous underwater vehicles using temporal fusion transformer-based fault diagnosis
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operate in challenging marine environments. The actuator faults, propulsion degradation and environmental disturbances can significantly compromise mission safety and tracking performance. Existing studies have primarily focused on either fault diagnosis or fault-tolerant control as separate tasks. A limited attention has been given to integrating fault diagnosis, predictive digital twins and uncertainty-aware control within a unified framework. title: Hydrodynamic Modeling of Maximum Tidal Levels at the Tondano River Estuary
abstract: The Tondano River Estuary is an area affected by the interaction of tides, currents, winds, and bathymetric conditions that affect sea level and hydrodynamic conditions of the coastal area. This study aims to analyze the maximum tidal height at the Tondano River Estuary using the MIKE 21 Flow Model (FM). title: A localized weighted ensemble adjustment Kalman filter for high-dimensional nonlinear data assimilation
abstract: Abstract Particle filters provide a nonlinear Bayesian framework for data assimilation, but global weights often degenerate in high-dimensional geophysical systems. Ensemble Kalman filters are stable with practical ensemble sizes, yet their Gaussian and locally linear updates can be restrictive for nonlinear observations and non-Gaussian forecasts. title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. title: Quantum authentication framework for digital twin–driven satellite networks
abstract: Abstract The integration of digital twin technology into large-scale Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations introduces critical security challenges, particularly under emerging quantum threats. This paper proposes a quantum-assisted multi-layer authentication framework for satellite–digital twin communication that combines entanglement-based verification with hardware-rooted identity using Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions (QPUFs). title: Comparison of Direct and Telescopic Grid Nesting in a High-Resolution Operational Ocean Model
abstract: High-resolution regional ocean models are typically nested within coarser parent models, with resolution ratios limited to avoid spurious artefacts. Consequently, a telescopic grid-nesting strategy is commonly adopted for very high-resolution applications by introducing one or more models of intermediate resolution. However, such an approach is complex and computationally expensive. abstract: Abstract Reconstructing past climates is challenging because pre‐instrumental observations are geographically sparse and proxy records are noisy; data assimilation offers one approach to address these limitations. Although such reconstructions are now widespread, the extent to which different proxy archives determine their accuracy remains unclear. abstract: Abstract. Accurately representing abyssal water masses and their inter-basin pathways remains a challenge for global ocean models and reanalyses. In this study, we investigate how horizontal and vertical resolution influence the simulation of abyssal waters by first evaluating three ocean reanalyses and one forward ocean model, focusing on Antarctic Bottom Water pathways from the Weddell Sea to the Argentine and Brazil basins and through the Vema Channel. abstract: Abstract Antarctic sea ice has declined since 2015, but placing this trend in a longer‐term context remains challenging. Ice core methanesulfonic acid (MSA) offers a potential record of sea ice variability beyond the instrumental period, yet its applicability in sectors including the Weddell Sea remains unclear. abstract: Abstract. The Ross Sea, Antarctica, is among the most seasonally productive areas globally, where different classes of phytoplankton, such as diatoms and haptophytes (Phaeocystis antarctica), play key roles in marine ecosystems and the carbon cycle. abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH 4 ) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract Previous studies have documented long-term changes in Antarctic sea ice extent and its interannual variability. Using satellite-derived SIC observations for 1979–2024 and a wavelet-based measure of interannual variance, we investigate changes in wintertime (July–September) SIC variability across the Southern Ocean. abstract: Abstract The extent to which coastal sea levels co‐vary with open‐ocean variability is explored through evaluation of a balanced dynamics framework relating sea level with pressure, density, and velocity along the continental shelf and slope seafloor. abstract: Warming of the upper ocean is expected to strengthen stratification and reduce the efficiency of wind-driven mixing, affecting water-column stability, nutrient supply, biological productivity, and oxygen ventilation. abstract: Abstract Vehicle-borne improvised devices (VBIDs) represent a severe threat in terrorist attacks due to their combined impact and explosive effects. abstract: Introduction . abstract: A dynamic simulation model was developed and calibrated to predict nutrient concentrations in a three-level cascade hydroponic system (CasH). abstract: Coral reefs are one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems in the ocean, but are now under increasing threat from climate related ocean warming. While numerous studies have focused on the impact of sea surface temperature (SST) on coral reef condition, those that specifically looked into whether long-term background SST variability had an impact on reef stability have had conflicting results, with some analyses showing negligible association and others showing significant associations. abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves are increasing in frequency and intensity globally against a background of long-term climate warming, yet their impacts on subsurface biogeochemistry in temperate shelf seas remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract The zenith total delay (ZTD) retrieved from 5G communication base stations represents a novel observation source for numerical weather prediction (NWP), leveraging the extensive global deployment of 5G infrastructure. abstract: Abstract We present a robust, global method to reconcile absolute water surface elevations (WSE) from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission with a large‐scale hydrodynamic model by iteratively correcting river bathymetry. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric boundary layer height (ABLH) plays an important role in air–sea interactions and regional climate over the western North Pacific (WNP). Using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1979 to 2025, this paper investigates the interannual variability, monthly variations, and seasonal spatial patterns of ABLH. abstract: Abstract Coastal decadal sea level anomalies (SLAs) in the U.S. east coast (USEC) play a critical role in modulating coastal flooding frequency, yet relative influences of tropical versus extratropical climate modes over the North Atlantic remain unresolved. abstract: Global climate change and intensifying marine heatwaves contribute to abrupt fishery collapses. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract. The Gulf of Maine and the surrounding Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf are experiencing rapid marine environmental change arising from complex regional dynamics that challenge near-term (1–10 years) predictive capabilities for valuable living marine resources. Here, using a high-resolution regional ocean model, we demonstrate skilful decadal forecasts of ocean bottom habitat characteristics including bottom temperature, dissolved oxygen (O2), pH and aragonite saturation state (Ωar). abstract: Recent observations in the eastern Arabian Sea reveal the persistent presence of surface-floating tarballs along India's west coast from May to December. abstract: Abstract Radionuclide pollution in coastal areas is of particular concern due to the persistence of radionuclides in the marine environment, their accumulation in sediments, and the potential consequences for human populations and ecosystem health. title: Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
abstract: Ocean surface winds and currents are coupled through air–sea interaction but are commonly retrieved independently from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). For operational single-geometry SAR, simultaneous wind–current retrieval is underdetermined and remains reliant on background information. abstract: Coastal caves developed in weak and heterogeneous cliffs constitute complex geomechanical systems in which lithological variability, structural discontinuities, groundwater seepage and marine erosion interact. Their stability assessment is particularly challenging in urbanised coastal and touristic attractive environments, where local failures may affect infrastructure and public safety. abstract: Abstract The mechanical behavior of natural gas hydrate-bearing sediments (HBS) is critical for safe and efficient gas production. abstract: Abstract Quantifying microbial cell abundance in natural environments with taxonomic resolution remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. While epifluorescence microscopy reliably enumerates free-living cells, it lacks taxonomic specificity and is less suitable for quantifying cells in sediments, soils, and on surfaces. abstract: Estimating eruption source parameters is critical for volcanic hazard assessments and understanding eruptive dynamics. abstract: Abstract. Marine heatwaves and coral bleaching pose significant threats to the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), particularly during austral summer when atmospheric conditions can significantly enhance ocean surface warming. One such condition is the development of doldrums, characterised by weak winds and reduced cloud cover, which promote increased solar heating of the ocean surface. abstract: The dynamics of sediment and biogenic materials are key to understanding fluxes within shallow coastal ecosystems. abstract: With the continuous increase in the operating speed of high-speed trains, aerodynamic performance plays an increasingly critical role in energy consumption, operational stability, and passenger comfort. abstract: Abstract Three decades of satellite altimeter observations reveal a continued rise in global mean sea level (GMSL), with the rate of rise reflecting the combined effects of decadal variability and long‐term warming. abstract: Abstract. Seasonal depletion of dissolved oxygen (DO) in stratified shelf seas has important consequences for benthic and pelagic ecosystems and biogeochemical cycling. There is a need to understand the importance of different processes contributing to the bottom water oxygen budget, and how those processes might change in a warmer ocean. abstract: This study presents an observation-based approach for identifying, characterizing, and classifying non-typhoon extreme waves in the Northeast Asian Marginal Seas using in-situ wave and wind measurements, with reanalysis data used to interpret the associated synoptic conditions. abstract: Wildfires in eastern Siberia have intensified significantly in recent decades. abstract: The performance of a full-scale top-hinged flap-type wave energy converter in the open sea is analyzed numerically in this study. abstract: Submarine sewage outfalls are widely used to mitigate the impacts of wastewater discharges on coastal recreational waters. title: Storm-modulated submesoscale dynamics over sloping topography in a wind-driven, non-tidal basin
abstract: Abstract. While ocean surface submesoscales have been extensively studied, their counterparts in the bottom boundary layer (BBL) remain little explored. These subsurface features, however, appear to play a key role in (i) boundary-interior exchange, (ii) forward energy cascade, and (iii) turbulent boundary mixing, which is an important driver of the overturning circulation. title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution and Circulation Links of Summer Precipitation in Central Asia: Roles of Pacific and Atlantic Sea-Surface Temperature Modes
abstract: Central Asia, as a typical arid and semi-arid region, experiences precipitation variability that critically influences water security and ecological balance. Based on ERA5-Land reanalysis data and 14 large-scale climate indices from 1980 to 2025, this study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of summer precipitation and its physical attribution by employing the Mann–Kendall trend test, Pettitt change-point detection, variance inflation factor (VIF), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), partial correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and composite analysis. title: Human-centred design approaches to tsunami mitigation under sea level rise in Kesennuma, Japan
abstract: Abstract. Human-centred design (HCD) is increasingly prioritised as studies show human experience is critical in infrastructure use, and recent policies call for more socially responsive design. Tsunami impacts intensify as sea level rise (SLR) raises baseline water levels and reduces existing defence effectiveness, yet HCD informed approaches are rarely tested under projected SLR. abstract: Long-horizon building-performance models commonly treat operational energy use and physical deterioration as independent processes, despite the potential for envelope degradation to increase thermal demand and for sustained HVAC operation to alter thermal–moisture exposure. This study develops an energy-data-anchored probabilistic digital-twin framework that integrates three coupled lifecycle states: structural/support-condition loss, envelope thermal and leakage loss, and thermal-load memory. title: Global scale river discharge and mean depth from radar altimetry and model
abstract: Rivers are vital for water security, yet scalable freshwater monitoring and global knowledge of river mean depth and discharge remains limited by sparse in situ data, satellite observations of river surface only and global river flow estimations relying on models with insufficient hydraulic information. Without a robust global product for river bathymetry derived from satellite altimetry, large-scale hydrodynamic assessments remain limited. title: Synthesis of the tethered balloon system and other TRACER campaign measurements elucidates aerosol property profiles
abstract: Abstract. Coastal urban environments exhibit strong vertical and horizontal heterogeneity in aerosol properties, complicating process-level understanding of aerosol–cloud interactions. This study analyzes tethered balloon system (TBS) measurements from 149 flights during summer over the greater Houston, Texas, region as part of the DOE Atmospheric Radiation Measurement (ARM) Tracking Aerosol Convection interactions ExpeRiment (TRACER) campaign. We characterize the vertical structure of aerosol number concentrations, size distributions, and inferred cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentration

title: Stratification dynamics in the southeastern Caspian Sea: Seasonal cycles, spatial patterns, and links to sea surface temperature
abstract: This study provides a quantitative characterization of the seasonal stratification cycle in the southeastern Caspian Sea using a multiyear hydrographic dataset (2011–2019) collected across seven cross-shore transects, spanning all four seasons including winter. MLD progresses from shallow spring mixing (mean ≈ 10 m) to deep winter convection (mean ≈ 57 m), with season explaining 76% of MLD variance (ANOVA, p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.76). title: Recent change in northward migration of the East Asian summer front and increased compound wet–hot conditions
abstract: The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. Using a front-tracking algorithm applied to ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2025), we identify northward migration of the EASF during both the active frontal season and late summer, with a more robust 1.92° shift in late summer. These shifts are associated with enhanced moisture transport, regional weakening of the upper-level jet, and localized sea surface temperature warming that has intensified and spatially broadened in recent decades. title: Changes in southeastern Pacific Ocean cloud fractions: cloud radiative effects and cloud controlling factors
abstract: Abstract Clouds play a critical role in Earth’s radiative balance through their radiative effects. Recent studies suggest that the current planetary energy imbalance is associated with a reduction in global albedo, largely resulting from decreases in cloud fraction. However, the southeastern Pacific Ocean, where maritime stratocumulus clouds dominate off the west coast of South America, shows increasing albedo associated with enhanced low cloud cover. title: Structure-Acoustic Coupling Analysis of Underwater Acoustic Radiation Characteristics of a Multiple Intersecting Spherical Shell Under Acoustic Excitation
abstract: The underwater acoustic radiation of deepwater submersibles has become a growing concern in both academic and industrial communities. This study investigates the structure-acoustic coupling characteristics of a novel deepwater pressure hull, idealized as a triple spherical shell. A numerical model is established using a combined finite element and boundary element method to analyze the vibro-acoustic response of the target structure. title: ENSO's Imprint on the Southern Ocean: Wind Waves Drive Surface Cross‐Frontal Flow
abstract: Abstract Tropical teleconnection associated with El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is widely recognized for regulating multiple physical processes in the Southern Ocean. However, despite its influence on Southern Ocean wind patterns, the response of surface flow has received little attention. Here, we investigate surface flow in the Southern Ocean using surface‐drifting buoy trajectories collected during September 2022–May 2023 and November 2023–June 2024. title: Cross-regional evaluation of thermodynamically consistent fractional-order integration for observation-constrained ocean heat content estimation
abstract: Abstract Ocean heat content (OHC) is sensitive to errors in the vertical representation of temperature, particularly in regions characterized by strong thermohaline gradients. This study evaluates an empirical fractional-order integral procedure in six scenarios encompassing the tropical Atlantic, Indian, equatorial Pacific, and South Atlantic oceans. title: Dynamic constitutive modeling and numerical implementation of geogrid-coral sand interface interaction under cyclic direct shear loading
abstract: Geogrid reinforcement can effectively improve the engineering properties of coral sand and has considerable potential for application in island and reef engineering. The reasonable modelling of interface is important for the holistic simulation of geogrid-reinforced coral sand geotechnical engineering subjected to waves, earthquakes, and other dynamic loads. Nevertheless, user-friendly interface model for the geogrid-coral sand interface remains scarce, and their implementation in numerical programs has not yet been reported. title: Metocean-stats v1.2: An open-source framework for reproducible and actionable metocean data analysis
abstract: Metocean analyses are fundamental to offshore and coastal engineering, maritime operations, and renewable energy development, where reliable estimates of winds, waves, currents, sea level, and related variables are required for structural design, safety assessment, and operational planning. Although large metocean datasets are increasingly available, analyses are often performed using ad hoc scripts and fragmented workflows, limiting reproducibility, transparency, and efficient knowledge transfer. title: A CFD-based initial framework for screening fixed floating-breakwater configurations for marine aquaculture
abstract: Floating breakwaters are increasingly considered for offshore applications, including marine aquaculture. However, existing studies have primarily focused on wave attenuation, while the potential of different configurations to provide favorable aquaculture environments remains insufficiently explored. This article aims to: (i) compare the hydrodynamic performance of various fixed floating breakwaters, including box-type, plate-attached, π-type, and hybrid systems, with a consistent width ( B f ) and configuration-dependent draft ( D f ); and (ii) propose an initial framework for their aquacult

title: Climatology and mechanisms of low-level jets over southeastern coast of mainland China during the early-summer rainy season
abstract: Abstract Low-level jets (LLJs) significantly impact early-summer rainy season over the southeastern coast of mainland China (SECC), yet northerly LLJs over this region remain understudied compared to their southerly counterparts. Utilizing decade-long hourly ERA5 reanalysis, this study establishes a comprehensive climatology and dynamical framework for distinct LLJ types over the SECC. Climatologically, northerly boundary layer jets (NBLJs) peak in April with a shallow core (~ 975 hPa) concentrated over the central Taiwan Strait. title: Wolf predation as a regulator of the state of island populations of wild reindeer in the early 21st century
abstract: The relationship between the wolf and the wild reindeer in the Arctic has always been a focal point for researchers and northern Indigenous communities. This predator species continues to exert significant influence on wild reindeer and caribou inhabiting remote island territories, and adjacent mainland coastal areas in the 21st century. However, warming in the Arctic is leading to profound changes in the established principles governing the formation and functioning of both reindeer and wolf populations. title: Boundary‐Aware Separation of Vortical and Wavy Motions in the Ocean
abstract: Abstract With the recent popularity of the tide‐resolving and submesoscale‐admitting numerical simulations, there is an increasing interest in separating vortical and wavy motions in the ocean. The recently‐proposed dynamics‐based decomposition exploits the relative magnitude of the relative vorticity and horizontal divergence in Fourier space and proves efficient. In this decomposition, physical variables over non‐water regions (e.g., coasts, islands, seamounts) are filled with zeros following standard practice. title: An operational wind-speed-dependent quadratic bias correction for Voluntary Observing Ship wind measurements evaluated against moored buoys and ERA5 reanalysis
abstract: Abstract Voluntary Observing Ship (VOS) wind reports constitute one of the densest marine in situ datasets, yet they carry a persistent, wind-speed-dependent negative bias that intensifies at low wind speeds. Using 18,957 collocated ship–buoy–ERA5 records over the nearshore waters of China, we diagnose this bias against two complementary references, a moored-buoy network and ERA5 reanalysis, and construct a correction that is deployable in practice: a three-parameter quadratic in the observed VOS wind speed itself, requiring no reference information at application time. title: Wind impacts on salinity and stratification in the Persian Gulf and on water exchange through the Strait of Hormuz
abstract: Abstract The Persian Gulf (PG) is a pronounced inverse estuary characterized by strong evaporation, hypersaline waters, and a reversed asymmetry in water exchange through the Strait of Hormuz, where the annual inflowing volume transport exceeds the corresponding outflow. This study uses a high-resolution three-dimensional hydrodynamic model to quantify wind effects on salinity redistribution, stratification, and high-frequency water exchanges. title: A Generalized Analytical Model for Marine Gas Hydrate Stability Zones With Thermodynamically Constrained Pressure–Temperature Phase Boundary
abstract: Abstract Accurate thermodynamic delineation of marine gas hydrate stability zones (GHSZs) is a fundamental prerequisite for assessing methane hydrate inventories, quantifying the vulnerability of methane dissociation to climate change, and evaluating overpressure‐induced submarine geohazards. However, the commonly adopted pressure–temperature phase boundaries are predominantly calibrated under idealized conditions and fail to capture natural marine conditions, leading to persistent uncertainties and systematic biases in global GHSZ delineation. title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. title: Wave-induced coupled dynamics of an OTEC spar platform with cold water pipe: An experimental investigation
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) is a promising renewable energy technology capable of providing continuous baseload power while simultaneously supporting freshwater production and other deep-seawater applications. As a carbon-neutral energy source, OTEC aligns with global Sustainable Development Goals related to clean energy and climate action. However, the commercial deployment of large-scale floating OTEC plant requires a thorough understanding of the coupled hydrodynamic behaviour of the floating platform and the cold water pipe (CWP), a critical component unique to OTEC plants. title: The Role of Local Wave Activity in Influencing Extreme Precipitation Patterns Over North and Northeast China
abstract: ABSTRACT Warm‐season extreme precipitation over North and Northeast China is a major regional hazard and is strongly influenced by large‐scale atmospheric circulation. However, how large‐amplitude wave activity varies among different spatial patterns of extreme precipitation remains insufficiently understood. title: Topographic Modulation of Multi-Source Internal Solitary Waves in a Complex Sea Basin: Nonlinear Dynamics and Energetics
abstract: Abstract Complex basin topography plays a fundamental role in modulating the dynamics and energetics of internal solitary waves (ISWs), yet their three-dimensional mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, a high-resolution non-hydrostatic numerical model is employed to investigate basin topographic modulations of the generation, nonlinear evolution, and energetics of multi-source ISWs in the Sulu Sea basin. title: Flooding with brackish water disrupts Liriodendron tulipifera sap flux in an ecosystem-scale experiment
abstract: Coastal forests are retreating due to sea‑level rise and extreme precipitation events, yet the physiological mechanisms that precede woody plant decline remain poorly constrained. We used the ecosystem‑scale TEMPEST (Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments) experiment; annual, plot‑level freshwater and saltwater flooding of a mid‑Atlantic deciduous forest, to quantify short‑ and long‑term responses of sap flux in three tree species: Acer rubrum, Fagus grandifolia, and Liriodendron tulipifera. title: Measuring large-scale mCDR using a novel Atmospheric CO₂ Perimeter Flux (ACPF) method
abstract: Achieving net-zero CO₂ emissions globally requires an annual removal of on the order of 7–9 Gt CO₂; but current CO₂ removal (CDR) measurement methodologies are not designed to quantify marine CDR (mCDR) at the megaton-to-gigaton scales required for climate relevance. This perspective presents a new methodology, the Atmospheric CO₂ Perimeter Flux (ACPF) method, an atmospheric-domain framework for the monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of marine carbon dioxide removal. title: Indian Ocean Convection Modulates the Early‐Winter Pacific‐North American Response to El Niño
abstract: Abstract The El Niño‐Southern Oscillation is a dominant driver of Pacific‐North American (PNA) variability on seasonal‐to‐interannual timescales through its influence on tropical Pacific convection. However, the early‐winter PNA response exhibits pronounced event‐to‐event diversity during El Niño. Here we show that this diversity is closely linked to variations in tropical convection across the Indo‐Pacific. title: Tsugaru Gyre development in summer 2025
abstract: Abstract The Tsugaru Warm Current (TWC) flows eastward through the Tsugaru Strait from the Japan Sea to the North Pacific, influencing the water-mass distribution, marine ecosystems, and fisheries in the confluence region east of Japan. In this study, we conducted shipboard observations during the transition phase of the TWC from its coastal mode to its gyre mode in early July 2025. Subsurface information obtained from these in-situ observations at key locations is highly valuable for validating model simulation products, together with satellite observations. title: Meteorological Impact Assessment Software for Maritime Transport in the Western Part of the Black Sea
abstract: Maritime transportation in the western part of the Black Sea is strongly affected by meteorological conditions such as wind, waves, and visibility. This paper presents a software system designed to evaluate and predict these impacts using real-time and historical data. The system integrates data processing, statistical analysis, and predictive models to assess navigational risks and support route optimization. title: Climate‐change‐amplified wind‐related economic losses during Cyclone Harry (2026)
abstract: Abstract Cyclone Harry affected Sicily, Calabria, and Sardinia between January 19 and 22, 2026, producing heavy rainfall, strong winds, and coastal impacts across the central Mediterranean. We assess how the associated meteorological conditions differ between the present climate (1988–2025) and a cooler past (1950–1987) using the multivariate ClimaMeter analog attribution protocol applied to the European Centre for Medium‐Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Reanalysis Version 5 (ERA5). title: Impacts of Sea Surface Temperature Warming Pattern Biases on Tropical Cyclone Activity and Hazard
abstract: Abstract Most climate models simulate greater warming in the equatorial eastern Pacific than in the west under historical forcing, resulting in a reduced zonal sea surface temperature (SST) gradient and a weakened Walker circulation. This contrasts with observed trends and highlights a persistent model–observation discrepancy with far‐reaching impacts on regional climate extremes. The authors' previous work showed that reducing mean‐state biases in a coupled model yields SST trends more consistent with observations. title: Tide-gauge-based diagnosis of sea-level-rise-sensitive threshold exceedance and adaptation-relevant elevation bands along Southwestern Taiwan
abstract: ABSTRACT Infographic of five tide gauges in southwestern Taiwan, 2004-2025: sea level peaks in August at every station, the seasonal range differs by station, and sea-level rise of 0.5 to 1.0 m adds up to 239 to 345 exceedance days per year. Sea-level rise is expected to increase coastal water-level exceedance, particularly in low-lying and subsidence-prone regions. This study develops a tide-gauge-based diagnostic framework to examine sea-level-rise-sensitive threshold exceedance and adaptation-relevant elevation bands along the southwestern coast of Taiwan. title: Forecasting coastal dune mobility: a logistic regression model driven by meteorological data and climate indices
abstract: Abstract. Predicting dune mobility under changing climatic conditions remains a challenge in aeolian geomorphology, particularly in data-scarce regions. This study presents a novel application of binomial logistic regression to forecast dune activation and migration using readily available meteorological data. We combine established dune mobility indices (Tsoar and Lancaster) into a new integrated index (TsoLa) and evaluate its performance against observed dune migration rates derived from satellite imagery. institutions: Instituto de Investigación en Paleobiología y Geología

title: Geomorphic Approach for Beach Downdrift of Fishing Ports and Marinas: Parabolic Model and Software MeePaSoL
abstract: Coastal erosion problems associated with a fishing port or marina on sandy coast are caused by imbalance of longshore sediment transport and bay shape formation on downdrift. Regardless of the availability of littoral transport, the tip of its outer breakwater would behave as an updrift control point for an embayed beach to form, by combined wave diffraction-refraction aided by nearshore current circulation.
