title: Sea Cucumber‐Inspired Double‐Network Biopolymer Hydrogels for Programmable Soft Machines
abstract: Engineering biopolymer-based hydrogels with robust load-bearing capacity, reversible mechanical programmability, and adaptive actuation remains difficult due to weak physical crosslinking and porous structure. Inspired by the mutable dermis of sea cucumbers, a collagen-alginate double-network elastomeric (CoDE) hydrogel integrates a covalently crosslinked collagen cryogel scaffold with an ionically crosslinked alginate sacrificial network. title: Hybrid Multi‐Gateway Authentication Protocol for 6LoWPAN‐Based Marine Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a secure and efficient three‐factor authentication scheme to address the security issues in the integration scenario of multi‐gateway wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and 6LoWPAN in marine Internet of Things (IoT). Existing approaches exhibit vulnerabilities to cryptographic breaches, single‐point failures, high computational costs, and inefficient long‐distance transmission in maritime settings. title: Characteristics and Ambient Conditions of Mesoscale Convective Systems Moving Offshore in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin, East China
abstract: Abstract This work for the first time studies the characteristics and environment conditions of mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) that move offshore (i.e., land to sea, LS) in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin (YHRB), East China. In the warm season (April–September), LS MCSs account for 25.5% of the total MCSs, exhibiting a decreasing trend from spring (April–May) to later summer (August–September). LS MCSs most frequently occur from late morning to early evening. title: Modeling the dynamic responses of a 2 × 2 gravity-type fish cage group under combined wave-current conditions
abstract: The hydrodynamic response of gravity-type cage groups under harsh open-ocean sea states is closely linked to long-term production safety. However, severe wave-current forcing may produce response transitions and internal load-path changes that remain insufficiently resolved for interconnected cage groups. This study develops a numerical model of a 2 × 2 cage group using the lumped-mass method and examines how wave height (H), wave period (T), and angle of attack (α) govern its motion responses, volume loss rate, and mooring tensions. title: Equivalent force-based Kalman-type filter and reduced system function for full-field response reconstruction
abstract: Abstract In structural health monitoring, full-field response sensing and monitoring are essential to establish a digital twin model. However, directly measuring all required structural loads and responses is costly and impractical. Simultaneous estimations of structural loads and responses are consequently developed, which is, however, an ill-posed problem. title: Rockfall hazard assessment at Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, Italy): implications for cultural heritage sites in a seismically active volcanic area
abstract: Coastal cliffs developed in volcanic tuffs are highly susceptible to instability due to the combined effects of structural discontinuities, marine erosion, and seismic activity. This study presents a multi-method assessment of rockfall hazard at the Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, southern Italy), an area affected by ongoing bradyseism and with a significant cultural heritage exposure. UAV-based photogrammetry, field structural surveys, and geomechanical characterisation were integrated to reconstruct the geometry and discontinuity network of the cliff. title: Effects of wind-wave misalignment on motion responses of a floating wind turbine with a shared-anchor mooring system
abstract: Wind-wave misalignment significantly affects the dynamic responses of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). A fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring numerical model was established in OrcaFlex for a FOWT with a three-line shared-anchor mooring system. The numerical analysis evaluated three representative sea states (LC1, LC2, and LC3) alongside multiple wind-wave heading combinations. title: Wave attenuation by mixed mangroves in hybrid Mangrove–Breakwater systems using a modified Ergun equation
abstract: Coastal hybrid protection schemes integrating mangrove vegetation with vertical impermeable breakwaters can effectively mitigate coastal inundation and seabed erosion triggered by storm surges. Nevertheless, most existing numerical models overlook the vertical stratification of mixed mangrove communities, which leads to systematic underestimation of flow resistance within vegetated coastal zones. title: Regional Trends in Northern Hemisphere Summer Extratropical Cyclone Activity and Their Link to Precipitation and Temperature Trends
abstract: Abstract In recent years a robust weakening of the storm tracks has been identified in reanalysis data. This trend has been linked to coinciding changes in surface temperature extremes and precipitation over land. Here we use a surface‐based metric to quantify regional trends in the boreal summertime low‐level extratropical cyclone activity (ECA) and link this to surface impacts. title: TREND AND ANOMALY OF TEMPERATURE SERIES IN WEST AFRICAN COASTAL URBAN AREAS: THE CASE OF ABIDJAN, CÔTE D'IVOIRE (1985-2024)
abstract: Climate change is accompanied by a growing intensification of temperatures at the local scale, as observed in several cities of the sub-region, yet their evolution and trends remain insufficiently quantified. This study aims to examine the trends and anomalies of temperatures in the city of Abidjan over the period 1985-2024. Daily maximum (TX), minimum (TN), and mean (TM) temperature data, provided by SODEXAM, were analyzed using the Mann-Kendall trend test combined with Sen's slope, as well as an anomaly index calculated relative to the 1985-2024 climatological normal. title: Revisiting how the euphotic depth is computed
abstract: The method of computing the euphotic depth, the depth horizon in the ocean above which light is sufficient for net primary production, has lacked consensus in the literature. Although many still use a % light level as a definition, a practice which dominates textbooks in oceanography, the modeling community uses a constant basal respiration to set the threshold. title: Nonlinear dynamics of time-variable slope circulation
abstract: Abstract. Bottom topography strongly constrains ocean circulation in the Arctic, and both theory and numerical modeling suggest that nonlinear flow–topography interactions influence slope-following currents. Yet, how such interactions modify the circulation response to time-variable surface forcing remains poorly understood. Using idealized shallow-water simulations of flow over a corrugated slope in a re-entrant channel, we investigate how nonlinear features arise and evolve under oscillatory forcing. title: Characteristics of the Southern Hemisphere jet streams based on ERA5 data for 2001–2025
abstract: A climatology of the Southern Hemisphere jet streams calculated for the first quarter of the 21st century using ERA5 reanalysis data is presented. An occurrence frequency of jet streams in various regions is investigated, and the seasonal and interannual variabilities of maximum wind characteristics (speed, level height, direction, and layer thickness) are analyzed. Climatological data on jet streams at flight levels intended for air navigation planning are provided.

title: Long-term spatio-temporal assessment of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI)
abstract: Climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme heat events have intensified thermal stress, particularly in Mediterranean regions, posing significant challenges to human health, quality of life, and sustainable urban development. Therefore, accurate assessment of outdoor thermal comfort has become increasingly important for supporting climate adaptation and planning strategies. This study aims to investigate the long-term (2000–2025) spatio-temporal changes of thermal comfort in Antalya (Türkiye) using the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). title: Thermal–Fluid–Solid Coupling Analysis of Enhanced Heat Transfer and Thermal Stress in Shark Skin Micro-Rib Tubes
abstract: A multi-field coupled numerical model integrating fluid flow, convective heat transfer, and thermal stress is established for a shark-skin-inspired V-shaped micro-rib heat exchange tube. title: Examining Correlation Structures of Planetary Boundary Layer Height using Large Global Ensembles
abstract: Abstract A proper localization length scale is critical for the success of ensemble-based data assimilation techniques to reduce spurious, long-distance correlations that stem from limited ensemble size. This study utilizes 960-member ensemble forecasts from the Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) to examine the structures of the correlations for the planetary boundary layer (PBL) height (PBLH). title: Offshore Freshened Groundwater Distribution Is Controlled by Along‐ and Cross‐Shore Topographic Variability
abstract: Abstract Offshore Freshened Groundwater (OFG) reservoirs are regarded as a potentially significant resource stored in continental shelves. While the role of subsurface geological conditions in controlling OFG has been widely recognized, the influence of the topography of the hosting continental shelf on OFG evolution remains poorly understood. abstract: Precipitation extremes have increased globally in recent decades, consistent with a warming climate. We find that 2024 experienced a record-high frequency of heavy (≥99th percentile; F P≥99 ) precipitation events globally based on MSWEP (Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation) observations from 1979 to 2025. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Underwater soft strata commonly occur beneath river and lake dike foundations. abstract: The Indonesian Maritime Continent (IMC) is a pivotal component of the global climate system, serving as the world’s primary tropical heat source and a region of intense convective activity. Despite its climatic importance, its complex geography and dependence on the Asian-Australian monsoon make it highly vulnerable to drought, which is further intensified by teleconnections such as El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). Hybrid coupling strategies combine mesh-based far-field solvers with near-field SPH to offer a solution; however, a core challenge has been maintaining consistent free-surface tracking along 3D interfaces under multi-directional waves. title: Predicting winter cold surge scenarios using ensemble forecasting and clustering techniques
abstract: East Asian cold surges develop through several distinct spatiotemporal evolution patterns, each characterized by a different intensity and duration. Beyond forecasting whether a cold surge will occur, anticipating which type will develop would allow the likely evolution scenario to be foreseen in advance, providing valuable lead time for disaster preparedness. title: A Bayesian MCMC approach for snow density estimation from SMOS over the Northern Hemisphere
abstract: Snow density is a key parameter for calculating snow water equivalent, snow albedo, snow emissivity, and snow mechanical properties. It is therefore essential in water resource management, snow-air energy exchange computation, cold regions engineering design, and avalanche prevention. In a warming climate, snow density is undergoing rapid changes, which pose challenges for static snow density evolution equations in predicting spatiotemporal variability. abstract: The safety of mooring systems is critical for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs), yet contact-based tension monitoring suffers from difficult installation, susceptibility to damage and limited long-term reliability. This study proposes a non-contact monitoring method based on the Vector Form Intrinsic Finite Element (VFIFE), which determines mooring tension from the measured motion of the floating platform. abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. title: Methodology for a human-centric CIM: Translating non-geocoded citizen perceptions into spatial indicators
abstract: To address the growing complexity between the built environment and urban life, modern urban planning has increasingly relied on digital technologies for decision-making, including City Information Modeling (CIM). While CIM has matured from standards and data integration to real-time analytics and digital twins, most initiatives optimize physical systems while struggling to incorporate “intangible” citizen-generated data. title: Secular polar motion from non-surface-loading processes estimated using satellite gravimetry
abstract: SUMMARY Polar motion (PM) provides an independent, observation-based constraint on global mass redistribution, but interpretation of its long-term variability is primarily limited by uncertainty in the glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) contribution, for which conventional model-based estimates exhibit substantial differences. title: A Generation Mechanism of Thorpe‐Detected Turbulence: A Case Study Using WRF Model Simulation
abstract: Abstract Turbulence in the free atmosphere has been widely estimated using the Thorpe method, which identifies vertical inversions in potential temperature profiles as evidence of overturning. However, the mechanisms driving Thorpe‐detected turbulence remain poorly understood, due largely to limitations in spatial and temporal resolution of observational and reanalysis datasets. abstract: Abstract Planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence modulates tropical cyclone (TC) intensity through competing mechanisms: (a) frictional dissipation that weakens TCs and (b) frictional convergence that drives stronger low‐level inflow and intensifies TCs. Three landfalling TCs (Beryl, Francine, and Milton) were simulated to examine how enhanced PBL turbulence affects TC intensity during landfall. abstract: Land-surface change and atmospheric variability jointly shape dust activity in arid regions. abstract: Abstract Typical climate model resolutions preclude the explicit simulation of most of the spectrum of atmospheric gravity waves (GWs). Climate models must therefore rely on GW parameterizations, which observations help constrain. abstract: Abstract Extreme hourly precipitation (EHP) across the Tibetan Plateau (TP) often triggers flash floods and landslides due to the region's complex and steep terrain, yet its inter-station covariations and formation mechanisms remain inadequately understood. Using climate network analysis of hourly station data and dynamic diagnostics, this study examines EHP synchronicity across the southeastern and northeastern TP and elucidates the underlying mechanisms from a perspective of sea surface temperature (SST)-forced circulation evolution. title: Sources of skillful seasonal forecasts of springtime CONUS tornado activity
abstract: Despite progress in continental United States (CONUS) tornado forecasting, operational seasonal outlooks remain challenging due to intrinsic predictability limits. While previous studies link the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) to spring tornado frequency, relying on single tropical indices misses crucial regional variability. Here, we present a novel hybrid dynamical-statistical framework that introduces a paradigm for long-lead predictability. abstract: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hydrological, environmental, and soil conditions at regional scales in highly urbanized landscapes. abstract: This study investigates the ultimate strength and nonlinear structural response of metallic I-core sandwich pressure hulls as an alternative to conventional ring-stiffened submarine pressure-hull structures. A key comparative investigation is conducted between two I-core configurations that differ fundamentally in the orientation of their core webs, which are aligned either longitudinally or transversely relative to the longitudinal axis of the pressure hull. abstract: Abstract Equatorially trapped Kelvin waves can occur through the depth of the troposphere and beyond. Previous works have demonstrated that these waves respond profoundly to the background flows through which they propagate, leading to variation in phase speed and dispersion characteristics. title: Spatiotemporal Covariability of Extreme Precipitation and Integrated Vapour Transport Over the Tibetan Plateau During 1979–2015
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme precipitation and atmospheric moisture transport are closely linked components of the Tibetan Plateau (TP) hydroclimate, but statistical covariability should be distinguished from causal control. We analyse extreme‐precipitation and integrated vapour transport (IVT) indices over 1979–2015 using APHRODITE precipitation and ERA5 reanalysis. title: Wind conditions shape co-migration fidelity in trans-Saharan birds at a Mediterranean stopover site
abstract: Weather is a key driver of bird migration, particularly near ecological barriers, where migratory species often converge before crossing. While its effects on individual timing are well documented, how weather reshapes the temporal assemblage of migratory bird communities remains unexplored. abstract: Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non-breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark-bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. title: Extreme wave height estimation using a hybrid distribution approach
abstract: Accurate estimation of design wave heights is paramount for the safety and resilience of coastal infrastructure. However, extreme value analysis with limited samples faces two critical challenges: spurious identification of bounded EV-III distributions due to statistical fluctuations, and severe underestimation risks stemming from uncertain finite upper limits. title: Intensification of East Asian summer extreme precipitation under a net-zero anthropogenic CO 2 emission scenario
abstract: Global warming has intensified extreme precipitation, a trend projected to continue as warming persists. However, how extreme precipitation characteristics respond to global warming mitigation strategies remains poorly understood. This study examines East Asian summer extreme precipitation responses under a net-zero anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emission scenario. abstract: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) increasingly rely on optical sensors for navigation, reconnaissance, and environmental monitoring; however, high-speed operation near the air-water interface generates free-surface waves and cavitation that create strongly non-uniform density and refractive-index fields, causing image distortion beyond the scope of conventional ray-tracing models. abstract: Abstract Turbulence represents a primary hazard for aviation, with Clear-Air Turbulence (CAT) posing a unique threat due to its visually undetectable nature. This study evaluates the 75-year temporal evolution of the macro-environmental atmospheric conditions favorable to CAT over Europe and North Africa from 1950 to 2025. title: Tracing the Journey of Microplastics from Aquatic Ecosystems to Seafood
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become an important environmental issue due to the widespread occurrence, persistence, and biological accessibility of small plastic particles in aquatic ecosystems. Fish and other seafood organisms are of particular concern because they may come into contact with microplastics at different stages of their life cycle. title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract: Abstract. Cloud vertical structure plays a central role in regulating Earth’s radiation balance and hydrological cycle, yet it remains poorly represented in weather and climate models due to limited high-resolution observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band cloud radars, we provide the first high-spatiotemporal-resolution characterization of cloud vertical structure across China for 2024 and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. abstract: The increasing demand for reducing fuel consumption and improving energy efficiency in maritime industry has intensified interest in solar thermal systems for auxiliary energy supply. In this study, a numerical model of a solar collector tube is developed in COMSOL Multiphysics. title: Bio-inspired trailing edge optimization for a double-suction pump impeller: a hybrid NSGA-II and CFD approach
abstract: Energy consumption reduction in pump systems has attracted increasing attention. Improving the efficiency of double-suction pumps can contribute to reducing energy consumption due to their extensive applications. This paper aims to optimize the double-suction pump by introducing the bionic structure inspired by the pectoral fin structure of humpback whales. abstract: Abstract We examined the evolution of shallow convective structures in the atmospheric boundary layer in response to changes in the basic state. abstract: Abstract. Warm-sector heavy rainfall (WSHR) features small spatial scales, posing critical forecast challenges, while its fractional contribution to regional heavy rainfall and its short-term precursors remain poorly quantified. abstract: Tubular joints are fundamental components in the design of offshore platforms, naval vessels, and marine superstructures, offering high strength-to-weight ratios and favourable hydrodynamic behaviour. abstract: : Rivers serve as the principal pathway for transporting microplastics from land to the ocean, thereby playing an indispensable role in their global transport. title: Interannual and seasonal evolution of supraglacial drainage systems on Nivlisen Ice Shelf, East Antarctica
abstract: Abstract. Supraglacial channel networks (SCNs) represent critical components of the surface drainage system on Antarctic ice shelves, facilitating the redistribution of meltwater, including into and out of supraglacial lakes, potentially influencing ice-shelf stability. title: Assessing power system vulnerability to climate-related stressors and shocks: The case of Indonesia
abstract: Climate change and extreme weather are increasing the vulnerability of power systems globally, particularly in emerging economies such as Indonesia. Yet, existing studies often assess these impacts in isolation, focusing on individual components or specific hazards, leaving system-level effects—at provincial and national scales—under-examined. abstract: Metro stations, characterized by enclosed spatial configurations, are highly vulnerable to extreme flooding, posing severe threats to human life and property. Understanding the hydrodynamic processes of flood intrusion and their implications for evacuation routes is therefore essential for urban flood risk reduction. abstract: Abstract. High-elevation alpine catchments are particularly affected by the global rise in temperature. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. abstract: Rollover stability is a critical concern for prestressed concrete bridge girders, particularly during handling, transportation, and erection when lateral restraint is limited. abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. abstract: Ocean wave energy has garnered significant attention as a sustainable power source, with the Oscillating Water Column (OWC) device emerging as a highly effective technology for wave-to-electricity conversion. abstract: Abnormal vibration is one of the primary causes of high-pressure fuel pipe failure. abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the feeding behavior of deformed and normal benthic foraminifera (Protista, Rhizaria) of the species Ammonia veneta . abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract A lot of cloud-to-ground lightning strikes sometimes occur around the Nansei Islands in April, while those April lightning bursts (ALBs) have not been investigated. abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. abstract: Seasonal flooding changes fish habitat availability and the transport, retention and recovery of genetic material, complicating environmental DNA assessments in connected river–floodplain systems. abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. abstract: The increasing need for renewable energy has resulted in the swift proliferation of wind power, both onshore and offshore. abstract: Abstract Recent observational studies have demonstrated that supersaturation fluctuations (SS’) in clouds induced by turbulence at scales smaller than 100 m can significantly affect microphysical processes such as aerosol activation and droplet condensation. title: Future Northeastward Shift of Extratropical Transition of Tropical Cyclones Over the North Atlantic in Downscaling Projections
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) often undergo extratropical transition (ET) at the midlatitudes, becoming post‐tropical cyclones (PTCs). abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the capability of the MLUCM BEP + BEM to reproduce intra-urban variability of air temperature and relative humidity in Lecce (Italy) during summer 2025. abstract: Dams in arid, data-scarce basins are designed to attenuate episodic flash floods, yet their performance under extreme operational stress or catastrophic failure is rarely evaluated against long-term observational records. abstract: Artificial Water Sites (AWS) are human-made or modified water sources constructed or maintained for livestock, select wildlife game species, or other management purposes in arid environments. This paper systematically examines the fundamental flaws in traditional design theories regarding the limitations of compression-shear stress paths and the assumption of constant soil parameters. abstract: Abstract Purpose Greater understanding of the contributions from different sediment sources and their linkages to the downstream suspended sediment load (SSL) is essential to advancing knowledge of catchment sediment transport dynamics and informing sediment management. abstract: Assessing long-term rainfall variability is crucial for understanding regional hydroclimatic dynamics and informing water resource management; however, studies integrating rainfall trend detection with homogeneity assessment are scarce in the Warangal district of Telangana, India. This study presents a comprehensive spatio-statistical analysis of long-term rainfall variability in the Warangal district of Telangana, using the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS) dataset. abstract: This study aimed to develop a framework for mitigating cost and schedule overruns through the integration of Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and the Analytic Network Process (ANP). abstract: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. abstract: Abstract. Historical text sources represent a central, yet methodologically challenging basis for the reconstruction of convective weather events. This study examines the extent to which historical reports on thunderstorms and hailstorms contain reliable climatological information, despite heterogeneous sources, varying degrees of detail and linguistic diversity. abstract: Strategic freight procurement is the mechanism by which a shipper converts a forecast of future transportation demand into a portfolio of contracted rates before the demand arrives. abstract: Abstract. Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. abstract: The increasing occurrence of extreme weather events since the beginning of the 21st century has led to the development of new methods to attribute extreme events to anthropogenic climate change. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. abstract: Abstract Intraplate volcanism in Northeast Asia, located in a distant back‐arc setting, challenges conventional models of mantle convection and volatile cycling. abstract: Maintaining spatially adequate thermal and air-quality conditions is challenging in commercial multi-tier layer houses because environmental gradients can develop simultaneously across longitudinal regions and cage levels. This observational field study characterized two commercial houses with distinct environmental-control configurations in southern Brazil using a three-level IoT monitoring network. abstract: Abstract High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. These keels have probably been formed early in Earth’s history, and the preservation of these deep, cold, and highly viscous roots in a convective mantle remains enigmatic. A classical view is that the excess density due to colder temperatures is compensated for by a light composition. abstract: Self-centring concentrically braced frames (SC-CBFs) are intended to limit residual deformation after strong earthquakes, but practical code-oriented procedures for their design remain limited. This study presents a force-based design (FBD) procedure for a horizontally post-tensioned SC-CBF consistent with Eurocode 8 and Eurocode 3. abstract: Abstract Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract. There are numerous subglacial lakes in Antarctica, typically covered by thick ice sheets. abstract: Abstract The impact of long-term snow cover variability on winter tourism in the mountainous areas of Poland is an increasingly important research topic, particularly in light of the anticipated effects of climate change. Available studies are often of regional scope, limited to higher elevations, while lower mountain ranges such as the Western Beskids remain insufficiently studied. abstract: The increasing adoption of portable and wearable audio devices is accelerating the use of piezoelectric actuators as alternatives to conventional dynamic speakers, enabled by their ultra-thin, lightweight factor, low power consumption, and ability to transform non-traditional surfaces into efficient sound-radiating elements. abstract: Abstract Despite extensive research on the Nile River Basin, few studies represent the entire basin as a connected hydrology–infrastructure–demand system. abstract: This paper explores how a case of collaborative governance between public authorities and civil society organisations (CSOs) in Sweden was affected by political changes and reforms (2014-2024) that eventually contributed to the closing down of the project. The case addresses state-civil society relations in Sweden and how political shifts affect collaborative policy implementation. The collaborative project was carried out over a decade at a regional level and addressed migrant integration through involvement in activities run by CSOs. title: CFD investigation of a novel gabion-based porous medium configuration for energy dissipation in ogee spillway stilling basins
abstract: Ogee spillways which provide very large discharge rates are extensively employed for civil engineering applications, but high velocity flows generated by Ogee spillways can be seriously harmful to downstream structures. This numerical investigation is conducted to assess the potential of adding porous media (uniform gabions and cross shaped gabions, with varying porosities: 30%, 40% and 50%) to the stilling basin at the bottom of ogee spillways to dissipate energy. title: Molecular evolution of oxygenated organic molecules in a cloud-influenced forested mountain environment
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) link the oxidation of volatile organic compound to secondary organic aerosol formation, yet their molecular evolution in cloud-influenced forested mountain environments remains poorly constrained. Here, gas-phase OOMs were measured using an iodide-adduct chemical ionization mass spectrometer at a high-altitude forested station in southeastern China during autumn 2023. title: Plasma-Driven Combustion of Aerosolized Energetic Ionic Liquids
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate plasma-driven combustion of energetic aerosolized ionic liquids under flowing conditions. A mixture of hydroxylammonium nitrate (HAN) and 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium ethyl sulfate ([EMIM][EtSO4]) is atomized through high-pressure injection into a nozzle, where HAN serves as the oxidizer, similar to the monopropellant AF-M315E (i.e., ASCENT), and EtSO4 provides the fuel. title: VOLUMETRIC ESTIMATION OF CO2 STORAGE POTENTIAL IN ÁGUA GRANDE FIELD, RECÔNCAVO BASIN
abstract: Earth's climate has been increasingly affected by anthropogenic activities, primarily fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, which release greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2). Geological carbon storage (CCS) stands out as a critical mitigation strategy to curtail these emissions, though effective subsurface containment requires a clear understanding of trapping mechanisms. This study investigates the carbon storage potential of a depleted reservoir using real field data from Brazil. title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. title: Comparative Numerical Analysis of Thermal Performance in Modified Horizontal U-Tube Ground Heat Exchanger
abstract: Geothermal energy stands out as a reliable and sustainable solution for heating and cooling buildings, delivering consistent baseload power unaffected by weather or geopolitical factors. Moreover, its subtle design blends seamlessly with the surroundings. This research evaluates the thermal performance of horizontal ground heat exchangers (GHEs), comparing around 17 configurations. A trench with dimensions of 28 m × 3 m × 5 m was modeled, maintaining uniform trench and pipe lengths of 18.35 m and 37 m, respectively, for all configurations. title: Tracking hydrological drought propagation in river networks: an event-based framework
abstract: Hydrological droughts are dynamic phenomena that evolve across space and time, propagating through river networks under the influence of climatic forcing, catchment properties, and human regulation. Despite substantial progress in drought research, most existing approaches rely on aggregated indicators or statistical relationships, limiting their ability to explicitly characterise how individual drought events propagate within connected river systems. title: Comparative Study of Hydrogen Yield from Organic-Rich Lithologies: Implications for Sustainable Energy
abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has increased interest in hydrogen as an alternative fuel that is both affordable and widely accessible. While substantial research has focused on hydrogen generation through serpentinization, the potential of organic-rich systems remains largely unexplored. Addressing this gap requires systematic analysis of various organic-rich materials such as shale, carbonate rocks, and coal to evaluate their capacity to release hydrogen gas under different geological conditions. title: Distinct Liquefaction Resistance of Fujian Sand Under the Combined Effect of Asymmetric Cyclic Loads and Fabric Anisotropy
abstract: Abstract Fabric anisotropy and load asymmetry can both significantly influence the mechanical behavior of sand. To clarify the coupled influence of fabric anisotropy and load asymmetry on liquefaction characteristics, sand specimens with different bedding angles were loaded by cyclic loadings of different degrees of asymmetry under undrained triaxial conditions. title: Three-parameter Kerr soil model: finite element formulation and applications in transient dynamic analyses
abstract: Soil-structure interaction is a topic of paramount importance in civil engineering, as the method of soil modeling directly influences the static and dynamic performance of structures supported by elastic foundations. Simplified models, such as Winkler's, while widely adopted, fail to adequately represent the effects of distributed stiffness and lateral interaction. In this context, multiparameter models, like those proposed by Pasternak and Kerr, offer a more realistic characterization of soil behavior. title: Signs of power: giant ficron handaxes may have played a non-utilitarian role in structuring social groups in MIS 9 Britain
abstract: Giant ficrons are a rare but recurrent sub-type of Acheulean handaxe, that in Britain are predominantly found in assemblages dating to the MIS 9 interglacial. A variety of theories have aimed to explain the striking size and appearance of giant ficrons as reflecting their use in specialised subsistence tasks or non-utilitarian display functions. title: Transport and fate of radon: a critical review of mechanisms and environmental influences
abstract: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas produced from the decay of uranium-238. It poses significant environmental health risks because it can migrate through soil, groundwater, and air before accumulating indoors. This review, based on a critical synthesis of 94 peer-reviewed publications (2009–2025), explores how radon moves and behaves, emphasising diffusion, advection, and dissolution, and the influence of soil properties, groundwater flow, building characteristics, and human activities. title: Collaborative Policy Modeling for Ecotourism Conservation and Development: A Multi-Case Empirical Study Based on Policy Instrument Taxonomy
abstract: The synergistic imbalance between conservation and development remains a core constraint on the sustainable development of ecotourism. Grounded in externality theory, this study constructs a three-dimensional modeling framework that integrates the quantification of positive externalities from ecological conservation, the pricing of negative externalities from tourism development, and the adaptation of policy instruments. title: Design and mechanical performance analysis of re-entrant auxetic structures fabricated using SLA 3D printing: a comparative study
abstract: Auxetic structures, with a negative Poisson’s ratio, have gained significant attention for aerospace and automotive applications due to their superior mechanical performance. In this study, two different Auxetic Structures were used, namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) and Re-entrant star triangular structure (B). title: Using forest structural complexity and topography metrics to characterise vertical microclimatic stratification
abstract: Understanding how topography and forest structure drive the transformation of incoming solar energy into local microclimatic conditions is essential for predicting forest resilience under climate change. Quantifying the importance of such attributes on the stratification of microclimates requires the integration of heterogeneous ecological data streams. title: Aerodynamic Characteristics and Wind Load Partitioning in Double-deck Girders: Effects of Inter-deck Clearance Height
abstract: The inter-deck clearance height (IDH), defined as the vertical distance between decks, is a key parameter in the aerodynamic design of double-deck bridges. This parameter governs both global aerodynamic characteristics and the allocation of wind loads across different subcomponents (top/bottom decks, windward/leeward trusses) of the girder, yet its effects remain underexplored. title: Numerical Investigations of a Novel Offshore Platform Blast Wall Design Using Energy Absorption Devices at Supports
abstract: Abstract Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. This study proposes a novel offshore blast wall concept incorporating energy-absorbing support devices comprising PMI foam-filled sliding cores and rotational springs. title: Crashworthiness assessment of thin-walled columns with functionally graded stiffness induced by multi-level spherical crush initiators
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the crashworthiness performance of thin-walled columns equipped with functionally graded, multi-level spherical crush initiators. The proposed concept extends previous solutions by introducing a sequence of embossments with varying diameters and depths along the column height, enabling controlled variation in local structural deformation resistance and progressive folding under impact loading. title: CT image-based experimental and numerical simulation methods for freeze–thaw concrete microstructure
abstract: Freeze–thaw cycling is a primary durability challenge for concrete structures in cold regions. This study presents an integrated experimental and numerical approach to visualize and quantify mesoscale freeze–thaw damage evolution in concrete. Indoor rapid freeze–thaw tests were conducted, combined with computed tomography (CT) scanning for three-dimensional (3D) microstructure reconstruction and finite element (FE) simulation for damage analysis. abstract: An experimental and theoretical program was conducted to enhance comprehension with regard to how variations in fibre ratio affect the structural performance of concrete beams. In this research a concrete mix with Three fibre volume fractions of 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5%were tested to evaluate the fibre effect on concrete strength. abstract: This paper argues that green hydrogen could be a driver of the technological transformation of a small open economy well integrated into the global energy market. Green hydrogen development is key to a sustainable transition of the economy. It can replace CO 2 -intensive technologies, e.g., in the transport sector, water cleaning facilities, and the steel industry. abstract: This study considers a thin elastic plate excited by a harmonic point force and coupled to locally resonant mass–spring attachments distributed along two opposing parabolic trajectories. The resulting resonator arrangement redirects part of the incident flexural-wave energy through repeated scattering along the curved interface, thereby reducing transmission beyond the curved array and producing a downstream shielded region. abstract: Abstract Melt extraction is a critical process for the formation of eruptible magmas. Magmatic textures and compositions illuminate magma dynamics during the emplacement of a large (2 m diameter) felsic enclave (LFE) within granitic mush in the Aztec Wash pluton (15.7 Ma, NV-USA). The LFE is an ellipsoidal microgranite mass inferred to have been nearly solid when it settled at the top of a crystal-rich zone of the magma body. title: Preloaded and premoistened foundation that overlaps sabkha collapse treatment with construction evaluated by coupled infiltration and consolidation analysis
abstract: Conventional improvement methods applied to sabkha soil (collapse soil) are time-consuming, lengthening the project schedule. This paper presents a novel preliminary concept for a pre-loaded, pre-moistened shallow foundation engineered construction. A single-footing cast directly on dry sabkha incorporates a 3 × 3 array of vertical holes through which distilled water is introduced, advancing as a Green-Ampt wetting front and dissolving the evaporitic bonds before superstructure load application. title: Theoretical, numerical and experimental study of flexural-wave bandgaps and transverse vibration isolation in sandwich metamaterials with asymmetric resonators
abstract: Abstract Broadband low-frequency vibration attenuation in lightweight sandwich structures remains challenging because conventional multi-resonator designs offer limited freedom for bandgap engineering under stringent spatial constraints. Here we introduce a metasandwich plate with asymmetric circular resonators (MPACR), in which broadband bandgaps are achieved through configurational asymmetry rather than increased structural complexity. title: Numerical evaluation of hydraulic performance of a laboratory-scale Archimedes screw pump
abstract: Archimedes screw pump (ASP) is a type of positive displacement pump for transporting water from lower to upper incline elevations. It is a simple and robust pump widely used for irrigation, flood mitigation, and in wastewater treatment plants. Although ASPs have been used for centuries, there is a lack of literature related to the optimal hydraulic performance and elucidating the underlying flow mechanisms. abstract: This study investigates the evolution of the internal chemical environment in autoclaved high-performance concrete (HPC) and the determination of the critical threshold for steel passivation. Conventional extraction methods are limited by the solubility product of Portland cement, obscuring the true pore solution chemistry. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the dynamic instability of pile foundations subjected to real seismic excitation through numerical analysis. The seismic input is extracted from ground motion records of the 1966 Peru earthquake, specifically the PER01 station record obtained from the official database of the Instituto Geofísico del Perú. title: FLOWS: a model to simulate water and solutes fluxes in agricultural and environmental systems: 2. Modules for specific applications in water and nutrient management
abstract: Abstract This paper is the second of two companion studies. The first paper focused on describing the model FLOWS, theory and the model benchmarking. This paper addresses FLOWS modules on specific applications: irrigation, temperature, organic carbon processes and nutrient transformation and transport in the soil. abstract: Abstract. Termites are major detritivores in tropical and subtropical ecosystems, yet their contributions to the terrestrial carbon cycle remains absent from process-based soil organic carbon (SOC) models. Here, we present a termite carbon module that explicitly represents termite-mediated litter consumption and transfer of ingested carbon into gaseous (CO2, CH4) and SOC pools. title: Rethinking flood protection in the Koshi River (Chatara-Koshi Barrage), Nepal: A hydrodynamic evaluation of structural mitigation pathways
abstract: This study evaluates the hydraulic performance of four structural flood-mitigation alternatives using a two-dimensional HEC-RAS model for a 50 km reach of the Koshi River between Chatara and the Koshi Barrage, Nepal. A 100-year design flood (27,401 m³ s⁻¹), estimated via Generalized Extreme Value flood-frequency analysis, was applied as the upstream boundary condition for existing-condition and alternative scenarios. abstract: Abstract Rare-earth (RE)-microalloyed Q235RE steel and conventional Q235 low-carbon steel were subjected to two carburizing–quenching routes: gas carburizing followed by oil quenching, and low-pressure carburizing followed by high-pressure gas quenching. abstract: Abstract Safe CO 2 storage requires injection designs that manage both when faults yield and how yielding spreads, yet temporal schedules and well layouts are often evaluated separately. title: A Strategy of Additional Carbon Acquisition by Non-Foliar Photosynthesis: Implication for Yield
abstract: Abstract Photosynthesis is traditionally studied in leaves, but it extends beyond foliar tissues to non-foliar organs (e.g. stems, fruits, sepals, and seeds) offering an underexplored avenue for enhancing plant productivity. This review investigates physiological, biochemical, and developmental roles related to non-foliar photosynthesis, emphasizing its contributions to carbon assimilation and crop production under varying environmental conditions by presenting an extensive compilation of published data with relevant studies. abstract: Abstract Many electrocatalytic reactions proceed via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanisms, which can be promoted by protic polymer coatings. However, polymers modulate the local reaction environment in many ways. To deconvolute the effect of local pH in protic polymer coatings from other contributions, we developed a method for operando determination of in-polymer pH values using electrochemical fluorescence microscopy. abstract: Abstract. Fatigue crack growth has been observed as a prominent damage mode in rain erosion of wind-turbine blades, where it is driven by cyclic pulse loading from liquid-droplet impacts. This study investigates fatigue crack growth in a thermoplastic polyurethane elastomer used for leading-edge protection, linking repeated droplet impacts to controlled cyclic loading in a lab test. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract This study targets the ultradeep, high-temperature, and high-pressure carbonate reservoirs in the Penglai Gas Area, Sichuan Basin. The existing acid fracturing technologies have ambiguous stimulation mechanisms and are difficult to regulate accurately. We conducted a series of physical experiments on the alternating injection of gelled acid and drag-reducing acid, aiming to optimize acid fracturing techniques and improve the reservoir stimulation performance. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Generated by differential surface heating within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), thermals are essential for sustaining flight in non-motorized aviation such as paragliding, hang gliding, and gliding. abstract: The rapid development of western China has intensified the human‑land conflict in the gully regions of the Loess Plateau, prompting local governments to reclaim land through loess high‑fill foundations (LHFF) to support urban construction. Due to the unique engineering properties of loess and the large thickness of compacted fill, LHFF undergo significant settlement during both the construction and post‑construction stages, posing challenges to subsequent engineering works. title: Self-Priming Centrifugal Chemical Pumps: A Review
abstract: This paper gives a thorough examination of the literature of self-priming centrifugal chemical pumps, focusing on their design, operational principles, and applications in various industries. They render surpassing advantages, including improved efficiency in handling liquids containing air or gas, and reduced maintenance requirements. abstract: Compound climate extremes pose an increasingly severe threat to our societies, ecosystems, and economies under climate change. title: Self-cleaning biomimetic superhydrophobic PVC plates for fouling mitigation in lamella settlers
abstract: Lamellar sedimentation is widely used in water treatment, but particle accumulation on inclined plates can obstruct channels and impair hydraulic performance. This laboratory-scale proof-of-concept evaluated the effect of surface wettability on sedimentation and residual fouling by comparing smooth PVC and biomimetic superhydrophobic (Sh) plates in a batch lamella settler. Quartz suspensions were tested at plate inclinations of 20°, 40°, and 60°. title: Efficiency of temporary bridge construction with reused superstructure girders
abstract: Rapid recovery of transport links after the destruction of bridges as a result of military operations is one of the main tasks that requires the development of unique and effective solutions for safe and continuous traffic. The purpose of the study was to analyse the engineering efficiency and reliability of reuse of superstructure girders on the example of the existing destroyed bridge crossing over the Teteriv River at km 78+850 of the M-07 Kyiv – Kovel – Yahodyn national highway for the construction of a temporary bridge. title: Process-based evaluation of green roof models for assessment of heat mitigation efficacy in WRF (v4.3.1) and EnergyPlus (v8.6.0)
abstract: Abstract. Green roofs mitigate urban heat, but to fully assess their impact, green roof models must be integrated into urban climate models, where they provide critical surface boundary conditions. Ensuring their reliability requires evaluation, yet such efforts remain limited in the literature. This study addresses that gap by evaluating two configurations of EcoRoof, the green roof module from EnergyPlus (ERo for the original version of the model, and ERm for a modified version), and a multilayer green roof parametrization for WRF (WRF-MLGR) (Heusinger et al., 2018; Sailor, 2008; Zonato et a

title: Energy management optimization algorithm for data center microgrids based on solid-state transformers
abstract: The proliferation of hyperscale data centers, together with tightening carbon-neutrality targets, exposes the limits of the line-frequency transformer (LFT) that still dominates data-center power distribution and motivates a fresh look at the conversion and dispatch layer. This paper develops an energy management framework for a data-center microgrid whose grid interface is a three-stage solid-state transformer (SST), so that renewable, storage, and IT loads sit on independently regulated AC and DC ports rather than behind a passive iron core. title: Landscape Architecture and Health: An Umbrella Review
abstract: Landscape architecture influences environmental conditions related to health, but evidence on how design features impact health is scattered across disciplines. The review aims to assess the evidence, identify pathways to health, and guide collaboration between landscape architects and public health professionals. Following PRISMA and JBI Umbrella Review guidelines, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Academic Search Complete, and GreenFILE. journal: Journal of Healthy Eating and Active Living

title: Multiscale Analysis on Seismic Response of Underground RC Structure with Uniformly Corroded Sidewall: Effect of Strengthening Using Various Methods
abstract: This study numerically investigates the seismic response of corroded underground reinforced concrete (RC) culverts strengthened using various methods. A multiscale model for corrosion and seismic analysis, accounting for strengthening effects, was first validated through quasi-static cyclic analysis of corroded RC columns with and without strengthening. title: Mechanical behavior of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V from cryogenic to elevated temperatures: A comparative study among multiple additive manufacturing processes
abstract: In this study, the microstructures and temperature-dependent mechanical behavior, including tensile and fatigue, of Ti-6Al-4V fabricated by five additive manufacturing (AM) processes were investigated. These include laser powder bed fusion, laser powder directed energy deposition (DED), laser wire DED, electron beam wire DED, and wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM). title: TECHNICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL SUPPORT FOR FEED MATERIAL MIXING
abstract: The article presents the results of a review study of modern approaches to feed material mixing and structural and technological solutions for mixing equipment used in compound feed production. The importance of high-quality mixing of complete feed, premixes, and protein-mineral-vitamin supplements for ensuring stable nutritional value, safety, and efficiency of animal feeding is substantiated. title: The enhanced capabilities of mid-infrared limb emission sounding to observe stratospheric aerosol injection geoengineering
abstract: Abstract. Using a model-based pseudo-reality (PR) future scenario and realistic pseudo-observations (POs) representative for a proposed satellite mission concept (CAIRT – the Changing-Atmosphere Infra-Red Tomography explorer), we analyse the capabilities of a high-spectral-resolution limb-emission sounding techniques to detect and quantitatively monitor very weak stratospheric aerosol injections (SAI) geoengineering interventions, in terms of the injected sulphur dioxide (SO2) and its evolution into sulphate aerosols (SA). title: Influence of irradiance and mixing layer height on the vertical trace matter distribution in the lower planetary boundary layer – drone-based investigation
abstract: Abstract. Drone-based atmospheric measurements allow time-resolved investigation of stratification in the lower atmosphere of many atmospherically relevant variables. Measuring a variety of variables can be used, e.g., for mixing layer (height, MLH) identification and examination of the representativity of ground-based measurements in the lowermost boundary layer. We present drone-based vertical profiling during two 2.5‑week summer field campaigns in rural Germany to investigate the vertical distribution of trace matter and meteorological variables in the lowermost troposphere. title: From lab to application: a review on fabrication techniques, engineering progress, and commercial prospects of MgB 2 superconducting wires
abstract: Abstract Since its discovery in 2001, magnesium diboride (MgB₂) has attracted significant interest for large-scale superconducting applications due to its high transition temperature (39 K), low material cost, and weak crystallographic anisotropy. This review critically assesses progress and remaining challenges in the industrialization of MgB₂ superconducting wires, covering material optimization, fabrication techniques, and emerging applications. title: Overheating Resilience of Shading Systems Across Climates: A Systematic Evidence Synthesis Using a Multiscale KPI Framework
abstract: Climate change is intensifying overheating risks in cities, where the Urban Heat Island effect and increasingly severe recent heatwaves are driving up thermal stress, cooling demand, and outdoor discomfort. Shading is among the most effective passive strategies for reducing solar-radiative exposure, yet research on shading systems remains fragmented across building and urban scales, climatic contexts, and performance indicators, limiting comparability across studies. title: Microscopic theory of drag in a Bose condensate interacting with a moving reservoir
abstract: We derive a microscopic theory of drag for a Bose-Einstein condensate interacting with a moving reservoir. Starting from interactions between a condensate and a drifting fermionic bath, we integrate out the bath degrees of freedom within the Born--Markov approximation to obtain an effective Gross--Pitaevskii equation with a drag potential. From this potential we derive an effective drag force and obtain a closed expression for the drag coefficient, determined by the reservoir density fluctuations and the condensate density profile. title: Contact lens with stretchable distributed-feedback laser for intraocular pressure monitoring
abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. Smart contact lenses are an attractive platform for continuous IOP tracking, and optical strain sensors are particularly promising thanks to their high sensitivity and natural readout. title: Optical properties and shape-dependent retrievals of the imaginary part of the refractive index of freshly emitted Saharan dust
abstract: Abstract. Mineral dust is a major contributor to atmospheric aerosols and plays a complex role in Earth’s radiation budget. However, large uncertainties remain in quantifying its direct radiative effects (DRE), primarily due to poorly constrained absorption properties. Most estimates rely on remote sensing or laboratory studies, with few in situ measurements of freshly emitted dust. This study presents ﬁeld data on dust optical properties collected during active dust emission in the Moroccan Sahara (September 2019). title: Precision measurement of ocean tides using cosmic-ray muons
abstract: Cosmic-ray muons provide a natural probe of the integrated mass along their trajectories. Here we show that cosmic-ray muons can monitor ocean-tide-induced variations in seawater overburden within an underwater tunnel. The observed modulation closely tracks independent tide-gauge measurements, yielding an attenuation response coefficient of $k=43.2\pm1.0$~counts$\rm /h/m$ and resolving meter-scale variations in seawater overburden. Linking Horizontal and Vertical Submesoscale Lagrangian Dynamics South of the Ibiza Channel
abstract: Fronts, eddies, jets, and meanders populate the ocean surface and play a key role in organizing transport and mixing across a wide range of scales. From a Lagrangian perspective, frontal structures are conveniently detected as surface filaments that act as barriers to horizontal transport. However, the degree to which these structures maintain coherence below the surface and the relationship between horizontal and vertical motions in their vicinity remain poorly understood. title: Parametric wave spectrum models for prediction of Stokes drift profiles
abstract: In this report, 15 variants of nine parametric models for non-directional ocean wave spectra are reviewed. They are compared against observation-based spectra created by taking spectra measured by moored buoys, binning by wind speed, and averaging. Surface Stokes drift (SSD) and Stokes drift profiles are computed using the model and observation-based spectra, and these are compared. This 'parametric wave model' strategy for estimating Stokes drift is contrasted with other methods for estimating Stokes drift, such as using spectra from a dynamical wave model. title: From Tunnel Overburden Reconstruction to Tidal Measurements via atmospheric muon
abstract: Muography with scintillator-based detectors enables the investigation of density distributions within large structures. The Hankuk Atmospheric-muon Wide Landscaping (HAWL) project is the first real-time portable muon tomography. It successfully charted the mountainous region of eastern Korea by measuring cosmic-ray muons with a detector operated in a moving vehicle. HAWL achieved a tunnel length accuracy of 6.0 % and an overburden measurement range of 8-400 meter-water-equivalent (m.w.e.). title: Similar evapotranspiration responses mask contrasting modes of water access during drought in California
abstract: Atmospheric warming raises evaporative demand, but actual evapotranspiration (ETa) may track demand or decouple under water limitation. Here, we quantified demand-tracking ability from regression slopes relating deseasonalized ETa and reference evapotranspiration (ETo) anomalies across California during 2008-2024. Forests and croplands retained similar positive tracking under severe drought, whereas grasslands and shrublands showed weak or negative responses. title: Active remodeling rescues a microswimmer from geometric trapping
abstract: Natural habitats confront microorganisms with heterogeneous, mechanically complex surroundings that shape how they move and explore. Most studies of motility in complex media treat the environment as either a homogeneous fluid or a rigid obstacle field. Here we instead study a medium that is simultaneously soft and reconfigurable --- deformable by the organism moving through it. title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. title: The hypervariational method: a general, automated technique based on innovations to tune the parameters of the Hybrid covariance matrix
abstract: The Hybrid forecast covariance model is an operationally successful way to build a background error covariance matrix. It is constructed as a weighted sum, with scalar weights, of the climatological covariance matrix and a localized ensemble covariance matrix, with a localization matrix typically depending on a localization length. For best performance, the Hybrid needs to be optimized by tuning those weights and, possibly, other parameters, such as the localization length. title: Climate Sensitivity Derived from First-Principles Temperature Feedback Circuits
abstract: A long-standing challenge in climate science since the Charney Report in 1979 is to determine how much the Earth's climate warms in response to a unit external energy input at the top of the atmosphere (TOA). In this study, we show from first principles that temperature feedback within an atmosphere-surface column operates as a set of feedback circuits, each governed by an intrinsic gain less than unity, leading to geometric amplification of energy through successive feedback cycles. title: GPU-Accelerated Nested Schur-Complement Solvers for Atmospheric Flow Simulations Using Horizontally-Explicit, Vertically-Implicit Schemes and Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
abstract: Horizontally explicit, vertically implicit (HEVI) time integration removes the acoustic time-step restriction imposed by fine vertical grids in nonhydrostatic atmospheric models, but requires fast solvers for the resulting vertical linear systems, especially on GPUs. We present GPU-accelerated nested Schur-complement solvers for these systems for a split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes applied to the compressible Euler equations with gravity. title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
abstract: We present a fully discrete energy conserving discretisation of the rotating shallow water equations with arbitrary order in space and time. A space time finite element discretisation is used, built from compatible finite element methods in space and continuous Petrov-Galerkin schemes in time. Projected auxiliary variables for Hamiltonian derivatives are necessary for exact energy conservation. title: Polarforming for MIMO Covert Communications
abstract: Covert communication conceals wireless transmission activity, but conventional multi-antenna designs rely mainly on spatial beamforming and can be constrained by limited spatial degrees of freedom. This paper investigates polarization-reconfigurable antenna (PRA)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) covert communication, where Alice and Bob perform transmit and receive polarforming, respectively, and Willie uses a vertically polarized antenna for radiometric detection. title: Interplay between Excitability and Noise in Analog Spiking Neurons
abstract: A spiking neuron is a dynamical system exhibiting a limit cycle (a spike) when subject to sufficiently excitatory input. Famous neuroscience experiments by Bryant and Segundo as well as Mainen and Sejnowski revealed that the spike times of some biological neurons are more reliable when subject to time-varying stimuli compared to constant ones. Provided with an industrial physics-based transient noise SPICE simulation framework compatible with foundry transistor compact models, we have demonstrated similar behaviours for a CMOS analog spiking neuron designed for neuromorphic computing hardware

abstract: Recently, the LHCb Collaboration reported a new narrow bottom-strange meson, $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ with mass $M= (5698.9 \pm 1.5 \pm 0.6)$~MeV, width $Γ<9.8$~MeV, and spin-parity $J^P=0^+$ in the $B_s^0π^0$ invariant-mass spectrum. abstract: We present WEEVIL (WatEr Emission of Vapor from Ice in the Laboratory), an experimental facility developed to study ice sublimation under laboratory conditions to support observations of comets and icy moons. The setup combines a submillimeter heterodyne radiometer and a high-vacuum cryogenic chamber, enabling spatially and temporally resolved monitoring of gas plumes formed during ice sublimation under controlled laboratory conditions. title: Entropy-Stable and Well-Balanced Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for the Compressible Euler Equations in Vector-Invariant Form
abstract: We develop structure-preserving methods for the compressible Euler equations with gravity in vector-invariant form and potential temperature as a prognostic variable within the flux-differencing discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) framework. By discretizing the nonconservative terms as symmetric and antisymmetric products, we derive two-point numerical fluxes that conserve both the thermodynamic entropy and the total energy. title: DeboRheo v2.0: Improved Robustness for Geometrical VOF Simulations of Viscoelastic Two-Phase Flows
abstract: We present DeboRheo v2.0, an unstructured, geometrically unsplit Volume-of-Fluid framework implemented in OpenFOAM for viscoelastic two-phase flows. Version 2.0 improves numerical robustness when large viscosity contrasts coincide with strongly deformed interfaces and thin viscoelastic lamellae or filaments. title: Accessing electronic entanglement via photo-assisted two-electron tomography
abstract: Witnessing entanglement between electrons propagating in quantum circuits requires accessing their two-electron coherences, which encode the two-particle quantum correlations generated by Coulomb interactions. Yet, experimental reconstruction of two-electron coherence remains a major challenge. We introduce photo-assisted two-electron tomography, a quantum coherence reconstruction protocol from dc-currents and time-averaged current correlations, routinely measured in electron quantum optics experiments. title: Global ice loss drives source-independent amplification of sea-level rise at Pacific and Indian Ocean Small Island Developing States
abstract: Abstract We quantify the spatial pattern (“fingerprint”) of sea-level rise caused by mass loss from the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets and from glaciers worldwide through 2100. Using ensembles of ice-sheet and glacier mass-balance projections and gravitational, rotational, and deformational sea-level modeling, we calculate normalized sea-level fingerprints and their impacts on Small Island Developing States. title: DNA-based monitoring uncovers contrasting salinity-driven diversity patterns of bacterial and protist plankton in the Baltic Sea area
abstract: Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. It remains unknown whether the same is true for protists. Moreover, changes in alpha diversity of both bacteria and protists across the brackish salinity gradient remain elusive. title: Plankton Ecology in the Philippines: Diversity, Dynamics, and Ecological Significance Across Tropical Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
abstract: Plankton communities in the Philippines occupy a critical ecological position in one of the world's most biologically diverse marine regions. Situated within the Coral Triangle and traversed by the Western Pacific Warm Pool, Philippine waters support extraordinary phytoplankton and zooplankton assemblages that regulate primary production, mediate carbon fluxes, and sustain the productivity of pelagic and coastal fisheries. title: Multiple strategies and cues define baleen whale migration
abstract: Migration is a do-or-die life-history strategy, yet factors shaping it remain poorly studied in many marine taxa, as direct observations are difficult. Building on animal migration theory, we used satellite tracking data from 21 southern right whales tagged in Aotearoa New Zealand to investigate migratory cues, timing and routes. Whales followed either a direct westward route or a longer, indirect route via higher latitudes when migrating from their wintering grounds to summer feeding grounds. title: Hidden subsurface suspended sediment export from Greenland's marine‐terminating glaciers
abstract: Abstract Runoff and calved ice volumes from the Greenland Ice Sheet are well constrained, but quantifying the associated suspended sediment flux remains challenging. Here we present near‐terminus observations from three glacierized fjords in southeast Greenland, combining full‐depth turbidity profiles and current velocity from summer 2024 to evaluate sediment export. title: Ancient terrestrial forests reborn as modern marine ecosystems under shifting sea levels
abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise and coastal erosion can submerge terrestrial carbon-rich landscapes, yet the ecological fate and climate significance of such relict coastal carbon deposits remain largely unknown. We report the discovery of submerged tropical peat reefs in the shallow coastal waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique; a legacy of ancient coastal forests now transformed into benthic marine habitats. abstract: Introduction . The coastline of a reservoir is a complex natural object, which geometry has irregularity and signs of selfsimilarity, and the length depends on the scale of measurement. Despite the widespread study of its fractal properties, the transition to a digital representation of the coastline is a complex procedure and is a current topic of research. title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. title: Contrasting microbiomes in deep-sea scleractinian and octocoral species from the South Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Abstract Deep-sea corals (DSC) are ecologically important, yet their microbiomes’ composition, structure, and host specificity remain largely unresolved in the South Atlantic, especially for octocorals. Here, we provide a comprehensive characterisation of DSC microbiomes, spanning Hexacorallia (Desmophyllum pertusum, Solenosmilia variabilis) and Octocorallia (Candidella imbricata, three Malacalcyonacea species), collected at ∼710 m depth in the Campos Basin, an active oil- and gas-producing region. title: Documented technology adoption in environmental impact assessment: a mixed-methods study of adoption–perception gaps in Korea
abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI, big data analytics, GIS, real-time monitoring, and predictive modeling, their integration into environmental impact assessment (EIA) practice remains poorly documented. This study employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design to examine documented technology adoption in Korean EIA and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA). title: Integrating Strategic Environmental Assessment into Regional Development Planning for Sustainable Development in Bireuen Regency
abstract: Regional planning in Bireuen has to respond to basic-service needs while also dealing with pressure on watersheds, forested land, and areas exposed to hydro-meteorological hazards. This paper examines how far the 2025-2029 Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is carried into the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (Indonesian term: Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Daerah/RPJMD), rather than remaining a separate compliance document. SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. It adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology combining doctrinal legal analysis with critical examination of national policies and plans, international commitments, judicial decisions, and institutional reports

abstract: Abstract. Coastal marine environments are hot spots in the global marine silicon (Si) cycle. Dissolved silicate (DSi) is an essential macronutrient for diatoms, which often dominate primary productivity in temporal coastal seas and constitute a key food source for grazers. Even though benthic release of DSi influences the ecology of coastal marine areas, direct rate measurements of DSi mobilisation remain scarce.
