title: An Ecosystem-Based Marine Spatial Planning Approach for Sustainable Natural Resources Management in the Bangladesh Delta
abstract: Despite the establishment of maritime boundaries with Myanmar (2012) and India (2014), which secured sovereign rights over approximately 118,813 km² of the Bay of Bengal, marine space is still managed on a sector-by-sector basis, and no marine spatial plan has been prepared. This study identifies significant ecological, economic, and cultural areas within Bangladesh's maritime zone, and proposes a framework for the blue economy and develops an ecosystem-based model of marine spatial planning (MSP). title: Cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in juvenile green and loggerhead sea turtles: an exploratory biologging study
abstract: Anthropogenic underwater noise is an increasing concern in marine environments, yet physiological responses of sea turtles remain poorly understood. We examined cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in three juvenile green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and four juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) maintained after incidental capture. title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. title: ECOCRITICAL PERSPECTIVES ON INTO THE BENEATH: GREG GARRARD’S FRAMEWORK IN DEPICTING MARINE ENVIRONMENTAL CRISES
abstract: This study aims to explore ecological phenomena in Rifqi Farizi’s novel Into the Beneath through the framework of Greg Garrard’s ecocriticism. The research focuses on identifying and analyzing the representation of five key ecological categories: pollution, apocalypse, dwelling, animals, and earth. The objective is to reveal how the novel reflects contemporary ecological anxieties and provides critical perspectives on humanity’s relationship with the ocean as a vital yet vulnerable ecosystem. A qualitative descriptive method was applied with textual data drawn from the novel. Data collection w

title: Measurements of the Size and Physical Properties of Marine Particles Using Atomic Force Microscopy: Implications for Marine Biogeochemical Cycles
abstract: Abstract Particle size and physical properties such as stiffness and adhesiveness affect sinking velocity and flux in the ocean, yet conventional two‐dimensional measurements lack accuracy and mechanical information. In this study, we applied atomic force microscopy (AFM) to quantify three‐dimensional size and physical properties of marine particles. Three hundred and sixty‐eight particles were collected using a marine snow catcher from the pycnocline and benthic boundary layer at three coastal‐to‐offshore stations in the northwestern Pacific. title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. title: Temperate marine macrophytes are highly variable sources of Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds – a comparative study from the Baltic Sea and NE Atlantic
abstract: Abstract. Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth’s ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. In this study, we set out to address this knowledge gap by quantifying ex situ the BVOC emission rates of three
institutions: Ollscoil na Gaillimhe – University of Galway

title: Combined effects of elevated temperature and fluoxetine exposure on early development of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus
abstract: Temperature rise associated with climate change increases the vulnerability of coastal species, which are also exposed to pharmaceuticals. We investigated the effects of thermal stress and fluoxetine (FLX), alone and in combination, on early developmental stages of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus, a key coastal species. Gametes, zygotes and embryos were exposed to ambient (18°C) and near-future projections (21°C, 24°C) to identify the most sensitive developmental stage to warming. In parallel, environmentally relevant FLX concentrations were tested under near-future temperature scenarios.

title: A source-to-sea decision-support framework for wet-weather wastewater load management: evidence from Jiaozhou Bay
abstract: Coastal concentration compliance can overlook increased wastewater throughput during wet weather. We developed a source-to-sea decision-support framework using 2019–2022 wastewater, river, and marine observations from Jiaozhou Bay, China. The analysis combined source-record auditing, hydraulic and concentration decomposition, benchmark comparison, and source–receptor chronology. At Loushan wastewater treatment plant, throughput increased by 87.5% from the second to the third quarter of 2020 while total phosphorus remained low at 0.06–0.07 mg L −1 . title: Geography Teaching Methods and Tools in the Republic of Kosovo
abstract: Методите и средствата за обучение са основни елементи в преподаването на география. Те позволяват ефективното усвояване на знания, умения и навици, като същевременно развиват мисленето, вниманието и мотивацията на учениците. Използването на съвременни технологии, като Google Earth, Google Maps, Bing и ГИС, улеснява визуализацията, анализа и разширяват възможностите за виртуални пътувания и изследвания. journal: Общество памет образование (История и обществени нагласи)

title: Acceptability of a Novel Prehospital Emergency Care System Evaluation Tool Among Southeast Asian Stakeholders: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: Introduction: Prehospital emergency care (PEC) systems vary widely in structure, capacity, and stage of development, and existing evaluation tools are not tailored to the contextual needs of Southeast Asia. To address this gap, the Prehospital Emergency Care System Evaluation Tool (PECSET) was developed as a 32-element, consensus-derived framework to support system assessment, prioritization, and quality improvement. title: FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT AND EXPORT SOPHISTICATION IN ASEAN-5 DURING THE ASEAN PLUS THREE COOPERATION PERIOD
abstract: Export sophistication is widely regarded as a channel through which trade contributes to sustained growth, yet evidence on its relationship with foreign direct investment (FDI) in Southeast Asia during the period of deepening ASEAN Plus Three (ASEAN+3) cooperation remains limited. This study examines trade with China, Japan, and the Republic of Korea (South Korea) and the relationship between FDI inflows and export sophistication in five ASEAN economies (Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand) over the period of the ASEAN Plus Three Cooperation Work Plan 2007-2017. journal: Journal of Applied Economics in Developing Countries

title: Mathematics anxiety and problem-solving ability in numerical methods courses: A repeated cross-sectional study across two Southeast Asian universities
abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) impedes mathematical learning by taxing cognitive resources, negatively affecting problem-solving ability (PSA). Some evidence suggests that the strength and nature of this negative association may vary across educational and cultural contexts. However, cross-cultural studies on MA and PSA, especially in Southeast Asia, remain limited. This study investigated cohort-level patterns of MA and PSA in a transnational Numerical Methods course at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) and Universitas Pahlawan (UP), Indonesia. title: Marine habitat use and movement of sympatric anadromous Dolly Varden and Arctic Char in the Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Objective Inuit subsistence fishers in Kugluktuk, Nunavut, Canada, have noticed changes in the timing and locations of their catches of Arctic Char Salvelinus alpinus and northern form Dolly Varden S. malma malma (collectively referred to by the community as “char”) in the past ∼20 years. In response, an ongoing research program was formed to study char in partnership with the Kugluktuk Hunters and Trappers Organization. journal: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society

title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: Abstract During the 70-million-year span of the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity up to fourfold. In the absence of adaptation, unicellular organisms living in this viscous environment were limited in their ability to move and acquire nutrients. We experimentally test the hypothesis that multicellularity evolved in order to overcome this viscosity-induced metabolic deficit. title: Gestión territorial y herramientas de apoyo a la decisión para la recolección de residuos en ciudades turísticas. El caso de Pinamar
abstract: El artículo aborda la gestión urbana de la recolección de residuos en ciudades turísticas caracterizadas por una marcada variabilidad estacional de la demanda, tomando al Partido de Pinamar, provincia de Buenos Aires, como caso de estudio. El objetivo es desarrollar una propuesta metodológico-operativa para el análisis y la gestión del servicio mediante la integración de variables territoriales, temporales y operativas. Metodológicamente, la investigación combina revisión bibliográfica y normativa, relevamiento territorial, entrevista semiestructurada a un supervisor de la empresa prestataria
institutions: Universidad de Ciencias Empresariales y Sociales

title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
abstract: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. title: Assessment of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Potential in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia: Energy Performance, Techno-Economic Feasibility, and Environmental Considerations
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion as a renewable electricity source in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia. Ocean temperature data from the World Ocean Atlas for 1955-2018 at station 21576 were analyzed to characterize the surface and deep-water thermal conditions and to assess the performance of an open-cycle Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion system. The assessment covered thermodynamic efficiency, electrical power generation, production cost, freshwater production, and potential environmental impacts. title: Nonlinear ocean wave propagation in a fractional perturbed Gerdjikov–Ivanov model with higher-order dispersive effects
abstract: Nonlinear dispersive wave propagation governs complex physical phenomena in both nonlinear optics and hydrodynamics, including optical fiber communications, ultrafast photonic systems, coastal environments, and marine systems, where higher-order nonlinear interactions and dispersive effects significantly influence wave evolution. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. institutions: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel

title: Particle-tracking assessment of potential groundwater pathways for radionuclide transport across the Futaba Fault, coastal Fukushima, Japan
abstract: Radiocesium deposited after the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident remains a long-term environmental concern, but its groundwater pathways toward inhabited coastal lowlands are poorly constrained. This study evaluates conservative groundwater pathways potentially relevant to radionuclide transport near the Futaba Fault in coastal Fukushima by coupling a steady-state MODFLOW-2005 model with MODPATH 7. title: Multi-predatory feeding aggregations in the Norwegian Sea: prevalence and ecological importance
abstract: Multi-predatory feeding aggregations (MPFAs) occur when several predator species concurrently exploit shared, spatially and temporally aggregated prey. Although MPFAs are well described in some marine ecosystems, their prevalence in the Norwegian Sea has historically been underestimated. Here, we synthesize existing biological, acoustic, visual and behavioural evidence to reinterpret classical predator-prey observations through the lens of MPFAs. journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

title: A Modular, Cloud-Based GIS Platform for Automated Wildfire Risk Index Mapping
abstract: Wildfires are a growing environmental and socio-economic threat driven by climate change and land abandonment. As fire frequency and intensity increase, suppression alone is no longer sufficient, making prevention and preparedness essential. Earth Observation and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) enable the integration of environmental and socio-economic factors into decision-support tools for wildfire risk assessment. title: From shark hunters to sea guardians: Environmental literacy transformation and socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people in Sapeken Islands, East Java-Indonesia
abstract: The Bajo people are known for their closeness to and dependence on the sea. Over the past few decades, the Bajo people have undergone significant changes that are worth examining. This study aims to analyze the socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people who inhabit Sadulang Besar Island, Sapeken Archipelago, East Java, with particular attention to how environmental literacy, intergenerational learning, and shifting livelihood strategies have contributed to changes in marine practices and ecological identity. title: Hydrodynamics of bio-mimetic sponge arrays with non-uniform triangular arrangement under wave actions
abstract: Bio-inspired marine structures have attracted increasing attention as nature-based solutions for modifying coastal hydrodynamics and enhancing momentum exchange. Previous studies on isolated and dual sponge-inspired elements have shown limited hydrodynamic effectiveness under relatively low-height waves, where velocity redistribution and turbulence generation remain weak. To address this limitation, the present study proposes and experimentally fabricates a bio-mimetic pillar coral composed of non-uniform triangular sponge elements arranged in a progressive three-line configuration. title: Ocean predators as indicators of nano- and microplastic prevalence in pelagic food webs
abstract: Abstract Quantifying nano- and microplastics (NMPs) in ocean predators is fundamental to understanding the prevalence of these contaminants and potential impacts on ecosystem health. Pyrolysis gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with lipid correction was used to determine NMP concentrations and polymer composition in the muscle tissue of two pelagic predators (dolphinfish [ Coryphaena hippurus ], yellowfin tuna [ Thunnus albacares ]) across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. institutions: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

title: Escalating competition in changing seas: baleen whales exploit killer whale prey herding
abstract: Climate change and other anthropogenic pressures are rapidly reshaping marine ecosystems, altering prey availability and predator interactions. Yet empirical evidence of how these relationships shift under changing conditions remains scarce. Drawing on over a decade of monitoring in a subarctic fjord system, we provide a rare insight into these dynamics. In northern Norway, the winter aggregation of herring (Clupea harengus) and their primary predator, the killer whale (Orcinus orca), has shifted northward under the combined influence of climate change and fishing pressure. journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

title: Unraveling the roles of shallow coastal habitats and salinity in shaping aquatic microeukaryotic communities using experimental and field approaches
abstract: Abstract Microeukaryotic communities in brackish coastal ecosystems are structured by complex interactions between environmental conditions and habitat heterogeneity. This study examines how moderate salinity levels (ranging from freshwater to salinity 6) and habitat type (water column, sediment, and biofilm) influence microeukaryotic diversity and community composition in shallow coastal waters of the Gulf of Finland, the Baltic Sea. title: Advanced Assessment of the Agro-Silvo-Pastoral Coherence in Transboundary Transitional Water Regions
abstract: Transitional waters play a vital role in the ecological health and sustainability of coastal areas. According to European Union legislation, transitional waters are coastal water bodies influenced by freshwater flows but are partly saline due to their proximity to the sea. This study focuses on agricultural and forestry regions adjacent to transboundary transitional waters—i.e., areas where two or more countries share an estuary, tidal inlet, delta, or lagoon and have a contiguous border in their territorial waters. The objective of the study is to determine the patterns of riparian agroforest

title: Marine holobionts: a model arena for host–microbe biology, from ecosystem function to biotechnology
abstract: Abstract Microbial symbioses are the operating system of marine biology. Nearly every macroscopic organism in the ocean exists as a holobiont, the consortium composed of a eukaryotic host and its bacterial, archaeal, microeukaryotic and viral partners. Marine holobionts span a broader range of the metazoan tree of life than likely any other ecological setting on the planet. This breadth makes the marine realm a uniquely informative system to investigate how host-microbe partnerships shape organisms and ecosystems. title: Interactions between multi-species marine predator aggregations and the energy landscape
abstract: Multi-species predator aggregations can be found in both coastal and pelagic ecosystems, forming for both foraging and refuging (resting) purposes. The energy landscape represents the power costs required to move through or reside within a habitat. As species may differ in their morphology, buoyancy and length, there may be species-specific heterogeneity in their energy landscapes. Here, we highlight how the energy landscape may influence the small-scale distribution of predators within an aggregation and potentially their ability to forage. title: Seascape genomics reveals high genetic diversity and apparent panmixia in endemic Southern Ocean phytoplankton
abstract: Abstract The adaptive potential and resilience of cold‐adapted phytoplankton to climate change have the potential to impact polar marine food webs and global biogeochemical cycles. Two central but poorly constrained facets of adaptive potential in polar phytoplankton are standing genetic diversity and its spatial structure. Here, we partially sequenced 30 field isolate genomes of a commonly‐occurring endemic Southern Ocean (SO) phytoplankton, the diatom Actinocyclus actinochilus , and analyzed patterns in standing genetic diversity and geographic structure. title: Small-scale fishers’ perceptions and behavioural responses to marine protected areas implementation
abstract: Marine protected area (MPA) implementation can lead to fishers’ displacement and opposition to conservation efforts. Yet, evidence on how MPAs affect fishing operations is limited, especially for the small-scale sector. Surveys and participatory mapping exercises (n=93) were carried out with small-scale fishers in four Mediterranean and one Black Sea MPA to investigate fishers’ behavioural responses and perceptions to MPA implementation. Industry-led mitigation of seal bycatch in North Sea pelagic trawl fisheries: Evaluating excluder device effectiveness and policy implications
abstract: Bycatch of marine mammals in commercial fisheries presents conservation, operational, and regulatory challenges, particularly in the Greater North Sea where trawl fisheries targeting forage fish overlap with seal foraging habitats. This study evaluates the effectiveness of two seal excluder devices—the DPPO’s excluder tube and the PFA’s excluder grid—designed to reduce incidental seal captures in sandeel and herring fisheries, respectively. title: Public perceptions and (lack of) support for mitigation of artificial light at night in coastal cities
abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is an expanding environmental pressure in urban areas, yet effective mitigation depends on public support. We investigated how residents of two Chilean coastal cities perceive ALAN, its impacts and potential mitigation measures. Respondents demonstrated asymmetric environmental literacy, recognising the societal benefits of lighting while showing limited awareness of its ecological consequences, particularly for coastal-marine ecosystems. title: Intra-annual dynamics of larval fish assemblages and their environmental associations in the central Southern Black Sea
abstract: Larval fish assemblages are crucial indicators for monitoring marine ecosystem dynamics and the recruitment potential of fishery stocks. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of larval fish assemblages in the central Southern Black Sea (Sinop) and the environmental parameters shaping these patterns. An intra-annual monthly sampling survey identified 35 species across 20 families; the assemblage structure was dominated by Engraulis encrasicolus, Gobius niger, Sprattus sprattus, Mullus barbatus and Trachurus mediterraneus. title: No effect of short‐term exposure to ocean acidification on individual‐level variation in behaviour and susceptibility to predation in a Great Barrier Reef damselfish
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification, caused by rising carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in the atmosphere, has been reported to negatively impact a wide variety of behaviours in fishes, including activity, exploration, and predator avoidance. These effects have been documented at the population level, but many animal species naturally show large and repeatable individual‐level differences in behaviour. title: Cumulative impact of climate change and adaptation measures on Venice and its lagoon
abstract: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-level rise and storm surges, still ensuring the lagoon-sea exchange. However, under climate change the frequency and duration of Mose closures will increase and this might modify lagoon water renewal and affect ecosystem properties. title: Effects of the summer season and religious holiday periods on tropospheric NO₂ levels in Türkiye’s coastal tourism destinations: A Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI and GIS-based analysis (2023–2025)
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric NO2 variations observed in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions—Türkiye’s prominent coastal tourism hubs—during the 2023–2025 period, within the context of seasonal summer intensity and short-term mobility during Eid al-Fitr (Ramadan Feast) and Eid al-Adha (Feast of Sacrifice). The study utilizes Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 data to generate daily regional median values for selected coastal tourism districts. title: Microphytobenthos Primary Production and Organic Matter Mineralization Along the Sea Level Gradient in a Tropical Mudflat
abstract: Tropical tidal flats represent more than half of the global tidal flat area, however information on the ecological and biogeochemical role of microphytobenthos (MPB) in tropical environments remains scarce. The objective of this study was to analyze the changes in sediment biogeochemistry, MPB, community composition and net metabolism along the sea level (SL) gradient in a tropical tidal flat (Punta Morales, Gulf of Nicoya, Costa Rica). title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. title: Self-reporting alkalinity-responsive hydrogel for visual monitoring and microenvironment remodeling of seawater-immersed infected wounds
abstract: Seawater-associated infected wounds involve alkaline and hyperosmotic stress, polymicrobial contamination, biofilms, and persistent inflammation, collectively delaying healing. Herein, we developed QCB-Au@SPG, a pH-responsive hydrogel integrating fluorescent antibacterial QCB-Au, an alkali-sensitive SA-PBA network, and photocrosslinkable GelMA. title: Assessment of disinfectant performance against fish-pathogenic bacteria in planktonic and biofilm states
abstract: Disinfecting fish farming equipment and facility surfaces with disinfectant is one of the primary biosafety measures to prevent disease introduction and transmission. However, the actual efficacy of approved disinfectants against fish-pathogenic bacteria and especially their biofilms remain largely undocumented. Six selected disinfectants were evaluated against seven common disease-causing bacteria and their biofilms. title: Marine radar reveals novel group foraging patterns in pelagic seabirds
abstract: Many seabirds are known to frequently feed within multi-specific feeding flocks. These aggregations bring facilitation to prey access as well as potential exacerbated competition. Once a feeding opportunity is found, birds rapidly aggregate to it through processes known as local enhancement. At a larger scale, seabirds may distribute themselves forming patterns such as rakes or clusters, which are thought to increase the probability to cue on other foragers. title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. title: Measuring Dry Deposition of Sea Spray Aerosol and Height of Aerosol Plume Using a Controlled Wave Pool
abstract: Abstract Deposition of sea spray aerosols facilitates atmospheric corrosion of materials, requiring maintenance and replacement over time. However, the dimensions of sea spray aerosol plumes produced from breaking waves have not been well‐characterized, limiting useful prediction of particle transport downwind and atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, this project aimed to measure sea spray aerosol production from breaking waves in a controlled environment at several elevations to obtain the height profile of an aerosol plume. title: Episodic High‐Latitude Occurrence of Walleye Pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) in the Central Arctic Ocean Associated With Warm Subsurface Conditions: Multi‐Year Environmental DNA and Larval Evidence
abstract: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). title: Carbon fluxes within an Arctica islandica habitat in the German Baltic Sea
abstract: Ongoing climate change and rising CO 2 emissions highlight the need to understand ecosystem carbon cycling to guide the conservation of carbon-rich, biodiverse habitats. We investigated organic carbon cycling and storage associated with the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica in the German Baltic Sea. Through filtration and bioturbation, A. islandica may enhance the burial of organic carbon in deeper sediment layers. title: Visualizing the penetration behavior of tapered thread piles via transparent soil: Effects of thread design
abstract: With superior construction efficiency and load-bearing performance, precast tapered thread piles hold significant potential for offshore and coastal infrastructure. However, their installation mechanics remain poorly understood, and visual experimental investigations are scarce. To address this knowledge gap, this study utilizes a developed optomechanically coupled testing system to investigate the continuous penetration process of tapered thread piles. title: Increases in foraging performance of humpback whales in multi-predator feeding aggregations with California sea lions
abstract: Marine predators frequently form ephemeral multi-predator feeding aggregations around dense prey patches, yet the mechanisms and outcomes of these dynamic events remain poorly resolved. We quantified how California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) presence influenced humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) foraging using 46 multi-sensor video tags (mean duration: 7.4 ± 7.1 h) deployed on fish-feeding whales in Monterey Bay, California, USA (2014-2023). abstract: La dependencia de procesos manuales para validar pagos universitarios suele provocar errores administrativos y retrasos que afectan a los estudiantes. abstract: Candida palmioleophila is an emerging opportunistic yeast frequently misidentified within the Meyerozyma guilliermondii complex, potentially obscuring its clinical and ecological relevance. abstract: Abstract Marine sediment cores from Antarctica are archived by national programs for reuse and resampling by future researchers, creating a resourceful way to conduct Antarctic science. With reduced budgets to conduct Antarctic field work and to collect new sediment cores offshore of the icy continent, the accessibility of these archived cores and availability of core data are in high demand. abstract: Sand lance ( Ammodytes japonicus ) is an important forage fish in the Harima-Nada Sea, Japan, but its stock has declined markedly in recent decades under concurrent changes in nutrient availability and water temperature. title: Revealing potential Atlantic salmon bycatch hotspots from pelagic fisheries landings across the Northeast Atlantic
abstract: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) marine survival has declined markedly over the past five decades, leading to concerns about future population viability. While many studies have explored the impacts of stressors such as climate change and predation, less is known about bycatch from pelagic fisheries targeting finfish species. abstract: Coastal cities have shifted from outward expansion to reworking the housing stock they already hold, and renewing aging communities has become harder to manage as a result. abstract: This study examines the characteristics of extreme rainfall in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, and its teleconnections with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting domestic, agricultural, and industrial water demands, particularly in regions where surface water resources are limited or unreliable. abstract: As built-up expansion in the Syrian coastal mountainous areas intensifies, its environmental impacts are becoming increasingly severe. abstract: Climate change is reshaping South Africa’s marine ecosystems and fisheries with consequences for ecological productivity, livelihoods and governance. abstract: Some conservation programs keep turtles temporarily under human care with the intention of releasing them later to strengthen wild populations. title: Biodiversity safeguards ecosystem services and functions worldwide

Here we synthesize 423 studies to determine how biodiversity affects ecosystem functioning and service delivery. title: Assessment of 226Ra and 228Ra activity concentrations in drinking water sources along Ghana’s coastal communities
abstract: This study reports a screening-level radiological assessment of drinking water sources – sachet water, tap water, borehole water and river water – across the Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions of Ghana. title: Experimental manipulation of ecological constraints influences conflict but not cooperation in the humbug damselfish Dascyllus aruanus
abstract: Animal societies vary widely in levels of cooperation and conflict, and understanding the causes of this variation is a central goal in evolutionary biology. As with other features of animal societies, relatedness, competitiveness and ecological constraints (e.g. habitat saturation and risks of dispersal) have been proposed as key factors explaining variation in cooperation and conflict. abstract: Co-management of Protected Areas (PAs) has emerged as a strategy to make forest restoration and biodiversity conservation more effective by encouraging the active participation of local people. abstract: Purpose - Southern Calabria represents one of the most geologically complex and diverse regions of the Mediterranean. Despite this exceptional geological richness, its geoheritage remains only partially documented and poorly integrated into structured geotourism strategies. In many Mediterranean regions, geotourism has proven to be an effective tool for sustainable territorial development, environmental education, and heritage protection, yet Southern Calabria still lacks a comprehensive and systematic geotouristic framework. abstract: Mangrove forests, recognized as the main ecosystem of coastal zones and providing various goods and services, are facing are facing increasing anthropogenic pressures and require continuous investigation. title: Chronic exposure to Salton Sea aerosols elicits pulmonary inflammation and shifts in murine lung and fecal microbiome diversity
abstract: Abstract Lung disease is rampant around the Salton Sea, California’s largest inland lake and a major source of airborne particulates. To examine root causes of pulmonary disease, we investigated the exposure impacts of spatiotemporal variation in aerosols collected near the Salton Sea on lung and fecal microbiomes. We collected dust during the summer and fall at three different sites around the Salton Sea from 2020 to 2022. title: Millennial‐Scale Deoxygenation in the Southern California Oxygen Minimum Zone Over the Last Glacial Cycle
abstract: Abstract Past variability of oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) provides key insights into future ocean deoxygenation. However, California margin OMZ records remain temporally limited, restricting evaluation of mechanisms across full glacial–interglacial cycles. Here, we reconstruct high‐resolution bottom water oxygen (BWO) over the past ∼140,000 years using redox‐sensitive trace metals from ODP Site 1017E in the Southern California OMZ. abstract: Understanding seabird diet is fundamental to assessing trophic interactions and predicting responses to environmental change. title: Probabilistic sustainability evaluation of hybrid breakwaters considering uncertainty in conceptualization and indicator weighting
abstract: One of the distinguishing features of hybrid infrastructure is the need to find balance between multiple functional performances. Multi-criteria decision analysis is an ideal tool for exploring this balance and identifying an ideal solution, but there are few examples of its application to coastal infrastructure. This study conducted a probabilistic, multi-criteria decision analysis-based sustainability evaluation of hybrid breakwater structures considering two sources of methodological uncertainty: conceptualization and weighting. abstract: Objective: This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the growth performance and total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) removal efficiency of two indigenous marine cyanobacterial isolates, Anabaena spp. and Oscillatoria acuta, under different initial ammonia concentrations, and to identify the most effective isolate for potential application in biological treatment of ammonia-contaminated saline waters. abstract: Abstract Chitinous cuticles are hierarchical biological composites in which the molecular organization spans multiple structural length scales. Although the relationships between chitin chemistry and mechanical performance have been extensively investigated, the structural factors governing transient thermal relaxation remain poorly understood. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are highly vulnerable to coastal environmental change and anthropogenic disturbance. The mangrove forests distributed along the eastern and western coasts of Shenzhen experience contrasting environmental regimes. The eastern coast is influenced by oligotrophic waters of the northern South China Sea and is dominated by native mangrove stands, whereas the western coast, located within the Pearl River Estuary, is subject to elevated nutrient inputs, intensive urbanization and extensive mangrove restoration. title: Nature-based experiences support lasting conservation behavior: longitudinal evidence from shark ecotourism in Hawaiʻi
abstract: Shark ecotourism is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for ocean sustainability, yet empirical evidence of its long-term impacts on conservation behavior remains limited. We employed a quasi-experimental, longitudinal design to evaluate whether participation in a shark ecotourism program in Hawaiʻi influenced individual conservation behavior over time. Survey data were collected from tour participants and a general public comparison group at the time of the tour and again two years later. title: Functional, communicative, and critical health literacy and stroke prevention behaviors among hypertensive patients in a Bugis Coastal Community, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Health literacy plays an important role in hypertension management and stroke prevention; however, conventional health literacy assessment approaches often overlook sociocultural contexts that shape health-related decision-making in culturally cohesive communities. This study assessed Functional, Communicative, and Critical (FCC) Health Literacy related to stroke prevention among hypertensive patients in a Bugis coastal community in Indonesia using a culturally contextualized approach informed by the Puangrimaggalatung framework. title: By the crossroad
abstract: Due to infrastructural work, Sydsvensk Arkeologi AB conducted an archaeological excavation in 2022 between the Scanian villages Fjälkinge and Gualöv, southern Sweden. The excavation revealed settlements and a cemetery from the Late Neolithic into the Pre-Roman Iron Age. Located at a plausible prehistoric intersection which connects the Lake Ivösjön to the Baltic Sea, and coastal south to the north, the site has the potential to provide new knowledge of ancient road systems and its possibilities for exchange of both ideas and people. abstract: Abstract Host–associated microbiomes play vital roles in species’ ecology and evolution, yet little is known about their shift during the transition from aquatic to terrestrial habitats. We characterize the skin microbiomes of three combtooth blenny species (Blenniella paula, Praealticus labrovittatus, Alticus arnoldorum) that occupy distinct positions along the intertidal gradient—from fully subtidal to intertidal and supratidal environments. abstract: Abstract Protozoan parasites in the genus Perkinsus proliferate within marine mollusc hosts through schizogony to produce intracellular daughter cells. This proliferation of P. olseni PRA-181 requires glycine betaine (GB) derived from host molluscs. Although GB exhibits diverse biochemical functions, its role in promoting cell proliferation is unique, and its underlying mechanism is unclear. title: Soil organic carbon dynamics and microbial responses to intercropping sweet corn with legumes under different row arrangements in coastal Odisha
abstract: Abstract Intercropping of cereals and legumes can improve resource-use efficiency and soil fertility compared with monocropping. A field experiment was conducted during rabi , 2023–24 at OUAT, Bhubaneswar, India to evaluate the effects of sweet corn ( Zea mays L.) intercropped with cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata ) and black gram ( Vigna mungo ) under different row arrangements on soil organic carbon (SOC), biological properties and soil fertility. abstract: The Gulf ecosystem health was of great concern after the explosion of the Deepwater Horizon oil platform (April 2010). After the spill, a large volume of oil trapped in the deep-sea plumes was transported offshore and to deep-water sediments, causing detrimental effects on the benthic fauna. This study provides the first dynamic evaluation of sugarcane field drainage water as a naturally occurring low-salinity injection brine through an integrated approach combining pore-scale and core-scale experiments. title: Effects of Composite Reclamation Models of Sea Buckthorn, A Pioneer Species in Semi‐Arid Regions, on Soil Quality and Microbial Communities
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐pit coal mining severely degrades soil and ecosystem functions, constraining regional sustainability. Vegetation‐based reclamation has therefore been widely adopted as an effective approach to promote soil recovery and ecosystem restoration. In this study, eight reclamation models were established at the Antaibao Open‐Pit Coal Mine, all dominated by sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) and combined with Chinese pine ( Pinus tabulaeformis Carr.), black locust ( Robinia pseudoacacia L.) and littleleaf peashrub ( Caragana microphylla Lam.). abstract: Ascetosporea is a group of parasitic protists within Endomyxa that primarily infect marine invertebrates and can cause serious damage to fishery resources such as oysters and prawns. Although approximately 50 species have been formally described, environmental DNA (eDNA) studies suggest that their diversity remains largely underestimated, with many lineages yet to be discovered. title: Have You Done Your Duty? Impact of Direct Mailing Campaign on Septic System Owners' Maintenance Knowledge and Behaviors in Coastal Texas Watersheds
abstract: As part of a watershed protection plan, the Texas Water Resources Institute and AgriLife Extension Service developed and distributed an educational postcard (``mailer'') about septic system maintenance to mailing addresses outside of public sewer service areas. The mailer was distributed four times within 1 year. The impact of this mailer was evaluated with a retrospective pre/post-test within a mailed survey. abstract: Skeletal systems couple rigid elements with contractile and connective tissues to transmit forces and control movement. abstract: Rapid coastal urbanization increases exposure to multiple hazards while intensifying competition for land essential for safe emergency refuge. This paper proposes a reproducible decision-support framework for planning Disaster Prevention and Relief Accessible Green Spaces (DPRAGS). title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors.

abstract: This study develops a web-based digital marketing platform for tourism-sector micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Rua Village to improve access to business information, product promotion, ordering, and transaction management. The research applies a software engineering approach through system analysis, system design, Agile Scrum development, and system testing. title: A new species of Doliocarpus (Dilleniaceae) from Brazil: the Atlantic Forest continues to reveal new findings on water vines
abstract: Abstract A new species of Doliocarpus (Dilleniaceae) endemic to the Brazilian Atlantic Forest is described. Doliocarpus amplexicarpus has been confused with D. schottianus , the most similar species occurring in the same phytogeographical domain, but the latter is found in the Serra do Mar Coastal Forests ecoregion, while the former occurs in the Bahia Coastal Forests ecoregion. abstract: Metal halide single crystals exhibit superior optoelectronic properties, promising for applications in optics and energy. title: Long-term spatiotemporal assessment of stable isotopic composition of precipitation across South Korea (2019–2023)
abstract: Mainland South Korea is a humid temperate peninsula characterized by strong seasonal climatic contrasts, complex topography, and a pronounced monsoon influence. title: Inventorization of spatial patterns and reassessment of benthic foraminiferal assemblages from mangrove ecosystems of Bay of Bengal
abstract: Mangrove ecosystems across the northeast coastal Bay of Bengal are highly productive yet increasingly showing vulnerability to climate change. This study presents a comprehensive inventory of benthic foraminifera from the Indian Sundarbans mangrove and the Budhabalanga estuary along with surrounding mangroves by integrating published records with new observations. title: Developmental temperature induces consistent patterns of plasticity in lower, but not upper, critical thermal limits in threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
abstract: Abstract Developmental plasticity, where early-life environmental cues shape developmental trajectories with lasting impact into adulthood, may play an important role in determining how species respond to changing thermal environments. title: Tolerance to heavy metals of bacteria from Brazilian deep aquatic environments
abstract: Abstract Bacterial resistance to heavy metals (HM) poses a significant risk to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated resistance to HM of 24 bacterial isolates from two deep aquatic environments in southern Brazil: the Guarani Aquifer System (GAS) water and the Rio Grande Cone (CRG) marine sediment. title: The late Miocene–earliest Pleistocene Calivil Formation in central Victoria: coarse-grained alluvial deposition following tectonism
abstract: The Calivil Formation is an extensive coarse-grained alluvial formation deposited within narrow valleys across the central Victorian highlands. title: Harem polygyny through resource defense territoriality in the sandperch Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae)
abstract: In reef fishes inhabiting sandy rubble habitats, such as sandperches, a mating system with territorial female-type harems has been widely confirmed. Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae) is a relatively large sandperch with large territorial home ranges. abstract: The self-excited oscillating water jet is widely used in ocean engineering. Its effectiveness stems from the impact of cavitation collapse driven by periodic pressure pulsations. This study investigated the flow field evolution and vortex stretching mechanisms of self-excited oscillating water jets using large eddy simulation. title: Titania nanosheet-graphitic carbon nitride interlayer engineering of antifouling polypyrrole membranes for effective filtration of aerobically treated oily wastewater

abstract: Fish eye lenses offer a chronological archive of individual life histories and preserve genomic DNA. However, integrating ecological and genetic data is hindered by post-mortem nuclease degradation, and standardized DNA preservation protocols for this tissue remain undefined. We evaluated chemical and thermal preservation methods to maximize DNA yield and integrity from fish lenses. abstract: We describe the first natural outbreak of infectious pancreatic necrosis (IPN) in farmed Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) in Norway. IPN was originally described in young salmonids, but the greatest losses have historically occurred in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) following sea transfer despite high vaccination coverage. abstract: The cross-hole sonic logging (CSL) method is a widely used nondestructive testing (NDT) technique for pile integrity assessment. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
abstract: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods.

abstract: Rural territories in developing countries face persistent socioeconomic inequalities that are rarely examined through systematic census data analytics at the parish level. abstract: Voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.3 is a key regulator of membrane potential and ionic homeostasis, particularly in immune signalling. Despite its importance, tools for directly visualizing Kv1.3 dynamics in living mammalian cells are limited, which restricts the comprehensive evaluation of its biological functions. abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) offer promise for flood resilience in coastal communities, yet public support remains a barrier to implementation. abstract: Social values are increasingly acknowledged in land management and spatial planning, particularly amid urbanization and sustainable development. Yet many planning systems have not institutionalized these values, leaving land-use decisions largely shaped by economic and technical rationalities. In Bangladesh, the forests and adjacent bodies of water provide protection against coastal hazards, support a variety of flora and fauna, capture carbon and sustain communities that rely on natural resources. abstract: Meteorological data are essential for forecasting and water resources management. abstract: This essay will bring together a body of work that attempts to capture human performance and natural phenomena on paper as a way of drawing and scoring encounters with place. title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically-driven strongly-interacting bosons
abstract: We study the exact nonequilibrium spectral function of a gas of strongly correlated Tonks-Girardeau bosons subjected to a strong periodic drive. abstract: Rivers and ports have historically shaped European cities, yet their wider territorial and spatial relationships remain insufficiently understood. This article proposes a multi-scalar, holistic and historically informed mapping approach to examine river port city territories as interconnected systems linking hydrology, logistics, urban form, governance and heritage. Building on the methodology developed for the Port City Atlas and refined for the River Port City Atlas, it investigates the Seine basin between Paris and Le Havre, revealing how inherited infrastructures and institutional fragment

title: Using spatio-temporal models to assist ecosystem-based fisheries management: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Tools to understand or predict ecosystem changes (e.g., fish community analyses) and the impacts of management measures on ecosystem components (e.g., ecosystem simulation models) are instrumental to the success of ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM). We developed a workflow using vector autoregressive spatio-temporal (VAST) models to assist EBFM in the Chatham Rise middle depth (CHAT MD) region, located in New Zealand waters. Our workflow employs research survey biomass catch rate data collected within the CHAT MD region and informs EBFM indirectly, by delivering inputs to ecosystem s
journal: Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries

title: The geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus Gray, 1838 (Mammalia, Chiroptera) in Guatemala, including the first record of N. lanatus Tejedor, 2005
abstract: We document the first confirmed record of Natalus lanatus from Guatemala, increasing the national bat fauna to 107 species, and present the first country-level synthesis of the geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus . Morphological analyses of N. lanatus ( n = 8) and N. mexicanus ( n = 8) show clear differentiation, with the first two FAMD dimensions explaining 61% of total variance. Voucher-based records further show elevational segregation, with N. lanatus occurring at 731–2,573 m and N. mexicanus from near sea level to 523 m.
institutions: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala

title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Arcuatula japonica (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) and its phylogenetic analysis
abstract: Arcuatula japonica (Dunker, 1857) (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) is a marine mussel distributed primarily in the northwestern Pacific. To clarify its evolutionary position and evaluate the taxonomic status of Crenellinae, we sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of A. japonica. The mitogenome is 16,198 bp in length and contains 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs), 22 transfer RNA genes (tRNAs), 2 ribosomal RNA genes (rRNAs), and 1 non-coding control region (CR), with an A + T bias (68.7%). Phylogenetic analysis based on 13 mitochondrial PCGs supports a sister relationshi
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Analysis of Fin Stabilizer Effects on 100 GT Fishing Vessel Resistance Using Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Fishing vessels require good hydrodynamic efficiency to limit propulsion power and energy consumption. Adding a fin stabilizer can modify the flow pattern, pressure distribution, wetted area, and consequently the total resistance; however, studies specifically addressing its resistance effect on a 100 GT fishing vessel remain limited. This study compares the flow characteristics and ship resistance before and after fin-stabilizer installation using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). The hull geometry was developed from a 25 GT fishing-vessel dataset through a scaling approach, producing a wor

title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and

institutions: East China University of Science and Technology

title: Agonistic interactions and vocalizations among Procellariiformes in multi-species feeding aggregations, observed through bird-borne cameras
abstract: Marine predators frequently aggregate at food sources, where interactions can range from cooperative group hunting to interference competition for resources. To investigate interactions at feeding aggregations among procellariiforms, we equipped wandering albatrosses Diomedea exulans with video cameras, collecting 43 hours of footage from 22 individuals. Cameras from eight birds recorded feeding aggregations, capturing a total of 62 minutes of footage (2.7% of observations). journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Chemical stress drives opposing bacterial biomass responses at the single-cell level
abstract: Abstract Microbial biomass is a central functional trait governing nutrient turnover and trophic transfer in aquatic ecosystems, yet how chemical stress reshapes biomass at the level of individual cells remains poorly resolved. Conventional toxicity assays primarily detect population-level growth inhibition and overlook sublethal physiological responses and heterogeneity within microbial populations. Here, we quantify single-cell dry-mass, a label-free proxy for cellular biomass and biosynthetic state, in the fast-growing marine bacterium Vibrio natriegens. Across thousands of cells, we assess

title: Phylogenetic Reconstruction of Cephalaspidea Using Multiple Datasets and Inference Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalaspidea is a key group within the Heterobranchia characterized by high species diversity and broad ecological disparity, and it is widely studied in marine ecology and systematics. Previous studies have proposed a preliminary phylogenetic framework for Cephalaspidea using few sanger sequenced phylogenetic markers and transcriptome‐scale datasets. However, relationships among several lineages remain contentious, which may partly reflect sparse sampling of key taxa and differences in topological signal among markers, datasets and analytical assumptions. To clarify the phylogenetic
institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Development of a city level nitrogen dioxide exposure (CLeNE) intelligence platform for West Africa
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major urban air pollutant, yet assessment of population exposure remains challenging across West Africa due to lack of uncoordinated sparse monitoring infrastructure. We present the City-Level Nitrogen Dioxide Exposure (CLeNE) platform, an interactive exposure intelligence system that integrates Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO 2 observations, population data, and city boundaries to quantify and visualize urban exposure burden. Population-weighted exposure (PWE) and a Normalized Population-Weighted Exposure Index (NPWEI) were developed to enable standardized compar
institutions: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology

title: Nanocomposite of TiO2 and Phase-transition-derived α-Fe2O3 for Enhancing Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
abstract: Although a-Fe2O3 is a promising photocatalyst for Advanced Oxidation Processes in dye-polluted wastewater treatment, its practical efficiency is limited by inherent drawbacks including rapid electron-hole recombination and poor electron mobility. This study proposes a TiO2/a-Fe2O3 nanocomposite system to enhance dye removal efficiency of a-Fe2O3, specifically Methylene Blue (MB), in which hierarchical porous, coral-like a-Fe2O3 was prepared via a thermal phase transition process from g-Fe2O3. X-ray diffraction analysis and peak deconvolution were used to confirm that the phase transition to a-
journal: VNU Journal of Science Mathematics - Physics
institutions: Ho Chi Minh City University of Science

title: Delineation of groundwater potential zones in Chalan Beel (inland wetland) for sustainable ecosystem in Lower Atrai River Basin NW Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in sustaining the ecological integrity and water security of the Chalan Beel, the largest inland wetland (5097 km2) in the Lower Atrai River Basin of northwestern Bangladesh. This study delineates groundwater potential zones (GWPZs) using an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach. Seventeen hydrogeological, topographic, climatic, and environmental thematic layers, including rainfall, soil type, soil permeability, groundwater level, aquifer depth, land use/land cover, geomorphology, d
institutions: Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: FECH negatively regulates protoporphyrin IX accumulation and shell coloration in the dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis
abstract: Shell color in mollusks, shaped by pigment synthesis and deposition, offers a readily observable natural trait. The dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis serves as an ideal bivalve model but has a uniform white shell, which limits its utility for genetic studies. In this study, we aimed to explore the feasibility of constructing a shell color‑based endogenous reporter by inducing pigment accumulation. Pigment feeding experiments showed that exogenous pigments, especially hemin, can efficiently accumulate in tissues ( p < 0.05) and induce visible changes in shell color. By screening the porphyrin m
institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry in Neurobiology: From Imaging to Proteomics
abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has emerged as a versatile approach for probing molecules with high selectivity and minimal perturbation. While applicable to diverse biomolecules, its use in protein studies has proven particularly powerful, especially in neurobiology, where precise molecular tools are essential. A key technology enabling such precision is genetic code expansion (GCE), which allows the incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAAs) bearing bioorthogonal handles into proteins. title: A new teleosauroid (Crocodylomorpha, Thalattosuchia) with a unique dentition from the Middle Jurassic of eastern Morocco
abstract: The Mesozoic and early Paleogene of Morocco provides a rich and extensive record of crocodylomorphs encompassing a wide range of skull, dental morphologies, and paleoecologies. Here we describe a new longirostrine teleosaurid thalattosuchian, Ctenosuchus tenuidens, gen. et sp. nov. with a needle-like dentition from a Middle Jurassic fluvio-lacustrine sequence of the Talsint–Anoual area of Figuig Province, southeastern Morocco. title: MONDE ·T: A database and interactive webserver for non‐standard amino acids and peptide components in the PDB
abstract: Non-standard amino acids (ncAAs) together with synthetic additions (like caps and linkers) are of wide interest for protein design and pharmaceutical optimization, as they can improve physicochemical properties and possibly reshape protein structure. Their inclusion in experimental structures has not been explored systematically. It remains elusive which components are those most impactful for protein design. We therefore collected all non-standard components present in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) into MONDE·T: A database of 1,210 unique ncAAs and 724 other synthetic components present in 23,1
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology

title: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi alleviate salinity stress in Avicennia marina through morphophysiological and biochemical modulation
abstract: Increasing salinity threatens coastal mangrove ecosystems worldwide by impairing plant growth, physiological function, and biochemical processes, ultimately reducing productivity and survival. The present study was conducted to examine the impact of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on Avicennia marina under different salt concentrations (9, 14, and 19 dS/m). This study included four treatments i.e. negative control (only salt: T1), species consortium of Glomus (T2), species consortium of Gigaspora (T3), consortium of both Glomus and Gigaspora spp. (T4) along with positive control (T0). The A

title: Vanishing Night Skies: An Ecological Perspective of India’s Rural - Urban Light Divide
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial light at night (ALAN) across India is increasingly transforming nocturnal environments with significant ecological consequences. This study investigates the rural–urban gradient of light pollution and its ecological implications by analyzing the spatial distribution and intensity of nighttime illumination across selected urban and rural regions of India. Nighttime radiance data derived from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) for 2024 were integrated with ground-based observations using a Sky Quality Meter (SQM) to evaluate variations in sky

title: Beyond Basic ICT Access: Pedagogical Integration of Geospatial Technologies in Geography Teaching in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Digital technology is now central to competence-based Geography education, yet access and pedagogical use remain uneven in Tanzanian public schools. This study examined how ICT integration supports Geography teaching and learning in Temeke Municipality. Its main objective was to assess whether available technology was being converted into subject-specific, learner-centred practice. A mixed-methods approach and cross-sectional survey design were used. The sample comprised 120 participants: 100 students, 16 Geography teachers, and four Ward Education Officers. Student and teacher questionnaires

title: Materialidades efímeras de las artes escénicas: el caso chileno-costarricense en la colección Huellas del exilio de Proyecto Arde y LaMAE
abstract: The purpose of this article is to analyze the theater posters and playbills that form part of Huellas del exilio collection, housed within the digital archives of Proyecto Arde in collaboration with LaMAE, and produced during the Chilean exile in Costa Rica. To this end, this study approaches these materials through the documentary typology of ephemera, investigating core axes related to: their participation within print culture, their modes of circulation and deployment across subjects and surfaces for public display, the forms of reading they elicit and their materiality. title: THERMAL COMFORT MAPPING OF PUBLIC SQUARES USING LANDSCAPE INTERVENTIONS
abstract: Rapid urbanization and rising temperatures had reduced the usability of public squares in tropical megacities, limiting their role as inclusive civic spaces. This study assessed outdoor thermal comfort and tested the effectiveness of landscape interventions in seven renowned public squares in Lagos, Nigeria: Tafawa Balewa Square, Muri Okunola Park, Freedom Park, JJT Park, Gani Fawehinmi Park, Iga Idunganran Palace Square, and Tinubu Square. A mixed methods approach was adopted, combining field climate measurements, pedestrian activity mapping, and microclimate simulation using ENVI-met and SOL
journal: International Journal of Environmental Design and Construction Management

title: Evaluating Carniolan honey bee (Apis mellifera carnica) lines under contrasting ecological zones
abstract: This study evaluates four breeding lines of the Carniolan honey bee, Apis mellifera carnica, across distinct ecological zones of Serbia and Montenegro. The objective was to assess phenotypic, morphometric, and isoenzyme polymorphism of local populations adapted to contrasting climatic and altitudinal conditions. Two Serbian lines (lowland Vršac and mountainous Vranje) and two Montenegrin lines (mountainous Bijelo Polje and coastal Sutomore) were examined. The material consisted of worker bees and queens from 40 honey bee colonies. Analyses included colony strength, brood development, honey and

title: Synergistic Co‐Fermentation of Ulva and Waste Activated Sludge for Sustainable Resource Recovery: Mechanistic Insights From Dissolved Organic Matter Transformation and Multi‐Omics Analysis
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation for volatile fatty acids (VFAs) production represents the sustainable and resource-recovery strategy for waste activated sludge (WAS) treatment, yet its efficiency is often hampered by low substrate C/N ratio and limited hydrolysis. Ulva, a macroalga responsible for extensive "green tides" that burden coastal ecosystems and economies, emerges as an ideal co-substrate for WAS anaerobic fermentation due to its high C/N ratio and biodegradability. This study established a novel Ulva-WAS co-fermentation system to boost VFAs production and explained the mechanism of acidogeni
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Experimental investigation of transient bed shear stress and scour formation at seawalls under tsunami bore impact using particle image velocimetry (PIV)
abstract: Abstract Tsunami bores generate short-duration, highly turbulent flows that impose intense bed shear stress on coastal structures, often leading to toe scour and structural instability. This study experimentally examines the transient evolution of bed shear stress and scour formation at four seawall geometries (box, curve, slope, and step types) using a dam-break wave testing facility and high-resolution Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). Controlled bores with initial reservoir depths ( H = 13, 15, 17 cm) propagated over a movable bed of 1 mm glass beads for scour experiments. PIV measurements
institutions: Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University

title: Assessment of Flood Risks on Power Infrastructure and Renewable Energy Installations in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: This research evaluated the flood hazards that impact power systems and renewable energy setups in the Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area (ONELGA) located in Rivers State, Nigeria. The primary goals included investigating how vulnerable energy infrastructure is to factors such as flood depth, speed, and duration; studying the vital interconnections between energy networks and other crucial services including water provision, healthcare, and transport; and calculating the economic damage and downtime caused by flood effects. A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was used alongside ca
journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025
abstract: Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. We performed whole-genome sequencing of 51 isolates and investigated their phylogenetic relationships. Phylogenetic analyses identified nine distinct genotypes, designated Kor24-25A to Kor24-25I. title: GNSS navigation interference disrupts telemetry tracking of raptors migrating between Europe and Africa
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference in war conflict zones can disrupt wildlife tracking for research and conservation efforts. In 2023 and 2024, we tagged Black Kites Milvis migrans in Moldova and Kazakhstan, respectively, with telemetry loggers, tracked them until September 2025 and found that 20 out of the 24 Black Kites had interfered (erroneous) geographical position fixes. title: Sympatric pikas partition microhabitats differently across a spatial-elevational gradient
abstract: Abstract How closely related, ecologically similar species co-occur and navigate competition remains a central question in community ecology. Microhabitat partitioning in patchy environments can support the co-existence of sympatric species on small spatial scales. We quantified niche spaces and directional niche overlaps of three cold-adapted, high-altitude pikas (Ochotona spp.) from the Trans-Himalayas to understand their responses to interspecific competition across elevational and spatial scales. Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment

title: Durability of TiAlCrN coated Ti6Al4V in saline and acidic media via multiphase analysis of passive film stability
abstract: Ti 6 Al 4 V components in aerospace and marine applications frequently suffer from coupled mechanical wear and corrosive degradation across severe temperature regimes. While TiAlN-based systems offer good wear resistance, tailoring Cr incorporation to concurrently enhance passivity without triggering microstructural embrittlement remains underexplored. Here, we test the hypothesis that precisely balancing the Cr/Al ratio governs the transition between dense passivation and defective oxide growth. Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: Facade and Opening Design Strategies for Enhancing Natural Lighting Efficiency in Classrooms at SD Labschool UPI
abstract: Natural lighting is an essential aspect of elementary school building design, as it significantly influences visual comfort and learning effectiveness. However, many classrooms in Indonesia do not meet the minimum illuminance standard of 350 lux specified in SNI 03-6197-2020. This study aims to evaluate and optimize facade and opening design strategies to improve the performance of natural lighting at SD Labschool UPI. The research employed daylight simulations using VELUX Daylight Visualizer on two building floors without the assistance of artificial lighting to analyze light intensity and di

title: Public health emergencies in Jordan: appraising multi-agency preparedness
abstract: Jordan faces a complex landscape of public health threats arising from infectious disease outbreaks, environmental hazards, technological incidents, humanitarian crises, and regional instability. These risks place sustained pressure on national institutions responsible for preparedness, response, and resilience. While multiple governmental and non-governmental agencies contribute to public health emergency preparedness and response (PHEPR), coordination gaps, overlapping mandates, and fragmented governance structures continue to challenge the effectiveness of a unified national response. title: Red Fluorescent Labeling of Myelin by Membrane‐Targeted tdTomato in Transgenic Mouse Lines
abstract: ABSTRACT Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin. Combining structural with functional imaging requires labeling of myelin with red fluorescence, as many functional sensors, including Ca 2+ indicators and genetically encoded metabolite sensors, fluoresce in the green spectral range. title: Untargeted metabolomic profiling of sweet potato latent virus infected Nicotiana benthamiana
abstract: Viral diseases, the second most significant biotic stress, cause substantial yield loss and quality deterioration in sweet potato, and sweet potato latent virus (SPLV) is one of the dominant viral pathogens infecting sweet potato in China. To investigate SPLV-induced metabolic changes, untargeted LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) was used on Nicotiana benthamiana inoculated with SPLV-infected sweet potato leaf sap. Principal component analysis (PCA) and orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) confirmed distinct metabolite profiles between infected and moc
institutions: Linyi Vocational University of Science and Technology

title: Cyanobacterial blooms at Canadian freshwater beaches: A prospective cohort study of exposure, health outcomes, and One Health implications
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms are an emerging One Health concern in freshwater environments, yet limited evidence exists on how humans and companion animals interact with bloom-prone waters or how these exposures align with water-quality indicators. This study characterizes recreational behaviours, environmental conditions, and illness patterns across multiple Canadian beaches to inform integrated monitoring and risk-management approaches. A prospective cohort study was conducted at seven freshwater beaches in Manitoba, Nova Scotia, and Ontario during the 2024 and 2025 summer seasons. Participants com
institutions: Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks

title: Northern movements of European Nathusius’ pipistrelle bats ( Pipistrellus nathusii ) before autumn migration
abstract: Despite decades of protecting migrating animals by international treaties, conservation efforts are severely hampered by our limited understanding of large-scale seasonal movements, particularly in cryptic migratory animals like bats. Banding data from a field site on the Latvian coast of the Baltic Sea suggests that some European Nathusius’ bats (Pipistrellus nathusii) move > 2000 km to their wintering range in Spain and France.
