journal: Isotopes in Environmental and Health Studies
institutions: Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Wildlife Research
Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies

title: Institutional Adoption and Economic Feasibility of Rainwater Harvesting in Existing University Buildings: A Review
abstract: Rainwater harvesting in existing university buildings requires an appraisal that connects institutional priorities, feasible retrofits and financial consequences. Selected reviews address system design, research trends and implementation barriers, providing a basis for examining how these considerations inform successive appraisal decisions. This critical narrative review develops a conceptual framework for Chinese universities through thematic synthesis of selected reviews and primary studies. title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. title: Flow Development and Performance Characteristics of an Axisymmetric Dual-bell Nozzle under Varying Nozzle Pressure Ratio Conditions
abstract: Dual-bell nozzles (DBNs) provide passive altitude compensation by adapting their effective expansion ratio through controlled flow separation and reattachment. In this study, the flow-regime evolution of an axisymmetric DBN is investigated numerically over a nozzle pressure ratio (NPR) range from 10 to 100. The nozzle geometry was generated using an in-house Method of Characteristics (MoC) design procedure combined with a constant-pressure extension contour. title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Water Footprint in Industry: Global Research Trends and Mapping of Scientific Networks
abstract: This study aims to reveal the development and intellectual structure of global scientific production on the Water Footprint (WF) in industry through bibliometric methods. A total of 3,052 research and review articles published up to 22.12.2025 and indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection database were included in the analysis. Publication trends, citation performance, and scientific collaboration structures were evaluated using performance analysis and science mapping approaches. title: Land of opportunity? Settling and social organization of the early Corded Ware groups in Central Jutland, Denmark
abstract: The breakthrough of aDNA research during the mid-2010s fundamentally shifted the dominant focus of research on the Corded Ware period in Europe, redirecting attention to questions about migration and the interdisciplinary integration of new and older approaches. Since then, the debate on migration in European prehistory has developed significantly, but previously central questions about aspects of social organization such as social stratification and gender roles during the Corded Ware period have yet to be fully reintegrated with recent aDNA-influenced perspectives. title: How Visual Resources Support Reading Comprehension: A Multimodal Analysis of English for Nusantara for Grade VIII
abstract: This study examines how visual resources accompanying reading materials in English for Nusantara for Grade VIII may support reading comprehension. A qualitative textbook content analysis was conducted on all 18 explicit Reading and Your Turn: Reading sections in Chapters 1-5. Meaningful visuals were defined as images or visual compositions that contributed information, organization, genre cues, or task meaning beyond decoration. journal: ELS Journal on Interdisciplinary Studies in Humanities

title: Compound and cascading climate risks in urban infrastructure governance and resilience across North America
abstract: North American cities are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards that do not occur in isolation. Extreme heat, drought, flooding, hurricanes, wildfires, wildfire smoke, and sea-level rise interact with aging infrastructure, uneven urbanization, social vulnerability, and fragmented governance systems. As a result, an initial climate shock can trigger cascading failures across energy, water, transport, telecommunications, housing, health, and emergency response systems. title: Flashy Neighbours: Psilocladus mantilleri Zeballos, Nunes, Silveira & Rosa, sp. nov., the First Termitariophile Firefly Larva (Coleoptera: Lampyridae)
abstract: ABSTRACT Fireflies are semelparous beetles whose immature stages are largely unknown. The comparatively few larvae known span diverse ecological niches, such as ground‐dwellers, aquatic (freshwater or marine), semi‐aquatic and arboreal. Psilocladus costae Vaz, Silveira & Rosa, 2020—a bromeliad dweller—is the only species of its genus and subfamily in which immature stages were studied. We collected firefly larvae in the Brazilian Cerrado inside termite nests and in the underground vaults surrounding them. institutions: Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas da Amazônia

title: Integrating Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Landuse/Land Cover Changes and Urban Growth in Modelling Surface Temperature Variations of Asaba Metropolis, Delta State
abstract: Rapid urbanization and land use/land cover (LULC) change have significantly altered urban thermal environments, intensifying urban heat island effects and increasing climate-related risks in developing cities. This study investigates the spatio-temporal relationship between LULC dynamics, urban growth, and land surface temperature (LST) in Asaba Metropolis, Delta State, Nigeria, over a 20-year period (2002–2022). title: Improving on the spatial location of geostationary satellite-derived FRP by accounting for parallax effect
abstract: When a satellite observes the Earth at an angle, the apparent position of elevated features, such as mountains, clouds or fires in high terrain, can be shifted from their true ground location. This effect, which may be particularly pronounced in the case of geostationary platforms providing observations under systematically high viewing angles in many places, is known as parallax displacement and becomes larger as terrain elevation and satellite viewing angle increase.Meteosat satellites operated by EUMETSAT provide frequent near-real-time observations that are essential for wildfire detection

title: Morphodynamic response to extreme basin flooding and its mechanism in a tide-dominant estuary
abstract: Extreme basin floods can strongly reshape tide-dominated estuaries, but their effects are often conditioned by antecedent channel geometry and human-induced river-bed incision. Here, we investigated the annual-scale morphodynamic response of the North Branch of the Changjiang (Yangtze) Estuary to the 2020 extreme basin flood using hydrological records, bathymetric surveys, surficial sediment samples, and Delft3D scenario experiments. journal: Engineering Applications of Computational Fluid Mechanics

title: Differences between PM2.5 chemical sources at semi-closed transport environments: comparing bus depots and metro platforms
abstract: Chemical composition and source contributions of PM 2.5 were investigated at a public-restricted bus depot in Valladolid (Spain) and two metro stations (Alto dos Moinhos and Quinta das Conchas) in Lisbon (Portugal) using positive matrix factorization (PMF). Locally derived sources dominated PM 2.5 in both environments, with OC-rich combustion emissions prevailing at the bus depot and Fe-rich wear processes at the metro stations as major components. institutions: Institute of Environmental Assessment and Water Research

title: Polycentric governance of cruise environmental impacts
abstract: Rapidly growing cruise ship tourism in northern regions has been a double-edged phenomenon, bringing monetary benefits to otherwise limited economic futures but also undesirable environmental impacts such as air pollution, wastewater discharge, and noise. This paper examines responses from five northern communities to these challenges, using a polycentric governance lens characterized by multilevel and overlapping decision-making centers. This study adds to a growing body of empirical research on how polycentricity is practiced, finding that affected communities display a variety of institutio
journal: Annals of Tourism Research Empirical Insights

title: Precursor-controlled PFAS contamination profiles in tropical nearshore sediments: dominance of hydrogen-substituted PFCAs and transformation evidence from Sanya, China
abstract: The environmental behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in tropical nearshore sediments remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to the contamination characteristics of emerging PFAS and precursor-related compounds. In this study, surface sediments from the tropical nearshore waters of Sanya, China, were investigated, and 46 PFAS, including legacy, emerging, and precursor PFAS, were systematically analyzed. title: Key Drivers in the Development of the Green Economy in the Gulf and Levant States
abstract: This study identifies the main factors and trends in green economy development across the Gulf and Levant countries and examines their spatial patterns. The environmentally significant processes observed in these countries suggest the possible, though not predetermined, onset of a long-term transition toward more sustainable economies. However, it remains too early to conclude that a genuine transition toward decarbonization is underway. title: Genotyping by Sequencing (GBS) uncovers genetic diversity and population structure for salicornia breeding programs in Iran
abstract: Salicornia, a succulent halophyte flourishing in coastal and mangrove ecosystems, holds significant economic and ecological promise. Establishing sustainable cultivation systems requires a profound understanding of its geographical distribution, genetic potential, and the identification of agronomically superior populations. Despite this potential, comprehensive genomic investigations into the genus remain scarce. title: Same hospital, same price, different protection: out-of-pocket expenditure for emergency trauma under public insurance, private insurance and self-payment in India
abstract: Background Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) finances 43.4% of total health expenditure in India, and emergency trauma—unforeseeable, unpostponable and costly—is among the sharpest tests of whether a health-financing mechanism protects households from catastrophic spending. Insured and uninsured patients are normally treated in different facilities at different tariffs, confounding the effect of the payment mechanism with the setting in which care is given. title: Selenium/Zinc nanocomposite (Se/Zn NC) bioengineered by Bacillus rugosus metabolites: physicochemical characterization, anti-inflammatory, and antidiabetic activities
abstract: This study reports the biosynthesis of a Selenium/Zinc nanocomposite (Se/Zn NC) using a marine bacterial extract from Bacillus rugosus SYG20. FT-IR detected Zn–O stretching vibrations at 614.81, 500.71, and 463.61 cm⁻¹, together with shifts in biomolecule peaks. title: COMPUTER MODELING OF ADHESION AND TRACTION FORCESOF A SHIP MOBILE ROBOT
abstract: The article addresses the scientific and practical problem of developing a computer simulation model of a ship mobile robot (SMR) to further automate maintenance processes for ships and port infrastructure facilities (pipelines, storage tanks, floating docks). Based on a review of existing solutions, the advantages of all-wheel drive wheeled platforms over tracked and legged counterparts in terms of manoeuvrability and energy efficiency are substantiated. title: Mitochondrial and retroviral markers reveal high genetic diversity and regional structure in the Lebanese Awassi sheep
abstract: Abstract The Awassi is a native sheep breed of Lebanon with high historical and economic value. Despite its importance, its genetic background has not been characterized, leaving limited understanding of its origins, diversity, and regional connections. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity and population structure of Awassi sheep from Lebanon and neighboring Syria using two complementary genetic systems that trace distinct evolutionary histories: maternal mitochondrial DNA and insertional polymorphisms of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retroviruses. title: Morphological Characteristics, Surface Circulation, and Physicochemical Properties of the Ébrié Lagoon in the Grand-Bassam Area (Côte d’Ivoire)
abstract: The Ébrié Lagoon, in the Grand-Bassam area, is exposed to various anthropogenic pressures that may alter is morphological and environnemental charactéristics. This study aims to characterize the morphobathymetric and hydrodynamic structures of this lagoon sector and to assess its physicochemical status. Bathymetric surveys provided 18,474 depth measurements, ranging from 0 to 19 m, over an area of approximately 42 ha. title: Long-term preservation of early-formed silicate reservoirs in the deep mantle: New insight from 146Sm-142Nd systematics in Hawaiian basalts
abstract: Short-lived radiogenic isotope systems provide unique constraints on the preservation of early-formed reservoirs in Earth's mantle. We present the largest high-precision μ 142 Nd dataset for a single hotspot, comprising 55 analyses of 29 shield-stage tholeiitic basalts from the Hawaiian Islands. Samples span the full geochemical range of the Loa and Kea trends and were analyzed using multiple chemical purification procedures and thermal ionization mass spectrometry to assess analytical reproducibility. title: Decoupling stress-corrosion-hydrogen interactions in Mg-Zn-Ca-Sn alloys: Achieving enhanced stress corrosion cracking resistance via Ga/In alloying
abstract: Despite recent advancements in corrosion resistance, magnesium (Mg) alloys still face significant challenges in structural applications due to their susceptibility to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) under combined mechanical stress and corrosive environments. The underlying mechanisms of SCC, particularly the interplay between stress, corrosion, and hydrogen, remain insufficiently understood, impeding the development of effective mitigation strategies. title: Renoprotective effects of dapagliflozin and montelukast for diclofenac induced acute kidney injury through network pharmacology and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract Diclofenac (DIC)-prompted acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated autophagy, all of which contribute to renal impairment. Using a network pharmacology approach followed by experimental validation, this study evaluated the reno-protecting actions of dapagliflozin (DAPA) and montelukast (MON) against DIC-induced AKI in rats, both alone and in combination. title: Coating-Free Low-Voltage Scanning Electron Microscopy for Native-Surface Imaging across Scale, Depth, and Time

Understanding such materials therefore requires one to observe them in their native states before imaging alters their structures. title: Shifting Dominant Air Pollution Sources in Sub-Saharan Africa’s Changing Urban Environment: Analysis of Elemental Composition and Source Contributions of Ambient Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Pollution in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Abstract Urban and economic expansion across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) may be shifting the relative contributions of dominant ambient air pollution sources, influencing both pollutant concentrations and composition, along with their associated health risks. However, city-scale data on the composition and source contributions are scarce, hindering source- and sector-specific policy interventions. Using samples from a large-scale, citywide monitoring campaign, we characterized the elemental composition and source contributions of PM2.5 pollution across the Accra metropolis, a major SSA city. title: Análisis por HPLC y capacidad antioxidante in vitro del extracto acuoso de Desmodium molliculum (Kunth) DC de Ayacucho
abstract: Background Desmodium molliculum is an Andean medicinal plant traditionally used for various ailments, whose chemical composition and antioxidant activity require investigation. To determine the phytochemical profile using high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection (HPLC-DAD) and to evaluate the antioxidant activity of the aqueous extract of D. molliculum from Ayacucho, Peru. Methods Plant material was collected in Pansa, Ayacucho (2,524 m above sea level). The aqueous extract was obtained by decoction and concentration. title: Distribution and life-history of spurdog (Squalus acanthias) along the Norwegian coast inferred from a five-year fishery-independent longline survey
abstract: Abstract Northeast Atlantic spurdog ( Squalus acanthias ) has recently shown signs of recovery from overfishing following international conservation measures. As the fishery slowly reopens, ensuring its sustainable long-term trajectory will require an understanding of its contemporary population structure, habitat use, and life-history traits across its distribution range. title: The Feral Life of Plastic Waste: Third Nature and Speculative Aesthetics
abstract: This article explores the interactions between plastic waste and non-human animals from a non-anthropocentric and future-oriented perspective. After a first introductory section, I argue for a plane of analogy connecting animals and plastics. If extended into the future, this plane of analogy shows a new feature: ferality. Contra Hegel, Heidegger, and some contemporary scholars, I contend in the third section that ferality cannot be framed as a regression of “second nature” (human culture) to “first nature” (non-human nature), but should be understood as post-domestic “third nature”. title: Evaluation of micro-litter pollution in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus Koehler, 1906 at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands)
abstract: Micro-litter (ML) pollution is increasingly being reported in Antarctic benthic ecosystems and the organisms inhabiting them. In this study, we assessed ML abundance and characteristics in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands), an area with significant human presence. Additionally, we considered the potential influence of local factors, including proximity to research stations and the bay entrance, as well as depth (5 and 15 m), on ML pollution. title: All Different All Equal: High Polymorphism in Nebela (Amoebozoa: Arcellinida) Revealed by Additional Sampling and Barcoding
abstract: Hyalospheniids are a conspicuous group of testate amoebae whose rich morphology has allowed their classification based on the characterization of their shells. However, recent studies showed the occurrence of convergences and phenotypic plasticity, which complicate their taxonomy. Molecular barcoding is the method of choice to resolve this diversity in an objective manner and accurately delineate species. title: Environmental factors associated with abundance and bioindicator potential of Australomicrodeutopus in tropical brackish water ponds

title: Improved geoid models for the state of São Paulo using the SHGeo package
abstract: Abstract The objective of this paper is to present the effort to establish the geoidal model for the state of São Paulo to be used for mapping purposes by the Instituto Geográfico e Cartográfico do Estado de São Paulo (IGC). This model is limited by 26ºS and 19ºS latitude and 54ºW and 44ºW longitude. The Stokes-Helmert geoid software (SHGeo) from the University of New Brunswick (UNB), Canada, was used. title: Relative Abundance, Length-Weight Relationship and Condition Factor of Bostrychus Africanus And Periophthalmus Barbarus From Bomu and Kono Creeks, Rivers State
abstract: This study investigated selected aspects of the ecology of two gobiid fishes, Bostrychus africanus and Periophthalmus barbarus, inhabiting Bomu and Kono Creeks, Rivers State, Nigeria. Fish specimens were collected from the intesrtidal mudflats using basket traps between May 2023 and April 2024. The specimens were assessed for relative abundance, length–weight relationship (LWR), and condition factor (CF) following standard fisheries research procedures. journal: JOURNAL OF BIOLOGY AND GENETIC RESEARCH

title: Post-wildfire changes to water quality: a review with implications for harmful algal blooms and reservoir resiliency
abstract: Abstract Wildfires wreak havoc on both urban and natural ecosystems and are expected to worsen under future climate conditions. Wildfires have the potential for long-term impacts on the health of downstream reservoirs. This study seeks to compile current literature worldwide regarding impacts of wildfires on reservoir water quality, with a special focus on the implications for harmful algal blooms. title: Modulation of precession-forced Asian–African monsoon and arid climate variability by obliquity
abstract: Precession and obliquity play vital roles in orbital-scale climate change. However, their combined effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine how obliquity modulates precession-driven climate responses across Asian–African monsoon and arid regions (AAMAR). Results demonstrate that under high obliquity, the minimum-precession-induced precipitation increase is weakened in the Asian–African monsoon regions but enhanced in the Asian–African arid regions. title: Bioaccumulation, food web transfer, and tissue distribution of polonium-210 and lead-210 in Canadian freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Understanding the bioaccumulation and trophic transfer of naturally occurring radionuclides is essential for assessing ecological risk in freshwater systems. This study provides a large-scale assessment of polonium-210 ( 210 Po) and lead-210 ( 210 Pb) bioaccumulation, trophic transfer and tissue-specific biodistribution in freshwater food webs across Canada. Activity concentrations were measured in water and biota samples collected from multiple ecozones and land-use settings. title: Depth and inter-annual variation of crustacean diversity within Ecklonia maxima holdfast communities in the Benguela-Agulhas transition zone of the South African coast
abstract: Abstract Kelp holdfasts form complex, three-dimensional biogenic habitats that support diverse macroinvertebrate assemblages, yet the crustacean fauna within these structures which are an important contributors to secondary production and trophic transfer in kelp forest food webs remains poorly quantified. We characterised crustacean assemblages associated with holdfasts of the kelp Ecklonia maxima at Miller’s Point, False Bay, South Africa, to test for effects of depth and interannual variation. title: Proteomic insights into the antifouling molecular responses of nature-inspired gallic and bile acid derivatives in Mytilus galloprovincialis
abstract: Nature-inspired compounds are increasingly recognized as promising sources of effective and environmentally safer antifouling (AF) agents. However, the development of new AF solutions under current regulatory frameworks requires a better understanding of the biological responses associated with their activity. Previous studies identified two synthetic derivatives of gallic and bile acids, 2-(3,4,5-trihydroxybenzamido)ethan-1-aminium bromide ( 1 ) and methyl deoxycholate ( 2 ), as potent inhibitors of Mytilus galloprovincialis larval settlement, a prominent biofouling species. title: Pine trees, wind and limestone degradation, South Florida, USA
abstract: Exposed limestone is subject to numerous pedogenic processes, many which cause surface degradation. The uprooting of windthrown trees is a major pedogenic process, as demonstrated in South Florida pine forests. The effects of Hurricane Andrew’s winds on two forest stands are documented; the Pine Island forest is rooted in exposed level Late Pleistocene limestone bedrock, and Lostman’s Pines in quartz sand overlying the level mid-Pliocene limestone bedrock. title: Hospital wastewater as a significant source of microplastics in Northern Iran: Abundance, polymer composition, and environmental risk assessment
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants increasingly detected in aquatic environments and wastewater systems, raising concerns regarding ecosystem and human health. Hospital wastewater has been identified as a source of MPs entering municipal systems; however, data on their occurrence, characteristics, and associated risks remain limited. This study aimed to characterize MP contamination in hospital wastewater and assess the associated environmental and health risks. abstract: La producción solar de sal depende de algo elemental y, a la vez, difícil de aislar: clima, agua marina y conectividad hidrológica. title: Non-exchangeable K sustains plant K uptake in alkaline Mediterranean soils
abstract: Abstract Aims Potassium (K) fertilization recommendations commonly rely on exchangeable-K soil tests, assuming that this fraction represents the soil’s capacity to supply plant-available K. However, limited crop response to K fertilization at insufficient exchangeable-K concentrations suggests contributions from additional soil K reservoirs. This study aims to quantify the contribution of non-exchangeable K pools to plant uptake in Mediterranean alkaline soils with differing mineralogical composition, under intensive agricultural conditions. title: Climate mediates land-use and within-lake drivers of seston stoichiometry: a large-scale assessment across tropical shallow lakes
abstract: Abstract Seston stoichiometry links nutrient availability to the structure and functioning of aquatic food webs, yet how in-lake conditions interact with broader climatic, geomorphological and land-use drivers to shape seston carbon-to-phosphorus (C:P) ratios remains poorly understood in tropical systems. We used regression tree analysis (RTA) to evaluate the relative importance of in-lake, lake–catchment and climate variables in explaining seston C:P variation across 95 shallow lakes and reservoirs spanning a semi-arid-to-humid climatic gradient in northeastern Brazil. title: Organic Matter Preservation and Hydrocarbon Potential of Microbialites: Insights From TOC Reconstruction in the Leikoupo and Dengying Formations, Sichuan Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Microbialites vary widely in organic matter abundance and preservation, making their hydrocarbon‐generating potential uncertain. Here, we compare microbialites from two contrasting depositional settings in the northwestern Sichuan Basin: the Middle Triassic Leikoupo Formation, deposited on a restricted evaporitic carbonate platform, and the late Ediacaran Dengying Formation, deposited on a relatively open shallow‐water carbonate platform. title: Evidence for cortisol production in a shark
abstract: Corticosteroids are essential regulators of numerous physiological functions in vertebrates, including energy balance, immune responses, osmotic balance and metabolism. The terminal corticosteroids are highly conserved across jawed vertebrates, where cortisol or corticosterone mediates these physiological responses. Elasmobranchs, however, have a unique dominant circulating steroid, 1⍺-hydroxycorticosterone, and since its discovery it has been presumed that elasmobranchs do not produce cortisol. title: Molecular identification of a fin whale stranded in Veracruz, southern Gulf of Mexico
abstract: Baleen whale strandings are rare in the southern Gulf of Mexico and can provide valuable molecular information where species are infrequently documented. We analyzed tissue from a highly decomposed whale stranded on the central coast of Veracruz, Mexico, by amplifying and bidirectionally sequencing the mitochondrial DNA control region. title: Ontogenetic changes in phototactic behavior of Pacific bluefin tuna (Thunnus orientalis) larvae and juveniles
abstract: In this study, to elucidate the development of visual function in Pacific bluefin tuna (PBT; Thunnus orientalis ), we analyzed ontogenetic changes in the expression of visual opsin genes from hatching through the juvenile stage and evaluated wavelength- and intensity-dependent photobehavior using projected light. RT-PCR analysis detected transcripts for all opsin genes except RH2A2, a green-sensitive RH2 opsin subtype, in larvae from the yolk-sac stage (1 day post-hatching; dph) onward. title: Progressive oxidative weathering raised sub-arc mantle fugacity on the Archaean Earth
abstract: Abstract In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. title: Tribological performance of PTFE/polyimide pulp/GCNT composites
abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant but suffers from poor wear resistance, limiting its application in demanding mechanical components. In this study, PTFE-based composites reinforced with polyimide (PI) pulp and graphitized carbon nanotubes (GCNTs) were prepared via a cold-press sintering process. The tribological properties were evaluated under different loads (2 N and 10 N) and frequencies (1 Hz and 4 Hz) using a ball-on-disk tribometer. title: Thermal Oxidation Increases Dissolved Carbon Leaching through Altered Microplastic Structural Chemistry and Accelerated Release Kinetics
abstract: Abstract We assessed the leaching potential of dissolved carbon (DC) from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics (MPs), selected for their differing polymeric structure and response to thermal oxidation. Although thermal oxidation alters the chemical structure and reactivity of MPs, the mechanisms influencing DC leaching remain poorly understood. title: Manta ray injury affects cleaner attraction, while cleaning behaviours reflect cleaner number
abstract: Abstract Cleaning mutualisms provide a useful framework for examining how cooperation and conflict are regulated, yet the extent to which client condition influences these dynamics remains unclear. We tested whether reef manta ray (Mobula alfredi) injury status is associated with cleaner engagement and behavioural dynamics at a cleaning station in the Philippines. title: Toxicological impacts of sulfamethoxazole on freshwater organisms – toxicity and oxidative stress
abstract: The continuous expansion of the pharmaceutical sector has intensified aquatic contamination, as persistent active compounds enter water bodies through urban, industrial, and agricultural runoff. Among these contaminants, sulfamethoxazole (SMX)—a widely used sulphonamide antibiotic—raises ecological concerns due to its persistence and potential for bioaccumulation. title: The Role of Environmental Policy in Preventing Oil Spillage: Balancing Energy Development and Agricultural Sustainability
abstract: Oil spillage poses profound threats to ecosystems and agricultural systems, particularly in regions where energy extraction coexists with farming communities. This comprehensive review explores how environmental policies mitigate spill risks, drawing on international conventions, national regulations, and case studies from Nigeria, the United States, Ecuador, and Norway. It analyzes policy mechanisms for prevention, enforcement challenges, and strategies for harmonizing energy development with agricultural sustainability. title: The overlooked role of food and cultural dimensions in recreational fisheries
abstract: Our study examines the diversity of values within a superficially homogeneous recreational fishery and its relationship to angler diversity. We collected data on fishing preferences, behaviors, catch usage, and sociodemographics from 443 shore anglers across 10 cities in the lower Great Lakes. We identified five coherent dimensions, including food, cultural, leisure, challenge/performance, and social-financial centrality, consistent with multidimensional value structuring in recreational fisheries. abstract: Archaeological shell remains are widely used to reconstruct littoral ecology and human foraging behavior at sites throughout the world, yet most models generally assume that shells are harvested and either consumed, or processed, at or near the shoreline. We present the results of estimated size measurements on California mussels (Mytilus californianus) from 1591 hinges and 210 whole shells recovered from CA-SBA-1010, California, USA, an archaeological site located over 13 km inland from the nearest rocky intertidal habitat to evaluate how assemblage-specific regression models can be used to i

title: Radiogenic isotope variability in contemporary mineral dust across the intermountain west of the United States
abstract: Mineral dust is a highly mobile component of Earth’s Critical Zone that influences ecosystem function, soil development, biogeochemical cycling, and environmental archives. Radiogenic isotopes provide a powerful means of characterizing dust because isotope ratios largely preserve source signatures during atmospheric transport. title: Geomagnetic instability as a potential deep-Earth forcing factor in the Permian environmental and biotic crisis
abstract: Abstract The Permian witnessed profound geomagnetic, environmental, and biotic upheavals, yet high-resolution paleomagnetic constraints across critical transitions remain sparse. Here, we present a 3.75-million-year magnetostratigraphic record from the Fengshan section (South China) spanning the Guadalupian-Lopingian transition (262.5-258.75 Ma). title: Microplastic Pollution in a Small River with an Agriculture-dominated Catchment under Different Rainfall Conditions: Transport Scaling, Characteristics and Ecological Risk Assessment
abstract: The agriculture cluster is recognized as a cryptic hotspot of microplastic pollution. Especially, rainfall-driven microplastic (MP) dynamics in small agricultural rivers have not been adequately quantified under various hydrological conditions. This study quantified MP concentrations, loads, characteristics, and ecological risks under baseline dry conditions and during four rainfall events of varying intensities in a small agricultural river. title: Application of Professional Ethics Principles and Prevention through Design (PtD) in Power Plant Layout Based on Site Investigation
abstract: The feasibility study (FS) is an early phase that largely determines the success of a power plant development project, in which the plant layout is one of the key decisions affecting technical, safety, cost, construction, and operational aspects. This study analyzes the application of Prevention through Design (PtD) in developing the layout of the Java Bali 2 Combined Cycle Power Plant (PLTGU) by using Site Investigation (SI) results. abstract: Abstract. Inter-array grid optimisation plays a critical role in the technical and economic performance of wind parks and is typically divided into two primary tasks: layout length minimisation and conductor size selection. This work proposes the consideration of three primary tasks, beginning with graph preparation to account for terrain profiles, soft and hard exclusion zones, and export cables. title: Public Perception of Geodiversity in Ubatuba, Brazil: A Step for Geoscience Communication and Geoconservation
abstract: Abstract Understanding public perceptions is essential for planning effective communication strategies to promote geoconservation. However, existing literature often oversimplifies this task, focusing mainly on socioeconomic data and scientific knowledge, while neglecting the influence of numerous other factors that shape perception. title: Non-destructive GARField NMR profiling to characterize release from opaque antifouling coatings
abstract: In this work, high-resolution one-dimensional (1D) 1 H NMR profiling is employed, enabling a novel non-destructive approach for characterization of release processes in optically opaque antifouling coatings. As a first case, the release of copper pyrithione (CuPy) from PDMS-based polymer networks is investigated. As the material releases, voids that fill with water are created, causing a detectable change in NMR signal. title: PENGARUH KESIAPAN TEKNOLOGI DAN KOMPETENSI DIGITAL SUMBER DAYA MANUSIA TERHADAP EFESIENSI OPERASIONAL PELABUHAN BELAWAN
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of technological readiness and human resource (HR) digital competence on operational efficiency at Belawan Port, specifically at the Primary Cooperative (Primkop) of Stevedoring Workers (TKBM) Upaya Karya. Digital transformation in the logistics sector demands alignment between technological infrastructure and user capabilities to achieve maximum operational efficiency. The method used is a quantitative associative causal research approach with purposive sampling techniques. From a total population of 3,883 workers, the sample size was set at 99 respondent
journal: JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND SOCIAL RESEARCH

title: Interfacial Salt Redistribution Enables Rapid Atmospheric Water Harvesting in a Biomimetic Multi‐Layer Hygroscopic Membrane
abstract: ABSTRACT Sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) offers a promising route for decentralized freshwater production, but practical water output is often limited by slow sorption kinetics in salt‐loaded hydrogel sorbents. Here, a biomimetic multi‐layer heterogeneous hygroscopic (MHH) membrane is developed to decouple vapor capture from bulk liquid storage. Inspired by the salt‐management strategy of Avicennia marina leaves, the membrane integrates an air‐accessible nanofiber interface with a brush‐like hydrogel reservoir. title: Foliar polystyrene nanoplastics modulate cadmium uptake and root-to-shoot translocation in hydroponic Spinacia oleracea L.: Time- and concentration-dependent responses
abstract: The accumulation of plastics and heavy metals (HMs) in the environment has become a significant global concern due to their persistence, ubiquity, and potential ecological impacts. Atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics (MP, NP) are capable of undergoing long-range transport and can be deposited onto plant shoots through precipitation, thereby exposing aerial plant tissues to these particulate contaminants. In this study, the effects of varying concentrations of polystyrene nanoplastics (PSNPs) (0, 10, 50, 100, 200, and 400 mg L-1), applied via foliar spraying, and cadmium (Cd) (0 and 5 mg L-1) w

title: Estimating the completeness of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects
abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. Despite the extensive efforts to profile various organs and their cellular compositions, we lack metrics to assess the completeness of the sequencing projects. title: Quantifying Pore-Throat Heterogeneity in Bioclastic Limestones Using Multifractal Analysis: Insights from the Upper Cretaceous Khasib Formation
abstract: Abstract The heterogeneity of carbonate reservoirs constitutes a critical control on fluid flow. Nevertheless, most previous studies rely on qualitative characterization and single-scale statistical methods, which hinder multiscale characterization of pore heterogeneity and localized preferential flow. Furthermore, few quantitative studies have systematically clarified the coupled mechanism of deposition, diagenesis, and reservoir heterogeneity. title: Design and hydrodynamic analysis of a new web-type mooring system
abstract: ”Y”-type branching is a common load-bearing topology in natural networks such as spider webs, where pretensioned radial and circumferential threads provide multiple load-transfer paths and enhance resistance to local damage. Inspired by this mechanism, this study proposes a taut web-type mooring layout for offshore floating platforms, with the main objective of redistributing mooring loads rather than significantly reducing platform motions. title: Wave-induced drift of pumice: transitions from forward to backward transport
abstract: Floating pumice rafts generated by eruptions of submarine volcanoes can be transported over large distances, yet the role of surface waves in controlling pumice drift remains poorly constrained. Wave-induced transport is often parameterized indirectly in numerical simulations despite limited experimental observations. Here we investigate the wave-induced drift of floating pumice using laboratory wave-tank experiments under controlled wave forcing. Natural pumice and analog cubes with characteristic sizes of 5–10 cm and a range of densities were subjected to regular waves with frequencies of 1.
institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: Trypethelium flavopigmentosum (lichenized Ascomycota: Trypetheliaceae), a new lichen species from Mt. Palhi, Dinagat Islands, Philippines
abstract: During our continued expeditions in the Dinagat Islands, southern Philippines, a new species, Trypethelium flavopigmentosum Taer & Aptroot, was discovered and is herein described. It closely resembles T. luteolucidum in the thallus and pseudostromata reacting UV+ yellow, the presence of lichexanthone, and the inspersed hamathecium. However, T. flavopigmentosum is distinguished by its prominent yellow pigment at the surface of the pseudostromata, inside with an additional yellow dusty granular pigment, and a smaller, 9–10-septate ascospore, 41–61 × 9–13 μm. title: Adaptive track control for unmanned surface vessels using model predictive control: accounting for water depth and speed variations
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is applied to track control of unmanned surface vessels. To adapt to dynamic changes in speed and water depth, a water depth and speed dependent predictive model, with coefficients identified from free running tests (e.g., acceleration and zigzag trials), is developed. The nonlinear least square method is used for parameter estimation of the model. Furthermore, a novel self-tuning method adapts MPC’s essential parameter, prediction horizon, to diverse operating conditions. Validation via manoeuvring simulations of the full-scale benchmark KVLCC2 ship covers under

institutions: HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts

title: Biomechanical analyses point to dense collagen fibre architecture in an Ediacaran frond
abstract: Ediacaran macrofossils record the earliest large and complex organisms on Earth. Despite extensive study, fundamental aspects of their internal anatomy and tissue composition remain poorly known, limiting understanding of how these organisms were constructed and functioned, as well as how their complex anatomies evolved. Here, we establish a new quantitative biomechanical framework to infer tissue properties in the Ediacaran frond Charniodiscus. Analyses of fossil morphology, numerical simulations and dimensional analysis indicate that the commonly preserved twisted forms reflect three-dimensi
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

title: Traveler's Palm ( Ravenala spp.) Across Habitats and Its Responses to Disturbance in North‐Eastern Madagascar
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Ravenala (Strelitziaceae) comprises six species of arborescent herbs endemic to Madagascar and iconic to this global biodiversity hotspot. We examined how Ravenala density responds to environmental gradients, land‐use type, accessibility and canopy disturbance. The study was conducted in north‐eastern Madagascar, a region heavily affected by deforestation in recent decades. We carried out species‐specific terrestrial sampling in different land‐use types (fallow land, vanilla agroforests and forest fragments) in human‐modified landscapes and in old‐growth forest. title: The cost of regulatory delay: quantifying how permitting timelines affect offshore wind energy costs
abstract: Abstract Rapid deployment of offshore renewable energy and transmission infrastructure can be a major contributor to energy system decarbonization. However, regulatory obligations frequently impose deployment delays that are typically not quantified in cost terms. The costs of such delays should be incorporated in project and technology assessments. Here, a framework is developed that treats the development lag between project inception and operation as a temporal proxy for regulatory and related obligations, and propagates it through a levelized-cost-of-energy calculation to quantify the cost

title: Optimisation of phase-dependent microalgal organic matter isolation and extraction methodology
abstract: Algal blooms are a global problem that lead to the formation of excessive algal organic matter, resulting in the deterioration of water sources and the disruption of water treatment processes. Methods for the extraction of algal organic matter from algal cells are time-consuming and sometimes ineffective in achieving cell lysis. This study aimed to optimise the extraction and characterisation of extracellular organic matter and intracellular organic matter from microalgae, as well as flow cytometry for assessment of microalgae population numbers and viability. title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. We show that plasma metabolic profiles exhibit distinct patterns associated with sex and age class ( n = 37). Sex is the dominant axis of variation, driving coordinated divergence across lipid

title: A recent doubling of global warming rate signals a 1.5 °C breach by 2028
abstract: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. Existing estimates place this exceedance in the early 2030 s but carry substantial uncertainty. Here we analyze the latest observational temperature records through 2025 and identify a statistically significant doubling of the global warming rate during 2011–2025 (0.40 °C per decade) compared to 1971–2025 (0.20 °C per decade). title: Persistent carcinogenic risk from PM2.5-bound metals despite substantial concentration reductions: Evidence from a Chinese megacity during the COVID-19 lockdown
abstract: Health benefits from emission controls are often inferred from reductions in fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) mass, yet this metric can underrepresent toxicity from PM 2.5 -bound metals. Using the COVID-19 lockdown as an intervention-like natural experiment, this study quantified how PM 2.5 -bound metals, emission sources, and inhalation health risks changed in Guangzhou, China. Hourly measurements of 16 metals were coupled with positive matrix factorization and source-specific risk apportionment for pre-lockdown, lockdown, and post-lockdown periods. title: Widespread Microplastic Burden in the Endemic Freshwater Fish Squalius pursakensis Sarısu Stream, Türkiye: Evidence of Chronic Environmental Pressure and One Health Implications
abstract: Abstract Microplastic (MP) pollution is increasingly recognized as a pervasive environmental stressor in freshwater ecosystems. This study evaluated the occurrence, characteristics, and ecological implications of MPs in the gastrointestinal tract of the endemic freshwater fish Squalius pursakensis from Sarısu Stream (Sakarya River Basin, Türkiye). MPs were detected in all examined individuals (n = 23), indicating a 100% prevalence. MP abundance ranged from 6 to 51 particles per individual, with a mean ± SD of 27.65 ± 11.49 MP/individual. title: Long-term peat thickness from cosmogenic 26 Al and 10 Be, Hautes Fagnes, Belgian Ardennes
abstract: Abstract. Upland peatlands are a major terrestrial carbon reservoir that may play an important role in the global carbon cycle. However, knowledge of upland peatlands before the Holocene remains speculative because of the poor long-term preservation potential of peat in upland environments. Here, we explore using paired 26Al and 10Be to simultaneously determine denudation rates and peat thicknesses averaged over multiple glacial-interglacial cycles. title: A histidine-mediated supramolecular mechanism links temperature and pH activation of the sperm channel CatSper
abstract: The cation channel of sperm, CatSper, is a sperm-specific calcium channel essential for male fertility across metazoans. CatSper is activated by intracellular alkalinization, membrane depolarization, and elevated temperature, which together ensure maximal current generation. However, the structural mechanisms by which these physiological stimuli jointly regulate channel activation remain poorly understood, in part because CatSper is an unusually complex ~15-subunit assembly organized in zigzag supramolecular arrays along the sperm flagellum. title: Synergistic microbiologically influenced corrosion of SLM TC4 by co-culture of Streptococcus mutans and Veillonella dispar
abstract: Abstract Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) is extensively utilized for oral implants due to its excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility. In the oral environment, microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) is typically driven by multispecies biofilms. Here, electrochemical, surface, and corrosion product analyses were used to investigate the MIC of selective laser melted (SLM) TC4 induced by mono- or dual-species biofilms of Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ) and Veillonella dispar ( V. dispar ). title: Clay minerals of modern alluvial deposits of the Indigirka River and its tributaries as indicators of depositional sources
abstract: To address the question of how the geological structure and composition of rocks in the Indigirka River basin influence the mineral composition of modern alluvial deposits, samples collected from the lower reaches of the river were analyzed. The composition of the samples was studied using X-ray diffraction analysis. Because of the similar mineralogical composition of the clastic component of the studied sediments, clay minerals were selected as indicators of changes in sediment sources. title: On the edge: habitat patchiness and island isolation fracture the distribution of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat
abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. Islands became isolated from ~6500 years before present (BP), with their current populations being considered relictual. title: Prediction and Model Validation of Corrosion Fatigue Life for BFRP Tendons Under Combined Acidic Environment and Temperature
abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread application of fiber‐reinforced polymers (FRP) in engineering is primarily attributed to their superior durability compared to traditional materials. However, under prolonged exposure to harsh service environments, the material inevitably undergoes progressive degradation. The existing durability studies and life prediction models have largely overlooked the synergistic effects of combined environmental actions and mechanical loading conditions. title: 16S rRNA amplicon profiling of Salvadora persica -associated rhizosphere bacterial communities under saline agricultural conditions
abstract: Salvadora persica (Arak) is a facultative halophyte adapted to arid and saline environments, yet its rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly characterised. We profiled bacterial communities associated with S. persica at Arak Farm, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3–V4 16S rRNA region and ASV-based analysis. Three rhizosphere composites and one adjacent bulk-soil composite were analysed. journal: Journal of Taibah University for Science

title: Experimental investigation of ground fissure reactivation and differential deformation under layered groundwater pumping–recharge conditions
abstract: Groundwater-level fluctuations can induce differential deformation at ground-fissure sites, yet systematic experimental investigations of hydraulic and layered deformation responses across fissures during pumping-recharge remain limited. This study focuses on the F 4 ground-fissure area in Yuhuazhai, Xi’an, and employs a large-scale physical model to investigate hydro-mechanical responses under layered groundwater pumping-recharge conditions. title: Alpine hazards, cultural memory, and storytelling's relevance for collective risk communication and disaster processing: A scoping review
abstract: Despite highly advanced technical monitoring for Alpine hazards, a persistent gap remains in translating risk information into community action. While storytelling holds significant potential for risk communication in the European Alps, its practical application in forming hybrid communication strategies remains underexplored. title: Tetrathionate sensing enables Vibrio parahaemolyticus to repress quorum sensing for intestinal colonization
abstract: Quorum sensing (QS) enables bacterial coordination of group behaviors, yet how enteric pathogens modulate QS during intestinal colonization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that Vibrio parahaemolyticus represses QS to promote gut colonization through sensing of self‑generated tetrathionate derived from host thiosulfate. We found that the cecal extracts from healthy mouse contained thiosulfate, which could be converted to tetrathionate by V. parahaemolyticus via the thiosulfate dehydrogenase TsdBA. title: Spatial distribution and environmental drivers of wild honey bee nesting patterns in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa
abstract: Spatial clusters of animal nests can be driven by mating behaviors, social benefits, and landscape heterogeneity. Unmanaged honey bees (Hymenoptera: Apidae: Apis spp.) have been documented nesting in clustered spatial distributions. However, environmental features influencing unmanaged honey bee nesting patterns have been largely understudied, especially for wild honey bees ( A. mellifera ) across Africa. title: Long-term patterns in phenotypic plasticity of chironomid head capsules in small high-elevation subarctic lakes: exploring possible mechanisms using multi-proxy paleolimnological records
abstract: Abstract We quantified temporal variation in the head capsule (HC) length of subfossil chironomids from two high-elevation subarctic lakes in northern Sweden and explored its potential drivers using chironomid assemblages, sedimentary pigments, and stable isotope analyses. Although establishing a reliable chronology was challenging because of the macrofossil-poor sediment context, radiocarbon dating indicates that the cores span approximately the last 5000 years, corresponding to the long-term cooling trend of the Late Holocene in this area. title: Undertow Structure and Stress Partition Beneath Plunging Breakers
abstract: Abstract Undertow beneath breaking waves controls nearshore mass balance and sediment transport, yet the transition between the lower wave–bottom-influenced region and the overlying flow affected by breaking-generated turbulence lacks a clear dynamical definition. This study investigates the vertical structure of undertow and turbulence beneath two regular laboratory plunging waves propagating over a sloping bottom, based on detailed velocity measurements. title: Assessing the eco-efficiency of offshore wind energy using a combined life cycle assessment and data envelopment analysis approach
abstract: This study develops an integrated Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)–Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) framework to evaluate the material eco-efficiency of 20 operational offshore wind farms in the United Kingdom. The framework incorporates a contribution-analysis step to identify the most environmentally relevant inventory flows before efficiency assessment. Harmonised cradle-to-grave inventories were constructed from the MEAOW model and remapped to ecoinvent v3.12 background processes. title: Emergency Response and Management of Pandemic Disasters and Their Environmental Dimensions: A Review of Lessons from COVID-19 in Bangladesh
abstract: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. This narrative review synthesizes 74 documents published between 2008 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, reports of intergovernmental and national agencies, and selected news and NGO records, to examine the emergency response to COVID-19 in Bangladesh, with the European Union as a comparator, and to connect that response to its environmental dimensions. title: Efficacy of Ccombody as an Immunoprophylaxis Strategy: Impact on Immune Gene Expression of Pacific White Shrimp ( Penaeus vannamei ) Against Acute Hepatopancreatic Necrosis Disease ( AHPND )
abstract: ABSTRACT Acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (AHPND) is caused by a plasmid bearing strain of Vibrio parahaemolyticus ( Vp AHPND ), which produces PirA and PirB toxins that specifically target and damage hepatopancreatic and epithelial cells of the shrimp gastrointestinal tract. The impact of AHPND, together with concerns regarding antibiotic resistance, has necessitated investigations into alternative forms of disease prevention. title: Stresses in Above‐Ground Storage Tanks Subjected to Flood‐Borne Debris Impact
abstract: ABSTRACT The objective of this study is to investigate the structural response of above‐ground storage tanks (ASTs) subjected to flood‐borne debris impact, a critical yet understudied aspect of flood‐induced loading. While past research has extensively examined AST performance under hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, limited attention has been paid to debris impact, which can contribute significantly to tank damage during floods. title: Habitat Suitability Modelling for the Krüper's Nuthatch (Sitta krueperi) in the Kaz Mountains and Surrounding Area
abstract: Biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation and climate change are among the primary environmental pressures affecting species distributions. The fact that species dependent on specific habitat conditions are particularly sensitive to environmental changes makes the identification of potential habitats crucial from a conservation biology perspective. title: Assessment of the Drainage Network Systems and Their Effects on Stormwater Flow and Flooding in Orogun, Ughelli North, Delta State, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding has become a recurring environmental challenge in many Nigerian urban centers, with Orogun town in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State experiencing increasing vulnerability to stormwater inundation. This study assesses the drainage network and its effects on stormwater flow and flooding in Orogun, employing a quantitative research methodology that integrates field surveys, hydrological measurements, and geospatial analysis. title: Bayesian assessment of return levels for observed temperature extremes across Odisha in India
abstract: Temperature-extreme risk is often assessed through trend-based indices, but regional climate-risk planning also requires uncertainty-aware estimates of rare thermal events and their spatial variability. This study presents a grid-wise Bayesian extreme-value assessment of observed temperature extremes over Odisha, India, using IMD daily maximum and minimum temperature data for 1951–2024. Annual and seasonal hot-day, warm-night, and cold-night block-extreme series were constructed for retained 1° × 1° grid cells. institutions: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College

title: Effectiveness of Geotechnical Investigations on Structural and Highway Construction in Nigeria
abstract: Geotechnical investigations are widely regarded as a crucial component of the safe, durable and cost-effective construction of structural and highway infrastructure in Nigeria. Rapid urbanization and increasing infrastructure demand have forced the need for detailed subsurface characterization in Nigeria, but lack of geotechnical research is still one of the leading reasons for construction failure. journal: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)

title: Reconstruction of an Ecosystem-Based Law Enforcement Model: Transformation of the Principle of Utility for the Restoration of Protected Forests
abstract: Indonesia, as a megabiodiverse country, faces serious challenges from the degradation of protected forests caused by land conversion into illegal agricultural areas. This study aims to analyze current law enforcement efforts against forest land conversion and formulate an environmental restoration-based law enforcement model grounded in the principle of legal utility. This study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive-analytical approach through a juridical-sociological study, comparing das sollen (legal norms) with das sein (practices in the field). title: Concentrations of uranium, cesium, and rubidium in drinking water and Monte Carlo–based age-specific health risk assessment of uranium
abstract: Freshwater is essential for life and the economy, yet its scarcity is worsening due to population growth, climate change, and unequal distribution. This study measures concentrations of uranium (U), cesium (Cs), and rubidium (Rb) in drinking water supplies across Arsanjan County, Iran, and evaluated the associated carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks of U using Monte Carlo simulation. Uranium concentrations were consistently below EPA and WHO guideline of 30 µg/L. The maximum Cs concentration was 0.63 µg/L, whereas Rb concentrations ranged from 2.04 to 13.94 µg/L. title: Data-driven accessibility to critical facilities using connected vehicle data: implications for future mobility and urban systems
abstract: Accurate measurement of accessibility to critical facilities is essential for equitable and efficient transportation and land-use planning, particularly in data-driven mobility systems. This study develops a novel hybrid framework to estimate travel time–based accessibility to schools and libraries using high-resolution connected vehicle (CV) data supplemented with Google Distance Matrix API to ensure complete spatial coverage. title: Ontogeny of rake mark scarring on common dolphins ( Delphinus delphis ): insights to aggression and affiliation?
abstract: Abstract Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. title: Taxonomic advancements in the Calotrichaceae: Resolving phylogenetic ambiguities and describing five novel species of Dulcicalothrix from the Konkan region of India
abstract: The taxonomy of heteropolar, tapering, and unbranched heterocytous cyanobacteria has undergone significant changes over time. Several novel species, genera, and families have been established using a polyphasic approach, which has provided a greater resolution in the systematics of these organisms. The Calotrichaceae, as of today, stands as a well-resolved and monophyletic clade with at least five genera. The family has had some major revisions as well as additions. title: Exploring Bacteria from Extreme Environments in Chilean Patagonia for Antitrypanosomal Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Extreme environments are recognized as valuable reservoirs of microbial diversity and chemical novelty. Adapted to harsh environmental conditions, bacteria isolated from extreme environments exhibit unique biosynthetic capabilities associated with the production of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains one of the most important neglected tropical diseases, affecting approximately eight million people worldwide. title: Variable response in riverine nitrogen exports to long-term temporal changes in watershed inputs
abstract: Aquatic nitrogen (N) pollution is a global problem, and understanding where best to implement mitigation strategies to reduce transfers from land to water is becoming increasingly urgent. Watershed nutrient budgets, using commonly available census data, can successfully predict riverine export spatially, albeit with variation related to fractional export. Furthermore, when using long-term data, watershed input-export trajectories vary and can be decoupled. title: Towards an understanding of socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons in the Venice Lagoon (Italy)
abstract: Abstract Socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons represent a growing challenge for sustainability governance, yet their dynamics remain poorly understood within complex Social-Ecological Systems (SESs). This study examines six emblematic conflicts in the Venice Lagoon (Italy), a complex SES undergoing profound transformations driven by land-use change and the privatisation of natural commons. title: Spatial prioritization of habitats and conceptual framework for impact assessment and mitigation planning for protected wetlands
abstract: Reconciling development and biodiversity conservation remains a critical challenge in contemporary conservation planning. Our study is based on a case study for the assessment of the Harike wetland, a Ramsar site and a Protected Area, a human-made reservoir, for understanding the impacts of proposed desilting operations and mitigation planning. A multi-taxa biodiversity assessment was undertaken to generate baseline ecological information for spatial prioritization, mitigation, and monitoring. title: Warming effects on population sizes and top–down control are dependent on temperature range
abstract: Rising global temperatures are expected to affect natural ecosystems, but predicting the consequences is challenging given the complexity of ecological communities. Natural communities are complex networks of interacting species, and temperature changes can thus influence species directly and indirectly via changes in their various interactions with other community members within and across trophic levels. title: Effects of Mineralogical Inhomogeneity on Aggregate Dust Optical Properties and Lidar Observables
abstract: Abstract Dust aerosols comprise irregular grains and aggregates with various mineralogical mixtures. However, most optical models use effective refractive indices to represent particles. This study develops an inhomogeneous aggregate model assigning mineral‐dependent refractive indices to constituent elements and representing global mineral volume fractions. title: Effect of thawing methods on color stability and underlying biochemical mechanisms in different regions of tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) fillets
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Thawing affects fillet color, determining consumer acceptance and market value of aquatic products. abstract: ABSTRACT Olive fruit fly ( Bactrocera oleae , Rossi) is one of the most significant pests in the Mediterranean olive groves, causing both quantitative and qualitative losses. Understanding its spatial and temporal dynamics is essential for effective and sustainable control of the pest. This study analyses an eight‐year dataset (2017–2024) of the olive fly populations on Samos Island, Greece, based on an extensive monitoring network of McPhail traps. abstract: Freezing fundamentally alters how minerals transform dissolved phenols in cold environments. As water freezes, solutes are excluded from the crystal lattice and concentrated into microscopic pockets of unfrozen liquid, creating reaction conditions far more extreme than those of bulk solution. abstract: In recent decades, extreme climate events have been recurrent in the Amazon, causing both intense droughts and prolonged rainy periods, impacting the population and economic sectors. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the spatial and temporal variation of precipitation using CHIRPS data in Pará state from 2001 to 2024.Precipitation data were obtained from CHIRPS and analyzed to identify spatial and temporal patterns. title: Balancing power generation with ecological impact: hydraulic and biological performance of a modernized adjustable-blade Kaplan turbine assessed using Sensor Fish technology
abstract: Hydropower remains a major source of affordable, clean, and reliable energy; however, aging infrastructure must be modernized to meet evolving environmental and operational requirements. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) operates 90 large Kaplan turbines within the Federal Columbia River Power System, many approaching the end of their service life. title: Tribal nations’ flood exposure and the U.S. national flood insurance program
abstract: Tribal nations experience significant flood impacts, yet participation in the National Flood Insurance Program remains limited. We analyze flood events, claims, and 57 Tribal Hazard Mitigation Plans, and insights from a tribal representative, to identify disparities in insured recovery. We show administrative, financial, and capacity constraints hinder mitigation progress. Strengthening equitable access to flood insurance, mapping, and federal mitigation resources could play an important role in improving tribal flood resilience.

abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. abstract: Transportation facilities such as bridges provide critical roosting habitat for bat species throughout California.This assessment analyzed 607 transportation facilities in Contra Costa County from the Federal Highway Administration's National Bridge Inventory dataset.The primary objective was to analyze the structural design elements of transportation facilities with confirmed bat use in Contra Costa County.The assessment prioritized facilities for field surveys using existing spatial datasets of predicted suitable habitat for bat species known to utilize bridges in Contra Costa County.The ass

title: Indigenous Planning: Utilising Kupuna Lensing for Pacific Disaster Risk Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Indigenous planning as a vital epistemological and practical framework for disaster risk reduction in the Pacific, centering Hawaiian knowledge systems. abstract: This paper revisits critical climate mobility literature that explores the role of images and visual materials within policy briefs and papers, published about a decade ago, to contrast those findings with present-day policy documents. Based on a discourse analysis of 10 recent IOM reports and policy briefs, we show that the written discourse has changed within the documents from a language of migration/displacement/refuge to one that is akin to climate (im)mobilities discourses. title: Magma Supply Dynamics at Mt. Etna (Italy) Inferred from Peripheral Soil CO2 Emissions: Insights into the 2018 Flank Eruption and the 2021 Paroxysmal Activity
abstract: Open-conduit volcanoes are characterized by continuous magma supply and persistent degassing, whereas eruptive activity occurs intermittently and is controlled by magma transfer and accumulation processes within the feeding system. At Mt. Etna, temporal variations in peripheral soil CO2 emissions provide a sensitive tracer of deep magma intrusions and can be used to quantify magma inputs into the feeding system. abstract: Neoporphyra hollenbergii is an endemic red alga from the Gulf of California, a region with notable cryptic diversity. We report its first complete mitochondrial genome and the first Bangiales mitogenome from the region. The circular mitogenome measures 31,565 bp (30.6% GC) and contains 50 genes, including 22 protein-coding genes, two rRNA genes, 24 tRNA genes, tatC, and orf813. abstract: Abstract. This study examines sub-watersheds in the arid northern region of Chile (26°41’–28°24’S), situated within the broader Copiapo watershed. abstract: This study aims to examine the conceptual debates in academic Ottoman maritime historiography and their instructional reflections in the 2025 secondary school (10th and 11th grade) History textbooks approved by the Ministry of National Education, alongside History Education undergraduate curricula. title: Uncovering rainfall dynamics in Pernambuco, Brazil, through innovative polygon trend analysis
abstract: Abstract This study applied the Innovative Polygon Trend Analysis (IPTA) and the Trend Polygon Star Concept (TPSC) to high-resolution precipitation records (1961–2022) across Pernambuco, Brazil, to assess the spatial variability of monthly rainfall trends and transitions. Monthly precipitation totals derived from 820 BR-DWGD grid cells were analyzed to characterize long-term changes in rainfall patterns across the semiarid Sertão, humid Zona da Mata, and transitional Agreste regions. abstract: Thiamine Deficiency Complex (TDC) is a reproductive disorder that affects recruitment of salmonine populations globally. Symptoms include behavioural and neurological abnormalities and high offspring mortality. TDC has typically been studied in hatcheries that rear embryos obtained from wild populations, and symptoms are mitigated by thiamine treatment. abstract: Abstract Iron plays a central role in defining the redox and surface chemical environment of soils and sediments, by mediating the behavior of nutrients, pollutants, and carbon compounds. However, the mechanisms that drive dynamic changes in Fe speciation and mineral composition can be difficult to trace. abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical pollution from rare earth elements (REEs) has emerged as a significant threat to the stability of freshwater ecosystems. Among these elements, europium oxide (Eu 2 O 3 ) is widely used across various industrial sectors; however, its specific impacts on fish physiology, health, and immune function remain poorly understood. title: A longitudinal analysis of diet quality, groundwater depletion and glacier thicknesses with implications for the sustainable development goal 2
abstract: Abstract The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG) underscores the need for eliminating hunger, improving nutrition, and promoting sustainable agriculture. For achieving SDG2, it is critical to address several factors such as agricultural production, groundwater depletion, and glacier decline under climate change. abstract: Abstract Bioactive secondary metabolites produced by the haptophyte microalga Prymnesium parvum are key mediators of ichthyotoxicity during harmful algal bloom events. title: Touring “Our USA”: Seeing US Empire in the Maps of Ruth Taylor White, 1920–1940
abstract: This article adds to histories of US empire, gender, race, and visual culture by more fully addressing white women’s role in sustaining colonial power through their production of an imperial visual culture between 1920 and 1940. It investigates the maps of a woman cartographer, Ruth Taylor White, across different geographical sites of US empire in the Pacific, Caribbean, and North American continent during a key moment in the history of US empire. abstract: This study investigates the integration of biological strategies into building systems and engineering through a multilevel biomimicry perspective. A systematic evaluation framework is established, categorizing biomimicry into two approaches (problem-oriented and solution-oriented), three levels (organism, behavior, and ecosystem), and five imitation dimensions: form, material, construction, process, and function. abstract: Sustainable development has guided global environmental governance for nearly four decades, yet continuing environmental degradation indicates persistent limitations in its implementation. This article examines whether clearer normative limits on natural resource use can strengthen sustainable development. It explores the Indonesian customary institution of Lubuk Larangan and identifies the principles of non-excessive utilization, sufficiency, and simplicity embedded in its Indigenous environmental wisdom. title: Analysis of urban heat islands in the study of urban environmental problems based on remote sensing
abstract: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Utilizing ArcGIS, the analysis processed Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery from August 2023. title: Sustainable Freight Transportation via Inland Waterways: Challenges and Strategic Solutions in Bangladesh
abstract: Inland water transport (IWT) is crucial for socio-economic development, facilitating rural connectivity, trade logistics, energy provision and tourism. Nevertheless, it is neglected due to historical underinvestment, inadequate infrastructure and regulatory inefficiencies in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the current state of freight movement via inland waterways, identifies key challenges and proposes strategies to improve sustainability. title: How Wisconsin Extension Educators Talk About Climate Change Without Talking About ``Climate Change''
abstract: Climate change touches all areas of Extension's programming. To understand how educators approach talking about climate change with constituents, we interviewed 15 Extension educators and three program managers in Wisconsin. Crops and Soils educators view climate change as interwoven with their work, Financial Education educators view it as mostly disconnected, and Community Economic Development educators range between these extremes. abstract: BACKGROUND: Leishmaniasis is a severe parasitic disease transmitted by sand fly bites.
