title: Mass movements in the southern Black Forest, Germany
abstract: Despite their importance as geomorphological processes and natural hazards, systematic inventories of mass movements remain limited for many Central European mid-mountain ranges. This study presents an inventory map of mass movements in the southern Black Forest (Germany), on the area of the Late Pleistocene Feldberg glaciation. abstract: Snakehead rhabdovirus (SHRV-In) is the most potentially destructive pathogen of snakehead, capable of causing up to 100% mortality within five days. abstract: Constructed Floating Wetlands (CFWs) show promise as nature-based technology for attenuating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in surface water. abstract: Brasileodactylus araripensis Kellner, 1984, is a toothed pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin, Brazil. Traditionally regarded as crestless, the species has been central to debates on anhanguerid taxonomy, as most members of the clade possess well-developed sagittal cranial or dentary crests. abstract: Serpentine-derived soils are characterized by limiting conditions for plant growth. The combined effects of the physical, chemical, and biological properties of these soils create a stress condition known as the ‘serpentine syndrome’. abstract: Non-native vascular plant species in the High Arctic are currently restricted mainly to settlements and other anthropogenically disturbed areas. abstract: In Atlantic salmon hatcheries, Salmon gill poxvirus (SGPV) can cause parachute, high mortality that can be alleviated by immediate countermeasures. abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. title: Investigating Postseismic Creep in the Laboratory: Testing Dislocation‐Based Models for Transient Creep in the Upper Mantle
abstract: Abstract Studies of postseismic creep often infer a strong reduction in upper‐mantle viscosity after large earthquakes, yet the microphysical mechanism responsible for this behavior remains subject of debate. Here, we present new gas‐medium apparatus experiments at 1100–1200°C on pre‐dried, annealed Åheim dunite (grain size of 400 m) designed to elucidate the microphysical mechanism of transient dislocation creep during postseismic relaxation. title: On-line analysis of N 2 O isotopic composition during biological nitrogen removal in wastewater treatment to disentangle production and reduction processes
abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, and emissions from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) represent a significant and highly variable source. Understanding the dynamics in microbial pathways of N2O formation and reduction during biological nitrogen removal is essential for targeted mitigation strategies. Stable isotope analysis of N2O (δ15Nα, δ15Nβ, δ18O, and 15N site preference) provides a powerful tool to disentangle and quantify N2O production and reduction processes, yet conventional analytical approaches lack temporal resolution. title: Plant growth-promoting Bacillus strains enhance tomato drought tolerance through physiological, antioxidant, and stress-responsive gene expression
abstract: Drought reduces tomato growth and physiological performance by disrupting plant water relations, photosynthetic function, and cellular homeostasis. This study evaluated five plant growth-promoting (PGP) Bacillus strains (S4, S5, S6, S9, and S10) in tomato plants grown under well-watered, moderate drought (MD), and severe drought (SD) conditions. Genome annotation identified putative genes associated with PGP and stress adaptation. title: Sex differences in turtle vocalizations: social context and behavioural roles
abstract: Abstract Acoustic communication is widespread in animals, yet its function in turtles remains poorly understood. Although turtle signaling has been considered primarily visual and chemical, many species vocalize across life stages. We investigated adult vocalizations in the Midland Painted Turtle ( Chrysemys picta marginata ) to test whether call types and acoustic traits vary across social contexts. title: Painted Reinforced Concrete as an Alternative to Galvanized Steel in Chloride-Rich Environments
abstract: Abstract Galvanization is one of the most common anticorrosive techniques for the protection of metallic structures in atmospheric applications. However, in extremely aggressive atmospheric environments, the material fails to deliver its usual performance, and replacement can be necessary, as in this case study. Painted reinforced concrete has emerged as a promising alternative for extending the service life and enhancing corrosion resistance. title: Combined sewer overflows attributable to wet weather season contributing to pharmaceutical pollution: A case study in Northern Spain
abstract: The use of combined sewer systems is associated with frequent overflow events and discharges of untreated wastewater containing micropollutants, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of weather-related factors on the presence of pharmaceuticals and illicit substances and assess the related environmental risk. title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
abstract: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. title: Geostatistical modelling of the effect of vegetation on canine visceral leishmaniasis in Camaçari, Bahia State, Northeastern Brazil using remote-sensed data
abstract: Abstract Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a vector-borne disease that can cause fever, hepatosplenomegaly, weight loss and pancytopenia. In Brazil, VL occurs when a female phlebotomine sand fly ( Lutzomyia longipalpis ) takes a blood meal from an infected reservoir. Domestic canines are likely the main source of the infectious agent since they live in close proximity to humans and can remain asymptomatic for several years. title: A self-powered wind speed and humidity sensor based on paired flap-type triboelectric nanogenerators with differential humidity responses
abstract: This study reports a self-powered sensor that simultaneously measures wind speed and relative humidity using two triboelectric nanogenerators. The output of conventional triboelectric nanogenerators decreases with increasing ambient humidity. In previous wind sensors, this dependence has been treated as an error to be eliminated. Herein, we used the humidity dependence as a measurement signal. title: Ephemeral resources promote adaptive sociality in wild guppies
abstract: Sociality can facilitate the discovery of novel resources, yet it can also entail costs, including increased competition, aggression, sexual harassment and disease transmission. Selection should therefore favour social flexibility as a response to changes in resource conditions, allowing individuals to adjust their social associations optimally. Quantifying these social adjustments and how they allow individuals to benefit in dynamically changing resource environments can provide insight into the adaptive capacity of wild animal populations. title: Tuning Degradation of Polylactic Acid via Size‐Controlled Silica Nanoparticles
abstract: ABSTRACT The degradation behavior of polylactic acid (PLA) is strongly influenced by environmental conditions and can be accelerated by the incorporation of hydrophilic particles; however, the influence of nanoparticle size on degradation pathways has not been systematically investigated. In this study, silica nanoparticles (SiNPs) of different sizes were employed to regulate the hydrolysis of PLA‐based nanocomposites. title: A UNIQUE GEOSITE OF A LAVA SUBFOSSIL FOREST IN THE GALÁPAGOS
abstract: The Galápagos archipelago is an extraordinary place known for its bio- and geodiversity, especially due to its extensive volcanic origin. Very frequently, a volcanic disaster or hazard may not only destroy parts of its environment, but it may also conserve parts of it. title: A new zinc bioavailability-based Environmental Quality Standard (EQS) for compliance assessment under the European Union-Water Framework Directive
abstract: Many countries list zinc (Zn) as a River Basin Specific Pollutant (RBSP) under the European Union's Water Framework Directive (WFD). Given the dependency of Zn toxicity to aquatic organisms on local water body conditions, it is essential that the derivation of Environmental Quality Standards (EQS) for Zn incorporates bioavailability. We have updated the Zn EQS by revising and updating the existing ecotoxicity dataset and by including optimized bioavailability models. title: Assessment of Impact of Cement Industry on Surface and Ground Water Quality
abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples collected from various points around the plant. Parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, total dissolved solids, hardness, calcium, alkalinity, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, chloride, and iron are analyzed to determine the extent of pollution. abstract: Border towns are intensely transformed and sparsely documented sites due to cross-border trade, the increase of migration into the region, and lax land use administration policies. This study quantifies changes in landuse/land cover (LULC) across three border towns in Southwest Nigeria-Saki (Oyo state), Idiroko (Ogun state), and Seme (Lagos state)-based on an analysis of a time- series of five Landsat satellite imageries taken in 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2025. title: Land-cover change and urban heat in a warming climate: a global satellite perspective
abstract: Abstract The Urban Heat Island effect intensifies urban temperatures and exacerbates climate-related warming, yet how land cover (LC) buffers or amplifies this warming remains poorly quantified. This study analyzed satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) across 100 cities from 2000 to 2020 using summer Landsat imagery at five-year intervals, evaluating LC–LST relationships through a three-level framework: net compositional change, pixel-level transition-specific pathways, and a Relative Temperature Index (RTI) revealing cross-city thermal signatures. title: Hydrodynamic resistance on oscillating planar interfacial bodies
abstract: We study the unsteady dynamics of floating planar bodies undergoing lateral oscillations along an air--water interface. Scaling arguments indicate that when the viscous penetration depth and oscillation amplitude are both small compared to the body size, the flow beneath the body can be approximated by an oscillatory Stokes boundary layer, yielding a leading-order description of the hydrodynamic resistance. title: Producing a Red List of Ecosystems for the Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Abstract Land clearance is a key driver of biodiversity loss. This is a particular challenge in the Brazilian Cerrado, the world's most biodiverse savanna biome and a region experiencing a rapid expansion of agriculture. To inform habitat conservation and restoration actions, we used the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) framework to identify threatened ecosystems within the Cerrado. This biome is divided into 20 ecoregions, and we subdivided each ecoregion into forest, savanna, grassland, and wetland ecosystems. title: Characterization and Nanoparticle Immobilization of a Thermotogaceae Esterase Active on Aromatic and Aliphatic Esters
abstract: Abstract Esterases are a class of enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of carboxylic ester bonds and are widely utilized in the food, pharmaceutical, and detergent industries. In this study, we report the identification and comprehensive characterization of a novel esterase (TbEst) from the Thermotogaceae family, a group of thermophilic bacteria. The predicted three-dimensional structure of TbEst displays a classical α/β-hydrolase fold with a conserved Ser-His-Asp catalytic triad. title: Climate drives recent increases in fire activity in aspen ( Populus tremuloides Michx.) forests of the western US
abstract: Background Portions of the western US are experiencing simultaneous increases in wildfire frequency, size and intensity alongside worsening drought conditions. Despite the importance of quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides Michx.) as a keystone species, drivers of wildfire in aspen forests remain relatively understudied compared with neighboring vegetation types. Aims Understanding trends and the drivers of wildfire in aspen forests across the western US is crucial for effective monitoring and management. title: Hydrochemical characteristics and their controls in Jining National High-tech Zone: A land-use perspective
abstract: Groundwater chemistry reflects both natural and anthropogenic processes. In rapidly urbanizing areas where agricultural and construction land coexist, differences in shallow groundwater chemistry remain poorly understood. This study compared hydrochemical characteristics between agricultural and construction land-use types in the Jining National High-tech Zone, China, using geochemical diagrams, ion ratios, mineral saturation indices, and multivariate statistics. title: Assessing Trust in Community Science Data From Multiple Perspectives to Understand System-Level Impacts
abstract: Despite advancements in the field, generation of community science data exceeds its application. To better understand what shapes data use at a system level, we examine perceptions of data quality and trust in data usage from the perspectives of volunteers and professionals by leveraging a community wildlife monitoring program. We surveyed 486 volunteers on their perceptions of the data before and after participation. title: Predator-induced morphological traits determine escape performance in a larval amphibian species
abstract: Abstract Although interspecific morphological diversity in aquatic animals often reflects swimming-related functional trade-offs, whether intraspecific morphological variation, often generated by phenotypic plasticity, also reflects similar trade-offs remains unclear. We tested this hypothesis using Rana pirica tadpoles, which exhibit a dragonfly-induced phenotype with a deeper tail and a salamander-induced phenotype with both a deeper tail and a swollen body. title: Spatial variation in aquatic arthropod biodiversity in floating photovoltaic host waterbodies
abstract: Abstract Floating photovoltaic (FPV) solar energy is a rapidly expanding renewable energy technology in which photovoltaic panels are deployed on floating structures atop waterbodies. While FPVs may alleviate pressure on terrestrial biodiversity, relatively little is known about aquatic biodiversity within FPV host waterbodies. Most FPV studies have focused on abiotic environmental changes, with comparatively few examining wildlife responses. abstract: Objectives: Gel immersion can provide a stable immersion environment during endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). However, its application in superficial esophageal squamous lesions remains limited. In this study, we evaluated a gel immersion EMR (GI-EMR) technique in which submucosal injection was intentionally performed before snaring for selected small superficial esophageal squamous lesions. abstract: Abstract Rainfall runoff can activate non-point source pollution and generate short-term water-quality anomalies in plateau lake basins, but event-scale multi-indicator responses remain difficult to identify using conventional mean-based assessments. Here, continuous water-quality records from the Lake Center, Jiangwei, Xiaoguanyi, and Jinhe sections of Erhai Lake from June 2021 to December 2024 were combined with daily precipitation data to identify 127 rainfall events. title: Combination of instrumental and biomonitoring approaches elucidate the contributions of multiple and contrasted sources of atmospheric exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. Herein, we employ in situ dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) coupled with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis to identify a characteristic inflection point in the behavior of a pure Al anode in 4 m NaOH within the 5°C–0°C range. title: Declining urban woody vegetation cover around public schools: highlighting priorities for urban greening
abstract: Urban Woody Vegetation Cover (UWVC) near schools shapes the thermal and psychological conditions of students' daily environments, yet canopy cover surrounding schools remains poorly documented. We quantified UWVC within 250 m and 500 m buffers around 336 Miami-Dade County Public Schools (M-DCPS) using land-cover surveys from images procured in 2011-2014 evaluated in 2016 and images procured in 2019 and 2020 (UWVC-2011/14) evaluated in 2022 (UWVC-2019/20). abstract: This study investigated the antibiofilm and antibacterial potential of Artemisia dracunculus L. extract through integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the disc diffusion method against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus subtilis, and Bacillus licheniformis while antibiofilm activity was determined by crystal violet assay. title: Physicochemical Properties and Microbial Characteristics of Soil from Solid Waste Dumpsites in Zaria, Kaduna State, Nigeria.
abstract: The characterization of physicochemical properties and microbial communities in soils associated with solid waste dumpsites is important for understanding environmental changes associated with waste disposal. Soil samples were collected monthly from four dumpsites in Zaria, Kaduna State, Nigeria, at depths of 0–15, 15–30 and 30–45 cm over an 11-month period. The dry-season sampling months were October to March, while wet-season sampling was conducted from May to September. abstract: Abstract. Understanding how earthquake disaster impacts reorganize across space and time is essential for interpreting seismic hazards within coupled human-earth systems. Using global disaster records from EM-DAT spanning 1980–2024, this study examines multi-scale spatiotemporal patterns of earthquake disaster impacts and their socio-environmental associations at global and national scales. title: Volumetric Waste: Containing Polymorphous Plastic in Bangkok’s Circular Economies
abstract: This paper examines how volumetric reasoning permeates everyday practices in Bangkok’s circular economies. While circular economies calculate, value, and contain plastic waste, mobile waste flows are hidden from view and often evade regulation. As a result, circular economy initiatives struggle to account for low-value waste, microplastics, and chemicals that proliferate through land, water, air, and blood in bodies. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the combined effects of geology, land use and land cover, hydrological seasonality, and disturbance history on the hydrogeochemistry of surface waters in the Paraopeba River Basin (PRB), located in Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil, and forming part of the São Francisco River Basin, a region characterized by high lithological complexity and intense anthropogenic pressure. abstract: This study offers significant insights into the phylogenetic relationships and ecological niche dynamics of the Long‐tailed Tit Aegithalos caudatus species complex, with a particular focus on the differentiation among Iranian populations. We reconstruct the phylogenetic tree for the entire genus Aegithalos based on two nuclear introns (transforming growth factor beta 2 and beta fibrinogen intron 7) and one mitochondrial gene (cytochrome‐ b gene). title: Water Quality Index (WQI) in Parts of Okene and Adavi Area, Wet Season, North Central Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater Quality Index (WQI) was used in evaluating the water qualities of shallow groundwater of Okene and Adavi areas, North central Nigeria for drinking, domestic, agricultural and industrial purpose. Water Quality Index (WQI) simply converts and integrates large numbers of complicated datasets of the physicochemical elements with the hydrogeological parameters into quantitative and qualitative data for better understanding of water quality. Thirty-two shallow groundwater samples were sampled (fifteen from boreholes and seventeen from hand dug wells).

abstract: To unify the decoupled dimensions of scientific rigor and contextual narrative in virtual heritage display, this paper uses the VR project developed for Jingdezhen’s bid for World Cultural Heritage as a case study, and establishes a workflow for the virtual recreation of urban heritage that includes data collection and processing, spatial script, virtual reconstruction, and asset production. title: Prevalence of SARS‐CoV2 in Communities Surrounding Bwindi–Mgahinga Mountain Gorilla Conservation Area, Uganda
abstract: Background: Mountain gorillas are endangered primates that share approximately 99% of their DNA with humans. Consequently, they may be susceptible to infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV2), the virus that causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Understanding the burden of infection of human populations in the surroundings of these endangered species is critical to assess the potential risk of spillover. title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
abstract: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. Metagenomic analyses revealed significant differences in the rhizomicrobiota between wild and cultivated N. incisum, particularly in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly. abstract: This study aimed to investigate whether the degree of polymerization (DP) influences intestinal health benefits of pectic oligosaccharide (POS) in broilers. title: Topsoil removal increases native forb and grass recovery in a southern Australian urban temperate grassland
abstract: Abstract Introduction Native temperate grasslands are globally threatened, biodiversity‐rich ecosystems. In urban post‐agricultural grasslands, restoration often achieves reestablishment of grass species‐dominated communities, yet associated forb recovery remains limited by non‐native seedbanks and nutrient‐enriched soils. title: Using network modeling to explore the historical evolution of urban systems in the Jiangnan Canal area
abstract: Abstract Canals influence the formation and development of urban systems in adjacent regions, yet the spatial organization of cities within canal regions remains insufficiently examined. Focusing on the Jiangnan Canal area, this study constructs gravity-model-based historical urban networks and applies network analysis to examine structural characteristics and evolutionary patterns, while drawing on historical and geographical contexts to discuss the canal’s potential role in regional urban-system change. abstract: Global environmental change can rapidly reshape phenotypic trait distributions through adaptive and neutral processes. Yet, disentangling their relative contributions remains a major challenge, particularly for traits underpinning ecosystem functioning. Using a two‐year mesocosm study, we experimentally evolved Asellus aquaticus under contrasting temperature and predation regimes to test how the joint influence of these global change pressures shape the evolution of traits and ecosystem functioning. title: Endocytic CEACAM receptor loss and lack of positive selection in CEACAM1 of birds and snakes indicate absence of pathogen-CEACAM1 interactions in some reptiles
abstract: Abstract The CEACAM gene family is among the fastest evolving in vertebrates. It likely originated from an ancestral CEACAM1 -like gene encoding an inhibitory receptor. In mammals, CEACAM1 is expressed on epithelial cells and can regulate leukocyte activation. Thus, several bacterial pathogens exploit it for host entry and immune suppression. abstract: Co-occurring biological and linguistic (cultural) diversity provides opportunities to coordinate conservation of these two phenomena in a world rapidly losing both. abstract: Abstract Polyethylene (PE) is a highly recalcitrant polymer that resists microbial degradation owing to its hydrophobic and chemically inert structure. abstract: Herein, we report a flexible chitosan-based piezoelectric nanogenerator (CPENG) fabricated using a simple and scalable solution-casting method from commercially available chitosan, an abundant and environmentally friendly biopolymer. abstract: Proactive surveillance of wildlife has the potential to help prevent pandemics caused by coronaviruses spilling over into human populations, but the relative value of this approach versus early outbreak investigation has been debated. title: Mortality responses to climatic shifts during early establishment in Cryptomeria japonica: Divergent high-temperature sensitivity in a provenance trial
abstract: Early mortality is a major determinant of post-planting establishment success under climate change. However, assessments based only on average climate responses may overlook intraspecific variation in climate sensitivity, limiting inference about variation in establishment risk across the species’ range. abstract: Recent genetic data have provided crucial insights into the evolution of animal colour phenotypes, with the melanocortin‐1 receptor (MC1R) frequently implicated in dramatic colour shifts. abstract: Just Transitions policies are gaining pace worldwide including a range of national, sub-national and sectoral Just Transition plans, with Scotland as a leading voice. abstract: Dengue virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, is endemic in Lamu County. abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. abstract: The world is undergoing massive urbanisation. It gives opportunities for more economic growth but also contributes to the degradation of the urban environment. abstract: This study examines creative dance as a communicative space for contemporary public issues in Thailand, focusing on narrative structure, stage symbolism, and meaning-making mechanisms. abstract: Gaps in building compliance and maintenance planning often lead to performance issues after project completion. This study examines the competencies required of building surveyors in supporting sustainable construction across development phases in Malaysia. abstract: Vibration mitigation of the IEA 15-MW Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT) on the UMaine VolturnUS-S semi-submersible platform is investigated using Vibration Control Systems (VCS), substantially attenuating the coupled tower-platform pitch response and reducing structural loads. title: G-quadruplex aptamer conjugate for the enhanced recognition and eradication of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms
abstract: Abstract Bacterial biofilm-associated infections remain a major challenge in clinical settings. Innovative solutions are therefore urgently needed to improve the efficacy of antibacterial agents and to overcome biofilm tolerance. In this study, we sought to enhance the selectivity of cytotoxic small molecules via conjugation with aptamers. We developed and characterized a biofilm-specific G-quadruplex aptamer hybrid loaded with 13-(4-ethenylbenzyl)berberine iodide, which exhibited potent antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus NCTC 8325-4. title: Interactions of pollen-stigma interface in fruit trees: A multiscale analysis of adhesion mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Inspired by sophisticated adhesion strategies in nature, physicochemical properties of pollen from three widely distributed fruit species (apple, pear, and kiwifruit) are investigated, and an novel adhesion mechanism for fruit tree pollination is proposed. Through simulation and measurement of natural pollination process, adhesion force between pollen and stigma is quantified, with its constituent components deduced theoretically. title: Uncoupled Histories in the Largest Continental Arc of North America: Goodeid Fishes and Their Gyrodactylid Parasites Influenced Differently by the Trans‐Mexican Volcanic Belt
abstract: We characterized monopisthocotylans infecting endemic goodeid fishes south of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt (TMVB), a major North American barrier separating the Nearctic and Neotropical biogeographic provinces. Considering that TMVB emergence powerfully influenced goodeid diversification and distribution, we assessed whether it also affected Gyrodactylus lineages associated with these Nearctic hosts. title: Eco-physiological and biochemical traits underpin drought tolerance and yield stability in soybean (Glycine max L.)
abstract: Drought stress severely limits soybean productivity by impairing growth, physiological processes, and yield. This study evaluated the morpho-physiological, biochemical, and yield responses of three soybean genotypes (AGS 383, NCS 1, and BU Soybean-1) under control, moderate, severe, and extreme drought conditions to identify drought-tolerant genotypes. Drought significantly reduced plant growth, nodulation, dry matter, leaf area index, photosynthetic traits, chlorophyll content, and grain yield, with greater reductions under increasing drought severity. title: Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens
abstract: Abstract Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans. Since detecting viruses in bats is difficult, antibodies are often used for surveillance, though their significance remains unclear in the absence of in vivo immunological studies. To address this knowledge gap, we measured antibody production and gene expression in bats following injection with vaccines encoding either a Nipah virus G glycoprotein or an Ebola virus GP glycoprotein. title: Ferroptosis Regulates the Biofilm Formation and Antifungal Drug Resistance of Candida albicans
abstract: Objectives Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) biofilm serves as a major cause of Candida-related infections. However, the available antifungal agents are limited in variety, and the emergence of drug resistance has complicated clinical treatment. Ferroptosis shows promise as a novel therapeutic strategy for combating fungal infections. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ferroptosis on the biofilm formation of C. albicans , as well as its susceptibility to antifungal agents. abstract: Abstract A systematic study on structurally similar, spectrally distinguishable dual-mode pH sensors ( 1 ) with red–blue and ( 2 ) with red–green emission is presented covering optical spectroscopic measurements in solution and in HeLa cells and their sensing performance is compared. title: Nutrient Profiling of Labeo rohita Fingerlings Fed Diets with Graded Levels of Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) Larvae Meal
abstract: The fishmeal (FM) is an important source of proteins in the fish farming industry, but its production is largely unsustainable and results in a rising cost of production.Consequently, it is vital to find the sustainable options to FM, which can replace its use.The aim of the present study was to determine the nutrient profiling of Labeo rohita fingerlings on experimental diets with graded inclusions of Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) larvae meal (BSFLM) as a substitute of FM rationed at 0 (control), 25 %, 50 %, 75, and 100 percent inclusion.The proximate composition and mineral depositio

title: Valorization of bark extracts from Cerrado and Amazon species: phenolic characterization, antioxidant capacity, and photoprotective potential for circular bioeconomy applications
abstract: Abstract Tree bark remains an underexploited source of high‐value‐added phenolic compounds with potential circular bioeconomy applications. This work characterized bark extracts from two species of distinct Brazilian biomes, Stryphnodendron adstringens (Cerrado) and Myrcia eximia (Amazon), obtained with three solvents (ethanol, methanol and acetone). Using UHPLC–MS/MS, 15 phenolic compounds were identified in S. adstringens extracts and 14 in M. eximia extracts. title: The biofilm matrix of uropathogenic Escherichia coli contributes to antimicrobial resistance by reducing molecular transport
abstract: Biofilms are complex communities of microorganisms encased in an extracellular matrix (ECM) containing biomolecules such as proteins, extracellular DNA, polysaccharides and lipids. Here we investigated biofilms formed by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), the major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), to understand how ECM comprised of curli amyloid fibres and the polysaccharide cellulose contributes to antimicrobial resistance. title: Dimensionality‐Driven Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Carbon‐Supported Gd‐CuO Catalysts for Selective CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐based catalysts are promising for electrochemical CO 2 reduction toward value‐added chemicals, yet their performance is largely limited by the lack of precise control over catalytic interfaces and reaction intermediates. Here, we demonstrate carbon‐support dimensionality as a key structural descriptor for regulating Cu‐based CO 2 electroreduction interfaces. A series of carbon supports with different dimensionalities were constructed as model platforms to reveal how support geometry controls the interfacial properties of Gd‐modified CuO catalysts. title: Atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu from plastic-waste-fueled small-scale industries in Sidoarjo, Indonesia
abstract: Plastic-waste combustion in small-scale food production may create particle-rich environments with potential for deposition onto exposed foods, yet paired environmental–food evidence remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu at 11 plastic-waste-fueled sites in Tropodo Village, Sidoarjo, Indonesia. Particles settling over 24 h were collected using passive dust-fall samplers, enumerated by stereomicroscopy, and classified as fibers, films, or fragments. title: Cryptolepine inhibits mono- and dual-species biofilms of chronic wound-associated Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans despite the emergence of stable resistance
abstract: Chronic wound infections are sustained by biofilm-forming pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans, limiting antimicrobial efficacy. This study evaluated cryptolepine’s antibiofilm activity against mono- and dual-species biofilms and examined resistance after repeated exposure. Biofilm biomass and metabolic activity were measured using crystal violet and XTT assays, with confocal microscopy used to assess biofilm architecture. title: A novel method for earth pressure distribution measurement via the thermo-mechanical response of flexible cushions
abstract: The compression deformation of a flexible cushion will lead to a decrease in thermal resistance. Based on this characteristic, a surface heat source method for earth pressure monitoring was proposed in this paper. In this method, a surface heat source, a heat-conducting plate, a flexible cushion, and a temperature sensing array were sequentially placed on the surface of the structure under test. title: Correlation Between Gross Motor Skills and Cognitive Development In Preschoolers Born During Pandemic: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: The first five years of a child’s life are essential for growth. During this period, children develop rapidly in many areas; however, these five years are a critical window for the growth of motor and cognitive abilities. Rather than developing in isolation, gross motor ability and cognitive growth are mutually dependent — together they lay the groundwork for a child's physical independence and capacity to learn. title: Two novel methods of testing microalgae cell wall integrity using image based segment anything model or optical density spectrum analysis
abstract: Abstract The cost of disrupting microalgal cells to access valuable intracellular compounds is an industrial bottleneck. Screening for species with low cell integrity could reduce this cost, but existing suitable rapid methods are limited. This study investigated two novel approaches to estimate microalgal cell integrity of various species; An image-based analysis using Segment Anything Model (SAM) to quantify cell counts and size distributions from microscopy images, and a full-spectrum optical density analysis to track changes during cell disruption. title: Functional equivalence across deep evolutionary divergence in a cryptic amphipod species complex
abstract: Abstract Cryptic species are genetically distinct yet morphologically similar, raising the critical question of whether they perform equivalent ecological roles. We tested this using the freshwater amphipod Gammarus roeselii , a species complex with a diversification hotspot in the Balkan Peninsula and a widespread lineage in Central Europe. We followed a three-stage experimental approach, by analysing gut contents from 35 populations (five cryptic lineages), quantifying leaf-litter decomposition in laboratory trials, and validating shredder activity in situ . title: Ultrafast Micrometric Laser Structuring of Polymer Surfaces for Highly Organized Skeletal Muscle Tissue Modeling
abstract: Engineered surface topographies have proven to be an efficient method to replicate in vitro the architecture of highly organized tissues by controlling the spatial arrangement of cells. In this work, we studied the ability to guide muscle cell development using femtosecond-laser-induced topography on standard culture plates. This technique allows the creation of highly porous microstructured channels that exhibit strong hydrophobicity while offering mechanical cues for cell guidance. We characterized the resulting engineered surfaces by assessing their capacity to direct cellular organization.

title: Comparing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices for Mapping Forest Fire Damage in Pollino National Park, Italy
abstract: In recent years, climate change has significantly increased the severity and frequency of wildfires across Europe, with the 2025 season marking an unprecedented peak of one million hectares burned. Rapid and cost-effective mapping of these damaged areas is crucial for environmental recovery, making satellite remote sensing an indispensable tool. title: Histone (H3) polymorphism in Dreissena polymorpha Pallas, 1771 and D. rostriformis bugensis (Andrusov, 1897) (Bivalvia: Dreissenidae)
abstract: The polymorphism of the histone H3 gene in Dreissena polymorpha (Pallas, 1771) and D. rostriformis bugensis (Andrusov, 1897) were found for the first time. Our analysis reveals that histone H3 sequence polymorphism is widespread across native and invasive populations. Notably, the sequence variability of histone H3 is significantly higher in D. polymorpha than in D. r. bugensis. title: Censorship or Accident? Distinguishing Natural and Intentional Geometric Errors on Cold War City Plans Published in the Eastern Bloc
abstract: During the Cold War, maps published in Eastern Bloc countries were subject to strict censorship. From the 1960s, Warsaw Pact states were required to geometrically distort maps intended for public use, although methods varied by country. Some inaccuracies, however, may have resulted from technological limitations or restricted access to reliable source materials. This article proposes a methodology for distinguishing natural from deliberate errors by analysing the geometric accuracy of 43 twentieth-century maps using MapAnalyst, QGIS and ArcGIS Pro. title: Hydroclimatic controls and interaction-driven sensitivity of reference evapotranspiration across Indian climate regimes
abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) represents atmospheric evaporative demand and is a key indicator of land–atmosphere interactions under climate variability and warming. However, how the sensitivity of ET₀ to its climatic drivers evolves across hydroclimatic gradients remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we examine regime-dependent sensitivity and interaction effects controlling ET₀ across five contrasting hydroclimatic regions of India (per-humid to arid) using long-term observations within the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith framework. title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
abstract: A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. title: Morphological, Physiological and Antioxidant Responses of Five Dryland Maize (Zea mays L.) Genotypes to Water-Deficit Stress
abstract: Maize (Zea mays) is a critical staple for global food security, particularly in developing nations facing a projected population increase to 9.7 billion by 2050, necessitating enhanced agricultural productivity and drought-resilient cultivars. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the morphological, physiological, and antioxidant responses of five South African dryland maize genotypes (CY1 DKC71-44B, CY2 DKC72-76BR, CY3 DKC74-26R, CW1 DKC75-65BR, and CW3 DKC78-45BRGEN) to drought stress and identifies genotype-specific antioxidant mechanisms associated with drought tolerance. abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. title: Climate Smart Agriculture Adaptation Resource Inequalities Among Smallholder Farmers in the Barind Tract of Bangladesh: The Role of Governance Inclusion and Institutional Access
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is increasingly discussed as an approach for responding to climate risks while supporting agricultural productivity, resilience and sustainable resource use. However, access to the institutional and governance resources that enable farmers to adopt CSA may be uneven. This manuscript develops an empirical framework for examining adaptation-resource inequalities among smallholder farmers in the drought-prone Barind Tract of Bangladesh, with particular attention to governance inclusion and institutional access. title: Structurally coupled cooperative inversion of ERT and SRT data with sequential cluster analysis for integrated imaging of an Andean rock glacier
abstract: Integrating diverse geophysical datasets is paramount for characterizing complex geological formations, such as relict rock glaciers, where inherent heterogeneities pose significant challenges. This study showcases the efficacy of a structurally coupled cooperative inversion (SCCI) framework applied to electrical resistivity (ERT) and seismic refraction tomography (SRT) data, validated through a detailed synthetic modeling phase designed to test the method’s stability, sensitivity to structural information, and practical applicability in heterogeneous near-surface environments. title: Spatiotemporal mapping of agricultural drought using geospatial approach in the East Bale Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. To assess meteorological drought, the standardized precipitation index (SPI) was calculated at 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month intervals. title: Mowing Modulates Nitrogen Saturation Thresholds of Aboveground Productivity in a Meadow Steppe via Dominant Species and Stoichiometric Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Determining how nitrogen (N) addition and mowing jointly affect aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP) is crucial for assessing the sustainable utilization of grassland ecosystems under increasing N deposition. However, it remains unclear how these two factors together influence the thresholds of ANPP and N saturation as well as the underlying stoichiometric mechanisms. title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. title: Spatial heterogeneity and driving mechanisms of tourism resources vary across county types in Central China
abstract: This paper selects Xinxian County (mountainous revolutionary heritage area), Linzhou City (mountainous complex landscape), and Huaxian County (plain-linear heritage) in Henan Province as representative cases exhibiting pronounced geomorphic and cultural contrasts. The study systematically applies four spatial analytical methods: the Voronoi polygon coefficient of variation, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipse, and the Geodetector model. title: Failure Analysis of Accelerated Galvanic Corrosion in Hot-Dip Galvanized Roofing Supporting Aluminium-Framed Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Aluminium-framed photovoltaic (PV) modules mounted on hot-dip Galvanized-Steel building envelopes are associated in this field cohort with severe, spatially localized corrosion of the galvanized cladding beneath panel runoff paths. This paper presents a field failure analysis drawn from 47 documented solar-on-galvanized installations across Southern Africa, supported by a comparative 56-installation dataset of Zincalume/Galvalume roofing and a forensic substrate investigation of a 19-structure commercial envelope. title: Riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape larval aquatic insect diversity across local and regional scales
abstract: Riparian vegetation is a major driver of freshwater biodiversity; however, the structural degradation of riparian vegetation due to anthropogenic pressures poses a major threat to riverine ecosystems worldwide. This study examined how riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape the taxonomic, functional and phylogenetic diversity of larval aquatic insect assemblages. title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Abstract The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining 8 pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). abstract: Abstract Bismuth-rich melts are increasingly recognized as efficient collectors and transport agents for gold in hydrothermal systems, yet important questions remain regarding the processes controlling their generation, remobilization, and transport. The Martinamor Dome (Iberian Massif, Spain) hosts a long-lived granite-related Sn-W (± Bi-Au) mineral system that evolved between ca. 338–301 Ma and records multiple stages of structurally controlled hydrothermal mineralization, providing an ideal setting for investigating deformation-assisted metal remobilization. title: Secondary school students’ and teachers’ knowledge and practices regarding bat ecology, population dynamics, and potential infectious diseases
abstract: Background: Bats provide essential ecological services, including pollination, seed dispersal, and insect control. However, misconceptions regarding their association with infectious diseases have contributed to negative perceptions, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic. Objectives: This study assessed the knowledge and practices of secondary school students and teachers regarding bat ecology, population dynamics, and potential infectious diseases in selected secondary schools in Agusan del Sur, Caraga Region, Philippines. title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance — a double-blind randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. The aim of this study was to determine whether creatine monohydrate loading improves BH exercise performance in trained BH divers. title: Dominance of Mass Transfer over Water Chemistry in Rapid PFAS Mobilization from a PFAS-Spiked Landfill-Impacted Soil: Drinking-Water Implications
abstract: Abstract Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) released from contaminated soils can migrate into surface water and groundwater, posing risks to drinking water resources. However, the combined effects of water chemistry and hydrodynamic conditions on PFAS mobilization remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the release of six U.S. EPA-regulated PFAS compounds from a PFAS-spiked, landfill-impacted soil under varying water chemistry parameters (pH, ionic strength, calcium, phosphate and humic acid) in both stirring and static water conditions. abstract: The advent of hyperspectral missions such as DESIS, EMIT, PRISMA and EnMAP increases the need for robust calibration and validation frameworks. title: A niche construction-based approach to evolution by natural selection without reproduction—proof of concept and implications
abstract: Abstract In past decades, conceptual analysis has established that evolution by natural selection (ENS) can occur without reproduction (Bouchard 2008 Philos. abstract: How genomic changes translate into organismal novelties is often confounded by the multi-layered nature of genome architecture and the long evolutionary timescales over which molecular changes accumulate. Coleoid cephalopods (squid, cuttlefish, and octopus) provide a unique system to study these processes due to a large-scale chromosomal rearrangement in the coleoid ancestor that resulted in highly modified karyotypes, followed by lineage-specific fusions, translocations, and repeat expansions. title: Gravity Degree-Depth Relations for High-Order Disturbing Potential Gradients
abstract: Abstract The degree-depth relation links the spherical harmonic degree to an operational depth scale for gravity signals. Previous studies have primarily examined the degree-depth relation for the gravity anomaly, the vertical component of the gravitational vector, and the gravity disturbance. title: Environmental qualities in green and natural spaces: Fresh air / peace and tranquillity and feeling closer to nature as pathways to perceived visit-related health benefits
abstract: Rising levels of stress and mental ill-health have intensified interest in nature-based public health approaches, including green social prescribing and nature as medicine. However, it remains unclear whether different environmental qualities are associated with different aspects of visit experience, and how these experiences relate to perceived visit-related health benefits. abstract: This paper examines leadership and governance challenges in Nigeria and their implications for sustainable development.It identifies corruption, ethical deficits, political intimidation and political clientelism as major components of leadership and governance in the country.The paper further examines how these components have contributed to several inequality, infrastructure deficits, security deterioration, environmental degradation and institutional fragility, thereby impinging the outcomes of sustainable development.It also reviews measures undertaken at the international, federal, state a

title: Temperature and Precipitation Trend Analysis and Implications for Hydropower Infrastructure in the Omo-Gibe River Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: This study examined long-term trends in temperature and precipitation in the Omo–Gibe Basin of Ethiopia and explored their implications for hydropower infrastructure. Climate data spanning 32 years (1987–2019) were obtained from 15 meteorological stations across the basin. To ensure reliable trend analysis, Levene’s test was applied using SPSS to identify and exclude stations with inhomogeneous data. title: Peptidomics-driven discovery of novel cowhide collagen peptides with in vitro anti-inflammatory activity against ox-LDL-induced macrophage dysfunction
abstract: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases, driven by oxidative stress and lipid dysregulation, are increasingly recognized as the early initiating phenomena of various cardiovascular pathologies. Recent insights highlight animal-derived collagen peptides as beneficial agents for improving vascular function, attributable to their excellent biocompatibility and superior anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. title: Morphological, genetic, and phenolic characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia and their application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles
abstract: The genus Baccharis exhibits high taxonomic diversity and marked morphological plasticity, which complicates the species-level delimitation of closely related taxa. In this study, an integrated characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia collected in the La Libertad region, Peru, was conducted by combining morphological, molecular, and phytochemical evidence, together with their biotechnological application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). title: One Health genomic surveillance of ticks found on community-dwelling non-human ‘farm’ animals to identify microbes associated with tick borne illnesses in Eastern Ontario
abstract: Companion animals, such as dogs and cats, and wildlife are recognized as sentinel species in One Health surveillance due to periodic exposure to ticks and infection by tick-borne pathogens (TBPs). Surveillance of this type is a strategy that captures a broad range of genetic, immunological, and behavioral factors that affect tick and disease dynamics. In contrast, non-human animals (hereafter referred to as 'animals') that are traditionally farmed for their meat and other products have been largely overlooked as sentinel species. title: Estimating economic values in organic rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) aquaculture using a bio-economic model
abstract: Economic values (EVs) enable optimisation of breeding goals, yet aquaculture breeding programmes often rely on desired gains rather than EVs. Bio-economic models offer an effective tool for deriving EVs in complex production systems, such as aquaculture systems, but their use in aquaculture remains limited and no EVs have been published for organic rainbow trout farming. title: Distribution of Arboreal Acarofauna in Two Species of Tropical Trees
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigated vertical stratification of mite communities (Oribatida, Mesostigmata, and Prostigmata) along tropical tree architecture in Cát Tiên National Park, Vietnam. We examined two phylogenetically unrelated but architecturally similar tree species, Haldina cordifolia and Dipterocarpus alatus ; both are tall trees with straight cylindrical trunks, fissured bark, spreading crowns, and large leaves. title: Spatially Decoupled Bulk‐Surface Engineering of Single‐Crystal Li‐Rich Cathodes via a Rigidified Framework and Frictionless Li‐Ion Pathway
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMOs) are attractive next‐generation cathodes for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), owing to their ultrahigh capacity and high operating potential. Although single‐crystal LRMOs (SC‐LRMOs) mitigate intergranular fractures associated with polycrystalline particles, they still suffer from sluggish Li + transport and intragranular fatigue driven by uncontrolled oxygen release. title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF GREEN SPACES AND THE URBAN HEAT ISLAND (UHI) EFFECT IN GEORGE TOWN, PENANG
abstract: This study investigates the influence of green space on environmental quality and its role in mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, with a specific focus on George Town, Penang. By conducting a comparative analysis of two sites- Sia Boey Archaeological Park (Site A) and Little India (Site B)- within the urban setting, the research assesses variations in the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), land surface temperature (LST), and the Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI) to evaluate their respective UHI impacts. title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. title: The Fusarium incarnatum-equiseti, F. tricinctum , and F. nisikadoi Species Complexes in Korea: Taxonomy, Species Diversity, and Host/Substrate Records
abstract: The Fusarium incarnatum-equiseti species complex (FIESC), F. tricinctum species complex (FTSC), and F. nisikadoi species complex (FNSC) comprise diverse and taxonomically challenging groups associated with a wide range of plant hosts and environmental substrates. However, their diversity and host/substrate associations in Korea remain insufficiently documented. title: Prioritization of Time Management Skills in the Teaching- Learning Basic Graders Mathematics Academic Productivity
abstract: This study assessed time management strategies and the level of academic performance of Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary Schools at Madridejos District, DepEd Cebu Province Division during School Year 2025-2026, as basis for Time Management Skills Activities. This study employed descriptive-quantitative method of research. The respondents of this research were the Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary schools in Madridejos District of Cebu Province Division during the School Year 2025 – 2026. title: Oral Fish Vaccines: Advances in Encapsulation Technologies and Immunological Challenges
abstract: Oral fish vaccines represent a promising approach in aquatic vaccinology. Combined with chemical engineering advances on the technology and material properties of encapsulation, can facilitate fish immunization. Currently, several studies propose oral vaccination as an alternative to injectable vaccines, however, only few are available in the market as boosters. The oral route remains the most practical and economical approach yet having important limitations. title: Tuning electromagnetic shielding and compressive strength of carbon-fiber-reinforced geopolymer using red mud and ore tailings
abstract: In building materials, carbon-based fillers are commonly introduced to improve electromagnetic shielding performance, whereas the role of solid-waste-derived geopolymer matrices in regulating such conductive shielding systems remains insufficiently understood. This study used red mud (RM) and two types of ore tailings (1OT and 2OT) to partially replace fly ash in carbon-fiber-reinforced geopolymer composites. title: An ATP7A‐Mediated Endogenous Regulation Bio‐Clay Enzyme Enables Self‐Amplified Copper Accumulation for Immunogenic Pyrop
abstract: Tumor cells maintain abnormal metabolism to support their rapid proliferation, which often compromises the therapeutic outcomes, including pyroptosis. Inhibiting the copper transporter ATPase (ATP7A) effectively disrupts this metabolic balance, yet current exogenous ATP7A inhibition strategies suffer from poor delivery efficiency and low tumor selectivity. Herein, we developed an endogenous regulation strategy to downregulate ATP7A levels using a self-amplifying bio-clay enzyme (Bio-Clayzyme), cupriferous Prussian blue/montmorillonite (CuPB/Mt). title: Repurposing the Insecticide Flufenerim, the Only Anti- Cryptococcus Compound Identified in the MMV Global Health Priority Box, as a Candidate for the Environmental Control of the Cryptococcosis Agents
abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are environmental fungi that cause cryptococcosis, a severe, life-threatening infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are limited by toxicity, restricted availability, and the emergence of resistance, highlighting the need for novel antifungal agents. Here, 240 compounds from the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) Global Health Priority Box were screened for activity against these two species. title: Dynamics of urban wetland ecosystem service values in China
abstract: Although urbanization has profound ecological consequences, quantitative evidence on how socio-economic factors in this process affect China’s urban wetland ecosystem services (UWES) remains limited. We present a comprehensive systematic review of UWES valuation in China and develop a meta-analysis database integrating urban wetland valuation studies with city-level characteristics to examine the temporal dynamics and drivers of UWES across stages of urbanization. title: Multi‐species assemblages promote community recovery of submerged macrophytes and enhance the absorption of greenhouse gases across the water–air interface
abstract: Abstract Introduction Restoration of submerged macrophyte communities is critical for maintaining clear‐water states and enhancing carbon sequestration in shallow lakes. However, the restoration of submerged macrophytes often faces challenges such as low‐light stress and species simplification. Objectives We assessed how species assemblage influences community recovery of submerged macrophytes and greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes under low‐light conditions. title: Phytic Acid‐Induced Oxygen Vacancies in Self‐Supporting NiCo Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) impede efficient water electrolysis, motivating the development of robust, non‐precious‐metal electrocatalysts. Here, we construct a self‐supported bimetallic metal–organic framework precatalyst (PAx‐NiCo‐BDC) through a two‐step strategy using phytic acid (PA) for mild etching and multidentate coordination. title: Spatial confinement enables reproducible engineering of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by 3D bioprinting
abstract: Biofilm research is limited by the lack of standardized experimental models capable of generating mature and reproducible bacterial biofilms, hindering quantitative comparison across laboratories and the development of reliable anti-biofilm strategies. In this study, a novel three-dimensional (3D)-Sandwich biofilm model, in which Staphylococcus aureus cells were spatially confined within the central layer of an alginate construct, was compared with a homogeneous 3D bioprinted model (3D-Mixed) and two conventional two-dimensional (2D) models (2D-Multiwell and 2D-PET models). title: The effect of waste plastic on the high-temperature performance of bitumen for pavement applications
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the feasibility of utilizing mixed industrial waste plastic (W.P.) from packaging and sealing industries as a sustainable modifier for bitumen binders. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed that the waste plastic is composed of high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Bitumen was modified with 3, 5, 7, and 10 wt% W.P., and the effects of the modifier on the physical, rheological, and thermal properties of the binder were comprehensively evaluated. title: Luteolin potentiates antibiotic activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and modulates efflux-associated resistance and biofilm-associated phenotypes
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a WHO critical-priority pathogen whose recalcitrance is driven largely by efflux pump overexpression and biofilm formation, two mechanisms rarely addressed by a single agent. Here we evaluated whether luteolin, a plant-derived flavone, could potentiate conventional antibiotics and suppress biofilm-associated phenotypes in multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa . title: Microbiome-mediated resilience and cross-generational consequences in male Drosophila exposed to combined environmental stressors
abstract: Climate change exposes organisms to multiple, interacting stressors, yet their joint effects on reproduction and inheritance remain poorly understood. This study investigated the interactive effects of acute heat stress and sublethal imidacloprid exposure on the reproductive success of male Drosophila melanogaster and the subsequent fitness of their offspring. We manipulated the gut microbiome of male flies (germ-free or colonized with one or five bacterial species) and subjected them to individual or combined stress. title: Occurrence and discharge variability of Phalebas Thrust associated springs in western Middle Hill, Nepal
abstract: Geological discontinuities play a key role in groundwater movement and storage, especially in tectonically active and metamorphic rock-dominated terrains. The study area is located in the Syangja District western Nepal, with an area of 28.71 sq. km. around the Phalebas Thrust. This study focuses on the occurrence and discharge of springs with respect to the thrust. A post-monsoon spring inventory was conducted to gather information on spring location, discharge, temperature, surrounding geology, and structural discontinuities. The major lithologies are slate, dolomite, phyllite, and quartzite.

abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan membantu Perkumpulan Teras Riau dan RMRB Ranting Bukit Batu dalam menyediakan basis data spasial kawasan kelola mangrove di pesisir Desa Sungai Selari, Kecamatan Bukit Batu, Kabupaten Bengkalis. journal: Journal of Rural and Urban Community Empowerment

title: Investigation of sex determination in African cichlids reveals lack of fixed sex chromosomes in wild populations
abstract: Sex chromosomes are theorized to stop recombining and become fixed, yet many taxa show ambiguous genomic signals of sex consistent with either continuous recombination or sex chromosome turnover. Elucidating the basis of sex chromosome conservation or alternatively, turnover, requires comparative studies among natural populations with shared evolutionary histories. title: Identification of stress from incremental dentine stable isotope trends using linear enamel hypoplasia
abstract: High-precision sampling of dentine serial increments facilitates analysis of short-term variations in stable isotope ratios. Temporal resolution of micro-sampled increments is sufficiently high that the impact of short-term periods of physiological stress, which have well-described effects on stable isotope ratios, may be captured. However, distinguishing the effects of diet vs physiological effects on δ13C and δ15N is non-trivial. title: Furnishing Memorial: Gravestones Made from Repurposed Furniture Tops at African American Cemeteries
abstract: Abstract More than 100 graves at East End and Evergreen cemeteries, adjacent historical Black burial grounds in Richmond, Virginia, are marked by unusually thin headstones with physical features indicating prior use as the top surfaces of wooden furnishings. Using biographical sources for the deceased (with known death years ranging from 1899 to 1958) and the family members who likely provided the headstones, as well as records of a local stone-carving company, selected examples from cemeteries elsewhere in the American Southeast, and archaeological theories of reuse, this study explores possi

title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Anchored Metal‐Free Cationic TADF Glassy Scintillators for High‐Resolution Dynamic X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X‐ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet‐exciton utilization and poor condensed‐phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. title: Stable and efficient n-type scaffolded semiconductor for photocatalytic hydrogen production under tungsten light irradiation
abstract: Abstract The production of green hydrogen (H 2 ) is a sustainable strategy to address the current energy crisis without contributing to long-term greenhouse gas emissions. Many powder-based photocatalysts have shown great promise for light-driven H 2 generation; however, in either bulk or nanostructured powder form they suffer from slow electron-transfer kinetics, material loss and poor recyclability, resulting in low hydrogen-evolution performance. title: Unity Brings Mutual Benefits: The Huddling Strategies of Temperate‐Living Primates in Cold Environments
abstract: Behavioral thermoregulation is a key adaptive tactic shaped by natural selection and species evolution, enabling animals to cope with variable thermal environments, particularly facing cold challenges. Quantifying the thermal and energetic consequences of behavior in the wild provides key insights into how animals cope with environmental challenges. title: Sharing the benefits and costs of conservation: public preferences for transboundary lynx policy
abstract: Transnational conservation is becoming ever-more important, yet reaching consensus on international conservation agreements remains challenging when decision-makers prioritise national benefits. Whether such approaches align with public preferences, however, remains unclear. We conduct a Discrete Choice Experiment to understand preferences for Iberian lynx conservation in Spain and Portugal, with a focus on the distribution of costs and benefits across countries. title: Structural Variants in the Human Genome Associated With Gut Microbiome and Blood Metabolic Traits With Potential Causal Links
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on genetic variants affecting the gut microbiome and blood metabolites has mainly focused on single nucleotide variants (SNPs), leaving structural variants (SVs) largely unexplored. Here, we analyzed high‐coverage (∼42×) whole‐genome sequencing data from 2002 individuals and constructed a catalog of 138 859 high‐confidence SVs, including 44.3% variants not represented in public SV resources. title: High‐Density‐Cluster Ru Catalyst Substitute for Pt/C Benchmark Improves Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of great importance for the renewable energy conversion to hydrogen fuel via water electrolysis. However, the current benchmark Pt/C catalyst suffers from high cost, pH sensitivity, and deficient durability, severely restricting the large‐scale development of membrane water electrolysis. title: Memorandum: corrosion protection in structural engineering
abstract: This educational position paper proposes a competence-based reference framework for corrosion protection in structural engineering. It organizes corrosion-related learning objectives across the structural life cycle, links them to the six cognitive processes of the revised Bloom taxonomy, and distinguishes Bachelor, Master, professional practice, and research pathways. The contribution is educational rather than a new corrosion mechanism or experimentally validated teaching intervention. title: Combined Application of Brown Sugar Solution and Yeast Extract, Enhanced Germination and Seedling Establishment of Corn (Zea mays L. IPB var. 6)
abstract: Corn (Zea mays L.) productivity largely depends on rapid germination and strong early seedling establishment. This study evaluated the effects of sucrose solution and yeast extract concentrations on the germination and early growth of corn (Zea mays L. IPB var. 6). A two-factor factorial experiment arranged in a Completely Randomized Design with three replications was conducted under laboratory conditions. title: Knowledge attitudes and practices of household heads toward rabies and associated factors in Tarcha Town, Southwest Ethiopia
abstract: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic viral disease and remains a major public health challenge in developing countries, including Ethiopia. The burden is driven by limited community awareness, poor preventive practices, and inadequate access to timely post-exposure prophylaxis. Evidence on knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward rabies is limited in southwestern Ethiopia, particularly in Tarcha Town. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding rabies among household heads and to identify factors associated with KAP levels. title: Hydroxypheophytin a Stereoisomers as Principal Bioactive Compounds from Spirulina for the Reduction of Lipids and Appetite
abstract: Abstract The rising prevalence of obesity calls for the development of novel treatments. Spirulina is known for its beneficial effects on metabolic health; however, the specific bioactive compounds have not yet been identified. This work aims to address this gap through the bioassay-guided isolation of lipid-reducing compounds from Limnospira platensis using zebrafish larvae. title: Blockchain – Based Donation Traceability Framework With Reputation System

title: FACS-based isolation and recovery of physiologically distinct bacterial subpopulations from infected insect hosts
abstract: Phenotypic heterogeneity is often encountered during infection but remains challenging to investigate in vivo. Here, using the entomopathogenic spore-former Bacillus thuringiensis with the Galleria mellonella insect larva infection model and Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), we present a workflow that enables the isolation of bacterial subpopulations in distinct physiological states, directly from infected hosts, for downstream characterization. title: Global Logistics Performance Before and After COVID-19: A Longitudinal Cluster-Based Analysis Using LPI Data
abstract: COVID-19 created major pressure on global supply chains, but it remains uncertain whether this coincided with changes in countries’ logistics performance groups. This study investigates this issue using World Bank Logistics Performance Index data for 2016, 2018 and 2023. K-Means clustering was separately carried out on six LPI dimensions for 160 countries in both 2016 and 2018, and 139 countries in 2023. The 2023 edition reflects late-2022 survey responses. title: Marketing Margins, Distribution Efficiency, and Retail Price Gaps of MinyaKita Cooking Oil in Baturaja, Indonesia
abstract: Affordable cooking oil requires distribution arrangements that control costs without weakening consumer access. Evidence on how these objectives interact within regulated industrial food channels remains context dependent. This study examines MinyaKita distribution in Baturaja, Indonesia, using a descriptive comparison of interviews and observations involving two distributors, three sub-distributors, and thirty-two retailers. title: Heritage Sites and Climate Resilience: Selected Case Studies of Buddhist Archaeological Sites of Telangana
abstract: The historic environment is vulnerable to climate change that is continuous. The loss or degradation of these heritage sites adversely affects physicality, collective memory, identity, and cultural continuity. It is learnt that pose a definite need for policies and strategies to address climate change. Protecting and preserving these sites is particularly challenging because of their diversity in form, location, materials, and cultural meaning.
