title: Revision of Central Asian Minnows (Cypriniformes: Pseudaspininae) Revealed a Novel Evolutionary Lineage of Generic Rank
abstract: Morphological and genetic revision of Central Asian minnows previously named as “Phoxinus” discovered a major novel evolutionary lineage of leuciscid fishes. According to both mitochondrial and nuclear DNA markers, the novel lineage is sister to large-sized fishes known as Altai osmans, the genus Oreoleuciscus; the high mtDNA p-distance between these lineages (0.113 ± 0.006) further supports the genetic distinctiveness of the new lineage. title: From Mexico to Argentina: Predicting the distribution of the invasive weed Tithonia tubaeformis beyond its native range using niche modelling
abstract: 1. Biological invasions are a major driver of global change, affecting biodiversity, ecosystem functioning and agricultural productivity. Tithonia tubaeformis (Asteraceae) is a weed native to Mexico that has become invasive in several regions worldwide, including Argentina, where it threatens crop systems. Here, we compared species distribution models trained with native- and invaded-range occurrences to estimate the potential distribution of T. tubaeformis in Argentina. title: Ultrasonic modification on the physicochemical properties, structure characterizations, and intestinal barrier-protective activities of raspberry polysaccharides
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess diverse biological functions, yet their macromolecular architecture frequently restricts molecular accessibility and limits their application as health-promoting ingredients. Here, we employed an ultrasound-driven strategy to remodel the molecular structure of raspberry polysaccharide (RAP) and investigated how controlled depolymerization governs its intestinal barrier-protective properties. title: A conceptual biocultural indicator framework for biodiversity in cultural landscapes: development and application in the Alhambra-Generalife-Albaicín (Spain) and Connemara (Ireland)
abstract: Abstract This paper develops a framework for the identification of biocultural indicators of biodiversity in cultural landscapes. To combat the persisting separation and dualistic conceptualisation of nature and culture in the heritage field, the framework views landscapes as dynamic assemblages of human and non-human actors. This highlights the significance of biocultural practices as indicators of how biodiversity emerges through the same human–environment relationships that give rise to both heritage and landscape over time. title: Water-scarcity footprints of industrial hydrogen production under Vietnam’s power-sector transition plan
abstract: Hydrogen can support industrial decarbonization, but its expansion may transfer environmental pressure to freshwater systems, where production in developing countries coincides with regional water scarcity. This study quantified the volumetric and scarcity-weighted blue-water implications of industrial hydrogen production under Vietnam's 2030 and 2050 power-sector transition scenarios. title: Green infrastructure in metropolitan planning: a comparative analysis of the plans of three European capitals
abstract: Green infrastructure has become a central axis of contemporary spatial planning. However, European cities display significant differences in the way they conceptualise and classify their green systems. This article comparatively analyses the conceptual frameworks and typologies of green infrastructure present in three reference planning documents: the Plan de Infraestructura Verde y Biodiversidad of Madrid, the London Environment Strategy of the Mayor of London, and the Berlin documentary ensemble formed by the Charta für das Berliner Stadtgrün and the Handlungsprogramm Berliner Stadtgrün 2030

title: Light‐Controlled Localized Delamination and Blistering of Azobenzene‐Containing Polymer Thin Films in an Aqueous Environment
abstract: ABSTRACT Blister formation in thin polymer films represents a localized delamination instability whereby interfacial failure leads to out‐of‐plane deformation of the supported film. It is relevant to coating failure, adhesion control, and directed surface patterning. Photoresponsive azopolymer films provide a unique model system, since mechanical stresses can be generated and tuned remotely by light. title: Time and Timelessness in Alexander's Search for Beauty
abstract: This paper explores Christopher Alexander’s theory of architecture and urban planning through the lens of time and timelessness. In so doing it traces his development from early systems thinking to his later metaphysical conception of living structure. It situates his work within the context of 20th-century urban thought and highlights his critique of mechanistic planning in favour of adaptive, participatory, and generated structures. title: What is the upper-bound circularity performance of wind turbine blade recycling? A comparative assessment of mechanical, thermal, and chemical routes under current and optimised conditions
abstract: The rapid deployment of wind energy is creating an end-of-life challenge for wind turbine blades (WTBs), whose large size and composite structure constrain recycling and material recovery. Existing studies compare WTB recycling technologies but rarely estimate upper-bound circularity performance under explicit technological, material-quality and substitution conditions. title: Thermochemical conversion of water hyacinth biomass into biochar and value-added products: mechanical design and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract The uncontrolled proliferation of water hyacinth in freshwater ecosystems represents a persistent environmental and energy-related challenge. While numerous biomass utilization strategies have been reported, the development of validated thermochemical conversion systems capable of transforming this invasive resource into stable value-added products remains limited. title: Protective responses and implications for vaccine designs against arboviruses in China: a 2026 perspective
abstract: Arboviruses have remained a persistent public health challenge, with their impact intensified by climate change, globalization, and vector expansion. As of 2026, China faces evolving threats from mosquito-borne viruses, including Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Japanese Encephalitis (JEV), and Chikungunya (CHIKV). This updated review synthesizes recent advancements in understanding human immune responses, pathogenesis, and vaccine development, with a particular focus on China’s unique epidemiological situation. title: Implications and Risks of Irregular Migration for Security, Stability, and Development in Libya
abstract: This article examines the implications of irregular migration for security, societal stability, and development in Libya, with particular attention to the country’s position as a country of origin, transit, and destination along Mediterranean migration routes. The analysis draws on a qualitative documentary review of historical scholarship, Libyan legal literature, institutional reports, and international policy materials, with particular emphasis on developments following the political and security crisis of 2011. abstract: Yenagoa, the riverine capital of Bayelsa State in Nigeria's Niger Delta, sits at the intersection of two compounding environmental stressors: climate-induced flooding and five decades of oil- and gas-related pollution. This paper applies the environmental justice (EJ) framework comprising distributive, procedural, and recognitional dimensions to examine how the burdens of these overlapping hazards are distributed across the city's population. abstract: Abstract Groundwater-level fluctuations are commonly used as recharge indicators because groundwater-level rises are often assumed to represent additions of recently recharged water to aquifer storage. In heterogeneous, multilayer aquifer systems, this assumption remains uncertain because groundwater-level variations may also reflect hydraulic connectivity, pressure transmission, storage redistribution, and groundwater mixing. abstract: The Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis International Database (BIAID) is an initiative aimed at pooling, standardizing and harmonizing bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) data across populations. This report provides a synthesis of the data currently available in the BIAID and an overview of the actions undertaken to date. title: Where did the language of the northeastern Estonian Poluverniki come from?
abstract: This study examines the linguistic origins of the historical community of Poluverniki in northeastern Estonia. Members of this group were typically bilingual and spoke a distinctive blend of dialectal Russian and Estonian. The prevailing scholarly view — based largely on non‑linguistic evidence — holds that the Poluverniki descended from a Votic‑like Southern Finnic population that was later linguistically assimilated by neighboring Russian dialects. abstract: Persea americana (Lauraceae) is a fruit widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, commonly known as the avocado. Although the seeds represent a considerable portion of the whole fruit, scientific research on their phytochemistry and biological effects is still in its early stages. abstract: The avian retina presents an elegant and highly accessible model for investigating the spatial and temporal dynamics of neurogenesis within the central nervous system. In recent years, the microtubule cytoskeleton has emerged not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a dynamic regulator of the transition of a morphologically homogeneous pool of multipotent progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons. abstract: Purpose: This descriptive pilot maps local-government capacity gaps and, in parallel, MSME resilience and digital readiness across four island subdistricts in Pangkep. abstract: The article follows the journey of the Pergamon/Zeus Altar from Bergama (present-day Turkey) to Berlin in the late nineteenth century and its reverberations in the present. title: A zebrafish model of NEXMIF-related encephalopathy identified drivers of hyperlocomotion and provides a scalable platform for drug discovery
abstract: X-linked Intellectual Disability type 98 (XLID-98) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with a broad phenotypic spectrum caused by pathogenic variants in the neurite extension and migration factor ( NEXMIF ) gene, formerly known as KIAA2022, KIDLIA , or XPN (OMIM 300524). abstract: Mountain tourism geosites, as a form of nature-based and adventure tourism, provide authentic experiences through hiking, crater exploration, scenic panoramas, and adventure activities. These experiences allow tourists to encounter natural landscapes while developing a sense of challenge, freedom, and connection with nature. This study aims to analyze the influence of attractiveness, accessibility, and perceived risk on tourist satisfaction and revisit intention. title: A standardized permafrost ground temperature collection for Canada 2025
abstract: Abstract. Ground temperature is an essential variable for monitoring the thermal state of permafrost, developing models, and conducting fundamental research. However, the usability of GT data in Canada is often hampered by inconsistent file formats, a lack of metadata standardization between organizations, and varied temporal resolutions. This fragmentation has prevented the development of a comprehensive benchmark dataset, leaving researchers reliant on small, ad-hoc data subsets for model evaluation. abstract: ABSTRACT High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. title: Assessing the Mining Effluent Impacts on Mercury Dynamics in Boreal Lakes
abstract: Abstract Mining wastewater and leakages into freshwater systems are a growing global concern, yet the impacts of bioleaching in open-pit mining on lake food webs and mercury dynamics remain understudied. This study examined three boreal lakes in eastern Finland: Jormasjärvi (primarily previously mining-impacted), Nuasjärvi (currently impacted), and Kiantajärvi (control). title: Fuel debris detection system using in-situ measurements of gamma rays and neutrons for investigation of fuel debris distribution
abstract: This paper presents a compact, integrated system for in-situ detection of fuel debris via simultaneous gamma-ray and neutron measurements, developed for application within the primary containment vessel (PCV) of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 1. The system combines a miniaturized CdTe detector with 100-ns signal processing for gamma-ray spectroscopy and a compact B-10 proportional counter structually designed to suppress its gamma-ray response, both enclosed in a shielded container weighing less than 8 kg. abstract: Research on the oral–gut axis has progressed from association studies to mechanistic understanding. However, the pathways by which oral-derived microorganisms, metabolites, and inflammatory signals traverse gastrointestinal barriers and affect intestinal homeostasis remain poorly defined. title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved. abstract: The ability to monitor the proliferative status of live cells both in vitro and in vivo over time has revolutionised our understanding of development, growth and disease. This was first made possible by fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell cycle indicator (Fucci) technology, which distinguishes specific cell cycle phases through the reciprocal degradation of fluorescently tagged, truncated forms of human CDT1 and GMNN proteins. title: The complete chloroplast genome of Erigeron sumatrensis (Asteraceae): genomic features and phylogenetic implications
abstract: Erigeron sumatrensis Retz. (Asteraceae) is an annual herb native to South America that has become a noxious invasive weed in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. Here, we report the first complete chloroplast genome of this plant species. The chloroplast genome is 152,974 bp in length and exhibits a typical quadripartite structure, consisting of a large single-copy (LSC) region of 84,615 bp, a small single-copy (SSC) region of 18,335 bp, and a pair of inverted repeat (IR) regions of 25,012 bp each. abstract: Abstract Objective RAP‐219, a potent selective negative allosteric modulator (NAM) of α‐amino‐3‐hydroxy‐5‐methyl‐4‐isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) associated with γ8 transmembrane AMPAR regulatory protein (TARPγ8), is in phase 3 development for refractory focal epilepsy. abstract: The intensive use of pesticides in agriculture has raised concerns regarding human health, biodiversity, and ecosystem functioning. This observational study evaluated how Conventional Management (CM), characterized by frequent insecticide applications (approximately 7–9 treatments per lettuce crop cycle), and Integrated Pest Management (IPM), characterized by reduced pesticide use (approximately 2–3 treatments per cycle), were associated with insect communities in lettuce crops in the Pan de Azúcar region, Chile. title: Dual Fluorophore System for Direct Measurement of Acidity of Aerosol Particles
abstract: Atmospheric aerosol particles exhibit diverse physical and chemical properties, depending on their composition and source, which are challenging to measure directly due to their chemical complexity. Aerosol acidity is a key chemical property that has significant implications for climate, heterogeneous chemistry, and human health. Here, we present a novel approach to measure aerosol acidity using carbon dots (CDs) as in situ fluorophores. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Chinese export porcelain as a site of transcultural image production and proposes motif migration as an empirically grounded framework within global art history. Focusing on the Maritime Silk Road from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, the study moves away from diffusionist and hybridity‐based explanations that frame decorative imagery as either copied or stylistically merged. title: EVALUATION OF OZONE THERAPY AS AN ADJUVANT METHOD IN THE TREATMENT OF ODONTOGENIC INFECTIONS
abstract: Ozone therapy has been investigated as an adjunctive approach in dentistry because of its antimicrobial properties and potential modulation of inflammatory responses. This exploratory randomized clinical trial evaluated ozonated water as an adjunct to standard treatment for severe odontogenic infections, compared with 0.9% normal saline (NS). abstract: 1. Human perceptions and knowledge are relevant to the management of environmental conflicts involving wildlife. At the forest-urban interface of northern Patagonia, expanding human settlements increase contact with wildlife, including owls and hantavirus reservoir rodents, altering habitat for both predators and prey, and exposing owls to toxicological threats due to rodent-control practices.2. abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. abstract: Abstract Composite photocatalysts were developed from hydrothermally synthesized barium titanate (BaTiO 3 , BTO) and zinc oxide (ZnO), combined by ultrasonic mixing in ethanol followed by calcination, and applied to remove a quaternary mixture of persistent pollutants in wastewater (ciprofloxacin (CIP), tetracycline (TC), methylene blue (MB), and methyl orange (MO)) in a heterogeneous photocatalysis process. abstract: Raw hyperspectral imaging (HSI) data require multiple processing steps before physically meaningful reflectance products can be derived. Quality issues at the radiance level – e.g., detector artifacts, low-signal regions, or excessive noise – can propagate through the processing chain and compromise subsequent analyses. abstract: Art toys have become highly influential across Asia, particularly in China, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, where culturally inspired character design has been used to strengthen tourism branding and enhance community product value, generating economic impact worth billions of baht. abstract: Abstract Most biological control programmes against invasive alien plants (weeds) utilise agents collected from indigenous populations of the target weed that are thought to have a long coevolution history between the target weed and the agent. These biocontrol agents are referred to as old associations. abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is an acute zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses. title: Species traits mediate terrestrial mammal density responses to human impacts
abstract: Human activities are reshaping ecosystems, but their effects on species population density remain poorly understood. Most studies focus on species presence–absence, thus limiting insight into how anthropogenic pressures affect population density. Emerging evidence suggests that responses of natural populations to human disturbance are highly variable, often contingent on species‐specific traits. abstract: Abstract Any single ecosystem will provide many ecosystem functions. Whether these functions tend to increase in concert or trade off against each other is a question of much current interest. Equally topical are the drivers behind ecosystem function rates. Yet, we lack large-scale systematic studies that investigate how abiotic factors can directly or indirectly — via effects on biodiversity — drive ecosystem functioning. abstract: Abstract Adhesion between thermosetting and semicrystalline thermoplastic polymers depends not only on interfacial chemistry but also on the spatial distribution of reaction products across the interface, yet how polymer crystallinity controls this distribution remains unclear. Here, we investigate how the crystallinity of polyamide 6 (PA6) controls the development of interfacial reaction zones and adhesion strength at epoxy resin (ER)/PA6 interfaces. title: Dispersal diversity buffers species vulnerability to local extinction
abstract: Predicting species persistence within ecological communities is a fundamental challenge for both empirical and theoretical ecology. Existing methods span from mechanistic models, whose parameters are difficult to estimate from data, to statistical tools whose context-specific parameters are less interpretable. abstract: This study investigates how Open Innovation Orientation contributes to adaptive island resilience through Renewable Energy Tourism Attractiveness, Green Innovation Capability, and Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem in Koh Larn Island, Thailand, and Jeju Island, South Korea. abstract: At the Ptolemaic Temple of 'Horus Behdet' at Edfu, Upper Egypt, the ‘legend of the Winged Disk’ is written on the walls and describes the battles between Horus and Seth. abstract: La taxonomía de los murciélagos neotropicales ha experimentado una rápida reorganización en los últimos años, frecuentemente impulsada por el descubrimiento de divergencia genética previamente no reconocida y la descripción de nuevas especies. abstract: ABSTRACT Shrub encroachment is rapidly transforming alpine meadow ecosystems worldwide, yet its consequences for belowground microbial organization remain insufficiently understood, particularly when different shrub species exert contrasting ecological effects. Here, we investigated how three dominant shrub species— Rhododendron capitatum , Salix oritrepha , and Dasiphora fruticosa —influence soil fungal communities across encroachment gradients in an alpine meadow on the northeastern Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. abstract: El estudio determinó la relación entre la planificación y control de proyectos tecnológicos y la gestión de la innovación tecnológica en unidades educativas particulares del cantón Milagro. title: Degradation of graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles by hypochlorite: impacts on physicochemical properties, antimicrobial activity and ecotoxicity
abstract: Abstract Graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles (GO-AgNPs) is a promising hybrid material for development of composites, sensors, catalysts, and antimicrobial systems. However, its degradation and life cycle remain poorly understood. Here, the chemical degradation of GO-AgNPs was investigated by sodium hypochlorite (bleach water) linked to its antimicrobial and ecotoxicological effects. This oxidative degradation was monitored up to 10 days at room temperature, revealing a progressive transformation of both components of the hybrid material. institutions: Brazilian Center for Research in Energy and Materials

title: Assessing climate change perceptions and climate-smart agriculture adoption among root, tuber and banana farmers in Eastern D.R. Congo
abstract: Perceptions shape human practices, including agricultural decisions, yet their influence on climate-smart agriculture adoption remains insufficiently understood in climate-vulnerable eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This study compared farmers’ perceptions of climate change with empirical climate data of the past three decades across South-Kivu’s agroecological zones (AEZ), eastern DRC. abstract: Abstract Background This surveillance study evaluated the polymorphisms of Pfk13 gene in samples from symptomatic individuals from eight geographically distinct locations in Kenya to determine the prevalence of mutations associated with partial artemisinin resistance. Methods Between 2018 and 2024, blood samples from individuals with symptoms of uncomplicated malaria at eight hospitals in four of the five distinct malaria transmission zones of Kenya were sequenced for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Pfk13 and Pfmdr1 . title: Safety as a strategic element of tourist destination branding to strengthen resilience in crisis conditions
abstract: The relevance of this study stems from the growing importance of safety in shaping the tourist appeal of regions amidst global instability, military risks and tourists’ heightened sensitivity to threats. The aim of the article was to provide a theoretical justification for the role of safety as a strategic element of tourism destination branding and to elucidate the mechanism through which it influences the formation of a region’s image, tourists’ trust, their intentions and the resilience of destinations in crisis conditions. title: Efficient Bipolar Hydrogen Peroxide Production Through Photoelectrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias‐free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H 2 O 2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H 2 O 2 production. title: Correlation of the Electrodeposition Parameters, Structural Features and Magnetic Properties of the Co-based Ternary Alloys

title: The Role of the Regional Spatial Plan (RTRW) in Preserving Environmental Sustainability in North Sulawesi Province
abstract: Regional development is essential to improving public welfare, yet poorly planned spatial development can threaten environmental sustainability. Although previous studies have examined spatial planning, environmental protection, and spatial law enforcement, limited attention has been given to the gap between regional spatial planning regulations and their implementation in maintaining environmental functions in North Sulawesi. This study aims to analyze local government policies on spatial planning and evaluate the implementation of regional spatial plans in protecting environmental functions.

title: Impact of Urban Air Pollution and Climatic Factors on Photovoltaic Performance: A Comparative Modelling Study Across Major Indian Cities
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems play an important role in India's transition towards renewable energy. However, their performance can be significantly influenced by environmental conditions that vary across different urban regions. This study investigates the impact of urban pollution and climatic conditions on photovoltaic efficiency in four Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur, and Bangalore. The research sought to answer three primary questions: (1) How do climatic variables such as temperature, humidity, solar irradiation, sunshine hours, and cell temperature affect PV efficiency? journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: Southern South American maize landraces: a source of phenotypic diversity
abstract: Abstract Maize ( Zea mays L.) is a globally important crop for food, feed, and industrial uses. Modern breeding increasingly targets traits beyond yield, including stress tolerance, nutritional quality, and pest resistance. Progress toward these goals is constrained by the narrow genetic diversity of commercial varieties, a consequence of the repeated use of a limited number of inbred lines. Maize landraces therefore represent valuable reservoirs of genetic and phenotypic diversity. title: Computerized Study of the Naval Electric Power Flow
abstract: Modelling and design of the naval electric power system (NEPS) represents a complete and great importance task, giving information for the generation, transmission and distribution system. NEPS is very complex as configuration, but also as technical electrical analysis. title: Tube-in-tube hollow RuCrMn oxide nanofibers for noble-metal-efficient oxygen evolution via Cr/Mn-regulated Ru active sites
abstract: Reducing the Ru content while maintaining high oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity remains a major challenge. In this study, single phase Ru 0.30 Cr 0.31 Mn 0.39 O 2 nanofibers were prepared through electrospinning process followed by temperature-regulated heat treatment. The temperature regulation process induces a unique formation of a hollow tube-in-tube structure while simultaneously influencing crystallinity and defect distribution. title: Energy expenditure of bonobos across their locomotor repertoire
abstract: Unlike quadrupedal mammals, primates use diverse locomotor modes adapted to arboreal environments. Such diversity of movements challenges allometric models, which underestimate energetic costs by focusing on steady-state walking. To address this, we combined ethological and biomechanical approaches to estimate the net metabolic cost of transport in bonobos (Pan paniscus). Using three-dimensional tracking and a point-mass model, we derived this estimate from net mechanical power and muscle efficiency across locomotor modes. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Decontamination Risk Management in Radioisotope Facilities: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: Background: Risk management in the decontamination process of radioisotope and radiopharmaceutical production facilities has garnered significant research attention due to its vital contribution to environmental safety and occupational health. While the volume of literary evidence regarding radiation safety continues to expand, study focuses and methodological approaches remains diverse. Objectives: This bibliometric analysis was conducted on decontamination risk management literature to broadly understand research patterns and directions. title: Analysis of bacteriophage diversity in Ganga river ecosystem: insights from metagenome-based sequencing
abstract: Water from the Ganga River and its tributaries is the main freshwater resource in the northern parts of India and has experienced rigorous ecological deterioration because of the continuous discharge of untreated polluted industrial and household effluents, resulting in increased chemical and microbial loads of pollution. Water is an essential requirement for millions of people and supports a complex ecosystem that includes a variety of microbial species. title: Putative functional redundancy in cyanobacterial microbiomes allows stable bioplastic production despite shifts in dominant populations
abstract: This study investigates whether a single initial cyanobacterial microbiome, originating from a mixed community, retains its capacity for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production under non-sterile long-term operation when subjected to cultivation conditions that promote different dominant cyanobacterial populations. title: Spatiotemporal patterns of antimicrobial resistance in shared human-animal waterpoints in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem, Kenya
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents an existential One Health threat. The spread of AMR in arid and semi-arid landscapes is modulated by ecological interactions and exacerbated by endemicity of livestock diseases and poor sanitation in shared human-animal systems leading to misuse of antibiotics. This study characterized the prevalence, resistance patterns, and spatiotemporal variations of AMR in surface water sources in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem (MME), a rapidly changing water-stressed socio-ecological landscape. Employing cross-sectional study design, water samples were collected from 28

title: Bayesian local clustering of functional data via semi-Markovian random partitions
abstract: We introduce a Bayesian framework for indirect local clustering of functional data, leveraging B-spline basis expansions and a novel dependent random partition model. By exploiting the local support properties of B-splines, our approach allows partially coincident functional behaviors, achieved when shared basis coefficients span sufficiently contiguous regions. This is accomplished through a cutting-edge dependent random partition model that enforces semi-Markovian dependence across a sequence of partitions. journal: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

title: p‐Block Aluminum Tailoring Termination‐Acidity of Two‐Dimensional MoS 2 Nanosheets for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) has shown promising electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity in acidic electrolyte, while its high‐pH alkaline HER performance is critically poor due to the sluggish water dissociation kinetics. Herein, utilizing local oxygen coordination brought by p‐block aluminum (Al 3+ ) cations, we report a termination‐acidity tailoring strategy to optimize the surface chemistry of MoS 2 catalyst to construct an acid‐like interface. title: FBMN-Guided Discovery of Cyanogrisides from Mutant Strain CRM005 and Structural Diversification
abstract: Abstract Through genome mining and metabolomic analysis of the mutant strain CRM005, combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) deduplication, five novel natural cyanogrisides (1–5) were selectively isolated and characterized, alongside six previously reported analogs (6–11). Antiproliferative assays demonstrated that cyanogriside K (8) exhibited potent and selective cytotoxicity against HCT-116 cells, with an IC50 value of 0.70 μM. Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: In the beginning was the name: naming and framing sustainable cultural tourism destinations in peripheral areas
abstract: Early-stage tourism development in peripheral areas often takes place under ‘below-zero’ conditions, where tourism is weakly established, place identities fragmented, and conventional branding strategies premature. In such contexts, the name of a place and its associated communicative framings become a first vital connector between potential visitors, local stakeholders, and the area itself. This article examines how naming and framing processes operate under these conditions and how they can be diagnosed and engaged to support sustainable cultural tourism development. journal: Journal of Policy Research in Tourism Leisure and Events

title: Differences in microbial composition and salt tolerance between rhizosphere and bulk soil of Kalidium foliatum
abstract: Salt is an important abiotic stress that affects plant growth. Research has shown that plants can recruit beneficial microorganisms from the surrounding soil. However, the ecological functions of the rhizosphere microbiome in salt tolerant plants have not been explored to a large extent. title: Periodic and aperiodic particle-reinforced composite-inspired metamaterials: Compressive and flexural properties
abstract: Traditional particle-reinforced composite materials face several challenges such as particle agglomeration, poor interfacial load transfer that can lead to premature failure, manufacturing complexities, and increased weight. Motivated by these limitations, this work designs, additively manufactures, and tests new classes of periodic and aperiodic particle-reinforced composite-like metamaterials (PRCM). title: Low-Resource Materials: Rethinking Resource Sustainability in the Construction Sector
abstract: In the European context of the ecological transition, the construction sector urgently requires a shift from resource depletion to preservation. This study addresses the heterogeneity of the definition of natural, artificial, renewable, and non-renewable resources in the literature, establishing a coherent framework. Based on the analysis of these definitions, the study delineates the concept of Low-Resource Materials (LRMs) as a dynamic repertoire characterised by renewable, restorable, reused, and recycled components aimed at safeguarding material assets. title: Energy-saving hydrogen production coupled with PET-derived ethylene glycol oxidation: Reaction mechanisms, catalyst design, and reactor engineering
abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), derived from PET hydrolysis, offers a thermodynamically favorable alternative to the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and can be coupled with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) to simultaneously produce value-added chemicals and H2. title: Challenges and trends in hydrogen production by electrolysis
abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has intensified research into hydrogen production via water electrolysis. In this context, this review provides an integrative analysis of recent advances in electrolytic hydrogen production, emphasizing electrocatalytic materials, electrolyte composition, process efficiency, techno‐economic feasibility, and the use of alternative feedstocks. title: The vitamin D paradox: Strong associations, weak clinical benefits
abstract: Vitamin D occupies a paradoxical position in contemporary medicine. Low circulating concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] are consistently associated with numerous adverse health outcomes, including cancer, cardiovascular disease (CVD), fractures, and autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs). Despite these epidemiological associations, large Randomized controlled trials and genetic-causal analyses have repeatedly failed to demonstrate substantial clinical benefits from vitamin D supplementation for several of these conditions. journal: Indian Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmacology

title: Observation of Daily Flood Hazard During the SWOT Cal/Val Orbit
abstract: Abstract Flood peaks can develop and recede within a day, making them difficult to capture with satellites with multi‐day revisit intervals. Here, we exploit daily observations during the Calibration and Validation phase of the SWOT mission to examine a short‐lived flood in May 2023 along the Du Gouffre River in Canada. Despite channel widths below 100 m, SWOT tracked day‐to‐day changes in water surface elevation, capturing a rapid rise of approximately 5 m consistent in timing and magnitude with in situ measurements. We derived flood extent based on classification and confidence information.

title: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
abstract: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. title: Under-platformization: platform literacy and the interplay between multiple actors in developing rural e-commerce in Central and Western China
abstract: Abstract Rural e-commerce in China’s central and western regions is often framed as a scalable pathway to rural revitalization. Yet, platformization may also stall, even when there is already a profitable rural industry. Drawing on interviews, fieldwork, and local archives, we examine the Bai silver handicraft cluster in Xinhua Village, Yunnan Province, which despite being a nationally recognized Taobao village, still exhibits under-platformization. title: Partial purification, experimental characterization of L-arginase from Alcaligenes aquatilis BC2 and determination of in vitro anticancer activity
abstract: L-arginase catalyzes the hydrolysis of L-arginine into L-ornithine and urea and plays a key role in the urea cycle. Interest in microbial L-arginases has increased because of their potential biotechnological and biomedical applications, including arginine-deprivation approaches in cancer research. In this study, extracellular L-arginase from Alcaligenes aquatilis BC2 was partially purified and biochemically characterized. title: Resilient skies: developing sustainable key performance indicators for airport operation and maintenance under public–private partnership frameworks in Egypt
abstract: The Egyptian airport sector has faced an 18% gap in operation and maintenance (O&M) efficiency relative to Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) benchmarks. This gap has driven a strategic shift toward Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) to improve efficiency and attract private investment. This study develops sustainable key performance indicators (KPIs) for O&M agreements at Egyptian airports. institutions: Modern Academy for Engineering and Technology

title: Narrativas de desapontamento em megaobras de urbanização turística
abstract: Embora as megaobras de urbanização turística e engordamento artificial de praias sejam frequentemente promovidas como soluções técnicas para a erosão costeira e o desenvolvimento territorial, seus efeitos sobre a experiência dos usuários e as tensões sociais geradas por essas intervenções permanecem subexploradas. Este artigo analisa as narrativas de desapontamento e insatisfação associadas a uma grande intervenção costeira realizada no Brasil entre 2022 e 2025. title: Analysis of the frequency of wildlife seizures carried out by PROFEPA during the period 2008-2018 in Yucatán, Mexico
abstract: Background. Wildlife represents a natural resource of major ecological, economic, cultural, and social importance. However, illegal extraction and unauthorized trade constitute significant threats to many species. In Mexico, few studies have systematically documented wildlife seizures conducted by environmental authorities. Objective. To analyze wildlife seizures carried out by the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (PROFEPA) in Yucatán, Mexico, during the period 2008–2018 to identify temporal patterns and the faunal groups most affected. title: Evolution of Nuclear Receptors as Environmental Chemical Sensors: Structural Innovation and Signaling Expansion
abstract: Abstract Nuclear receptors (NRs) are a superfamily of ligand-regulated transcription factors that translate chemical signals to gene regulatory responses. Although traditionally viewed through the lens of endocrinology, mounting evolutionary and comparative evidence demonstrate that nuclear receptors originated as environmental chemical sensors long before the emergence of complex hormonal systems. title: Effect of the Stepped Parallel Groove Number and Surface Roughness on Friction Enhancement of Rubber Blocks in Glycerol Solutions
abstract: Abstract In work environments where walking surfaces may be contaminated by liquid, safety footwear must provide high slip resistance. One method to enhance friction on wet or contaminated interfaces is to regulate fluid pressure through surface texturing of the footwear outsole. However, the optimal texture geometry and distribution for achieving high friction, as well as the effect of rubber surface roughness on texture performance, remain unclear. title: Hydrogel mechanics across application domains: a regime-based framework for rational design
abstract: Hydrogel technologies have rapidly evolved from simple hydrated materials to multifunctional systems for soft robotics, drug delivery, tissue engineering and surgical simulation. As their complexity increases, designing hydrogels for a specific application requires identifying which mechanical phenomena govern material behaviour under the relevant operating conditions, rather than optimising individual properties in isolation. title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal‐Bacteria Interactions
abstract: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. title: Using Whole Genome Sequencing to Decipher the Metschnikowia pulcherrima Complex
abstract: Metschnikowia pulcherrima, an ascomycetous yeast, has been frequently isolated from various substrates associated with agriculture such as nutrient-rich plant materials (fruit, fruit juices and fermenting grape must), soil and with various insects including fruit flies. Due to the growing consumer demand for wines with reduced levels of additives such as sulphites, there has been great interest in this yeast species for its ability to compete with other fungi. title: Designing a multifunctional peptide with biofilm-disrupting and fibroblast migration-promoting activities for infection management
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain difficult to manage due to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens and the persistence of biofilm-based infections. Thus, novel therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotics are needed. In this study, we designed a multifunctional antimicrobial peptide, TR‑MOD, based on venom gland–specific transcriptomic data from the spider Araneus ventricosus . abstract: Abstract Background Global identity (GI), a sense of belonging to a global society, is gaining attention as a key factor for promoting pro‐environmental behaviours (PEB) to tackle the global environmental crisis. Among such global predicaments, plastic waste and pollution remain pressing issues. Although prior research has established a link between GI and PEB, the underlying psychological pathways have not been comprehensively explored. title: Programming multiconfiguration into bistable robots via traversable energy landscapes
abstract: Abstract Soft robots using bistable structures often face limitations due to a fixed energy landscape, which restricts their configurational adaptability and functional diversity. To address this challenge, we introduce an energy-landscape-traversing (ELTra) bistable structure that enables on-demand reconstruction of the energy landscape, continuous stabilization of intermediate states, and precise modulation of energy release, capabilities that are challenging to achieve with conventional systems. title: Integrated adsorption–membrane process for lithium recovery from shale gas flowback fluid
abstract: Shale gas fracturing flowback fluid represents a promising unconventional lithium resource with concentrations reaching industrial grades, while simultaneously presenting significant wastewater treatment challenges. This study systematically investigates the complete research chain from flowback fluid characteristic analysis through extraction technology optimization to engineering feasibility validation, with particular emphasis on environmental sustainability and circular economy principles. title: Home Learning Support and Parenting Style as Factors in the Academic Performance of Grade 1 Learners of Hinatuan North Central Elementary School, Schools Division of Surigao del Sur: A Descriptive-Correlational Approach
abstract: This study examined the relationship between home learning support, parenting style, and academic achievement among Grade 1 learners at Hinatuan North Central Elementary School, Schools Division of Surigao del Sur, during School Year 2025–2026. Employing a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, the study involved 74 parents or guardians whose responses were analyzed alongside learners’ academic achievement obtained from official school records. title: First cytogenetic characterization of the southern pygmy perch Nannoperca australis (Teleostei: Percichthyidae): Karyotype, heterochromatin and repetitive DNA organization
abstract: Abstract Chromosome organization and repetitive DNA distribution are important components of genome evolution in teleost fishes but remain poorly characterized in many species of ecological and conservation relevance. We performed a detailed cytogenetic analysis of the southern pygmy perch, Nannoperca australis , a small freshwater species widely used in studies of population structure and evolutionary ecology in southeastern Australia. institutions: Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Animal Physiology and Genetics

title: Superpiles: The Impact of Mantle Temperature on Large Low Velocity Provinces
abstract: Abstract Among the most prevalent features in Earth's deep mantle are the Large Low Velocity Provinces (LLVPs), hypothesized to be hotter and compositionally distinct from the surrounding mantle. LLVPs have previously been viewed as either active superplumes rising through the mantle or passive piles shaped by large scale convection. title: Synergistic synthesis optimisation and B-site substitution engineering boost low-temperature CO oxidation over LaFeO 3 perovskite catalysts
abstract: This study develops a dual strategy of synthesis optimisation and B-site substitution to improve low-temperature CO oxidation of LaFeO3 perovskites. A modified co-precipitation method uses organic additives (F127, sucrose, citric acid) as surface area promoters and an ammonia precipitant. title: Comitative-based inclusory constructions in Lithuanian and their cross-linguistic background
abstract: In this contribution, I examine Lithuanian constructions of the type mes/jūs/jie su X ʻwe/you/they with Xʼ that refer to only two participants. title: From Guided-Tour Priorities to Tourist Advocacy: Factors Associated with Value for Money and Intentions to Recommend in South Africa’s Western Cape
abstract: This exploratory study examines whether stated guided-tour priorities and tourist characteristics are associated with value-for-money evaluations and positive recommendations in South Africa’s Western Cape, and whether value adds explanatory information to tourist advocacy. Survey data from 451 participants were analysed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests, hierarchical binary logistic regression and robustness checks. title: Metabolomic fingerprinting of an artisanal blue-veined cheese: Impact of cave microenvironment and producer
abstract: Artisanal blue cheeses are highly valued products due to their unique quality attributes. This study conducted a large-scale longitudinal investigation into the influence of the producer and natural cave microenvironment on the metabolomic profile of PDO Cabrales cheese during ripening. Cheeses from three producers and ripened in three different caves were analysed for composition, free fatty acids, free amino acids, volatile compounds and biogenic amines using physico-chemical and chromatographic techniques. title: Stabilization of expansive soil using talcum powder and cement: swelling reduction and strength development
abstract: Abstract Expansive soils are considered one of the most problematic soil types worldwide due to their significant volume change behaviour in response to variations in moisture content. This study investigates the stabilization of expansive soil using a combination of cement and talcum powder in order to improve its engineering performance. title: Ethogram of zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) after exposure to nitrates
abstract: Abstract Nitrate pollution is one of the most widespread forms of contamination, and in high concentrations has adverse effects on aquatic ecosystems. Fish are susceptible to this contaminant and are known to modify their behaviour in a variety of ways when exposed, but most information regarding changes in behaviour pertains only to long‐term or chronic exposure. title: La‐Mediated Interfacial Electric Field Effect Steers Mesoscopic Mass Transport for Highly Selective Urea Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling active site urea adsorption with mass transport is critical to precisely tuning the selectivity of the electrocatalytic urea oxidation (UOR). However, current research on selectivity remains focused on atomic‐level active sites, while often neglecting the vital influence of mesoscopic mass transport from electrode structures. Herein, we utilize the lanthanide (La) mediated interfacial electric field strategy to regulate ion deposition behavior, enabling the controllable synthesis of catalyst mesostructures. title: Why Sustainability Polarizes: And How to Bridge the Divide
Parental responses to climate threat: Italian validation of the Climate Self-Protection Scale and the role of eco-defenses, epistemic stances, and eco-anxiety
abstract: Climate change has psychological repercussions that challenge individuals’ basic assumptions about stability and safety and contribute to emotional suffering. Parents may be particularly vulnerable to eco-anxiety, given concerns about the long-term impact on their children’s well-being. This research, conducted in Italy, examined how defenses against climate change (“eco-defenses”) and epistemic stances (trust, mistrust, credulity) shape parents’ eco-anxiety across two studies. title: SPATIO-TEMPORAL STRUCTURE OF MOLLUSC COMMUNITIES IN LAKE ZIENKOLO: INFLUENCE OF PHYSICOCHEMICAL GRADIENTS (NORTHERN CÔTE D'IVOIRE)
abstract: Aquatic molluscs play an essential role in the functioning of lakes and are commonly used as indicators of water quality. However, their diversity remains little studied in the reservoirs of northern Côte d'Ivoire. This study characterizes the composition and spatio-temporal structure of these communities in Lake Zienkolo (Korhogo). It also evaluates their relationships with the physico-chemical parameters of the water. title: Sociodemographic Factors and Land Use Shape Perceptions of Ecosystem Services in Reservoirs of Semiarid Regions
abstract: Abstract Community perceptions of ecosystem services are shaped by individuals’ local contexts and their direct interactions with the environment. Examining these relationships enables a better understanding of how human perceptions of ecosystem services are associated with anthropogenic environmental change. In this study, we assessed the relationship between ecosystem service perceptions in riverside communities of semiarid reservoirs and sociodemographic variables, as well as the extent to which different land uses and land covers influence these perceptions. title: Geologically constrained dynamic evolution and early warning of urban resource-environment carrying capacity: a case study of Jinan, China
abstract: Urban resource environment carrying capacity (RECC) is increasingly challenged by nonlinear interactions among socioeconomic development, resource depletion, and geological environmental degradation. However, existing assessments often neglect the cumulative feedback effects of groundwater depletion and geological responses. This study develops a city-scale system dynamics (SD) model integrating six subsystems (population–economy, land, water resources, ecology, environment, and geological environment) to simulate RECC evolution in Jinan, China, during 2021–2031. title: Kano-IPA-based post-occupancy evaluation of an urban sports park for active health: a case study in Mianyang, China
abstract: Against the backdrop of “Healthy China” and urban renewal, urban sports parks are critical public spaces for promoting residents’ active health. Taking Sanjiang Sports Park in Mianyang as a case, this study used a mixed-methods approach integrating Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE) with the Kano–IPA model to evaluate spatial performance and health service functions. Based on 236 valid questionnaires, the results showed that user-oriented facility planning, safety design, and age-inclusive configuration significantly improved usage willingness and experience satisfaction. title: High-purity ammonia recovery from anaerobic digestate via nitrogen stripping coupled with PFSA membrane separation
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a crucial raw material that is widely used in fertilizers, chemical manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals and has attracted increasing interest as a hydrogen carrier and clean fuel. However, conventional NH 3 production is energy-intensive, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives, including NH 3 recovery from waste streams. This paper presents a perfluorinated sulfonic acid (PFSA) membrane-based separation process for high-purity NH 3 recovery from anaerobic digestate. title: Reconfiguring interfacial hydrogen-bond networks to enhance anodic oxidation for efficient wastewater treatment
abstract: Abstract Anodic oxidation is a pivotally electrochemical technology for wastewater treatment containing emerging contaminants such as isothiazolinone antimicrobials, but sluggish interfacial water-splitting kinetics for hydroxyl radical (•OH) formation and a limited oxidation range, constrain its industrial scalability. This study leverages Fe 3+ to strengthen interfacial water hydrogen bond, accelerating •OH formation and high-valent iron production, thus enhancing oxidation kinetics and scope. title: A Radiation‐Modulated Frost Index Improves the Representation of Frost Stress and Yield Response in Winter Wheat
abstract: ABSTRACT Late spring frost is a major abiotic stress affecting winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production, yet its impact on yield remains difficult to quantify because crop responses depend not only on the intensity of low‐temperature exposure but also on environmental conditions following frost events. Conventional frost indices are primarily temperature‐based and therefore do not fully capture variability in yield responses under comparable thermal stress conditions. journal: Journal of Agronomy and Crop Science

title: Impacts of climate change on blue and green waters in Tekeze-Atbara watershed, Nile basin
abstract: This study examines the impacts of climate change on blue water flow (BWF), green water storage (GWS), and green water flow (GWF) components of water resources in the Tekeze Atbara watershed of the Nile basin. It employed five CMIP5 climate models under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios along with a satisfactory SWAT model with acceptable predictive uncertainty. title: Club de ciencias: Una investigación sobre la calidad del agua y la desigualdad urbana
abstract: Este estudio analiza una actividad desarrollada en un club de ciencias, basada en el aprendizaje por proyectos, cuyo objetivo fue investigar el problema de la calidad del agua distribuida en diferentes barrios de una ciudad. La actividad se desarrolló con estudiantes de tercer año de secundaria de una escuela pública del interior del estado de São Paulo, Brasil, en el marco de los clubes juveniles. Para ello, dos docentes, uno de sociología y otro de química, trabajaron junto con los estudiantes en el desarrollo del proyecto a lo largo de un año académico, articulando debates sobre sociología

title: The Access Paradox: A Decade of Expanded Influenza Vaccine Access That Did Not Close a Racial Disparity
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Despite more than a decade of expanded influenza vaccine access through Medicare, pharmacy-based programs, and community clinics, older African Americans remain vaccinated at markedly lower rates than older White and Asian adults. This study examines why the disparity has persisted and whether U.S. vaccination policy evidence was ever designed to address it. title: Biofilm and multidrug-resistance Acinetobacter spp- correlation by phenotypic and molecular methods
abstract: Background: Acinetobacter species are major causes of ICU-acquired infections, including ventilator-associated events, urinary tract infections, and bloodstream infections. Their ability to form biofilms contributes to resistance against multiple antibiotics and disinfectants. This study evaluated the prevalence of biofilm-forming Acinetobacter spp. isolated from clinical samples using phenotypic and molecular methods.Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 106 clinically significant, non-duplicate Acinetobacter isolates were collected from routine clinical specimens. title: Sexually dimorphic control of excitatory synapse maintenance in ventral hippocampal circuits by Neurexin2α ligand Vstm2b
abstract: Abstract Neuronal networks rely on precise synapse formation, maturation, and maintenance orchestrated by synaptic adhesion molecules including α- and β-neurexins (Nrxns). Through unbiased proteomics, we identified Vstm2 family members as α-Nrxn-specific interactors that require inclusion of an insert at alternative splice site 2 (SS2) in α-Nrxns. In particular, as a selective ligand of axonal Nrxn2α SS2+ , Vstm2b promotes glutamatergic presynaptic assembly. title: The role of rural tourism in promoting small farmer’s income: Evidence from the sub-Himalayan region of Eastern India
abstract: Rural tourism is increasingly recognised as a viable non-farm livelihood strategy for small and marginal farmers, especially in regions with strong tourism potential. However, despite its growing policy relevance, empirical evidence on its role in improving farmers’ income in the sub-Himalayan region of Eastern India remains limited. This study examines the determinants of farmers’ participation in tourism-led livelihood activities and estimates the impact of this participation on household income. Primary data were collected from 400 households across eight villages in the Jalpaiguri and Alip
journal: Local Economy The Journal of the Local Economy Policy Unit

title: Tree-ring chronologies reveal unexpected geographic patterns of drought vulnerability in western Canadian forests
abstract: Adaptive reforestation under climate warming will increasingly involve northward or upslope movement of tree species and seed sources. However, in western Canadian boreal and sub-boreal forests, release from cold constraints may be offset by emerging drought limitations, where low evapotranspiration has historically supported tree growth despite modest precipitation. We used 392 tree-ring chronologies from western Canada to compare drought resistance, recovery, and resilience among seven common conifer tree species across regional climatic gradients. title: Carbonyl‐Site‐Mediated Oxygen Reduction in Fluorenone‐Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) photosynthesis from molecular oxygen and water offers a sustainable route for decentralized oxidant generation, yet elucidating the molecular‐level active sites for oxygen activation in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains challenging. Herein, we report a fluorenone‐containing COF, FO‐Tp, as an efficient photocatalyst for H 2 O 2 production, delivering a rate nearly ten times higher than that of fluorene‐based COF, highlighting the crucial contribution of fluorenone carbonyls to photocatalytic oxygen reduction. title: Synchrony of floral volatile emission with diurnal pollinators of possible decomposition mimic Asarum savatieri (Aristolochiaceae)
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Floral scent is crucial for mediating plant-pollinator interactions, a primary driver of angiosperm diversity. The dynamic nature of olfactory cues means they can be fine-tuned to suit pollinator activity, making them an effective method of adaptation to local pollinator niches. Asarum sect. Heterotropa is one of the most species-rich lineages in Japan with remarkable variation in floral scents. title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. title: Structural control of Fe(II)-based multivalent glycan assemblies enables intramolecular avidity and ultra-high-affinity binding
abstract: Abstract Multivalent glycan recognition depends critically on the spatial organization of saccharides, yet quantitative design rules linking glycan geometry to binding remain poorly defined. Here, we report atomically-precise Fe(II)-based glycoassemblies that enable independent control of glycan valency, spacing, and topology within discrete molecular scaffolds. Using monomeric Griffithsin as a model lectin, we uncover that subtle changes in glycan presentation drive discrete transitions from partial site engagement to high-avidity, multi-site binding, spanning a > 10³-fold range in affinity.

title: Modulating Spin‐States of Active Catalysts for Efficient Urea Oxidation in Anion Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer
abstract: ABSTRACT The electronic properties of active M(O)OH catalysts can be effectively modified by tailoring the characteristics of their corresponding precatalysts. Herein, we report a coordination site‐modulated precatalyst to access active catalysts for efficient electrocatalytic urea oxidation in an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. A two‐dimensional NiFe‐coordination polymer (NiFe‐2D) was constructed via selective site engineering using hydrazine. title: Amorphized and Oxidized Layered PtSe 2 as an All‐in‐One Electrocatalytic Platform for Hydrazine‐Assisted Water Splitting
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrazine‐assisted water electrolysis is a promising energy‐saving alternative to conventional water splitting; however, noble‐metal catalysts suffer severe deactivation from nitrogen‐intermediate poisoning during sustained anodic operation. Herein, amorphized and oxidized layered PtSe 2 is presented as an all‐in‐one bifunctional electrocatalytic platform solving this challenge. title: Hand-in-river: Design of direction-dependent virtual cues of assistive/resistive force via auditory displacement and pitch variation
abstract: This paper investigates the role of sound-only manipulations in eliciting pseudo-force perception during lateral hand movements within a virtual river environment. title: Navigating drought and food security in Southern Angola: A water-energy-food nexus system approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Southern Angola has been facing water scarcity, drought, and food insecurity due to climate change. The provinces of Namibe, Cunene, and Huila have experienced a sustained and unprecedented decline in rainfall, which has adversely affected water, energy, and food production. This research examines the water-energy-food (WEF) resources in southern Angola and proposes strategies to address the challenges of drought, population growth, and food insecurity, through an integrated approach to manage the referred resources. title: Namangan viloyati sharoitida yetishtirilgan kishmishbop uzum navlarining morfologik va biologik ko'rsatkichlarini baholash
abstract: В статье представлены результаты оценки некоторых морфологических и биологических показателей кишмишного винограда, выращенного в различных регионах Наманганской области. В исследованиях наблюдались высота территории выращивания винограда над уровнем моря, сроки и время сбора урожая, внутренняя температура винограда, твердость плодов, размер зерен и показатели массы. Полученные данные показывают, что при оценке морфологических и биологических особенностей винограда необходимо учитывать условия возделывания и сбора урожая.

title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
abstract: Soils are Earth's largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. title: Risk mapping with community participation: strategies for risk and disaster management
abstract: Risk must be understood as a social construction; public participation is thus essential for the development of integrated plans and policies that are effective and sustainable. This action-research presents participatory mapping carried out in the community of Guarará, municipality of Franco da Rocha, São Paulo, Brazil. The research was carried out in partnership with residents and representatives of public authorities and academia in order to understand the problems and analyze proposals in the local territory. abstract: Introduction We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1’s proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. title: Larval habitat characteristics and physicochemical associations of culicine mosquito assemblages in Hormozgan Province, southern Iran
abstract: Understanding the ecological characteristics of mosquito larval habitats is essential for effective vector surveillance and control. This study investigated larval habitat characteristics, water physicochemical properties, and culicine mosquito assemblages in Hormozgan Province, southern Iran. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from September 2016 to April 2017 across four counties representing diverse ecological conditions. title: Adaptive multi-objective energy management and coordination of EV and FECV stations with power-to-hydrogen/hydrogen-to-power integration using a UT-ARO framework
abstract: High penetrations of renewable energy sources (RES) and the growth of electric/fuel-cell vehicles (EV/FCEV) are compelling distribution system operators (DSOs) to co-manage electricity and hydrogen while preserving feeder security. In this article, a security-oriented, multi-objective framework is presented for a radial feeder, jointly minimizing operating cost, losses, and emissions while maximizing voltage security via a voltage-stability index (WSI). title: Accelerated aging and health in people experiencing homelessness in New Mexico: a latent class analysis
abstract: People experiencing homelessness (PEH) experience elevated rates of premature mortality and health conditions typically observed in housed individuals 15–20 years older, a phenomenon termed accelerated aging (AA). To investigate which groups of adult PEH are at risk of AA. Guided by the behavioral model for vulnerable populations, we assessed how factors, including physical health, healthcare access, environmental stressors, mental health, and substance use, cluster to create distinct profiles indicative of AA among PEH. journal: GRID - Architecture Planning and Design Journal

title: Balancing Productivity, Ecology, and Social Well‐Being: Insights From Three Decades of Farmland Transformation in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Balancing food security, social equity, and ecological sustainability remains a persistent challenge in global agricultural systems. While economic and ecological aspects of land‐use transitions have been extensively studied, the long‐term dynamics of social functions and their interactions with other functions are less understood. This study investigates the decadal spatiotemporal patterns, functional relationships, and spatial association factors of farmland multifunctionality in China's major grain‐producing regions in 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020. title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture
abstract: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero strategies is poorly understood. Using integrated modelling and 12 key performance indicators, we assess the sustainability and resilience of two simulated circular strategies implemented within a business as usual and three net zero greenhouse gas emission pathways for Ireland’s land sector. title: Biodiversity Action Planning Within a Global Agricultural Supply Chain
abstract: ABSTRACT Agriculture is a primary driver of biodiversity loss through habitat conversion and degradation. Companies are increasingly being asked to investigate, disclose, and act on their biodiversity impacts by both regulatory policies and voluntary commitments. Yet companies lack practical guidance for identifying actions that mitigate negative externalities and improve natural systems on commodified lands and throughout their supply chains. title: Beyond species niches: genotype-driven adaptation across climates in multi-country progeny trial networks
abstract: Abstract Niche-based models have been widely used to identify potential species for deployment in target environments; however, these approaches rely primarily on natural distribution data and may underestimate the full adaptive potential of commercial species. In contrast, large-scale tree breeding trial networks provide direct empirical evidence of performance, but their implementation is costly and time-consuming. abstract: Konsumsi energi listrik pada mesin perkakas merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam mendukung efisiensi proses pemesinan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh variasi kecepatan putaran spindle terhadap konsumsi energi listrik pada Bench Drill Ixion BT 25 serta menentukan kecenderungan kecepatan putaran yang menghasilkan penggunaan energi listrik lebih optimal. title: Descriptor‐Informed Screening of Interface‐Active Molecules for Efficient Magnesium Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable magnesium batteries offer a compelling pathway toward sustainable energy storage, yet realizing this vision demands scalable electrolytes formulated with widely accessible salts, such as magnesium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (Mg(TFSI) 2 ). Progress in Mg(TFSI) 2 ‐based electrolytes has been severely hindered by low Mg stripping/plating efficiency, arising from sluggish Mg 2+ desolvation kinetics and uncontrolled interfacial reactions. abstract: Low-temperature rechargeable batteries are crucial for energy storage under subzero conditions but remain limited by sluggish ion transport, severe interfacial polarization, and slow charge-transfer kinetics. Dual-ion batteries (DIBs), employing both cations and anions as charge carriers, offer fast ion-storage kinetics and reduced desolvation barriers, yet practical applications are hindered by sluggish dual-ion diffusion, electrolyte incompatibility, and poorly understood interfacial processes. title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Next – Generation Polymers for Drug Delivery: Conductive, Bioresorbable, and Biodegradable Polymers

abstract: Self-propelled liquid metal-aluminium hybrid machines represent a promising class of autonomous motion systems capable of sustained movement without external power sources. While interactions between machines and their environment inevitably occur, the fundamental question of how spatial confinement affects the motion dynamics and the controllability of speed, direction and lifetime of such liquid metal machines (LMMs) remains underexplored. title: Ecological responses of soil bacteria to rapid and slow temperature fluctuations
abstract: Fluctuating temperatures profoundly affect microorganisms' coexistence, biogeographic distributions and responses to future climate change. However, how microorganisms respond to fluctuating temperatures with different frequencies in natural communities remains unknown. We conducted a 120-day temperature manipulation experiment with soil-bacterial communities subjected to constant low, medium and high temperatures, as well as fluctuating temperatures with three different frequencies. title: ASSESSMENT OF DOMESTIC WASTE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND HOUSEHOLD AWARENESS OF MODERN TECHNIQUES IN SAMINAKA TOWN, KADUNA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Household solid waste management strains environmental and public-health systems across sub-Saharan Africa, where collection infrastructure has not kept pace with urban growth and open dumping or burning is often the only option. Kaduna State assessments have documented these service gaps, yet no published study examines how households in the state's smaller towns manage waste or what they know about modern alternatives. title: Ecological and life history traits predict urban tolerance in North American birds
abstract: Abstract Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. Additionally, understanding whether shared evolutionary history influences urban tolerance could shed light on its evolutionary origins and reveal the extent to which urban landscapes filter out entire taxonomic clades, homogenizing biodiversity. title: Scaling paludiculture: stakeholder perspectives on adoption and enabling conditions in England
abstract: Paludiculture, the cultivation of wetland species on rewetted peatlands, is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for climate mitigation, biodiversity restoration and peat conservation; however, its adoption remains limited in the United Kingdom. This study examines stakeholder perspectives on the adoption of paludiculture and the enabling conditions required to support its scale-up. abstract: Abstract The fungal-algal-bacterial (FAB) consortium composed of Euglena mutabilis, Talaromyces, and Acidiphilium acidophilum is a natural acid-tolerant assemblage whose heavy metal handling may depend on interspecies cooperation rather than a single-organism uptake alone. abstract: This study investigates the application of an EPS light-gauge steel composite envelope system in rural buildings located in the hot-summer and warm-winter region of Hainan. An experimental building was constructed in Shitang Village, Ding’an County, Hainan Province, using traditional brick structures as a control for comparison. title: Dynamics of Soil Microbial Biomass Carbon and Total Nitrogen Under Different Land Use in Indo-Myanmar Hotspot Region, Nagaland
abstract: Abstract Soil microbial biomass and nitrogen, a vital nutrient pool for ecosystem nutrient cycling is affected by several factors including climate, edaphic, and land-use change. Focusing on Phek, India which lies within the Indo-Myanmar Biodiversity Hotspot, this study investigates how land use system (forest, permanent agriculture, horticulture, and jhum cultivation) season and soil depth influence soil microbial biomass carbon (MBC) and total nitrogen (TN). title: The soundscape wheel: a conceptual map for tourism geographers
abstract: Soundscapes are receiving increasing attention in tourism studies. Much focus is given to noise generated by tourism, whereas the role of sound in experiences of place has received less attention. To address this gap, we introduce a ‘soundscape wheel’ as a theoretical and applied tool that can inform transdisciplinary work across tourism studies.
