abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), land surface temperature (LST), and their integrated indices in capturing dry-season drought dynamics in the dipterocarp deciduous forest ecosystems of Yok Don National Park from 2014 to 2024. abstract: The use of the up-to-date antiretroviral therapy (ART), including the integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (INSTIs), has significantly reduced mortality associated with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Nonetheless, some INSTIs like dolutegravir (DTG) have been found to affect fetal development, particularly regarding neural tube defects. title: Climate Change and Extreme Weather Effects on Nebraska Corn Production: Differential Responses in Irrigated and Non-irrigated Systems
abstract: This study investigated the effects of climate change-driven extreme weather in July, especially drought, on corn yields in Nebraska. The yields of irrigated and non-irrigated (rainfed) corn were compared using data over 20 years, from 1998 to 2018, to see the effect of irrigation on reducing crop losses during the drought period. title: Helminth parasite body size scaling with host species size
abstract: Host and parasite body size frequently scale positively (often referred to as Harrison's rule), potentially as a result of fundamental constraints on large parasite species simply being morphologically incapable of infecting small host species, or through a variety of alternative proposed mechanisms. title: Body size, season, and host taxon predict patterns of monogenean gill parasite infection in two assemblages of darters (Percidae: Etheostomatini) in Tennessee
abstract: Parasites are an important component of freshwater ecosystems due to the ways they regulate energy flow and shape community structure. The goal of this study was to analyze infection patterns of monogenean gill parasites (genus Aethycteron) that have specialized on darters (genus Etheostoma), freshwater fishes native to North America. We sampled hosts from two stream sites in Tennessee and evaluated whether prevalence and intensity of infection varied in the hosts by site, season, body size, sex, or host taxon. abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to investigate the recent research hotspots and frontiers in the field of exosomes, offering a comprehensive review of advancements in exosome research and elucidating their implications and future directions. METHODS: English-language exosome-related literature indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection database from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024, was retrieved, and the data were analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer software. title: Influence of geographical origin on pistachio shell gasification: Experimental performance, supply chain feasibility, and sustainability assessment
abstract: Pistachio shell waste represents an abundant, underutilised lignocellulosic residue with potential for decentralised renewable energy production and waste valorisation. This study presents one of the first integrated assessments of pistachio shell waste sourced from major producing locations, combining feedstock characterisation, oxygen-limited gasification, supply-chain evaluation, life-cycle assessment (LCA), and techno-economic analysis (TEA). title: Path analysis of social, economic, and environmental impacts of large-scale public investment projects
abstract: This study examines the perceived social, economic, and environmental impacts of Istanbul Airport, Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge (YSS), and Northern Marmara Motorway (NMM) based on surveys with 995 residents across 25 neighborhoods. Three separate path models were developed to analyze perceived social, economic, and environmental impacts. abstract: Introduction The development of high-performance and cost-effective electrode materials is crucial for the advancement of next-generation energy storage devices. title: From random walks to thermal rides: universal anomalous transport in soaring flights
abstract: Cross-country soaring flights rely on intermittent atmospheric updrafts to cover long distances, producing trajectories that alternate between rapid relocation and local exploration. From a large dataset of paraglider, hang glider and sailplane flights, we uncover a universal transport law: beyond short ballistic times, horizontal motion is persistently sub-ballistic, with a Hurst exponent ≈0.88 largely independent of aircraft type. title: Colonial legacies and branded identities: labour market exclusion among India’s Denotified Tribes
abstract: After the 1857 rebellion against colonial rule, the British Colonial government enacted Criminal Tribes Act of 1871 to control some sections of Indian society. The Act notified the nomadic, semi-nomadic, and tribes as hereditary criminals. This CT Act was later repealed in 1952, and denotified all the affected communities, known as ‘de-notified tribes’ since then. title: Uncovering the role of biogeography, resources, food web composition and time during microbial primary succession
abstract: Ecological succession is shaped by multiple processes that operate simultaneously across spatial and temporal scales. While classical succession theory generally focuses on a single trophic level within a single location, often in plants or other macroscopic organisms, recent efforts have extended this framework to microorganisms across multiple ecological dimensions. title: When heritage becomes a burden: an evidence-based reference class of tourism stress in historic cities
abstract: Overtourism and carrying-capacity models have traditionally explained heritage-city stress through visitor volume and density. However, these approaches provide limited explanation of why comparable tourism pressures produce different forms and levels of stress across historic cities. This study addresses this gap by examining heritage stress as a perception-driven, context-dependent process shaped by interactions among spatial, social, infrastructural, cultural, and governance conditions. abstract: The Eisenia nordenskioldi complex exhibits remarkable morphological stasis alongside profound genetic diversification, harboring extensive cryptic diversity throughout its range. Distributed broadly across the Palearctic realm, including northern and northeastern China, this species complex remains taxonomically poorly resolved. abstract: Achieving sustainable biomanufacturing requires understanding how process format and facility design influence environmental performance. Using process-modeling software, this study compared three monoclonal antibody (mAb) drug-substance manufacturing scenarios: single-use fed-batch (SU FB), stainless-steel fed-batch (SS FB), and single-use continuous (SU Cont). title: Integrating rainfall event and antecedent depths into a single probabilistic framework for deriving event depth-duration-antecedent depth-frequency curves
abstract: This paper aims to show how rainfall event depth and antecedent depth can be integrated into the same framework for deriving depth-duration-antecedent depth frequency (DDAF) curves, which map a mathematical relationship between event depth, duration and antecedent depth for a given return period. These curves are obtained by means of a multi-step analysis of annual extrema in the trade-off between event depth and antecedent depth, which are dealt with by means of copula-based bivariate distributions for various durations. title: Hatching failure and embryo mortality in endangered populations of Eurasian Curlew ( Numenius arquata )
abstract: Hatching failure represents a significant and growing barrier to reproductive success in threatened birds and yet is often poorly understood. Populations of the Eurasian Curlew Numenius arquata in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland have experienced significant declines over recent decades, and low breeding productivity is a major barrier to conservation efforts. abstract: Background: Population density and the scarcity of physical play areas compel teenagers to seek alternative social spaces through digital platforms. abstract: This study assesses the environmental and economic performance of hybrid solar-assisted greenhouse drying and its integration with hydrogen-assisted biological biogas upgrading at a municipal wastewater treatment plant in Italy. title: Everyday climate change as an embodied, intersectional, and situated experience: Insights from Catalonia
abstract: Climate change is not a distant risk but an everyday lived experience. This article examines climate change in Catalonia, Spain by focusing on daily routines, relationships, and emotions. In doing so, it moves beyond predominantly abstract, technical, and quantitative approaches to the climate crisis by foregrounding everyday experiences through three mutually constitutive dimensions: embodiment, intersectionality, and situatedness. title: Anything But Another Essay: Zoology student perceptions of UnEssay projects
abstract: Abstract Training innovative and diverse scientists starts with creative teaching practices. Much of the existing literature on nontraditional teaching practices in college science courses has focused on in-class active learning activities. Few studies have examined what students perceive they learn from creative, project-based learning in an organismal biology course. title: Spatial and genetic dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein2 in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: BACKGROUND: Malaria rapid diagnosis tests (mRDTs) detecting Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (Pfhrp2) are the most widely adopted diagnostic tool in malaria-endemic areas. However, extensive polymorphisms in Pfhrp2 could modify Pfhrp2 epitopes, rendering it undetectable by Pfhrp2-based mRDTs. abstract: ABSTRACT Background/Objectives Dental shade guides are widely used for clinical color determination; however, their chromatic stability under routine clinical use remains uncertain. abstract: Flooding has become one of the most devastating environmental hazards affecting communities and public institutions globally, particularly in developing countries. In Nigeria, recurrent flooding along the River Benue has continued to disrupt socio-economic activities, including access to education. This study examines the effects of flooding on students’ access to secondary education in Fiidi Ward, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State, Nigeria. abstract: Abstract Funding acknowledgements have become a valuable data source in recent years. The validity of acknowledgements as indicators of direct project-level support, however, remains contested for several reasons. This study examines the reliability of funding acknowledgement data by comparing publications that acknowledge the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Framework Programme in Scopus with publications officially recorded as project outputs in the CORDIS database. title: First evidence of Tahyna virus in Central Italy and seasonal dynamics of its putative vector, Aedes caspius
abstract: Tahyna virus (TAHV) is a neglected mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus pathogenic to humans. In Italy, TAHV was first recorded in Friuli Venezia-Giulia and then repeatedly in Emilia Romagna Region (Northern Italy). abstract: Molecular clocks convert evolutionary distances into geological times to infer time-scaled phylogenies. abstract: Inorganic fertilizer was introduced to farmers in the past century by the government to replenish nutrients absorbed by crops grown in the fields. abstract: Dietary exposure of the population of the French West Indies to the organochlorine insecticide chlordecone (CLD) through the consumption of contaminated foodstuffs remains a major public health concern. abstract: Abstract Potato scab, caused by species of the genus Streptomyces is a significant disease affecting potato production worldwide, leading to economic losses. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence and distribution of Streptomyces species associated with potato scab in Brazil and to characterize two new species. A total of 91 Streptomyces strains were isolated from symptomatic potato tubers collected across seven states. abstract: Uintatheres, mammals belonging to the extinct order Dinocerata, are among the most recognizable of all Paleogene (~66-23 Ma) organisms. Unmistakable for their bizarre skulls with multiple pairs of horns and saber-like upper canines, uintatheres have captivated paleontologists since the late nineteenth century. abstract: Abstract Glucosinolates (GLS) in Brassicaceae crops are known to suppress soil nitrification. Sorbitol-citric acid (SorCA) modification has previously been reported as an effective approach for improving wood properties. abstract: Objective Forest gaps are considered microsites for tree species regeneration. title: Radiological screening of naturally occurring radionuclides in soil and crops at a surface water-irrigated site: a case study from Lege-Amara, Ethiopia
abstract: Naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORMs) possess a wide range of radionuclides that are dependent upon local geology and anthropogenic activity. This study reports baseline 232 Th, 226 Ra, and 40 K activity concentrations in paired soil-vegetable samples collected from the surface water-irrigated Lege-Amara agricultural region through gamma-ray spectroscopic analysis employing a NaI (Tl) scintillation detector. title: Prioritising Functional Characteristics for Maritime Liquid Hydrogen Storage and Transportation Using the House of Quality
abstract: This study addresses the need to prioritise functional characteristics for safe and feasible maritime liquid hydrogen (LH2) storage and transportation during early-stage system development. Quality Function Deployment (QFD) was applied through a House of Quality (HoQ) to map seven techno-socio-economic key performance indicator (KPI) categories against seven system-level functional characteristics for the LH2CRAFT concept. title: Evolutionary constraint on a core winter proteome across independently cold-adapted PACMAD grasses
abstract: Grasses in the Panicoideae, Aristidoideae, Chloridoideae, Micrairoideae, Arundinoideae, and Danthonioideae (PACMAD) clade independently colonized cold environments from warm-climate ancestors, but whether their molecular responses to freezing reflect shared evolutionary solutions or lineage-specific innovations remains poorly understood at the protein level. We used comparative proteomics to test whether protein-level cold responses show stronger cross-species conservation than previously observed at the transcript level. title: Nutritional, bioactive, and textural contribution of traditional totopos from the Zapotec culture of Mexico
abstract: Abstract This study characterizes the nutritional, bioactive, and textural composition of totopos , a traditional maize product from the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Oaxaca, Mexico, prepared with the native Zapalote Chico landrace and baked in the comixcal , an ancestral oven. Proximate analysis showed low moisture levels (4.0–5.2%), which favor shelf stability and contribute to their characteristic texture. title: Trojan terephthalates for scalable poly(ethylene terephthalate) depolymerization
abstract: Escalating reliance on plastics and fossil-fuel price volatility demand recycling strategies that recover monomers without degradation. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), despite being the most widely produced and recycled polyester, degrades during thermomechanical recycling, relegating recyclate to low-end applications. Herein, we show that incorporating 2.5–5 mol% dimethoxy-functionalized Trojan terephthalates (DMTPA) in the PET backbone enables Lewis acid-mediated depolymerization in subcritical water at 180 °C while preserving PET processability. title: Microstructural Characterization of Hybrid Polypropylene-Glass Fibre Reinforced Concrete Using Scanning Electron Microscopy
abstract: Concrete is a brittle cementitious material with limited tensile strength and a tendency to develop microcracks and propagate cracks under mechanical and environmental loading. The incorporation of fibres can improve crack control and enhance the integrity of the cementitious matrix. The present study experimentally investigates the microstructural characteristics of hybrid polypropylene (PP) and glass fibre reinforced concrete with different total fibre volume fractions and fibre combinations. title: Effect of Antibiotic Incorporation on the Porosity of Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) Bone Cement: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) is widely applied in orthopedics. Antibiotic-loaded PMMA has been extensively used, and its mechanical impact, especially porosity, is of widespread importance. We assessed the effects of commercially available and add-on antibiotic PMMA in terms of porosity. The study evaluated seven high-viscosity bone cement groups (S1-S7), with six specimens per group: an antibiotic-free control, three commercially antibiotic-loaded, and three manually antibiotic-loaded with gentamicin, vancomycin, clindamycin, or their combinations. title: Development and validation of a simple impulse-based method for inductor design in electromagnetically driven tools for high-speed material processing
abstract: Electromagnetically driven tools offer a promising way to accelerate conventional tools to high speeds in order to take advantage of the beneficial effects of high strain rates in material processing. However, the systematic design of inductors for such systems is still largely based on time-consuming coupled multiphysics simulations, which hinders industrial implementation. This paper presents and validates a two-step, pulse-based methodology for the simple design of inductors for electromagnetic drive systems for high-speed tools. title: Friends and foes in the avocado Agroecosystem: a comprehensive review of microbial interactions and associated Mycoviruses, from pathogenesis to biocontrol
abstract: Avocado production is increasingly constrained by a complex community of fungi that can function as destructive pathogens, opportunistic colonisers, or beneficial symbionts. These interactions span the entire production chain, from soilborne root pathogens such as Phytophthora cinnamomi and Rosellinia necatrix, to vascular wilt complexes caused by Harringtonia lauricola (formerly Raffaelea lauricola) vectored by ambrosia beetles, and postharvest pathogens including Colletotrichum, Lasiodiplodia, Pestalotiopsis, and Alternaria. title: STATISTICAL, MOLECULAR, AND ULTRASTRUCTURAL INSIGHTS INTO THE STRESS-ALLEVIATING POTENTIAL OF AUTOCHTHONOUS STEPPE BACTERIAL LINEAGES
abstract: The identification and characterization of multi-stress tolerant Plant Growth-Promoting Bacteria (PGPB) are essential for developing sustainable agricultural strategies to mitigate the effects of abiotic stress factors and intensive agrochemical usage. This study aimed to evaluate the stress tolerance of eleven autochthonous strains isolated from steppe zone previously exposed to glyphosate application. title: NATURAL RESOURCE WEALTH MANAGEMENT AND POVERTY REDUCTION IN RIAU PROVINCE
abstract: Natural resources, specifically in Article 33 Paragraph (3) of the 1945 Constitution, are controlled by the state. These natural resources must be utilized to the greatest extent possible for the prosperity of the people. Riau is rich in natural resources, particularly petroleum, natural gas, rubber, palm oil, and forest products. title: Tailoring Fusion Proteins for Interfacial Nanoparticle Functionalization: Toward Fluorescence-Guided Imaging
abstract: Abstract Fusion proteins are specially designed molecules created by linking two or more peptides that were originally encoded by separate DNA sequences. To improve control of protein adsorption on poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) surfaces, we developed fusion proteins comprising a polyester substrate-binding domain (SBD) fused to superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP). The subunits were connected via flexible (GGGGS)n or rigid (EAAAK)n linkers with n = 1, 2, or 4. title: Accounting and Taxation in the Hotel Industry of the Autonomous Region of Madeira: Challenges, Strategies and Perspectives
abstract: This study examines accounting and taxation in the hotel sector of the Autonomous Region of Madeira, with a focus on the interaction between specific tax regulations and financial management practices that impact companies' economic sustainability. The study discusses the diversity of applicable tax regimes, including rates on revenue and taxable profit, and the importance of adapting to legislative reforms to optimize the tax burden and liquidity. title: Coupling Photocatalytic Water Oxidation and Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction for Formate Production
abstract: Abstract Artificial photosynthesis represents a promising route for converting sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals, yet conventional systems are often limited by the sluggish kinetics and high overpotential of the oxygen evolution reaction. Inspired by the electron transport chain between PSI and PSII in natural photosynthesis, we report an artificial photosynthesis system that spatially separates solar energy capture and storage from CO2 conversion to formate using a redox mediator. title: Apollonian Order and Dionysian Chaos: An Iconographic Analysis of Titian’s Bacchus and Ariadne
abstract: This paper examines Titian’s Bacchus and Ariadne through an iconographic and philosophicalanalysis, employing Friedrich Nietzsche’s concepts of the Apollonian and Dionysian asarticulated in The Birth of Tragedy. Bacchus embodies the Dionysian principle, representingecstasy, rupture, wine, excess, and the dissolution of established boundaries. Ariadne, bycontrast, emerges as a figure of order, transformation, and divine transcendence, particularlyat the moment of her abandonment by her lover. title: OCCURRENCE OF SOILS AND WEEDS ON TOPOSEQUENCES UNDER SEDIMENTARY AND BASEMENT COMPLEX FORMATIONS IN NIGER STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: The relationship between soil properties and weed distribution across two geological formations were evaluated on morphological, physical, and chemical properties, and their influence on weed distribution along two toposequences in different geological formations, Minna (Basement Complex) and Bida (sedimentary formation) in Niger State.. title: Effects of raw material (chilled/defrosted) and long-term frozen storage on volatile compounds and quality markers of mechanically separated common carp (Cyprinus carpio)
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the impact of raw material thermal history (chilled vs. defrosted) and 12-month frozen storage (-18 °C) on the quality of mechanically separated common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Between months 6 and 12, a significant increase in volatile concentrations – primarily hexanal - and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) was observed, alongside a decrease in total volatile basic nitrogen (TVBN). title: Observation of electrically generated polaron-polaritons in a monolayer MoSe 2 microcavity
abstract: Quasiparticles arising from the interaction between mobile impurities and a quantum many-body environment-known as polarons-play a pivotal role in shaping the optical and electronic properties of low-dimensional systems. Here, we report the direct observation of electrically generated polaron-polaritons within a monolayer molybdenum diselenide microcavity. title: How communication fosters climate-related communicative self-efficacy among young people: insights from a pedagogical intervention in Climate Change Education
abstract: Climate Change Education increasingly emphasizes participation and agency alongside knowledge acquisition. Within this context, self-efficacy plays a central role, yet the relationship between communication and self-efficacy in climate education remains ­underexplored. To investigate this relationship empirically, a communication-based workshop entitled ‘Climate Talks: Speak Up – Cool Down!’ was conducted with 140 secondary school students aged 14–18 in Tyrol, Austria. title: Structure–Processing–Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε-Caprolactone, and Water
abstract: Abstract Water-soluble poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is melt-processable and ductile but has low strength and dimensional stability that restrict its use. abstract: , carbon starvation triggers large-scale proteome remodeling, with global proteolysis supplying both the amino acids (AAs) and ATP for protein synthesis. This remodeling occurs in two phases, with a short preparatory phase relying on constitutive proteolytic machinery and fueled by residual carbon waste, and a more extended phase, relying on starvation-induced protein components synthesized during the preparatory phase and fueled by AA catabolism. title: Legacy effects of land use land cover change on species distribution dynamics: evidence from a landscape of diverse biogeographic crossroads
abstract: Abstract Context Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a key driver of biodiversity distribution, yet species responses vary among taxa, habitats, and regions. Because species responses are context-dependent, understanding how ecological characteristics and landscape history influence biodiversity distribution is essential for conservation planning. title: Root‐mediated trade‐offs in nitrogen acquisition and utilization affect yield and grain composition in short‐stature corn
abstract: Abstract Plant architectural traits play a critical role in shaping nitrogen (N) uptake, allocation, and overall performance in corn ( Zea mays L.). Recently developed short‐stature corn hybrids exhibit enhanced belowground growth compared to conventional tall‐stature hybrids; however, how these traits influence N uptake, internal partitioning, grain yield, and composition remains unclear. title: Occurrence and concentration variability of pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and polyphenols in Nyabugogo River, Rwanda
abstract: Pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and polyphenols are increasingly detected in aquatic environments, impacting water quality and aquatic life. This study screened these contaminants in Rwanda's Nyabugogo River, analysing 45 water samples from rural, peri-urban, and urban areas using solid-phase extraction and LC-MS/MS. Fifty-seven pharmaceuticals, five pesticides, and four polyphenols were quantified, with the highest average concentrations of albendazole (960 ng/L), metalaxyl (70 ng/L), and caffeic acid (49 ng/L). title: Plant functional type composition drives summer carbon cycling in an ombrotrophic peatland
abstract: Abstract Peatlands are globally important carbon sinks because plant CO 2 uptake outweighs microbial decomposition. These ecosystems are characterised by a distinct microtopography of hummocks and lawns, supporting vegetation communities composed of various plant functional types (PFTs). In this study we assess the direct effects of PFT removal and microhabitats, and the indirect effects mediated through microbial community composition on CO 2 and CH 4 emissions. title: Aerobic Exercise Ameliorates Osteoarthritic Chondrocyte Degradation in Osteoarthritis via Regulating E2F8/NLRP14 Signaling Pathway
abstract: Although physical activity is known to mitigate disease risks, its protective molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. E2F8, a regulator of cell cycle and metabolism, showed significant differential expression between osteoarthritis (OA) and exercise models, suggesting it may link mechanical activity to OA alleviation. In vitro, Interleukin-1 Beta (IL-1β) simulated inflammation. In vivo, OA was induced in rats via Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) injection. title: Monthly Rhythms of Intercity Travel: A Seasonal Analysis of Population Mobility Between Chinese Cities
abstract: Abstract With the continuous improvement of China’s high-speed transportation system and the deepening of regional integration, intercity travel has become increasingly frequent and has emerged as an important field for studying spatial linkages and regional interaction among cities. Based on AMap Migration big data, we analyze the monthly rhythms and seasonal fluctuations of intercity travel throughout 2023. title: Lived multifunctionality: Indigenous perceptions of shifting cultivation landscapes in the Naga Hills of Myanmar
abstract: Shifting cultivation is frequently misrepresented in policy and environmental discourse as ecologically destructive and economically inefficient. This study examines the lived multifunctionality of shifting cultivation (jhum) landscapes in the Naga Self-Administered Zone of Myanmar, where Indigenous Naga communities depend on diverse land-use mosaics for livelihoods, cultural reproduction, and ecological resilience. title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
abstract: Abstract Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. title: Modeling Logical Interdependencies: Quantifying Systemic Risk From Rule‐Governed Actions
abstract: Systemic risk in critical infrastructure is often analyzed through physical, geographic, and cyber interdependencies. Yet infrastructures are also interdependent through the governing rules that organize human action. These rule-mediated connections are a form of logical interdependency, and breakdowns in rule-governed action can create pathways through which disruption spreads. This paper develops a framework for diagnosing and quantifying this underrecognized source of systemic risk. title: Probing Triplet Photochemistry in Ru(II) Porphyrins Using Singlet Oxygen Generation and Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
abstract: Porphyrins are known for their rich triplet-state photophysics, making them attractive platforms for light-driven applications. Compared with extensively studied Pd(II) and Pt(II) porphyrins, Ru(II) porphyrins remain less systematically explored, particularly for triplet-driven reactivity. Here, we demonstrate that a single porphyrin framework can perform complementary functions: generate singlet oxygen (1O2) and photosensitize triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC). abstract: Agricultural lands in East Kazakhstan region cover a significant area, with large portions of pasture and cropland situated in close proximity to operating industrial facilities. Despite this, no comprehensive integrated assessment combining remote sensing, ground-based soil monitoring, and flora survey had previously been conducted for the zone of influence of the Nikolaevskaya enrichment plant. title: Portrayal of Caste and Social Identity in Contemporary Telugu Cinema: a Study of Andhra Pradesh
abstract: The treatment of caste in Telugu cinema is socially significant given its political and fan and community allegiances. The political, fan and community allegiances of the Telugu cinema make its treatment of caste socially consequential. The focus of this study is on how caste and social identity has been depicted in current Telugu cinema (from 2000 to nowadays) in the context of Andhra Pradesh. title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
abstract: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. The goal of chemists is to establish green, inherently safe, highly efficient and sustainable synthetic methods. Here, we report a green approach for the halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn and FeX3, as well as a nucleophile at room temperature under visible-light irradiation in AcOH/CH3CN, without strong oxidants and any ligand. title: The model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii forms mutualistic interactions with Verticillium fungi
abstract: Abstract Algal–fungal interactions are widespread in natural environments and contribute to key ecological processes such as primary production, nutrient cycling, and soil formation. Yet, molecular mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly understood due to the complexity of natural systems and the lack of experimentally tractable models. Here, we describe a genetically tractable interaction between the model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and the soil-borne fungus Verticillium dahliae. abstract: ABSTRACT Shape memory polyurethane (SMPU) exhibits excellent shape memory behavior; however, its relatively low mechanical strength and thermal stability limit its use in demanding structural applications. In this study, carbon fiber (CF) mat‐reinforced SMPU composites containing multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were fabricated using a solvent casting technique to investigate the combined effects of CF mat reinforcement, MWCNT incorporation, and post‐fabrication annealing on the thermal, mechanical, morphological, and shape memory properties of SMPU composites. title: Redesigning Iran’s water-energy-food nexus: A path to sustainability and shared value creation
abstract: The Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus is a critical framework to address interconnected resource management challenges in Iran, particularly amid increasing environmental constraints and socio-economic pressures. This study applies the System Redesign toward Creating Shared Value (SYRCS) methodology to redesign the WEF nexus, emphasizing stakeholder engagement, sustainability, and systemic reforms. title: Engineered Artificial Minerals (EnAM) Approach for Chromium Recovery and Stabilization in Steelmaking Slag
abstract: Steelmaking slag represents one of the largest industrial by-products, with estimated annual generation exceeding 500 million tons worldwide. These slag materials contain valuable alloying elements such as chromium, nickel, and vanadium that remain in the slag. Chromium, in particular, has a dual role: it is essential for corrosion resistance of steels but creates environmental and resource recovery challenges when transferred into the slag. title: Integrated Damping Solid-State Circuit Breaker for Inrush Current Suppression in DC Microgrids with Reconfigurable Voltage Sources
abstract: Solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) provide fast, arcless fault clearance, resulting in a longer service life compared to mechanical circuit breakers (MCBs) in DC grids. Black-start operations refers to the process of restarting a grid without an external power source, usually using the system’s internal energy storage system (ESS). SSCBs can be damaged by inrush currents during black-start operations in DC microgrids because power semiconductors have limited current-handling capability. abstract: Abstract Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-( l -α-aminoadipoyl)- l -cysteinyl- d -valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) are standard therapies for estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer, but their efficacy is limited by drug resistance. While dysregulation of alternative splicing has been implicated in cancer progression, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we uncover a splicing-mediated mechanism whereby exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 drives its overexpression in CDK4/6i-resistant breast cancer cells. title: Correlation between mechanical performance and structural evolution in PLA toughened with reactive polysiloxanes during accelerated aging
abstract: Polylactide (PLA) is a sustainable thermoplastic with considerable industrial potential; however, its limited durability under outdoor exposure restricts its broader use in engineering applications. This study investigates the effect of two reactive polysiloxane modifiers (MODs), denoted MOD1 and MOD2, incorporated at 1–5 wt%, on the mechanical performance and aging behavior of PLA under simulated outdoor conditions involving UV-B radiation, elevated temperature, and humidity. title: Liquid-Crystalline Polymer Alloy Design through Interfacial Reactions Enabled by In Situ Polymerization and Reactive Blending
abstract: Abstract Liquid-crystalline polymers (LCPs), an important class of super engineering thermoplastics, exhibit outstanding melt processability and are attractive materials for designing high-performance polymer alloys. However, the fundamental insights required to overcome macroscopic phase separation arising from the intrinsic structural disparity between liquid-crystalline and isotropic polymers, and the design guidelines built on these insights, have not yet been clearly established. abstract: A Reforma Tributária do Consumo altera não apenas a estrutura jurídica da tributação sobre bens e serviços no Brasil, mas também a lógica econômica do planejamento tributário empresarial. Com a instituição do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e da Contribuição Social sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), a não cumulatividade passa a operar em bases mais amplas, enquanto a apropriação, a utilização e a monetização dos créditos dependem de processos fiscais, financeiros, documentais e tecnológicos integrados. title: Sex-specific determinants of blood lead levels in Korean adults
abstract: Abstract Blood lead level (BLL) in Korea has declined but remains a public health concern because there is no safe level of exposure. We aimed to identify sex-specific determinants of BLL in Korean adults using an integrated, data-reduction approach. We analyzed data from the third cycle of Korean National Environmental Health Survey (KoNEHS, 2015–2017), a nationally representative survey of adults aged 19 years or older. abstract: Abstract Seismic safety assessment of nuclear power plant (NPP) sites depends critically on the simultaneous characterisation of ground motion intensity and the capacity of the local soil to amplify that motion. abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a composite‐modified cementitious system incorporating nano‐TiO 2 and carboxylated cellulose nanofibers (CCNF) was developed to unveil the synergistic mechanism between point‐like nucleation induced by nano‐TiO 2 and interface‐induced deposition regulated by CCNF, and to establish its relationship with surface stability, pore structure, and ion transport behavior. title: Effects on selected fecal bacterial populations and safety assessment of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus LRa05
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to investigate the effects of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus LRa05 on fecal bacterial populations and evaluate its safety profile. First, the effects of LRa05 on selected fecal bacterial populations were evaluated in a rodent model. Second, safety assessments were conducted through genetic stability testing, acute oral toxicity test in male and female mice and rats, and teratogenicity study. title: Sustainable energy transition options for Russia
abstract: Following the Paris Agreement, one way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and minimise the consequences of climate change is to pursue the goal of a sustainable energy supply by renewable energy sources. This study explores transition pathways towards sustainable energy system in the regions of Russia. Potential scenarios are presented in the power, heat, transport, and industry sectors. title: Coherent Absorption Reveals Colors Hidden in a Grey Fabry–Pérot Cavity
abstract: ABSTRACT Thin dielectric films are known to show distinct colors, depending primarily on the film thickness. In the present article we show that a specialized thin film Fabry–Pérot resonator, that we name conductor–dielectric–conductor (CDC) matched cavity, appears grey when observed under ordinary conditions (i.e., by analyzing the transmitted or reflected incoherent white light). title: Photo‐Induced Electrochromism: Toward a Self‐Coloring Smart Window
abstract: ABSTRACT Smart windows that dynamically regulate solar radiation are crucial for reducing building energy consumption. Electrochromic (EC) smart windows offer high‐performance optical modulation but require an external power supply, whereas photochromic (PC) smart windows are self‐powered but suffer from low modulation and poor bistability. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel photo‐induced electrochromism (PIEC) mechanism in a proof‐of‐concept smart window operating with both light and electricity as stimuli. title: CRISPR-enhanced microalgae for carbon sequestration and carotenoid production: opportunities and fundamental constraints
abstract: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constrained by low carbon conversion efficiency, reduced photosynthetic performance, and competing metabolic fluxes that limit product yield. The emergence of CRISPR/Cas-based genome engineering has enabled precise and multiplexed modulation of microalgal metabolic networks, offering new opportunities to overcome these limitations. abstract: ABSTRACT In mechanical systems, the energy dissipation and wear caused by friction usually lead to the failure of materials during their service life, thereby driving the demand for polymer composite materials with both tribological properties and self‐repairing capabilities. Studying polymer composites with self‐lubrication and self‐repairing functions is an effective approach. title: Pyrolysis temperature controls the accessible pore volume and capric acid encapsulation efficiency of coconut shell biochar
abstract: Waste-derived biochar is a low-cost scaffold for shape-stabilized phase change materials (PCMs), yet how pyrolysis temperature governs the pore volume a molten PCM can reach remains unresolved. Here we decouple surface area from pore accessibility by preparing ZnCl 2 -activated coconut shell biochars at 550, 700, 850 and 1000 °C under an identical protocol and impregnating them with capric acid. title: Contrasting short- and medium-term effects of N-enriched biochar on greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient use efficiency in a maize-wheat rotation
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are a key contributor to climate change, and biochar has been proposed as an amendment to reduce GHG emissions while improving soil properties and crop yield. However, the impact of N-enriched biochar (NB) on GHG emissions, global warming potential (GWP), and GHG intensity (GHGI) remains poorly understood in rainfed maize-wheat cropping systems. We evaluated the performance of two types of NB (NB1 and NB2) produced from pristine biochar (PB) with a two-year field trial. institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Identification and Characterization of a Previously Uncharacterized Metagenome-Derived Chitinase and Its Application in N -Acetyl- d -Glucosamine Production from Crayfish Shell Waste
abstract: Abstract The generation of agricultural and food-processing byproducts has increased rapidly, highlighting the importance of their high-value utilization. In this study, a putative chitinase gene was identified from a metagenome-assembled genome. The enzyme plays a key role in chitin hydrolysis and was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli as a recombinant protein with a molecular weight of approximately 39.2 kDa. title: Poisoned arrows in the Danish Early Mesolithic: Testing lithic ballistic morphometrics against faunal and archaeobotanical data
abstract: Throughout human deep history, lithic tool components became periodically very small. Such microlithic tools are the signature artefacts of the European Mesolithic in general, and the iconic Danish Mesolithic in particular. Sandwiched between the end of the Pleistocene and the emergence of agricultural lifeways, the Danish Mesolithic is characterised by marked changes in microlith design from lanceolates to geometrics and finally to transversal forms with wide front edges. These changes are synonymous with the transitions between the traditionally defined cultures of the Early, Middle and Late

title: Conservation genetics of the spotted bat: Insights from ancient, historical, and modern samples
abstract: Spotted bats (Euderma maculatum) are cryptic (nocturnal, volant, and roost solitarily) and thus their biology remains largely undescribed. Only 35 specimens were known to science before the mid-1960s. Hence, they are ideal candidates for genetic studies to uncover population genetic diversity and structure, and thereby inform conservation. We analyzed nuclear microsatellite loci (N = 17) and mitochondrial control region sequences from 121 individuals spanning ancient (up to 2,100 years BP), historical (1904-1991), and contemporary (1994-2025) timeframes across the species' range in western Nor

title: Causal inference in conservation policy: Evaluating the effects of Protected Areas on deforestation and well-being in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: The Peruvian Amazon, one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth, is under increasing pressure from deforestation, threatening both ecological wealth and local livelihoods. Protected Areas (PAs) have emerged as one of the main conservation strategies; however, questions remain regarding their effectiveness in reducing deforestation and their socioeconomic impact. This study evaluates the effects of PAs, their Buffer Zones (BZs), and Regional Conservation Areas (RCAs) on deforestation and household welfare between 2001 and 2023. title: Validity of STEM-Based IPAS E-Worksheets for Elementary School Students
abstract: Purpose of the study: This study aimed to determine the validity of a STEM-based Electronic Student Worksheet for elementary school science learning (IPAS) based on material suitability, language clarity and readability, display and navigation quality, and the integration of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics components. Methodology: This study employed a research and development approach focusing on the expert validation stage. title: dbcan-nf: a Nextflow pipeline for accurate CAZyme annotation in metagenomes
abstract: Abstract Motivation CAZymes (carbohydrate-active enzymes) are crucial for carbohydrate degradation in any ecological environments. However, CAZyme annotation is not easy in whole genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomes, due to the lack of accurate, scalable, robust, and reproducible workflows. We previously published dbCAN as a web server and associated standalone tool run_dbcan that performs CAZyme annotation with assembled genomes as the input but not with raw WGS reads. title: Defining Typical Family Agricultural Holdings Engaged in Milk Production Through Cluster Analysis in Croatia
abstract: This study investigates the dairy sector in the Republic of Croatia, which is characterized by pronounced structural heterogeneity. On the one hand, there are highly productive farms comparable to the leading milk producers in the European Union, and numerous small and medium-sized farms that face the challenges of maintaining competitiveness and further development. In order to design effective development and sectoral policies, it is necessary to identify and distinguish the dominant types of dairy farms and their specific development needs. title: Molecular evidence of a dominant multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii lineage in a tertiary hospital in northern Peru
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Acinetobacter baumannii is a major nosocomial pathogen because of its genomic plasticity and capacity to acquire multidrug resistance (MDR), particularly resistance to carbapenems. The World Health Organization classifies carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii as a critical-priority pathogen. Molecular epidemiological data from Latin America remain limited, especially for northern Peru. title: Revision of Neanderthal Activity Zones at Kůlna Cave: Use-Wear Analysis of the Micoquian Lithic Industry
abstract: Abstract Investigating the spatial organisation of Neanderthal sites offers critical insights into their behavioural patterns, adaptive strategies, and site use. Studying how different lithic tools are organised in space and linked to specific functions is therefore essential. Kůlna Cave provides evidence of multiple occupation areas characterised by distinct activity patterns, making it a particularly suitable Neanderthal site for investigating spatial organisation and testing related hypotheses. title: Integrated experimental and computational evaluation of a Marsilea minuta-loaded hydrogel for enhanced wound-healing
abstract: Background Marsilea minuta L., a medicinal aquatic fern is of ethnopharmacological importance as per various traditional systems of medicine. It is used to treat skin disorders like wound in India.This study aims to explore the effect of the methanolic extract of M. minuta by using both in silico and in-vivo techniques in the treatment of wounds. Methods The plant material Marsilea minuta L., (MEMM) was defatted first with petroleum ether to remove the fat and then extracted with solvent methanol in a Soxhlet apparatus. title: First records of Gigaspermum mouretii Corb. and Oedipodiella australis (Wager & Dixon) Dixon (Gigaspermaceae) from Saudi Arabia, with biogeographic implications
abstract: This study documents the first records of the moss family Gigaspermaceae in Saudi Arabia. Two taxa were discovered in the southern and western highlands: Gigaspermum mouretii Corb., recorded from several granite slopes in Al Bahah and Mecca provinces, and Oedipodiella australis (Wager and Dixon) Dixon, found at multiple localities in the Asir Mountains. The material of G. mouretii is unequivocally paroicous and fertile, with sessile sporophytes bearing giant spores, thereby providing clear morphological support for its separation from G. repens. title: A provincial environmental technology transition indicator for Vietnam: Green finance, spatial diffusion, and absorptive capacity
abstract: This paper develops and validates a provincial Environmental Technology Transition (ETT) indicator for Vietnam and uses it to assess whether green finance is associated with cleaner technology upgrading, eco-innovation, and energy-efficiency improvement. Using a balanced panel of 63 Vietnamese provinces over 2014-2024 (693 observations), the study combines indicator construction, principal-component validation, Spatial Durbin modelling, and an IV-spatial estimator to examine both within-province and cross-province technology-transition dynamics. title: Trophic position structures physiological trade-offs between metabolic and detoxification pathways in sympatric passerines
abstract: Abstract Resource use links ecological context to organismal performance, yet whether dietary breadth or trophic position is more closely associated with physiological state in wild birds remains unclear. We used a natural trophic gradient in a sympatric passerine assemblage to test whether trophic position and isotopic niche breadth are associated with integrated physiological phenotypes. We studied three co-occurring passerine species in central Chile spanning a trophic spectrum (granivorous, omnivorous, insectivorous). title: Stage-specific shifts in bacterial and fungal amplicon profiles of garlic bulbs during cold storage
abstract: Garlic bulbs can remain externally intact while microbial and tissue changes develop during cold storage, so endpoint inspection may miss distinct intermediate states. We characterized cold-stored garlic across four storage stages by combining bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing with culture, quantitative PCR (qPCR), photography, and cryo-scanning electron microscopy. title: The influence of lakes and reservoirs on estimated flood peaks at hourly vs. daily timescale in the Alps
abstract: Abstract. Water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs can play a crucial role in reducing flood peaks both on daily and hourly timescales. While the effect of water bodies on flood peaks at different time resolutions has been demonstrated in the past, it remains unclear how they affect the ratio between daily and hourly peaks. title: Two new species of the Neoperla (Formosita) lushana-group (Plecoptera: Perlidae) from China, supported by morphological and mitochondrial COI data
abstract: The Neoperla (Formosita) lushana-group is revised using an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological and molecular evidence. Two new species of this group are described and illustrated: Neoperla foping Wang, Wang & Li sp. nov. from Shaanxi Province and Neoperla huangi Wang, Wang & Li sp. nov. from Hunan Province. title: Gross and Histopathological Charactersation of Pulmonary Abscessation due to Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli in a Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus): A Case Report
abstract: Bacterial lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) can result in severe and fatal diseases in non-human primates (NHPs), and the disease process of pulmonary abscessation in the Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus), an endangered West and Central African cercopithecid, has been underreported. A gross and histopathological evaluation of a 12-year-old captive female C. torquatus that had a 14-month history of intermittent coughing and that had a polymicrobial co-infection with S. aureus and E. coli is presented. title: Environmental Footprint of Kerala’s Coir Processing Transitions
abstract: This article examines the historical transition of Kerala’s coir industry from traditional retting practices to mechanized production, highlighting the shifting burdens on ecosystems and workers. Retting once imposed severe localized pollution on aquatic systems, with high biochemical oxygen demand and phenolic loading creating anoxic conditions, while mechanization reduced reliance on water bodies but introduced energy intensity, synthetic effluents, and hazardous occupational exposures. title: Mechanical Irreversibility and Strength Overcompensation in a Gypsum Dehydration–Rehydration Cycle
abstract: Abstract Dehydration–rehydration reactions of hydrous minerals modify rock strength, fluid transport, and deformation in reactive geological environments. Although dehydration‐induced weakening is widely studied, the mechanical consequences of subsequent rehydration remain poorly constrained. We combine triaxial compression tests with microstructural and pore‐network analyses of original gypsum, fully dehydrated anhydrite, and rehydrated gypsum. title: Protected-area-based nature-based governance and green-blue infrastructure-to-built conversion: spatial regression discontinuity evidence from Kinmen National Park, Taiwan
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) and green-blue infrastructure (GBI) are increasingly promoted for sustainable built environments, yet boundary-based evidence on specific land-conversion mechanisms remains limited. This study evaluates Kinmen National Park, Taiwan, using a spatial regression discontinuity design (Spatial RDD) on 30 m grid cells for 2014–2024. GBI-to-built conversion (G2B) is the primary outcome; strict built-up change, developed-land change, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) change, and GBI fragmentation are contrasting or secondary outcomes. title: Ultraconserved element phylogenomics reveals novel insights into the historical biogeography of euophryine jumping spiders (Araneae: Salticidae)
abstract: The Euophryini is one of the largest tribes of jumping spiders (Salticidae), with diverse morphology, ecology and behaviour, and is an important focus of systematic and evolutionary studies of jumping spiders. Notably, it is the only salticid tribe that has diversified nearly equally across both the Old and New Worlds, making its historical biogeography particularly intriguing. However, understanding its biogeography has been challenging without the application of phylogeny-based biogeographical analytical approaches. title: Morphofunctional indices and ontogeny of long bones of the limbs in the frogs
abstract: Anuran limbs offer a valuable model for exploring how selective pressures, developmental constraints, and morphological evolution interact. While previous research has largely focused on total limb length, little is known about ontogenetic changes in the proportions of individual limb bones. This study introduces a novel approach using morphofunctional indices to investigate the functional roles of frog limbs, linking morphology to habitat use and locomotion. title: Honey Bees as Bioindicators of Environmental PFASs Contamination and Potential Effects on Gut-Microbial Communities
abstract: Honey bees are valuable bioindicators of environmental contamination due to their wide foraging range and exposure to diverse biotic and abiotic stressors. This study evaluates the use of honey bees as bioindicators for detecting per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in areas with varying levels of exposure risk (high-, intermediate-, and low-), as well as their potential effects on gut-microbial communities. title: Temporal dynamics of association patterns in Geoffroy's spider monkeys, Ateles geoffroyi: a multiscale approach using temporal multiplex networks
abstract: Collective patterns of sociospatial behaviour are the result of internal and external factors operating at different temporal scales and can give rise to social structures. In species with high degrees of fission–fusion dynamics, individuals can respond to behavioural drivers by joining or departing from subgroups, thereby modulating how often they co-occur in the same subgroups. Their collective patterns of co-occurrence can help us understand how groups respond to their changing environments. title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite.

title: Corrosion Resistance of Boronized Carbon Steel in a Galinstan–Refrigerant Two-Phase Agitated System
abstract: Abstract This study experimentally evaluates, for the first time, the corrosion resistance of boronized carbon steel in environments containing liquid Galinstan (GaInSn) and selected organic refrigerants (n-pentane and R1233zd(E)) at 150 °C for up to 80 days. The tests simulated gas–liquid-metal two-phase exposure under pseudodynamic conditions, where the test coupons and corrosive media were mechanically agitated. title: A Visual Analysis of the Uneven Contribution Towards Sustainable Climate Action: An Analysis of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13
abstract: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is a measure of a country's economic capacity. Hence, the correlation between GDP pc and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the present study, Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13), provides a clear indication of the extent to which individual countries comply with the goal. SDG 13 comprises four subgoals: CO₂ emissions from fossil-fuel combustion and cement production; greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions embodied in imports; and CO₂ emissions embodied in fossil-fuel exports. title: Gut microbiomes of the little free-tailed bat ( Mops pumilus ) show high prevalence of potential bacterial pathogens but limited responses to land cover
abstract: Land cover change is a threat to wildlife globally. It may also impact the gut microbiome harbored by wildlife, with implications for their health, conservation, and One Health more broadly. Bats are a diverse group of mammals that can be found in a range of habitats, with differing degrees of anthropogenic disturbance. Here, we analyzed the V3–V4 region of 16S rRNA from fecal samples from 109 individual little free-tail bats ( Mops pumilus ) in northeastern Eswatini. title: Local knowledge and social innovation for inclusive community based tourism in Kampung Yoboi, Papua, Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Community-based tourism connects livelihoods, cultural continuity, environmental stewardship, and local participation. However, local knowledge does not automatically become tourism value, tourism activity does not automatically constitute social innovation, and social innovation does not necessarily produce inclusive development. Drawing on social innovation theory, this study examines the conditional pathways connecting these processes in Kampung Yoboi, an Indigenous lake-based settlement in Papua, Indonesia. title: Rapid protamine evolution suppresses meiotic drive in Drosophila
abstract: Many animal species replace histones with protamines during spermatogenesis. Although essential for sperm function, protamines evolve rapidly for reasons that remain unknown. Using in vivo gene replacement, we examined the causes and consequences of the rapid evolution of Mst77F , a protamine essential for male fertility in Drosophila melanogaster ( D. melanogaster ). title: The Critical Role of Economies of Scale: A Techno‐Economic Assessment of Small‐ Versus Large‐Scale Biogas Upgrading in Rural Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT Access to clean and affordable energy remains a major challenge in rural Tanzania, where dependence on traditional biomass continues to drive deforestation, indoor air pollution, and energy insecurity. Biogas offers a promising alternative, yet limited evidence exists on the technical and economic feasibility of decentralized upgrading systems in rural settings. Building on the experimentally implemented and validated pilot‐scale waste‐to‐fuel system, this study undertakes a techno‐economic assessment of small‐ and community‐scale biogas upgrading under rural Tanzanian conditions. title: The scientific consensus on the beauty of snowflakes: A case study for the aesthetics of science
abstract: Philosophers of science interested in aesthetics have tended to privilege the epistemic and cognitive dimensions of science. Historians of science interested in aesthetics have largely focused on the aesthetics of scientific images and artefacts. Productive exchanges between these traditions of scholarship have been few and far between. title: Prediction of Self‐Starting of a Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Using Static Torque
abstract: ABSTRACT The ability of vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) to self‐start is critical to their performance. There is disagreement in the literature over some of the factors affecting their self‐starting ability and there is very limited information on how the starting azimuthal angle affects self‐starting. We present a series of wind tunnel experiments in which we measure the static torque and self‐starting of a three‐blade VAWT for a range of initial azimuthal angles, which we find to have a very strong effect on the ability to self‐start. title: Developing High‐Performance Biodegradable Poly(Butylene Succinate) Composites Through Synergistic Effects of Fiber Surface Mineralization and Soybean Protein Bonding Onto Sisal Woven Fabrics
abstract: ABSTRACT The environmental challenges of traditional petrochemical composites have driven increasing research into sustainable alternatives. Poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) composites reinforced by sisal fabric present a promising route, yet their performance is limited by poor fiber‐matrix interfacial bonding and inadequate resin infiltration into the narrow inter‐fiber spaces. title: Distinct Genetic Determinants of Plasma Inflammatory Proteins in Tanzanian and Dutch Populations
abstract: Understanding the genetic regulation of plasma inflammatory proteins is essential for bridging the gap between genetics and disease biology. While studies in European populations have highlighted significant genetic influences on inflammatory protein levels, African populations remain underrepresented in immunogenetic research. Here, we compare the genetic determinants of 72 inflammatory proteins quantified using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel in two cohorts from the Human Functional Genomics Project. title: γ‐Ray Controlled Topological Evolution of Binders for Stable and Activated Li─S Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT γ‐ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent‐free cross‐linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three‐dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. title: Microalgae pathway to premium vegetable oil: Fermentation strategy to produce Auxenochlorella protothecoides single cell oil analogue to olive oil
abstract: Microalgae are increasingly recognized as a sustainable oil source due to unique biological and ecological advantages. This study aims to develop a scalable heterotrophic high cell density fermentation strategy for microalgae Auxenochlorella protothecoides ( AP ) to produce single-cell oil analogue to olive oil. A batch fermentation yielded a dry cell weight (DCW) concentration of 20.0 g L -1 with 18.7% (w/w) oil content at a high glucose to yeast extract (YE) ratio of 3:1 (g/g). title: The complete mitochondrial genomes of Colias lada and Colias wanda (Lepidoptera: Pieridae: Coliadinae) and their phylogenetic analyses
abstract: The complete mitochondrial genomes of two Qinghai-Tibet Plateau butterflies, Colias lada and C. wanda, were assembled from next-generation sequencing data, measuring 15,078 bp and 15,144 bp. Both contain 13 PCGs, 22 tRNAs, 2 rRNAs and one control region. Phylogenetic trees based on the 13 PCGs and 2 rRNAs using ML and BI methods, with high support values, show that C. wanda, C. lada and C. sifanica share a recent common ancestor, and reconstruct the relationships among the Coliadinae genera.

title: Taxogenomic Characterization and Comparative Genomic Analysis of Hermanozyma buritii sp. nov., f.a., a Yeast Species Isolated From Plants and Soil
abstract: ABSTRACT Four yeast isolates with an affinity to Hermanozyma ubatubensis and Hermanozyma aechmeae (Ascomycota, Saccharomycotina, and Metschnikowiaceae) were obtained from plant and soil samples collected at different localities in Brazil. Analyses of the D1/D2 domains of the LSU rDNA gene and phylogenomic data indicate that these isolates represent a new species within the Herm. ubatubensis clade. We propose the name Hermanozyma buritii sp. nov., f.a. to accommodate these isolates. The holotype is CBS 19561. The MycoBank number is MB864970. title: Irrigation-driven modulation of growth and stress resilience in cork oak (Quercus suber L.) seedlings in nursery environments
abstract: Cork oak (Quercus suber L.) is a keystone species of Mediterranean forestry, increasingly threatened by prolonged droughts and anthropogenic pressures. Improving nursery seedling quality is therefore essential for successful reforestation. title: Field evaluation of Bacillus -based consortium biofertilizer for rhizosphere zinc availability, grain biofortification and paddy yield
abstract: The zinc (Zn) deficiency in submerged rice limits productivity and nutritional quality. This study evaluated the potential of zinc-solubilizing plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to enhance Zn availability and uptake in rice under submerged conditions. Field experiments were conducted over two years using five Bacillus-based biofertilizer formulations: three single-strain inoculants (B. megaterium AN24 as BF-1, B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-2, B. megaterium AN31 as BF-3) and two combined formulations (B. megaterium AN24 + B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-4, B. megaterium AN24 + B. megaterium AN3

title: DNA Barcoding Validation of Medicinal Ipomoea Species from the Morning Glory Family
abstract: The growing consumption of herbal products has been accompanied by a concerning increase in the use of adulterants during production, which could affect the quality of traditional herbal medicine. DNA barcoding is a powerful method for accurately identifying plants at various taxonomic levels, and for authenticating medicinal plants. In this study, the DNA barcoding regions rbcL and ITS were used to corroborate the botanical classification of commercial seeds from five Ipomoea species and one hybrid, all commonly used as herbal medicines and widely cultivated as ornamentals. title: Structural basis of antigenic drift in FMDV O/Cathay topotype variants revealed by porcine-derived single B-cell neutralizing antibodies
abstract: The porcinophilic O/Cathay topotype variants of foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) continuously accumulated mutations over time and produced antigenic drift, leading to diminished serum neutralization and compromised vaccine efficacy. However, the structural basis underlying this divergence remains poorly defined. Herein, we observed that the newly emerging O/Cathay variants in China exhibited marked neutralization escape from porcine immune sera. title: GC–MS-based chemometric profiling of volatile oils from Ocimum varieties reveals bioactive markers associated with anti-skin cancer activity
abstract: Abstract Skin cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide. Basil oils have been traditionally used for alleviating various diseases. This study investigated the chemical profile and anticancer activity of five basil oils’ varieties (purple, lemon, Italian, Asian, and local). Hydrodistilled oils were analyzed using GC–MS, identifying 44 volatile constituents mainly belonging to oxygenated monoterpenes and phenylpropanoid derivatives. abstract: The growing demand for sustainable bioinputs has driven the production of microbial biosurfactants from low-cost substrates. This study evaluated the biosurfactant production by the strain Bacillus licheniformis UCP 1014 utilizing crude glycerol and corn steep liquor as agroindustrial as substrates, using Rotatable Central Composite Design (RCCD). title: Heavy metal exposures and constipation among United States adults
abstract: Constipation is a common gastrointestinal disorder that can substantially impair quality of life. Environmental exposure to heavy metals has been implicated in gastrointestinal dysfunction; however, population-based evidence regarding their associations with constipation remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of blood lead, mercury, and cadmium levels with constipation among US adults. title: Unveiling the gut microbiome-immune-brain axis in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is frequently associated with gastrointestinal disturbances, suggesting that gut microbiota alterations may contribute to disease pathophysiology through the gut-immune-brain axis. However, the mechanisms linking gut dysbiosis to neural dysfunction remain poorly defined. Here we show that gut microbiota from SCZ patients is associated with systemic immune dysregulation and altered brain-immune homeostasis in recipient mice. title: Systemic drivers of declining coconut productivity on peatlands in Indragiri Hilir, Indonesia: A systems thinking approach
abstract: Declining coconut productivity has become a major challenge for smallholder farming systems on tropical peatlands. While previous studies have identified biophysical, economic, and institutional challenges affecting coconut production, limited attention has been given to how these factors interact to shape system behaviour over time. This study investigates the systemic drivers underlying declining coconut productivity in the peatland-based smallholder coconut farming system of Indragiri Hilir Regency, Indonesia, the country’s largest coconut-producing region, using a systems thinking approach
journal: Journal of Open Innovation Technology Market and Complexity

title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety

title: Investigating the association between weather variables and Aedes albopictus abundance in Windsor, Ontario
abstract: Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) is notorious for transmitting several pathogens of public health importance. The mosquito has also displayed a great capacity for dispersal. Within the last 30 years, the mosquito has been documented on every continent except for Antarctica. The species was first noted in Canada in 2016 in Windsor-Essex, Ontario. Since then, Ae. albopictus has been found every subsequent year in active surveillance trapping (2017-2023). title: Spatiotemporal variations in power grid carbon intensity and their impact on steel fiber-reinforced concrete emissions
abstract: China's energy transition has created unprecedented spatiotemporal heterogeneity in power grid carbon intensity, yet conventional life cycle assessment methodologies using national averages potentially misrepresent emissions for electricity-intensive products. This study develops a spatiotemporally explicit framework using steel fiber production to examine these impacts. Analysis of 31 provinces reveals 24-fold spatial variation (0.04-0.97 kg CO₂e/kWh), with steel fiber emissions ranging from 0.72-4.35 kg CO₂e/kg. title: Agroecological desert truffle cultivation promotes soil conservation and functionality in semi-arid Mediterranean areas
abstract: Soil degradation driven by agricultural intensification and land abandonment represents a major challenge in dryland regions worldwide, where soils with low organic matter and structural stability are highly vulnerable to erosion, nutrient depletion and loss of biological functionality. The cultivation of desert truffles ( Terfezia claveryi Chatin), involving an ectendomycorrhizal symbiosis with Helianthemum almeriense Pau and relying on low input agroecological management, has been proposed as a sustainable alternative for soil conservation. title: A pH-stimulated responsive micro-drug delivery system loaded with gastrodin that improves type 2 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly increasing global metabolic disease. The development of effective oral hypoglycemic agents, primarily derived from natural compounds, remains a significant challenge. In this study, we developed pH-responsive sodium alginate (SA) microspheres combined with low methoxy pectin (LMP) that are loaded with gastrodin (Gas) (denoted as Gas@MPs) and successfully delivered Gas to the gut for controlled release. title: Hidden in the deadwood: Taxonomically curated barcode library reveals deep genetic divergence in Eurasian saproxylic beetles
abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. abstract: Abstract The efficient synthesis of poly(ester amide)s (PEAs), which combine polyamide-like mechanical strength with polyester-like biodegradability, has remained a longstanding challenge. Herein, we introduce a unique coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization (CROTCP) mediated by a tetranuclear titanium catalyst. title: Design and optimisation of defected ground structure slotted MIMO antenna for maritime mobile, broadcasting and fixed mobile communications
abstract: Abstract The proposed article presents a novel dual-port MIMO antenna design incorporating a defected ground structure (DGS) and passive slots to achieve enhanced performance in terms of high isolation, high gain and multiband response. Unlike conventional approaches, the proposed antenna undergoes a three-stage design evolution, introducing triangular and D-shaped slots in the patch, as well as vertical and horizontal slits in the ground, and optimising inter-element spacing to minimise mutual coupling. title: Reduction of off-flavour formation and improved α-oligoglucoside utilization enable use of Saccharomyces eubayanus as a novel lager brewing yeast
abstract: Lager beer, made by fermentation of barley malt using the hybrid yeast Saccharomyces pastorianus, is extremely popular worldwide. The low genetic variation of S. pastorianus strains limits the scope of development for novel lager beer types. The wild ancestor Saccharomyces eubayanus has potential for lager brewing, but its application is constrained by formation of phenolic off-flavours (POF+ phenotype) and limited uptake of the wort α-oligoglucosides maltose and maltotriose. title: Assessing the metabolic rate in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, Progressive Muscular Atrophy, and Primary Lateral Sclerosis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether resting energy expenditure (REE) differs between patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), progressive muscular atrophy (PMA), and primary lateral sclerosis (PLS). METHODS: Patients with ALS, PMA, and PLS were enrolled between 2017 and 2021 in a prospective cross-sectional study. REE was measured by indirect calorimetry. title: Chitosan polymeric nanoparticles loaded with a grapefruit-derived flavonoid-rich extract containing naringenin: antibacterial activity, cytotoxicity evaluation and DFT interaction analysis
abstract: Naringenin is a bioactive flavonoid with reported anti-bacterial and cytotoxic properties; however, its biomedical applicability is limited by poor aqueous solubility and restricted bioavailability. In this study, chitosan-based polymeric nanoparticles loaded with naringenin (Chito-NPs/NAR-EtOH) were designed as a biocompatible delivery platform to enhance NAR-ETOH dispersion and biological performance.
