title: Towards Common Ground: Perspectives on Energy Transitions in Canadian Oil and Gas Producing Municipalities
abstract: Abstract Oil and gas producing municipalities host Canada's highest‐emitting industries while facing economic and social risks as the country pursues carbon neutrality. Understanding how these communities envision their economic futures, and the barriers and enablers they encounter in pursuing low‐carbon opportunities, can inform decision‐makers seeking both emissions reductions and more resilient local economies. Although the all‐inorganic CsPbI 3 is a particularly promising representative, low‐threshold laser operation remains challenging in CsPbI 3 thin films due to phase instability and difficulties in preparing high‐quality thin films within low‐loss optical resonators. abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire effects on soil can differ among soil properties, soil depths, and fire-severity classes, yet their longer-term trajectories remain poorly resolved in subtropical pine plantations. We evaluated temporal convergence of burned soils toward an unburned reference following an April 2022 wildfire in a Pinus massoniana plantation in central China. title: A Predictive-Correlational Study of Error Patterns in the Four Fundamental Operations as Predictors of Mathematical Problem-Solving Performance Among Grade 6 Learners in Portlamon Elementary School, Division of Surigao del Sur: Basis for a Targeted Mathematics Intervention Program
abstract: This study examined error patterns in the four fundamental operations as predictors of mathematical problem-solving performance among Grade 6 learners at Portlamon Elementary School, Division of Surigao del Sur, as a basis for developing a targeted mathematics intervention program. A quantitative predictive-correlational research design was employed involving 31 Grade 6 learners with complete and valid responses. title: Intensified Centrifugal Dewatering of Bauxite Residue for Potential Caustic Liquor Recovery: An Upper-Bound Laboratory Consolidation Study
abstract: Bauxite residue (red mud), a highly alkaline byproduct of the Bayer alumina process, poses major environmental and geotechnical challenges owing to its fine particle size, residual caustic content, and long-term storage risks. This study proposes an integrated centrifuge-assisted framework for sustainable bauxite residue management by combining alkaline-conditioned flocculant-assisted centrifugation with potential caustic liquor recovery under intensified high-G consolidation. title: High-temperature Raman spectroscopy of lawsonite: constraints on bonding changes and dehydration
abstract: Abstract The Raman spectrum of lawsonite is characterized in situ at high temperatures through its dehydration temperature under vacuum. The structural reorganization associated with dehydration appears to initiate in the Si and Al-dominated layer of the structure, and proceeds between 525–550 and 725 °C. The loss of water from the structure appears complex, with the first structural reorganization associated with dehydration occurring at 550 °C, coexistence of lawsonite and the initial dehydration products up to 700 °C, and rapid disappearance of lawsonite between 675 and 725 °C. title: Integrating AEC Interdisciplinary Competencies for MT Education: A DACUM-based Approach
abstract: MT construction requires effective interdisciplinary collaboration across AEC disciplines. However, MT-related competencies remain fragmented within many AEC curricula. This study developed an MT competency framework using employed DACUM-based mixed-method approach that combined quantitative and qualitative strategies to evaluate three discipline-specific MT competency panels of architects, engineers, and CMs 251 MT-related duties and tasks were identified and thematically coded into 18 competency areas. abstract: The small Indigenous Carib village of Chinese Landing located in Guyana has held legal land title since 1976. The Caribs were famed for their gold mining and metallurgy before European arrival, and gold mining remains integral to their identity and livelihoods. Although Chinese Landing is unusual in some respects, in general its struggle to preserve and implement its rights since 1995 is typical of the 200+ government-recognised Amerindian communities in Guyana. title: Future in- and out-of-state air pollutant emissions under decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts
abstract: Many U.S. states have adopted the goal of achieving carbon neutrality in the coming decades. Pathways for achieving these targets would likely yield a reduction of air pollutant emissions as well. We assess several state-level decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts, including electrification of buildings and transportation and decarbonization of the electric grid, estimating their impacts on in- and out-of-state emissions of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and several air pollutants. title: Population genetic data for 23 STR loci of the Miskito ethnic group in Honduras
abstract: The Miskito constitute Honduras’s largest indigenous population (~ 80,000 individuals), yet population-specific genetic databases essential for accurate forensic analysis remain unavailable. Allele frequencies for 23 autosomal short tandem repeat loci were determined from 100 unrelated Miskito individuals (52 females, 48 males) from four settlements in Gracias a Dios department. title: Formulation and Comprehensive Evaluation of a Polyherbal Anti-Acne Face Pack Using Medicinal Plant Extracts for Topical Skin Care Applications
abstract: Acne vulgaris is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder that affects a large proportion of adolescents and adults worldwide.Conventional therapies are often associated with adverse effects, poor patient compliance, and the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the need for safer and more effective alternatives.The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a polyherbal anti-acne face pack containing Azadirachta indica, Ocimum sanctum, Piper betle, Rosmarinus officinalis, Cucumis sativus, and Aloe vera.The selected medicinal plants were authenticated, subjected to pharmaco

title: Receptor Binding Drives Toxicokinetic Processes: Insights from Two Amphipod Species Exposed to Insecticides Targeting the Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
abstract: Abstract Insecticides targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are used because of their high neuroactive efficacy. However, they can also exert substantial toxic pressure on nontarget aquatic invertebrates. A previous study suggested that irreversible receptor binding is the main driver of thiacloprid bioaccumulation. title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta‐Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain. METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. abstract: Identifying seismogenic faults, their geometries, and associated slip rates is essential for assessing seismic hazard estimates. During earthquake sequences, complex fault systems are often activated, involving the rupture of multiple segments. Identifying these fault segments remains a challenging task. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskites offer a promising pathway toward solution‐processable monolithic lasers. abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic transformed political communication patterns and encouraged candidates to adopt campaign strategies based on digital technologies.Objective: This study analyzes cyberpolitics in the political communication of the Gibran Rakabuming Raka–Teguh Prakosa ticket in the 2020 Surakarta mayoral election, focusing on campaign planning, message design, media strategy, voter segmentation, and digital political communication.Methods: This study employs a qualitative descriptive-exploratory case study within a constructivist paradigm. title: Endotoxins and Biological Implications—Review
abstract: Endotoxins, also known as lipopolysaccharides (LPSs), are structural components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and some cyanobacteria. They are among the most potent pyrogens and remain a persistent challenge in environmental, occupational, and clinical settings. This review brings together current understanding of their structure, stability, and methods of detection, while also highlighting the main routes through which humans are exposed. title: Predicting the habitat suitability and hotspot regions of the near threatened Socotra bluet on the Socotra Archipelago using an integrated modelling approach
abstract: The Socotra bluet (Azuragrion granti) is an endemic, Near Threatened damselfly restricted to the Socotra Archipelago whose persistence depends on scarce freshwater refugia under a changing climate. We used an integrated modelling framework, MaxEnt species distribution models coupled with spatial hotspot statistics (Getis-Ord Gi* and Local Moran's I) and landscape metrics, to map current and future habitat suitability (SSP126, SSP245, SSP370 for 2021-2040 and 2041-2060) and to identify priority conservation zones. abstract: BACKGROUND: Planetary health is an increasingly important transdisciplinary approach in nursing because it links human health and equity to the integrity of Earth's natural systems. Climate change is a major component of planetary health, but it is not synonymous with the broader approach, which also encompasses biodiversity loss, pollution, resource pressures, environmental sustainability, and the transformation of health systems. title: The dual role of ungulates in the post-ingestion seed fate of an invasive forest tree
abstract: Acacia species are widespread invasive plants in Mediterranean ecosystems, including in central Portugal, where they promote significant negative impacts. These species exhibit vigorous regeneration strategies, with seed germination being facilitated by scarification, which may be achieved with high temperatures during fires, and passage through animals’ digestive tracts. We conducted feeding trials with captive domestic goats ( Capra hircus ), red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) and wild boar ( Sus scrofa ) to evaluate the potential of these ungulates to disperse or predate Acacia seeds. abstract: Abstract Offshore oilfield produced water (OPW) is a highly complex and hypersaline effluent from oil and gas extraction industry. Since the water‐soluble organic (WSO) compounds in its composition are challenging to be eliminated, their treatment by various advanced oxidation processes (AOP) have been proposed. abstract: Genetically encoded bioluminescent calcium indicators enable excitation-free imaging of Ca2+ dynamics with low background and without excitation-associated photobleaching. However, many exhibit lower dynamic ranges than their fluorescent counterparts, motivating the development of new sensor configurations, particularly for imaging in the red optical window, where tissue absorption and scattering are reduced. abstract: As part of the global effort to replace petroleum-based materials with sustainable alternatives, there is growing interest in enhancing the toughness of biological materials for durable textile applications. Functional composites derived from renewable sources, such as fungal hyphae, have attracted widespread attention. However, mushrooms remain comparatively underexplored, despite their rich natural polysaccharide content and favorable processability. abstract: Collective future thinking involves individuals’ imagining the future of the group they feel they belong to. In the present study, we examine how individuals from Türkiye and Poland, two countries with different sociocultural and geopolitical contexts, simulate the future of their own country and that of Russia and Ukraine in the context of the Russia-Ukraine War. title: Choroidal Melanoma Treated With Ruthenium‐106 Eye Plaque Brachytherapy: Results of an Australian Statewide Service From November 2020 to January 2025
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Uveal melanoma is a rare but aggressive malignancy, predominantly affecting the choroid. title: Optimization, microstructure, and durability of sawdust ash concrete modified with Conplast SP430 superplasticizer
abstract: The use of sawdust ash (SDA) as a supplementary cementitious material offers an opportunity to valorize biomass waste and reduce dependence on Portland cement, but its incorporation can affect workability, strength development and durability. This study investigates the combined effects of SDA replacement and Conplast SP430 dosage on the fresh, hardened and durability performance of concrete. SDA replacement levels of 0–40% and Conplast dosages of 0–7.6 L/m 3 were investigated, followed by microstructural and elemental characterization of the resulting concrete using BSE-SEM and EDS. title: Fiscal Policy, Institutional Quality, and Economic Growth in West African Countries
abstract: This research paper will aim at investigating the interactions between fiscal policies, institutional quality and macroeconomic growth performance in West African countries for the period 2000 2024. This paper will employ the two-step system GMM estimation technique in handling issues concerning growth persistency, individual heterogeneity, simultaneity and endogeneity in the case of institutional, fiscal policy and growth relationship. title: Flavin-dependent halogenases from Cortinarius mushrooms for the regioselective chlorination of anthraquinone pigments
abstract: Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) are valuable catalysts for the late-stage diversification of small molecule scaffolds, modulating their biological activities and/or introducing orthogonal functionalities for regiospecific derivatization. This study broadens the repertoire of FDHs by discovering two such enzymes (CkHAL1 and CsHAL2) from Cortinarius mushrooms that chlorinate anthraquinone skeletons from the emodin family when expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. title: Synthesis of novel bis(6-ethyl-4-hydroxy-2H-chromen-2-one) derivatives as potential acetylcholinesterase and monoamine oxidase inhibitors
abstract: A novel series of bis(6-ethyl-4-hydroxy-2 H -chromen-2-one) derivatives 7a–d featuring para-halogenated (F, Cl, Br, I) phenylmethine linkers were synthesized and evaluated as dual acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibitors for potential Alzheimer's disease therapy. title: Closing the loop: enabling 100% sand replacement in mortars through in-situ PVAc–silicate stabilization of untreated demolished concrete
abstract: Natural sand depletion and the rapid accumulation of construction and demolition waste (CDW) have become major barriers to sustainable construction and circular resource management. Although recycled fine aggregates have been widely studied, current approaches typically allow only partial sand replacement or rely on energy-intensive pretreatment methods, such as thermal activation, carbonation, acid washing, or nanomaterial modification, to achieve acceptable performance. title: Effect on mechanical properties, corrosion behaviour and fracture behaviour of FSWed AA 6061-T6 and AA 2024-T3 by using different pin profiles
abstract: Friction Stir Welding (FSW) is widely validated as a solid-state joining process that has gained significant attention for the welding of aluminum alloys in aerospace and automotive applications. In this study, the effect of Tool Pin Profiles (TPP)—Taper Threaded (TTPP), Square (SPP), and Cylindrical Threaded (CTPP)—on the flow of material, mechanical properties, corrosion properties and microstructure of dissimilar aluminum alloys AA6061-T6 and AA2024-T3 was investigated. title: Electronic structure, NBO, and radical stability analyses of thymol and carvacrol along metabolic transformation pathways: a DFT study
abstract: Abstract Understanding the proposed reaction mechanisms and radical stabilization processes leading to the formation of the two bioactive monoterpenes, thymol and carvacrol, remains challenging because of complex reaction networks, tautomeric interconversions, and electron delocalization effects. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed at the B3LYP/6-311 + G(d) level using Gaussian 09 software. title: Dietary Turmeric Enhances Physiological Resilience of African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) Following Aeromonas hydrophila Challenge: An Integrated Physiological Assessment
abstract: Improving physiological resilience to bacterial infection has become an important objective in sustainable aquaculture because disease outbreaks continue to compromise fish health, survival and production efficiency. Although dietary turmeric (Curcuma longa) has been reported to improve fish health, its effects on the integrated physiological responses associated with bacterial challenge remain poorly understood in African catfish (Clarias gariepinus). title: Comparative Study of Garuda (Khrut) Mythical Creature Visual Representation in Indonesian and Thai Architecture
abstract: Indonesia and Thailand share a common mythical heritage, Garuda (Khrut), which serves both as a spiritual figure and a symbol of national identity. However, significant differences exist in the stylistic approaches, symbolic narratives, and functional placements of Garuda imagery, shaped by each nation's unique historical, religious, and socio-cultural contexts. This study explores how the visual language of Garuda in architecture contributes to contemporary expressions of national identity and environmental design in public spaces. journal: Nakhara Journal of Environmental Design and Planning

title: Leaf silicon and calcium differ between grassland plant functional groups while only calcium responds to soil background
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Grasslands are biodiversity-rich ecosystems in which plant functional diversity strongly influences ecosystem functioning. Silicon (Si) and calcium (Ca) are often overlooked in trait-based frameworks despite their roles in plant physiology, stress tolerance and nutrient dynamics. This study investigates how leaf Si and Ca vary among plant functional groups, how they relate to soil Si and Ca availability, and whether they are associated with specific leaf area (SLA). title: ‘Life has become a lot easier’—the acceptability of the treatable traits clinic experience to people with bronchiectasis
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The treatable traits approach involves the identification of traits that are measurable and clinically relevant to the patient, which informs an individualized management plan. While improved quality of life and health outcomes have been demonstrated, the acceptability of this approach to people with bronchiectasis has not been explored. The aim of our study was to explore the acceptability of the treatable traits approach to people with bronchiectasis in a regional setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: An exploratory qualitative study. title: Novel use of far UV-C light as a surface disinfectant in the poultry industry: trials on broiler farms show reduced bacterial burden in poultry anterooms and on wellington boots
abstract: Abstract Far ultraviolet-C (UV-C) irradiation at 222 nm has widely been shown to deactivate bacteria, viruses and fungi in in-vitro experiments. However, there are few studies testing the technology on real life surface. There are no peer reviewed studies on the efficacy and feasibility of far UV-C disinfection in real-life agricultural settings. The aim of this study was to investigate whether far UV-C irradiation installations on UK broiler poultry farms could reduce bacterial surface burden. title: N-LAS-IAM: Climate change in a balance-of-payments framework
abstract: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing heterodox models are mostly closed or global, while balance-of-payments-constrained growth models treat climate in reduced form and incompletely formalise the financial channel. title: Taxidermy preparation of Oreochromis Niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758) using siliconized synthetic fiber as a filling material: technical report and photographic record
abstract: The preparation and preservation of animal specimens constitute important tools for the teaching of zoology, comparative anatomy, morphology and ichthyology. Among the different techniques used for fish preservation, three-dimensional preparation allows the external configuration of the specimen to be maintained, facilitating its use in educational and exhibition activities. This study aims to describe the taxidermy preparation process of a Nile tilapia specimen, Oreochromis niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758). title: Resurvey of Boreal Earthworm Communities in Southern and Northern Finland
abstract: ABSTRACT In northern boreal Europe, the Last Glaciation Maximum resulted in a tabula rasa of earthworm species, post-glacial recolonisation of few peregrine species. Boreal forests represent 11.5% of the Earth’s land area, and their cold winters represent the harshest season for earthworms. These biotopes are subject to substantial global changes, notably climate change and land use intensification, which might impact earthworm populations. abstract: Los llamados cruces léxicos en español (Kontamination/Blending, en alemán e inglés) son formaciones, cuyo estatus morfológico es muy discutido hoy en día (Maribel, jein, Ostalgie, Brunch, Brexit). title: Peruvian native chili peppers (Capsicum spp.): A comprehensive review of their diversity, phytochemical richness, industrial potential, and future perspectives
abstract: Peru is one of the countries with the greatest diversity of native chili peppers, which make a significant contribution to the highly valued gastronomy of this nation. However, the use of these chili peppers remains localized, resulting in a limited number of studies focused on these species, which restricts their industrial utilization and increases the risk of extinction. title: Spondin 1 Enriched in p16Ink4a Reporter-Labeled Fibroblasts Promotes Melanoma Cell Proliferation in Vitro and Is Associated with Poor Prognosis
abstract: The tumor microenvironment contains phenotypically diverse stromal cells that can support tumor progression; however, the identity and function of stromal populations expressing the senescence marker p16Ink4a in melanoma remain poorly defined. We combined p16-CreERT2-tdTomato lineage tracing with single-cell RNA sequencing in a syngeneic YUMMER1.7-H2B-GFP5 melanoma model to characterize p16Ink4a-lineage-positive [p16-Lin(+)] stromal cells and identify candidate mediators of tumor–stroma interactions. title: Effect of different molecular weight and concentrations of chitosan on the phenology of tomato in greenhouse conditions
abstract: The use of synthetic fertilizers is among the most expensive and pollutant supplies in agriculture.An alternative to reduce their use is through complementary products such as biostimulants like chitosan.Biostimulants represent a sustainable alternative to chemicals as they contain or help generate beneficial substances for plant growth.The present study evaluated the effect of different molecular weights of chitosan (low, medium, and high) and different doses (120, 210, and 300 mg) on the growth of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) plants in greenhouse conditions.The evaluated variables were p

abstract: The continuous discharge of pharmaceutical residues into the environment remains a critical ecological concern. Conventional WWTPs inadequately remove many recalcitrant pharmaceuticals and may alter the composition of microbial communities. This study analyzed the dynamics of microbial communities under pharmaceutical stress, and utilizing their selective pressure to isolate individual strains with biodegradation potential. abstract: This study reviews developments in experimental studies of photo-induced cooperative phenomena (photo-induced phase transition, PIPT), which involve ultrafast dynamical changes in electronic, spin, and lattice structures. The growth in PIPT research has been driven by deep collaboration among quantum beam, materials, and theoretical sciences. title: Universal hydrogen-free synthesis and elemental doping of two-dimensional transition metal selenides
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal selenides (TMSs) feature notable bandgap flexibility, versatile doping characteristics, and practical manufacturability, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation electronics. However, their synthesis remains a critical bottleneck, as conventional chemical vapor deposition (CVD) routes require H2 assistance for selenization, raising safety, cost, and quality concerns and constraining elemental doping. abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate whether didymin confers neuroprotection against retinal ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury by modulating microglial pyroptosis and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: A mouse retinal IR injury model was used to evaluate the neuroprotective effects of didymin and its regulation of pyroptosis and inflammation in vivo. abstract: ABSTRACT Polypropylene is extensively used as a packaging material, creating a huge amount of waste after use. This work highlights the use of recycled polypropylene (rPP), starch phthalate, and modified nanosilica to produce sustainable packaging material. Both starch and nanosilica are functionalized to improve overall compatibility by increasing dispersion within the rPP matrix. abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of calcium stearate (CaSte) coating on the moisture sorption, crystallinity, and caking behavior of ʟ-lysine-carbonate (LyC) granules. CaSte was applied to LyC granules by intermittent rotary-drum spray coating, and the resulting granules (LyC-CaSte) containing 0.64% (w/w) CaSte were compared with untreated LyC granules and continuously hot-air-treated granules without CaSte (LyC-C). abstract: ABSTRACT Trap states govern charge transport, accumulation, and local‐field distortion in polymer dielectrics, yet quantitative mapping of their energy, density, and spatial distribution remains challenging. Here, triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG)‐enabled constant‐charge spectroscopy based on dielectric‐barrier discharge (DBD) is developed to resolve trap energy, density, and spatial distribution. title: Neanderthal woodworking at Abric Romaní: Insights into the role of wood in a Middle Palaeolithic domestic context
abstract: Wood technology likely played a key role in human evolution, yet it remains poorly documented because organic materials rarely preserve in archaeological contexts. The Middle Palaeolithic site of Abric Romaní (Capellades, Barcelona) provides exceptional evidence of Neanderthal woodworking preserved through travertine incrustation. abstract: Root systems demonstrate peculiar anatomical plasticity, with structural traits altering predictably across root orders to optimize water uptake, transport proficiency, and mechanical assistance. This is the first comprehensive study to elucidate the anatomical structure and hydraulic specialization across five successive root orders of Vincetoxicum capparidifolium (Wight & Arn.) abstract: Severe dendrite growth and interfacial instability hinder the practical application of aqueous zinc metal anodes. title: Temporal dynamics and species-specific responses to biotic and abiotic drivers shape seedling establishment in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Seedling establishment is a critical demographic bottleneck for species regeneration and diversity maintenance in forests, yet the temporal contributions of biotic and abiotic factors remain poorly understood. This is because most previous studies focused disproportionately on biotic factors or limited abiotic factors and used observational data lacking standardized baselines for seedling age. abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from the oil and gas (O&G) sector are a major source of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. Russia is a leading CH 4 emitter, with the O&G sector accounting for approximately 80% of its total fossil fuel‐derived CH 4 emissions. However, long‐term emission trends remain unclear due to significant discrepancies between bottom‐up inventories and atmospheric model estimates. title: Determination of an indicator of extinction risk for forest fragments of the Atlantic Forest
abstract: As transformações ambientais que ocorrem no meio ambiente pressionam os ecossistemas florestais de forma a ocasionar o desequilíbrio nas suas funções ecológicas, além de contribuir para a perda desses ecossistemas. title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Mediation as a Tool in Resolving Intertribal Land Disputes: The Case of Eyumojock Sub-Division
abstract: Inter-tribal land disputes constitute one of the most pervasive conflicts in rural Cameroon, particularly in the South-West Region where customary land tenure systems intersect with population growth and inter-ethnic relations. In Eyumojock Sub-Division, intertribal land disputes between the Ebinsi, Ayuk’aba, Bakwele, Afap, Ogomoko, Kembong, and other indigenous groups threaten social cohesion and economic development. title: Comparative Assessment of Bio-Oils from Agriculture Biomass Waste and Conventional Fossil Fuels: Evaluating Their Potential as Sustainable Industrial Fuel Alternatives
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy and the environmental impacts of fossil fuel dependence have intensified interest in biomass-derived fuels, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria where agricultural residues remain largely underutilized. This study assessed bio-oils obtained from agricultural biomass in comparison to traditional fossil fuels as a source of industrial energy. title: Electrification reshapes BRICS vehicle urban mining: Material flows and circularity by 2050
abstract: Vehicle electrification is increasing demand for critical battery materials and shifting end-of-life management from whole vehicle scrap toward component-level streams, especially retired vehicle batteries. The five BRICS founding countries—Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—represent a critical and diverse testing ground for this transition because they combine large and growing vehicle markets, divergent electrification pathways, and uneven recycling capacities. title: Low levels of Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda J.E. Smith) damage in Bangladesh are linked to farmers’ integrated pest management practices and weather conditions
abstract: Fall Armyworm (FAW), Spodoptera frugiperda , is recognized as a major threat to maize production in Africa, the Americas (its native range in North, Central, and South America), and increasingly in Asia following its recent spread across the continent. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of FAW pest dynamics and yield impacts in Bangladesh, focusing on the efficacy of agroecological, cultural and chemical pest management practices. title: Migration as Method, Death as Border: Necropolitics and Speculative Cosmopolitanism in Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West
abstract: This article’s distinct intervention is to theorize Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West as practicing speculative cosmopolitanism: a narrative method that couples the “autonomy of migration” with informal, care-based affiliations beyond the nation-state. title: Greening cities to ensure biosphere functional integrity: Insights from Rotterdam and Lagos
abstract: The Earth Commission has proposed that 20-25% of every square kilometre of managed lands, including in cities, be reserved for nature to ensure its local functioning and human wellbeing -biosphere functional integrity boundary (BFI). This research adopted a multi-method justice-oriented approach grounded in the Earth System Justice framework to assess the challenges and opportunities of implementing this proposed biosphere functional integrity boundary in Rotterdam and Lagos. title: Hydrogen’s future in Türkiye: Storage, natural gas integration, and energy transition
abstract: Hydrogen stands out as a clean energy carrier that plays a critical role in the global energy transformation. Türkiye's increasing energy demand, dependence on fossil fuels, and carbon emission reduction targets place hydrogen technologies at the center of national energy policies. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the integration of hydrogen into energy systems could contribute to reducing global carbon emissions by up to 20%. This study comprehensively examines Türkiye's hydrogen potential, its integration with existing energy infrastructure, and hydrogen storage solutions.

abstract: This integrative review evaluates the current state and evolution of biochar research in arid and semi-arid agroecosystems by integrating scientometric analysis with a critical narrative synthesis. Specifically, it examines publication trends, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution while assessing the relationships among feedstock types, pyrolysis conditions, biochar properties, soil-crop interactions, labile carbon fractions, microbial processes, and practical applicability under water-limited conditions. Recently, short- and medium-chain carboxylic acids (CAs) have emerged as greener alternatives to amines as the organic component of SHSs. title: Core–Shell Upconversion Platform Based on an Amino-Functionalized ZIF-8 with a Covalently Anchored Ruthenium Nitrosyl Complex for Controlled Release of Nitric Oxide in Biological Media
abstract: Abstract The development of nitric oxide (NO) donor agents capable of controlled NO release upon light irradiation in the biological window is relevant for phototherapies. The cis-[Ru(dc-bpy)2(SO3)(NO)]+ complex (dc-bpy = 2,2′-dicarboxybipyridine) is synthesized and anchored onto a NaYF4:Yb,Tm@ZIF-8-NH2 nanoplatform. The isolated complex presents high stability under basic conditions (pH 9) and an absorption band in the visible region up to 405 nm. A core–shell platform of upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) coated with ZIF-8 is synthesized and functionalized with amino groups (UCNP-ZIF-8-NH2).

title: An antimicrobial cyclic peptide with multitarget efficacy for acne
abstract: Abstract Acne vulgaris is a complex inflammatory disorder, and current treatment options are often limited by antibiotic resistance and cutaneous irritation, underscoring the urgent need for safer multi-target therapeutic alternatives. In this study, a novel antimicrobial cyclic peptide (AMCP) was systematically evaluated for its multidimensional anti-acne efficacy, and a penetration enhancer was developed for improving the transdermal penetration. At a concentration of 20 µg/mL, AMCP inhibited dihydrotestosterone (DHT)- and linoleic acid (LA)-induced lipid synthesis in SZ95 sebocytes by 40.0%
institutions: Key Laboratory of Synthetic and Biological Colloids, Ministry of Education

title: Pour une poétique réaliste de l’image photographique
abstract: Par le passé, certains philosophes soucieux de réaffirmer le droit du réel à parler de lui-même ont pu s’accorder sur une représentation idéalisée des procédés photographiques. Puisque l’action causale de la lumière sur une surface photosensible n’implique pas que des états intentionnels du photographe entrent en jeu dans la genèse de l’image, l’image résultante a longtemps été pensée comme un enregistrement objectif de l’état de choses initial. title: Pressure-Induced Modulation of Electronic, Elastic, and Optical Traits in Hexagonal La₂O₃ for Advanced Solid-state Battery Cathode Frameworks
abstract: In this study, we systematically investigate the composition-dependent elastic, mechanical, and thermophysical properties of the hexagonal close-packed (HCP) structured rare-earth metal chalcogenide, lanthanum oxide La2O3, at a constant temperature of 300 K. Atomistic simulations were executed across a hydrostatic pressure range of 0–100 GPa using the well-established Lennard-Jones (L-J) interatomic potential model. title: Uso de realidad virtual inmersiva como recurso didáctico para la comprensión del sistema nervioso central
abstract: La enseñanza de la neuroanatomía mediante recursos bidimensionales puede dificultar la comprensión espacial de las estructuras cerebrales, lo que ha favorecido la incorporación de metodologías inmersivas en educación superior. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo evaluar la viabilidad pedagógica de la realidad virtual (RV) inmersiva y analizar el aprendizaje asociado a su uso como recurso didáctico para el estudio del sistema nervioso central. title: Identification of germplasm and genomic markers associated with reduced T‐2 and HT‐2 mycotoxin accumulation in oat
abstract: Abstract Harmful T‐2 and HT‐2 mycotoxins are produced by Fusarium langsethiae and Fusarium sporotrichioides in developing oat ( Avena sativa L.) grain. This study identified oat genotypes with consistently low toxin accumulation across environments. Toxin enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay and fungal DNA (quantitative polymerase chain reaction) levels were quantified in 19 oat genotypes grown at two Irish sites under natural infection. title: One Health assessment of Leptospira circulation in aquatic ecosystems, wild rodents, and livestock in Kazakhstan
abstract: Background and Aim: Leptospirosis is an important zoonosis maintained through interactions among environmental reservoirs, wildlife, livestock, and humans. Despite ongoing veterinary surveillance, information on the environmental circulation of Leptospira spp. in Kazakhstan remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the circulation and diversity of Leptospira spp. in major aquatic ecosystems of Kazakhstan using metagenomic sequencing within a One Health framework, complemented by rodent surveillance and livestock serological data. title: Mechanisms underlying the adverse health outcomes of dibutyl phthalate and bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate based on network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation
abstract: The widespread use of dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) has raised concerns about their potential toxicity to human health. This study aimed to identify the potential targets of DBP and DEHP and their related pathways. Potential target proteins were predicted by functional enrichment analysis and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify hub targets, while molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations validated the interactions between DBP and their target proteins. title: An integrated framework for characterising livestock systems and assessing ruminant performance across heterogeneous production environments: Evidence from Nigeria
abstract: Globally, livestock production systems (LPS) are crucial for supporting livelihoods and ensuring food security. This study developed and applied an integrated livestock production zone (LPZ) framework to characterise (LPS) and evaluate ruminant performance across Nigeria’s diverse agroecological environments. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining expert consultations, a literature review, and a participatory on-farm survey across 12 states with 1,404 participants. title: Evaluating the multi-scale performance and mechanical behavior of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) mixtures incorporating waste-derived oils and vacuum bottom rejuvenators
abstract: Maximizing the utilization of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) while maintaining long-term fatigue durability is essential for sustainable pavement infrastructure. To address this challenge, this study aims to establish a multi-scale framework for evaluating and optimizing rejuvenator performance in high-RAP mixtures. Accordingly, the efficacy of three distinct rejuvenators—Waste Engine Oil (WEO), Lubricant Oil (LU), and Vacuum Bottom (VB)—was investigated in restoring the chemical and mechanical properties of bitumens and mixtures incorporating 30%, 45%, and 60% RAP. abstract: Abstract The Apollonia Formation is among the least-studied unconventional gas reservoirs in Egypt, characterized by relatively high porosity (20–35%) and extremely low permeability (< 0.1 md). This study presents an integrated, multidisciplinary evaluation of well BED 9–3 in the BED 9 Field, Western Desert, Egypt, aiming to demonstrate that nitrogen foam hydraulic fracturing, when systematically coupled with comprehensive petrophysical characterization, provides an effective and technically validated route to commercial productivity in tight carbonate reservoirs. title: QSPR Approach to Predict the Physicochemical Properties of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons Using Degree-Based Topological Indices
abstract: The persistent harmful effects of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) and other organic contaminants make water pollution a major environmental concern. Comprehending their physicochemical behaviour is essential for determining their influence on the environment and directing pollution control measures. Chemical graph theory makes extensive use of topological indices (TI) to forecast the physicochemical characteristics of these organic molecules by developing a Quantitative Structure-Property Relationship (QSPR) model. title: Integrated network pharmacology and experimental validation reveal the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of Wuwei Shaji Powder in hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury
abstract: Abstract: Background: Hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury (HIRI) is primarily mediated by oxidative stress and inflammatory activation, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Objectives: This study aimed to elucidate the key active ingredients, hub targets and molecular pathways through which Wuwei Shaji Powder may exert anti-inflammatory effects in HIRI using integrated network pharmacology and experimental validation. title: A life cycle-based Green Manufacturing framework for environmental decision-making: an application to heavy-duty vehicle chassis frame rail manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Heavy-duty vehicles (HDV) are essential to global transportation and logistics systems, yet environmental assessments have predominantly focused on the use phase, leaving the environmental impacts of the manufacturing stage comparatively underexplored. This study evaluates the cradle-to-gate environmental performance of steel chassis frame rail manufacturing using a process-level Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on primary industrial data collected directly from the shop floor. Environmental impacts were assessed using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) and Environmental Footprint (EF) 3.1

title: Bridging the cultural divide to improve drinking water security, sustainability and resilience in first nations communities: A case study from Australia
abstract: First Nations communities (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples) in remote Australia experience disproportionate risks to drinking water security, compounded by climate change. Community drinking water systems are operated predominantly by government service providers to meet regulatory requirements, yet many systems fail to meet quality standards. title: Biopriming of Durum Wheat Seeds with Diazotrophic Bacteria Improved Physiological and Biochemical Pathways Under Salt Stress
abstract: A significant strategy for sustainable management, by decreasing the use of chemical fertilizers, can consist of technology based on suitable levels of plant growth promoting bacteria (PGPB) seed biopriming. The main goal of this work was to demonstrate the positive effect of PGPB as seed biopriming factor on the growth of durum wheat plantlets under stress. plantlets physiological and biochemical pathways modifications were assessed in controlled growth chamber under salt stress. title: Environmental Determinants of Mental Health: a multilevel theoretical framework for understanding mental health and wellbeing
abstract: The present paper develops Author’s concept of Environmental Determinants of Mental Health for 2025 into a Multilevel Pathways Framework for the Environmental Determinants of Mental Health. The framework explains how natural, built, social and digital environmental conditions may influence mental health and wellbeing through environmental encounters, direct exposure, appraisal, access or avoidance, and biopsychosocial mechanisms. title: Short‐Term Weather Variability Alters Plant Carbon Balance in Arctic Tundra Species
abstract: ABSTRACT Increasing weather variability is an aspect of global change with poorly understood impacts on organisms and ecosystems. Model predictions have shown that weather variability can diminish physiological performance, but empirical corroboration remains limited. Here, we explore the effects of short‐term variation in temperature and light on plant physiological functioning and the resulting leaf carbon balance. title: The heterogeneous impact of conditional cash transfers on child labor in Indonesia: Evidence from PIP and PKH programs
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of Indonesia’s conditional cash transfer (CCT) programs, Program Indonesia Pintar (PIP) and Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH), on child labor, utilizing data from the 2023 Indonesia National Socioeconomic Survey (SUSENAS). To address potential selection bias, we employed propensity score matching (PSM) to estimate the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT). The findings revealed a nuanced landscape. title: WHEN WASTEWATER SPEAKS: DECODING THE CHEMICAL FINGERPRINT AND ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS SIGNATURE OF FUNTUA TEXTILE EFFLUENT, NORTHWESTERN NIGERIA
abstract: Textile manufacturing is a water-intensive industrial activity whose wet-processing operations can generate chemically complex effluents containing colour-producing substances, suspended and dissolved solids, organic matter, salts, nutrients and potentially toxic metals. Conventional wastewater assessments commonly report these constituents independently, which may obscure the overall environmental character of the effluent. title: Plateau–Rayleigh Instability–Driven Shell-First Growth of (Ge, Si1– x Ge x )–AlN Core–Shell Crystals Exhibiting Telecom E-Band Photoluminescence

Herein, we report mixed-source hydride vapor phase epitaxial growth of (Ge, Si1–xGex)–AlN core–shell crystals on Al-based nanoabsorbers. Nano-CT and microscopy resolve hollow, partially filled, and filled morphologies that together support a Plateau–Rayleigh-instability-mediated shell-first model in which an Al-derived shell-like structure precedes filling by Ge-containing or Si–Ge-containing material. title: Interactions between lactobacillus and yeast: A recent update
abstract: Abstract Lactobacillus and yeast are microorganisms widely distributed in nature. Their interactions significantly impact fermentation processes, human health, and medical care. However, there is a lack of a systematic summary of the characteristics of these interactions, and the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain unclear. This review systematically summarizes the characteristics of Lactobacillus and yeast interactions, highlighting both mutualistic symbiosis and antagonistic effects. title: Duck nesting response to experimental management of upland habitats in California
abstract: Abstract Habitat loss and limited upland nesting cover likely constrain waterfowl productivity in intensively managed wetland landscapes in California, USA. We evaluated whether experimental manipulations of upland habitats, including the seeding of native plants, dense nesting cover, or cereal grains, could enhance nesting vegetation and improve duck nest density and nest survival in a Mediterranean climate. title: A Fish MDA5 Integrates Canonical RIG‐I and MDA5 Ligand Recognition
abstract: RIG-I and MDA5 are cytosolic RNA sensors that recognize distinct viral ligands in mammals, yet RIG-I has been independently lost from multiple teleost lineages. How RIG-I-deficient vertebrates preserve recognition of RIG-I-associated viral RNA remains poorly understood. Here, we show that MDA5 from the large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea, Lc), a teleost species lacking RIG-I, recognizes both 5'-triphosphate dsRNA (5'ppp-dsRNA), the canonical ligand of RIG-I, and long dsRNA, the classical ligand of MDA5. title: Catalytic Performance of Nickel Oxide Loaded Refluxed Chicken Eggshells-Derived Calcium Oxide in Pyrolysis of High-Density Polyethylene
abstract: The main objective of this work is to investigate the performance of nickel oxide-loaded refluxed chicken eggshells in the pyrolysis of high-density polyethylene using a fixed-bed reactor. Nickel oxide at 5 wt.% was loaded onto the refluxed calcined chicken eggshell via the incipient wetness impregnation method and characterised for phase analysis, surface morphology, and textural properties. title: La adaptación como puesta en acción y encarnación
abstract: Since the seminal studies of Stam, Hutcheon, and Sánchez Noriega, research on novels adapted into films has focused on the transpositions between page and screen. This proposal examines an intermediate step: the adaptation of a novel into a screenplay. It aims to show that screenwriting is a genre whose dominant function is enactment and embodiment. Due to this distinctive quality, the screenplay has the capacity to reveal the constitutive dimension of language. title: Resistance to Bemisia tabaci Asia I in Capsicum Reduces Whitefly Performance and Is Associated With Lower Pepper Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (PepYLCV) Disease
abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread development of insecticide resistance and stricter regulations on pesticide use highlight the need for natural pest resistance in crops. In pepper, viral diseases such as pepper yellow leaf curl virus (PepYLCV), transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci , are a major constraint in tropical regions. In this study, we explored genetic variation within Capsicum spp. to identify sources of resistance against B. tabaci Asia I and assessed whether plant resistance is associated with reduced PepYLCV disease. title: Possible observational survey strategies to maximize exoplanet yields: a report from the survey strategies task group in the exoplanet science yields working group
abstract: We present a variety of possible observational sequences from planet detection to characterization (i.e., survey strategies) for the initial exoEarth detection and characterization survey phase of the Habitable Worlds Observatory. An array of survey strategies were collated by the HWO Exoplanet Survey Strategies Task Group; by investigating and comparing expected resultant exoEarth yields for multiple survey strategies, we can better understand the most efficient strategy to characterize multiple planets in unconventional ways. title: Organizational Growth Reconsidered: A Systems‐Based Review and Research Agenda
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent years have witnessed a significant increase in post‐ and degrowth research, which explores the social and ecological consequences of, and alternatives to, economic growth. To date, however, the debate has primarily occurred at the macroeconomic level, leaving a gap in our understanding of the role of organizational growth in a post‐growth context. abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. title: Heterogeneous co-circulation of multiple DENV-1 and DENV-2 genotypes in Vung Tau during the 2023 dengue outbreak in Vietnam
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a significant global health threat, particularly in hyper-endemic regions like Vietnam, where the co-circulation of multiple serotypes and genotypes complicates disease control. In 2023, 6.5 million dengue cases and 6,800 deaths were reported globally, marking the largest dengue outbreak in the world. Vietnam recorded 149,557 dengue cases and 36 deaths, with a notable dominance of the DENV-2 serotype. title: Narrativas familiares en torno a la atención del Estado mexicano en la búsqueda de personas desaparecidas
abstract: This research arises from the painful reality of disappearances in Mexico. The country is experiencing an accelerated increase in such problem and has been unable to respond promptly and effectively to the needs of disappeared persons’ relatives, who are indirect victims. This situation has created an implicit expectation that families themselves will lead efforts to search for, locate, and identify disappeared persons. title: Soil Organic Carbon Dynamics and Carbon Management Index under Forest and Agricultural Land-Use Systems in the Western Himalayas
abstract: Himalayan soils are highly susceptible to the impacts of climate change and land-use shifts. Soil organic carbon (SOC) and the carbon management index (CMI) are key measures of soil health in response to land use changes. This study assessed total organic carbon (TOC), carbon fractions, carbon pool index (CPI), CMI, and physicochemical properties in forest and agricultural land-use systems in the temperate western Himalayas. title: Implementation of the EU Nitrates Directive in Germany—a critical review
abstract: Abstract Background Under the EU Nitrates Directive, Member States are required to adopt suitable measures to comply with the limit value of 50 mg NO 3 l −1 in groundwater. In Germany, the Fertiliser Application Ordinance (Düngeverordnung; DüV) defines the code of good agricultural practice with regard to nitrogen fertilisation. More than 30 years after the ordinance first came into force, the deficits and the ineffectiveness of the German water protection policies are evident. title: Collection-informed environmental prioritization of unused household pharmaceuticals using FASS 2025 classification, risk quotients, and TOPSIS-based decision analysis
abstract: Unused household pharmaceuticals may contribute to environmental release, yet household accumulation is rarely evaluated alongside available environmental risk information. title: Nanostructured Hybrid Matrix Device: An Engineered Approach for Localized Photodynamic Therapy in 9L/lacZ Cell Models
abstract: Abstract Gliosarcoma treatment remains a challenge due to its aggressiveness and high recurrence rates. This study describes the development and characterization of a novel hybrid drug delivery system (DDS) for localized photodynamic therapy (PDT). The system consists of a PVA/gelatin hydrogel encapsulated with hydroxyapatite microspheres (meHAp) loaded with chloroaluminum phthalocyanine (ClAlPc). title: Ambient particulate matter exposure and children's blood pressure in rural California, 2019-2022
abstract: Elevated blood pressure (BP) in children is a risk factor for adult hypertension and is increasing globally. Ambient particulate matter (PM) is associated with increased BP in children in urban areas, but data from rural regions are sparse. The Children's AIRE study enrolled children 6-8 years in 2017-2019 and collected data bi-annually through Spring 2022. Residential addresses were spatially linked to regulatory air pollution monitors to determine long-term (12-month) and short-term (7-day) exposure to PM 2.5 and PM 10 . title: Atomic oxygen-induced oxidative degradation of carbamazepine: Mechanistic insights from reactive molecular dynamics
abstract: Abstract Carbamazepine (CBZ) is a persistent pharmaceutical contaminant that is poorly removed by conventional wastewater treatment processes. Although non-thermal plasma can promote efficient CBZ degradation, the elementary molecular mechanisms governing its initial oxidative transformation remain incompletely understood. In this work, atomic-oxygen-induced CBZ oxidation was investigated using DFTB-based reactive molecular dynamics (RMD) simulations combined with stationary thermochemical and reaction-path analyses. title: Becoming a Male Nurse in the Maldives: A Descriptive Phenomenological Study of Lived Experiences
abstract: Similar to worldwide trends in the nursing profession, in the Maldives, male nurses' participation in the workforce continues to be shaped by gender dynamics and is often affected by meaningful opportunities and distinct challenges. This study aimed to gain a deeper understanding of why men choose nursing, their working experiences, and career trajectories, offering insights into the challenges and opportunities they encounter. abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoresponsive polymers are highly anticipated for passive thermochromic smart windows, yet the instability and too‐high mobility of their light‐scattering states for separated phases remain significant hurdles. title: FROM EXPLOITATION TO EMPATHY: THE POETICS OF WOUNDED NATURE IN CONTEMPORARY INDONESIAN POETRY
abstract: This study examines the contemporary ecological paradox: despite growing public awareness of the environmental crisis, destructive practices continue. With a critical-qualitative design and interpretive orientation, this study combines close reading with the latest wave of ecocriticism (ecopoetics, material ecocriticism, posthuman/multispecies) to unravel how poetry constructs ecological moral criticism, fosters empathy, and formulates human-more-than-human relations. title: Occurrence, spatiotemporal distribution, and ecological risks of antibiotics in a river basin of eastern China
abstract: Abstract The widespread use of antibiotics has resulted in their frequent occurrence in aquatic environments, raising ecological concerns; however, conducting precise monitoring and tracing of a broad spectrum of antibiotics concurrently in complex river networks at the watershed scale still faces significant challenges. This study investigated the pollution characteristics of 32 target antibiotics in a major river basin in eastern China. A total of 184 river water samples collected across 2024–2025 were analyzed. title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. title: “It’s important, but at a cost…”: healthcare professionals and people with aphasia describe what influences use of a novel, digital communication aid
abstract: PURPOSE: Safe and quality healthcare requires effective patient-provider communication. Aphasia is a communication disability that leaves people at risk of ineffective communication and inadequate care. Modifying the environment is one way to support communication. A novel mobile communication aid-The Aphasia App-was designed to support hospital interactions between healthcare professionals (HCPs) and people with aphasia (PWA). title: Inequities in heat-related emergency department visits in California from 2005 – 2017
abstract: Rising temperatures and extreme heat pose a substantial threat to human health through increases in heat-related morbidity and mortality. Moreover, social determinants of health can exacerbate the impact of heat on susceptible populations. This study investigates the inequities in heat-related emergency department (ED) visits in California from 2005-2017, focusing on how social determinants of health, represented by the California Healthy Places Index (HPI), may influence the associations between temperature and ED visits. title: Two novel tribes of Lamiaceae supported by phylogenomics and morphology
abstract: Plastome-based classifications recognize 12 subfamilies and 22 tribes within Lamiaceae. However, the deep phylogenetic relationships and tribal limits of Pogostemoneae sensu lato remain uncertain because nuclear phylogenomic investigations and assessments of cytonuclear discordance remain limited. University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: How directionality emerges through frame layering: An analysis of Swedish research and innovation policy on agri-food
abstract: Transforming agri-food systems is widely seen as necessary to address overlapping ecological and social crises. Public research and innovation policy is a central mechanism through which such transformations are steered, yet it is often articulated in ways that obscure the normative commitments legitimising particular pathways. Using critical frame analysis and drawing on debates around directionality and the contrasting paradigms of sustainable intensification and agroecology, we analyse Swedish agri-food research and innovation policy from 2017 to 2025. title: Genomic characterization of pre‐Green Revolution wheat landraces from the Nepalese and Bhutanese Himalayas reveals geographically structured diversity
abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) landraces collected before the widespread regional adoption of Green Revolution cultivars provide a historical record of locally maintained germplasm. We characterized a panel of 202 accessions collected from Nepal and Bhutan between 1952 and 1958. Genotyping by Random Amplicon Sequencing-Direct yielded 30,228 high-quality markers; removing 38 close genetic duplicates produced a nonredundant panel of 164 accessions. title: High summer temperatures in Central Europe during the Bølling period (∼14.6-14.0 cal ka BP) inferred from plant macrofossils using a novel European calibration dataset
abstract: Quantitative reconstruction of past temperatures is essential for understanding regional climate variability, and plant macrofossils provide valuable paleoclimatic records due to their sensitivity to summer conditions. However, no plant macrofossil-based quantitative summer temperature reconstructions have been available from Central Europe, limiting our understanding of regional Lateglacial climate dynamics. institutions: Institute of Botany of the Slovak Academy of Sciences
Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Botany

title: Ten–eleven translocation 3 activates the TGF-β-like ligand Scube3 to promote renal fibrosis: mechanism and translational potential
abstract: Resident renal fibroblasts are a predominant source for myofibroblasts that produce ECM to contribute to renal fibrosis in the course of chronic kidney disease (CKD). The mechanism whereby fibroblast-myofibroblast transition (FMyT) is driven remains incompletely understood. In the present study, we investigated the involvement of ten-eleven translocation 3 (TET3) in regulating FMyT and renal fibrosis focusing on the regulatory mechanism and translational potential. We report that TET3 deletion in primary renal fibroblasts dampened myofibroblast transition in response to pro-fibrogenic stimuli.

title: Functional traits of restored grasslands resemble positive reference sites but differ from degraded grasslands
abstract: EUNIS habitat types are a widely accepted reference for conservation in Europe. Their site conditions are well described, but plant functional traits are not included in habitat descriptions. However, characterization is necessary for trait-based restoration. This approach uses taxonomic knowledge for the selection of the species pool and specific trait values to decide about relative species abundances. title: Who Plans to Marry? Economic Security and Marital Intentions Among Never‐Married Adults in Türkiye
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To examine how three dimensions of economic security, namely employment position, wealth, and income, are associated with the marital intentions of never‐married adults in Türkiye, and to formally test whether these associations differ by gender. Background Marriage remains the dominant pathway to family formation in Türkiye, yet marriage is increasingly postponed amid economic uncertainty. title: Modeling and experimental validation of dynamic defocusing effects in femtosecond laser ablation of complex gear surfaces
abstract: Femtosecond (fs) laser ablation has emerged as a disruptive technology for the ultra-precision finishing of aerospace face gears. However, its application to complex 3D curved topologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by spatially varying nonlinear laser-material interactions. In this study, we propose a comprehensive 3D nonlinear mathematical model for the fs laser ablation of 18Cr2Ni4WA alloy steel to reveal the mechanism of spatial light field distortion. title: Geographical Ranks of Ecosystem Sustainability: Evidence from a 66-Year Provenance Trial of a Keystone Boreal Forest Species
abstract: Understanding the spatial determinants of long-term forest ecosystem sustainability is a prerequisite for designing effective climate adaptation strategies. Long-term provenance trials serve as invaluable in situ laboratories for assessing the adaptive capacity of keystone forest species under novel climatic regimes. This study capitalizes on a unique 66-year-old experiment involving 44 climatic ecotypes of Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris L.) – a foundation species of the Eurasian boreal and temperate forests – in Belarus to quantify, for the first time, the relationship between geographical ori

title: Efficient enzyme-mediated degradation of various emerging pollutants, including 2-mercaptobenzothiazole, paracetamol, and sulfamethoxazole, using HRP@UiO-66-NH2
abstract: The increasing contamination of water sources due to industrialization and population growth poses significant environmental and health risks, even at trace pollutant concentrations. Enzymatic bioremediation, particularly using horseradish peroxidase (HRP), has shown great potential in pollutant degradation due to its high selectivity and catalytic efficiency. However, limitations such as poor operational stability and reusability hinder its large-scale application. University of Arkansas at Little Rock

title: Spatial spillovers of local government fixed investment on fiscal gap: empirical evidence from spatial Durbin model
abstract: Over the past 20 years, the contribution of fixed asset investment by local government to economic growth and fiscal revenue has been significant. However, the traditional “investment-tax” linear model fails to fully account for the dynamic evolution of the fiscal gap within the complex spatial interactions. Therefore, it is essential to establish a simplified equilibrium model incorporating spatial interactions to examine the relationship between fixed asset investment by local government and the fiscal gap. Changchun University of Science and Technology

title: Musculoskeletal symptoms and biopsychosocial factors among nursing students: implications for protecting the future health workforce
abstract: Background Musculoskeletal disorders are an important occupational health concern among healthcare professionals and may emerge before entry into the workforce. Identifying musculoskeletal symptoms and their biopsychosocial correlates among nursing students may provide opportunities for early prevention and health promotion. Objective This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms and identify associated biopsychosocial factors among nursing students in Türkiye. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 213 nursing students (77% female) in Türkiye. Data we

title: Post-weaning DHA or EPA supplementation attenuates depressive-like behavior and myelination deficits induced by maternal high-fat diet in rat offspring
abstract: Abstract Depression affects younger populations, while imbalanced diet may contribute to disease development, with myelin abnormalities representing one possible underlying mechanism. We previously showed that maternal high-fat diet (HFD; 60% energy from fat) during pregnancy and lactation induces depressive-like behavior and myelin-related alterations in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of rat offspring. We investigated whether post-weaning docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)- or eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-enriched diets until adulthood could reverse these abnormalities. Depressive-like behavior was asses

title: The Visible and the Invisible: Contested Evidence, Photography, and the Politics of Remembering Japanese Atrocities in Asia
abstract: From 1931 to 1945, Japanese wartime photography was determined by a censorship system that shaped what could and could not be seen. The survival of the Mainichi Shimbun’s wartime negatives, hidden in an underground temple vault at the end of the war despite official orders to destroy them, offers rare material traces of this censorship process. This article examines how claims about photographic evidence framed as authenticity, veracity, and proof have been mobilized in debates over Japanese wartime imagery by analyzing two highly contested images from 1937 published in the Mainichi newspaper

title: Social Capital at the Service of Informal Export: The Case of Moroccan Women Entrepreneurs
abstract: This research explores the mobilization of informal social capital as a mechanism for circumventing institutional barriers to export among Moroccan women entrepreneurs. The study specifically examines how informal social networks compensate for the failures of the formal market and facilitate the internationalization of women-owned businesses in a constrained economic context. The empirical investigation relies on an exploratory qualitative approach following an abductive logic. The corpus of primary data was built from semi-structured interviews conducted with 14 Moroccan women entrepreneurs

title: Integrating multi-environment and path coefficient analysis for the identification of yellow rust-resistant bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes
abstract: Rapid turnover of varieties and limited access to rust-resistant wheat varieties across agroecologies are due to the rapid mutation of yellow rust pathogens. This study aimed to identify high-yielding, yellow rust-resistant genotypes and assess the severity of yellow rust across wheat growth stages. 150 bread wheat genotypes were evaluated using an alpha lattice design with two replications at three locations across two major wheat-producing areas of Ethiopia (Arsi and North Shewa) during the 2022 and 2023 main cropping seasons. title: Development of Sustainable Thermoplastic Zein by Partial Substitution of Glycerol with Olive Oil or Oleic Acid: a New Route for Injection-Molded Biopolymers
abstract: Thermoplastic zein formulations containing 25 wt% total modifier were processed by extrusion and injection molding. Glycerol was progressively replaced with oleic acid (OA) or olive oil (OO) at substitution levels ranging from 2.5 to 10 wt%, while maintaining the zein and total modifier contents at 75 and 25 wt%, respectively. The formulation containing 10 wt% OO could not be successfully processed. title: Metabolic and neural responses to ultraprocessed foods: a randomized, controlled, crossover study
abstract: Dietary patterns worldwide have shifted toward increased consumption of ultraprocessed foods (UPFs), which has been linked to higher disease burden. One proposed mechanism underlying both UPF consumption and metabolic disease is altered post-ingestive responses relative to nutritionally similar foods. Here we report the effects of food processing on post-ingestive metabolism and brain response in a randomized, crossover study involving 57 healthy-weight adults who consumed a nutritionally matched UPF or non-UPF meal. title: Experimental infection of avian paramyxoviruses in chickens and mice
abstract: Avian paramyxoviruses (APMVs) are being increasingly detected in wild birds, yet the pathogenic potential of novel species remains poorly defined. We characterized the molecular determinants and pathogenicity profiles of seven APMV strains. Sequence analyses identified conserved hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) receptor-binding and V protein immune-modulatory motifs, whereas F cytoplasmic-tail motifs, P and W trafficking signals, and L methyltransferase motifs were strain-specific. title: Estrategia de aprendizaje de la prueba de fluoresceína basada en el método de casos
abstract: A didactic strategy based on the case method is presented for teaching the fluorescein test to 34 forensic science professionals. The objective was to evaluate the integration of chemical foundations, criminalistic interpretation, and legal support in solving a crime scene simulation. Under an interpretive paradigm, technical reports were analyzed using a competency-based evaluation rubric. Results indicate that 100% of the groups successfully identified the suspect through morphological comparison. title: La sibila del Oriente, de Calderón de la Barca: de la descuidada y sombría naturaleza al resplandor de la verdad revelada
abstract: En la primera jornada de la comedia presenta Calderón un mundo inacabado, una «mancha» natural, que la Sibila interpreta mediante la síntesis de tres árboles simbólicos (ciprés, palma y cedro). En la segunda, con su intervención y con la madera del Árbol de la Cruz, se inicia la construcción del templo de Salomón, que pone orden y reglamenta legal, religiosa y moralmente, aquel caos natural. title: Protein homeostasis and inter-organellar signaling under salt stress
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic constraint on plant growth, productivity, and global food security. It disrupts cellular protein homeostasis (proteostasis) at every step, from synthesis to degradation. Plant survival under salt stress therefore depends on the coordinated regulation of protein synthesis, folding, post-translational modification, trafficking, quality control, and turnover. title: Invisible Wounds, Colonial Scars: Slow Violence and Eco-Orientalism in South Asian, Malay, and Arab Fiction
abstract: The paper explores intersections of slow violence, eco-orientalism and colonial ecologies in fiction work in three postcolonial literary traditions: South Asian, Malay and Arab. Based on the work of Rob Nixon’s Slow Violence and the Environmentalism of the Poor (2011b), it examines the way in which postcolonial authors describe the gradual environmental degradation by colonial and neo-colonial powers. title: Implications of genes involved in inflammatory regulation, cytoskeletal organization and extracellular matrix integrity for susceptibility to high-altitude pulmonary edema: A pilot whole-exome sequencing study
abstract: High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a potentially fatal form of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema that develops in susceptible individuals following rapid ascent to high altitude. Although exaggerated hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction is central to its pathophysiology, additional physiological mechanisms may also underlie individual susceptibility to HAPE. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) enables the identification of coding variants that may contribute to disease susceptibility. abstract: ABSTRACT Detection of magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) relies on their nonlinear magnetic response, changing with the local environment in vivo. Employing an effective viscosity model within stochastic coupled Néel–Brownian simulations, we quantify how viscosity (0.8–50 000 mPa·s) affects signal intensity of single‐frequency magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS, 25 kHz) and frequency‐mixing MPS (FM‐MPS; f H = 40.5 kHz, f L = 0.063 kHz). title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeO x ‐modified Co 2 C catalysts. title: A comparative study on the effects of clove oil, flaxseed oil, and almond oil as an additive on the lubricating characteristics of chemically modified used coconut oil
abstract: Abstract Lubrication is widely associated with contact surfaces having relative motion to decrease friction and wear. The majority of locally available lubricants have petroleum products as a base, which are toxic to the environment. The excess usage of petroleum products is also causing drastic fossil fuel depletion, emphasizing the necessity of an alternative to these locally available lubricants. title: Heliocide H2 and cadinatriene glucopyranoside as promising dual β-lactamase inhibitors against antibiotic resistance: an integrated computational study
abstract: Antibiotic resistance mediated by β-lactamase enzymes poses a major obstacle to the effective treatment of bacterial infections. Among these enzymes, serine β-lactamases and metallo β-lactamases are of particular concern, as they hydrolyze β-lactam antibiotics, rendering them ineffective. This study aimed to identify putative dual β-lactamase inhibitor candidates with predicted activity against both classes of β-lactamases using a comprehensive in silico approach. title: From bodyweight to biomarkers: Season‐associated metabolic, endocrine and haematological shifts in breeding stallions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Breeding stallions are subjected to sustained seasonal metabolic, endocrine, and immune demands requiring systemic energy engagement. Prospective longitudinal data in the same individuals are limited. OBJECTIVES: To screen adaptive responses of breeding stallions of clinical relevance through longitudinal characterisation of temporal changes across the mating season and negative photoperiod: (i) health and nutritional status; (ii) oxidative status and immune modulation; and (iii) metabolic and endocrine biomarkers as correlates of reproductive potential. title: Epigenetic signatures of different types of childhood maltreatment in a high-risk sample: a preregistered replication study
abstract: Abstract Childhood maltreatment (CM) has long-lasting effects on physical and mental health with CM type specific effects being reported. Epigenetic processes, like deoxyribonucleic acid methylation (DNAm), might mediate this link, and CM types might be linked to differential alterations in DNAm. While a study by Cecil et al.
