title: Presenting ReadingFood and its infrastructure
abstract: In this paper, we provide general information on the ReadingFood project, discussing its architecture and infrastructure choice(s). After presenting the CorpusEye environment, we give some “appetizers” of the diverse studies that can be done with this system. First, we present a taxonomy developed to cover food and drink in the three languages, and we explain the need to disambiguate for a fine-grained classification in this domain. title: A Journey Through ICPIG History: From Its Origins to the 36th Edition
abstract: The International Conference on Phenomena in Ionized Gases (ICPIG) is one of the longestrunning and most influential international conferences in plasma physics. Founded in Oxford in 1953 by Hans von Engel and Gordon Francis, ICPIG has played a central role in fostering scientific exchange and collaboration within the plasma community for more than seventy years. title: Generalizing the Peramorphosis Test to Detect Heterochronic Changes in an Explicit Phylogenetic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterochrony, defined as evolutionary changes in developmental timing, is a key mechanism underlying morphological diversification across taxa. Although several quantitative approaches have been developed to detect heterochronic patterns using geometric morphometric data, most are limited to pairwise comparisons among extant species and do not explicitly incorporate phylogenetic structure. title: Tightening the loose equilibrium concept: New seasonal insights with benthic insect data from National Ecological Observatory Network streams
abstract: The loose equilibrium (LE) hypothesis predicts that biotic assemblages will exhibit modest change from year-to-year but will not follow directed trajectories away from a stable baseline over longer periods of time. Using 8 years (2016–2023) of data from 21 National Ecological Observatory Network streams, we test the LE hypothesis for benthic insect assemblages. title: Neighbor Noise Problem in Multifamily Housing: An Integrative Framework for Resolution
abstract: Multifamily housing is common in urban areas, and neighbor noise is a frequent problem. In this study, a governance-based approach was designed for managing and preventing noise problems, marking an advance from conventional noise-reduction technologies. Using qualitative methods, including interviews with residents and professionals, the proposed framework categorizes five key sectors: individual, community, society, industry, and public. title: Precision Bioremediation of Chlorinated Ethenes in Heterogeneous Aquifers through Substrate Hydrological Coupling and High-Resolution Molecular Tracking
abstract: Abstract Applications of bioaugmentation in chlorinated solvent remediation are often hindered by unpredictable field performance and the inability to verify the colonization of inoculated strains in heterogeneous aquifers. This paper presents a field-validated engineering framework that addresses these limitations by integrating stress-tolerant strain selection, substrate hydrological coupling, and high-resolution molecular tracking. abstract: Nos proponemos indagar en las movilidades que realizan estudiantes de educación secundaria agraria, en una institución del partido de Magdalena (provincia de Buenos Aires, Argentina). title: Distribution of TENORM-contaminated soils in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia
abstract: Radioactive contamination in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia, a major tin- and rare earth-producing region, has rarely been studied, although material stored near mineral-processing workshops may pose a long-term health risk. We collected 46 soil samples around 9 mineral-processing workshops in the Selindung District, Pangkal Pinang City: residential soils from 20 locations at two depths (n = 40) and 6 workshop-related sediments. title: Promoting subjective well-being through pet leisure: motivation, participation, and place attachment in urban spaces
abstract: While pet ownership is increasingly recognized as a vital contributor to human well-being, the specific behavioral and psychological mechanisms linking pet-related activities to owner happiness remain underexplored. This study establishes an empirical framework to investigate how pet leisure shapes human subjective well-being (SWB) through the lens of leisure theory and environmental psychology. title: Escalating soil CO 2 degassing correlates with ground uplift and seismicity during the ongoing unrest of Campi Flegrei (2005–2025)
abstract: The mechanism driving accelerating unrest at the densely populated Campi Flegrei caldera since 2005 remains debated. Analyzing an unprecedented two-decade geochemical dataset, we show that escalating soil CO 2 fluxes closely tracks caldera uplift, revealing magmatic fluid pressurization at 3- to 4-kilometer depth and heating as the fundamental driver of the unrest. title: Fashioning the Maghrebi Woman Writer: The Reception of Elissa Rhaïs in Spanish Periodicals of the Interwar Period
abstract: This study explores the diverse representations of Elissa Rhaïs in the Spanish press and provides a comparative framework through which to understand her contributions to the literary field. Born to a Jewish family in Blida, Rhaïs made her first steps into the publishing world with the novel Saâda, La Marocaine (1919) and the short story Le café chantant (1920), which received significant attention during the interwar period. title: Isolation structural characterization and molecular docking analysis of bioactive phytoconstituents from Hiptage madablota Gaertn root as human pancreatic lipase inhibitors
abstract: This study explores the phytochemical profile and computationally predicted interaction potential with human pancreatic lipase of the ethanol extract of Hiptage madablota Gaertn., a plant of ethnopharmacological relevance. title: Economic Linkages and Multiplier Effects of Ethiopia’s Forest Sector and Wood Processing Industries: A Social Accounting Matrix -Based Analysis
abstract: The economic contributions and intersectoral linkages of Ethiopia’s forest sector and its downstream wood processing industries have historically been undervalued in national policy frameworks. Utilizing the 2010 Social Accounting Matrix (SAM) as a structural baseline framework, complemented by a mixed-methods approach including key informant interviews (KIIs), this study analyzes the structural dependencies and macroeconomic impacts of these interconnected sectors. title: Description of the symptoms of Biscogniauxia on cork oak and identification of a fungal complex
abstract: In this study, based on research conducted between 2023 and 2024 in the Mamora cork oak forest, various symptoms were observed and described in cork oak trees: defoliation and dieback of branch tips, abnormal discoloration of young shoots, twigs, and branches, alterations to the bark and wood, sap flow from branches and trunks, and bark peeling.The dieback was observed on old cork oak stumps and on young trees from reforestation projects.This study aimed to identify and study the fungal complex associated with the cankers visible on the trunks and branches of the cork oak.Samples taken from th

title: Cell plasticity in cancer and therapy resistance
abstract: Cancer cell plasticity, the ability of tumor cells to switch between distinct cellular states, has emerged as a key mechanism driving tumor progression, metastasis and therapy resistance. Cancer cells exploit diverse plasticity mechanisms, including dedifferentiation, transdifferentiation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition and stem cell-like reprogramming, to adapt to changes in their microenvironment or therapeutic pressures. title: Spatially heterogenous distributions of dipteran abundances identify priority areas for haemosporidian parasite surveillance
abstract: How changes in one facet of biodiversity affect others remains poorly understood. Changes in dipteran populations, for example, might impact the spread of haemosporidian parasites. Using biomonitoring data from 934 Lithuanian freshwater sites (2013 − 2022) and a hierarchical Bayesian GLM with spatial correlation, we examined ecological quality, elevation, land-use, and climate as drivers of the abundance of dipteran families containing pathogen vectors. title: Host‐mediated filtering and interspecific associations structure strongyle parasite communities in Sable Island horses
abstract: Mixed-species parasite infections are common in wildlife, yet the ecological processes that structure these communities remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that host-mediated and extrinsic environmental filtering, alongside biotic interactions, act concurrently to shape parasite community composition, and that these structuring patterns would depend on parasite traits or evolutionary history. title: Comparing mating systems and the strength of sexual selection across three congeneric species of pipefish spanning the continuum of sexual dimorphism
abstract: The strength of sexual selection is often linked to genetic mating system and is thought to be a driving force in the evolution of sexual dimorphism. Here, we compared selection between males and females across three closely related species: the dusky (Syngnathus floridae), Northern (S. fuscus), and Gulf (S. scovelli) pipefishes, using new and previously published datasets. title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans
abstract: The gut microbiome is crucial for health and is affected strongly by lifestyle1. Many microorganisms commonly found in non-industrialized populations are disappearing or have become extinct in industrialized populations2–6. Studying which microorganisms have been long-term residents of the human gut and may have co-evolved with humans2,7,8 could provide insights into how microbial biodiversity loss affects human health. title: State-matched redox nanomedicine for cell fate control and multicompartment therapeutic windows
abstract: Tumors persist under sustained redox stress by coupling increased reactive-species production to antioxidant buffering, metabolic plasticity and multicellular support. This creates therapeutic vulnerabilities whose tractability depends on the biological state of the exposed compartment. title: Distinct prosocial behaviors associated with persistent symptom trajectories in psychiatric disorders
abstract: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. Although social contexts strongly shape prosocial behavior in healthy individuals, its relevance across psychiatric disorders remains unclear. We examined whether context-dependent prosocial behaviors were associated with baseline psychiatric symptoms and longitudinal symptom trajectories. abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Environmental gradients structure plant communities at fine to coarse scales. Along elevational gradients, abiotic conditions influence community assembly by filtering species based on their functional strategies, which themselves may be phylogenetically structured. However, it remains challenging to identify which abiotic factors and functional traits are most relevant for gradient-wide assembly, particularly when potential drivers covary. title: Maternal edible THC consumption alters offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in rhesus macaques
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model. METHODS: Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. title: A Parallel One‐Field Fictitious‐Domain Finite Element Method for Large‐Scale Fluid–Structure Interaction
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a distributed‐memory finite‐element framework for large‐scale incompressible fluid–structure interaction (FSI) based on a monolithic one‐field fictitious‐domain formulation. The velocity and pressure are defined on a fixed Eulerian background mesh and discretized using Taylor–Hood finite elements with quadratic velocity and linear pressure approximation, while the immersed solid is represented by an updated Lagrangian mesh. title: Grapevine rhizosphere microbial activity and nitrogen nutrition vary with tree planting age in a temperate vitiforestry system
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Agroforestry, i.e., the planting of trees within agricultural systems, has been shown to enhance soil fertility, biodiversity, and the functioning of ecosystems. In temperate vineyards, vitiforestry represents a new type of agroforestry combining perennial grapevines and trees, either within or around vine rows. However, the effects of trees planted within vine rows on belowground microbial processes and grapevine growth remain underexplored. title: Influence of researcher presence towards nest attendance and breeding of barn owls Tyto javanica javanica
abstract: Human disturbance to nesting raptors can influence breeding success, especially during early breeding. This study examined the impact of researcher presence, a relatively low impact human disturbance, on eastern barn owls Tyto javanica javanica during monitoring of 57 nest‐boxes in oil palm plantations in Malaysia over a period of 30 months. We analysed the impact of number of researcher visits on breeding success of barn owls, and recorded the immediate response of barn owls to researcher presence, namely nest‐box return times. title: Tracing soil–water signatures from contrasting land uses in low-flow streamwater of a mixed headwater catchment
abstract: Baseflow sustains water delivery from headwater catchments during non-event conditions and low flows. However, in mixed land-use headwater catchments, how land-use-related soil–water storage signatures are represented in low-flow streamwater and vary seasonally remain poorly understood. To address this gap, a two-year study involving monthly monitoring of a hilly purple-soil headwater catchment was conducted. title: Variability of suspended sediment transport dynamics between seasons and flow pathways in a small agricultural catchment
abstract: Abstract Suspended sediment dynamics in small agricultural catchments are shaped by the interaction of overland and subsurface flow processes, yet no event-scale, flow pathway-specific comparisons of seasonal discharge (Q)–suspended sediment concentration (SSC) relationships within a single catchment exist. This study addresses this gap by analysing Q–SSC relationships during 18 overland flow events (2014–2016) using high temporal resolution (1-min) discharge and turbidity data combined with event-based SSC monitoring at three different flow pathways within the Hydrological Open Air Laboratory

title: Isolation and Structural Elucidation of Flavonoid Compounds from the Bark of Arcangelisia flava (Yellow Wood) from Kalimantan and Their Cytotoxicity Test Against MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells
abstract: Arcangelisia flava (L.) Merr., locally known as “akar kuning,” is a traditional medicinal plant from Kalimantan with limited evidence regarding its anticancer compounds. This study aimed to isolate bioactive compounds from A. flava bark and evaluate their cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Dried bark was macerated in 95% ethanol, fractionated with n-hexane, ethyl acetate, and n-butanol, and the ethyl acetate fraction was further purified by chromatography. journal: Fundamental and Applied Research in Medicine and Allied Sciences Indonesia

title: Evaluación de tratamientos pregerminativos en semillas de Malpighia glabra L
abstract: Background. Malpighia glabra is a native fruit species, with great nutritional and economic potential to which several biological activities are attributed. However, it presents serious problems related to its germination. Objective. To evaluate the physiological response of M. glabra seeds and seedlings subjected to four pregermination treatments. Methodology. The pregerminative treatments used were: 1) control (water), 2) immersion in water at 60°C for 5 min, 3) immersion in water for 48 h, 4) immersion in gibberellic acid (AG3) for 48 h. title: Common genetic control for grain filling duration and kernel weight in grain sorghum
abstract: KEY MESSAGE: The genetic control of GFD in sorghum closely overlaps with that of grain size, is influenced by both pre- and post-anthesis processes, offering new opportunities for yield improvement through targeted breeding and inter-racial trait introgression. The duration of the grain filling period has been associated with yield increases in cereals including maize and sorghum. The genetic control of grain filling duration (GFD) is however not known in sorghum. title: Global stability of leaning-type steel box arch bridges: mechanistic insights and quantitative evaluation of key design parameters
abstract: Leaning-type arch bridges are attractive for wide-deck urban applications, but their elastic global buckling mechanisms and parameter sensitivities remain insufficiently quantified. This study investigates a leaning-type steel box arch bridge using a three-dimensional finite element model validated against field-measured arch deflections and hanger forces. title: Yellow in Color Naming and Matching: Lexical Concentration and Local Convergence in Delayed Matching
abstract: ABSTRACT Yellow is an established color category despite being generated by a mixture of primaries on RGB displays. We examined its lexical accessibility, representative‐color selections, and matching accuracy using two complementary tasks. A web‐based survey asked participants to list 10 color terms and select their best representatives from a 64‐field RGB grid. Analyses included English, German, Latvian, and Slovenian samples, comprising 396 participants. title: Research progress on ATP-citrate lyase and its inhibitors: a metabolic-epigenetic perspective
abstract: ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) is a key enzyme in cellular metabolism that catalyses the cleavage of citrate to produce acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA), thereby bridging energy metabolism and epigenetic regulation. Acetyl-CoA serves as a common substrate for de novo lipogenesis (DNL) and histone acetylation. Aberrant ACLY activity is closely associated with various pathological conditions, including metabolic diseases, Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), cancer, and neurodegenerative diseases, positioning ACLY as an important therapeutic target for these diseases. journal: Journal of Enzyme Inhibition and Medicinal Chemistry

title: Trait-mediated cascades link enhanced ultraviolet radiation to pollination and reproductive success in Lysimachia arvensis and Lysimachia loeflingii
abstract: Environmental change can reorganize plant function across biological levels, yet experiments linking physiological acclimation, development, ecological interactions and reproduction remain scarce. I tested whether enhanced ultraviolet (UV) radiation generates coordinated responses across these levels using plants from 24 species-specific populations (12 per species) of two closely related species, Lysimachia arvensis and L. loeflingii , sampled at 19 localities. title: Dual‐Comb Spectroscopy With Fully Controlled Repetition Rate and Offset Frequency of Quantum Cascade Laser Frequency Combs
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum cascade laser frequency combs (QCL‐FCs) are promising light sources for sensing applications, thanks to their convenient electrical pumping, chip‐scale footprint, high optical power, and relatively broadband emission in the mid‐infrared molecular fingerprint spectral region. title: From Difficult Heritage to Difficult Temporality: The Political Life of History in Cities With Scarce Heritage
abstract: This article examines the challenges in self-narration faced by cities with short, sparse, and monotonous histories. Moving beyond the concept of “difficult heritage,” which focuses on problematic historical content (e.g., legacies of forced labor), the authors introduce “difficult temporality” to describe a structural scarcity of historical events. Through case studies of five Russian cities (Kovrov, Chernogorsk, Inta, Dudinka, and Susuman), the article identifies core and supplementary strategies these communities use to construct a usable past. institutions: Ural Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

title: Nutritional, Bioactive Compounds, and Antioxidant Properties of Temanggung’s Robusta and Arabica Coffee By-products: A Comparative Chemometric Analysis
abstract: Coffee by-products, including coffee husk and coffee pulp, have attracted increasing interest as a source of nutrition and bioactive compounds.This study aimed to investigate the different nutritional composition and bioactive compounds of coffee by-products obtained from arabica and robusta coffee processed in Temanggung, Indonesia.Four samples were evaluated: CHA (dried coffee husk arabica), CHR (dried coffee husk robusta), CPA (dried coffee pulp arabica), and CPR (dried coffee pulp robusta).Macronutrients, minerals, Total Polyphenol Content (TPC), Total Flavonoid Content (TFC), and antioxid

title: Heat Unit Accumulation, Heat Use Efficiency, Yield, and Sweetness of Sweet Corn (Zea mays saccharata Sturt L.) under Tropical Lowland Conditions
abstract: Temperature is an important environmental factor influencing phenological development and productivity of sweet corn through heat unit accumulation. This study evaluated heat unit accumulation, heat use efficiency (HUE), yield components, and sweetness of seven commercial sweet corn cultivars grown under tropical lowland conditions during one growing season. The experiment was arranged in a randomized complete block design with seven cultivars and three replications. title: Unleashing the Potential of Autologous Platelet Concentrates in Bone Regeneration: A Focus on Their Synergy With Biomaterials
abstract: Bone defects present significant clinical challenges worldwide, as conventional treatments such as autografts and allografts are constrained by limited supply, immune risks and insufficient bioactivity. Derived from the patient's own venous blood via centrifugation, autologous platelet concentrates (APCs) offer an autologous, readily accessible source of growth factors and immune-related cues that can support osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and regenerative microenvironment remodeling. title: Thermostability and pH Differentiation in Geobacillus Hydrolases: A Comparative Perspective
abstract: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent source of industrially relevant enzymes, particularly hydrolases such as proteases, lipases, and carbohydrate-active enzymes. Although many individual enzymes have been characterized in detail, comparative synthesis across catalytic classes within the genus remains limited. title: An assessment of the sensory attributes and the consumer acceptance of new experimental and commercial spekboom products
abstract: Spekboom (Portulacaria afra), a succulent viewed as both environmentally and socioeconomically acceptable, remains underutilized. This study investigated the culinary potential and consumer acceptability of spekboom across diverse flavour profiles and textures. A sensory assessment was done using Just-About-Right analysis and overall liking of new experimental (relish, pickle, lemon curd, and salad sprinkle) and commercial (preserve, chutney, pickle, and chicken spice) spekboom products, followed by a consumer survey to evaluate drivers of adoption and willingness to try spekboom-based product

title: Geoevents as a New Category of Geotourism: A Conceptual Framework and Theoretical Foundations
abstract: Planned events are increasingly recognized as important components of tourism development and destination promotion, whereas geotourism research has primarily focused on geoheritage, geodiversity, geoeducation, and geotourism products. The article conceptualizes geoevents as a new category of events that directly utilize geographical space, geodiversity, and geoheritage as their fundamental thematic and organizational components. title: A multi-domain mixture approach integrating urinary phenolic endocrine disruptors, blood metals, and ambient air pollutants in relation to neurodevelopmental trajectories from birth to 36 months
abstract: Non-persistent phenolic endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), bisphenols, parabens and triclosan, blood metals and ambient air pollutants are each linked to adverse neurodevelopment, but they are rarely analyzed together. In the Korean Children's Environmental Health Study, neurodevelopment was assessed by Denver II at 6 months and Bayley-III at 12, 24 and 36 months. title: Gendered landscapes of loss: climate change, disaster, and women's resilience in rural India
abstract: This article examines the gendered dimensions of climate-induced disasters in rural India through a systematic archival analysis of five community testimonies published by the People's Archive of Rural India (PARI). Drawing on stories from Odisha, Maharashtra, Assam, and Kerala, the study analyses how climate change manifesting as erratic monsoons, intensifying floods, accelerating riverbank erosion, and catastrophic landslides disproportionately impacts women in agrarian and indigenous communities. title: Angles of trust in transboundary water cooperation: Capturing the multidimensional and dynamic nature of trust in the Sava and Syrdarya river basins
abstract: Trust is frequently invoked to explain cooperation or conflict in interstate relations over shared water resources. Drawing on qualitative research in the Sava River Basin in Southeastern Europe and the Syrdarya River Basin in Central Asia, this article suggests three key dimensions through which trust can be better understood – its sources, levels, and intensities. title: Multi-scale connectivity and distribution: vulnerability in global food trade networks via static-dynamic integration
abstract: Abstract The global food trade network (FTN) is one of the key mechanisms for safeguarding national food supplies, and identifying its vulnerability is of considerable importance for maintaining global food security. This study develops a vulnerability assessment framework for the FTN that provides systematic analysis at the overall, cluster, and individual levels, integrating static and dynamic assessments within a unified analytical framework. title: Programming Host–Guest Interactions in Covalent Organic Frameworks with Arylazopyrazole Photoswitches
abstract: Abstract Programming host–guest interactions in porous crystalline materials using external stimuli offers a promising strategy for adaptive molecular separations but remains challenging because adsorption is often governed by pore structure rather than tunable molecular interactions. Here, we report a series of photoresponsive covalent organic frameworks (LACOF-1) incorporating arylazopyrazole (AAP) photoswitches that enable light-controlled modulation of CO2 adsorption through molecular photoisomerization. title: Environmentally friendly polymer-modified K+-rich waste bentonite composites for achieving colloidal and thermal stability in water-based drilling fluids
abstract: Bentonite is widely used in industrial applications due to its ability to swell and form colloidal dispersions in water. However, certain bentonites exhibit poor colloidal behavior due to unfavorable chemical or mineralogical characteristics. This study examines a waste bentonite from Cyprus exhibiting such limitations. Even though thermal alkali activation with Na 2 CO 3 was performed to bring the sample into compliance with API specifications, the colloidal performance remained unsatisfactory. title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin.

title: Isolation, Characterization, and Phytotoxic Activity of Streptomyces spp. from Diseased Potato Scab Tubers
abstract: Abstract Biological herbicides serve as highly efficient and eco-friendly weed control agents, which typically consist of natural secondary metabolites, such as phytotoxic metabolites produced by Streptomyces sp. However, the isolation of phytotoxic compounds from pathogenic Streptomyces strains has been insufficiently investigated. Here, a total of 50 strains of the Streptomyces genus were isolated from the potato tubers with typical common scab (CS) symptoms using the culture-dependent method. title: Desafíos y oportunidades en los procesos de construcción y gestión de datos: Aportes para una estrategia sanitaria en la provincia de Buenos Aires (2024-2025)
abstract: Los instrumentos estructurados de registro son centrales para la gestión sanitaria, pero su diseño y las condiciones organizacionales que lo rodean inciden fuertemente en la calidad de los datos producidos. Este artículo presenta una investigación cualitativa documental, de diseño flexible, sobre los procesos de construcción y reporte de datos cuantitativos en salud, realizada en tres municipios del conurbano bonaerense y dos direcciones del Ministerio de Salud de la provincia de Buenos Aires (julio 2024-marzo 2025). abstract: The consequential measurement of conveyor infrastructure is the associated roads that provides linkages to neighboring cities and municipalities. A good road transport at the city level is crucial in the movement of constituents and conveyor of goods with low of occurrence costs. Good city road infrastructure is associated not only with the economic growth but also contributory with poverty reduction as stated by various studies. title: Pyroelectrically driven cold-hot energy harvesting for green hydrogen production of Ag-decorated Ba0.7Sr0.3TiO3 nanofibers
abstract: Temperature fluctuations, ubiquitous in daily life, remain underexplored for hydrogen production. Here, we demonstrate hydrogen evolution by harvesting energy from cold–hot alternations between 293 and 323 K (20-50 °C) using pyroelectric Ba 0.7 Sr 0.3 TiO 3 nanofibers (BST NFs) and Ag-decorated BST nanofibers (BST/Ag NFs). title: How past natural disturbances and human land use dynamics shape the current structure and composition of moist Afromontane forests
abstract: Historical knowledge of the landscape is essential to understand the current ecosystem. We studied how common natural disturbances and land use changes are, and how these histories affect current forest structure and tree species composition. We used data from 44 key informant interviews and inventories from 125 forest sites. Regarding natural disturbances, we found that they are rather infrequent, even if there are reports from many places of occasional wildfires, storms causing windfalls, landslides and various dieback of trees. title: A Journey through Solvent Space: New Solvates of Probucol
abstract: Abstract A systematic expansion of the solid-form landscape of the antihyperlipidemic drug probucol was carried out using a diverse set of solvents spanning a broad physicochemical space, providing insight into the formation of probucol solvated forms. Five new solvates were discovered (with cyclohexane, carbon tetrachloride, tetrahydrofuran, 1,4-dioxan and dimethylsulfoxide), and comprehensively characterized, including their crystal structures, infrared spectra, thermal behaviour and solid-state stability. title: Evaluation of Herbicide Alternatives to Glyphosate for Weed Control in Fallow Fields
abstract: Efficient weed control in fallow fields prior to maize planting faces critical challenges due to herbicide resistance and the need to reduce reliance on glyphosate. This study evaluated non-selective and selective herbicide strategies in an on-farm strip-plot validation trial (6 ha) with nested subsampling (n = 6 quadrats per treatment plot). Nine treatments were evaluated, including synthetic herbicides (glyphosate, 2,4-D, paraquat, glufosinate-ammonium, and saflufenacil + clethodim) and commercial bioherbicide (BH02). title: Confucian ethics and the narrative construction of sustainability and food safety: a case study of ‘ A Bite of China ’
abstract: As public concern about food crises has risen, China faces the challenge of rebuilding confidence in its domestic food supply chains. In response, state media has intentionally utilised culturally rich, visually appealing storylines to reframe food governance through traditional ethical ideals and ecological sustainability. This study examines how Confucian ethics are incorporated into the Chinese food documentary ‘A Bite of China’ and how the series constructs narratives of food safety and sustainability. title: MEDIATING EFFECTS OF MEMORABLE TOURISM EXPERIENCES ON TOUR GUIDES’ ATTRIBUTES EFFECTS ON ENHANCING REVISIT INTENTION
abstract: Tour guide attributes’ roles have emerged as a crucial element affecting tourists’ memorable experiences and intention to revisit destinations along Thailand Andaman Coast, especially within the foreign tourist context. However, few studies have investigated the influences of specific tour guide attributes individually. Based on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) model, this study examined the influences of tour guide attributes (TGA) on memorable tourism experience (MTE) and revisit intention (RVI) among foreign tourists along Thailand's Andaman Coast. title: Teachers who stay: the role of professional identity in teacher retention
abstract: Drawing on interviews with mid- and later-career teachers from primary and secondary schools in one region of England, this small-scale study examined why participants had chosen to stay. They described how their moral purpose and agency helped them manage multiple challenges over time, and how these had contributed to their sense of professional identity and decisions to stay. title: When Geography Dilutes Accountability: Managerial Discretion and Fiscal Expansion in Local Government
abstract: Democratic accountability assumes that the citizens who bear the costs of government decisions can sanction the officials who make them. We identify a structural break in this assumption. When a city funds itself through taxes that fall partly on nonresidents (highway travelers, commuters, and regional shoppers who cannot vote in local elections) the electoral link between bearing costs and imposing sanctions weakens. title: Multi-factor assessment of future climate hazards to apple production across Switzerland’s growing regions
abstract: Abstract Apple production is likely to face increased climate hazards in the future resulting from climate change. The magnitude and relative importance of different climate hazards remain unclear, especially when considering multiple emissions scenarios. Here, we perform a multi-factor climate hazard assessment for apple-growing regions in Switzerland that considers summer heat, summer drought, spring frost, and insufficient winter chill as sources of climate hazard. title: A reliability-guided RGB-IR object detection network with complementary information decoupling for autonomous driving
abstract: Abstract Autonomous driving systems require robust object detection under complex open-road conditions, where RGB images are sensitive to illumination changes and background interference, while infrared images may suffer from weak textures and unreliable thermal responses. To improve RGB-IR detection performance, this paper proposes a Feature-level Scale-aware Multispectral Fusion Network, termed FSMF, for autonomous driving scenarios. title: Design hybrid renewable energy systems for electric vehicle charging stations at various sites in Pakistan
abstract: The number of EVs is increasing rapidly globally, and that means the need for more sustainable and economical charging. A continuous supply of clean energy is required for the Highway EV charging stations that are crucial for intercity mobility functions. One of the possible solutions is a hybrid renewable energy system technology, which has wind and solar photovoltaic (PV) energy. title: Molecular, agro-morphological, and phytochemical analysis of goldenrod (Solidago spp.) genotypes grown under two contrasting climates
abstract: Solidago , belonging to the Asteraceae family, is used as an herbal medicine and possess diuretic, anti-microbial, cytotoxic, anti-inflammatory, gastroprotective and immunobiological properties. However, the extent to which genetic differences among wild and cultivated Solidago materials contribute to variation in agronomic performance and phytochemical quality under contrasting environmental conditions remains insufficiently understood. title: What are pulsar companions made of? Using gravitational tides to probe their compositions
abstract: Low eccentricity, short orbital period pulsar companions may provide a probe to study novel dense and stable exoplanet internal compositions due to the potentially significant orbital evolution they experience caused by strong gravitational tides. We model the tidal characteristics such as apsidal motion constants, orbital precession, and tidal deformability for a variety of equations of state to be compared with values recovered via pulsar timing for a sample of four systems: PSR J1719-1438b, PSR J0636+5128b, PSR J2322+2650b, and PSR J1807-2459A b. title: Radiocarbon dating of wooden beams at Herodium palace-fortress: Modeling tree-felling events and their implications on site chronology
abstract: The site of Herodium is best known for its impressive, well-preserved palace fortress, built by Herod the Great, towards the end of the 1st century BC. The site's conical shape, artificially created to transform it into Herod's monumental burial complex, is clearly seen from afar. The impressive preservation of wooden beams and posts at the site has allowed for a rigorous radiocarbon study of the beams' felling dates and their potential implications for the timing of construction activities at the site. title: Co-founder selection from a marriage market perspective: How the dark triad shapes judgments of interpersonal attraction, resources, and equity demand
abstract: Co-founder selection is a pivotal decision in new venture formation, yet how lead founders evaluate potential partners remains underexplored. Drawing on insights from marriage market theory, we conceptualize co-founder selection as an act of individuated judgment guided by cooperative logic and associated joint utility projection, wherein lead founders assess co-founder candidates based on social-emotional, instrumental, and distributive considerations reflected in interpersonal attraction, resource contributions, and equity demand. title: Phenolic Profiles of Nelumbo nucifera from Manipur Against Neurodegenerative Inflammation

title: Absorption and toxicity of mineral oil after dermal and mucosal surface exposure: a review
abstract: Dermal and mucosal surface exposure to mineral oils occurs in the occupational setting. To evaluate exposure levels at which toxicity occurs, we collected data on non-cancer toxicity of crude oil, refinery streams and refined mineral oils. This included extraction of no-observed-adverse-effect levels (NOAELs) and lowest-observed-adverse-effect levels (LOAELs). title: Psychotropic drugs in drinking water? A scoping review of evidence on diazepam and fluoxetine
abstract: The global prevalence of mental disorders has increased considerably in recent decades. This evidence, associated with population growth and the expansion of access to medications, favors the growing global consumption of psychotropic drugs. Consequently, an increasing load of these substances is introduced into the environment, especially into water bodies, characterizing them as emerging contaminants. abstract: Pyrolysis offers a promising route for valorization of waste tires. However, waste tire pyrolysis oil (WTPO) contains high concentrations of heteroatoms, limiting its direct use as a fuel. In this study, the transformation of WTPO fractions and representative compound groups during hydrotreating was investigated under a range of operating conditions. Temperature was identified as a key factor controlling the balance between hydrogenation and thermal cracking. abstract: Social Key Performance Indicators (SKPIs) and the competitiveness they can bring is studied and applied to a case in the energy sector (district heating). A case study has limited generalizability, but we argue that the case serves as a critical case, informing other companies on actions to take for increasing their competitive advantage by social value inclusion. abstract: Rising maize prices and increasing competition caused by rising human food demand are forcing poultry producers to seek alternative energy sources. Newly released grain sorghum varieties in western Ethiopia may serve as a viable substitute, but their effects on laying hen performance and profitability need assessment. title: Effects of organic and conventional management on morphophysiological parameters and antioxidant profile of tomato fruits (Solanum lycopersicum L.), ‘Big Río’ variety
abstract: Mexico is one of the main tomato-producing countries and relies heavily on synthetic chemical fertilizers, whose negative effects within and beyond production systems have already been described. In this context, organic agriculture offers an alternative to reduce chemical fertilizer use. The objective of the present study was to evaluate two management systems, organic and conventional, in terms of plant morphophysiological parameters, yield, and the antioxidant profile of fruits of the ‘Big Río’ variety of Solanum lycopersicum L. title: Constraining Fault Kinematics and India‐Tarim Convergence Partitioning in Southwestern Tibet With Geodetic Block Modeling
abstract: Abstract How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. In this study, we derive high‐resolution velocity fields for the southwestern Tibetan Plateau using both GNSS and InSAR observations. title: Review of educational interventions for patients requiring palliative care: A scoping review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life of individuals with serious, progressive illnesses. Therapeutic patient education is a key approach for enhancing patient autonomy and empowerment. However, structured educational interventions for patients receiving palliative care remain poorly documented in the literature, in contrast to the growing body of evidence regarding education for caregivers and healthcare professionals. abstract: This article investigates the motivational grammars of villains in Hollywood superhero films through the lens of Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Human Values. By analyzing the discourse of eight iconic antagonists, we identified three clusters: Ambiguous Tragedians, whose villainy emerges from wounded subjectivity and marginalization; Revolutionary Calculators, who justify domination through distorted appeals to justice and order; and the Chaotic Nihilist, represented solely by Heath Ledger’s Joker, who embodies systemic collapse and anarchic spectacle. title: Burned habitats facilitate predation and lead to long‐term reductions in prey success
abstract: Intensifying wildfire regimes under global change are expected to shift species interactions through changes in habitat structure and composition, vegetation productivity, and sensory cues. Yet there is little evidence of how burn-induced changes in habitat composition and structure modify predator-prey relationships. We investigated how wildfires influence relationships between mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and cougars (Puma concolor) in the US Intermountain West using high-resolution telemetry data, kill site locations, and annual measures of mule deer fawn production. title: Venom composition of the Iberian adder (Vipera seoanei) from northern Portugal reveals limited sex and size variation
abstract: Snake venom is a complex and dynamic ecological trait, with high potential for intraspecific variation. In this study, the venom composition of the Iberian adder ( Vipera seoanei ) from the Peneda Mountains of northern Portugal was investigated to explore whether venom varies with body size and sex. Venom proteomes from six individuals representing juvenile, subadult, and adult males and females were characterised using LC–MS/MS, while individual variation was assessed from SDS–PAGE profiles of 18 snakes. abstract: This study is devoted to investigating soliton solutions and qualitative analysis of the M-fractional extended nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation with cubicquadratic nonlinear terms. This research is motivated by the significance of the extended NLS model in optics, quantum mechanics, plasma physics, electromagnetic wave propagation, and the approximate description of dense quasione- dimensional Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs) involving repulsive contact interactions and long-range dipole-dipole attraction. title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. title: Electrons Hopping Across a Molecular Network: Spectra and Symmetries
abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed for rings with L=3,4,5, and 6 nodes, filled with one, two or three electrons. title: Geopolitical risk and accounting conservatism: does financial reporting opacity matter? Evidence from an emerging market
abstract: As global markets increasingly navigate extreme external shocks, understanding how macroeconomic turbulence reshapes corporate financial reporting strategies remains a critical challenge for stakeholders. This study investigates the empirical relationship between macro-level geopolitical risk (GPR) and accounting conservatism (AC), while examining the moderating role of financial reporting opacity (FRO) in an emerging market setting. title: Naringenin Delays Aging in Drosophila through FoxO-Mediated Autophagy and Intestinal Homeostasis Preservation
abstract: Abstract Naringenin (NAE), a natural flavonoid with established geroprotective properties, has unclear mechanisms in intestinal aging. abstract: Freshwater fish have evolved to forage in a range of habitats, from open water in lakes to benthic shorelines and streams. Much research has focused on how prey differences, such as zooplankton versus benthic macroinvertebrates, might select for divergence in predator traits across this habitat gradient. abstract: Extreme meteorological events, such as typhoons, constitute severe external shocks that significantly impact macroeconomic operations and fundamental corporate activities. Grounded in stakeholder theory, this study employs a two way fixed effects difference in differences model alongside the VaR-BEKK-MVGARCH-DUMMY-T framework. abstract: ABSTRACT Natural‐fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites often suffer from limited mechanical performance and poor moisture resistance due to weak interfacial adhesion between hydrophilic fibers and the hydrophobic epoxy matrix. abstract: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) has achieved clinical success in liver-directed therapies, but its translation to solid tumors remains limited by heterogeneous delivery and context-dependent target dependence. This review compares non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, glioblastoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma across four interconnected dimensions: resistance networks, tumor microenvironmental reprogramming, metastatic progression, and delivery-system design. title: Is the Object Obsolescent? On Reuse Beyond Simondon
abstract: The article critically examines the status of the obsolescence of technical objects within the context of contemporary consumer society, taking Gilbert Simondon’s philosophy of technology as its central theoretical framework. The author argues that obsolescence is not primarily a technical phenomenon, but rather a social, symbolic, and economic one, produced by market dynamics, advertising, and the logic of permanent innovation, which detach the object from its structural durability. title: Design Approaches for Oxygen Reduction Systems for Warehouse Storage Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen reduction systems (ORS) are protection systems, with a design protection objective to limit fire spread beyond the point of ignition. Research has shown that the prescriptive design methods, in VdS 3527, EN 16750, and ISO 20338, are not appropriate as prescriptive design methods as they result in insufficient protection levels. title: Assessing the genetic diversity in potato genotypes to enhance yield and quality in temperate region of Kashmir valley
abstract: Potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) is a food crop of a global significance, and the production of high yielding cultivars that matches a specific agro-climate, is important to achieve food security. This study explored the genetic variability, association of traits and phylogenetic variation available in 53 genotypes of potato, which were grown in temperate environment of Kashmir valley in India. title: Biotechnological upgrading of palm kernel meal for poultry nutrition: Challenges and opportunities
abstract: In recent years, fluctuations in the cost of traditional feed ingredients for poultry farming have compelled producers to explore alternative raw materials to reduce costs. Palm kernel meal (PKM), a by-product of the palm oil extraction industry, is one such alternative. title: The future of urban construction: aligning urban transport, and energy planning for sustainable cities
abstract: Electrifying construction logistics is essential to sustainable cities; however, current planning practices seldom integrate construction transport, temporary sites, and charging infrastructure into urban and energy planning. This study adopts a systems perspective to investigate how construction logistics can transition toward zero-emission operations. title: How much would egg and duckling predation need to be reduced to reverse declines of ground-nesting waterfowl in Finland? A demographic scenario analysis
abstract: Abstract Populations of water- and wetland-associated birds have declined globally due to multiple pressures, including habitat loss, climate change, and predation. Ground-nesting waterfowl are particularly vulnerable to predators, and the spread of invasive mammalian predators like raccoon dogs ( Nyctereutes procyonoides ) has intensified this threat in parts of Northern Europe. abstract: Abstract Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, yet their biodiversity remains understudied compared to humid tropical forests. We integrated functional trait ecology with environmental vulnerability assessments to evaluate multi‑causal disturbances affecting amphibians and reptiles in Oaxaca, Mexico, a hotspot of endemism and biodiversity loss. abstract: Abstract The performance of a single cross is determined by the additive effects of the parents and their interactions, which can be estimated through general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA). abstract: Labor scarcity has accelerated interest in robotic transplanting, whose reliability depends on seedling geometry and root plug cohesion. This study optimized pro-tray configuration, substrate composition, and seedling age for chili and brinjal plug seedlings. abstract: Abstract Understanding how ecological communities respond to environmental change over long timescales is essential for predicting modern ecosystem dynamics. Here, we reconstructed functional community composition and trophic network structure of seven mammal communities from the eastern region of Oregon. abstract: Abstract Vehicular emissions are an important source of urban air pollution that can age through atmospheric processes, but how their health effects change during atmospheric aging remains poorly understood. abstract: The continuous use of a narrow genetic base in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) breeding programmes has constrained the development of high-yielding cultivars with superior fruit quality and broader adaptability. abstract: Innovation has become a critical capability for local governments seeking to improve service delivery, organizational effectiveness, and responsiveness to community needs. However, empirical research on local government innovation remains fragmented, with limited attention to multidimensional measurement frameworks, particularly in decentralized governance contexts. abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. abstract: Abstract Amphibian declines driven by the fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) pose major challenges for conservation, particularly for cold-adapted species occupying habitats where temperatures may be less limiting to Bd growth. title: Travel time budgets and the potential to replace travel by car in urban regions: A case study from Finland
abstract: A shift towards sustainable modes of transport (walking, cycling, and public transport) is urgently needed to reduce the negative externalities of private car use. Whereas active travel is a feasible alternative for relatively short distances, public transport can substitute for a larger share of car use. City regions are often seen as the main targets for this mode shift given the availability of public transport options and the proximity of services. abstract: Abstract Soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] is a versatile leguminous crop that plays a vital role in biodiesel production, livestock feed, and enhancing global food security. Soybean production and productivity in Ethiopia are low compared to the national potential, mainly due to the lack of high‐yielding genotypes. Substantial genetic variability is essential for developing high‐yielding, climate‐resilient soybean varieties. abstract: Abstract Amber is one of the most important national treasures in Lithuania, as well as in some other Baltic countries. In the recent era, some other materials that resemble amber have been introduced in the market, which are sometimes sold as real amber. This is considered as fraud and will, in turn, destroy the whole Amber trade. abstract: To address the inefficient gas extraction problem of high‑gas low‑permeability coal seams in Guizhou Province, this study investigates the permeability‑enhancing mechanism and field performance of liquid CO₂ phase‑change fracturing, taking local anthracite and bituminous coal as research objects. title: Tuning e-fuel product distribution by combining a Na-promoted Fe-based catalyst with BETA zeolites in CO2-modified Fischer-Tropsch synthesis
abstract: The integration of acidic zeolites with Fe-based catalysts provides a promising strategy to overcome the broad hydrocarbon distribution of CO 2 -modified Fischer-Tropsch synthesis (FTS) through in situ product upgrading. title: Beyond the outlet: How lateral seepage shapes controlled drainage performance in a sandy soil
abstract: Controlled drainage (CD) is used in temperate humid regions to reduce water and nutrient losses. Although CD effectiveness has been widely evaluated, the role of lateral seepage in sandy soils remains underexplored and neglecting it may overestimate reductions in water and nutrient losses. The objective was to evaluate CD performance in a sandy loam field prone to lateral seepage and quantify how lateral seepage alters estimates of water and nitrate losses from the field. title: Lighting the way: Radiation use efficiency and phenotypic variation of candlenut (Aleurites moluccanus), a tropical oilseed tree
abstract: The candlenut tree ( Aleurites moluccanus (L.) Willd) is gaining interest as a potential feedstock for bioenergy development, with particular attention to its oil, which constitutes ∼60 % of its seed endosperm. Despite its many uses and history of human relationships, its productivity and role in ecosystem function remain uncertain. title: Recent trends in (commercial) power-to-methanol technology
abstract: Methanol based on CO 2 and H 2 produced from renewable energy is anticipated to be an important building block in a sustainable economy. While the synthesis of e-methanol looks similar to conventional methanol synthesis at a first view, important boundary conditions are different along the scale from catalyst to process level. title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
abstract: Community question-answering (cQA) platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer “best” or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. abstract: Climate justice scholarship has converged on a trivalent model of distributive, procedural and recognition justice, yet this model remains largely anthropocentric, vulnerable to technocratic and market-based capture, and silent on both the epistemic marginalisation of Indigenous and Global South knowledge and the structural drivers of the crisis. title: On the price elasticity of residential electric vehicle charging in Denmark
abstract: As power systems increasingly rely on renewable energy generation and accommodate flexible loads, understanding short-term demand flexibility becomes essential. Denmark provides a particularly relevant setting with a high share of variable renewable generation and widespread electric vehicle (EV) adoption. abstract: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with ascending infection and inflammation at the fetal-maternal interface recognized as major contributors to its pathophysiology. Gardnerella spp., key species associated with bacterial vaginosis, have been implicated in adverse pregnancy outcomes; however, the mechanisms underlying their ability to ascend and trigger inflammatory responses remain poorly understood. abstract: The root meristem is essential for stem cell maintenance and root development in plants. title: How safe from Listeria monocytogenes are frozen ready-to-eat fish products, either cooked or smoked, when stored under refrigeration after purchasing?
abstract: This research aimed to access the incidence of Listeria sp. and L. monocytogenes in frozen ready-to-eat (RTE) fish products immediately after purchasing, and after refrigerated storage. Out of 72 kani-kama samples, 17 (23,6%) and 16 out of 48 samples (33,3%) of smoked salmon samples, tested positive for Listeria sp. by the traditional culture method, whereas 45,8% and 56.2% were positive by PCR, for kani-kama and smoked salmon samples, respectively. title: Vermicompost-assisted Azotobacter and Bacillus inoculation enables partial substitution of mineral NPK and improves maize yield, nutrient uptake, soil fertility, and biological activity
abstract: Reducing dependence on mineral fertilizers requires integrated nutrient management (INM) strategies that sustain maize productivity while improving soil functioning. A field experiment evaluated nine combinations of mineral NPK, farmyard manure, vermicompost, and Azotobacter - Bacillus inoculation in a randomized block design with three replications. The 75% NPK treatments integrated with either FYM or vermicompost and inoculation formed the leading treatment group. title: Leukemia: Root Causes and Resolutions
abstract: Background: Leukemia affects individuals across all age groups and accounts for over 600,000 incident cases and more than 300,000 deaths worldwide annually. Despite advances in chemotherapy, targeted therapies, immunotherapy, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, it remains a major clinical challenge due to disease heterogeneity, treatment-related toxicity, relapse, and therapeutic resistance. title: Improving the efficiency of helitack crew deployment through spatial optimization
abstract: Background Improving the deployment of helitack crews is crucial for limiting the growth of newly ignited wildfires. Aims We evaluated whether an optimization model could improve deployment in areas where high-intensity fires could occur compared with the current heuristic approach. Methods The model maximized coverage of areas with high potential intensity values using a fixed number of deployment sites. title: The schism of strategic planning in the climate crisis
abstract: Strategic planning is traditionally defined as a broader, more flexible process compared to statutory spatial planning. It most often involves investments and partnerships in urban development projects, increasing carbon emissions as a result. This creates a schism between the stated sustainable development objectives and the actual consequences of strategic planning. This study first tracked this schism in academic discourse across three different approaches to strategic planning. abstract: Multifunctional and environmentally friendly hydrogel materials were developed through the reaction of chemically crosslinking biocompatible polymers and natural crosslinkers present in grape pomace, a waste product left over during the wine making process. This interesting approach to designing hydrogels, especially considering that many synthetic crosslinking agents, such as N, N’-methylenebisacrylamide, epichlorohydrin, and glutaraldehyde, all of which are harmful and toxic. title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. title: From molecular advances to limited clinical impact: The persistent gap in chromoblastomycosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chromoblastomycosis (CBM) is a chronic implantation mycosis of considerable morbidity, first described more than a century ago, predominantly affecting rural populations in tropical and subtropical regions. Although historically associated with impoverished settings, an increasing number of cases have been reported in both endemic and non-endemic areas, including high-income countries, reflecting an underrecognized epidemiological landscape. title: Breeding of high-yield cold-adapted lipase fungi, optimization of fermentation conditions and isolation and purification of lipase
abstract: Abstract Cold-adapted lipases have attracted extensive research attention in enzymology owing to their unique low-temperature adaptability and catalytic properties, and investigations in this area continue to deepen. This study aimed to efficiently produce a cold-adapted lipase to overcome the limitations of conventional lipases under low-temperature conditions, such as low activity, high cost, and restricted applicability. title: Balanced phosphorus supply and foliar Zn-EDTA improve nutrient acquisition, physiological Zn function, and potential seed Zn bioavailability in blackgram grown on Zn-deficient soil
abstract: Phosphorus (P) - zinc (Zn) interactions regulate nutrient acquisition, physiological function, productivity, and seed nutritional quality. However, their integrated effects in blackgram remain insufficiently characterized. A single-season field experiment was conducted with blackgram cv. VBN 8 on a Zn-deficient Typic Haplustalf using a 4 × 3 factorial randomized block design (FRBD) with three replications. All plots received a uniform basal application of 25 kg ZnSO₄ ha⁻¹. title: Lightweight CNT Fabric Current Collectors Enabling Silicon Anodes in High-Capacity Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) require metallic current collectors such as copper for anodes and aluminum for cathodes, adding significant weight without contributing to the capacity. This is especially problematic for Si-dominant anodes, with mass loadings lower than 2 mg cm–2. Here, copper is replaced with lightweight, non-woven carbon nanotube fabrics (CNTfs) combined with high-capacity Si/PPAN active material to form a self-standing composite anode. title: A study of the greenhouse gas emissions inventory and driving factors decomposition in Tongzhou, China
abstract: Abstract District-and county-level greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories remain insufficiently developed, limiting the formulation of targeted mitigation policies at the grassroots governance scale. Taking Tongzhou District, Beijing, as a representative rapidly urbanizing megacity sub-center, this study developed an integrated district-level GHG emissions inventory covering energy activities, agricultural production, LUCF, and waste treatment from 2018 to 2020, and applied the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method to identify sector-specific driving mechanisms. title: Conservation agriculture optimizes soil nitrogen stabilization and availability to crops under rice-based cropping
abstract: Conservation agriculture (CA) is increasingly promoted in the Indo-Gangetic Plains to address sustainability challenges in soil-plant-environment system. Efficient nitrogen (N) management plan under CA is one of those challenges, which restricts its wider adoption. We hypothesized that appropriate CA management option optimizes the balance between soil N stabilization and N availability to crops. title: “My feet are no longer swollen”: Testing a co-designed podoconiosis protective footwear among rural female farmers in Rwanda
abstract: Podoconiosis is a disabling neglected tropical disease (NTD) caused by prolonged occupational exposure to alkaline red clay soil, disproportionately affecting female farmers in Rwanda. Although preventable through the consistent use of protective footwear, such as farming boots, high costs and limited availability at local markets impede rural farmers' access to appropriate footwear. Among female farmers, gender norms and cultural expectations further constrain their ability to access and wear farming boots. This qualitative community-based participatory project aimed to test a women-centered

title: Predicting connectivity from movement trajectories and step selection
abstract: Predicting and mapping connectivity are essential for ecology and conservation in the face of environmental change. Yet connectivity modeling is challenging because it requires understanding how organisms successfully move across complex landscapes. GPS tracking increasingly produces detailed data on movement trajectories and fine‐scale resource selection, yet it remains unclear how to reliably link such data to connectivity models without relying on individual‐based simulations. title: Dental microwear unveils environmental control of feeding ecology in Miocene squirrels from the Iberian Peninsula
abstract: Reconstructing the dietary and habitat preferences of extinct taxa is essential to understand the selective pressures that drive morphological and behavioral evolution, which provides a necessary framework for understanding macroevolutionary patterns and how extinct lineages navigated ecological shifts across time and space. This study examines the degree to which environmental changes influence dietary intake by analysing dental microwear in Heteroxerus rubricati , an extinct xerine squirrel from the Middle Miocene (Aragonian) of the Iberian Peninsula. title: Sun Protection Behaviors of Adolescents Diagnosed with Cancer and Their Healthy Peers
abstract: Background: Skin cancer is a major public health problem worldwide. It is important to determine adolescents’ sun protection behaviors and develop protective behaviors to prevent skin cancer and sun-related skin problems that may occur in later life.Objectives: The aim of this study was to evaluate the sun protection self-efficacy, decision balance perceptions, and sun protection behaviors of adolescents diagnosed with cancer (ADC), the factors affecting these behaviors, and the difference between the variables in ADC and their healthy peers.Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional, and comp

title: Climate change education for children: a critical integrative review and the participation–emotion–resilience (PER) framework
abstract: Climate change education (CCE) in early childhood and primary settings has expanded rapidly, yet remains unevenly theorised with respect to children’s participation, emotional experiences, and resilience. While existing approaches frequently emphasise knowledge acquisition, pro-environmental behaviour, or coping skills, they offer limited explanatory insight into why children’s engagement with climate issues can simultaneously create agency, anxiety, hope, or disengagement. title: Heavy metal contamination in branded and non-branded turmeric powder from Khulna, Bangladesh: Exposure assessment and potential carcinogenic risk
abstract: Turmeric is vulnerable to heavy metal contamination due to metal uptake from contaminated soils, irrigation water, post-harvest processing or via adulteration. This research assessed the concentrations of heavy metals (Pb, Cr, Cd, Mn, Cu) alongside non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks in fifteen non-branded and five branded powdered turmeric samples acquired from eight sampling locations in Khulna, Bangladesh. title: How German electric utilities navigate sector coupling: strategy archetypes and industry implications
abstract: Sector coupling is widely regarded as a cornerstone of Europe's energy transition, yet research has often overlooked the strategic behaviour of electric utilities as key actors. This paper addresses this gap by analysing how different types of utilities strategically respond to increased sector coupling. Drawing on a literature review and 36 semi-structured interviews with senior energy professionals in Germany, we apply an integrated strategy lens combining resource-based and position-based perspectives. title: Exposure route, not dose, is the primary driver of infection patterns for a respiratory virus
abstract: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. However, the relative contributions of these variables to infection heterogeneity remain poorly quantified because small sample sizes in controlled in vivo experiments limit their statistical power and scientific scope. title: Parents’ perspectives and roles in influencing 10–12-year-old children’s fruit and vegetable consumption: a qualitative study in Sweden
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parents play a central role in shaping children's health behaviours and dietary habits. Previous research has provided insight into parents' feeding practices, especially regarding preschoolers. Less is known about how parents of 10-12-year-old children, whose fruit and vegetable (F&V) intake is particularly low relative to recommendations, perceive F&V and translate their intentions regarding F&V into everyday practices. title: The Genus Weissella: A Review of its Antimicrobial Potentials, Functional Characteristics and Uses in Food Biopreservation
abstract: Background and Aim: Heterofermentative lactic acid bacteria belonging to the Genus Weissella possess unique metabolic capabilities with distinct value for natural food preservation. This review has synthesized current insights into the physiological characteristics, antibacterial pathways and antifungal mechanisms of Weissella species, with their practical uses within diverse food systems and safety problems restricting their commercial adoption. title: A socially informed optimization framework for rural electrification planning across alternative electricity demand scenarios: A case study in Bolivia
abstract: Achieving universal electricity access remains a global challenge, particularly in remote rural areas where grid extension is technically or economically unfeasible. Existing approaches provide cost-optimal and technically feasible solutions for decentralized energy system design, but often fall short in delivering context-sensitive electrification strategies that combine microgrids and stand-alone systems while accounting for social and operational constraints. title: One Metric, Many Meanings: Reconciling Water Use Efficiency Definitions
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Water Use Efficiency (WUE) is widely used to describe carbon-water coupling, but its meaning varies among disciplines, measurement approaches and spatial and temporal scales. We review commonly used WUE definitions and formulations and clarify their conceptual differences. title: Physical Characterization of Volcanic Aquifer Systems in the Southwestern Ethiopian Highlands: A Case of the Gilgel Gibe Catchment
abstract: Volcanic aquifers are globally important groundwater resources, but their pronounced heterogeneity arising from lava emplacement, volcanic facies, structural features, and differential weathering makes hydrogeological characterization challenging. In many developing regions, limited field data further constrain aquifer characterization, increasing uncertainty in groundwater development and management. title: Zero-waste valorization of feldspathic minerals: Technical, economical, and environmental assessment
abstract: Feldspathic minerals, though abundant, are underutilized for metal extraction. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of the novel POTASSIAL process, an integrated, near-zero-waste flowsheet designed to recover potassium chloride (KCl), aluminum oxide (Al 2 O 3 ), and silicon carbide (SiC) from a K-feldspar concentrate. An alternative route producing Ca-silicate from marble sludge residues was also considered. title: Innovation bridging sustainability: the role of digital finance, institutional policy stringency, and climate physical risks for advancing energy transformation
abstract: Abstract Transitioning to low-carbon sources is decisive for the sustainability of Green Silk Road economies, which are currently struggling with climate change and energy crises. This paper investigates the role of digital finance in advancing energy transformation across Green Silk Road economies, with a comparative focus on 76 advanced and 72 emerging economies from 2004 to 2023. title: Perceptions and emergency medical service use for acute myocardial infarction among community-dwelling older adults: an embedded mixed method study
abstract: Acute myocardial infarction is a medical emergency where timely treatment is critical to improving survival. Older adults, however, delay seeking treatment and experience increased mortality because of misunderstandings and negative attitudes toward emergency medical services, especially when experiencing atypical symptoms. This embedded mixed-methods study explored perceptions of acute myocardial infarction, emergency medical service utilization, and their related factors among older adults and caregivers in urban and peri-urban communities. abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric new particle formation is driven by condensable vapors such as sulfuric acid and highly oxygenated organic molecules (HOMs). Measuring these gases is challenging because they are present at trace concentrations, they are easily lost through condensation onto surfaces, and they include a wide range of chemically diverse species. abstract: The cGAS–STING pathway is composed of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) and the stimulator of interferon genes (STING). It plays a critical role in detecting DNA damage and activating the innate immune system for pathogen defense. The pathway has been extensively studied for its potential in cancer therapy, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immunity. abstract: Proteostasis is essential for cellular health, with its disruption contributing to aging, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disorders. While the upstream proteotoxic stress-sensing and protein-folding mechanisms in the ER and cytosol are well studied, the transcriptional regulation of proteostasis remains incompletely understood, particularly concerning the temporal epigenome dynamics, chromatin landscapes, and co-regulatory networks underlying dynamic proteostasis control. title: Teacher beliefs about climate action teaching: Exploring variation across instructional phases and types of action
abstract: Abstact Climate change education requires fostering students' skills in making informed decisions on climate-related actions. Thus, teacher education must equip teachers for such “climate action teaching” and may build on investigating teacher beliefs. Using the Theory of Planned Behavior, we examine which instrumental, injunctive, capacity, and autonomy beliefs shape teachers’ perceptions of climate action teaching. title: Dietary hot red pepper powder modulates laying performance, hematology profile, and hepatic antioxidant status in laying hens under tropical conditions
abstract: Hot red pepper (HRP) has emerged as a phytogenic feed additive with the potential to enhance laying performance in laying hens by improving gut health and mitigating oxidative stress. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of dietary inclusion of HRP powder on the productive performance, hematological and biochemical profiles, intestinal morphology, oxidative stress markers, and liver histopathology of laying hens reared under tropical conditions.
