abstract: Abstract The olive oil industry generates a significant amount of by-products during harvesting and oil extraction, creating environmental challenges while offering opportunities for valorization within livestock production systems. This review provides a structured synthesis of current knowledge on chemical composition, nutritional characteristics, bioactive properties, processing strategies, and feeding applications of major olive oil by-products, including olive pomace, olive cake, olive leaves, and olive mill wastewater. abstract: The composition of a polyclonal antibody response is hard to measure experimentally but contains vital information about the robustness of immunity. Here, we argue that the statistics of neutralization titers alone can be used to make quantitative predictions about the composition of the response, circumventing challenges arising through sequencing and monoclonal antibody expression. abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. Vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and ocean sensing all depend on recognizing underwater signals, but to our knowledge LALMs have not been systematically evaluated on them. abstract: Cylindrical or spherical windows often appear in experiments and real applications. Measuring through those windows requires projecting 3D points to pixels, which is different to compute due to refraction. A point may have multiple projected images but cannot be efficiently determine with the existing projection algorithms. abstract: A combination of remote sensing techniques, open space data and field testing was developed to derive astronomical and meteorological parameters and assess Dark Sky brightness of the hitherto unstudied Schist Villages region in the mountainous Interior Center of Portugal. This study covered the period 2012-2017 and established the methodology for regular light pollution and sky brightness studies in the region using satellite imagery to reduce cost and time and increase accuracy of the final analysis. abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. abstract: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is an optical probe of orbital time reversal symmetry breaking. Although frequency integrated MCD is related to the self-rotation contribution to orbital magnetization at zero field, its magnetic response generally differs from the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility. title: Soliton dynamics in the Gardner-Ostrovsky equation
abstract: We investigate soliton formation and interactions in the non-integrable Gardner-Ostrovsky equation (alias the rotation-modified Gardner equation) with anomalous (positive) dispersion. This equation is relevant to the description of wave dynamics in plasmas and other dispersive media. We show that a special class of solitons, characterized by zero total mass and non-monotonic asymptotics, can emerge from pulse-like initial perturbations. title: Expressiveness, Equivalence, and Uncertainty in Velocity Obstacles and Closest Point of Approach Metrics
abstract: Time to Closest Point of Approach (TCPA), Distance to Closest Point of Approach (DCPA), and Velocity Obstacles (VOs), are widely used to assess and mitigate collision risk in autonomous navigation, yet their relationship and behavior under uncertainty remain largely unexplored. title: Assessing flood-related wellbeing from public discourse in Ireland using large language model as judge, 2012--2025
abstract: Flooding is an environmental hazard that produces social and psychological consequences for exposed individuals, shaping threat appraisal, perceived coping capacity, access to social support, and confidence in institutional response. This paper studies flood-related wellbeing in Ireland from 2012 to 2025 using large-scale, unobtrusive public discourse from Meta Content Library. abstract: acousticHelmholtzFoam is an OpenFOAM application that computes time-harmonic acoustic pressure fields in heterogeneous gas-liquid media on unstructured polyhedral meshes. abstract: We propose a protocol to prepare and probe dark states in a single-molecule electron spin resonance based on atomic force microscopy (ESR-AFM), thus extending existing techniques developed to address Rabi oscillations. To this end, we simulate in analogy to atomic physics the coherent manipulation of a three-level system in the V-configuration using a multifrequency magnetic field. title: Differences among preparatory processes preceding major earthquakes in Kamchatka, 2014-2025, including the MW 8.8 event
abstract: Earthquake preparation involves progressive damage accumulation, strain localization, and changes in the organization of seismicity. We investigate preparatory processes preceding seven episodes of major earthquakes in the Kuril - Kamchatka subduction zone during 2014 - 2025, including the 29 July 2025 MW 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. abstract: This paper studies tetrahedral meshes as the body representation for differentiable simulation and computational design. Fixed-connectivity meshes degrade under large morphs, while remeshing from scratch discards node correspondence. abstract: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. abstract: Cooperative behavior can improve environmental quality, whereas selfish defection can degrade shared resources. abstract: EnRoute is an iOS application designed to support more sustainable everyday choices in transportation and fast fashion consumption. We describe three design iterations and the user research and field evaluations that shaped each one. abstract: We produce degenerate photon pairs called signal and idler via parametric down-conversion (PDC) in a Fabry-Pérot waveguide resonator having close to a 2GHz bandwidth in the telecom C-band. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) should abstain from scientific multiple-choice questions when no option is valid, but frequent abstention alone does not demonstrate sensitivity to answer availability. abstract: Information sharing, threat perception, and collective evasion highlight the advantages of swarm intelligence. abstract: The marine environment absorbs the largest share of the ecological burden generated by international shipping, an industry that carries over eighty per cent of global trade by volume. abstract: Marine fishery and aquaculture processing generate substantial volumes of biological byproducts—fish skin, bone, scales, and viscera—that remain underutilized as feedstocks for higher-value bio-based materials. title: Ireland & the Ocean: a decade dive review into Ocean Literacy
abstract: Human and natural systems are deeply interconnected, influencing one another for centuries. In recent decades, the protection of the marine environment has gained prominence, particularly following several reports linking climate change, biodiversity loss and ocean pollution to human health. Ocean Literacy (OL), a framework that promotes education for sustainable development (ESD) focused on the ocean, is emerging as a strategic bridge between education, sustainability, and public policy. While global attention in OL has increased, Ireland’s efforts are still fragmented, low and inconsistent.

abstract: Abstract This article examines the legal implications of autonomous fishing vessels ( AFV s) under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea ( LOSC ). abstract: We read with great interest the report describing the first robotic totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass (TECAB) in Southeast Asia. abstract: A popular misconception holds that piracy is a crime confined to the high seas. abstract: The aggressive policy of the russian federation remains a source of threats to the security of Ukraine's maritime trade today. title: National Symbols and Identity in Hungary and the EU
abstract: The history of symbols is as old as humanity itself, and they continue to play a key role in expressing national identity today. The external function of symbols is to express sovereignty – as a representation of autonomy and independence – while their internal function is to express identity (emotional attachment to the community). abstract: Maritime crimes constitute a significant threat to Nigeria’s national security, economic stability, and regional maritime governance. abstract: Toxic trace elements in edible oils pose public health risks because of their persistence, bioaccumulation, and, for some elements, carcinogenic potential. abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent, genetically determined, and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis. abstract: The vegetation associations and landforms of Rangimata / Shag Rock, Te Whanga, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island are described, and the avifauna, flora and mycobiota (lichenised and non-lichenised) documented. abstract: The growing detection of microplastics (MPs) in the human body has raised concerns about the potential entrance of MPs into the food chain and subsequently into humans. abstract: Antibiotics and their transformation products (TPs) make up a critical class of emerging contaminants. abstract: Abstract Sri Lankan cuisine is a layered ethnic food heritage shaped by tropical agriculture and by centuries of Arab, Portuguese, Dutch, and British contact atop a South Indian rice-and-curry foundation, and it is increasingly encountered by global audiences not at the destination but on digital platforms. abstract: Abstract Emerging water pollutants such as pharmaceutical (PhACs) and microplastics (MPs) are progressively detected in aquatic environments, raising alarms about their mutual toxicological effects on non-target biota, particularly fish. title: Integrating free-living amoebae into climate-microbiome and One Health frameworks
abstract: Climate change is altering microbial ecosystems at a global scale, yet the role of free-living amoebae within these shifting microbiomes remains incompletely understood. Free-living amoebae occupy soil, water, air, and built environments, where they contribute to microbial diversity, regulate nutrient cycling, and host diverse bacterial, fungal, and viral microorganisms. abstract: Oil plays a significant role in the Brazilian and global energy matrices. Brazilian oil production is predominantly offshore, particularly in pre-salt fields. abstract: Abstract Seafood supply chains face increasing disruption from climate change, pandemics, and changing market conditions, creating challenges for maintaining both resilience and sustainability. Understanding the perspectives of people working in the industry and supply chain (i.e. stakeholders) are crucial to developing context-specific and practical pathways for supporting continued seafood supply, livelihoods and profitability. abstract: Abstract. Snow algae are psychrophilic and psychrotolerant photosynthetic microorganisms found on every continent, predominantly in polar and alpine environments. Along with contributing to terrestrial carbon cycling and food webs, colourful snow algal blooms formed on snow surfaces can substantially reduce albedo and accelerate snowmelt. abstract: ABSTRACT The graphical abstract links rainfall data, statistical tests, spatial outputs, and hydrological implications for the Wami basin. abstract: Remote ecosystems are often assumed to be insulated from chemical contamination; however, increasing human visitation may compromise this perception. abstract: Microbial contamination of drinking water remains a major public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, particularly where water quality deteriorates between treatment and household consumption. abstract: Microbiome-based dryland restoration is promising but weakly validated. abstract: En este ensayo se examina la evaluación en la educación superior con especial atención a las escuelas normales de México como instituciones clave en la formación de docentes de educación básica. El texto analiza la necesidad de transitar desde una visión burocrática y punitiva hacia una más crítica, ética y emancipadora hacia la transformación de la práctica. La aportación central reside en diez estrategias pedagógicas orientadas a democratizar las dinámicas en el aula, como la coconstrucción de criterios y la calificación compartida. title: Color vision of the endemic Nēnē, or Hawaiian Goose (Branta sandvicensis): a case study
abstract: Abstract Color vision is a key aspect of bird vision; however, only 2 out of the 172 species in the Anatidae family have been fully studied. We characterize the color visual system properties of a third species, the Hawaiian island endemic goose, the Nēnē ( Branta sandvicensis ). We measured eye size, ocular media transmittance, retinal opsin sequences, photoreceptor sensitivity, and relative photoreceptor densities. title: LSD treatment affects working memory-related brain function in patients with major depressive disorder
abstract: Abstract Classic psychedelics, including lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), are currently under investigation for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Cognitive dysfunction is common in MDD, but effects of psychedelic treatment on cognitive brain function, measured by magnetic resonance imaging, are sparsely reported. The present study investigated effects of LSD treatment on working memory-related brain function in patients with MDD. title: The China-Plus-One Dividend and Domestic Reform: India's Manufacturing Ascent During the Modi Era
abstract: Was India's manufacturing ascent after 2014 earned at home or handed to it by geopolitics? This article argues that it was both, and that neither alone is sufficient. The US-China trade war (2018), the pandemic (2020) and Western "de-risking" (2022 onward) produced a large external shock: China's share of US goods imports fell from about 22% in 2017 to about 9% in 2025 [1][2]. title: Articulations of poisoning: historicity, relationality, and contextuality of Chlordecone pollution in the French Antilles
abstract: Chlordecone, a highly persistent organochlorine insecticide, was widely applied to banana plantations in Martinique and Guadeloupe from 1972 until being banned in 1993. Classified as both a carcinogenic and an endocrine disruptor, the chemical compound has generated widespread protests, epidemiological debates, and political critique. abstract: When the withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) took legal effect on 29 January 2025, the Community lost the three states whose insecurity had dominated its agenda for more than a decade. title: Structural Safety Certification in India: Evaluating Regulatory Fragmentation, Institutional Accountability and Enforcement Gaps
abstract: India’s recurring building collapses expose a regulatory paradox: an elaborate body of technical standards coexists with a certification system that cannot reliably demonstrate whether a building was safely designed, constructed, altered and maintained. This article evaluates structural safety certification as a problem of public law and regulatory governance rather than a narrow engineering formality. abstract: Summary A rapid two-dimensional (2D) Occam’s inversion method is developed to interpret ultra-deep borehole azimuthal resistivity (UDAR) measurements acquired in complex dipping formations and along arbitrary well trajectories. While conventional one-dimensional (1D) inversion approaches are computationally efficient, they are inadequate to capture lateral variations of electrical resistivity and structural complexity, hence limiting their accuracy and reliability in realistic geological settings. Here we show that healthy Kenyan adults living in regions with higher malaria transmission and broader infectious exposure have distinct baseline immune profiles. title: “We will get you”: linguistic ideology, power, and the distortion of meaning in Twitter discourse
abstract: This is a case study of the meaning of a tweet by @KyleHibbee007 in the context of the 2021 Scottish Parliamentary elections. abstract: Communities on the frontlines of climate change face disproportionate risks of multiple hazards. Although community resilience depends on effective risk communication, most research focuses on the information that individuals receive from authorities rather than that which they produce or exchange themselves—that is, “community-based risk communication”. abstract: This paper presents a case study of the entrepreneur and landowner Anton Kajfež and his successors, owners of one of the largest companies in Kočevje and Lower Carniola before World War I and during the interwar period. The company focused primarily on the timber and wine trade and became a significant shareholder in many regional companies and banks. Kajfež promoted the local Slovenian economy and used his wealth to strengthen it through a series of projects aimed at surpassing the Gottscheers, a local group of German origin, in the Kočevje economy and politics. title: Extreme drought stress diminished soil carbon sequestration and restructured microbial communities at the Dajiuhu subalpine peatland, Central China
abstract: Peatlands store approximately 30% of global terrestrial soil carbon, yet how subalpine peatlands respond to extreme drought remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of the historically severe 2022 Yangtze River Basin drought by comparing carbon fluxes, soil nutrients, and soil bacterial communities with those of the pre-drought year (2021). title: Educating for a climate-changed future in India: diagnosing a mandate-without-mechanism condition
abstract: India’s constitutional provisions, Supreme Court directives, and National Curriculum Framework make its formal commitment to climate change education unusually explicit, yet classroom implementation remains uneven. This article combines analysis of India’s multilevel policy architecture with a structured review of 72 empirical studies published from 2007 to 2026. title: Implementing sustainable procurement through category management and ESG-based supplier evaluation: an EPC case study supported by the Operational Ethical Dilemma
abstract: Sustainable procurement has become a strategic organizational priority as companies increasingly seek to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into procurement decision-making while maintaining operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness. Despite the growing body of literature on sustainable procurement, limited research has examined its practical implementation within complex project-based industries. title: The orthodox left organizations in Israel: between theological rejection and humanistic reframing of redemption and messianism
abstract: This article examines how Orthodox Left civil society organizations in Israel engage with messianic ideas in relation to dominant Religious Zionist interpretations that frame the establishment of the State of Israel as the beginning of a divine redemptive process. Focusing on organizations such as The Faithful Left, Tag Meir, and the Yashar platform, the study analyses how Orthodox activists reinterpret, reject, or reframe messianic theology within a religious nationalist context. title: Endangered mammal occurrence records from Environmental Impact Assessment and post-EIA monitoring in the Republic of Korea
abstract: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and post-EIA monitoring generate substantial biodiversity information through ecological surveys conducted before, during and after development projects. In the Republic of Korea, these records have accumulated in individual assessment reports, but their reuse has been limited because occurrence information is dispersed across documents and is not generally available in a structured format. title: Climate Change Disinformation| Unraveling Debunked Climate Change Disinformation and Responses to Fact-Checks: Evidence From the United States, Netherlands, and Philippines
abstract: Although climate change skepticism and denialism have been considered influential narratives in the contemporary digital information landscape, we know little about how such narratives are legitimized in climate change disinformation across different national settings. Against this background, this study relies on an in-depth qualitative content analysis of fact-checked disinformation in the Netherlands, the United States, and the Philippines as contrasting global cases. title: Dual Cuisine Nationalism: Food, Identity and the Making of the Nation in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: ABSTRACT The United Arab Emirates (UAE) presents a distinctive case of nation‐building, as its citizens constitute a demographic minority. Nation‐building in the UAE involves accommodating non‐citizens while maintaining a distinct citizen‐centred national identity. This study argues that the UAE constructs national identity through a dual process of culinary nationalism, in which food serves both as a symbol of indigeneity and a marker of cosmopolitan inclusion. title: Use of insects as an alternative protein source in tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) feeding
abstract: The use of alternative protein sources in fish diets has gained increasing attention due to the need to reduce costs and dependence on conventional ingredients in aquaculture. In this context, insects have considerable nutritional potential as feed ingredients, particularly the black soldier fly, Hermetia illucens. However, information regarding the effects of these ingredients in tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) diets remains limited and scattered across different studies. title: From Facebook to political actions: nationalism, patriotism, and participation in Vietnam’s digital sphere
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between three types of social media use and four dimensions of political participation on Facebook. Taking Vietnam as a context, we further looked into the mediating role of two related but distinct concepts of nationalism and patriotism in this process. Findings from a cross-sectional survey revealed that active nonsocial Facebook use was positively related to nationalist and patriotic attitudes. title: Validating national reuse indicators from regional demolition data: a Swedish example
abstract: Construction accounts for a substantial share of global emissions and waste, highlighting the need to shift from linear to circular resource flows and to prioritise deconstruction and reuse over demolition and disposal. Enabling this transition requires reliable methods for identifying and quantifying products embedded in existing buildings. This Swedish study examines whether key performance indicators (KPIs) derived from demolition‑permit documentation can be generalised across regions to support product‑level stock estimation for circular construction. title: Climate Change Disinformation| Seeking the Truth Among Dead Crops: Carbon Footprint Victimhood, Platformed Conspiracism, and Climate Countermovement in Turkey
abstract: After years of climate inaction, Turkey’s ratification of the Paris Agreement in 2021 prompted the Justice and Development Party’s discursive shift from high-carbon hegemonic agenda to green developmentalist rhetoric. This policy change provoked a backlash among conspiratorial climate-denial networks on social media. title: Effectiveness of Gradual Filtration Technology for Drinking Water Quality and Student Competence in Jayapura, Indonesia
abstract: Access to safe, high-quality drinking water remains an unmet basic need in many religious educational institutions, particularly Islamic boarding schools in Papua. This study evaluated pretest–posttest changes associated with an appropriate-technology multi-stage filtration system designed to improve drinking water quality and students’ water-management competencies at Papua Madani Boarding School (PMBS), Jayapura City. title: La Satisfacción del Usuario como Indicador Estratégico de la Calidad Hospitalaria: Una Revisión de Alcance
abstract: El estudio analiza la satisfacción del usuario como indicador estratégico de la calidad en los servicios hospitalarios. Se realizó una revisión de alcance (Scoping Review) siguiendo la metodología del Joanna Briggs Institute y PRISMA-ScR. abstract: Spodumene [LiAl(Si 2 O 6 )], as an important Li source, is crucial for sustaining the global Li supply. abstract: Glucocorticoids are upregulated during acute challenges, contributing to maintenance of energy balance. However, if this upregulation exceeds a threshold or becomes chronic, it can lead to harmful effects. Investigating the factors behind between-individual variation in the magnitude of the response to acute stress and how effectively individuals regulate this response to return to baseline glucocorticoid levels (recovery capacity), is therefore important. title: TWO CONCEPTS OF POLARIZATION : Urban–National Tension and its Effects on the Liberal Trajectory of Cities
abstract: Abstract This study examines how urban–national polarization shapes how progressive cities exercise local autonomy. It introduces a new framework for assessing polarization within specific policy domains, distinguishing between ideological and pragmatic polarization. The analysis focuses on five liberal‐oriented policy domains: gender equality, environmental sustainability, LGBTQ+ rights, immigration, and religion–state relations through the case of Tel Aviv–Jaffa, Israel. title: Cyanobacteria in sustainable agriculture: from bioactive metabolites toward mechanistically validated biostimulants
abstract: Cyanobacteria are emerging as multifunctional components of sustainable agroecosystems, with the potential to influence nutrient cycling, soil structure, plant-associated microbiomes, and crop responses to environmental stress. This review integrates current knowledge of the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these effects, emphasizing nitrogen fixation, nutrient mobilization, phytohormone biosynthesis, extracellular polymeric substances, biocontrol-related metabolites, and stress mitigation. title: The Active Archive: Haptic Reconstruction in Albertina Carri's Los Rubios (2003)
abstract: The fragility of memory beyond any specific context is a biological and universal bodily process. That is the initial reflection behind Albertina Carri’s 2003 Los Rubios, a film that, through its retelling of autobiographical events from the Argentinian Dirty War, breaks documentary conventions and maximises the audiovisual medium to portray an erased history. title: BACTERIAL DIVERSITY ON SELECTED DUMPSITE IN MADONNA UNIVERSITY, ELELE NIGERIA
abstract: Improper waste disposal poses serious environmental and public health risks, as dumpsite serve as reservoirs for diverse microbial populations, including pathogenic bacteria. This study investigated the bacterial diversity of selected dumpsites in Madonna university with the aim of isolating, identifying and comparing the bacterial species present in soil samples collected from three dumpsites (A, B and C). title: Beyond Impoverishment? A Socio-Ecological Analysis of the Drivers of Child Trafficking and Migration Between Two Fishing Communities
abstract: Popular discourses on the drivers of child trafficking and migration are dominated by notions of household poverty and economic hardship. While these are key drivers of trafficking and migration in sub-Saharan Africa, the taken-for-granted status of these drivers within anti-trafficking discourse and intervention often obscures and/or blurs diverse contextual factors that inform practices conceptualized as trafficking in children. title: Protocol for integrative transcriptomic/metabolomic analysis: A case study on factors influencing the oyster-POMS disease
abstract: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying complex biological interactions requires comprehensive approaches that capture these interactions across multiple regulatory and functional levels. Here, we present a protocol applied to the host-pathogen-environment interactions underlying Pacific oyster mortality syndrome (POMS) in Magallana gigas . abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the United Nations 2030 Agenda's call for firm‐level Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) implementation, no validated diagnostic exists to assess whether small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) have developed the operating capability that SDG‐implementation adequacy requires against absolute biophysical reference points, rather than relative improvement against firm‐specific baselines. title: Political Advantage, Political Risk: The Nascent Stage of Statoil’s International Expansion, 1978–1999
abstract: This article analyses how the dynamics between the Norwegian national oil company Statoil and its government owner gradually changed during the 1980s and 1990s, as Statoil invested in politically risky business environments outside its domicile. Yet, despite this seemingly profit-maximizing behaviour, the NOC was closely intertwined with its government owner and this owner’s pursuit of a value-based foreign policy with emphasis on support for poverty reduction, democracy, human rights and peace building. title: Scaling Productivity in Harsh Rainfed Ecosystems: The Strategic Role of Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) in Pali, Rajasthan
abstract: Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) were evaluated to assess the productivity, technological gaps and economic performance of improved crop production technologies under farmers’ field conditions in Pali district, Rajasthan, during 2018-19 to 2022-23. Demonstrations were conducted on six major crops green gram, cluster bean, sesame, wheat, mustard and cumin using improved varieties and recommended agronomic practices, with adjacent farmers’ fields maintained as local checks. title: Ontological frictions in disaster risk assessment: evidence from Yaqui territories, Mexico
abstract: Purpose In Indigenous communities where governance integrates land, ancestors and more-than-human beings, standardised risk assessments overlooking relational ontologies may produce incomplete evaluations and inadvertently deepen vulnerabilities. This article analyses ontological frictions in disaster risk assessment (DRA) arising from the encounter between standardised frameworks and Indigenous relational ontologies enacted through governance systems. title: Baseline blood-based DNA methylation in impaired fasting glucose and impaired glucose tolerance: epigenome-wide differences and associations with subsequent progression to type 2 diabetes mellitus
abstract: Aims Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) differ in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) progression risk, but whether they have distinct blood DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns and CpG features associated with progression remains unclear. title: Direct aging of laser powder bed fusion 17-4 PH stainless steel: Nanoscale precipitation and grain boundary segregation
abstract: Direct aging (DA) of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) 17-4 PH stainless steel bypasses solution annealing to achieve single-step precipitation hardening, but its effects on grain boundary (GB) chemistry remain poorly understood. title: Brand Matters: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Quality, Reputation, Pricing and Advertising on Generation Z's Purchase Decisions for Nike Footwear in Kathmandu Valley
abstract: Background: Nike has established itself as a globally recognized athletic and lifestyle brand, and its footwear enjoys strong appeal among Generation Z consumers even in emerging markets such as Nepal, where the brand maintains no official retail presence. In Kathmandu Valley, Nike's market standing is sustained largely through imported product quality, brand reputation, and exposure to global advertising, yet little empirical research has examined how these brand-related factors, together with pricing and brand loyalty, jointly shape Gen Z's purchase decisions in this context. abstract: Many ceramic companies that use clay as their chief raw material are springing up across the country. There is need to continuously explore for clay deposits to feed these industries. Atomic Absorption Spectrometry was used to analyse the oxide contents of fifteen clay samples obtained by pitting and trenching methods from Abia, Imo and Anambra States in the Anambra geologic basin of Nigeria. title: A Review of the Biological Activity and Potential Applications of Compounds from Elsholtzia ciliata for the Treatment of Dermatological Diseases
abstract: In the context of increasing antibiotic resistance and associated adverse effects, treatments for dermatological conditions such as acne vulgaris and atopic dermatitis remain limited. This narrative review synthesises studies published mainly between 2010 and the first quarter of 2026, retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Vietnam Journals Online, with the aim of evaluating the potential dermatological applications of compounds isolated from Elsholtzia ciliata. title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids in the Management of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention
abstract: PURPOSE: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids lower triglycerides and modulate inflammation, thrombosis, and endothelial function, providing a rationale for their use in cardiovascular prevention. This review examines the influence of formulation, dose, and patient selection on clinical outcomes. title: Islamist Right-Wing Populism, Authoritarian Majoritarianism, and Conditional Cosmopolitanism: Supporter Perspectives from Turkey and Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Cosmopolitanism is most widely understood as a political position that, based on a shared status of citizens of the world ( kosmopolitês ), all human beings are equal. Populism and cosmopolitanism are typically framed in opposition to one another. However, such accounts overlook a crucial dimension: how supporters of populists engage with cosmopolitan discourses themselves. abstract: Abstract Microalgae are promising renewable resources for textile dyeing and functionalization, but their industrial transfer remains limited. This work developed and optimized whole microalgal biomass-based formulations for application onto 100% linen fabric using dip–pad–dry processes compatible with conventional textile finishing lines. Textile substrate screening, binder selection, cross-linker optimization, fixation auxiliary strategy, and guar gum stabilization were sequentially evaluated. abstract: Introduction: This study was conducted to provide etiological data for the prevention and control of vector-borne infectious diseases in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC).The study aimed to taxonomically classify flea species, characterize the profiles of flea-borne pathogens, and identify potential novel pathogenic bacterial species. title: Counterinsurgency and territorial control: security practices in Turkey’s Kurdish peace process
abstract: Turkey’s 2013–2015 Kurdish Opening collapsed not despite its reformist rhetoric but alongside a counterinsurgency apparatus that remained firmly in place. Drawing on twelve months of ethnographic fieldwork and 115 interviews conducted in the border provinces of Van and Hakkari, I examine how territorial control continued to structure state governance throughout the ceasefire period. abstract: Social science on wildfire has garnered increased attention with scholarship particularly focused on pre-fire and near-term impacts. However, the long-term impacts of wildfire and long-term recovery are less well understood and less represented in scholarship. This article takes up the questions of long-term wildfire recovery with special attention to time. title: ‘Stuck in a Time Warp’ or ‘Going Forward With Care’? Traversing the Environmental Politics of Genetic Modification in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: This article offers an environmental politics history of genetic modification (GM) in Aotearoa New Zealand. GM has been on political agendas for half a century. It has again come to the fore with proposals to enable the technology after decades of stringent regulations. To better contextualise the major changes now in motion, this article traverses the evolution of GM politics in Aotearoa. We identify five key eras of GM politics, drawing on a database of social science literature and media and policy documents spanning the 1970s to today. title: Necropolitics under competitive authoritarianism: martyrdom, fatalism and contested responsibility for death in Turkey
abstract: Blame avoidance is usually theorized through democratic institutions, where elections, opposition parties, courts and independent media can contest official accounts of failure. This article extends blame avoidance theory to competitive authoritarianism by developing the concept of necropolitical blame avoidance: the conversion of responsibility-threatening deaths into governable objects of meaning, distribution and credit. title: Influence of Monitoring and Evaluation Systems on the Performance of County Flagship Projects in Kwale County, Kenya
abstract: Kenyan counties are required by law to operate integrated monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems, yet about 30% of the flagship projects in Kwale County continue to run late and over budget. This study examined how three features of the county’s M&E system, namely data quality, budgetary allocation and the technical capacity of M&E personnel, influence the performance of these projects. title: Factors influencing tourist satisfaction with street food experiences in Hanoi: An empirical study toward sustainable tourism development
abstract: This study examines the factors influencing tourist satisfaction with street food experiences in Hanoi from the perspective of sustainable tourism development. Although street food is widely recognized as a key component of Vietnam’s culinary tourism, empirical evidence remains limited for Hanoi, where long-standing culinary heritage coexists with rapid urbanization, increasing tourist demand, and challenges related to service consistency, hygiene, space management, and price transparency. title: The oldest trees of the Mediterranean
abstract: The Mediterranean region hosts some of the oldest trees in Europe growing in high-elevation environments and reaching ages well beyond 800 years. We here present eight of these sites from the Atlas Mountains in the west to the Taurus Mountains in the east and discuss their potential for high-resolution climate reconstruction using dendrochronological techniques. abstract: Coconut value addition offers considerable scope for improving the income of coconut growers in Kerala. This study examined stakeholder interest and influence and prioritised the constraints perceived by coconut growers in the southern Kerala districts of Thiruvananthapuram, Alappuzha and Kollam. abstract: Background: Hotel swimming pools are widely used for leisure, yet inadequate disinfection and maintenance can turn them into vehicles for recreational water illness. abstract: This article analyzes the impact of transport infrastructure on agricultural market integration and spatial inequalities in Benin. The data comes from the National Institute of Statistics and Demography (INSTaD) of Benin, collected between November 2025 and January 2026 from a sample of 1,920 households distributed across the country's twelve departments. abstract: Objective(s): To characterize the structural chemistry, physicochemical properties, skin bioactivities, formulation aspects, sustainability, therapeutic applications, commercialization, and regulatory aspects of sophorolipids, rhamnolipids, and mannosylerythritol lipids as biosurfactants with focus on their potential in leave-on cosmetic and topical pharmaceutical formulations, as well as highlight research and development gaps. abstract: The compressive strength of concrete is a critical parameter that governs the safety and durability of reinforced concrete structures. In Nigeria, the frequent collapse of buildings has been largely attributed to the use of substandard construction materials, particularly poor quality concrete aggregates. abstract: The present study investigated problematic exercise from a qualitative perspective. abstract: Central areolar choroidal dystrophy (CACD) is a rare monogenic hereditary retinal dystrophy characterised by progressive retinal pigment epithelium and choriocapillaris atrophy, photoreceptor loss, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. abstract: Consumer goods firms face a persistent tension between supply chain resilience and operating efficiency. abstract: Matrilineal Family Practices on Christian Marriage in Ashanti-Ghana. abstract: LLM-based agents face challenges in personalized interactive tasks due to heterogeneous, multi-typed, and implicitly constrained long-term traces. Most methods use single-vector representations, blurring type distinctions and relational structure. We propose HGP, a hybrid graph memory framework. Lumen-bench: Cross-Lingual Safety Gaps and the Say-Do Problem in Tool-Calling Large Language Models
abstract: When a large language model refuses an unethical request, what does refusal mean? In conversation, refusal is bounded by what the model says; once the model is equipped with executable tools, what it does can diverge from what it says, a failure mode that English-only evaluations cannot fully reveal. We introduce Lumen-bench, a behavioral benchmark of tool-calling ethics spanning 30 models, five languages (Portuguese, English, Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi), 108 Portuguese-authored scenarios, six social-pressure conditions, two system prompts (ethical and neutral), and 21 generic tools. title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models
abstract: Humans perceive far more in a scene than what is explicitly depicted: a single glance captures past causes and future trajectories; a quick peek determines if a vehicle can fit between two parked cars; a few seconds of video reveals who holds authority in a room; and a fleeting clip highlights subtle abstract patterns like unwritten rules or hidden labels. This capacity reflects a form of humanity's sixth sense: an intuitive reasoning mechanism that recovers implicit information beyond raw sensory perception. title: The Missile and the Toll: Two-Way Flow Through the Strait of Hormuz
abstract: Tolls for safe passage and attacks on shipping are usually treated as mutually exclusive: either ships pay or attacks happen. We argue they are complementary. In a Stackelberg escalation game for the Strait of Hormuz, the enforcer chooses an attack intensity and a toll schedule; the response is to pay, cross exposed, wait, reroute, or exit. Attacks create the willingness to pay; tolls harvest it. The model predicts asymmetry across trade forms: a toll where the cargo owner can pay and the vessel owner will consent, and none where either fails. title: Adapting English Quality Classifiers for Multilingual LLM Pretraining Data Selection
abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) pretraining highlight the role of high-quality training data in improving performance. While model-based filtering has proven effective in selecting high-quality subsets from web-scale corpora, especially for high-resource languages, low-resource languages face challenges due to limited availability of annotated data. This work explores extending quality filtering to over 100 languages by proposing a multilingual adaptation approach that converts an existing English quality classifier into a multilingual variant. title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate
abstract: Descriptions of how people use AI are becoming training data for the next generation of models. We ask whether what a model reads about its users changes how it treats people. Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning, we train Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora built from the same 1,625 real-world usage scenarios. The corpora differ only in the predominant motive they attribute to users of AI chatbots: helping others (prosocial), exploiting others (antisocial), legitimate self-advancement, or task completion. title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. title: The Curse of Knowledge in Role-Playing Language Models
abstract: Role-playing language models speak as characters in games and agent simulations, where the system records what each character can hear, see and understand. We test whether characters respect these boundaries in 480 scenes, each with a counterfactual twin that changes only the hidden fact, so mentions of the twin's fact measure guessing. title: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X): Prototype Design and Adaptation for Spaceflight
abstract: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X) is a compact and low-cost scintillator-based instrument designed to detect ionizing radiation, including cosmic-ray muons. Built around a plastic scintillator, a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), and a dual-core Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller, the v3X achieves a 400 microsecond dead time per event, sustained event logging at 700 Hz, and two-detector coincidence triggering for more accurate counts. This paper first summarizes the design, firmware, and demonstrated performance of the v3X prototype. It then outlines the design changes needed to prepare

title: Split Skies: Operational Experiences Extending a Multi-Cloud Network Telescope into the Asia-Pacific
abstract: Comprehensive visibility into Internet Background Radiation (IBR) requires diverse measurement infrastructure. Recent work showed that cloud IBR depends on the provider making single-provider telescopes systematically biased. These studies relied entirely on Western providers and left the Asia-Pacific region as a blind spot. In this report we extend a multi-cloud network telescope onto Tencent Cloud inside mainland China. We detail how Internet fragmentation, geo-politics, and provider rules complicate global measurement through strict onboarding barriers and an unreliable management plane. On

title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.

title: Electromagnetic isospin breaking in hadronic vacuum polarization within a VMD model
abstract: One of the challenging components of modern lattice-QCD computations of the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $(g-2)_μ$ is the isospin-breaking correction due to electromagnetism. Dominated by long distances, this correction suffers from severe signal-to-noise issues and finite-volume effects. To provide infinite-volume benchmarks for various quark-level Wick contractions, we estimate their sizes phenomenologically at the physical point, using a previously developed vector-meson-dominance model. title: AdHImEx: Adaptively High-Order Implicit-Explicit Transport for Large Time Steps
abstract: Adaptively Implicit-Explicit (AdImEx) time stepping provides stability for large time steps for mass-conservative transport, making it attractive for the numerical representation of advection in weather and climate prediction. Existing AdImEx transport schemes become first-order accurate in the large-time-step, implicit regime and may require multiple sparse matrix solutions per time step. This work introduces AdHImEx, a new AdImEx scheme that addresses both limitations simultaneously. title: SoK: Privacy-Preserving Order Matching
abstract: Privacy-preserving order matching enables traders to discover and execute compatible orders while limiting disclosure of sensitive trading information. Existing systems span financial markets and blockchain-based asset exchanges and employ diverse market structures, privacy mechanisms, and trust assumptions, making their privacy guarantees difficult to compare. We present a systematization of privacy-preserving order matching covering 22 protocol families. title: AI-Generated Disinformation in the UK: Risk of Harm, Context, and Classification
abstract: More people across the UK are today exposed to more AI-generated and AI-altered disinformation and misinformation than ever before - exposing individuals and society to a growing range of harmful consequences and potential consequences. We analyse evidence from a dataset of 112 pieces of AI-generated or AI-altered disinformation or misinformation seen tens of millions of times across the UK between 1 January 2025 and 31 March 2026. title: The Constitution Speaks Nheengatu: An Open MT System and Reproducible Corpus Pipeline for the Amazonian Língua Geral
abstract: Nheengatu (yrl), the Amazonian Língua Geral, has 6--10 thousand speakers and is co-official in São Gabriel da Cachoeira (Brazil), yet remains poorly served by evaluated Portuguese--Nheengatu MT resources. We present the largest parallel corpus assembled for the language (14.5k Portuguese--Nheengatu pairs), anchored by the 2023 official translation of the Brazilian Federal Constitution; the first MT evaluation set built from transcribed spontaneous speech; and, to our knowledge, the first open-weight MT models dedicated to bidirectional Portuguese--Nheengatu translation. title: ALP interactions with mesons and baryons at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$: a general field redefinition invariant approach
abstract: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. title: Pulsations and constraints on time lags in two distinct ULXs: NGC 5204 X-1 and NGC 55 ULX-1
abstract: The nature of ultra-luminous X-ray sources (ULXs) is shrouded in mystery as they're believed to be point sources with luminosities above the classical Eddington limit for a 10$M_{\odot}$ black hole (BH), but generally fit into the classification tree of super-Eddington X-ray binaries. title: Magnus: neutrino oscillation probabilities for any Hermitian Hamiltonian, any number of flavors, and any matter profile
abstract: Neutrino oscillation probabilities computed with the Magnus expansion, for an arbitrary number of flavors and any Hamiltonian, time-dependent or not. Every truncation of the series lives in the Lie algebra, so the evolution operator it exponentiates is unitary exactly rather than to the accuracy of the truncation.

title: The magic cost of fermionic randomness
abstract: Sampling-based quantum advantage raises a basic resource question: how much non-Gaussianity is needed to reproduce the random-matrix statistics often associated with quantum chaos? Passive fermionic linear optics preserves Gaussian structure, and even Haar-random mode mixing fails to anticoncentrate for Slater inputs. We show that overcoming this obstruction requires an extensive input resource. For any pure half-filled input state, the one-body defect $ν$, defined as the summed occupation variance of the natural orbitals, must scale linearly with system size. title: Translation Tag Team: Formal Rules and LLMs Translate More Macros Together Than Apart
abstract: Modern critical software infrastructure is largely written in C. Since C lacks memory safety, researchers are investigating automatic translation of C to safer languages like Rust. But real-world C software consists of more than just C code, often using named code fragments called macros which are not part of the C language proper. State-of-the-art techniques avoid translating macros by preprocessing C code first before translating it. title: Are Language Models Script-Aware?
abstract: Language models frequently generate outputs in unintended languages or scripts, a phenomenon known as off-target generation. While existing research has focused on language selection, the dimension of script knowledge remains understudied: before any linguistic understanding can occur, users must recognize the graphic symbols in a model's response. We investigate whether Small and Large Language Models (SLMs and LLMs) possess script knowledge by testing them on multi-scriptic languages. title: Searching for hot water world candidates with CHEOPS: II. A low-density super-Earth orbiting the K dwarf TOI-2211
abstract: Small exoplanets on close-in orbits are exposed to high levels of stellar irradiation, which can effectively remove low-mass primordial H/He envelopes through atmospheric escape. Under these conditions, planets whose masses and radii are incompatible with both bare rocky interiors and extended H-dominated atmospheres are therefore expected to host high mean molecular weight atmospheres, making them promising candidates for volatile-rich hot water worlds. title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
abstract: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. title: Weakly supervised seawater intrusion mapping via multi-source remote sensing data fusion
abstract: Seawater intrusion is a typical disaster in the coastal critical zone. Assessing its damage to the soil-vegetation continuum faces several bottlenecks. To address these issues, a weakly supervised mapping method for seawater intrusion is proposed. This method utilizes the Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud platform. It fuses Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, Sentinel-2 optical data, topographic data, and land cover semantic data. title: ENSO-Flavor Differences in Indonesian Marine Heatwaves: Satellite SST, Physical Covariates, and Coral Habitat Suitability
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the Indonesian Seas develop within a long-term rise in sea surface temperature and strong interannual climate variability. We analyze daily NOAA Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature version 2.1 for 1982–2022 and compare five Eastern-Pacific (EP) with five Central-Pacific (CP) El Niño events. MHWs are detected against a fixed 1982–2011 baseline, and each event is represented by the common 1 July–30 June window spanning its developing and decaying phases. title: Hyperspectral Attribution of Climate-Driven Coastal Ocean-Colour Shifts Using UAV, Satellite and Phytoplankton Pigment Observations
abstract: Marine ecosystems, which are changing due to climate interaction along the coastlines, are also changing ocean-colour properties by altering the phytoplankton communities, suspended solids, dissolved organic matter, and water optical properties. These changes should be monitored continuously to comprehend the response of the ecosystem and sustainability of coastal management. title: Microbial deamination of peptides and proteins as a source of persistent marine dissolved organic matter
abstract: Abstract Refractory dissolved organic nitrogen is a major component of the ocean's nitrogen pool, yet the mechanisms producing and preserving it remain poorly understood. Here, we show that deaminated peptides (DAPs), derived from microbial processing of proteinaceous material, are ubiquitous across oxygenated marine environments—from productive coastal waters to the oligotrophic ocean—and persist from surface to bathypelagic depths. abstract: Accurate monitoring of sea cucumbers from UAV imagery remains challenging because submerged individuals often exhibit low contrast, camouflage against coral-rubble backgrounds, and weak boundary information under water-surface disturbance. In particular, key visual cues such as body contours, surface texture, and papillae-like structures can be severely blurred in aerial images, limiting the reliability of automated recognition. abstract: Abstract Summer monsoon rainfall over India, vital for the socio-economic welfare of more than a billion people, exhibits large interannual variability. The sea surface temperatures of the Pacific and Indian oceans have been identified as the two most dominant factors affecting the seasonal rainfall over India. However, the combined influence of these two oceans, especially during the last several warming decades, is not well understood. abstract: Creating high-precision bathymetric models continues to be a major challenge, especially in complex environments where numerous factors restrict data gathering. To address these issues, this study introduces and evaluates a weighted average data fusion method. The approach was implemented during a comprehensive measurement campaign, in which weights were assigned to each dataset according to its estimated accuracy. title: Using 210Pb and related proxies to decode event-driven sedimentation in shelf environments: The Laptev Sea case study
abstract: The reliability of 210 Pb dating relies on the assumption of continuous sediment accumulation, which may not hold in dynamic environments. This study assesses its applicability in sediment cores from the Laptev Sea shelf and compares the results with cores from the East/Japan Sea under more stable conditions, using literature data. title: Species-specific phenological indicators reveal topographic–climatic associations with evergreen-tree phenology in subtropical hilly regions
abstract: Evergreen-tree phenology is an important ecological indicator of forest responses to climate change and local environmental heterogeneity. In subtropical hilly regions, frequent cloudy and rainy conditions, complex terrain, and weak seasonal greenness signals hinder species-level phenological retrieval and interpretation. Here, we evaluated the ecological indicator value of the start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and length of season (LOS) for eight representative evergreen tree species in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. title: Improved low-noise waveform feature purification processing for low-signal-to-noise ratio sub-bottom profile data and its application in marine placer exploration
abstract: Sub-bottom profile (SBP) measurement is a widely used hydroacoustic geophysical method for continuous imaging of submarine stratigraphy. Conventional processing pipelines rely on basic filtering and envelope extraction, which fail to handle field data with waveform clipping, repeated navigation coordinates, and heavy background noise. Existing commercial seismic software and published algorithms are mainly designed for conventional seismic data and lack customized processing frameworks adapted to high-frequency SBP signals with instrument-specific distortions. Strong Fully Reprocessable Engineered Wood Composites
abstract: Developing fully reprocessable engineered wood composites (EWCs) with high mechanical strength under mild fabrication conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, a hyperbranched adhesive with complementary imine-bond and hydrogen-bond networks was designed and combined with wood particles to fabricate a wood composite (WP/HTP) by hot pressing at 120°C. title: Development of a Towing System Design Program Based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual
abstract: Marine towing is required for transporting ships and floating structures and for salvage operations of damaged vessels. Safe towing operations require the estimation of towing resistance, selection of an appropriate tug and towing equipment, and verification of the towing system. However, the design procedure based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual involves repeated manual calculations using tables, curves, and empirical criteria, which can be time-consuming and prone to reading errors. title: Multiobjective Optimization of Cross-Flow Membrane Channel Geometry via Integrated CFD Modeling and RSM-Desirability Function Analysis
abstract: Abstract Pressure-driven membrane separation processes are pivotal for seawater desalination and wastewater recovery. However, the geometric configuration of the flow channel strongly influences mass-transfer performance and energy consumption. title: A new piece in the puzzle: The palaeoecological significance of bryozoans over 7000 years in Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan)
abstract: ABSTRACT Submarine caves are cryptic, climatically sensitive habitats with long‐term ecological dynamics that are poorly understood. We present the first palaeoecological analysis of bryozoans from Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan), based on a sediment core spanning approximately the last 7000 years. abstract: The methods used in monitoring the increasing drought are vitally significant. In order to determine and monitor drought, many scientific studies have been carried out in our country, especially using the standardized precipitation index (SPI). abstract: Migration into Sahul is one of the earliest migrations which required open-sea voyages. Two primary routes from Sunda-the northern and southern routes-have been proposed, yet the details of human dispersal into and within Sahul remain unclear. title: Institutional Strengthening of Mama-Mama Papua in the Development of Ikan Asar Businesses Based on Local Resources: A Study of the Kampung Bright Gas Program in Imbi Village, Jayapura
abstract: Ikan asar (smoke fish) processing industry is one of the growing local economic sectors in the coastal area of Dok 8, Imbi Village, Jayapura City. For the local community, particularly coastal women known as the “Mama-Mama Papua,” smoked fish holds not only economic value but also serves as a distinctive feature of the local community, representing food processing knowledge passed down through generations and forming an integral part of the social and cultural life of the coastal community. title: Enabling global prediction of marsh vegetation survival during extreme storms
abstract: Flood protection by coastal vegetated systems depends on the persistence of vegetation structures, but it is currently impossible to predict vegetation survival during extreme storms. Using the largest artificially generated waves in the world, we here quantified the persistence of tidal marsh vegetation by measuring stem breakage of winter-state vegetation (3 species and mimics) during extreme storms with up to 2.0 m significant wave height, 4 m water level and 8 s peak period waves. title: Inside or out? Modeling climate effects on western Atlantic bluefin tuna distribution
abstract: The rapidly changing ocean environment is driving shifts in fish distribution, fishing effort, catch, and catch rates. Previous assessments of western Atlantic bluefin tuna have struggled to reconcile conflicting trends in US and Canadian catch per unit effort (CPUE) indices in the northwest Atlantic, likely due to changes in bluefin distribution in recent decades. title: Super Warm Early Eocene Simulations With HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL
abstract: Abstract The early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO; 53.3–49.1 million years ago) represents the period of greatest sustained warmth in the Cenozoic (last 66 million years), with proxy‐data indicating global‐mean temperatures 10–16°C above preindustrial and atmospheric concentrations of 1,200–2,500 ppmv. This extreme greenhouse climate provides insights into Earth's climate sensitivity and feedback mechanisms and offers a stress‐test for evaluating climate models under vastly different boundary conditions. Here we present the first application of the HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL model to the super‐warm EECO.

title: Study on the Preparation and Properties of Polypropylene Cable Insulation Material Modified With Cycloolefin Copolymer
abstract: ABSTRACT Polypropylene (PP) is a promising recyclable cable‐insulation material, but its poor low‐temperature toughness limits application in cold regions. In this work, cycloolefin copolymer (COC) was introduced into PP by melt blending, with maleic anhydride‐grafted polypropylene (PP‐g‐MAH) used as a compatibilizer, to improve mechanical toughness while maintaining favorable dielectric performance. title: Educating character, difference and the “great questions” curriculum
abstract: Purpose This article examines difference in interdisciplinary character education programs in higher, secondary and elementary education. Such successful “classical education” curricula focus on “Great Books” or “classics,” but their canon-based approaches have drawn criticism for difficulties with incorporating difference. The innovative, inquiry-driven “Great Questions” curriculum of Villanova University's Humanities major represents a “classical” approach that remains grounded within its formative Augustinian tradition while reflectively opening to noncanonical texts. title: Sai số nội suy hình học và khoảng cách tuyến trong khảo sát địa hình đáy
abstract: Khảo sát địa hình đáy là cơ sở quan trọng cho thiết kế và khai thác các công trình hàng hải. title: Lubricant-Engine Suitability Evaluation for Fuel Efficiency in Fishing VesselUsing Temperature and Color Degradation
abstract: Engine performance in fishing vessel depends on the reliability and efficiency of diesel engine, in which the lubrication system plays a key role in reducing friction, controlling operating temperature, and minimizing component wear. However, field observations in small-scale fisheries indicate that many fishermen select lubricants based on habit, price, or availability rather than manufacturer specifications, which may reduce engine efficiency and increase fuel consumption. title: PHOTOCHEMICAL DEGRADATION PATHWAYS OF LINEAR LOW DENSITY POLYETHYLENE REVEALED BY INTEGRATED FTIR, RAMAN, AND AI-ASSISTED SEM ANALYSIS
abstract: Linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) is the dominant polymer in agricultural films, mulch covers, and packaging throughout Ecuador and Latin America, where intensive agricultural economies drive high per-capita consumption. Its prolonged outdoor use under intense equatorial UV radiation accelerates photooxidative degradation, generating microplastic particles that have been detected in remote ecosystems including the Antarctic region, underscoring the global reach of local plastic degradation. title: Brief communication: Mass balance of glaciers in the Eastern Hindu Kush from 1979 to 2002 using KH-9 panoramic and SPOT-5 stereo imagery
abstract: Abstract. Glaciers exhibit region-specific mass loss patterns in response to ongoing climate change. In this study, we provide a geodetic mass balance assessment for glaciers within the Hindu Kush region spanning the period 1979–2002, utilizing KH-9 panoramic imagery and SPOT-5 stereo satellite imagery. Our analysis reveals a moderate mass loss of −0.13 ± 0.12 m w.e. a−1, a rate similar to post-2000 observations given their uncertainties. title: eDNA metabarcoding reveals invertebrate diversity in the blackwater pools of southeast Queensland peatlands
abstract: Despite harbouring a disproportionate diversity of rare and endemic species, the pyrophilic peatlands of southeast Queensland remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding their invertebrate communities. In the physically and chemically extreme blackwater pools, meiofaunal assemblages likely form critical trophic links but have never been described due to their small size and low public profile. title: Fossil flora and palaeoclimate of the Upper Cretaceous Horseshoe Canyon Formation, Horsethief Member, at Morrin Bridge, Alberta, Canada
abstract: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation in southern Alberta, Canada, preserves abundant plant fossils from the upper Campanian to upper Maastrichtian. However, studies describing the macroflora are taxonomically out of date, and limited work has been done to utilise the flora for palaeoclimatic reconstruction. Fifty-eight plant taxa are documented from the Morrin Bridge locality within the lower Maastrichtian Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. title: Relationship between land-use change and flow patterns: a duration curve analysis in the Babahoyo River basin, Ecuador
abstract: Anthropogenic land use and land cover changes alter watershed hydrological processes by modifying the partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff. This study aimed to analyze the relationship between land-use change and flow regime in three sub-basins of the Babahoyo River basin, Ecuador, by using flow duration curves, Mann-Kendall test and Runoff coefficient: Zapotal (2,980 km 2 ), Echeandia (382 km 2 ), and San Pablo (1,387 km 2 ). title: Necessity or Indulgence: Reconsidering Space Exploration
abstract: Taking the debate over whether space exploration constitutes a necessity or a mere indulgence as its starting point, this essay adopts a philosophical and interdisciplinary perspective to re-examine the value of human space activities inspired by the Pale Blue Dot photograph. The study breaks down the binary opposition between necessity and indulgence, arguing that this distinction is not purely economic but hinges on definitions of resource purposes and human civilisational goals. title: 3D crustal seismic structure of southern mainland Portugal from combined local earthquake and active source tomography
abstract: Summary We present P- and S-wave seismic tomographic models for southern mainland Portugal, specifically for the region south of the 39° N parallel. These models were obtained using local seismicity and wide-angle refracted and reflected seismic profiles, considering a spatial resolution of approximately 10 km in latitude and longitude, and 3 km in depth, the highest spatial resolution so far compared to previous models of similar or broader regional scope. The aim is to improve the understanding of continental seismicity and to correlate seismic heterogeneities with crustal tectonic structure

title: MONKI: a three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulator for transfer of polarised light in planetary atmospheres
abstract: Abstract. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool for characterising planetary atmospheres and surfaces. For the design and operation of spectro(polari)metric instrumentation, numerically simulated signals of the measured radiation are essential. Here we present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an efficient and accurate radiative transfer code written in Fortran, based on the Monte Carlo method. MONKI computes both total and polarised radiances reflected and transmitted by a planetary atmosphere, fully accounting for the polarisation of light in all orders of scattering. title: A dual role of precipitation amount and temperature determines precipitation isotopic trends in Southeast Alaska
abstract: Southeast Alaska is one of the wettest places in the world, with some locations within the region receiving upwards of 6 metres of precipitation annually. Given the region's abundant precipitation, it is important to understand the mechanisms controlling the hydrologic cycle to better constrain past and future trends in climate. Accomplishing this requires the evaluation of isotopes in precipitation, as this is key to untangling the many drivers of the water cycle. journal: Isotopes in Environmental and Health Studies

title: In-flight receiver calibration of the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) by passive Earth observations
abstract: Abstract. Post-launch characterization of the receiver telescope of the laser altimeter is essential for achieving precise georeferenced planetary measurements and for radiometric calibration to passively measure surface reflectance. For the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) aboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), such in-flight calibration was originally planned during a lunar flyby but could not be performed due to an unexpected reboot of the instrument. title: Entanglement and apparent thermality in simulated black holes
abstract: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. Nevertheless, we show that a bipartition across the event horizon yields a reduced density matrix whose mode occupations follow an apparent thermal Fermi-Dirac distribution. title: SUSTAINABLE CONSTRUCTION PRACTICES FOR REDUCING ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS IN METRO RAIL DEVELOPMENT

title: Flyway-scale migration phenology identifies mismatches between migration timing and European hunting regulations
abstract: The study of bird migration timing is pivotal for the identification of the onset of pre-breeding migration, when, according to the European regulatory framework, the hunting seasons should end following Article 7.4 of the EU Birds Directive. Member States may use different data sources, including citizen science platforms, to determine this onset. Here, we used data from eBird, a citizen science platform, to describe the timing of pre- and post-breeding migration of the Song Thrush (Turdus philomelos) across the Western Palearctic. For EU Member States, we compared the onset dates of pre-bree

Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior

title: Improved assessment of in-situ and recoverable resources in brine deposits of the Lithium Triangle: A geostatistical perspective
abstract: Continental brine deposits hosted in salar-type systems of the Central Andean Lithium Triangle (Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile) account for more than 60% of known global lithium resources, making the accurate spatial characterization of lithium concentration a matter of paramount importance for resource evaluation and investment decision-making. title: Metastable and Stable States in Covalent Organic Frameworks Controlled by Synthetic Selection Pressure
abstract: The synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has long followed a thermodynamics-driven approach, aiming to obtain highly ordered stable crystalline materials while overlooking metastable structures with unique dynamic characteristics. Inspired by the biological concept of "selection pressure," we propose that the harshness of synthetic conditions serves as a key selection pressure governing the final state of COFs. title: Findings on the efficacy of sonic debridement in chronic wound management – a case series
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the physiological rationale, mechanism of action, and emerging clinical evidence supporting sonic debridement as an adjunctive approach for wound hygiene and maintenance debridement in chronic wound management. METHODS: A structured review of wound healing principles, biofilm biology, and current debridement modalities was performed alongside analysis of clinical observations and case series data using a sonic debridement device. title: Análise integrada do comportamento não estacionário de fenómenos hidrológicos extremos: caso de estudo da bacia hidrográfica do rio Muriaé (sudeste do Brasil)
abstract: O estudo analisou o comportamento não estacionário de eventos hidrológicos extremos na bacia do rio Muriaé (8,126 km2, sudeste do Brasil), uma região propensa a inundações fluviais. Foi utilizada uma metodologia que combina a técnica das séries de picos acima de um limiar, POT (do inglês Peaks Over Threshold), e a estimativa da taxa de ocorrência por Kernel (KORE). Comparativamente à série de máximos anuais, a POT permite selecionar múltiplos eventos extremos por ano, resultando em amostras com maior número de elementos, logo, mais representativas do fenómeno em estudo. title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or ‘mountain’ - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Which One Tastes Better? Testing Distinct Baits to Evaluate Fruit‐Feeding Butterfly Assemblages (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in a Subtropical Region
abstract: ABSTRACT Standardised sampling protocols are essential for improving biodiversity assessments, particularly for indicator groups such as fruit‐feeding butterflies. Although fermented banana is the most widely used bait in tropical regions, rotten fish is the best bait for catching fruit‐feeding butterflies in high‐altitude sites. Few studies have evaluated the effectiveness of alternative attractants in the subtropical region worldwide, where environmental conditions and resource availability differ markedly. We tested the effectiveness of two bait types, fermented banana with sugarcane juice
institutions: Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora
