title: An analytical model for rotors in confined flow across operating regimes
abstract: Rotors operating in confined flows, or blockage, are commonly encountered in wind and water tunnels, as well as in shallow or dense deployments of hydrokinetic turbines. Confinement induces a streamwise pressure gradient in the channel, modifying the rotor induction, thrust and power. To account for these effects, physics-based or empirical blockage corrections are used as a transfer function between the dynamics of an object operating in confined and unconfined settings. title: The Promise and Perils of Private Enforcement under EU Law: The Digital Services Act in Context
abstract: Abstract This article offers a conceptual account of private enforcement under EU law, focusing on the DSA. It argues that the damages action under the DSA derives directly from Union law and cannot be reduced to a declaratory reference to national law. Situated within regulatory theory, it shows how private enforcement may complement public enforcement while raising concerns about access to justice, compliance incentives, and democratic legitimacy. journal: Cambridge yearbook of European legal studies

title: Mechanisms of long-term degradation in plasticized PVDF pressure barriers under offshore service exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is commonly used as a pressure sheath material in offshore flexible pipelines; however, there is limited experimental data from long-term service exposure. In this study, three PVDF layers recovered from a flexible riser after ten years of offshore operation were examined to understand the degradation mechanisms that occurred under field conditions. institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

title: Flow Dynamics with Jet-induced Vortex Control in a Slotted Vertical-axis Wind Turbine
abstract: This study investigates the aerodynamic impact of passive blade slots on the unsteady flow dynamics of a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) operating at low tip speed ratios. A two-dimensional URANS-based numerical investigation using the k–ω SST turbulence model was performed to analyze the creation of slot-induced internal jets and their interaction with the surrounding flow field. title: The Use of Styrofoam as an Innovative Building Component in Calabar, Cross River State: Implications for Sustainable Architectural Practice
abstract: The persistent housing deficit, indoor thermal discomfort, and rising energy demand in Nigeria’s humid-tropical climate have triggered a search for innovative building components that advance energy efficiency and sustainability in the construction industry. In Calabar, Cross River State, where rapid urbanization and informal construction patterns coexist with climatic vulnerability, the adoption of expanded polystyrene (EPS), commonly known as Styrofoam, as an architectural component remains under-explored, particularly in walling, insulation, and prefabricated systems. title: Assessing earthquake potential and fault activity from a newly estimated high-resolution geodetic velocity field in Hispaniola
abstract: Abstract The transpressive plate boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates in Hispaniola is a complex system of strike-slip faults, subduction zones, fold-and-thrust belts, and normal faulting. Tectonic deformation studies in this region have traditionally relied on sparse Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks. Here we present a new assessment of deformation in Hispaniola using a dense 3D velocity field generated by integrating existing GNSS observations with new Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) velocities. title: Improved desalination by polymer grafting
abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionisation (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilisation. Here, we show that suitably chosen polyampholytic block copolymer grafting can substantially enhance CDI performance, via a combination of dipolar response and steric effects. title: Beyond the trail: how tourist access shapes mammal activity in a highly visited national park in Costa Rica
abstract: Introduction: Ecotourism can alter wildlife behavior without affecting species diversity, but this is a poorly known subject. Objective: To evaluate the influence of tourist access on medium- and large-bodied mammals in Manuel Antonio National Park, Costa Rica. Methods: From April 2021 to August 2022, camera traps monitored mammals along public trails during periods of restricted and unrestricted tourist access associated with COVID-19 policies and weekly closures. title: Life-cycle incremental cost-benefit model for passive buildings and a case study in Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. title: 10-kHz coherent anti-stokes Raman spectroscopy thermometry in an arc heater

title: Cellulose-based bioplastics for a circular bioeconomy: Properties, applications, market potential, consumer acceptance, and future perspectives
abstract: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. title: Rural place leadership across the Anglo-Scottish border: analysing the evolution, resilience and success of the Borderlands partnership
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership, a cross-border initiative seeking to address common challenges in the Anglo-Scottish rural periphery. Utilising a path-tracing methodology, a timeline was constructed to identify key events in the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership which created opportunity spaces for institutional entrepreneurship and generative place leadership. title: Forward self-similar solutions to the MHD-Boussinesq system with Newtonian gravitational field
abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence of forward self-similar solutions to the three-dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic-Boussinesq (MHD-Boussinesq) system with a Newtonian gravitational field. By employing a blow-up argument and the Leray-Schauder theorem, we construct a forward self-similar solution to this system without imposing any smallness assumptions on the self-similar initial value.
journal: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications

title: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
abstract: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. Here, we introduce a climate-feedback into an IO system via the crop sector to illustrate the potential couplings between climate change and material and economic flows. title: Recharge Performance of Pond-Based Managed Aquifer Recharge in the Ramganga Basin
abstract: Groundwater underpins India's water and food security but faces growing stress from overexploitation and climate change. This study evaluates the hydrologic performance of small-scale, pond-based Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) interventions implemented under government development programs, in the context of India's plan to construct 14 million additional recharge structures. Focusing on the groundwater-stressed Ramganga basin, the study draws on three years of participatory monitoring of 23 recharge structures. title: Association of Long-Term Residentially Assigned Speciated Atmospheric Mercury Emission Flux with All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality
abstract: Abstract Mercury (Hg) is a persistent global pollutant, but population evidence on residentially assigned species-specific atmospheric Hg emission flux and mortality is limited. We analyzed UK Biobank cohorts for all-cause/other-cause (N = 322,666), cardiovascular disease (N = 344,333), and cancer mortality (N = 381,432). Annual EDGAR v8.1 fluxes of total Hg, gaseous elemental Hg (Hg0), gaseous oxidized Hg (Hg2+), and particle-bound Hg (Hg–P) were assigned to geocoded residences. title: Between Custom and Sanction: Theft in the Vinodol Code and the Poljica Statute
abstract: This paper addresses the regulation of theft as an illicit act in two major medieval Croatian legal monuments: the Vinodol Code (1288) and the Statute of Poljica. Rather than offering a systematic comparison of legal systems, the study concentrates on the legal nature, normative structure, and penal treatment of theft within these statutory frameworks, situating the offence in its broader social and institutional context. title: The effects of asynchronous interruption on arc motion characteristics of a triple‑break medium-voltage DC air circuit breaker
abstract: Abstract Multi‑break DC air circuit breakers are subject to asynchronous interruption due to dispersion of operating mechanisms, resulting in nonuniform transient voltage distribution among the breaks and thereby compromising interruption reliability. A controllable two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-external circuit coupled model is established for a 9 kV/100 kA triple-break DC air circuit breaker composed of three series-connected independent arc chambers. title: Techno-economic comparison of fossil, renewable-carbon and recycling pathways for polypropylene
abstract: Polypropylene production relies predominantly on fossil resources for process energy and carbon feedstock. This study compares fossil primary production, renewable-carbon primary routes based on biomass, renewable hydrocarbons, or CO2 and hydrogen, and recycling pathways under German industrial cost conditions within the European carbon-pricing framework. Literature-based process data are harmonised to a functional unit of 1 tonne of polypropylene pellets at the plant gate. title: Selection and characterization of rhizobacteria from cocoa soils in Ecuador with potential for cadmium mitigation

title: H–D Exchange in Ultraviolet-irradiated Water: Methane Ice Mixtures
abstract: Abstract The deuterium-to-hydrogen (D/H) ratio in solar system volatiles is commonly used to diagnose volatile formation conditions. This ratio may be altered by a range of processes under solar nebula conditions, however, including energetic processing of icy grains. In this study, we investigate the effects of ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on the H/D exchange in mixed methane–water ices, a model system for water and organics ice mixtures. title: DYNAMIC ANALYSIS OF FLUID-CONVEYING CARBON NANOPIPES USING A NOVEL SPECTRAL ELEMENT FORMULATION
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of fluid-conveying double-walled carbon nanotubes (DWCNTs) is important in nanoscale fluid-transport systems because fluid–structure interaction, interwall forces, size-dependent effects and environmental loading can significantly influence their vibration characteristics. Therefore, this paper aims to control the dynamic vibration of flowing fluid through DWCNT systems to enhance their integrity and reliability. title: Environmental Perception and Intelligent Navigation for Autonomous Delivery Robots in Complex Scenarios
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) face perception and navigation challenges in complex scenarios. When operating in real world urban environments, ADRs have trouble negotiating upturned streets, uneven terrain, and moving obstacles. This review covers three key areas: environmental perception, navigation techniques, and mechanical adaptability of delivery vehicles. The reviewed studies show that navigation has evolved beyond avoiding obstacles, to its current state of considering whether the ground can be traversed. title: Thermal resilience under climate extremes: simulation-based assessment of heatwave impacts in informal buildings in Cairo
abstract: Abstract Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves. Informal settlements are particularly vulnerable to heat stress due to inadequate housing conditions and socioeconomic constraints. In Egypt, informal housing accounts for 38.6% of the national housing stock, yet the risk of indoor heat stress remains underexplored. This study proposes a quantitative method to identify and classify heatwaves in Cairo and assess their impact on indoor overheating and heat-stress risk. Heatwave characteristics were analyzed for historical (2010–2024) and futur
journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: Pazy-winged aircraft aeroelastic control benchmark: An open simulator
abstract: A hierarchical nonlinear control benchmark is presented for gust load alleviation (GLA) and maneuver load alleviation (MLA) in a highly flexible winged UAV. The benchmark utilizes a reduced-order nonlinear aeroelastic model, which has been shown to be suitable for real-time control. This work builds on an existing moving-horizon estimation (MHE) and model predictive control (MPC) strategy for flexible aircraft stabilization by building a control framework designed for a wider range of aggressive movements in turbulent environments. title: Improved seasonal hydrological forecasting for Great Britain
abstract: Abstract. Great Britain’s variable maritime climate has until relatively recently limited the utility of seasonal hydrological forecasts. The latest generations of seasonal atmospheric forecasting systems have created new opportunities to improve flow forecasting across Great Britain, such as for the UK Hydrological Outlook. Here, newly-developed high-resolution rainfall forecasts derived from historical weather analogues (HWA) conditioned on large-scale circulation patterns are used to drive a monthly-resolution national-scale hydrological model. title: Complex-valued modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation
abstract: Motivated by the introduction of the Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation as a higher dimensional generalization of the Korteweg-de Vries equation, in this paper we introduce the modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov (mZK) equation as a 2-dimensional generalization of the complex-valued modified Korteweg-de Vries equation. We initiate the mathematical analysis of the mZK equation on $ \mathbb{T}^2 $ by proving a local well-posedness result in Sobolev spaces and by establishing a failure of uniform continuity. We also note that the real-valued version of the mZK equation has physical significance.

title: The adaptability of seed drills in modern crop production technologies
abstract: The relevance of this study stems from the fact that the transition of farms from traditional tillage to minimum and no-till techniques requires seed drills capable of operating consistently under varying conditions of crop residue, soil moisture and field micro-relief. A lack of alignment between the design of the seed drill and the cultivation technology leads to uneven seed placement, excessive fuel consumption and increased costs for renewing the machinery and tractor fleet. title: Apparent ecological network expansion masks structural reorganization and corridor vulnerability in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization is reorganizing landscape connectivity, yet whether increases in ecological sources or corridors actually represent stronger regional networks remains unclear. Using three representative time slices (2013, 2018, and 2023) in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration, China, we integrated InVEST–MSPA, Conefor, circuit theory, complex-network analysis, Louvain community detection, and edge collective influence (ECI) to examine stage-specific network reorganization and corridor vulnerability. title: ENHANCING SOIL PROPERTIES AND CAPSICUM (CAPSICUM ANNUUM VAR. GROSSUM L.) PRODUCTIVITY THROUGH THE APPLICATION OF RICE STRAW-DERIVED BIOCHAR
abstract: Capsicum, often known as sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum var. grossum L.), is becoming more and more popular in Bangladesh as a vegetable. However, a number of obstacles must be overcome for its production to occur, such as limited cation exchange capacity, poor soil fertility, fast mineralization of soil organic matter, and acidity of the soil. These problems are addressed by applying biochar, a carbon-rich biomass made by pyrolysis under low or no oxygen conditions, as a soil amendment. title: An improved yaw attitude model for GPS Block IIF satellites during eclipse seasons
abstract: Abstract This study improves the operational eclipse-season yaw attitude model for Global Positioning System (GPS) Block IIF satellites by using Reverse Kinematic Precise Point Positioning (RKPPP) yaw estimates as an observation-driven reference. Using a 7.5-year global GPS tracking dataset, we reconstruct yaw attitude time series over eclipse season maneuvers and compare them with the current operational attitude model. abstract: Hybrid design approaches are essential for developing porous lattice structures with integrated multifunctional performance. While previous studies have focused on hybridization among different topologies, combining distinct structure types-such as integrating the high mechanical strength of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) sheet structures with the meta-structural characteristics of strut-based architectures-remains underexplored due to challenges in creating effective connections between these disparate forms. title: From forest to farmland: seasonal habitat suitability and risk areas of human–elephant conflict in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) of Thailand
abstract: The Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) is currently undergoing drastic economic income development and some of the most rapid landuse changes in Thailand. This area is also amongst the highest for human–elephant conflict (HEC) especially around the Eastern Forest Complex (EFCOM). Studies regarding ecological risks to the wild Asian elephant ( Elephas maximus ) and the population’s impact on human well-being in the area are limited. abstract: ABSTRACT Phase‐change metasurfaces have attracted significant attention for reconfigurable photonic devices owing to their ability to tune optical responses between amorphous and crystalline phases. Despite their potential in optical switching, communications, and signal processing, achieving large optical modulation while maintaining low optical loss and strong field confinement remains a major challenge. title: Performance degradation and failure mechanisms of pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid sucker rods after long-term downhole service
abstract: Pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid composite rods are increasingly used as sucker rods, yet the relationship between degradation accumulated during long-term downhole service and subsequent longitudinal splitting during retrieval and drum winding remains insufficiently understood, particularly for rods containing a carbon/glass hybrid transition region. This study compared five specimens sectioned from a pristine 22 mm-diameter parent rod with five specimens sectioned from a service-aged parent rod retrieved after 435 days of actual downhole service. title: Blue‒green water demand, water footprint, and productivity: an experimental study for effective agricultural water management in a semi-arid area of southern Ethiopia
abstract: Water scarcity constrains agricultural production in semi-arid regions and particularly affects water-sensitive crops such as haricot bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.). Although supplemental irrigation is widely promoted in these environments, the partitioning of haricot bean water use into green (rainfall) and blue (irrigation) components has not been quantified for southern Ethiopia, and this partition determines how far the crop draws on contested dry-season water sources. A field experiment was conducted at Ambara, Arba Minch Zuria Woreda, in a randomized complete block design with six stage-s

title: Beyond wind-sector management: optimal wind farm operational planning for balancing fatigue damage and extending lifetime
abstract: Abstract. We present an optimization framework for long‑term wind farm operation that balances fatigue loads and energy yield to extend turbine and farm lifetime. The approach plans per‑turbine derating setpoints for discrete wind conditions using an engineering wake model and surrogate models for power and damage. We formulate the problem as a nonlinear program and solve it either for the full farm in a single run or iteratively per turbine. title: Signatures of photospheric convection throughout the solar atmosphere: the EVE Sun-as-a-star mHz continuum
abstract: Abstract Convectively driven motions in the solar photosphere can generate broadband Doppler variability across the chromosphere, transition region and corona. Here we investigate this variability using “Sun-as-a-Star” observations from the Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment (EVE) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory, constructing high signal-to-noise Doppler power spectra by incoherently averaging spectra from 3-hour sequences of the centroid wavelengths of emission lines that span wavelengths 35–104 nm. The spectra reveal a broad power-spectral continuum with two “Harvey” components

title: Urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites integrated with beneficial microbes enhance nutrient uptake and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Low nitrogen use efficiency of prilled urea contributes to substantial economic loss and environmental pollution through leaching, denitrification, and ammonia volatilization. This study evaluated urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites (NCBPCs), synthesized from clay-acrylic acid + aczrylamide-based polymer composite grafted with maize flour (NCBPC-M) and mango kernel flour (NCBPC-MK), integrated with phosphorus- and zinc-solubilizing bacteria ( Lactococcus lactis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ), as a sustainable alternative nitrogen source in a maize–wheat cropping system. title: Wave-induced erosion and notch development at the Fimbul Ice Shelf front
abstract: Abstract. Ocean waves erode the waterline of Antarctic ice-shelf fronts and carve a thermo-erosional notch. The notch is hidden from satellites, yet it preconditions front collapse and footloose calving, so the link between notch growth and observable front retreat matters for how wave-exposed ice shelves lose mass. We study this link at the Fimbul Ice Shelf, East Antarctica, in January–February 2024. The widely used White et al. title: Distributed Observation Scheduling and Sensor Fusion For Large Agile Constellations
abstract: With the rapid increase in interest towards large scale earth observing satellite constellations, the problem of properly commanding and utilizing these systems has become increasingly relevant. This work focuses on a complete distributed approach to this problem, incorporating an observation task allocation and scheduling algorithm in addition to a sensor data fusion algorithm for end-to-end target coverage and processing. title: Tame Discrete Sets on Affine Semisimple Homogeneous Spaces
abstract: Winkelmann conjectures that every smooth flexible complex affine variety of dimension at least two is a Rosay--Rudin space. We verify this for every positive-dimensional quotient $G/H$ with $G$ a connected complex semisimple algebraic group and $H$ a closed connected reductive subgroup. Weak and strong tameness coincide, every injection between tame discrete sets extends to a holomorphic automorphism, and complements of tame, finite, or empty sets are Oka. title: Gen-EBM: an energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that depend sensitively on climate feedbacks. We introduce the Geneva Energy Balance Model (Gen-EBM), a new 1-D latitudinal EBM for rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. title: Global Well-Posedness and Persistence of H2 Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Primitive Equations with Horizontal and Topography-Adapted Thermal Diffusion
abstract: We study the three-dimensional primitive equations with full viscosity and horizontal thermal diffusion in bounded domains. We establish global well-posedness for admissible $H^1$ initial data and persistence of $H^2$ regularity on the flat-bottom cylinder. The higher regularity analysis combines fractional hydrostatic Stokes regularity with anisotropic estimates of the vertical transport. title: Global well-posedness for the 2D primitive equations with subcritical horizontal dissipation
abstract: We establish global well-posedness of classical solutions to the two-dimensional primitive equations with fractional horizontal dissipation for arbitrarily large initial data in the full subcritical range $1<α\leq2$. Together with the known ill-posedness results for $0\leqα<1$, this establishes the sharp dissipation threshold for large-data global well-posedness in the corresponding solution framework. title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
abstract: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break. title: Global stability and sharp decay for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without thermal diffusion
abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with positive horizontal and vertical viscosity and without thermal diffusion. Our main results are fourfold. First, for every integer \(s\ge4\), we prove that sufficiently small, compatible, doubly periodic \(H^s\) perturbations of a stably stratified rest state with an affine temperature profile generate unique global strong solutions; the horizontal velocity and temperature remain uniformly small at the initial Sobolev order despite the derivative loss in the full diagnostic vertical velocity, and strict stratification persists.

title: Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
abstract: We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. title: Global regularity and infinite Prandtl-number limit for 2D Boussinesq temperature patches in $W^{k,\infty}$ and $C^{k,γ}$: lower-order case
abstract: We study global regularity and the infinite Prandtl number limit for temperature patches of the two-dimensional nondiffusive Boussinesq system on $\mathbb R^2$, with velocity dissipation $Λ^{2α}$, $\frac12<α\leq1$. We establish global well-posedness for $θ_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty$ and divergence-free $u_0\in W^{1,p}$, $2\leq p<\infty$. Under suitable profile and striated regularity assumptions, we prove global persistence of $C^{1,γ}$ and $C^{2,γ}$ patch boundaries for every $0<γ\leq1$, allowing nonconstant profiles and including the Lipschitz endpoints $W^{2,\infty}$ and $W^{3,\infty}$. title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
abstract: Cloud droplets respond to turbulent motion with finite inertia and settle under gravity, while condensation and evaporation change their sizes. The nonuniform accumulation of cloud droplets in turbulent flows, known as preferential concentration, has attracted sustained interest because it affects droplet collision and coalescence rates. We develop an analytical theory that quantifies the coupled effects of droplet inertia, gravitational settling, and phase change on concentration changes. title: Model-Order-Adaptive Channel Estimation for AFDM Systems with Fractional Delay and Doppler
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility communications owing to its ability to exploit multipath diversity. However, channel state information (CSI) acquisition remains challenging in channels with fractional delay and Doppler and an unknown number of propagation paths. In this paper, we investigate the channel estimation for AFDM systems. We first analyze the AFDM response in the presence of fractional-delay-induced frequency wrapping. title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. title: Spectral gap for the stochastic primitive equations under degenerate Brownian forcing
abstract: We prove a weighted Wasserstein spectral gap for the three-dimensional primitive equations on $\mathscr E=\{u\in H^1\cap L^8: \partial_zu\in L^4\}$ under finite-rank additive Brownian forcing that is phase-complete finite Fourier and satisfies a quantitative quadratic saturation condition. In particular, four real forcing directions suffice and this number is optimal within the phase-complete class. title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. title: MUNITE: Unified Multimodal Latent Inference for Any-to-Any Multimodal Generation
abstract: We introduce MUNITE, a latent-variable framework for flexible any-to-any multimodal generation that treats encoding and latent generation as the same inference problem under different amounts of observed evidence. Given any subset of modalities, MUNITE models the conditional distribution over the latent representation associated with the complete observation. title: Instantaneous gap loss of Sobolev regularity for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation
abstract: We prove instantaneous loss of Sobolev regularity across a fixed gap for the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic equation on $\mathbb R^2$. title: A Fully Discrete, Mass-Conservative Adaptive Discontinuous Spectral-Element Method for the One-Dimensional Richards Equation in Mixed Form
abstract: We present and analyze a spatially and temporally adaptive high-order method for the one-dimensional Richards equation describing vertical water transport in unsaturated soil, with an emphasis on resolving sharp wetting fronts while satisfying a fully discrete water mass balance. The spatial discretization uses an arbitrary-order local discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element formulation with collocated Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, and the time integration is based on a high-order Rosenbrock-Wanner method. title: Enhanced analogue quantum computation with a logically-encoded XX gadget
abstract: The introduction of two-body XX interactions has been shown to improve the performance of quantum annealing in solving certain combinatorial optimisation problems and would enable the simulation of a broader class of many-body Hamiltonians. Due to experimental constraints, such interactions are typically not natively available on analogue quantum devices. To overcome this limitation we introduce the truss gadget. title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
abstract: This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. title: Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
abstract: We present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3D numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. Each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the González-Guzmán-Sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. title: Optimal Gating for Dead-Time-Constrained Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: We develop a Fisher-information framework for optimizing single-photon detector gating in periodic experiments, in contrast to previous more empirical or heuristic gating choices. After each photon detection, such a detector is insensitive for a dead time, so that an early background detection can obscure a later signal. Gating preserves availability for informative photons by selectively deactivating the detector. title: Multi-scale spectral statistics of intermediate quantum chaos in ultracold erbium collisions
abstract: Characterizing intermediate quantum chaos in systems with mixed phase spaces requires probing spectral correlations across multiple scales. Here, we present a multi-scale statistical analysis of the resonance spectra of ultracold 166Er and 168Er atoms using higher-order spacing ratios, spacing increments, and the accumulated power spectral density of decimated level sequences. title: Event Generation for Neutrino and Muon DIS at the LHC
abstract: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. title: Chinese Botany at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair
abstract: This article examines the Chinese botanical exhibits at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair as part of global knowledge formation within Austro-Hungarian Empire. It argues that these exhibits were not static displays but dynamic objects mediating trade, science, and imperial representation. Drawing on customs records, diplomatic correspondence, exhibition catalogues, and contemporary reports, the study traces their trajectory from collection across treaty ports and Southeast Asia to exhibition and reception in Vienna. Threshold Type Responses of Indo Pacific Coral Reefs to Local Human Induced Degradation
abstract: Coral reef ecosystems face cumulative pressures from ocean warming, ocean acidification and diverse coastal human disturbances. As ecologically critical habitats and socio economic resources for coastal human communities, reef systems require improved understanding of how local anthropogenic activities drive degradation trajectories. Existing monitoring datasets covering the Indo Pacific region provide large scale observational evidence to disentangle reef responses against human related stressors and distinguish threshold driven shifts from gradual dose response decline. title: From Digital Visibility to Completed Purchase in Online Retail
abstract: Online enterprises can buy digital visibility before they have earned confidence in the transaction that follows. This study develops and tests a dual pathway model in which digital promotion shapes purchase intention through attitude, while perceived transaction security operates through trust and post-purchase satisfaction. The model also separates purchase intention from completed-shopping behaviour, allowing the analysis to identify where favourable evaluation fails to become action. title: Governing access: Freedom of information, knowledge politics, and the limits of transparency in public health research
abstract: Introduction Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are presented as mechanisms of transparency and democratic accountability, yet their operation as tools of public health research remains under-examined. This study examines how FOI regimes shape, rather than simply enable, researchers’ access to institutional knowledge across Nigeria, the United Kingdom (UK), and the United States (US).Theory Drawing on governmentality and epistemic injustice, FOI is conceptualized as a site of knowledge governance through which legal exclusions, commercial secrecy, bureaucratic discretion, and institutional prac

title: From emergence to exposure: one health attribution of azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus in Southeast Asia
abstract: Southeast Asia is a hotspot for azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus yet remains underrepresented in global surveillance. Disciplinary approaches, including genomics, environmental sampling, and social science, have progressed but remain poorly integrated. We outline a One Health attribution framework linking selection pressures, environmental reservoirs, exposure pathways, and clinical resistance signals to prioritise surveillance, target interventions, and allocate resources where they will have greatest impact.

title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. title: Data Sharing in Nigerian Genomics: Addressing Legal Fragmentation and Ethical Dilemmas
abstract: This study examined the legal and ethical challenges associated with genomic data sharing in Nigeria with focused on issues of consent, privacy, data ownership and international collaboration. Using doctrinal method, the study reviewed scholarly literature, national policies, institutional practices and international instruments to identify gaps in genomic data sharing. title: Coastal Vegetation as Nature-Based Solutions: A Bibliometric and Proxy Matrix Review of Ecosystem Services and Coastal Protection
abstract: Climate change and coastal development are intensifying coastal hazards and increasing the need for evidence-based Nature-based Solutions (NbSs) in integrated coastal zone management. However, proxy-based evidence for evaluating the ecosystem services and coastal protection functions of coastal vegetation has not been systematically synthesized across these dimensions. title: Current gender equality status in EU blue economy – Gaps and recommendations for a more inclusive and fair sector
abstract: Gender equality and the empowerment of women are core priorities of the European Union. However, strategic sectors such as the blue economy remain comparatively underexplored in terms of structural and cultural barriers to female participation with both traditional and emerging industries being still male dominated. Against this backdrop, this paper presents the findings of a systematic review of publications from 2010 to 2024 addressing gender equality issues in the European Union blue economy. title: Implementing Bow-tie analysis to assess the main concerns regarding biodiversity change in European Seas
abstract: Marine biodiversity is adversely affected by many human activities and their pressures. As such, there is the need for a cause-consequence-response method to objectively address the risks associated with those adverse changes. Such a method is the ISO-accredited Bow-tie technique as an objective and structured approach giving the causes, preventative control measures, mitigation and compensation measures and consequences of changes to biodiversity. title: Estimating net fixed nitrogen loss in the Baltic Sea from deep-water excess N2 accumulation
abstract: We quantified excess N2 accumulation below the halocline of the Baltic Proper using in situ N2/Ar measurements combined with N2/Ar estimates derived from the three-dimensional ERGOM–MOM biogeochemical model. The observed temporal increase in excess N2 was subsequently converted to nitrogen loss. title: Marital Status Diversity and Organisational Performance in Star-rated Hotels in Coastal Kenya: A Mixed-methods Study
abstract: This study examined the association between employees’ marital status diversity and their ratings of organisational performance in star-rated hotels in Kenya’s coastal region. A mixed-methods design was adopted, drawing on questionnaire responses from employees and semi-structured interviews with operational managers in 11 hotels in Kilifi, Mombasa and Kwale counties. title: Reforming Institutional Design for Fairness: Evictions from Toronto Community Housing, 2002–2014
abstract: Abstract This article examines institutional safeguards for fairness in rent-arrears evictions from the Toronto Community Housing Corporation (TCHC). It reconstructs the reform sequence that led to the adoption of a novel—possibly unique—institutional mechanism: the Office of the Commissioner for Housing Equity (OCHE), an independent accountability mechanism for procedural fairness in evictions. title: From Regional Deformation to Critical Coastal Infrastructure-Scale Ground Instability Across the Caspian Port Network: Insights from Multi-Temporal Radar Satellite Earth Observation
abstract: The Absheron Peninsula contains a dense network of Caspian ports and industrial terminals where vertical land motion (VLM) may affect infrastructure performance. We analyzed fourteen port-associated coastal analysis zones using ascending and descending Sentinel-1 SBAS-InSAR observations from 2017 to 2024. abstract: Abstract Animal-borne tri-axial accelerometers are increasingly used to investigate animal behaviour and energetics. Critical methodological details, such as device placement and dynamic range, are frequently underreported. This lack of reporting hampers study replicability and interpretation of results. It also complicates comparisons between studies. abstract: Teluk Bintuni Regency is dominated by rivers, estuaries, swamps, and coastal areas, so water transport is the main mode connecting communities across districts. Ethical practices are fundamental principles that guide teachers’ professional conduct, ensuring fairness, integrity, accountability, respect, and responsibility in educational settings. title: The just price: a market-process account
abstract: Abstract When is a price just? This paper develops a new theory of justice in pricing, grounded in the Austrian market process tradition. Prices, I argue, are not merely outcomes to be evaluated against an external standard of fairness. They are instruments through which the competitive process performs morally significant functions: communicating information, generating incentives and coordinating the plans of millions under pervasive ignorance. abstract: We present a comprehensive DNA barcode reference library of invertebrate species samples from chameleon habitats in South Africa. abstract: Abstract The third edition of the Society for Ecological Restoration's International Principles and Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration places recovery of “native ecosystems” at the center of what counts as legitimate ecological restoration. Here I argue that, in the Anthropocene, this emphasis reflects a value‐based choice rather than an ecological inevitability. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Japanese perceptions of the European Union's Indo‐Pacific Strategy through interviews with government officials and foreign policy influencers. Respondents considered the EU to be a highly important actor in the Indo‐Pacific context. Three‐quarters of respondents considered the Indo‐Pacific Strategy document to be sufficiently important that it constitutes an upgrade or a positive transformation of the existing relationship. title: Perceiving Protection: Public Interpretation of Institutions in Managed Flood Settings
abstract: ABSTRACT Floods rank among the most frequent and widely managed hazards worldwide. While considerable research has examined public perceptions of flood risk, less attention has been paid to how people interpret institutional presence, action, and responsibility in flood‐prone settings shaped by infrastructure and governance systems. abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread synthetic contaminants that can accumulate in food, such as chicken eggs. abstract: Irregular migration to Europe by sea, though risky, remains one of the most popular migration options for many Sub-Saharan Africans. This study examines the drivers of irregular migration decisions using an incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment in rural Gambia, the African country with the highest per-capita rate of irregular migration to Europe. abstract: This study aimed to identify and document the ethnic meat products of Borno State, Nigeria, addressing a critical gap in the documentation of Nigeria's intangible culinary heritage. abstract: Abstract. We present a flatfile containing ground-motion intensity measurements from 694 shallow earthquakes. The dataset includes 8,086 three-component acceleration records that were uniformly processed. abstract: Disasters have devastating effects on communities, especially where knowledge and perception are limited, vulnerability is high, and capacity is low. Nigeria has suffered from recurrent flood disasters, with Kaduna State among the affected regions. Household heads are important elements in flood disaster management, and their knowledge and risk perception are crucial. abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is increasingly recognised as an important anthropogenic pressure affecting nocturnal biodiversity, particularly in oceanic islands with high endemism levels. abstract: The primary objective of this study is to explore the role of Blue Accounting in flood disaster mitigation, with a particular focus on addressing persistent gaps in water resource management and fostering transparent, data-driven governance within flood-prone regions. Yet their evaluation often gives less attention to the cultural, educational, and experiential conditions through which ecological functions become publicly understood and maintained. abstract: This study examined ethical leadership, accountability, and transparency in school governance among public elementary schools in Banaybanay District, Division of Davao Oriental, as a basis for governance improvement. title: Accelerated weathering of limestone for CO 2 capture and storage: a critical review of unbuffered, buffered, and modified pathways
abstract: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. abstract: This study focuses on the shade-grown coffee agroforestry system of the Cacahuatique Mountain Range in Ciudad Barrios, El Salvador, a region with a long tradition of coffee cultivation under tree cover. All Salvadoran coffee is produced under shade, a practice that preserves greater biodiversity than sun-grown systems. abstract: Seafaring is a demanding occupation characterized by prolonged periods away from home, long and irregular working hours, physical workload, fatigue, confined living conditions, limited shore leave, and reduced social interaction. These conditions can negatively affect the mental and physical health of seafarers and increase their vulnerability to psychological difficulties. title: How does climate risk affect fisheries? New evidence from the operating cash flows of Chinese listed firms
abstract: Listed fisheries companies depend heavily on natural conditions, leaving their operations particularly exposed to climate change. Using Chinese listed fisheries companies as the research sample, this study examines the effect of regional climate risk on operating cash flow and investigates potential mitigating mechanisms. The results show that regional climate risk significantly reduces operating cash flow. title: The EU challenge to make its ports more sustainable and competitive: The case of the Green Ports Project for the Port of Naples
abstract: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be understood only in terms of logistical performance but must be assessed within a governance model capable of integrating environmental sustainability and territorial resilience. abstract: Chemical weathering plays a pivotal role in the Earth's surface material cycle and global climate regulation. It not only facilitates the reconstruction of palaeoclimate characteristics but also provides essential insights into Earth's evolutionary history. The Rb/Sr ratio has been widely applied in studies of chemical weathering and palaeoclimate reconstruction. However, its effectiveness and applicability remain limited. title: Strategic Pathways for Magnesium–Aluminum‐Layered Double Hydroxides: Multidimensional Footprints of Production Routes
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium–aluminum‐layered double hydroxides (MgAl‐LDHs) are used in flame retardants, remediation, and catalysis. Sustainability comparisons of industrial routes are insufficient. This study couples techno‐economic analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate two routes (hydrothermal synthesis and modification) at 1000 t/a using industrial data. Both yield 99.9% pure products with distinct energy structures: Synthesis consumes more electricity but less gas/water; modification cuts electricity by 33.9% but needs more gas/water for grinding. We employ an observation-based Emergent Constraint (EC) framework to refine future projections of maximum temperature (tasmax), minimum temperature (tasmin), Summer Days (SU), and Ice Days (ID). title: People are good at stewardship
abstract: Abstract Environmental sciences and policy have long been framed on the premise that environmental harm is an expression of human nature rather than a product of specific historical and political arrangements. This framing has shaped a generation of interventions designed to constrain human behaviour rather than enable human capacity. abstract: This study aims to explore the meaning of pantun in the “belatik” art of the Jerieng community in Bangka and connect it with the concept of ecocriticism. The focus is to identify representations of ecological concepts, including pollution, wilderness, apocalypse, dwellings, animals, and the earth. title: Retrieval Quality, Evidence, and Appropriate Abstention in Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can give fluent and useful answers, but they can also produce information that is false or not supported by evidence. This problem is often called hallucination. In this paper, we study how the quality of the evidence retrieved is associated with differences in the answers given by an LLM. abstract: The study focuses on sustainable tourism in small island developing states (SIDS), using resort destinations in the Maldives as a case study. Small island destinations face unique ecological and socio-economic vulnerabilities, making the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework which evaluates environmental, social, and economic sustainability critical to their long-term viability. abstract: Abstract Motivation Debt‐for‐nature swaps (D4NS) have re‐emerged as a potential instrument to address the dual challenges of sovereign‐debt distress and environmental degradation. abstract: The article addresses the complex relationship between the cultural adaptation of migrants and their perception of local traditions. Based on exploratory fieldwork conducted in the summer of 2025 in the Faroe Islands, using 30 in-depth ethnographic narrative interviews, the analysis focuses on how Polish migrants interpret the practice of Grindadráp (traditional pilot whale hunting). title: Sacred forests in space and time: Intangible Cultural Heritage and naturebased solutions
abstract: Sacred forests have a long history of protection and many of them are old-growth forests with centuries old trees important for conservation. Some of these forests can be traced back to lands and territories inhabited for millennia by Indigenous peoples. These sites are considered important in the development of religion and spirituality in our distant ancestors and today their Intangible Cultural Heritage demonstrates a special relationship between people and nature. abstract: According to the “Child Labour Survey” published by TÜİK in 2019, “the number of children between the ages of 5 and 17 who were engaged in economic activity across Türkiye was identified as 720,000”. The fact that 63.3% of these children were employed as wage earners indicates that child labour is not confined solely to the informal sector, but has also reached a considerable level within formal employment. title: Too cool, low, and slow: Camera traps used to determine leopard tortoise occupancy in arid areas of South Africa
abstract: The leopard tortoise (Stigmochelys pardalis) is the only large tortoise in southern Africa and is the most widespread of any sub-Saharan testudinid. However, the population trend of this species is unknown, and it has become increasingly rare outside fenced areas and farmland. Little is known about their behavioural ecology in response to environmental stimuli. Accurate information for quantifying activity patterns, distributions and wildlife behaviour can be obtained using camera traps. title: Sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices, skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among Malaysian national-level outdoor athletes
abstract: Outdoor athletes in equatorial regions are exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation year-round, increasing the risk of cumulative photodamage. However, evidence on sun protection behaviours and personal UVB exposure among athletes in tropical settings remains limited. This study assessed sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP), skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among national-level outdoor athletes in Malaysia. title: Blood companions: the Holocene record of ectoparasites
abstract: Abstract The Holocene fossil record of human and animal ectoparasites comprises specimens from sites worldwide, providing a unique perspective on human mobility, domestication and zoonotic disease. Lice, fleas, bedbugs, louse flies, ticks and mites have been recovered from sites with diverse preservation conditions, ranging from desiccated deposits to permafrost. Relevant contexts include mummies, coprolites, caves and house floors. abstract: This article examines Indigenous epistemology, its role in critiquing epistemic dominance, and its relevance to environmental law and sustainable development. It focuses on how the recognition of Indigenous peoples can extend beyond the acknowledgment of their identities and collective rights to include recognition of their epistemic authority in environmental decision-making. abstract: This study examines the interplay between African traditional religion, Islam, and Christianity in shaping slavery and the African diaspora, highlighting a shift from humane master-slave relationships to dehumanization during medieval Christian Europe, culminating in the transAtlantic slave trade. abstract: Africa has acquired strategic, economic, and diplomatic importance for emerging powers such as India and China in the 21st century. This article presents a comparative study of the African policies of India and China, analyzing the historical, political, economic, security, and social perspectives of both countries. abstract: Migration is an intrinsic and historically significant aspect of human civilization, mirroring natural phenomena such as the movement of birds, the dispersal of seeds, and the flow of rivers across borders. While migration has long been a driving force behind cultural and economic development, it has become a contentious issue in the contemporary global landscape. abstract: Purpose This study examines how toilet graffiti can be documented and organised as a researchable form of vernacular material for qualitative research. Rather than analysing the content of graffiti, the study focuses on the methodological and ethical conditions under which ephemeral and anonymous expressions found in public toilets can be rendered researchable. This article contextualises these disparities within the historical dynamics of fossil capitalism and an international legal framework characterised by enduring global inequalities and differentiated responsibilities. abstract: In a world of rapid technological advancements and global challenges, education must equip students with the skills to navigate complexity, uncertainty, and ethical dilemmas. This paper explores integrating socioscientific issues (SSIs) into the Cypriot primary science curriculum to foster critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and interdisciplinary learning. abstract: Environmental conservation is an important issue that should be instilled in students through education, as it plays a vital role in shaping environmentally responsible attitudes and behaviors. abstract: The literature and international organizations have recommended many environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. abstract: Abstract. Air pollution in cold wintertime urban areas is a ubiquitous problem. The presence of this PSL is well documented, but its height, the rates of exchange with the background atmosphere, and the interplay between vertical mixing and chemistry remain poorly quantified. abstract: This study appraised the governance structure in Nigeria petroleum industry, and as contained in the recent enacted PIA 2021 which is now the principal legal instrument as far as Nigeria’s petroleum industry is concerned. abstract: Climate change has intensified the need for legal frameworks that recognise environmental protection as an essential component of constitutional governance. In recent years, climate litigation has emerged as a significant pathway through which constitutional courts interpret and enforce environmental rights, particularly in relation to future generations. abstract: Despite their potentially major impacts, little is known about how El Niño impact the U.S. economy. El Niños are distinct from other commonly studied weather shocks because they are a global phenomenon, unfold over a period of months, can be forecast months in advance, are relatively infrequent, and have very different effects on weather outcomes depending on the time of year and region. These features make traditional analytical methods ill-suited to studying the economic impacts of El Niño events. title: Infrastructure and Inclusiveness in Election Administration: Insights from India’s General Elections
abstract: The Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) elections of India, represent the world’s largest democratic exercise, requiring an extraordinary scale of logistics, manpower and infrastructural readiness. abstract: This article examines the identification and acquisition of documents for the Australian Joint Copying Project (AJCP) from 1939 to 1954. It argues that the AJCP’s evolving scope reflected Australia’s shifting geopolitical identity and intellectual ambitions in the Pacific. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

abstract: A long‐term perspective on landscape evolution is critical for understanding past land‐use activity, land cover–climate feedbacks and, notably, for establishing a factual basis for conservation. title: Cultural Heritage and Tourism Development of Rivers State
abstract: Rivers State, located in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, possesses a rich cultural heritage that holds immense potential for tourism development. The state's diverse ethnic composition, traditional festivals, historical landmarks, and unique architectural expressions provide a significant opportunity to boost tourism and, in turn, drive economic growth. journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND CULTURAL STUDIES

title: Why do People in the Netherlands Reject or Minimise the Idea that Racism is Structural, Despite Substantial Evidence that Structural Discrimination Exists?
abstract: This article examines an apparent paradox in contemporary Dutch society: the persistence of substantial empirical evidence of structural discrimination alongside continuing resistance to, or minimisation of, the concept of structural racism. Drawing on Dutch and international scholarship, governmental reports and social-psychological theory, the article distinguishes structural racism from individual prejudice and argues that discriminatory outcomes do not necessarily depend upon conscious racist intentions. title: Beyond the Stage: Economic Impact and Tourism Multipliers of Music Festivals in Emerging Indian Destinations
abstract: In recent years, the consumption patterns of live music in India have broken out of conventional metropolitan hubs and found an eager, mobile audience across smaller towns, rural valleys, and scenic regional getaways. While traditional music business scholarship primarily focuses on recorded music, streaming royalties, catalog publishing, and copyright litigation, this study shifts critical attention to the broader macroeconomic spillovers generated by live concerts and multi-day music festivals in non-metropolitan environments. title: Schumpeterian disaggregation and integrated assessment: An endogenous, stock-flow consistent economy in disequilibrium for FRIDA v2.1
abstract: Abstract. Integrated assessments of climate change require models capable of capturing the coupled dynamics of natural and socioeconomic systems. This paper presents the economy module of FRIDA v2.1, a Schumpeterian, disequilibrium framework of endogenous growth designed to address several limitations of contemporary integrated assessment models (IAMs). title: Humanity Injustice in the Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) Program
abstract: The ideal of social justice mandated by the fifth principle of Pancasila remains challenged by persistent inequality, uneven access to welfare, and gaps between public policy objectives and their implementation in Indonesia. The Free Nutritious Meals (Makan Bergizi Gratis, or MBG) Program represents an important case for examining whether state welfare policies have realised substantive social justice or merely administrative distribution. This study aims to critically analyse the relevance and actualisation of Pancasila’s fifth principle through a philosophical examination of the MBG Program

title: Trials, Tools and Triumphs: A Phenomenological Study of Senior High School Female Students in Male-Dominated TVL Specialization
abstract: Female participation in some specializations within the senior high school Technical-Vocational-Livelihood (TVL) track is still low, which can potentially create gender-related challenges for female students. This study looked at the real-life experiences of senior high school female students in nontraditional, male-dominated TVL specializations, focusing on their challenges, ways they cope, and achievements. journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal

title: How Does the Issue of Social Forestry Affect the Knowledge of the Young Generation? Case Studies from Universities in Indonesia
abstract: Social forestry has emerged as a key agenda for the Indonesian government, aimed at reducing inequality in forest land tenure, enhancing community welfare, and minimizing conflict. Despite the many challenges of issuing social forestry management permits, specific issues, such as transdisciplinary science, regeneration, and youth engagement as drivers and actors at the site level, have yet to receive adequate attention. title: Reward System and Employees’ Effectiveness in Deposit Money Banks of Southeast, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between reward system and employees’ effectiveness of deposit money banks in south east, Nigeria. Three research objectives, research questions and hypotheses were formulated. The study adopted survey research design and Pearson correlation coefficient was used to test the stated hypotheses and the findings showed that there is significant relationship between pay raise, profit sharing and employee productivity, innovativeness and Initiative. abstract: Investasi rendah karbon menjadi fokus transisi energi global, termasuk pengembangan Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) lintas negara antara IndonesiaSingapura. Kerja sama ini menimbulkan kebutuhan kepastian hukum bagi investor asing karena melibatkan lebih dari satu yurisdiksi. abstract: This study examines the public evidence available for assessing Morocco's nuclear power decision readiness across the 19 infrastructure issues of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Milestones Approach. A documentary assessment separates established institutional foundations, evidence of preparatory activity, and matters that remain unverified. An author-developed Level 0–3 scale describes the maturity of the documented arrangements within their stated scope; it is neither an IAEA scoring system nor a test of Milestone 1 attainment. title: Legal Pluralism and Building Permit Enforcement in Tanzania: Contradictions of the Dual Land Tenure System
abstract: Tanzania operates a dual land tenure system. It recognises granted and customary rights of occupancy. The statute treats the two forms as equal, as set out in section 18(1) of the Village Land Act. The Constitution and the Court of Appeal confirm that customary rights are property. Yet building permit enforcement is built around granted title. A landholder in a declared planning area must obtain a permit before development. Regulation 124(1) of the Local Government (Urban Authorities) (Development Control) Regulations (2008) imposes this duty. In practice, the permit route presupposes a survey
journal: East African Journal of Law and Ethics

title: Where Commitment Dissipates: An Attenuation Cascade Theory of Gender in Climate Resilience Policy
abstract: Climate policy increasingly recognises that unequal social relations shape climate risk, yet this recognition has not consistently changed budgets, eligibility rules, or outcomes. This article examines where near-universal gender commitments weaken and what determines the scale of that loss. Using theory-building thematic synthesis, it integrates feminist political ecology, intersectionality, social vulnerability theory, the capabilities approach, and transformative resilience with research on policy evaporation and gradual institutional change. title: Assessing A Rural Community-Based Entrepreneurship in Malaysia: Are we there yet?
abstract: This article draws upon research undertaken in two rural communities in Malaysia under the program My Village My Future, a community-based entrepreneurship program initiated by the government to develop rural areas. Little is known about the success of rural community-based entrepreneurship. The paper uses various community-based entrepreneurship models to explore rural community-based entrepreneurship's roots, challenges, and issues. This study aims to explore the suitable model of community-based entrepreneurship in rural areas. This paper follows a case study method of a narrative approach

abstract: The general opinion is that education is an instrument of ensuring positive changes in the society however; positive changes have not been achieved in Ogbomoso prior to the arrival of Christian Mission. Traditional education was then characterized with vocational training such as basketry, blacksmithing, carving, arts, crafts, sculptures, painting and decoration. This education is not formal because there are no lesson notes, curriculum, school register and school buildings as in the western sense. title: Data infrastructure fragmentation and policy failure: Evidence from Indonesia’s food security governance
abstract: Indonesia’s food security governance faces a structural paradox: a 2025 budget allocation of IDR 155.5 trillion coexists with 23.28 million undernourished citizens and a 13-year absence of a National Food Plan. This study argues that data infrastructure fragmentation is the principal structural barrier underlying this paradox. We propose a three-dimensional typology (horizontal, vertical, and temporal) as an analytical framework for diagnosing this barrier. journal: Jurnal Tata Kelola dan Akuntabilitas Keuangan Negara

title: Community-Based Event Management Model for Community Empowerment and Sustainable Rural Tourism in Tua Tourism Village
abstract: Background: Rural tourism becomes more durable when residents can transform local culture, social networks, and community resources into visitor experiences without weakening local identity. In Tua Tourism Village, village events offer this possibility, yet their continuity is affected by limited managerial skills, financing, digital communication, and formal operating procedures. title: Policy-Robust Space Investment Strategies: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation under Competing Societal Paradigms
abstract: Although competing societal needs have intensified pressure on public budgets, public investment in space has expanded considerably. Decision-makers must prioritize space investments while considering economic, social, environmental, and strategic objectives. However, the relative importance of these objectives may vary across different policy perspectives. This study frames the prioritization of space investments as a multidimensional decision-making problem and develops a method for evaluating the robustness of space investment strategies under different societal paradigms. title: Coupling microalgal bioremediation of recirculating aquaculture effluents with photobiological hydrogen production
abstract: Abstract Recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) effluents contain substantial nitrate and phosphate loads, posing a significant eutrophication risk to aquatic ecosystems if left untreated. While microalgal bioremediation is a promising strategy, expanding opportunities for valorisation is crucial for its successful implementation. This study couples the cultivation of nitrate-utilizing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-1690 in RAS effluent with photobiological hydrogen (H 2 ) production to achieve nutrient removal, bioenergy production, and high-quality biomass. title: Assessing the Influence of Tourism Development on Wildlife Conservation In GISHWATI-MUKURA National Park, Rwanda
abstract: This study examined the influence of tourism development on wildlife conservation in Gishwati-Mukura National Park, Rwanda. It specifically assessed the influence of income creation, community-based tourism activities, and ecotourism activities on wildlife conservation. A descriptive research design was employed, targeting a population of 475 individuals, from whom a sample of 217 respondents was selected. journal: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management

title: The Nigerian Civil War: Causes, Resolution, And Post-War Reconciliation Efforts
abstract: The Nigerian Civil War, which ranged from 1967 to 1970, stands as a pivotal moment in the nation's history, marked by intense ethnic tensions and a profound struggle for control over resources and power. This abstract explores the multifaceted problems that led to the outbreak of the Nigerian Civil War, the approaches taken to resolve the conflict, and the subsequent efforts to foster reconciliation among the warring factions. journal: JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND SOCIAL POLICY

title: ‘I Have Been There Too’: motivations and expectations of young people with previous experience of being in a NEET situation becoming peer mentors- a qualitative study
abstract: This study explores how young people with previous experience of being in a NEET situation describe their motivation and expectations for serving as mentors for peers who are not in education, employment, or training. Using a qualitative, inductive design, five mentors aged 18–24 participated in individual in-depth interviews before beginning mentor training. Thematic analysis identified two overarching themes: Inspiring meaning for others and oneself and Providing support fosters resilience and growth. All this in the face of these abiding challenges – the fact that students come from social-economically diverse backgrounds, non-uniform, diverse pedagogical systems impart their education, and infrastructure is a barrier to the quality of education in a developing country. abstract: O trabalho analisa o papel do significante “mudança” no discurso político de Mauricio Macri em campanha e durante seu governo (2015-2019). title: Unpacking climate justice rhetoric: a comparative content analysis of international city networks
abstract: Purpose The rising membership and influence of international city networks have positioned cities as important actors in global policy debates on climate change and sustainability. This study aims to clarify how these networks frame and incorporate justice in their climate actions. Design/methodology/approach The study selected four prominent city networks (C40, CityNet, ICLEI and UCLG) and applied a content analysis method to examine how they interpret justice in 64 documents published by them between 2016 and 2022. title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DALAM KAITANNYA DENGAN PELESTARIAN LINGKUNGAN DAN MASYARAKAT WILAYAH PESISIR DAN PULAU-PULAU KECIL DI INDONESIA
abstract: Wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil di Indonesia memiliki potensi sumber daya alam yang melimpah, namun sekaligus sangat rentan terhadap degradasi lingkungan dan masalah ketimpangan sosial-ekonomi. Kehadiran berbagai aktivitas industri dan korporasi di sekitar kawasan ini membawa dampak ekologis dan sosial yang signifikan, sehingga menuntut optimalisasi pelaksanaan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji dan menganalisis implementasi program CSR dalam kaitannya dengan pelestarian lingkungan serta pemberdayaan masyarakat di kawasan pesisir dan pulau-pulau k

title: Drivers of Employee Engagement in Nepal's Private Sector: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Recruitment, Training, Performance Appraisal, and Compensation Practices in Kathmandu Valley
abstract: Background: Employee engagement is a key driver of a company's competitive advantage and performance. Employee engagement creates opportunities for employees to connect with their managers, employees, and organizations through the human resource management practices. Purpose: The objective of this research is to study the impact of human resource management practices on employee engagement in private sector of Kathmandu valley. title: LEXICAL-SEMANTIC FEATURES OF ENGLISH AND UZBEK TRADE TERMS
abstract: The article is devoted to the lexical-semantic features of trade terms in English and Uzbek languages. Trade terminology is one of the oldest and most dynamic layers of economic vocabulary in both languages. The study covers polysemy, synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy and homonymy, as well as semantic changes and borrowings. The article material consists of English trade terms and their Uzbek equivalents drawn from explanatory and bilingual dictionaries, legal and normative documents and commercial texts. Definitional, componential, etymological and comparative methods were applied in the article.

title: Exploring the Rule-of-Law Approach to Collaborative Data Security Governance in BRICS
abstract: Data has become a foundational strategic resource in the digital age, and data security has emerged as a crucial issue that aﬀects national security, economic development, and social stability. With the expansion of data sovereignty approach and the collective rise of the “Global South,” the BRICS countries have initiated their respective data legislation processes and changed the passive position of developing countries in the formulation of international data rules through coordinated governance.
