title: Urban commons in a contested trajectory of new municipalism: rethinking public–common partnerships in the case of Kültürpark İzmir
abstract: Within the contested terrains of post-neoliberal urbanism, what are the possibilities (and limits) of urban commons? The article focuses on the case of Kültürpark in İzmir to provide critical answers by highlighting its counter-hegemonic potential of public–commons partnerships. Established as a cultural and ecological landmark, the park has recently become a site of intense struggles over urban futures: municipal projects seeking market-oriented valorization have clashed with civic mobilizations defending its ecological, cultural, and symbolic significance. title: Application of a Naegele’s Formula Adapted to the Long Count Mayan Calendar to Calculate the Expected Date of Birth During a Leap Year
abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether the Naegele formula applied to the Mayan calendar can improve the accuracy of due date prediction. Methods: A database of pregnant women who gave birth during the leap year 2016 was analyzed (post hoc analysis). The date of the last menstruation (confirmed by ultrasound) was converted to the Mayan date using an online converter. title: Caste as Ecology: The Mangrove Archive, Slow Violence and the Labouring Dalit Body in the Sundarbans Stories of Shyamal Kumar Pramanik

title: From representation to equitable participation: An overview of multicultural education research published in 2025
abstract: Multicultural education research has expanded rapidly, but its definitions remain varied and the distinction between representation and equitable participation remains unresolved. This thematic-bibliometric review of one publication year examines 210 English-language articles published in 2025 and classified in the field of Social Sciences in Scopus, the sole database. title: Empowering risky choices: care ethics and risk management in participatory immersive performance
abstract: This article examines audience engagement in immersive theatrical productions, focusing on why some participants thrive while others feel fearful or reluctant. It critiques traditional risk management systems for overlooking psychological and social risks in participatory art. Using insights from Joan Tronto’s care ethics and Paul Slovic’s risk perception, this study proposes that grounded risk management in care ethics can enhance audience experiences. title: Dynamic management simulation of grasslands in the Spanish Cantabrian Coast for climate change impact assessment
abstract: Permanent grasslands are a fundamental ecosystem for the biodiversity, agricultural, livestock and economic productivity of the Spanish Cantabrian Coast (northern-northwestern Spain). In the context of climate change, it is necessary to quantify precisely how the productivity of these agricultural systems will evolve and whether it will be necessary to introduce adaptation measures. title: Unlocking Employee Performance Through Internal Marketing: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Organizational Commitment in Nepal's Service Industry
abstract: Background: Employee performance is critical to service organizations, where employee attitudes and organizational support can directly shape service delivery. Internal marketing practices such as empowerment, rewards, supportive supervisor relationships, and career opportunities can strengthen organizational commitment and enhance employee performance. However, limited evidence exists on these relationships in Nepal’s service industry, particularly regarding the mediating role of organizational commitment. title: Legal Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers from the Perspective of International Law and Its Implementation
abstract: Background: Indonesian migrant workers continue to face various forms of vulnerability, including exploitation, unpaid wages, physical and psychological violence, human trafficking, document confiscation, and limited access to justice in destination countries. International law has established a broad framework for protection through human rights instruments, migrant worker conventions, and International Labour Organization standards. title: Evaluating the association between household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and selected placenta-related complications in The Gambia, Kenya and Mozambique
abstract: Placenta-related complications contribute substantially to maternal and perinatal mortality globally, with the greatest burden in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, the potential influence of inadequate household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) on these outcomes remains poorly characterised. We investigated associations between household WASH conditions and selected placenta-related complications, including pre-eclampsia, small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and stillbirth, in The Gambia, Kenya and Mozambique. title: Indigenous Women’s Wisdom in Sustainable Natural Resource Management: A Participatory Environmental Justice Perspective
abstract: Sustainable natural resource management has yet to adequately recognize and integrate indigenous women’s traditional knowledge. This article examines its legal status, the challenges to its recognition, and the legal reforms needed to strengthen it from a participatory environmental justice perspective. title: Urban heat as a structural development challenge in rapidly growing cities
abstract: Urban heat is increasingly emerging as a major constraint on sustainable development, particularly in rapidly growing cities of the Global South. Although urban heat is commonly addressed through local adaptation and urban heat reduction measures such as urban greening, cool and super cool roofs, and building retrofits or passive design, these interventions are increasingly implemented against a backdrop of accelerating planetary warming, fiscal constraints, and persistent socio-economic inequalities. title: Necrocities as Borderscapes: Necropolitics and the Production of Refugee Life in Offshore Detention
abstract: This paper examines refugee narratives to illustrate how necropower is exercised within borderscapes where life is presented at its extreme limit. Using Behrouz Boochani’s No Friend But the Mountains, I explore refugee camps as necrocities embedded within broader borderscapes that deny refugees free movement, access to civic life, and the status of being full human beings. abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) can impair broiler performance, redox balance, and skeletal health. abstract: Fundamentally, teacher empowerment is a measure expected to improve the school-based management participation of teachers. In this study, the researcher selected the 197 elementary school teachers in Sta. Cruz North District, Davao del Sur as the respondents of the study. Stratified random sampling technique was utilized in the selection of the respondents. Non-experimental quantitative research design using descriptive-correlational method was employed. title: Income Stability and Financial Resilience as Determinants of Well-Being Among Cruise Line Employees
abstract: This study examined income stability and financial resilience as determinants of well-being among cruise line employees residing in Pampanga, Philippines. A descriptive-correlational design was used with 128 respondents who met the study eligibility criteria and were selected through purposive screening followed by simple random sampling. title: A Southern European Portrait of Learning Outcomes

It contributes to the comparative literature on education, training, and youth transition regimes through an analysis of interactions between these actors in three local contexts. The fieldwork was conducted in Castelló (Spain), Pesaro- Urbino (Italy), and the rural areas and tourist resorts in the district of Thessaloniki (Greece). title: Global warming and the National Cattlemen’s Association 1986–1996
abstract: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. Using scientific studies, archival documents, media interviews, and various government reports, we analyzed how the National Cattlemen’s Association (NCA), a trade association for the U.S beef industry, reacted to news about its products’ impacts on global warming between 1986 and 1996. title: Evaluating the impact of triple-drug mass drug administration using human and mosquito-based indicators of lymphatic filariasis in Samoa, 2019 – 2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: For lymphatic filariasis (LF) elimination, the World Health Organization recommends multiple rounds of mass drug administration (MDA) to interrupt transmission. While LF antigen (Ag) is routinely used to monitor progress, recent evidence suggests more time-sensitive indicators are needed during the immediate post-MDA period. In Samoa, triple-drug MDA was distributed in 2018 and 2023. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Samoa's second round of triple-drug MDA on human and mosquito-based indicators of transmission. abstract: This article critically examines the impact of illegal and informal mining in Peru and its relationship with the violation of fundamental rights, with particular emphasis on the rights to health, a healthy environment, and effective judicial protection. abstract: Natural gas is the main component of Nigeria's Gas Decade Strategy (2021–2030), which aims to promote regional industrialization and domestic growth. The country has significant gas reserves that place it among the top nations in Africa. Africa's steel, petrochemical, manufacturing, and fertilizer industries depend on a steady supply of gas, which helps close the gap in energy access. title: Good Intentions, Bad Law: The Constitutional Vulnerability of the New Hate Speech Offence in New South Wales
abstract: In this comment I examine the constitutionality of the new New South Wales (‘NSW’) offence of publicly inciting racial hatred in s 93ZAA of the Crimes Act 1900 (NSW). I argue that, despite pursuing important public order and anti-racism objectives, s 93ZAA is a poorly designed and ineffective legislative response to the serious harms posed by hate speech, and ultimately risks imposing an impermissible burden on the freedom of political communication mandated by the text and structure of the Australian Constitution.

abstract: The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is a large-scale development initiative through which China seeks to promote economic cooperation, regional connectivity, and infrastructure development. The China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a major component of the BRI. This study examines the role of CPEC in Pakistan’s economic growth, with particular focus on three key areas: infrastructure development, employment generation, and energy production. abstract: Abstract This research reveals a psycholinguistic effect whereby more precise words in product communications increase consumer perceptions of product uniqueness. abstract: Ludwig van Beethoven’s last three piano sonatas, Opp. 109, 110, and 111, have captured the imaginations of critics from the nineteenth century to the present. As “late” works penned towards the end of the composer’s life, these sonatas have often been read as infused with existential or transcendental meaning, frequently aligned with Beethoven’s own experiences. abstract: Customary forest governance in Papua reflected the complex dynamics of legal pluralism, where state and customary law interacted in the management of community living spaces. This research aimed to analyze the governance of the indigenous forest by the Yongsu Desoyo community through a traditional zoning system consisting of sena, buso, and sasena as cultivation land, utilization zone, and sacred zone. abstract: Contractual stability in land management is crucial for incentivizing long-term investment, enhancing productivity, and promoting sustainable agricultural development. However, contractual instability remains a prominent issue in China’s land leasing market reform, and its causes and impacts require systematic analysis. abstract: The purpose of the study was to determine the genesis of development and economic essence of taxes for Ukrainian agriculture within the framework of transformation of special tax regimes, the land base of tax payments and the influence of tax changes on the activity of agricultural enterprises. title: A Territorial Approach to Transitioning Oil and Gas Producing Regions: Comparative Practices and Prospects for Canada
abstract: Abstract Oil and gas transitions are relatively new and especially difficult because the sector is large, economically central, and deeply embedded in national energy systems. Territorial approaches—grounded in regional political economies, institutions, and community impacts—offer a politically feasible way to begin meaningful oil and gas transitions in Canada's producing regions. abstract: In the context of the global biodiversity crisis, biodiversity conservation is of the utmost importance for all habitats, from the most natural to those most heavily modified by humans, such as agroecosystems. As the general public widely recognizes biodiversity loss, agroecosystems could be ideal environments for citizen science, increasing biodiversity knowledge of these areas and raising public awareness. title: Poetic Opacity and the Limits of Translation
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that translations of poetry cannot function as substitutive reproductions of their originals due to the medium-specific opacity of the poetic form. Drawing on the concept of poetic opacity and on type-token distinction, I contend that a poem’s aesthetic identity resides in a distinctive, linguistically rooted interplay of form and content, one that resists full transfer across languages. abstract: This essay critically examines the Faculty Performance Incentive Program in Mexican higher education from a Foucauldian perspective. Its objective is to examine the institutional rationality underpinning this evaluation and incentive mechanism, with particular attention to its connections with surveillance, the regulation of conduct, the intensification of performance demands, and the differential classification of academic staff. abstract: How do states navigate economic crises? How do crises affect state capitalist systems? This article explores how the government of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) understood and responded to the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis and the 2007–2008 Global Financial Crisis. title: From policy to practice: Healthcare providers' experiences in implementing vaccination strategies in Mozambique
abstract: Introduction: Achieving full immunization coverage remains a persistent challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, leaving children vulnerable to preventable diseases. In Mozambique, only 38% of children aged 12–23 months have received the basic antigens, and even fewer have completed the national immunization schedule. abstract: The ecosystem concept, borrowed from natural sciences, helps social scientists study organizations, economic regions, and the complex relationships between organizations and people. abstract: Forest ecosystems play a crucial role as regulators of the global carbon cycle. abstract: Since antiquity, speechmaking has been a vital medium through which societies articulate ideas, values, and collective concerns to both specific and general audiences. abstract: Influenza vaccines targeting both hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) might offer broader protection than current vaccines, which primarily target HA. abstract: This study examines the potential of community-based tourism (CBT) as a pathway to sustainable development in Jaflong, Bangladesh, an ecologically sensitive and culturally diverse destination, where the uneven participation of different community groups remains insufficiently examined. abstract: ABSTRACT Online flash sale events create urgency, scarcity and deep‐discount conditions, yet little is known about how consumer decision‐making styles vary across product involvement levels and how they are associated with situational involvement. abstract: In recent years, mass media has played a crucial role in shedding light on contemporary socio-political issues across the world. Many filmmakers address pressing social concerns through cinema, creating awareness among audiences and encouraging public discourse. Such representations often help draw attention to the problems faced by victims and vulnerable communities, thereby fostering empathy and understanding. abstract: Rural youth participation in deliberative consultation has the potential to revitalize grassroots good governance; however, insufficient participation remains a persistent challenge. Based on fieldwork in townships in North China, this qualitative study employs Coleman’s rational choice theory as an analytical framework. title: The Rise of Disconnective Power: How Digitalisation Supports Global Fragmentation
abstract: Although often seen as a threat, digital connectivity is increasingly exploited by autocratic regimes to achieve their aims. This essay advances the concept of disconnective power by examining how states use digital tools to foster disintegration at the domestic and global levels. abstract: Effective institutional communication is central to transparent, inclusive, and participatory governance in higher education. This article examines communication policy and practice at Makerere University, focusing on stakeholder access to information, feedback, participation in decision-making, and the alignment between communication policy and implementation. abstract: This study examined the opinions of extension workers on participatory training in the Sudanese states of Gezira, Sinnar, and Gedarif. Data were collected from a sample of 205 extension workers using structured questionnaires, supported by secondary sources. abstract: En Argentina, la Garza Cucharona (Cochlearius cochlearius) ha sido históricamente considerada una especie ocasional o extremadamente rara. Los arroyos y riachos de la región chaqueña podrían albergar poblaciones densas, mientras que en Misiones el sistema de arroyos del Parque Nacional Iguazú y el río homónimo Iguazú son clave para la población de Garza Cucharona. title: Economic determinants of the formation of China’s diversified and sustainable foreign policy and trade
abstract: This article examines how China is making its foreign policy and trade more diverse and resilient. China’s economy has slowed, and the country faces strong technological pressure from the United States. In response, Beijing is using several tools: the “dual circulation” strategy, the new 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), and a shift of trade toward ASEAN and Belt and Road partners rather than Western markets alone. title: Sugarcane farming practices and household income levels nexus: A case of Ndhiwa Sub-County, Homa Bay County, Kenya
abstract: Sugarcane farming is the main economic activity in Ndhiwa sub County. While the activity remains an important source of rural livelihoods, there is limited research with regards to the contribution of sugarcane farming to household income. While its contribution to rural incomes is significant, limited empirical evidence exists on how different dimensions of sugarcane production including land allocation, farming practices, labor structures, payment systems, and value chain participation affect household income. title: Tribal Federalism: Expanding the Indian Gaming Paradigm
abstract: Federalism has long been celebrated for its ability to foster policy innovation, transforming states into “laboratories of democracy.” Yet, federalism discourse has largely neglected Indian tribes, the third sovereign in the American constitutional order. Tribes regularly implement novel policies. However, tribal policy innovation is hindered by uncertainty over whether tribes or states govern Indian country activities. title: Frontex Accountability and Fundamental Rights: Legal Remedies and Institutional Reform in the European Union
abstract: The European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) has become central to the management of the external borders of the European Union because of its increasingly operational capabilities. The broadening of its remit to improve border security and border management is intended to strengthen security and the control of migration, but it has raised concerns about respect for fundamental rights. This paper explores how far Frontex can be held legally liable for breaches of fundamental rights resulting from its activities. abstract: La gobernanza del sistema alimentario urbano es determinante para garantizar el acceso equitativo a alimentos nutritivos. Este estudio analiza la gobernanza alimentaria en el Distrito Metropolitano de Quito (2020-2025) y su incidencia en la seguridad alimentaria de los hogares. title: De las tensiones evaluativas al diseño didáctico: Hacia una secuencia de evaluación integrada al proceso de aprendizaje
abstract: Este estudio estudia las tensiones epistémicas de la evaluación del aprendizaje en la producción científica iberoamericana e internacional reciente, confrontando las intenciones de la racionalidad instrumental con las de la racionalidad práctica. Mediante una investigación documental cualitativa y alcance analítico, se sistematizó un corpus especializado con criterios rigurosos de inclusión y exclusión (2018–2026). title: Drivers and Barriers to Online Freelance Portal Adoption Among Urban Youth in Nepal: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Perceived Usefulness, Social Influence, and Digital Accessibility
abstract: Background: The growth of digital technologies has expanded opportunities for online freelance work among youth. Online freelance portals enable access to global employment and income opportunities, but adoption may be constrained by digital literacy, technology access, payment concerns, and job security. Purpose: The purpose of the study is to identify the factors influencing the intention to adapt and use online freelance portals among the youths of the Kathmandu Valley. title: Tracing jealousy and envy: A semantic journey through English with HTOED
abstract: Abstract This study offers a diachronic analysis of jealousy‑ and envy‑related vocabulary in English, drawing on 95 lexical items from the Historical Thesaurus of the Oxford English Dictionary ( HTOED ). While research on emotion concepts has traditionally focused on synchronic patterns and metaphorical structuring, comparatively little attention has been paid to the historical development of these notions. abstract: Este artículo analiza la película 20.000 especies de abejas (Estibaliz Urresola Solaguren, 2023) desde una perspectiva que entrecruza la teoría queer, la visualidad háptica y el análisis de la temporalidad fílmica, a partir de la hipótesis de que la directora construye una estética cinematográfica que habilita un punto de percepción trans e infantil. title: The Source(s) of Miguel de Unamuno’s ‘El buen bandolero’
abstract: Abstract Miguel de Unamuno’s oeuvre comprises a substantial number of texts whose main scope is religion, almost exclusively Christianity. This should come as no surprise in a person who had a very idiosyncratic creed, and whose “agonic” take on faith and transcendence dominated much of his life. Precisely because he was so invested in and knowledgeable about religion, it is surprising to find that he used “el buen bandolero” to refer to “el buen ladrón” (“the good thief”)—the latter being a phrase with long-standing idiomatic status to refer to one of the criminals crucified next to Jesus. title: Sanctions and the Use of Force in International Relations: Exploring a Multifaceted Nexus
abstract: This article explores the complex relationship between sanctions and the use of force. It reveals a multifaceted interrelationship that, to some extent, reflects the complex nature of sanctions themselves. After reviewing and assessing the key issues arising in relation to sanctions – particularly the legality and legitimacy of autonomous (i.e. non-UN) sanctions – the article examines a selection of concrete situations illustrating four distinct ways in which sanctions interact with, or otherwise become relevant to, the use of armed force. title: Professional Development, Research and Pedagogical Competence on the English Language Proficiency of Foreign English Teachers in Vietnam
abstract: Foreign English teachers in Vietnam play an important role in English language education, yet limited empirical evidence explains how professional development, research competence, and pedagogical competence relate to their English language proficiency. This study examined the relationships among these teacher competencies and determined their predictive effects on English language proficiency. A quantitative quasi-descriptive correlational and causal-comparative design was employed. title: Petroglyphs as petrofacts? Exploring the visibility and physicality of lines, furrows, and cavities in Bronze Age rock art
abstract: Abstract This text concerns tangible and sensory aspects of petroglyph production with a primary focus on south Scandinavian Bronze Age rock art. The core of the study is based on an experimental trial of making a cupmark, a circle motif, and a shallow boat motif on a small granite outcrop. The aims were to measure time expenditure, the impact of water on the process, evaluate sensory aspects (e.g. colour, sound, and smell), and measure the visibility of the petroglyphs over time. title: Total constitutionalism in different contexts under scrutiny Introduction to the Special Section
abstract: This Special Section sets forth the thesis that European constitutionalism is evolving towards what many call ‘total constitutionalism’. This evolution is driven by civil society’s demand for government services, elite special interests, economic globalisation, and judicial activism. The process is far advanced, with courts rendering judgments across a wide range of political and policy domains, to the point now of substituting themselves for legislatures and even constitutional conventions, with far-reaching implications for majoritarian democracy. title: Administration of the Local Curriculum on “Durian at Ban Pa Daeng” at Ban Pa Daeng School, Kaeng Krachan District, Phetchaburi Province
abstract: This action research aimed to (1) investigate local knowledge concerning durian in Ban Pa Daeng, (2) administer a local curriculum based on this knowledge, and (3) examine the outcomes of implementing the curriculum at Ban Pa Daeng School, Kaeng Krachan District, Phetchaburi Province. The target group comprised 105 participants: two school administrators, four teachers, 92 Grade 5 students, one community leader, four local wisdom experts, and two parents. title: Teleosemantics and Ethology
abstract: Abstract The debate between different versions of teleosemantics has largely centered around which alternative offers the most plausible account of the contents of simple animal representations. A serious issue is that theorists not only disagree on which proposal best explains the contents of these representations but also on what the contents actually are. title: Putting place first: towards a new vision for UK industrial strategy
abstract: This paper challenges the longstanding dominance of agglomeration theory in shaping the UK’s approach to industrial and regional strategy. While agglomeration thinking, rooted in urban economics, has played an influential role in government policy for two decades, persistent spatial inequalities, institutional fragmentation and the underperformance of the UK’s largest cities raise serious questions about its suitability as a universal framework for national industrial policy. The paper argues that the UK economy is better understood as comprising three distinct types of firm–place relationship

title: The Long Trajectory of Rubber Physics: 3500+ Years and Counting
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural rubber has followed an extraordinary trajectory from an indigenous Mesoamerican technology to an industrially essential material. This selective history begins with processing Castilla elastica latex more than three and a half millennia ago to produce durable ceremonial and practical objects. title: EU Values and the Demise of Constitutional Prudence
abstract: Abstract This article presents two interconnected arguments. First, a method other than the doctrinal method is needed to study EU constitutional law. Using the ruling in Commission v Hungary as the central example, the article demonstrates that EU constitutional law is not just legal but also political in nature. Following Martin Loughlin, the article therefore argues that the method of EU constitutional law is ‘the method of prudence’. title: Institutions, legitimacy, and divergent regime trajectories after political openings: a comparative analysis of Tunisia, Egypt, Turkey, and Indonesia
abstract: Why do similar political openings produce divergent regime trajectories? This article develops a comparative institutional framework to explain variation in post-authoritarian outcomes through a structured comparison of Tunisia, Egypt, Turkey and Indonesia. It argues that political openings generate uncertainty but do not determine political outcomes. title: Does power-sharing facilitate memory-sharing? Bosnian Croat narratives in post-war Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This study examines how Bosnian Croat wartime narratives intersect with perspectives on post-war power-sharing in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Drawing on media, NGO reports and semi-elite interviews, it shows that despite shared wartime narratives, particularly those depicting Serbs as aggressors, competition within the consociational system has led to narrative divergence between Bosnian Croats and Bosniaks. abstract: Frente às aceleradas mudanças nos contextos agrícolas mundiais, com tendência ao monocultivo, à homogeneização e à perda da variabilidade genética das espécies cultiva das, o presente estudo teve como objetivo demonstrar a importância dos conhecimentos dos povos indígenas no manejo da agrobiodiversidade, com ênfase na familiarização da mandioca. title: Does conservation status predict research output?
abstract: Abstract The Endangered Species Act (ESA) of 1973 uses the best available science to protect threatened and endangered species, but limited knowledge of listed species can undermine conservation success. This study examined whether ESA‐listed species receive more peer‐reviewed publications than ecologically similar non‐listed species. We randomly selected 50 ESA‐listed species across five taxonomic groups (birds, fish, herpetofauna, invertebrates, and mammals), pairing each with a comparable non‐listed species, and compared annual peer‐reviewed publication counts. abstract: Background: Student satisfaction is an important indicator of educational service quality and can influence students’ perceptions of institutional performance, engagement, and continued affiliation with an institution. In an increasingly competitive higher education environment, private colleges must understand which dimensions of service quality most strongly shape students’ experiences. title: From Exclusion to Protection: Chinese Merchant Capital in the Philippines Under US Law and Empire, 1921–1926
abstract: Abstract Scholarship about the Chinese Question has largely understood it as a “coolie” question, but what if it was reframed in terms of merchants? Well-studied US anti-Chinese laws like the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act targeted working-class rather than elite Chinese, like merchants and students. But in 1921, the US-controlled Insular Government in the Philippines enacted a statute known as the Chinese Bookkeeping Act (Act No. 2972), marking a moment when US Chinese exclusion laws were directed toward businessowners. title: O AVANÇO DO PODER JUDICIAL : EFEITOS EM PARTE DA GLOBALIZAÇÃO, DO PLURALISMO DAS FONTES JURÍDICAS E DA COMPLEXIDADE DOS FENÔMENOS SOCIAIS
abstract: Il contributo tratta del progressivo avanzamento del potere giudiziale (c.d. giudiziarizzazione), che negli ultimi decenni ha guadagnato decisamente terreno rispetto al principio di legalità (legale), sempre più indebolito da fattori sia endogeni che esogeni al mondo del diritto. In particolare, lo scritto evidenzia come, tra le cause storico-sociali lato sensu extra-giuridiche, la globalizzazione e il pluralismo delle fonti giuridiche, insieme alla complessità dei fenomeni sociali, abbiano contribuito e contribuiscano all’affermarsi della giuristocrazia.

title: Governments or facilitators? Power and politics of multi-level sustainable energy governance in Surat, Gujarat
abstract: Urban areas are becoming strategic sites in the ongoing sustainable energy transition, driven by the new opportunities and imperatives presented by decentralized sustainable energy technologies. However, the presence of cities in the global clean energy landscape remains underwhelming. Despite national programs encouraging urban energy transition in India, the response has largely failed to meet the goals. title: Creativity, Psychological Capital, and Stress Resistance as Predictors of Academic Achievement: Evidence from Postgraduate Fine Arts Students
abstract: This study investigates the relationships among creativity, psychological capital, stress resistance, and academic achievement within Fine Arts education. Using product-of-coefficients (delta-method) tests of the indirect effects, it examines how psychological capital and stress resistance mediate the impact of creativity on academic performance among postgraduate Fine Arts students. title: Hospitality for the Truth in 3 John and Its Implications for Contemporary Christians
abstract: Hospitality has been a veritable tool widely used to achieve certain purposes, good or bad in human endeavours. It is a virtue Jesus enjoyed from different persons while on earth and recommends same. The church after him continues to use hospitality to alleviate people’s suffering and support itinerant preachers and missionaries. title: Modern grass phytolith assemblages from the Maloti-Drakensberg Mountains, southern Africa
abstract: Montane grasslands dominate the Maloti-Drakensberg mountain range in southern Africa and rank among the region's most biodiverse and sensitive ecosystems. Reconstructing their long-term dynamics remains challenging, as widely used palaeoecological proxies such as pollen offer limited taxonomic resolution for distinguishing grasses. abstract: ABSTRACT The problem of heavy metal pollution in aquatic ecosystems is becoming increasingly critical. ZIF ‐8 is a representative metal–organic framework ( MOF ) that exhibits exemplary Cu 2+ adsorption characteristics and is amenable to large‐scale synthesis. abstract: Abstract People’s perceptions of others, particularly those from other countries, can shape their attitudes and willingness to offer solidarity. We study public beliefs about the gender composition of forcibly displaced populations in a large online survey experiment. Participants ( n = 13,008) representative of the adult population of six EU countries, consistently underestimated the share of women among the people displaced by the Russian war on Ukraine. title: A Phase 1/2 Trial Evaluating the Safety and Immunogenicity of an mRNA-based Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Candidate Encoding Hemagglutinin and Neuraminidase
abstract: Hemagglutinin (HA) is the principal immunologic target of most licensed seasonal influenza vaccines. Targeting both HA and neuraminidase (NA) might improve vaccine effectiveness. This randomized phase 1/2 study evaluated an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine, encoding HA and NA of A/H1N1, A/H3N2, B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata (FLUm4HA-4NA). abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the impacts of environmental regulations on reduced water pollution. This is achieved in the empirical context of discharge limits and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) discharges in the Swedish pulp and paper industry for four decades, also highlighting the role of a major regulatory regime shift in the country. title: From policy proliferation to coherence: Translating agroecological evidence into subnational food-systems governance in Vihiga County, Kenya
abstract: Sustainable agriculture in Kenya is governed by numerous policies addressing crops, soils, livestock, water, agroforestry, climate change, biodiversity, nutrition, marketing and social inclusion. Yet the existence of many broadly supportive instruments has not produced coherent agroecological implementation at the subnational level. This study examined how policy proliferation, fragmented mandates, and weak coordination affect the translation of agroecological evidence into county food-systems governance, using Vihiga County as a case study. title: Linguistic Sciences in Andalusia During the Emirate and Caliphate Periods Through the Book Al-Muqtabis by Ibn Hayyan al-Qurtubi (d. 469 AH / 1076 CE)

title: Rethinking body partonymy: transverse analogous paradigms across world languages
abstract: The part-whole relations of body-part lexemes, or “body partonymy,” might seem like a key source of evidence for shared conceptual systems in support of embodiment theories of cognition, but widespread variation in this lexical field across world languages calls this assumption into question. Recent studies focus on radical mismatches and random overlap relative to isolated frames of contrast such as body joints, reference languages, and ad hoc hierarchies. title: Revisión y discusión sobre la presencia y distribución del Taguató Negro (Parabuteo leucorrhous) en el noreste argentino
abstract: El Taguató Negro (Parabuteo leucorrhous) presenta poblaciones regulares y de mayor densidad en las selvas montanas de las Yungas del noroeste de Argentina. La población del nordeste tendría una densidad muy baja y, en los últimos 65 años, solo se conocen dos registros documentados en Misiones y pocos reportes de observación. La especie fue señalada para las provincias de la región chaqueña (Chaco, Formosa y Santiago del Estero) y de la Mesopotamia (Corrientes y Entre Ríos). title: Illness perceptions, treatment attitudes, and social relationships among clinic-attending adults with bipolar disorder in Kerman, Iran: a qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Background Bipolar disorder is a chronic psychiatric condition in Iran; however, little is known about how patients in non-Western, collectivistic contexts – particularly in southeastern Iran – perceive their illness, form treatment attitudes, and manage social relationships. This qualitative study therefore explored illness perceptions, treatment attitudes, and social relationships among clinic-attending adults with bipolar disorder in Kerman, Iran. title: Strengthening the Paris Agreement Through Collective Decisions: Achievements and Limitations
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its bottom‐up architecture, the Paris Agreement succeeded in securing broad participation but remained vulnerable to challenges concerning both the adequacy of national mitigation commitments and their implementation. This paper assesses the extent to which Parties to the Paris Agreement have succeeded in ensuring the effective functioning of the Paris framework through their collective decisions. It analyses two dimensions: the operationalisation of the Paris mechanisms and rules and the coordination of national efforts in the areas of mitigation pathways and climate finance.

abstract: FUNDAMENTOS // Las cohortes poblacionales permiten estudiar trayectorias de salud y bienestar en la infancia y la adolescencia, así como sus determinantes y su utilidad para orientar políticas públicas. title: Decolonizing the University: A Critical Exploration of the Rhodes Must Fall Movement and the Politics of Reckoning in Higher Education
abstract: The longstanding and ongoing liberation struggles for a decolonized African university, a search for a modern African identity, an epistemic citizenship, and an autonomous African development raised the question of decolonization when a Black student hurled a pail filled with human excrement against the Cecil John Rhodes statue at the University of Cape Town, South Africa, sparking the formation of the RMF movement on March 9, 2015. abstract: En este artículo presentamos un análisis descriptivo de corte cualitativo de los subtítulos en español europeo y en español latino de la miniserie británica Adolescence (Graham & Thorne, Netflix 2025). title: Effectiveness of a Virtual Reality Immersion Process as a Nonpharmacological Intervention for Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia and Immediate Well-Being in People Living in Nursing Homes: Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) are common among nursing home residents, notably those with Alzheimer disease and related diseases, impacting both themselves and health care professionals. Nonpharmacological interventions, including virtual reality (VR), have shown promise, but evidence from multicenter ecological studies remains limited. title: Alfonso de Cartagena: Defining a Moral System
abstract: The vision of the best form of government which Alfonso de Cartagena (1384–1456) defends in his writings is shaped by the character of the kingdom of Castile. He is keenly aware of the need to articulate a moral programme adapted to the circumstances of his time. title: Between Treaty Signature and Ratification: France and the 1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness
abstract: Abstract This article investigates the legal consequences of treaty signature not followed by ratification, focusing on France’s 64-year-old signature of the 1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness. France’s engagement with the 1961 Convention is unusual, raising multiple questions. abstract: This paper explores these connections- boxing, boxers of leadership, the ring, drama and knockout effects. It enunciates a metaphorical framework that equates leadership to boxing. title: When and How Do Women Directors Matter for Corporate Sustainability? The French Case
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines when and how board gender diversity matters for corporate sustainability. Using a sample of French listed firms over 2006–2024, we combine dynamic system GMM estimations with difference‐in‐differences tests around France's phased board gender quotas. The results show that greater female board representation is associated with stronger ESG performance, but that this relationship is highly contingent. title: A Systematic Investigation of Bias in Large Language Models for Advertising Relevance
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to judge how well an advertisement matches a query, but the fairness of these judgments has received limited attention. We conduct a systematic study of fairness in relevance judgments made by LLMs for queries and advertisements. Our counterfactual framework examines the effects of advertiser identity and possible popularity, input language, and demographic wording. title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
abstract: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. title: WorkflowOps: Learning Agent Collaboration Priors for Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestration
abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex knowledge work, yet their orchestration layers remain largely memoryless: each new task is decomposed, assigned, and executed from scratch with no benefit from prior successful executions. We present WorkflowOps, a multi-agent workflow orchestration framework that learns agent collaboration priors from historical workflows and expands its agent pool on demand to cover new capability requirements. title: Understanding the Hierarchical Structure and Functional Landscape of the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
abstract: AI agents increasingly rely on tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to complete user tasks. Hundreds of thousands of MCP servers are listed across marketplaces, yet they are organized only by coarse, marketplace-specific server categories. This makes it difficult for agents and users to identify tools for a given operation, find functional alternatives, and assess how those alternatives differ. abstract: AI-Native video creation is shifting from isolated video clips toward iterative video creation workflows. However, existing datasets remain largely video clips, representing video generation and editing as separate tasks rather than connected stages of a video creation workflow. In this paper, we introduce Sora100K, a dataset that represents the AI-Native video creation workflow as a structured video creation trajectory. title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness
abstract: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research (OEDR) systems primarily generate reports from scratch, making them inefficient for scenarios where research reports need to be continuously maintained as new information emerges. We introduce \textbf{Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research (Incremental-OEDR)}, a research setting that treats a report as an evolving research state and incrementally updates it by preserving valid knowledge, revising outdated or incomplete content, and incorporating newly available information. title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents
abstract: The Model Context Protocol provides a shared interaction substrate for the agentic web, allowing heterogeneous services to expose capabilities through a standardized interface. Learning to use this ecosystem entails a hierarchy of capabilities: tool-format skills, server-level transfer, and cross-server composition. We present MCPDisCo, an ecosystem-scale reinforcement learning framework for MCP-native agents. title: Distributed Model-Free Turbine Repositioning for Wake Overlap Minimization in Floating Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: This paper presents a model-free method for turbine repositioning control in floating offshore wind farms. The method uses a distributed online optimization framework to mitigate the wake effect. Conventional approaches rely on centralized, model-based control architectures, which suffer from poor practical feasibility. To overcome this limitation and address nonconvexity and inaccessible gradient information, we incorporate physics-informed knowledge of wake dynamics into the control system design. title: Debug2Fix: Can Interactive Debugging Help Coding Agents Fix More Bugs?
abstract: While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. Debugging and investigation of runtime behavior remains largely a manual, developer-driven process. Popular coding agents typically rely on either static analysis of the code or iterative test-fix cycles, which is akin to trial and error debugging. title: Log Density Spectrum Based Decoding of Polar Codes for Channels with Strong Phase Noise
abstract: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed in applications that act on users' long-term behavior histories, from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising systems. These applications demand the user dimension of LLM intelligence: inferring a person's preferences, intent, and likely future actions from weeks to years of behavior data. Yet current models are trained on static text or synthetic data, neither of which captures how user behavior evolves over time. title: Beyond the Transcriptome: Chromatin-Informed Prediction of Cell-State-Dependent Perturbation Responses
abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function. Existing predictors primarily rely on transcriptomic measurements, although chromatin accessibility provides complementary information about the cellular context in which perturbations act. Using this information requires linking chromatin context to specific perturbations and accounting for baseline differences between independently sampled control and perturbed populations. title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. title: Testuary: Agentic Test Generation with Zero-Shot Parallelism
abstract: Agentic approaches for automated test generation can reach high-quality results, but they improve a given test suite incrementally, so a weak starting point may lead to many iterations or insufficient tests. To address this, we present Testuary, which provides the agentic phases with an improved starting point. abstract: Norway’s outer border north of Svalbard crosses deep-sea plains in the Nansen Basin and onto the southern flank of the Gakkel Ridge. title: Enhancing AUV path planning via state-aware adaptive particle swarm optimization in complex marine environments
abstract: Path planning for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in complex marine environments requires an optimizer that can account for coupled path-quality and safety criteria while adapting its search behavior to individual particles. This paper proposes Adaptive Elite Particle Swarm Optimization (AEPSO) for three-dimensional marine environments that include seabed terrain, obstacles, and ocean currents. title: Optimisation-based motion control for AUVs under non-linear wave-current disturbances
abstract: With the increasing exploitation of marine resources, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are being applied more extensively in a variety of tasks, such as maritime search, rescue, and marine archaeology. The attitude stability of AUVs can be significantly disturbed by highly non-linear waves and currents near the sea surface, yet the influence of wave non-linearity on AUV motion and the associated control strategies remains insufficiently studied. title: Modular dual-critic reinforcement learning control for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in complex and uncertain ocean environments require reliable path-tracking and obstacle-avoidance capabilities to maintain safety in the presence of currents and obstacles. Traditional end-to-end deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods often struggle with coupled navigation objectives, which can lead to oscillatory control and unreliable trajectory recovery. title: A vision-based docking planning network for robust recovery of autonomous underwater vehicles
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) are core intelligent platforms in fields such as marine resource exploration and offshore engineering operations. Stable underwater autonomous recovery technology is crucial for ensuring the continuous safety and efficient operation of AUVs. During close-range docking, AUVs rely heavily on optical beacons for localization. abstract: This narrative review examines the design of power electronics for deep-sea energy and industrial systems, where converter performance is constrained by electrical demands and prolonged exposure to pressure, seawater, temperature cycling, and limited maintenance access. title: Low-cost single-beam SONAR localization in AUVs: Systematic experiments with acoustic and optical perception
abstract: This work presents a low-cost acoustic sensing framework for underwater localization and perception using single-beam sonars (SBS) and a forward-looking sonar (FLS). A Kalman filter (KF) based sensor fusion approach is developed to integrate SBS measurements with inertial sensing, incorporating pre-filtering and confidence-based gating to mitigate acoustic outliers and reflective disturbances. title: Consensus Collision‐Free Trajectory Planning for Multi‐AUV Formation Gathering
abstract: ABSTRACT Formation gathering of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is a fundamental prerequisite for cooperative underwater missions. It enables AUVs initially located at dispersed positions to form a prescribed geometric configuration before formation‐based exploration, observation, or survey tasks. title: Direct Acoustic Versus AUV-Assisted Hybrid Reporting for Subsea Pipeline Monitoring: A Matched End-to-End Evaluation
abstract: Subsea pipeline monitoring must deliver urgent alarms quickly while moving much larger inspection records over constrained underwater links. This creates a deployment choice: send all data through a prioritized acoustic network, or collect routine records with an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) undertaking a finite collection mission. title: SA-SRDC-Loc: Single-AUV-assisted three-dimensional underwater localization via selective residual distance learning and depth-constrained robust optimization
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional localization in underwater acoustic sensor networks remains challenging because irregular acoustic propagation and multi-hop connectivity weaken the relationship between network topology and physical distance. This paper proposes SA-SRDC-Loc, a single-AUV-assisted localization framework that treats successive AUV reports as temporally ordered observations of one continuously moving platform rather than as independent anchors. title: Nonlinear hydrodynamic coupling effects of free-surface and bottom boundaries on an AUV
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) frequently operate in shallow waters, where they are simultaneously subjected to the coupling effects of free-surface wave-making and bottom boundary restrictions. Existing studies have primarily focused on single-boundary conditions, leaving the complex, non-linear coupled hydrodynamics in dual-boundary shallow water environments insufficiently understood. title: Integrating model predictive control and reinforcement learning for robust Six-DOF AUV trajectory tracking
abstract: To address model uncertainties, ocean-current disturbances, and real-time control requirements in six-degree-of-freedom AUV trajectory tracking, this paper proposes a residual-learning-enhanced MPC–PID hierarchical control framework. An outer-loop kinematic model predictive controller generates constraint-aware velocity references, while an inner-loop inverse-dynamics PID controller provides nominal dynamic compensation and fast velocity tracking. title: Frequency-adaptive wave disturbance observation and prescribed performance fast super-twisting control for ROV station-keeping
abstract: This paper addresses the station-keeping control problem of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) under near-surface head-sea conditions, where narrow-band wave disturbances induce significant periodic motion. Instead of treating wave effects as unstructured lumped disturbances, a frequency-adaptive disturbance rejection framework is proposed by combining EKF-based frequency estimation, harmonic extended state observation, and prescribed-performance fast super-twisting sliding mode control. abstract: To fulfill the requirements for rapid development of high-performance AUV motion control systems, a three-dimensional (3D) path- following control system is designed and implemented based on the MOOS-IvP/ArduSub architecture. Using Lyapunov stability theory, an adaptive line-of-sight (ALOS) guidance law with variable look-ahead distances (VΔ-ALOS) is designed. title: Underwater Platform for Long-Term Observation Using a Cable-Restricted Underwater Vehicle and Its Design Concept for Trajectory Planning
abstract: Long-term and repeated observation of shallow seafloor environments is required to evaluate temporal changes in seagrass meadows and other coastal ecosystems. In this study, we propose a cable-restricted observation system consisting of an underwater vehicle, a tether cable, and a seafloor station equipped with a reel. abstract: Autonomous visual tracking of a moving target by a rudderless underwater vehicle is complicated by nonlinear dynamics, intermittent visual observations, environmental currents, and constrained distributed thrust. This paper combines a recurrent SAC–LSTM policy with a finite-horizon model-based residual correction. title: Breeding emperor penguins show interannual recurrence in shelf-break associated foraging areas across contrasting sea ice conditions in the northwestern Weddell Sea
abstract: Abstract The emperor penguin Aptenodytes forsteri is highly sea ice dependent and vulnerable to climate change, yet the at-sea distribution and habitat associations of breeding adults remain poorly understood for colonies in the western Weddell Sea. We tracked nine breeding adults from Snow Hill Island, the northernmost known colony, during chick-rearing in 2023-24 and 2025-26, and analysed 38 foraging trips using kernel utilisation distributions, habitat-selection models and hidden Markov models. abstract: For autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), SINS/DVL/USBL integrated navigation provides continuous underwater positioning. However, multipath propagation, non-line-of-sight (NLOS) effects, and prolonged USBL outages can degrade acoustic measurements and yield innovations with heavy tails. abstract: This study presents solutions utilizing varying degrees of autonomy in seaport operational systems, including port infrastructure, environmental monitoring systems and autonomous equipment for transshipment terminals. title: Navigating Inuit concerns: assessing management options for expedition cruise tourism in Nunavut waters
abstract: This paper examines the governance and regulatory frameworks for expedition cruise tourism in the Canadian Arctic, with a particular focus on Nunavut. The aim of the study was to assess effectiveness among these frameworks in addressing previously identified concerns among Inuit communities about increased marine navigation activities across their homeland. title: Deep reinforcement learning-based path following of a bio-inspired autonomous underwater vehicle under ocean currents
abstract: Bio-inspired autonomous underwater vehicles (BI-AUVs) offer high propulsive efficiency and maneuverability by imitating fish morphology and locomotion. However, oscillatory fin motion and fluid–structure interactions generate nonlinear hydrodynamic forces, making model-based controller design under environmental disturbances challenging. This study proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based path-following framework for ocean currents conditions. title: A review of the development, research progress and key challenges in underwater bionic soft robotics
abstract: Conventional rigid underwater robots possess high structural stiffness and exhibit a single mode of locomotion, showing poor adaptability in complex flow fields, narrow spaces and eco-friendly underwater operations. In recent years, underwater bionic soft robots have achieved rapid development boasting a rich variety of bionic prototypes as well as innovative actuation and control strategies. abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric deposition of the essential micronutrient, iron (Fe), can have an important influence on primary production and marine biogeochemistry. abstract: Cold seeps are natural “outcrop” evidence of marine gas hydrates and represent one of the most direct indicators of gas hydrate occurrence. abstract: To elucidate the mechanism limiting wave-glider speed under high sea states, a hydrodynamic model of the semi-passive submerged glider was developed. abstract: Abstract Arctic Ocean (AO) shelf permafrost is the most popular and best-known type of subsea permafrost. Genetically, it is analogous to the ordinary subaerial permafrost. abstract: Corrosion considerably affects the safety and life cycle of underwater vehicles. title: Underwater Relative Pose Estimation and Tracking Between AUVs Based on a Hull-Integrated Laser-Beam Marker
abstract: Close-range tracking between autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) requires continuous six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) relative pose feedback, yet target boards and protruding light arrays are difficult to integrate into compact streamlined hulls. title: Response-Tunable Adaptive LOS-Based Guidance for Depth-Tracking Control of Underactuated AUVs in the Presence of Time-Varying Disturbances
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) have been extensively employed in diverse marine applications, where depth-tracking control remains a critical technical challenge. Although previous studies have investigated various guidance law designs for underactuated AUVs, compensation for the attack-angle effect induced by heave velocity remains underexplored, particularly in the presence of extreme time-varying external disturbances and sharp path curvature variations. title: Role-Guided Risk-Aware Attention for Multi-AUV Target-Zone Reaching under Active Defense
abstract: Cooperative target-zone reaching by multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) under active defense remains challenging because each vehicle must make sequential guidance decisions under nonlinear hydrodynamics, sonar-limited perception, obstacle constraints, and defender interference. This paper proposes a role-guided risk-aware attention variant of multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG), termed role-guided risk-aware attention MADDPG (RGRA-MADDPG), for attacker-side multi-AUV target-zone reaching under active defense. title: Near-Bottom Currents at DeepInsight Hill (Mohns Ridge) from In Situ Measurements, Global Ocean Models, and Biological Flow Indicators
abstract: Characterizing near-bottom ocean currents at deep-sea topographic features requires observations across multiple scales, from basin-wide circulation models to local in situ measurements. This study addresses this challenge at DeepInsight Hill, on Mohns Ridge, by combining eight months of in situ current measurements, global ocean model predictions, and novel ROV-based biological flow indicators. The flow regime shows a striking decoupling between tidal pressure and near-bottom currents. title: Online health monitoring framework of deep-sea UUVs via multi-sensor fusion and Koopman operator-based residual inference
abstract: Deep-sea unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) depend on reliable propulsion systems during cruising, docking, and observation missions. However, online propulsion health monitoring remains challenging because high-frequency reference states are difficult to obtain in real time, while the nonlinear dynamics of UUVs make the relationship between thruster inputs and state responses difficult to characterize accurately. title: From surface to deep sea: A depth-resolved vertical profile of microplastics in the Canary Basin
abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination of the open ocean is well documented, yet the vertical structuring of MPs and the role of water masses in shaping deep-water inventories remain poorly resolved along the eastern boundary of the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre. Here we present a high-resolution vertical profile of MPs in the Canary Basin, based on discrete water samples collected during the MSM/127 cruise (R/V Maria S. abstract: Abstract The reconstruction of past marine bottom-water redox conditions are crucial because it reflects changes in ocean circulation, surface productivity, and the precipitation–evaporation balance. However, long-term (Myr scale), high-resolution (mm scale), redox reconstructions remain scarce because traditional discrete-sample analyses are highly time-consuming. While the Japan Sea is known for past high-frequency fluctuations of deep-water redox conditions, the existing records are limited to the past 640 kyr at a relatively low resolution. title: Interplay between fluids, seismic and aseismic deformation concurrently to a Mw 4.6 earthquake in the western part of the Sea of Marmara
abstract: Summary The North Anatolian Fault (NAF) in the Sea of Marmara is characterized by varying mechanical behaviors and fluid manifestations along its path. In the present study, we investigate an earthquake sequence including a Mw 4.6 earthquake that occurred on November 27, 2013, in the partially creeping section of the NAF in the Sea of Marmara. title: Exploring the Quellerflächen: Knowledge production on Danish internal colonial expeditions to Schleswig's west coast, 1859–1863
abstract: Between 1859 and 1863, Danish government official Arthur Earl of Reventlow traveled to North Frisia several times to explore possible ways to develop new agricultural areas in the Wadden Sea. Although expeditions have become a focus in the history of science, little research has addressed the journeys of officials into state peripheries. While these did not travel to “exotic” landscapes like conventional expeditions, their goals were nearly identical: to expand knowledge and increase control over areas where state authority was weak. title: Life at the edge: Planktic foraminiferal distribution through the California Current Oxygen Minimum Zone
abstract: Abstract Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs) are expanding globally, reshaping marine ecosystems, and creating physiologically challenging conditions for many marine organisms. Vulnerable communities will likely shift toward taxa adapted to low-oxygen conditions. Such adaptations are rare in eukaryotes, but some foraminiferal taxa can survive, and even calcify, in severely oxygen-depleted environments. title: Shipborne Measurements of Mineral Dust and Black Carbon Aerosols Over the Southern Ocean in the Austral Summer
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric mineral dust and black carbon (BC) aerosols play important roles in the Earth's climate system, yet direct observations over the Southern Ocean (SO) are scarce. In this study, we present the characteristics of airborne water‐insoluble particles (WIPs) collected during a cruise of the R/V Shirase in the Australian and Indian sectors of the SO from December 2022 to March 2023. title: The Leviathan's Reckoning
abstract: Set in 1847 during the peak of the North Atlantic whaling industry, The Leviathan's Reckoning presents a poignant narrative of human greed, moral tension, and nature's retribution. Driven by an insatiable hunger for whale oil profit, Captain Fred Winston of the brig Sea Serpent ignores an elderly fisherman's stern warnings regarding the cursed waters of Death Valley, going so far as ordering the innocent man's demise to protect his commercial interests. abstract: The bryoflora of Ryazhkov Island (408 ha) has been supplemented by 9 new moss species (Anomodon viticulosus, Dicranum leioneuron, D. septentrionale, Drepanocladus polygamus, Fissidens adianthoides, Pseudoleskeella papillosa, Scorpidium cossonii, Sphagnum fimbriatum, S. subfulvum), the first of which is included in the Red Data Book of Murmansk Region [2025]. title: Remote shores: Shellfish gathering in the Kodiak Archipelago, Gulf of Alaska
abstract: Geographic isolation, local ecology, and cultural context mediate shellfish use in the Gulf of Alaska. Chirikof Island, located at the southwest end of the Kodiak Archipelago in the central Gulf of Alaska, provides an excellent example of subsistence in a place of extreme isolation and exposure. Previous archaeological survey has suggested that Alutiiq and possibly Unangax̂ peoples lived on Chirikof for short periods over the past 4500 years, where they came to hunt local fauna. RATES OF CHANGES IN THE POPULATION OF SEMIBALANUS BALANOIDES (L.) FOR TWO TYPES OF LANDSCAPE OF TERIBERSKAYA BAY DURING CLIMATE WARMING
abstract: A method for early detecting of climate-related changes in littoral communities has been developed using bioindication based on the dynamics of estuarine populations of the barnacle Semibalanus balanoides (Crustacea, Cirripedia). It has been established that climate-related changes in barnacle abundance depend on the slope and topography of the biotope. The population's response to environmental changes in a littoral biotope with a significant steep occurs later and is less pronounced than in a biotope with a flat landscape.

title: Strain Spectral Features of Internal Waves in Prydz Bay, Antarctica
abstract: Abstract Internal wave (IW) spectrum serves as a fundamental tool for characterizing IW fields, understanding their underlying dynamics and quantifying IW-driven mixing. Prydz Bay, as one of the critical hubs for energy transfer and water properties exchange in the Southern Ocean, however, remains poorly studied in terms of its IW spectrum. title: Stratigraphic Geochemical Variations in Western Pacific Fe–Mn Crusts: Controls of Phosphatization on Element Redistribution
abstract: Ferromanganese (Fe–Mn) crusts are important archives of long-term oceanographic and redox conditions, but post-depositional phosphatization can alter their primary hydrogenetic geochemical signatures. This study investigates mineralogical and geochemical variations among representative stratigraphic layers in Fe–Mn crust cores recovered from western Pacific seamounts to better understand the effects of phosphatization on crust evolution. abstract: Based on material collected during the 2021 expedition of the MMBI RAS to Grønfjord Bay (Spitsbergen), the species composition and structure of polychaete taxocenes were analyzed. The distribution of polychaete taxocenes in Grønfjord Bay exhibits distinct zonation, caused by the transition from stable habitats at great depths to the variable conditions of shallow periglacial areas. title: Critical raw material concentrations in the Antarctic Peninsula and recalibration of the potential ecological risk index for polar regions
abstract: Critical raw materials (CRMs) are emerging inorganic pollutants because of their technological use and release into remote marine environments. However, their occurrence, distribution, and ecological significance in Antarctic waters remain poorly understood, and existing risk indices have not been adapted for CRMs in these systems. This study investigated selected CRMs in surface waters collected from 21 stations across the Antarctic Peninsula and Horseshoe Island during three consecutive Turkish Antarctic Expeditions (2023-2025). title: Hydroacoustic Recordings During a Submarine Seismic Swarm near Torishima Island: Comparing CTBT IMS Hydrophones and JAMSTEC Fiber-Optic Strainmeters
abstract: Abstract On 08 October 2023, a series of submarine earthquakes that took place in the Izu-Ogasawara Islands, Japan, excited at least 14 hydroacoustic signals (i.e., T -waves or H -waves) over a period of three hours. These signals were detected by the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) International Monitoring System (IMS) hydrophone station HA11 at Wake Island. title: Dynamic UAV-based search operations using probabilistic diffusion modeling of Man Overboard incident victims
abstract: More than 70% of the people that fell overboard cruise ships in the period 2010–2019 lost their lives (CLIA, 2025) . This paper presents a strategy for reliably predicting the area a person may be in after a man overboard incident, and describes in detail the search methods to find them utilizing UAV technology. The search area prediction method employs an Extended Kalman Filter that capitalizes on the information from the Leeway model to track the missing person in the sea by taking into account the uncertainty of the movement of the person and the weather conditions in the area. abstract: This paper presents a benchmark study of linear wave-induced motions and global loads, organised by the MARSTRUCT Virtual Institute with the objective of quantifying the hydrodynamic modelling uncertainty and its consequences for extreme load prediction across different hull forms. This is a follow-up to a benchmark study Parunov et al. title: New Ocinaropsis from West Africa (Lepidoptera, Lasiocampidae)
abstract: The second species of the African genus Ocinaropsis Aurivillius, 1905, Ocinaropsis tinubu sp. n., is described from West Africa. It occurs in the West Sudanian savanna ecoregion, spanning from eastern Senegal to northern Ghana, and the Guinean forest-savanna ecoregion in northern Nigeria. The type species of the genus, Ocinaropsis obscura Aurivillius, 1905, is reportedly found in the KwaZulu-Natal–Cape coastal forests ecoregion in South Africa and the Maputaland coastal forests and woodlands ecoregion in southern Mozambique, over 4500 km away from the new species. title: Moving-Window Weighted Least Squares with Edge Optimization for Schuler Oscillation Suppression in Inertial Navigation Systems
abstract: To address the reliance of damping-network-based Schuler oscillation suppression on external aids in pure inertial navigation systems, as well as the edge effects and low computational efficiency of time–frequency transform methods, this paper proposes a moving-window weighted least-squares edge optimization (MWLS-EO) algorithm. title: Locomotion and hunting strategies of large vertebrate predators in pelagic waters
abstract: Many of the key dynamics that shape predator-prey interactions are governed by the physical and physiological principles which determine how animals move and perform in their environments. This opinion paper outlines the foundations underlying marine vertebrate predator-prey encounters within the context of pelagic habitats. Variables, such as maximum swimming speed, acceleration and manoeuvrability, play crucial roles in dictating the outcome of predator-prey encounters. title: BATHYMETRIC DISTRIBUTION OF SHELL-BEARING GASTROPODA OF THE COAST OF NOVAYA ZEMLYA
abstract: The bathymetric gradient plays an important role in the formation of the structure of marine bottom communities. In this paper, the bathymetric distribution of shell Gastropoda off the coast of the Novaya Zemlya archipelago is analyzed. The change in species richness in depth shows the greatest decrease in the number of species in the range of 60–100 m. title: Morphological Study of Some Reptadeonella Busk, 1884 (Bryozoa, Cheilostomatida) From Brazil With the Description of Two New Species and an Updated Identification Key to the Genus
abstract: Reptadeonella Busk, 1884, is one of the most common bryozoan genera reported from warm waters across all oceans and is currently represented by 29 species. Almost half of this diversity has been described in the past 10 years, including the recognition of 12 new species and documentation of morphological variations. In this work, we analyzed types of some Reptadeonella already reported from Brazil and more than 60 newly collected specimens, including comparisons between newly budded (young) and mature zooids to assess ontogenetic variation within species and colonies. title: Exploring Spitsbergen’s Potential for Sustainable Development and Geopark Creation
abstract: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. title: Multiyear dual-isotope fingerprinting at South Asian receptor sites constrains carbon monoxide sources and enhanced oxidation
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. Based on nine winter-long dual-isotope campaigns at two South Asian receptor sites intercepting the continental outflow, we quantified CO source contributions and emission–sink dynamics. title: Global length–weight relationships of deep‐pelagic fishes: Coverage, biases and variability
abstract: Length-weight relationships (LWRs) are morphometric tools that allow body mass to be estimated from fish length, providing input for fisheries, ecological and biodiversity studies. For deep-pelagic fishes, however, LWR data remain fragmented and unavailable for most species. Here, we present a global synthesis of LWRs for deep-pelagic fishes, consolidating available data into a single harmonised dataset and mapping taxonomic and geographic gaps. title: A reliability analysis method for Christmas tree in operating conditions based on FEMCA, FTA and numerical simulation
abstract: The installation and recovery process of Christmas tree is complex and technically difficult, and it bears high internal and external loads during production and has extremely high requirements for operation reliability. To ensure the safe operation of China's first domestically produced deepwater subsea Christmas tree installation and production conditions, a reliability analysis method for Christmas tree in operating conditions based on FEMCA, FTA and numerical simulation is established. title: Biostratigraphy of the Famennian Makarovian Regional Substage (Devonian, South Urals)
abstract: The paper presents a bed-by-bed description and paleontological characteristics of the carbonate deposits within the stratotype area of the Makarovian Regional Substage (Famennian), including Cheiloceras ammonoid and Zilimia polonica brachiopod beds. The authors have studied two sections located along the Sikasya and Ryauzyak river valleys on the western slope of the South Urals. In the stratotype area, the Makarovian is composed entirely of polymictic bioclastic limestone. title: Pharmakos and Sacrificial Womanhood: The Politics of Social Order in Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu’s the Legendary Inikpi
abstract: Communal survival, gender, tragedy and sacrifice are recurring subject matter in Greek and Igala cultural and literary traditions. This study compares Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu's The Legendary Inikpi to examine how sacrificial womanhood is constructed and used to sustain social order within two distinct cultural logics.
