title: Exploring supply chain management challenges in food provisioning on maritime training vessels: post-consumer food waste and the potential role of digitalisation
abstract: Achieving sustainable consumption at sea requires understanding the organisational mechanisms that shape food provisioning under uncertainty. Using a mixed-methods case study of a maritime training vessel, this study combines semi-structured interviews with key provisioning stakeholders and an exploratory survey of student–cadets to examine the organisational mechanisms generating plate waste and the potential contribution of digitalisation to more sustainable provisioning. title: Accounting and Maritime Accounting: Differences and Relationships
abstract: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. Maritime accounting refers to accounting practices adapted to shipping, port, marine, and fisheries industries. However, its conceptual boundaries and scope remain insufficiently defined in the literature. abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of cultural tourism in safeguarding regional history and ethnic identity, focusing on the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Arts in Nukus, Uzbekistan. Known globally as the "Louvre of the Desert," the museum holds a unique dual repository consisting of the world's second-largest collection of Soviet avant-garde art and an extensive archive of traditional Karakalpak applied arts alongside ancient Khorezm archaeological antiquities. title: Latent Gestures: Autobiographical Perception and Queer Recognition in the South East Archive of Seaside Photography
abstract: This practice-based paper examines how embodied, queer and neurodivergent modes of perception shape the interpretation of photographic archives. Focusing on Latent: A Hidden History, a project developed through the South East Archive of Seaside Photography (SEAS), it explores how mid-twentieth-century seaside photographs, produced under the social and legal constraints of male homosexuality, can be reengaged through sustained acts of photographic looking. title: Conservation Messages as Catalysts of Post-Visit Action: Insights from Zoo and Aquarium Visitors
abstract: Zoos and aquariums face an urgent challenge to convey conservation messages that motivate visitors to change their environmental behavior. This study explores the reflections of 768 visitors to one of twelve zoos and aquariums in Australia, USA, and Canada regarding the features of conservation messaging that prompted their post-visit involvement in specific environmental behaviors. Thematic analysis uncovered eight features of conservation messaging that visitors felt prompted them to adopt new behaviors or increase their engagement in existing environmental actions. title: Upper Palaeolithic mariners? Evaluating experimental evidence for intentional early seafaring
abstract: Brought to popular consciousness by Thor Heyerdahl in the 1940s, the role of seafaring in human migration has been intensely debated. Aiming to stimulate discussion around the ways in which experimental archaeology is used to support such grand narratives, the authors of this debate critically assess a recent claim for Upper Palaeolithic seafaring in the Japanese archipelago. Here, they argue that creating a boat for which there is no archaeological evidence with generic tools that were not widely available in the region risks a confounding circularity of logic.

abstract: ABSTRACT The first zoea of two Synalpheus species, namely: S. antillensis and S. cf. townsendi , are herein described. They were also compared with the genus descriptions and with their respective species complexes available in the literature. Morphological information on Synalpheus zoea I exhibits an increase from 19 to 21 species, and it corresponds to 12% of the total number of species. title: Impacts of the 2026 US-Iran War on Environmental Security in the Middle East
abstract: Modern warfare does not merely inflict human casualties; it also degrades the environmental systems vital for daily life. The 2026 US-Iran conflict poses a severe threat to regional ecosystems, as belligerents deliberately target critical infrastructure and weaponize natural resources to secure military advantages or compel concessions. Oil and gas tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside refineries and energy installations throughout Iran and the Arab Gulf states, have emerged as primary targets. abstract: After the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality were put forward, the pressure of emission reduction in the shipping industry has been accelerated to transmit to ports, and the green and low-carbon transformation of mechanical and electrical equipment has thus become an important starting point for the implementation of emission reduction. title: Relocating Large Hollow‐Bearing Tree Trunk Sections to Restore Forest Owl Breeding Habitat: When Is It Warranted?
abstract: ABSTRACT Relocating large hollows to minimise the potential impacts of development on threatened species is generally considered too difficult and/or too costly. Small and medium‐sized hollows are commonly relocated, recreated by carving into a living surrogate tree, or replaced with nest boxes; however, larger hollows, which take much longer to form naturally, are far less represented in the landscape, are preferred over nest boxes by large forest owls, are being destroyed during vegetation clearing and are not being replaced. title: Evaluation of Seed Viability and Quality for Santigi (Pemphis acidula J.R. Forst and G. Forst) Conservation: Assessing the Effect of Chemical and Physical Scarification
abstract: Pemphis acidula J.R.Forst. and G. Forst. or santigi is a plant native to Indonesia, widely recognized for its high economic value. Although listed as Least Concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), its existence in the wild is increasingly threatened by land degradation, climate change, and it suffers from low natural seed germination rates. This study aimed to evaluate the seed viability and quality of P. acidula and assess the effectiveness of chemical and physical scarification techniques on the viability of santigi seeds. title: The Phantom Naturalist: What do we know about the nineteenth-century natural history collector Alfred Crossley?
abstract: Born in Halifax, UK, in 1839, and shipwrecked on Madagascar as a youth, Alfred Crossley had returned to the island by 1869 and in the ensuing eight years made hugely important collections of mammals, birds, butterflies, and other natural history specimens. Many of these are now in major museums in the UK and Europe (including numerous holotypes), but unknown quantities went to private collectors and are now lost. title: Ruth Stephan’s Andean Journey: The Peña Pancho Fierro and Transnational Indigenism in The Tiger’s Eye Magazine
abstract: In 1946, shortly after World War II, U.S. poet Ruth Stephan travelled to Peru seeking artistic direction. In Lima, she joined the indigenist avant-garde of the Peña Pancho Fierro, led by Alicia and Celia Bustamante and José María Arguedas. title: ECOCRITICAL AND ECOTOURISM ANALYSIS OF EBIET SONGS
abstract: This study examines the ecocritical dimension and the potential of ecotourism in the lyrics of Ebiet G. Ade, an Indonesian musician known for his sensitivity to humanitarian and environmental issues. Using an ecocritical approach, this study aims to explore how Ebiet's songs represent the ecological crisis, the relationship between humans and nature, and spiritual reflections on natural disasters that occur in Indonesia. title: A Love Made of Stones: Contemporary Anishinaabe Lyric and Asiniig Sovereignty
abstract: This article delves into the literary motif of the stone (asiniig) in contemporary Anishinaabe poetry as an ontological assertion of Indigenous sovereignty. By synthesising Michelle Raheja’s “visual sovereignty” (2007) and Kenneth White’s “geopoetics” (1979; 2004), I trace how poets Kimberly Blaeser, Louise Erdrich, and Denise Sweet deploy an Indigenous geopoetics that challenges settler-colonial cartographies. title: The social life of viruses: a queer sort of science
abstract: A burgeoning microbiology field, sociovirology is the study of how viruses interact with one another and the effects such interactions have on social evolution. Challenging dominant narratives that viruses are individualistic pathogens, sociovirologists explore the social interaction of viruses through the language of cooperation, altruism, and cheating, social concepts with biological definitions. abstract: The article analyzes the current state and prospects of implementing fiber-optic technologies in unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) as an effective response to the challenges of modern electronic warfare. Their potential applications are considered both in the field of intelligence gathering and for the delivery of explosives to designated targets.The classification features of drones are systematized, their main functional purposes are defined, and the advantages and limitations of traditional radio-controlled systems are examined. title: Influence Without Alliances: China, Pakistan, and Indirect Military Engagement in the Persian Gulf
abstract: This article examines how China expands security influence in the Persian Gulf without alliances, bases, or direct intervention. It introduces indirect military engagement to explain influence through technology diffusion, defence-industrial cooperation, intermediary partnerships, and partner adaptation. Focusing on Pakistan, it argues that Chinese systems gain regional relevance through Pakistani absorption, localisation, training, maintenance, and demonstration. title: Modern Air Operations and Wylie’s Cumulative and Sequential Operational Patterns
abstract: Strategist Joseph Caldwell Wylie argued that strategies were implemented through two general types of operational patterns: sequential and cumulative. This article discusses the conceptualisations of these two patterns and then applies them to three modern air war cases to bring out their subtleties and nuances. Wylie’s simple typology has a surprising depth that makes it useful to air strategists when considering future air operations whether in peace of war.

title: Etymologies of Australian reptiles
abstract: Australia, covering almost 7.7 million km2 (3 million mi2), is a mega-biodiverse region with 19 recognised families, 164 genera, six subgenera, 1152 species, and 60 subspecies of reptiles. This study resolves the etymologies of their scientific names (nomina). Most generic and subgeneric names (69%) are derived from Greek, while half (50%) of species and subspecies originate from Latin. Greek-derived names are more often composites than Latin-derived ones. abstract: Libya, one of the largest countries in North Africa, is characterized by a Mediterranean climate along its northern coast and an extensive hot desert climate across much of its territory. These environmental conditions provide suitable habitats for a diverse assemblage of scorpion species adapted to arid ecosystems. Despite this ecological suitability, the scorpion fauna of Libya remains inadequately documented, with previous studies largely restricted to individual species or limited geographic regions. title: A review of the southern African spider beetle genus Scaleptinus Borowski, 2006 (Coleoptera: Ptinidae: Ptininae) and notes on their unusual male genitalia
abstract: The spider beetle genus Scaleptinus Borowski, 2006 (Coleoptera: Ptinidae: Ptininae) was created to reclassify two morphologically distinct, scale-covered species of Ptinus known from the arid western regions of Namibia and South Africa. In this same publication, two new species, S. beardae and S. similis, were each described from single male specimens. Morphological examination reveals that S. beardae is within the range of morphological variation seen in S. squamulosus and is here proposed as a junior synonym. title: Apatite Geochemistry as a Key to Typification and Petrogenesis of Pegmatites from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
abstract: Apatite is a sensitive indicator of magmatic and post-magmatic processes in granitic and pegmatitic systems. This study investigates accessory apatite from different types of pegmatites and granites of Larsemann Hills (East Antarctica) in order to classify the pegmatites and reconstruct their formation conditions. The results show the Types I and III pegmatites crystallized at higher temperatures than Type IV pegmatites with miarolitic cavities and the Progress granites. abstract: This research article analyzes the lifestyle and economic activities of the population of Dingilji—a historical and cultural center in the lower reaches of the Amu Darya River—including the history of their involvement in viticulture. title: Development's Race Problem: Post‐Black Lives Matter Erasures, Palestine and the Politics of Publishing
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite efforts by critical scholars of development to centre race in their analysis, Development Studies remains entangled in its racist history and contemporary imperialism. New troubling forms of oppression and control within the discipline's approach to race have emerged, marking the post‐Black Lives Matter era as a point of transition between old and new erasures of race. We argue that although race is no longer ignored, the discursive and material boundaries within which it can be discussed have been erected through silencing, censorship, regulation and appropriation. title: Further revisions to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks, with a response to Sternes et al. (2024)
abstract: One specimen of Otodus auriculatus and three specimens of O. megalodon are added to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks. Criticisms of the Lamnoidea hypothesis and reconstruction of Cretalamna sp. by Sternes et al. (2024) are responded to. Included is discussion of the validity of rostra, regional endothermy, and bauplans as evidence for the Otodontidae + Lamnidae clade, as well as phylogenetic analyses incorporating these families. This is the third installment in a series of papers compiling the catalogue.

abstract: Conversations about student debt frequently target attendees of four-year and professional institutions, since higher-cost institutions are more likely to lead to high levels of debt. While some research has focused on financial aid and college funding at community colleges, we have comparatively limited scholarship regarding conceptualizations of student debt. title: Predominance of Externally Mixed Black Carbon Over the Tibetan Plateau During the Asian Summer Monsoon
abstract: Abstract The mixing state of black carbon (BC) strongly influences its lifetime and radiative forcing over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). Previous observations, mostly conducted during the non‐monsoon season, suggested that thickly coated BC dominates due to long‐range transport from South Asia. Here we report near‐surface BC mixing state measurements during the 2021–2023 summer monsoons at seven sites across the central–southern TP. title: Disney's Location Strategy in China: Balancing Global Brand Identity and Local Adaptation
abstract: Multinational companies face a persistent tension between maintaining a consistent global brand identity and adapting to local consumer preferences. Disney's long-term presence in China provides a useful observation sample for examining this issue. Since the opening of Shanghai Disneyland in 2016, Disney has accumulated substantial operational experience in the Chinese market. This article examines how Disney has adapted to the Chinese market while maintaining its core brand identity. title: Ampliación del rango de distribución de Thyroptera discifera en Bolivia y registro más austral
abstract: En el Neotrópico, los únicos murciélagos que poseen discos de succión en los pulgares y patas traseras pertenecen a la familia Thyropteridae. De las 5 especies descritas para el género, solo Thyroptera tricolor y T. discifera están presentes en Bolivia. While enhancing performance, the swirl distortion induced by such inlets severely restricts engine performance and operational stability. title: Inventory and Diversity of Macroscopic Fungi in the University of Bengkulu Campus Area
abstract: Fungal diversity is an important component in maintaining ecosystem balance, especially in campus environments that have a variety of habitats such as soil, litter, and vegetation. title: Lontaraq: Script Its History, Development, And Spread
abstract: This article aims to reconstruct the origin, development, and spread of the Lontaraq script, the only script still in use among those once employed in South Sulawesi. title: Pre-Colonial Trade in a Border Region: A Case Study of Illela-Konni Trade Relations, 1700-1900 A.D
abstract: This paper examines Illela and Konni trade relations from 1700 to 1900 and argued that the relations are influenced by geographical and historical factors. The objective of the paper is to analyse how these factors shaped trade between the two towns. Through a critical analysis of oral interviews, archival records, travellers' accounts, and relevant secondary literature, the paper found out that variations in climate, soil, vegetation and resource endowments created patterns of comparative production that encouraged sustained exchange in grains and livestock which in turn developed the trade.

abstract: The article considers the application of the concept of linguistic worldview in translation education at the university level from the perspectives of both the teacher and the students. Special attention is paid to those dimensions of translation that linguistic worldview can help elucidate, and thus help to formulate a strategic approach that balances creativity with awareness of the cultural specificity of the source material. By treating the source text as an expression of a specific linguistic worldview, students can gain increasingly more sensitivity to intercultural and pragmatic aspects

abstract: Argument A history of “common sense” concerns as much the epistemological concept as the very architecture of human rational judgment. The historian of medieval philosophy Étienne Gilson (1884–1978) cast nineteenth-century Jesuit appeals to common sense as a costly defense against the Cartesian problem of certainty: when intellectual first principles are fused with sensus communis , metaphysical realism is at risk. title: Western Media Representation of Africa: The Role of Bad Governance
abstract: The Western media's depiction of Africa has long been entrenched in a narrow and conclusively negative narrative. Even in the digital age, mainstream Western outlets continue to present stories from Africa through a lens that perpetuates outdated stereotypes, portraying the continent as mired in a "dark age"characterised by archaic practices and perpetual strife. title: From Fragmentation to Routinization: The European Union’s Collective Securitization of Russia, 2014–2022
abstract: This article examines the European Union’s collective securitization of Russia across two critical junctures: the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Why did the EU, long energy-dependent and internally divided, adopt substantial but fragmented measures that changed little in 2014, yet achieve unprecedented unity, scope, and institutionalization after 2022? title: Attributes of the destination image of Vietnam for international tourists
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research is to synthesize specific attributes of the destination image of Vietnam as perceived by international tourists by reviewing previous works from 2008 to 2022. This paper aims to address the following research questions (adopted from Echtner and Ritchie, 1993): What images or characteristics come to international tourists' minds when they think of Vietnam as a tourist destination? title: Trascendencia en ciencia ficción: análisis comparativo de la Saga Ringworld y Childhood’s End
abstract: This paper examines the connections between science fiction and religion through the lens of transcendence in two iconic works: Ringworld by Larry Niven and Childhood’s End by Arthur C. Clarke. Using the concept of the novum as a starting point, it explores how both authors interpret transcendence from a secular perspective that nonetheless carries strong religious associations. title: Together we stand: challenging the effects of international sanctions on Iran–Russia regional cooperation, 2007–2024
abstract: This article examines the evolving Iran–Russia strategic partnership within the context of prolonged sanctions, shifting regional power dynamics, and the decline of US-led unipolarity. It argues that shared pariah status and opposition to Western hegemony have fostered a pragmatic alliance spanning political, military, and economic domains, while sanctions have reshaped regional alignments and encouraged alternative connectivity initiatives such as the International North–South Transport Corridor. title: Taxonomic revision of Vaccinium myrtillus (Ericaceae)
abstract: Vaccinium myrtillus has commonly been recognized as encompassing plants from Eurasia, Japan, and North America. Published molecularbased phylogenetic data, however, suggest that V. myrtillus is not monophyletic and might best be divided into distinct taxonomic entities. I examined herbarium specimens collected from throughout the range of V. myrtillus s.l., finding morphological characters that serve to justify the division of V. myrtillus into such entities. title: A Psychological Data Analysis of Female Filipino Domestic Workers with a History of Suicide Attempts: Basis for Mental Health Program
abstract: Filipino domestic workers have been known to endure various challenges inherent to overseas employment, which may contribute to elevated psychological distress and suicidal behavior within this population. However, existing mental health programs are deemed insufficient due to their lack of long-term effectiveness and tailored approach. abstract: Abstract Vervaeke and Mastropietro’s 4P model of knowing is a non-representational and process-oriented framework that integrates four interrelated ways of knowing: propositional, procedural, perspectival, and participatory. In this paper, we revise this model, drawing on the enactive approach and insights from Madhyamaka and Yogācāra Buddhist traditions of philosophy. title: Units, Assemblages, Compilations: The “Composite Nature of Early Chinese Texts” Reconsidered
abstract: Abstract The “composite nature of early Chinese texts” is a familiar way of thinking about textual formation in early China. It highlights how a text is comprised of small, movable textual units called “building blocks,” how an assemblage of building blocks stands either on its own or as part of a larger whole, and how a composite structure is the “norm” rather than exception in early Chinese writings. title: Reinforcement Learning-Based 3D Beam Adaptation for Underwater Wireless Optical Communication with AUVs
abstract: Underwater Wireless Optical Communications (UWOC) provide essential high data rates for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), but reliable connectivity is critically affected by transmitter-receiver misalignment. This work addresses the beam pointing problem for a moving AUV subject to unknown ocean currents through a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework. title: SURGE: Sonar-fUsed Reconstruction and localization via image-gated Graph Estimation
abstract: Remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) are widely used to explore and inspect underwater environments such as caves, shipwrecks, and submerged infrastructure. These missions require accurate 3D understanding of the surrounding environment, which depends on both reliable vehicle localization and metric scene reconstruction. However, external positioning is often unavailable underwater, requiring small ROVs to rely primarily on onboard perception. title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
abstract: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. title: Three-dimensional Lagrangian ecosystems: carbon dynamics and potential for artificial fertilization
abstract: Transient supplies of nutrients to the surface ocean, both natural and artificial, stimulate blooms of phytoplankton and the formation of organic matter, driving air-sea gradients and uptake of CO$_2$. However, quantifying the associated carbon budget remains challenging, as it requires tracking the coupled biophysical evolution of water masses while they are transported, stretched and diluted. title: The contribution of Soviet scientists to the emergence of high-energy neutrino astrophysics: from the Cherenkov effect to underwater and in-ice telescopes
abstract: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Francis Halzen @for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.@ This article examines the Soviet contribution to the broader historical development of high-energy neutrino astrophysics. title: Autonomous thermodynamic cycles via robotic mobility and sensing
abstract: Thermodynamic cycles are the foundation of energy conversion across natural and engineered systems, transforming heat into useful work. However, these cycles traditionally operate between fixed thermal reservoirs, restricting them to specific locations and temperature differences. Here, we introduce autonomous thermodynamic cycles enabled by robotic mobility and sensing, allowing robots to perform thermodynamic cycles by accessing spatially varying temperature fields. title: A regression-based maneuvering model for inland waterway ships in shallow rivers with real bathymetry and current fields
abstract: This paper presents a regression-based maneuvering model for inland waterway ships operating under realistic environmental conditions based on computational methods utilizing the unsteady Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) equations, across a wide range of water depths, from deep to shallow water conditions. title: From paleolandscape to seafloor: Holocene transgressive evolution of a low-relief landscape in the Eastern North Sea
abstract: Rising sea level threatens coastal communities globally, making it important to understand long-term landscape responses to anticipate future changes. Submerged paleolandscapes in the eastern North Sea offer an archive of past environmental changes due to sea level rise and coastal retreat. However, these paleolandscapes remain largely unstudied, and particularly their long-term geomorphological and sedimentary responses to sea level rise are still poorly understood. abstract: Gridded sea ice concentration (SIC) data are fundamental for understanding long-term polar climate. Since 1978, daily SIC data have been derived from passive microwave (PM) satellite observations. As SIC is not directly observed, it is obtained through an algorithmic inversion of PM brightness temperatures. Differences between PM-SIC algorithms lead to uncertainty in SIC data. abstract: Abstract Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. abstract: This essay interrogates the maritime as a concept and principle of colonization in Hegel’s philosophy of history and seeks to interrupt this imperializing logic with an alternative conception of the maritime from Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner . abstract: Manatees are charismatic, wide-ranging megaherbivores increasingly threatened with extinction across much of their distribution. Although many studies have documented threats to manatee populations, no standardized framework has been applied to quantify their vulnerability, leaving available knowledge scattered and lacking a comprehensive assessment of impact magnitude and spatial scale. To do this, a documentary review of scientific articles, theses, and institutional documents located in academic databases and open-access repositories was con-ducted, which allowed for systematizing the existing work and outlining the main theoretical and teaching approaches present in the literature. title: Review of reintroduction as a conservation tool for Pacific salmon in western North America
abstract: Abstract Objective Reintroduction of Pacific salmon Oncorhynchus spp. into historically occupied habitat is a widely used management strategy in western North America. Since the last major review, new information on donor populations, fish passage, dam removal, ecological interactions, monitoring, and cultural and societal considerations has emerged. We conducted a comprehensive review to synthesize these advances and inform best practices. journal: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society

title: Genetic analysis of bone morphometry and ivory vertebrae in threespine stickleback
abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. Here, we examine the largely unexplored genetic architecture of internal bone microstructural variation between marine and freshwater stickleback. Micro-computed tomography X-ray analysis revealed differences in the porosity, bone thickness, and bone volume fraction within armor plates and vertebrae from a marine and freshwater stickleback. title: Uncoupling of seagrass host selection and succession for microbial guilds in meadow chronosequence
abstract: Succession describes the predictable assembly of communities and habitats towards increasingly complex ecosystems. In marine meadows, the relative roles of succession and host selection in structuring microbial communities and functions remain unclear. Using chronosequences of the pioneering seagrass Halophila ovalis , we examined bacterial community succession (16S rRNA gene) and functional genes linked to nitrogen fixation and sulfur cycling ( nifH , soxB , aprA , dsrA ) across meadow sediments and seagrass microbiomes (rhizoplane and phylloplane). title: Resilience assessment of pile-supported wharves under the effects of sequential earthquake and soil liquefaction incorporating vine copula captured dependence
abstract: Pile-supported wharves (PSWs) constructed in seismically active coastal environments are susceptible to earthquake-induced liquefaction and the cumulative effects of sequential seismic events. This study develops a probabilistic framework to assess the seismic resilience of conventional and seismically isolated PSWs subjected to mainshock-aftershock (MS-AS) sequences while accounting for liquefaction-induced soil degradation. title: Effect of the MOPA Laser Cleaning Parameters on the Surface Evolution of the Epoxy Coating on AH36 Steel
abstract: High-power laser cleaning has been extensively adopted to remove organic coatings, but pulse duration, pulse energy, and overlap rate must be adjusted to limit residue and thermally affected surface modification. In this work, a 1000 W MOPA pulsed fiber laser was used to strip a 75 ± 5 μm thick iron-red epoxy primer from AH36 marine steel. title: Aterian Lithic Technology and Functional Studies in North Africa: A Review of Current Evidence and Perspectives
abstract: Abstract In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of Homo sapiens and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. Recent archaeological discoveries have yielded a range of technological innovations, which are likely connected with ecological adaptations as well as new social and symbolic practices. title: Presence and characterization of microplastics in pet blood (dogs and cats): Evidence of environmental contamination
abstract: Increasing evidence identifies microplastics (MPs) as ubiquitous environmental contaminants, across marine, terrestrial, and atmospheric ecosystems. Their size and physicochemical properties facilitate widespread distribution and bioavailability, raising increasing concerns regarding their potential impact on animal and human health. Their presence in aquatic organisms (e.g., fish, mussels), marine mammals, and birds is demonstrated but evidence related to dogs and cats are relatively few. title: Exploring the potential of cold plasma for nitrogen enrichment in diverse soil types of Kerala
abstract: Atmospheric cold plasma is a novel green technology which generates highly reactive species at room temperature. Cold plasma exposure converts inert atmospheric nitrogen to plant available nitrates and ammonium ions in the soil. The present study aims to standardise voltage levels in major soil types of Kerala for achieving sufficient nitrogen enrichment with minimal impact on soil microbial activity. title: Widespread hybridization in sympatric populations of allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803): A transnational perspective for conservation and management
abstract: The dynamics of hybridization between co-occurring species in environments that have been modified by anthropogenic activities are important for generating new understandings of how species respond to disturbance and to support conservation management. Accordingly, the patterns of hybridization between anadromous allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803) were investigated, where these species historically co-occurred across rivers in Europe. institutions: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

title: Paleoseasonality through serial stable isotope analysis of Pleistocene to recent Etheria elliptica shells from the middle Atbara River, eastern Sudan
abstract: Rainfall magnitude and seasonality are primary determinants of African savannas today, governing essential aspects of biomass production, such as primary productivity and the amount of tree cover. It remains unclear to what extent past seasonality differed from today, potentially accounting for differences in habitats and faunal diversity. Stable isotopes along with trace elements of the growth layers in bivalve shells provide valuable insights into paleoenvironmental conditions, including rainfall, river productivity, and water temperature. Gastropod Diversity at Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, India: A Historical Baseline from August–November 2017
abstract: Motivation: Historical biodiversity records provide useful reference points for coastal biodiversity monitoring, particularly in areas subject to continuing human use. Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, supports a diverse molluscan fauna, but historical records of its gastropod assemblage remain limited. Objectives: This study documents the gastropod assemblage recorded at Azheekkal during August–November 2017 and provides a historical reference dataset for future biodiversity assessments. title: Flowing between worlds: Water onto-epistemologies and educational plurality
abstract: Educational philosophy has been landlocked—built on terrestrial metaphors of ground, foundation, and territory that reproduce a sovereign ontology separating knower from known. This paper develops water onto-epistemologies as an alternative orientation, drawing on Indigenous philosophies, decolonial theory, Japanese aesthetics, and oceanic thought to argue that water offers not merely a different metaphor but a different grammar for educational thinking—one rooted in relationality, opacity, and movement. title: Análisis bioarqueológico de restos humanos del Período Arcaico Tardío (3950-1550 cal AP) en Talcahuano-1, sur de Chile: avances en la identificación de patologías y reconstrucción de estilos de vida
abstract: The Talcahuano-1 archaeological site in Southern Chile provides a unique context for studying Late Archaic (3,950 – 1,550 cal BP) populations. This study revisits three human burials previously analyzed for funerary practices, paleopathology, and lifestyle. Using updated methods and stable isotope analyses, new insights into diet, chronology and health were gained. Results reveal evidence of a marine-based diet, marked musculoskeletal stress, and pathologies such as porotic hyperostosis and treponematosis. title: Bocachico (Ichthyoelephas humeralis) en Ecuador: revisión sistemática y análisis espacial de su distribución
abstract: Ichthyoelephas humeralis (bocachico) is a native fish species of high ecological and socioeconomic importance in Ecuador. This study integrates a systematic review and a spatial analysis to synthesize its distribution, biology, ecological requirements, economic importance, threats, and conservation strategies. Under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 29 available studies on the species were analyzed, primarily addressing biological, ecological, and use aspects. title: Identifying counties with suitable habitat for host-seeking Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto-infected Ixodes pacificus nymphs across seven states in the western United States
abstract: Abstract Background Tick surveillance is used to monitor acarological risk for Lyme disease. Most human infections arise from the bite of a Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto (Bbss)-infected nymphal tick. Tick surveillance records documenting the densities of host-seeking Bbss-infected nymphs are limited in the western US, where Ixodes pacificus (Cooley and Kohls, 1943) is the primary vector. title: Leviathan: fast, memory-efficient, and scalable taxonomic and pathway profiling for (pan)genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics
abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. title: Penerapan Kepemimpinan Digital dalam Mendukung Keberlanjutan Koperasi Unit Desa Lawallu, Kabupaten Barru
abstract: Lawallu Village Unit Cooperative (KUD), located in Barru Regency, South Sulawesi, is a community-based economic institution with strong social capital, yet it still faces limited digital leadership capacity in managing services, administration, and data-based decision-making. Most service processes remain manual, archives are not yet digitized, and internal communication lacks standardization. This community service program aimed to strengthen the digital leadership capacity of the cooperative's management board and key members through flexible, self-paced web-based learning. title: Mediaciones, medialidades y testimonios: entre cinedocumental, arte y memoria. Un análisis de Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra y Este arte que abraza
abstract: This article examines how documentary cinema establishes relationships between art and memory in three documentaries: Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra, and Este arte que abraza. The analysis identifies three distinct forms of mediation, mediality, and testimonial practice. Lemebel is an authorial and didactic documentary centered on the recovery of the artist’s archive and the reconstruction of his life and work. title: From national to global: Mapping global center-pivot irrigated cropland with knowledge-guided data augmentation
abstract: Center-pivot irrigated cropland (CPIC) is a large-scale, intensive agricultural irrigation practice with high water-use efficiency. This characteristic enables CPIC to increase crop yields and promote agricultural development, while simultaneously causing groundwater overexploitation and subsequent environmental issues. Mapping the global distribution of CPIC is critical for enhancing water resource management, guiding agricultural policies, and assessing ecological impacts. title: A 500 m deep multipurpose research borehole and monitoring station in Delft, the Netherlands
abstract: The 500 m deep DAPGEO-02 multifunctional research borehole and monitoring station was drilled in Delft in spring 2022. Dinoflagellate biostratigraphy reveals that the borehole goes through the Neogene Upper North Sea Group, including the Waalre, Maassluis, Oosterhout, Diessen, and Groot Heide formations. Below, a stratigraphic gap exists between the late Miocene Diessen and the middle Miocene Groote Heide formations, followed by a much larger gap between the Groote Heide and the lower Eocene Dongen formations. title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. title: Mortality From 1918-1919 Spanish Flu Among the American Expeditionary Forces Analyzed Through People-Powered Research
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Card Register of Burials of Deceased American Soldiers, 1917-1922 holds the burial cards of American servicemen and women who died at sea or overseas during or after World War I (WWI). We aimed to use this online register to study mortality statistics in the American Expeditionary Forces (AEF) during the 3 waves of Spanish flu in 1918 and 1919. However, the register, which includes 104 file units, lacks database query functionality. title: Villa Ögel: A Vanishing Example of Modern Heritage at Şaşkınbakkal
abstract: This study investigates Villa Ögel, a rare surviving example of Suadiye’s modernist garden-villa era (1940s–1950s), to illuminate its architectural, historical, and socio-cultural significance amid Istanbul’s rapid urban transformation. Suadiye is a coastal residential district on the Anatolian side of Istanbul, with Villa Ögel located in Şaşkınbakkal, a smaller micro-geographical area within the broader Suadiye neighborhood, representing a specific locality within its wider urban and historical context. title: Olinto Dini ( 1805–1866 ) physicist by choice, naturalist by fate
abstract: The naturalist Olinto Dini (18051866) is known within the Tuscan scientific panorama of the 19th century for his studies of the geology of the Garfagnana Valley in Northern Tuscany (Italy).He retired from a teaching position in physics at the University of Pisa, for family reasons, at a very early stage of his scientific career.Nevertheless, he maintained close contacts with the academic world in Pisa, as testified by the correspondence preserved within the "Olinto Dini" collection, housed at the library of the Domus Galilaeana in Pisa.This paper gives a brief overview of his main contributio

title: Review of Salmonid Alphavirus: Focus on Viral Survival, Shedding, Detection and Effects of Vaccination
abstract: This review of salmonid alphavirus provides a collection of the most recent knowledge on the factors relevant for the transmission and control of the virus including updates on SAV survival, viral shedding, detection, and effects of vaccination as reported in peer-reviewed literature, presentations, theses, and annual reports. SAV can survive in all water types, being the longest in colder marine waters without organic loading. The biophysical properties of SAV indicate a moderate to high robustness. abstract: 23-Demethylgorgosterol is an unusual marine sterol scaffold characterized by an atypical 22,23-cyclopropyl-containing side chain and an uncommon sterol substitution pattern. Its recent access through an efficient semi-synthetic route enables systematic structural diversification. In this study, we completed the semi-synthesis and prepared the unnatural diastereomer together with a series of structurally diverse intermediates and derivatives. title: An Energy Integration Free Kubo-Bastin Formula Decomposition
abstract: Kubo formulae play a central role in modern spintronics and condensed matter physics, serving as the foundational ground for studying transport responses in the linear regime. In this work, we propose a reformulation of the widely used Kubo-Bastin decompositions that eliminates the need for numerical energy integration. title: Indian MAHASAGAR and the Evolution of India's Maritime Diplomacy
abstract: India's maritime diplomacy has undergone a decisive transformation over the past decade, evolving from a continental-focused posture toward a proactive, maritime-centric vision for the Indo-Pacific. This article examines that evolution and assesses the operational relevance of minilateral architectures in advancing India's strategic objectives. abstract: Cytochalasins are a very intriguing group of natural compounds. Since the first isolation of the well-known cytochalasins A and B in 1966, over 300 analogues have been described as metabolites, primarily produced by various fungal genera. Their bioactivities, targets, total syntheses, and biosyntheses had been also extensively investigated. abstract: Conspectus The ever-increasing demand for advanced X-ray detection technologies calls for a revolution in conventional inorganic scintillators. abstract: This study develops the Sargassum-Based Concrete Integrated Carbon Evaluation Framework (SBC-ICEF) to assess the environmental implications of incorporating processed Sargassum particles into concrete for potential non-load-bearing wall applications in coastal China. title: Macroevolutionary insights into the range limits of species and lineages
abstract: Understanding the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that determine the range limits of species is an important goal in biology. Much work has focused on understanding the range limits of populations and individual species, whereas the factors that determine the distributions of evolutionary lineages have received less attention in the range limits literature. In this review I highlight recent macroscale insights into the range limits of flowering plant lineages, and briefly compare these to findings from other taxa. title: Re-evaluating ecoinvent’s suitability for direct product material footprint calculation
abstract: Abstract Sustainable Development Goal 12.2 aims to achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources by 2030. Its target indicator, the material footprint, is a key macroeconomic indicator for impacts related to resource extraction. On the microeconomic scale, it is complemented by the product material footprint (PMF). title: EFFECTS OF INVASIVE FISH SPECIES ON NATIVE SPECIES AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: Biological invasions have emerged as one of the major drivers of global biodiversity loss, threatening native species, ecosystem functioning, and human well-being. This review examines the impacts of invasive species on native fish species and aquatic ecosystems, with emphasis on mechanisms of invasion, pathways of introduction, ecological consequences, and management strategies. Deliberate and accidental introductions facilitated by globalization, aquaculture, trade, and transportation have accelerated the spread of invasive organisms across freshwater and marine environments. title: Pedro Carrere. Un japonista español en el México finisecular: colección, mediación y práctica artística
abstract: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Carrere stands out; however, his diplomatic career and collecting activities have lacked a systematic reconstruction until now. abstract: Objectives: The present study aimed to assess the neuroprotective properties and memory enhancement of the ethanolic extract of Sargassum tenerrimum (ST) with regard to the scopolamine-induced amnesia model in Wistar rats and explore the underlying mechanism involved in cholinergic neurotransmission. Methods: The extract was administered orally once daily for 14 consecutive days at doses of 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg. title: Genealogies of protest and resistance in the Scottish Highlands and islands after 1750
abstract: Abstract Histories of protest in the Highlands and Islands have been largely limited to the study of dramatic and large-scale events driven by issues of possession of and access to land after 1850. Most research to date has tended to focus on the crofting counties of the north-west of the region and the paradigmatic land raid, with alternate forms of protest and at different times often relegated to little more than a footnote. abstract: The article analyzes the meeting of experts in Latin American arts held in Quito in June 1970, which was part of the study project on the cultures of Latin America proposed in 1966 during the Fourteenth General Conference of UNESCO. Based on a documentary analysis of the sources related to this initiative from UNESCO’s digital archive, the article identifies the project’s objectives, phases, and methodology, highlighting the proposals made at the Quito meeting within this framework. title: The worth of high-resolution inventories: disparities between monthly and annual emission trends in the cement industry
abstract: Abstract Distinctive emissions from individual plants are pivotal for unraveling net-zero paths in the cement industry, as aggregated figures obscure substantial plant-specific variation. We estimated the high spatiotemporal emissions broken down from national to plant levels and from yearly to monthly scales using the Tier 2 bottom-up approach based on the 2006 IPCC Guidelines. title: A record of emplacement conditions from trapped volatile gases within nuclear test debris
abstract: Nuclear melt glass provides a valuable archive of information about the nature of the nuclear detonation. Study of melt glasses provides information on the device materials and performance, the emplacement conditions, the venting conditions (if any), and future environmental and human health impacts. Despite extensive study, direct records of redox conditions and cooling histories of the post-detonation environment are sparse. title: Prevalence and multimorbidity patterns of thyroid dysfunction in Chinese adults
abstract: The risk of thyroid dysfunction (TD) persists in the Chinese population. However, large-scale epidemiological studies investigating TD prevalence and its geographic disparities are limited. Previous studies have mostly focused on associations between TD and individual organ systems or single medical conditions. This nationwide, large-scale study utilized data from the Meinian Health Check-up database across all 31 provinces of the Chinese mainland. title: Illusions of peace: eurocentrism, endemic violence and the burden of the Postcolony in the Central African Republic
abstract: This paper interrogates how Eurocentrism structures what counts as violence and, by extension, what counts as peace. Using the Central African Republic (CAR) as a site of analysis, it argues that violence cannot be understood through calamitous moments but through the endemic conditions embedded in la longue durée that shape life in the Postcolony. title: Declines in the diversity of fish represented in British domestic recipes over the past 100 years
abstract: Abstract Fish and shellfish are nutritionally important foods, yet consumption in many high‐income countries remains low and concentrated on a narrow set of environmentally costly species. In the United Kingdom, fish consumption is dominated by a small group of fish, the ‘Big Five’, which is often treated as an inevitable outcome of supply, convenience and ingrained consumer preferences. title: Ecological considerations for reintroducing Chinook salmon upstream of Shasta Dam
abstract: Abstract In this assessment, we reviewed existing literature to assess the ecological risks, benefits, and uncertainties associated with reintroducing Chinook salmon ( Oncorhynchus tshawytcha ) into the McCloud River, a tributary of the Sacramento River, California. Two source populations are being considered for reintroduction by co‐managers in the basin (the Winnemem Wintu Tribe, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration): existing winter‐run Chinook salmon (WRCS) from the mainstem Sacramento River, and Chinook salmon from New Zealand (NZ

title: Facies and paleogeographic conditions of the Late Paleozoic flora burial and preservation in the Southern Tien Shan (based on the Karachatyr Mountains localities)
abstract: The article examines the facies and paleogeographic conditions of flora fossil burial and preservation in the Upper Paleozoic deposits of the Karachatyr Mountains (Southern Fergana, Southern Tien Shan). The study aims to reconstruct the sedimentary environments which controlled the terrestrial vegetation transport, accumulation, and preservation in the Late Carboniferous — Early Permian. title: Energy Efficiency Measures vs. Biofuels - Implications for Vessel Operational Performance
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the relative importance of energy saving measures (ESMs) and alternative biofuels for the improvement of ship efficiency and for compliance with new regulations imposed on the maritime transport sector. In light of the fact that ESMs have proven that they are capable of providing a significant fuel saving potential by enhancing the hull condition, propulsion, and internal combustion efficiency as well as through operational optimization, the aim of this study is to investigate the advantages and disadvantages of ESMs compared to biofuels. title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. abstract: This article examines the monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča region (today divided between Italy and Slovenia), promoted by the Italian government and local authorities during the interwar period. Following Italy’s victory in the war, the liberal state – and even more emphatically Mussolini’s regime – fostered a patriotic cult that supported the dictator’s efforts to present Fascism as the rightful heir to that victory. abstract: Background Padang City is vulnerable to flooding because of its coastal and low-lying areas, high rainfall, and drainage systems that are not yet fully optimal. Drainage management is therefore an important part of government efforts to prevent and reduce flood risk. This study aims to describe and analyze drainage management by the Padang City Department of Public Works and Spatial Planning (PUPR) in flood prevention. title: The Efraim Berkovici Collection: Poesiealbum and Diary Writing in "Ilaniah" Children's Village
abstract: In September 1947, a train traveling under the auspices of the Red Cross departed Romania carrying over 420 Jewish children, via Prague, to the Netherlands. The children, among them Holocaust survivors from Transnistria, had been gathered from different parts of Romania, including orphanages, and were taken to the “Ilaniah” children’s village, located on the grounds of a former Jewish psychiatric hospital in Apeldoorn. A smaller group of over thirty Jewish child survivors from Germany arrived a few weeks later. In October 1948, these children boarded a ship, the Negba, and departed for Israel.

abstract: This article reassesses the transimperial flight of enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans from the Dutch island of Curaçao to the Spanish mainland of Tierra Firme, particularly Coro, during the eighteenth century. Owing to Spain's policy of royal asylum, enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans could obtain freedom upon entering Spanish territory. Drawing on a detailed 1775 runaway register and colonial correspondence, the article reconstructs who fled, how they escaped, and why they undertook the maritime crossing. abstract: This paper aims to fill in the gaps in the social history of the Ottoman borderlands by exploring the social integration and agency of freed slaves in Early Modern Ottoman Sarajevo. abstract: Manyu Division, in the South-West Region of Cameroon, possesses one of the richest natural tourism endowments in Central Africa, anchored by Korup National Park among the oldest and most bio-diverse rainforests on the continent. It extends across the Takamanda highlands, the Cross River and its tributaries, a landscape of waterfalls, wildlife corridors, and geological formations that together constitute a natural capital of world-class quality. title: Scholars and Literati at the Académie Philomathique of Paris (1788–1800)
abstract: This document offers a concise portrait of the scholars who belonged to the Académie Philomathique of Paris from its founding in 1788 to the turn of the nineteenth century, in 1800. abstract: Cartagena, Spain, is a unique Mediterranean coastal city defined by its transition from a rigid 18th-entury military stronghold to a dynamic modern center. While its ancient ruins are well-documented, the city’s later layers – specifically its modernist architecture and institutional landmarks – are often overlooked in urban discourse. title: “A Vile Character”
abstract: Alfons Sutter was perhaps the most notorious German police agent in the Łódź ghetto. A native of Łódź, he and dozens of other Volksdeutsche (ethnic Germans) were hired by the criminal police (Kriminalpolizei, or Kripo) after Nazi Germany conquered and annexed the city. abstract: ABSTRACT Central bank gold vaults occupy a paradoxical position in contemporary monetary systems: They are among the most symbolically charged and institutionally significant spaces of modern finance, yet they have received almost no scholarly attention. abstract: The Gulf of Zula–Danakil corridor of Eritrea represents a unique “rift–reef–refugium” setting exceptionally rich in geological attractions (such as volcanic cones, hot springs and reef beds) and archaeo-paleontological heritage. abstract: This two-breathed essay emerges from the convergence of Indigenous and settler practices of knowing, feeling, and moving. abstract: Vibrio cholerae serotypes that belong to the non-O1 and non-O139 category, especially O27, are emerging opportunistic pathogens being increasingly associated with severe septicemia, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Most non-O1 or non-O139 serogroups cause sporadic infections, but certain strains of Vibrio cholerae, including the O27 serotype, have acquired additional virulence factors, raising concerns about their potential for more invasive disease. abstract: Designing an efficient and cost-effective port network requires accounting for practical constraints, such as port time operation windows. title: Teaching for resilience in university outdoor education fieldwork: a poetic inquiry
abstract: Outdoor education is a well-established and growing field in Australia. University courses are vital for preparing outdoor educators and outdoor education teachers to work with school-aged students across various outdoor roles. These courses offer more than the preparation to instruct outdoor activities; they also prepare graduates to teach in, through, about and with outdoor environments. abstract: ABSTRACT Dunaliella species are among the most significant biological sources of carotenoids, notably beta‐carotene. Given that chemical synthesis offers a more cost‐effective alternative to biotechnological cultivation, optimizing production strategies is essential for economic viability. This study investigated the optimization of bioproduct synthesis in a Brazilian strain of Dunaliella salina by evaluating the effects of high photon flux density (PFD) and temperature under low‐salinity conditions (1 mol L −1 NaCl) to facilitate downstream processing. title: Evaluation of Iron Ore Dust Emission Rates and Associated Bacterial Load
abstract: The National Industrial and Mining Company (SNIM) is facing significant dust emissions, raising serious environmental and public health concerns. This study aimed to characterize airborne dust emissions from mining activities and to assess their physicochemical and microbiological composition. Dust samples were analyzed and found to contain hazardous heavy metals, including lead, copper, nickel, and cobalt. abstract: Over the last decades, the rapid expansion of plastic production, combined with poor circularity, inadequate waste management, and the long-term persistence of synthetic polymers, has led to widespread environmental contamination. Plastics are now so pervasive that they have been proposed as a defining feature of the so-called Plasticene . abstract: The oropharyngeal cavity of turtles exhibits considerable morphological diversity associated with differences in habitat, diet, and feeding strategies. abstract: ABSTRACT Interactions between microbes shape the structure and function of microbial communities. While studying interactions is key to understanding microbial communities as a whole, gaining a detailed mechanistic view is challenging due to the number of co-occurring interactions. Here, we focus on a single class of shared nutrients, the cobalamin (vitamin B 12 ) family of enzyme cofactors known as cobamides, to study nutrient interactions in laboratory consortia of increasing complexity. title: The Eastern Flank as NATO’s Geopolitical Code
abstract: This article focuses on NATO’s Eastern Flank. It addresses the identified research gap in literature concerning the insufficient conceptualisation of NATO’s Eastern Flank. Specifically, the authors attempt to answer two fundamental questions: what geographical area constitutes NATO’s Eastern Flank, and which member states should be considered part of it? abstract: We present the first integrated data on sexual dimorphism based on body measurements of adults and juveniles, together with information on the reproductive biology of the snail-eating snake Sibon nebulatus, based on specimens from isolated humid montane forest enclaves (“Brejos de Altitude”) in the state of Ceará, northeastern Brazil. title: Hydropeaking Catalyzes Redox Reactions in Impacted Aquifers: A First Field Evidence
abstract: Abstract Hydropeaking indicates the sudden and frequent fluctuation of river stage caused by the operation of hydropower plants. This river alteration affects numerous physical, chemical, biological, and ecohydrological processes in surface water bodies. The impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydraulics has been investigated only recently through modeling and experimental studies at multiple spatial scales. title: Market Trends and Challenges for Alabama's Emerging Oyster Aquaculture Industry
abstract: Different marketing channels influence farm profitability by affecting the costs that producers incur and the prices they receive. This article quantifies oyster sales volume and price by market channel in Alabama's commercial oyster aquaculture sector and assesses challenges to expanding farm businesses. The results show that many oyster producers are selling exclusively through one channel, which raises questions about their resiliency and their capacity to adapt to a dynamic single market. abstract: Apicomplexan parasites of insects represent a largely unexplored branch of the tree of life. Their small size and lack of informative phenotypic traits can obscure their diversity and many lineage-specific adaptations to different host species. To better understand how these parasites have evolved, we have sequenced and annotated the genome of a neogregarine parasite of moths in the family Noctuidae, including Helicoverpa armigera. title: Isolation of indigenous soil bacteria with potential application for diuron removal
abstract: Diuron is a widely used herbicide in sugarcane, cotton, coffee, and citrus production and is classified as a priority pollutant. Physical and chemical remediation of pesticide-contaminated sites is often technically complex and costly. Microorganism-mediated bioremediation offers an environmentally compatible and cost-effective alternative, particularly when pollutant-specific indigenous microorganisms are used. title: Spatio-temporal patterns of diversity and distribution of common Megachile bees across agroclimatic gradients in Eastern India
abstract: Abstract Bees of the genus Megachile (Megachilidae; Hymenoptera) are among the most efficient pollinators of wild and cultivated plants, yet their diversity, distribution, and seasonal dynamics remain inadequately documented across varied agroclimatic landscapes in India. Despite their recognized contribution to crop pollination, previous studies have largely overlooked spatial and seasonal variation in Megachile assemblages, especially in Eastern India. abstract: Wetlands are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, and their loss increasingly compromises landscape connectivity essential for persistence of waterbird populations. In the Mediterranean region, and particularly in northwestern Africa, conservation prioritisation has largely focused on sites supporting high bird numbers, while the role of wetlands in maintaining functional connectivity remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the deadliest malignancies worldwide, and effective therapies are still lacking. Actinomycetota are among the richest microbial sources of bioactive secondary metabolites, and three agents in clinical use against pancreatic malignancy derive from them — streptozotocin, everolimus and doxorubicin — though all three are indicated for neuroendocrine rather than ductal tumors. abstract: Abstract Turbo-vapor compressors (TVCs) are critical for generating vacuum pressure in a novel combined cycle for electricity and freshwater production. This paper presents a new TVC design comprising a single axial compressor rotor directly driving a single axial turbine rotor, aiming to improve efficiency, increase allowable mass flow rate, and reduce cost and losses. abstract: Giardiasis, caused by Giardia intestinalis, is a prevalent intestinal protozoan infection worldwide. Clinical manifestations are variable, and many infections remain asymptomatic. Disease pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving brush border enzyme deficiency, apoptosis, dysbiosis and increased intestinal permeability. abstract: Anisakis spp. are foodborne parasites of major public health concern due to their dual role as infectious agents and potent allergens. This study investigated the prevalence, infection intensity, and allergenic potential of Anisakidae in ready-to-eat fish products available on the Astana market (Kazakhstan). abstract: ABSTRACT Wetlands are critical components of natural water infrastructure, delivering hydrological regulation, biodiversity support, and climate resilience, yet they continue to deteriorate globally. This article provides new causal evidence on the effectiveness of International Environmental Agreements (IEAs) by examining the impacts of wetland designation under the Ramsar Convention. abstract: This article examines funerary monetary deposition in 75 documented contexts from the South/Tavşandere Necropolis of Parion, dated from the Late Classical/Early Hellenistic to the Roman Imperial period. abstract: The islands of Te Whanga Lagoon, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island are scarcely documented. Two of the islands are shell cays, Moturangaranga and Hi’Tara. In this paper the geology, physiography, landforms, vegetation associations and some of the biota of Hi’Tara are documented. abstract: From the emergence of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula in the 7th century AD, to its expansion and development across continents of the world, series of factors have come into play to make the religion distinct among other forms of religions. abstract: Free-living amoebae, living in freshwater ecosystems, constitute an important ecological group among microscopic eukaryotic organisms. Various amoebae belonging to the order (Adl et al.) can be used as potential bioindicators in assessing the trophic state, organic matter loading, microhabitat characteristics, and ecological variability of water bodies. abstract: Abstract To address the difficulties in conventional elevation surveying caused by the strong topographic relief in mountainous areas and the dual constraints imposed on GNSS gravity potential leveling by the selection of the absolute gravity potential reference and local short wavelength terrain effects, a terrain corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method is proposed. title: Classification of mobile robots for rescue operations
abstract: Search and rescue operations in case of disasters are typically time-sensitive and are conducted under hazardous conditions, with limited access to the affected area. Despite the advances in disaster risk management, events such as earthquakes continue to cause significant loss of life, underscoring the need for more effective rescue techniques. abstract: Domestic wastewater generated from daily household activities can degrade environmental water quality if discharged without adequate treatment. Filtration is one of the most widely applied preliminary treatment methods due to its simplicity and effectiveness in increasing water quality. Activated wood carbon (AWC) is widely used as an adsorbent in filtration systems. abstract: Demulsifiers are fundamental in oil production because of their role in improving water-oil separation efficiency. abstract: Soil salinity is a major environmental constraint that adversely affects microbial growth and plant productivity. abstract: Abstract The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends, in part, on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. abstract: The global refugee crisis situation is increasingly being subsumed under the humanitarian-development nexus (HDN), which, otherwise, informs humanitarian interventions within the normative framework of northern stakeholders including development agencies. While refugee studies have already explored HDN, there is still a lack of critical research on HDN, especially in the context of neoliberal governance. abstract: Abstract Animals are often trapped to learn more about a species’ behavioural ecology, either invasively with live traps or non-invasively with hair- or camera traps. abstract: This mixed-methods study used a triangulation design to evaluate municipal libraries in Western Visayas as vital community learning spaces. abstract: The rapid growth of global maritime trade has increased the risk of occupational accidents at container terminals, necessitating a strong Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) system. This study aims to examine the relationship between the implementation of internal OHS audits, communication patterns, and hazard control at container terminals in Semarang City. abstract: This study investigates the primary and secondary buckling behavior of thin-walled composite cylinders subjected to external pressure using analytical formulations and finite element (FE) modeling. abstract: Abstract. Airborne fungi play a pivotal role in ecosystem functioning, agriculture, people health and wellbeing, yet their response to increasingly frequent climate extremes remains poorly understood. There is thus a need for long-term studies that can capture both seasonal and annual dynamics of fungal remnants in the air. abstract: Safeguarding old-growth and primary forests is essential for biodiversity conservation, climate regulation, ecosystem resilience and cultural heritage, yet these forests remain rare, fragmented and increasingly threatened across the EU. abstract: Abstract Halophytes, naturally adapted to survive and grow under high-salinity conditions, harbour complex internal microbiomes composed of endophytic microorganisms that persist within plant tissues without causing disease. abstract: Urban-tree controversies often arise when evidence measured at one biological or geographical scale is used to justify management decisions at another. Senyawa dalam daun binahong dapat menghambat pertumbuhan bakteri Sthapylococcus aureus dan Eschercihia coli. Tujuan penelitian ini untuk mengetahui aktivitas antibakteri sediaan spray kombinasi daun Sirih (Piper betle) dan daun binahong (Anredera cordifolia) terhadap bakteri Escherichia coli dan Sthapylococcus aureus. title: Reimagining the way we care for our Planet: advancing biodiversity conservation through the hopeful vision of Laudato si’ and Half-Earth
abstract: To be responsible stewards of our planet, we must urgently explore, discover, and learn as much as possible about biodiversity, and identify the network of places where we have the greatest opportunity to safeguard the most species. This paper explores how the complementary visions of Pope Francis’s Laudato si’ and E.O. Wilson’s Half-Earth call for a transformative shift in humanity’s relationship with the natural world, offering a hopeful, unifying framework that combines scientific rigor with moral urgency. title: Heritage everywhere and nowhere: displaced heritage discourse in Swedish hydropower transitions
abstract: Hydropower infrastructures are central to sustainability transitions but are also embedded in historically layered landscapes of meaning, identity, and governance. This article examines how cultural heritage is mobilised and constrained in the relicensing of Swedish hydropower facilities under the National Plan for Modern Environmental Conditions (NAP). title: Flooding and Health
abstract: Global warming and rapid demographic transitions have drastically increased populations in flood-prone areas, escalating global disease burdens, hospitalizations, and mortality. Flooding triggers severe health crises, including water-borne, vector-borne, and respiratory diseases, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups like the elderly and those with chronic comorbidities in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). journal: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research

title: Length-Weight Relationship and Condition Factors of Ichthyofauna Species of Okamini Stream, New Calabar River Segment, Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the length–weight relationship and condition factors of ichthyofauna species in Okamini Stream, a segment of the New Calabar River, Rivers State, Nigeria. Fish samples were assessed for length, weight, length–weight relationships and condition factors across sampling Stations and Months and analysed following standard method using identification keys and measuring instruments. title: The Identification and Morphological Description of Parmarion martensi in The Protected Forest Area of The Southern Tip of Tarakan
abstract: This study aims to identify and describe the morphology of shell-less snails (slugs) in the Gunung Selatan Protected Forest area of ​​Tarakan City. The research used a descriptive qualitative approach with a purposive sampling method. Sampling was conducted from November to December 2025 at four observation stations, each using a 20 x 20 meter plot. The results showed that one shell-less snail species was found at all observation stations, namely Parmarion martensi. This species has unique morphological characteristics in the form of a reduced shell as a form of adaptation to its environment.

title: Spatial and Social Mechanisms for Urban Development through Community Festival:
abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the social and spatial mechanisms of two community festivals regarded as cultural capitals through a comparative lens. One is the floating Hikiyama in the Karatsu Kunchi festival in Karatsu City, Japan; the other is the revival of the creation and procession of Sapao in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Although the two festivals originated in different periods and contexts, they share a common feature: utilizing cultural capital to develop urban space while playing a key role in generating local economic value. journal: International Review for Spatial Planning and Sustainable Development

title: PLACE-BASED INTERPRETATION OF ORANG ASLI LIFE-COURSE HERITAGE
abstract: This study reframes Orang Asli (OA) cultural practices as a life-course and spatial system within Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) Domain 3. It connects them to care settings, households, Adat institutions, burial boundaries and ancestral sites. Studies emphasise festive events, weakening recognition of continuity across life phases. The research combined interviews with OA knowledge holders and representatives with ethnographic, academic and heritage sources. Content analysis coded manifestations by social role, ritual purpose, symbolic meaning, participation pattern and community context.

abstract: The Laleaua Albă (White Tulip) magmatic complex (LA) consists of small-scale composite andesitic–dacitic dikes representing the third volcanic phase (8.5–8.0 Ma) of the Gutâi Volcanic Zone (GVZ) within the Neogene–Quaternary volcanic chain of the East Carpathians (Romania). The LA comprises two composite dikes that crosscut older volcanic units. The outcrop, at the sampling site exhibit a tulip-shaped light-colored dacitic core – containing abundant mafic microgranular enclaves (MME) – surrounded by a dark gray andesitic envelope. title: Apportioning Sources of Nitrogen Oxides in California's San Joaquin Valley Using Observations From Three Airborne Field Campaigns
abstract: Abstract Emissions of nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO 2 ), a precursor to ozone and secondary aerosol formation have become increasingly important to understand as ozone production transitions to NO x limited in most regions of the US. Recent studies suggest that NO x emissions associated with agricultural activities, particularly cropland soils, are an increasingly important contributor. California's San Joaquin Valley (SJV) is a prominent agricultural region, with large‐scale cropland and livestock operations that are known sources of nitrogenous emissions.
