title: SMONG'S NARRATIVE IN THE CHILDREN'S BOOK "ITAM AND U": INTERTEXTUALITY, SIGNS OF NATURE, AND DISASTER EDUCATION
abstract: This study analyzes the representation and function of smong narrative in the children's book "Itam and U" as a disaster literacy media based on local culture. Smong is an oral tradition from Simeulue that functions as a tsunami early warning system through poetry and collective memory. Using a computer-aided qualitative content analysis approach, the study extracted and analyzed text from 48 pages of the book to identify patterns of smong representation, nature signs, and disaster risk reduction education. The results of the study show that smong is not presented as a separate exotic element

title: Effect of Selected Food Crop Outputs on Poverty Level of Farm Households in Rivers State
abstract: This study examined the effect of selected food crop outputs on poverty level of farm households in Rivers State. The primary data of the study were collected from a sample of 820 respondents based on the copies of questionnaires completed and returned. The data collected were analyzed using binary logit regression involving the odd ratios and marginal effects. The estimated binary logit results showed that yam production decreases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.028%. The results showed that an increase in cassava production increases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.034%.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE

title: Regional economic impacts and emission responses under solar radiation modification
abstract: Abstract Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system's response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the spatial distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. title: Boreal Peatland 24-hour Solar-induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence Measurements under Continuous Daylight Conditions during the Summer Period
abstract: Continuous ground-based observations of solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) from northern peatlands remain uncommon, despite their potential to complement ecosystem carbon flux measurements and support satellite-based monitoring of vegetation activity. Here, we present continuous SIF estimates using data acquired with the Fluorescence Box (FloX) at two boreal peatland sites in northern Finland during the 2023 and 2025 growing seasons. title: Subspecific identity of channel-billed cuckoos (Scythrops novaehollandiae) vagrant to Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: The channel-billed cuckoo Scythrops novaehollandiae is an occasional vagrant to Aotearoa New Zealand, with eight confirmed records. There are three described subspecies: the nominate form from Australia; S. n. fordi from Sulawesi; and S. n. schoddei from the Bismarck Archipelago. No previous studies have identified the subspecific identity of any channel-billed cuckoos in New Zealand. title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. title: Hauntological ecologies and temporalities of post-socialism: Disco Elysium between Estonia and China
abstract: This paper examines the video game Disco Elysium (ZA/UM, 2019) as a pivotal cultural text for understanding the hauntological dimensions of post-socialist experience. The game’s transnational journey and profound reception from Estonia to China reveal a shared, yet differentially articulated, structure of feeling shaped by the aftermath of collapsed socialist projects and the ascendancy of neoliberal capitalism. title: Economic, environmental and public health impacts of gas flaring in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria
abstract: Over the past six decades, billions of cubic feet of gases associated with crude oil exploration have been flared. Unfortunately, gas flaring has continued despite successive legislative interventions, with limited implementation of effective remediation strategies in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria. Gas flaring involves the combustion of associated gases produced during oil extraction, which contain particulate matter (soot), carbon dioxide, sulfur oxides (SOx), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and volatile organic compounds. title: Regional and Temporal Dynamics of Dengue in Mexico (2020–2024): A Comprehensive Epidemiological Analysis
abstract: Dengue remains a major public health concern in Mexico, with incidence and clinical burden increasing substantially in recent years. Using national surveillance data from 2020 to 2024, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the changing epidemiological landscape, with an emphasis on geographic distribution, temporal trends, serotype dynamics, and disease severity. Over this period, Mexico saw an almost fivefold increase in dengue cases, reaching over 123,000 confirmed infections and 426 deaths in 2024, the highest annual number recorded. title: The Philosophy of Sambulu in the Life of the Kaili People
abstract: This research article is motivated by the culture of the Kaili community regarding the existence of Sambulu as a traditional custom (adat) that embodies philosophical meanings and values in community life. The research questions are: (1) what is the status of the Sambulu tradition in Kaili culture? (2) what is the philosophical meaning of Sambulu in the life of the Kaili people? and (3) why is the application of Sambulu's philosophical values needed in Kaili community life? title: Geographic and host-associated morphometric variation in Gyrodactylus atratuli Putz and Hoffman, 1963 and Gyrodactylus mediotorus King, Marcogliese, Forest, Mclaughlin and Bentzen, 2013 (Monogenea: Gyrodactylidae) from leuciscid fishes, with first records from Mexico
abstract: Abstract The present study reports the first records of the viviparous monogeneans Gyrodactylus atratuli and Gyrodactylus mediotorus from leuciscid fishes in Mexico, providing new insights into intraspecific haptoral sclerite variability across hosts and geographic regions in North America. Nuclear rDNA (ITS region) genetic analyses confirmed species identities; Mexican G. atratuli sequences showed a 0.7% divergence from Canadian specimens, while Mexican G. mediotorus sequences exhibited a 0.2–0.8% divergence from other North American populations, including those from Texas and Canada. title: The taxonomic status of Eurypterus podolicus Chernyshev, 1947 (Arthropoda: Eurypterida), from the Silurian of Podillia, Ukraine
abstract: This article presents the results of an investigation into the complex history of the eurypterid species "Eurypterus podolicus Chernyshev, 1947", for which neither an original description nor a type series is known. The study confirms that this species is a nomen nudum, as it was never formally described. Moreover, the specimens of "Eurypterus podolicus" from the Borys Chernyshev's collection lack distinct morphological features that would justify recognizing it as a separate species.

title: Sacred Grove as a Community-Oriented Biodiversity Preservation: A Research in the Shekhawati Terrain of Thar Desert
abstract: Sacred Groves, commonly known as Orans or Devbanis in local vernacular, exemplify community-driven biodiversity preservation within the Shekhawati region of the Thar Desert. The community firmly prohibits hunting, logging, and farming in these village commons, which are governed by the residents and dedicated to local deities. Environmental and Biological Importance Sacred forests act as "mini biosphere reserves" and provide refuge for fauna in this arid region. title: Floristic Diversity and Ethnomedicinal Importance of Vaatangi Sacred Grove, Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Sacred groves are patches of forest under community based protection, revered as the abode of local deities and maintained through indigenous cultural beliefs. The present study documents the floristic diversity and ethnomedicinal significance of the Vaatangi Sacred Grove located in Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India. The grove, presided over by Lord Shiva, encompasses one hectare of dry deciduous forest with a documented history exceeding 100 years. journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Beyond two alleles: multiallelic genotypic selection and its estimation from time-series data
abstract: Genetic diversity is central to evolutionary change, with both natural selection and random genetic drift depending on variation within a population. An individual in a diploid population carries two alleles per locus, yet the population as a whole can harbour many alleles, giving rise to a rich spectrum of homozygous and heterozygous genotypes. Such multiallelic variation is common at biologically and medically important loci such as the major histocompatibility complex, the ABO blood group system, and genes underlying monogenic diseases. title: Egyptian Blue Production and Lead Metallurgy in a Late Hellenistic Workshop on Kos (Greece): A Case of Multicrafting
abstract: Abstract A well-preserved late Hellenistic workshop in the agora of Kos provides a rare opportunity to examine pigment production embedded in a multicrafting setting. Excavations of a room in the eastern stoa have revealed fire-structures, Egyptian blue pellets, a range of mineral earth pigments, litharge rods, lead slag, tools and other production debris, demonstrating both pigment manufacture and lead metallurgy within a single workshop space. title: The geometry of gametic dispersal in a flying mammal, Rhinolophus hipposideros
abstract: Abstract Dispersal influences population and evolutionary dynamics, in a manner that depends on by which dispersal strategies gene flow occurs. In some species, mating partners move exclusively for mating, dispersing genes but not individuals. This is the case in many bat species, of which the lesser horseshoe bat ( Rhinolophus hipposideros ) shows a genetic structure at a fine spatial scale suggesting restricted dispersal. title: In What Ways Does Technology-enhanced Teacher Professional Development Change Learning Outcomes in Numeracy, in Marginalised Rural Schools in Bangladesh? A Coarsened Exact Matching Study
abstract: This paper addresses gaps in the international evidence base on the impacts of technology-enhanced Teacher Professional Development (TPD). In particular, it addresses the ways in which teachers’ participation in technology-enhanced TPD changes learning outcomes, in the contexts of marginalised rural schools. Examples of such evidence, arising from large scale studies and conducted by researchers from the global south, are rare. title: The spatial politics of (neo-)imperial mobility control
abstract: What can the study of past imperial practices of mobility control tell us about the present? In this article, we engage with the growing literature that examines how past colonial and imperial practices shape present state strategies of population control, by focusing on the spatial politics of imperial transport practices, and the lessons they provide for understanding similarities between historical and contemporary (neo-)imperial forms of population management. abstract: Abstract Agroforestry systems (AFS) are sustainable land use strategies that promote productivity and environmental conservation. title: Variation in soil phosphorus adsorption and desorption characteristics across agro-ecological zones in Central Nepal
abstract: Phosphorus (P) adsorption and desorption regulate P availability, soil fertility, and the risk of P loss from terrestrial ecosystems; however, these processes remain poorly characterized in Nepalese soils. Despite their significance, there is limited understanding of these processes in Nepalese soils. This study aimed to explore how P adsorption and desorption vary across agro-ecological zones in central Nepal. title: An agenda for plastics crisis research in the synthetic age
abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth-dependent economies instead of a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within-field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field could study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. title: TRANSFORMING THE IMAGE: REFUGEEHOOD, AESTHETICS AND THE POLITICS OF EQUALITY
abstract: At the centre of the image representing refugeehood are bodies forced to leave their homelands. Yet the political significance of refugee images cannot be inferred from visibility alone: visual representations may document suffering while also fixing refugeehood within recognizable figures of tragedy, victimhood, and helplessness. This article asks how different visual regimes configure the relation between the refugee, the image, and the spectator, and under what aesthetic conditions that relation may become a site of political subjectivation rather than the reproduction of victimhood. abstract: Abstract The development of intensified catalytic processes for biomass valorization is a key strategy to improve the sustainability of chemical manufacturing. In this work, we compare a conventional two-reactor and a single-reactor tandem process for the production of the furfural-derived amine 1-(furan-2-yl)-4-methylpentan-2-amine (F-ALD-1-NH2), combining technoeconomic analysis (TEA) and cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA). title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices in School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management of Elementary School Heads in Fourth Congressional District of Quezon: Basis for Development of School Safety Manual
abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of elementary school heads in School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (SDRRM) in the Fourth Congressional District of Quezon, Philippines, during School Year 2024–2025, as a basis for developing a School Safety Manual. Anchored on the Knowledge–Attitude–Practice Theory and Comprehensive School Safety Framework, the study employed a quantitative descriptive–correlational design involving 38 elementary school heads selected through cluster sampling. abstract: Abstract Context Investigating how habitat specialists express population-level differences in habitat preferences and movement behaviour across contrasting landscapes and abiotic environments allows us to distinguish patterns that are consistent across populations from those that are population-specific responses to local conditions. title: Bodies in Motion: Images of Women in the Magazine Frou-Frou (Rio de Janeiro, 1923–1927)
abstract: In the 1920s, Rio de Janeiro emerged as a cosmopolitan capital marked by rapid urban development and profound social change. During this period, women experienced greater freedom of movement and expanded opportunities for participation in social life outside the home. At the same time, fashion underwent radical change: while Paris remained an important reference point, North American influences—circulating primarily through cinema—gained increasing prominence. abstract: Hexastylis viridistylis (Aristolochiaceae) is described as a novel species distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of morphological characters including style and ovary color and dimensions, stamen morphology, calyx tube dimensions, and fruiting characteristics. title: Developing Sustainable Tourism Through Ecotourism: Theoretical Foundations and Practical Directions for Uzbekistan
abstract: This article analyses, from both theoretical and practical perspectives, the role of ecotourism in shaping sustainable tourism. Drawing on a review of international literature, it examines the three pillars of ecotourism (nature conservation, local community well-being, and environmental education) and synthesises their interrelationships. It then identifies the potential of ecotourism in Uzbekistan, the problems currently constraining it, and the mechanisms through which it can be developed. abstract: This study investigates the technical, economic and environmental feasibility of a hybrid solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, battery storage and diesel-generator system for supplying Koluama 1 and Koluama 2 communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A bottom-up electricity load assessment was conducted using household appliance inventories and estimated electricity requirements for residential, educational, healthcare and commercial consumers. title: Effects of Organic Fertilizer Substitutions on Latex Yield and Soil Fertility in Hevea brasiliensis Plantations: A Case Study in Southern Philippines
abstract: ABSTRACT Rubber plantations can be a major source of income for small landholder farmers in rural communities across Southern Asia. However, rising fertilizer costs and progressive soil degradation threaten long‐term productivity and economic viability. To address this challenge, we conducted fertilizer trials across two field sites (Acrisols and Cambisols) in the southern Philippines, to evaluate the effects of reduced chemical fertilizer rates and organic fertilizer substitution on latex yield and soil fertility in mature rubber plantations. title: Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of Nanomaterials Drive Photochemical Production of Reactive Species and Pollutant Degradation in Surface Waters
abstract: Reactive intermediates in surface waters are widely attributed to dissolved organic matter (DOM). Natural, incidental, or engineered nanomaterials simultaneously occur at parts per billion and can function as photocatalysts, yet the photochemical role of nanomaterials at environmentally relevant concentrations remains overlooked in surface water photochemistry. title: Equity in the Technology Sector for Pasifika Learners in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Pasifika peoples remain significantly underrepresented in Aotearoa New Zealand’s technology sector; despite comprising 8.9% of the population they make up less than 3% of those in digital and IT pathways. This disparity reflects structural inequities that constrain access, progression and representation, with clear impacts on workforce participation, education and economic outcomes. Using Pacific research methodologies, this qualitative study evaluates the effectiveness of micro-credentials and Pasifika-led IT programmes in addressing these inequities. title: Entangled Naturalisms: : Drawing nature beyond media.
abstract: This paper presents practice-based and theoretical contributions exploring how field drawing, site-specific practice, environmental humanities, walking and durational practices, and embodied experience can extend architectural drawing methodologies beyond medium-specificity and dualistic culture. Drawing as a situated and embodied practice — entangled with analogue, digital, and hybrid media, on-site, in motion, with collected data, images, traces, memories, and matter — can shift practice toward drawing from within an environment in intra-action, with all actors active in the drawing process.

title: Monsters of finance
abstract: Abstract An anthropology of horror can serve as a vernacular critique of financial speculation. Drawing on fieldwork in San Pedro, Paraguay, I track horror across three registers: pombero tricksters; plata yvyguy (buried money) as a founding myth of postwar finance; and obligations binding sesame farmers to monsters, patrones , and creditors. title: Shifting Alignments in India’s Southeast Asia Policies
abstract: Drawing on historical and contemporary sources, this research argued that India’s policies toward Southeast Asia have been shaped by the interplay of three primary drivers: security maximization, economic maximization, and power maximization. The dominance of one driver or a combination of drivers varies across temporal phases, producing shifting alignments in India’s policy orientation and its regional engagement with Southeast Asia. This research applied neo-classical realism to examine the evolution of India’s foreign policy towards Southeast Asia from the Cold War through the post-Cold War

title: Voluntary Migration and Internal Displacement: A Study of Unhomeliness in Thrity Umrigar’s The Museum of Failures
abstract: Migration in today’s world is the most debatable topic that involves the movement of people from one place to another both individually or collectively. The traditional notions of voluntary migration often highlight the movement undertaken by an individual as a search for a better lifestyle, a better job offer, or for educational purposes. This study attempts to break this traditional notion of voluntary migration by stating that movement is also triggered by pain. title: Coupling advanced treatments with reactive barrier infiltration for pharmaceutical micropollutants removal in the context of water reuse
abstract: Recharging aquifers with treated wastewater provides multiple benefits for sustainable water management, but micropollutants in effluents can threaten groundwater quality, aquatic ecosystems, and human health. Infiltration-based recharge can improve water quality and remove micropollutants, a performance that can be enhanced by reactive barriers. Advanced treatments such as nanofiltration or ozonation can also achieve high micropollutant abatement. title: Readers of the Living: Interpretive Mastery and Natural Thinking in Plutarch, Celsus, Origen, and Porphyry
abstract: Abstract This article examines the intersection between imperial writings on animals and post-Hellenistic debates about exegesis. It is the first study to argue that interpreters drawing on Aristotelian theories of voice and Hellenistic ideas of natural sympathy treated the meaningful but non-verbal animal as a test case of nature’s availability to reading, and as an opportunity to reflect on how exegetes transfer their skills between literature and the natural world. title: Effect of Phlogopite and Zeolite as a Countermeasure for Radiocesium Uptake Into Herbage
abstract: ABSTRACT The effects of applying Finnish phlogopite and artificial zeolite to reduce radiocesium transfer to herbage in a grassland were assessed over a seven‐year period. In all experimental plots, potassium chloride was applied to increase the exchangeable potassium content (ExK) to 400 mg K 2 O/kg in 2015. After 2016, the same amounts of nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium fertilizers were applied twice a year. title: Niallia Circulans mediated Bio-fabrication of ZnO nanoparticles: Synthesis, characterization, and multifunctional applications
abstract: The current study addresses increasing global problems (agricultural sustainability, environmental contamination, and antimicrobial resistance) by means of sustainable and multifunctional biosynthesized Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The study utilized a cell-free supernatant of a novel endophytic bacterial strain (Niallia Circulans) to synthesize ZnO NPs. title: “But Grief Isn’t the End of Any Story”
abstract: In this article, I argue that the genre of memoir, and grief memoirs in particular, can be read as an exploratory space through which ecological grief can be acknowledged and engaged with. As I suggest, grief memoirs and their genre affordances for channeling loss—through aspects of commemoration, meaning-making, relationality, community, and more—can be mapped onto ecological grief in meaningful ways. title: Integrating the Diverse Values of Nature Into Environmental Law and Policy: Insights From Scottish Peatland Restoration
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper aims to arrive at a better understanding of the integration of the diverse values of nature (instrumental, intrinsic, relational) into (environmental) law and policy, using peatland restoration in Scotland as a case study. It argues that adopting a pluri‐value approach is a useful tool for both the design and implementation of environmental law and policy. title: Steel robots and space turtleships: the divergence of Korean animation and Japanese anime
abstract: During the Park Chung-hee military dictatorship, Korea shadowed Japanese industrial upgrading at every stage. The same was true in animation, in which Korea took Japanese animations, indigenized them, and imbued them with a techno-nationalism that positioned Korean animation as both dependent on Japan and destined to overcome it. Instead, the opposite happened: today South Korean animation is a pale shadow of Japanese anime’s global success. This essay argues that this divergence, rather than the result of flawed state policies or overdependence on outsourcing, is the result of objective shift
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema

title: Renewable water treatment using electrodialysis for hydrogen production
abstract: Hydrogen production in arid and semi-arid regions is constrained by water availability and groundwater quality. This study presents a proof of concept treatment integrating alkaline softening and electrodialysis (ED) to condition real brackish groundwater for hydrogen production. ED is particularly attractive for waters with low or moderate salinity, as it provides an alternative to conventional reverse osmosis that operates at low pressure while enabling progressive deionization. Real brackish groundwater from Castilla La Mancha, Spain, characterized by high mineralization and a complex ionic

title: Extreme Necessity on the Fringe – Copycat Crimes During the Great Famine of 1695–1697 in Finland
abstract: This article delves into three similar robbery-murders committed during the Great Famine of 1695–1697 on the periphery of Finland. The seventeenth century in Europe was marked by several famines, but Finland was especially hard-hit. The murders all occurred within six months of each other and were driven by hunger. The victims, defenceless women, were murdered in their sleep while their husbands were away. title: A case for empire: Why the United States intervened in Venezuela in 2026?
abstract: This research article analyzes the U.S. military operation “Absolute Resolve” on Janu- ary 3, 2026, which resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife by Delta Force units supported by air and naval assets. Employing a qualitative interpretive case- study design, the study examines the event through five analytical levels: civilizational, geopoliti- cal, international relations, political philosophy, and military. The findings show that the inter- vention reflects persistent imperial logic, thalassocratic geopolitical imperatives, a shift toward offensive realism
journal: Military Studies Journal for Strategy Technology and Defense Sciences

title: Temporal shifts in insect cuticular hydrocarbons in response to experimental desiccation
abstract: Insects are vulnerable to desiccation as they are small and have a high surface area-to-volume ratios. Over 80% of their body water is lost through the cuticle, but insects possess specialised cells that synthesize cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) to form a hydrophobic waxy barrier that reduces water loss. However, how rapidly CHCs are synthesized and transported across the cuticle under desiccating conditions remains poorly understood. title: Fear of the super competitor? Deer respond more strongly to pigs than coyotes
abstract: Abstract Wildlife species face complex trade-offs when maximizing foraging efficiency while minimizing risks from predation and competition. Behavioral responses to these pressures often vary based on intrinsic factors like sex, and can have important implications for individual fitness and population dynamics. However, the relative importance of predation versus competition in shaping behavior, and how this differs between sexes, remains poorly understood. title: An Innovative Approach for Estimating Coseismic Surface Uplifts Using Ionospheric Observations From Remote GNSS Stations: First Application for the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake
abstract: Abstract The M w 7.7 Myanmar earthquake on 28 March 2025 ruptured ∼480 km of the Sagaing Fault. Its fault slip distribution remains poorly constrained by three‐dimensional surface displacement data due to sparse GNSS‐coverage near the fault. Satellite‐based synthetic aperture radars capture meters of right‐lateral displacements but isolating vertical crustal movements from these measurements is challenging. institutions: Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research

title: Travel history and occupation among diagnosed Cutaneous Leishmaniasis cases in Guyana: A multi-site retrospective case series, 2017–2021
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) in Guyana has not been systematically characterised in the peer-reviewed literature for several decades. This study aimed to describe the demographic, occupational, geographic, and clinical profile of diagnosed CL cases at Guyana's principal diagnostic sites, and to test, within this case series, whether field-based occupation is associated with reported interior travel and whether travel history is associated with time to presentation. title: Leaf Morphological Responses to Serpentine Soils in Shikoku, Japan: A Review of Common Patterns and Developmental Diversity
abstract: ABSTRACT Serpentine soil mosaics are found in Shikoku, Japan, and many plant species that inhabit these habitats change their morphology and anatomy in response to the soil chemical and physical properties. To clarify commonality and diversity in leaf morphological responses, we reviewed studies on phylogenetically distinct taxa occurring in serpentine areas, including the woody plants Eurya japonica Thunb. var. japonica (Ternstroemiaceae) and Ligustrum japonicum Thunb. title: Multi-criteria assessment of bio-based construction on circularity, environmental impact and feasibility
abstract: Over the past decade, the construction industry has increasingly prioritized climate neutrality. In line with this, the EU Green Deal and its ‘Fit-for-55’ legislative package aim to reduce total emissions by 55% by 2030. A major challenge in achieving this goal is addressing the embodied carbon of building materials, which arises from production, transportation, and end-of-life stages. Reaching such targets requires a fundamental shift from the current linear construction model toward a circular and low-carbon approach. journal: GRID - Architecture Planning and Design Journal

title: From “common sense” to “good sense” climate adaptation: extreme heat in the austere city
abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that ‘common sense’ provides an adequate framework for understanding how people respond to climate change. Appeals to ‘common sense’ naturalize individual responsibility, obscuring the structural conditions that shape adaptive capacity, and we propose ‘good sense’ as a more accurate account of how people actually reason about and adapt to climate change. The paper draws on ethnographic fieldwork to examine everyday responses to extreme heat in a low-income neighbourhood in Manchester, UK. title: Evaluation of the Plant Growth-Promoting Potential of Bacillus subtilis Isolated from the Rhizosphere of Berberis aristata for Improving Drought Stress Tolerance in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum)
abstract: The rhizosphere is a very favourable environment for the presence of a wide range of microorganisms, which allow many beneficial interactions between the plants and microorganisms. Bacillus species are known as plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to improve the growth and productivity of plants, among these microbes. All seven isolates were found to be Gram-positive bacteria and had multiple plant growth promoting abilities such as phosphate solubilization, zinc solubilization, production of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), phytase, siderophores, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) and 1aminocyclopropan
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: SCREENING OF PROBIOTIC BACTERIA FOR ARAPAIMA GIGAS AND FIRST REPORT OF DISEASE CAUSED BY ENTEROBACTER CLOACAE
abstract: O “Arapaima gigas” é uma espécie importante e estratégica para a aquicultura na América do Sul, gerando impactos econômicos e sociais significativos, especialmente na região amazônica. No entanto, desafios sanitários podem limitar sua produtividade. Este estudo realizou o isolamento, a caracterização e a identificação de bactérias autóctones do intestino de “A. gigas” provenientes da aquicultura amazônica, visando identificar isolados bacterianos com potencial probiótico. title: Assessment of Aspergillus niger and Bacillus subtilis Potential in the Biodegradation of Cassava Peels
abstract: The processing of cassava for human consumption leads to the generation of large quantities of cassava peel waste. The continuous accumulation of these peels has contributed to environmental pollution, thereby placing significant pressure on waste management systems. This study aimed to assess the biodegradation potentials of Aspergillus niger and Bacillus subtilis, individually and in combination, using cassava peels as the substrate. Cassava peels were obtained from Sokoto Central Market, Nigeria and subjected to biodegradation using laboratory-maintained isolates. Biodegradation efficiency

title: Ungrievable lives: State and non-state authoritarianism in the making of Uyghur foreign fighters
abstract: While there is a broad literature on the policies of authoritarian regimes toward their populations abroad, we know far less about the inclusionary and exclusionary policies of authoritarian host states toward displaced populations residing within their own territories. This article examines how Uyghur refugees who fled China and arrived in Turkey via third countries between 2014 and 2016 were channelled into conflict zones in Syria through the interaction of state institutions, diaspora organisations, and armed non-state actors. title: Contribution of subnational regions to national climate change mitigation targets
abstract: This study developed a methodology for analyzing the mitigation measures expected of each region within a country, as well as the resulting regional energy supply–demand balances, given national decarbonization targets and assumed future energy system conditions. Using national-level values as an overarching framework, the method represents interregional energy flows and constructed two scenarios: (1) a scenario in which all regions make efforts of equal stringency to collectively achieve the national target (CN1) and (2) a scenario in which each region seeks to achieve carbon neutrality indep

title: Oportunidades y Barreras de la Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria frente al Desarrollo Sostenible en América Latina: Una Revisión Exploratoria
abstract: Introducción: La Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria (ESPS) abarca una serie de prácticas colectivas que parecen contribuir al Desarrollo Sostenible (DS) pero cuya evidencia se encuentra dispersa en América Latina. Objetivo: Mapear la evidencia sobre la vinculación entre ESPS y DS en América Latina, identificando oportunidades, desafíos y vacíos en la literatura. Método: Se realizó una revisión exploratoria siguiendo las recomendaciones PRISMA-ScR. Resultados: Se incluyeron 15 estudios de 3670 recuperados. title: Traditional preservation practices of asala fish (Schizothorax spp.) among Himalayan communities of Darjeeling, India
abstract: Abstract Traditional fish preservation practices are an important part of the cultural heritage and food systems of the Darjeeling Himalayas. In this study, the traditional methods used by local communities to preserve asala fish ( Schizothorax spp.) have been documented. Data were collected from the 50 respondents over the age of 18 including fish farmers, hatchery operators, fish processors, traders, and household members engaged in fish production, preservation, and marketing. title: Depresión psicótica: una revisión sistemática de su clínica, diagnóstico y tratamiento
abstract: Psychotic depression (PD) is a severe manifestation of major depressive disorder characterized by the presence of psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations and delusions, alongside the typical signs and symptoms of depression. This condition poses significant challenges in both diagnosis and treatment due to the complexity of its clinical presentation. A systematic review was conducted with the aim of outlining the fundamental aspects of PD, including its definition, clinical features, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic strategies. title: Konstrukcija Drugosti i socijalno-ontoloških granica u filmu Avatar: put vode
abstract: Using a three-part ethnographic approach – combining production analysis, narrative interpretation, and reception studies – this paper examines James Cameron’s Avatar: The Way of Water (2022). Grounded in theories of representation and social ontology, the study analyzes how the sequel negotiates the dichotomy between Self and Other. While seemingly promoting ecological awareness and anti-colonialism, the film reinforces structures embedded in colonial and neoliberal logic. title: Climate change threatens montane and cloud forest tree species in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract Montane and cloud forests are high-elevation ecosystems dependent on specific environmental conditions and increasingly threatened by fragmentation, isolation, and climate change in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. We quantified changes in climatic suitability for two characteristic tree species of these ecosystems, Drimys angustifolia and Ilex microdonta , under future climate scenarios, assessing range contraction and expansion, potential losses of suitable areas, and opportunities for ecological restoration. title: Tablewares and Ten-Footers: The Materiality of Irish Immigrant Life in Nineteenth-Century Lowell, Massachusetts
abstract: Abstract The Irish immigrant experience in 19th-century North America is often framed in terms of processes of oppression and racialization. However, archaeological and documentary evidence from the industrial city of Lowell, Massachusetts, complicates this narrative, because Lowell’s Irish population transcended the initial trauma of immigration and the challenge of anti-Irish prejudice by leveraging the powers of the Catholic Church and of community-building mechanisms, such as residential clustering and voluntary associations, to become a major political force in the city. title: The Cultural Foundations of African Religions
abstract: Two great world religions now occupy the African stage: Christianity and Islam. However, they rest upon a foundation of African spirituality that assumes very diverse forms. Distinct indigenous religious traditions are associated with the four great ethno-linguistic phyla that have historically come to define the continent’s social and cultural life: the Afro-Asiatic, Nilo-Saharan, Niger-Congo, and Khoisan. title: Differences in mating behaviours associated with morphological traits between two co-existing Japanese dojo loach species of the genus Misgurnus (Cypriniformes: Cobitidae)
abstract: Most cobitid loaches (Cypriniformes: Cobitidae) exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism associated with mating behaviour. However, empirical evidence linking this differentiation in mating-related morphology to reproductive isolation remains limited. In Japan, the dojo loach (Misgurnus anguillicaudatus sensu lato) comprises two distinct species: a cryptic species (Misgurnus sp. Type I sensu Okada et al. title: The Music of the IPTA: An Exercise in Soviet Cosmopolitanism
abstract: There has been no dearth of interest in the politics of IPTA in Indian intellectual circles. Moreover, in Indian Bengal, shaped by thirty-four years of communist party rule, the IPTA movement has been romanticised as an urban elite’s excursion (declassing oneself) into the lives of the rural peasantry and the urban working class. title: GEOLOGICAL, MINERALOGICAL AND GEOCHEMICAL CHARACTERISATION OF THE ILUHAGBA MARBLE DEPOSIT, SOUTHEASTERN ISANLU, CENTRAL NIGERIA: IMPLICATIONS FOR INDUSTRIAL APPLICATIONS
abstract: Marble, a metamorphosed limestone, is a critical raw material used in constructions, production of cement and soil improvement additives globally. In Nigeria, marble occurs as relict carbonate within the “Pan-African” (late Proterozoic) migmatite-gneiss-schist complex, such as the Isanlu region, central Nigeria. title: Revisions to the 2023 U.S. 50‐State National Seismic Hazard Model
abstract: We present an update to the 2023 U.S. 50‐state National Seismic Hazard Model, based on questions and comments received from a range of users, as well as additional internal and building code reviews since its initial release. title: Cadmium and lead: genotoxic effects on the broodstock of the fish Prochilodus magdalenae (Characiformes: Prochilodontidae)
abstract: Introduction: Heavy metals such as cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) pose a significant threat to aquatic ecosystems due to their persistence, capacity for bioaccumulation, and genotoxic potential. These contaminants are of particular concern in tropical freshwater systems, where they may impact native species of ecological, economic, and nutritional importance, such as Prochilodus magdalenae, a migratory fish endemic to the Magdalena–Cauca River basin in Colombia. title: Salinity and Sodicity Tolerance in Rice: Physiological, morpho-anatomical, Molecular and Hormonal Mechanisms with special Reference to Traditional Landraces
abstract: Soil salinity and sodicity are critical abiotic stresses severely affecting global rice production by causing osmotic stress, ionic toxicity, oxidative damage and nutrient imbalance, collectively impairing plant growth and yield. This review highlights the physiological, morpho-anatomical, molecular and hormonal mechanisms involved in salt tolerance, with special focus on traditional landraces as reservoirs of adaptive genetic diversity. title: Climate at the Apex: The Emerging Role of Apex Courts in Global Climate Governance
abstract: Abstract This article offers the first global mapping and comparative analysis of climate litigation reaching domestic apex courts. Drawing on a novel dataset, it identifies more than 360 cases decided between 1995 and 2024, with a sharp rise since 2015. Apex courts are defined as the highest domestic judicial bodies with final jurisdiction over climate-relevant matters. Our analysis shows that apex court decisions lean modestly toward outcomes supportive of stronger climate action. title: Risk and Cost Assessment of Suez Canal Transit Compared with Alternative Multimodal Corridors for Container Shipping between Abu Dhabi and Constanța
abstract: This paper quantifies the operational risk and the transport cost of a 10,000 TEU shipment between Abu Dhabi and Constanța South and compares the Suez Canal route with the Cape of Good Hope detour and with two multimodal corridors through Iran. One framework is applied to all four routes: a documented risk register, an expected-delay model, a Markov chain and an exposure-time model for the Suez Canal segment, a Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 runs, reliability importance measures, and a Benchmark Index combining cost, time, capacity, energy and risk cost. title: Impact of sequential extraction on structure and antioxidant activity of fucoidan from Turbinaria spp.
abstract: Sequential extraction has recently emerged as an alternative strategy for the comprehensive utilization of brown seaweed biomass, enabling the recovery of multiple bioactive compounds, including fucoidan. However, its influence on fucoidan structure and bioactivity remains insufficiently understood. title: Habitat Use, Resource Acquisition, and Risk Management of Raccoons in Human-Modified Landscapes across North America
abstract: Urbanization creates concentrated food sources, artificial habitats and fragmented living environments for adaptable medium-sized carnivores. However, ecological studies of raccoons mostly carry out separately on habitat utilization and so on, which hinders the understanding of their continued existence in human-altered landscapes. During the period from 2000 to 2026, a systematic review in line with PRISMA guidelines was carried out on the content carried in Science Network, focusing on North American raccoons. title: MOSQUE TOURISM AND URBAN CULTURAL IDENTITY: A SUSTAINABLE PLANNING FRAMEWORK FOR MALAYSIAN CITIES
abstract: This article examines mosque tourism as a spatial and cultural mechanism shaping urban cultural identity in Malaysian cities. Focusing on Kuala Terengganu, Melaka, George Town, and Putrajaya, it investigates how mosques function beyond religious institutions to contribute to urban placemaking, heritage representation, and tourism development. abstract: Abstract Background Liver fibrosis is a progressive pathological disease characterised by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix and damage to hepatocellular architecture. Despite increasing therapeutic requirements, existing antifibrotic therapies are limited. Amaranthus spinosus , an ethnomedicinal plant used by many tribal groups in India, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its antifibrotic effectiveness remains unknown. title: NAHDLATUL ULAMA’S CULTURAL DA’WAH STRATEGY IN BUILDING RELIGIOUS HARMONY IN JEPARA REGENCY: RITUALIZED BRIDGING IN A POST-CONFLICT SETTING
abstract: Purpose: This study analyses how Nahdlatul Ulama’s (NU) cultural da’wah strategy and the role of religious leaders build religious harmony in Jepara Regency, Central Java, a post-conflict area that experienced religiously charged unrest in 1998 and a church-construction dispute lasting nearly two decades. title: Patients’ and Health Care Workers’ Perspectives on Barriers to Hypertension Care in a Pastoralist Setting
abstract: Hypertension affects about one in four Kenyan adults, yet only 15.5% of those affected are aware of their status. No measured prevalence estimate exists for Mandera County, where pastoral mobility, 77% absolute poverty and sparse health services are likely to compound underdetection, while evidence from transitioning pastoralist populations shows that their historically low cardiovascular risk is rising. abstract: BACKGROUND: Surgical site infections (SSI) associated with spinal cord stimulation (SCS) implants pose risks of morbidity, mortality, and increased healthcare costs. Immunocompromised patients are especially vulnerable due to impaired immune responses, delaying diagnosis and increasing complications. Current guidelines recommend SCS explantation for deep or inadequately treated superficial SSI, though the role of capsulectomy remains underexplored despite its use in other fields like plastic surgery and cardiology. title: Hepatitis aguda de origen desconocido: Revisión narrativa sobre el potencial rol del Adenovirus F41
abstract: La hepatitis de origen desconocido (HOD), reportada en más de 1,000 casos en 35 países hasta julio de 2022, representa un desafío en salud pública, especialmente en niños, con una posible asociación al adenovirus humano (HAdV), subtipo F41, aunque su papel etiológico sigue siendo debatido. title: RESISTIVE LITERATURE IN THE DISCOURSE OF SUFISM: A CONTEXTUAL LINGUISTIC STUDY OF THE TEACHINGS OF SHEIKH YUSUF AL-MAKASSARY
abstract: This study examines the Sufi teachings of Sheikh Yusuf Al-Makassary as a form of resistive literature, namely a spiritual discourse that functions as a resistance against physical colonization, cultural domination, and epistemic oppression during the colonial period. title: The empirics of the tourism–growth nexus: how does tourism specialization affect regional growth paths?
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the link between tourism specialization and regional growth rates and factor accumulation. Based on convergence growth theory, we use a Bartik instrument to address the endogeneity of tourism intensity in explaining GDP per capita growth rates. Using data for Spanish provinces over the 2002–2018 period, we find that tourism positively affects regional economic growth. Nonetheless, there is evidence of an inverted-U relationship, indicating that the growth-enhancing effects of tourism diminish at high levels of overnight stays per capita. title: Rethinking municipal electricity in South Africa: Rooftop solar PV, revenue and just energy transitions in the City of Johannesburg
abstract: South Africa’s deepening electricity crisis, marked by persistent load-shedding and escalating tariffs, has accelerated private solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. This rapid transition has raised concerns about municipal revenue erosion, cross-subsidisation and energy inequality. The City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality (CoJ) is at the centre of this transition, and is grappling with the implications for its business model and how private solar PV can be leveraged to support a just energy transition. title: Double Standards Regarding Animals as Silent Agents in Legislation: The Case of Wild Fish Welfare in Finland
abstract: Fishing is one of the most widespread forms of wild animal use, yet welfare norms governing this practiceremain limited. Recent legislation in Finland aims to improve fish welfare, with both the new Animal Welfare Act (AWA), effective from 2024, and amendments to the Fishing Act introducing provisions on the handling and killing of fish. abstract: Organisms that make up the soil fauna are involved in several activities related to the functioning of the soil ecosystem. They present high diversity and are distributed throughout the world, in different conditions, and can be used as bioindicators of soil quality among different management conditions. There are few studies carried out on soil fauna in South America, mainly involving mountainous regions, which are suffering strong anthropogenic impacts. title: People of Three Rivers: Rematriating Wiradjuri Living Waters
abstract: Wiradjuri are freshwater people whose identity is constituted through relationships with three interconnected rivers: Wambuul (Macquarie), Galari (Lachlan) and Marrambidya (Murrumbidgee), with Milawa (Murray) marking the Nation’s southern boundary. A companion article develops the freshwater ontology through which Wiradjuri understand themselves as the people of three rivers; this article extends that work by examining rematriation as the return of ancestral relationships, responsibilities and authority between Wiradjuri peoples and living waters. abstract: Abstract Background: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is associated with substantial psychiatric morbidity, yet the nature and scope of integrated child and adolescent psychiatry within specialist CSA services in Ireland are poorly described. Methods: This retrospective chart review included all children and adolescents referred to an embedded child and adolescent psychiatry clinic within The Alders Unit, a specialist CSA service, between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2025. title: Impact of stress combination on Brettanomyces bruxellensis growth and volatile phenol production
abstract: Brettanomyces bruxellensis is a major wine spoilage yeast responsible for the production of volatile phenols, including 4-ethylphenol (EP) and 4-ethylguaiacol (EG), from grape-derived hydroxycinnamic acids. title: Exercise and white matter hyperintensities: a randomized clinical trial
abstract: Abstract Subcortical vascular cognitive impairment (SVCI) is a risk factor for dementia. White matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions are considered a hallmark of SVCI. We investigated the impact of progressive resistance exercise training (RT) on WMH in individuals with SVCI. This 12-month, single-blinded, proof-of-concept randomized clinical trial involved 89 community-dwelling individuals aged 55 years or older living with SVCI. abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease–mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) promotes coronary artery calcification (CAC), MicroRNAs may serve as potential biomarkers for its progression. abstract: A potential solution to the problem of management of ever-increasing plastic waste through chemical recycling using nuclear energy is presented in this paper. The nuclear plant is co-located with the plant decomposing the plastic waste into feedstock chemicals and the one upcycling the feedstock chemicals into high value industrial products such as steel and transportation fuel. title: From Foraging to Dairy Pastoralism: Indigenous Transformation Among Sami in Early Modern Northern Fennoscandia
abstract: Aboriginal societies worldwide have independently transformed their modes of production. In northern Eurasia, this included a shift from transport-oriented reindeer herding toward a pastoral economy between the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries. This article examines whether this transition among the Indigenous Sami of northern Fennoscandia was accompanied by intensified milking and a more elaborate dairy culture. abstract: Industrialization, urbanization, and agricultural practices have substantially increased the accumulation of contaminants in the environment, often adversely affecting nontarget aquatic species. Cladoceran species are considered valuable bioindicators in ecotoxicity studies because they are easy to culture, have transparent bodies, and are highly sensitive to chemical pollution. abstract: ABSTRACT The Pinerolo‐Sanfront Unit (PSU), the structurally lowest tectonic unit of the Dora‐Maira Massif (Western Alps), has been regarded as a monocyclic unit composed of Permo‐Carboniferous sediments and Permian granitoids that were metamorphosed during the Alpine orogeny. abstract: Objective: Acinetobacter lwoffii is an environmental organism and skin commensal with low intrinsic virulence. title: Diapausing adult female mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) in overwintering sites in Estonia in 2023–2024: Species composition and variation
abstract: In temperate regions, several mosquito species overwinter as diapausing females in sheltered habitats, enabling them to serve as early-season vectors of mosquito-borne pathogens. While overwintering species compositions have been documented in several parts of Europe, no comprehensive data exist for Estonia or for the Baltic region. title: Microbial Primer: Mirror bacteria
abstract: Mirror bacteria are hypothetical synthetic organisms built from molecules of opposite chirality to those used throughout nature. This primer discusses their potential dangers: because of their chiral mismatch to the natural environment, mirror bacteria could plausibly evade predation, immunity and other ecological control mechanisms to a degree never seen before. This property could simultaneously make them unprecedented invasive species and dangerous pathogens.

title: Asymptotic behavior of lidar scattering properties of absorbing dust aerosols across Rayleigh and geometrical-optics regimes: theory and implications
abstract: Lidar ratio (S), linear depolarization ratio (δ), and single-scattering albedo (ω) are central quantities for dust typing and property retrieval in lidar remote sensing. We investigate their dependence on size parameter (x) and iron oxide fraction of mineral dust using TAMUdust2020 and triaxial-ellipsoid calculations. Results show a consistent asymptotic structure that is weakly sensitive to particle shape in both limits of scattering theory. abstract: This article examines how embodied knowledge contributes to both the reproduction and possible reorientation of meat consumption. abstract: Five waves of the Young Lives Indian survey are analysed using sequence and regression analysis. abstract: Combining sedimentation and flotation for fine-particle removal from mineral suspensions is challenging because the two processes favour different particle sizes, aggregate structures and interfacial conditions. abstract: In primeval forests, it is possible to recognise patches that differ in structure and composition. title: Electromagnetic Compatibility Testing of Military Ships
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing of military ships is an essential process for ensuring the correct and safe operation of electrical and electronic systems under complex operational conditions. This paper presents a methodology for assessing electromagnetic compatibility at the ship level, considering the vessel as an integrated system. abstract: This paper seeks to show how contemporary ecological elegy, specifically elegy proleptically lamenting the “end of nature,” opens up new scripts for mourning in the Anthropocene. abstract: A future energy system centred on renewables and hydrogen requires reliable, high-density storage and cost-effective transport at scale. Metals (and metal oxides) offer a compelling pathway for a fast integration of hydrogen into a sector coupled energy system: circular energy carriers that provide safe and dispatchable energy. This review discusses the role of hydrogen in metal reduction processes for renewable energy storage, with subsequent metal oxidation delivering heat and hydrogen for industry and grids. title: THE INSTITUTIONAL ROLE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT IN SHAPING THE URBAN SPACE OF POST-REFORM KHERSON (SECOND HALF OF THE 19TH CENTURY)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to define the institutional role of the Kherson City Duma and the city administration in shaping the urban space of post-reform Kherson based on an analysis of municipal records, as well as to analyze the mechanisms through which local self-government influenced the modernization of the city’s infrastructure, socio-functional organization, and management practices, which shaped the nature of the city’s urban transformations during the post-reform era. title: Petal infrared transmission warms flowers and reduces microbial abundance
abstract: Flowers create distinct internal microclimates, yet how these conditions filter microbial abundance remains poorly understood. We tested whether petal light transmission and internal floral temperature influence microbial abundance in two co-occurring species, Lyonia lucida and Lyonia fruticosa (Ericaceae), which have translucent petal 'windows' that modify internal light environments. We measured internal and external floral temperatures, quantified culturable microbial abundance (yeasts, molds, bacteria), and assessed ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) petal transmission using spectrometry.

abstract: The floristic diversity of India contains a large variety of Anukta dravyas (extrapharmacopoeial drugs) which are not included in classical Ayurveda textbooks and API and is being used extensively from decades. Many plant medicines with therapeutic qualities were not listed in classical treatises due to the innumerability of plant species. Therefore, no any classical herbal pharmacopeia is available which enumerates all the medicinal plants. abstract: Modern slavery in Nigeria is a huge concern that calls for attention; research proves an estimated 1.6 million people suffering from modern slavery, this should be about 7.8 people out of every thousand facing and enduring the torture and evil of modern slavery. abstract: This work investigates an MnBr₂–Ne–HBr source driven by a semiconductor linear-transformer-driver (LTD) excitation system as a radiation source for differential-absorption sensing and high-speed optical diagnostics. This is the first implementation of a manganese-halide laser source of this type using semiconductor pumping. title: Impacto de la obesidad sarcopenica sobre la composición corporal, el desempeño funcional y el riesgo de caída en adultos mayores residentes en comunidades rurales del Ecuador
abstract: La obesidad sarcopénica es un síndrome geriátrico caracterizado por la coexistencia de exceso de tejido adiposo y disminución de la masa y función muscular. Esta condición se asocia con alteraciones de la composición corporal, deterioro funcional, fragilidad y mayor riesgo de caídas, constituyendo un importante problema de salud pública en la población adulta mayor, especialmente en comunidades rurales. title: Formulation, Characterization and Biological Evaluation of Ciclopirox Olamine- Loaded Vaterite Carrier- Based Hydrogel for Enhancing Antifungal Activity
abstract: The present study aimed to develop a Ciclopirox olamine-loaded calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) vaterite nanoparticle hydrogel as an enhanced topical antifungal delivery system. Ciclopirox olamine-loaded CaCO₃ nanoparticles were prepared using a microemulsion-based method and evaluated by physicochemical, computational, pharmaceutical, and microbiological approaches. title: Humanitarian Response Strategies and Managing Climate-Induced Displacement in Ogoja Local Government Area of Cross River State, Nigeria
abstract: The study investigated humanitarian response strategies and managing climate-induced displacement in Ogoja Local Government Area of Cross River State, Nigeria. Two objectives guided the study: to analyze the influence of emergency relief on managing climate-induced displacement and to examine the influence of rehabilitation strategies on managing climate-induced displacement in Ogoja Local Government Area. abstract: Abstract Pressure-assisted freezing produces frozen foods with finer ice crystals, less drip loss and longer microbiological shelf life than conventional freezing, but its adoption has been limited because the conventional implementation, pressure-shift freezing (PSF), requires a hyperbaric pump delivering 100–200 MPa whose capital cost and mechanical complexity are the principal barrier to industrial deployment. title: CONTAMINATION BY POTENTIALLY TOXIC METALS IN SURFACE WATERS IN BRAZIL
abstract: Contamination of surface waters by potentially toxic metals represents an important environmental concern due to their persistence, bioaccumulation, and potential effects on aquatic ecosystems and human health. This study aimed to analyze scientific evidence on the occurrence of these elements in Brazilian surface waters, considering the main metals detected, their sources, temporal distribution, quality standards, environmental risks, and monitoring gaps. A qualitative systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 recommendations, with searches in SciELO, Scopus, Web of Sci

title: Maize (zea mays l.) yield, and selected chemical properties of soils as influenced by lime and manure application in acid soils of Meket District, northeastern Ethiopia
abstract: Acid affected soils have been expanding in the Ethiopian highlands, and caused serious yield decline. Organic amendments and lime have been used to manage soil acidity. However, the rate and the right combinations have not been sufficiently documented for various crops and locations. This study aimed at investigating the effects of four manure rates (0, 4, 8, and 12 t ha-1), with three lime rates (0, 1.5 and 3 t ha-1 CaCO3) on maize yield, and selected soil chemical properties. title: Climate change, urban flooding and the politics of elite-led urban expansion in Islamabad: A political ecology study of state power, land use, and flood vulnerability
abstract: This study examines the ways elite-led urban expansion in Islamabad has disrupted natural drainage channels and heightened flood vulnerability. The study uses a qualitative political ecology case study that is based on policy and planning document review, historical maps and satellite images. Interviews and focus groups discussions were conducted with planners, engineers, officials, and residents in both urban centers and low-income neighborhoods. title: From resilience to healing: urban poor women and socio-ecological repair in Phnom Penh
abstract: Over 60% of Phnom Penh’s lakes and more than 40% of wetlands have been in-filled for the construction of real estate, causing social and environmental harm. This happens side by side to the government’s endorsement of urban resilience as a principle to drive more inclusive and sustainable urban growth. This paper positions resilience within Phnom Penh’s structural violence. Using Boung Tamok Lake and the Tompoun/Cheung Ek wetlands as case studies, it explains how in-filling constitutes slow violence that generates ecological destruction and perpetuates chronic urban trauma in urban poor women.

title: El silencio sobre los archivos desplazados: un acercamiento inicial en América Latina
abstract: Este artículo presenta un primer acercamiento al fenómeno de los archivos desplazados en América Latina. Su punto de partida es una encuesta sobre reclamaciones de archivos liderada en 2024 por María Cristina Betancur, para el Grupo de Expertos sobre el Patrimonio Archivístico Compartido, y publicada por el Consejo Internacional de Archivos en 2025. Inicialmente, se exponen algunos antecedentes internacionales sobre archivos desplazados y un acercamiento teórico al tema. Continúa con la metodología enmarcada en la investigación cualitativa, la investigación documental y la técnica de encuesta.
journal: Investigación Bibliotecológica Archivonomía Bibliotecología e Información

title: Symbolic Communication and Regional Variation in Prehistoric Rock Art: A Comparative Study of Lascaux and Bhimbetka
abstract: The paper focuses on the prehistoric rock art as a symbolic communication method, by conducting a comparative study of the Lascaux cave paintings in France and the Bhimbetka rock shelters in India. Based on the material methods, the spatial organisation, and the symbolic interpretation, the paper places both sites in an archaeological and other anthropological context that are associated with rock art studies. It discusses the relationship between environmental situation and cultural practice and their influence on visual expression in the Upper Palaeolithic period in Europe and South Asia. It

title: Asymmetrical dilemmas and oil compromises on an extractive frontier
abstract: Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork with Quichua communities along Ecuador’s Lower Napo River, this article examines local engagements with the Ishpingo–Tambococha–Tiputini (ITT) oil project. It argues that acceptance of extractive projects is best understood as a response to asymmetrical dilemmas in which impacts, benefits, and opportunities are unevenly distributed through time and space. While oil extraction may indeed constitute a local dilemma, it is a highly asymmetric one. title: Arabic Journalism in India: Historical Development and Contemporary Trends
abstract: Arabic journalism in India occupies a distinctive position in the history of Indian journalism and Indo-Arab intellectual relations. Although Arabic is not a major vernacular language of India, it has enjoyed a long and distinguished history as a language of religion, scholarship, education, literature, and international communication. The emergence of Arabic journalism in the nineteenth century transformed this scholarly tradition by providing Indian Arabic scholars with a regular medium for communicating contemporary religious, educational, literary, social, political, and cultural ideas. title: Salinity-induced solubilization and betaine protection synergistically boost anaerobic acidogenesis of waste activated sludge: Osmoprotection mechanisms and life cycle assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Anaerobic fermentation is crucial for sludge resource recovery, but its efficiency is limited by slow hydrolysis. Although salinity enhances hydrolysis and organic matter release, it severely inhibits microbial activity. This study exploits the synergistic interplay between salinity-induced solubilization and betaine-mediated salt-stress alleviation to enhance the synthesis of volatile fatty acids (VFAs). title: Gill-tissue bioaccumulation of heavy metals in oreochromis niloticus and labeo coubie and associated drinking-water health risk in the lower river Niger, Lokoja, Kogi state, Nigeria
abstract: Bioaccumulation of aquatic pollutants by fish in the lower River Niger at Lokoja can expose those who consume them to elevated risk, yet species specific bioaccumulation and consumption risk data are lacking for these fish communities. title: Effects of growth media modulation on cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities of postbiotic metabolites produced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4 produces various postbiotic metabolites with known anticancer and antioxidant activities, but its anti-inflammatory effect remains unclear. In this study, we compared postbiotic metabolites produced by L. plantarum I-UL4 with commercial de Man, Rogosa and Sharpe (MRS) medium (PMM) and a reported refined formulation (PMF) for their volatile compound profiles, cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects on LPS-stimulated THP-1 leukaemia cells. title: THE BESOEKISCH EXPERIMENTAL STATION AND HIGH-YIELD CROP PRODUCTION (1910–1942)
abstract: This study examines the role of the Besoekisch Proefstation as a colonial agricultural research centre that supported the plantation industry in the Besuki Residency in the early 20th century. The institution served to increase productivity and reduce losses caused by pests, plant diseases and soil degradation. This study employs historical methods to investigate the institution’s establishment, its organisational structure, and its impact on the development of colonial plantations. abstract: Abstract Quantifying energetic electron precipitation is essential for understanding ring current and radiation belt loss, as well as magnetosphere‐ionosphere‐atmosphere coupling. The count rate ratio between the 90° and 0° telescopes (CR 90 /CR 0 ) on POES/MetOp satellites is a commonly used proxy for precipitation and pitch‐angle diffusion rates (). title: A debate for inclusive community development: Uncovering marginalized perspectives
abstract: The paper draws on participatory development, social justice, and decolonization frameworks, emphasizing inclusive development as a tool to address historical and ongoing exclusions. Using a desktop qualitative literature review, the paper collected secondary data from publicly available sources. abstract: This paper examines canalised urban waterways as active ecomorphological agents in the Anthropocene city through a comparative study of Isparta, Türkiye, and Chelmsford, United Kingdom. Focusing on Isparta’s Çayboyu canal and associated stream system, and Chelmsford’s canalised corridor shaped by the Rivers Chelmer and Can, the paper investigates how urban waterways form and modify relationships between urban morphology, spatial memory and public space. title: Effects of Fecal Subsampling on Dietary DNA Metabarcoding in Wild Boars (Sus scrofa)
abstract: Using DNA metabarcoding, we examined dietary components of the wild boar (Sus scrofa) and tested a common but rarely examined assumption that a small fecal subsample represents the dietary signal of an entire fecal mass. We analyzed multiple subsamples taken from the same fecal mass as well as already separated fecal pieces collected on Shodoshima Island, Japan, in May, July, and September, using chloroplast trnL and mitochondrial COI markers to infer plant and animal dietary taxa, respectively. title: Doble suicidio (1969) de Masahiro Shinoda: una enunciación sobre la historia y las formas del cine en Japón
abstract: This article analyzes the film Double Suicide (1969), directed by Masahiro Shinoda, as an aesthetic and critical proposal that repositions cinema within a continuum of visuality in Japan. Based on a dialogue between historical-cultural analysis and film analysis, the study is organized into two sections: “The Edo Period: Its History and Culture as the Foundation of Symbolism in Double Suicide” and “Performing and Visual Arts in Double Suicide: Resource and Memory.” The first section examines how the historical-cultural references of the Edo period—including ukiyo-e and calligraphy—shape the fi

title: Biophilic Architecture for Psychological Recovery and Biodiversity Conservation in Nigerian Rehabilitation Environments: Advancing Sustainable Development Goal 15
abstract: Over time, biophilic architecture has become a research-backed design philosophy that intentionally brings nature into the human-made world to improve human health. In the context of mental health care in Nigeria, especially in rehabilitation centers, where psychological healing is a common focus amid fast-paced urbanization and rising mental health problems, biophilic design not only impacts healing but also contributes to environmental sustainability. This study explores the potential of biophilic architectural strategies, which can support psychological healing and biodiversity conservation

abstract: This study examines the Casbah of Algiers as a living urban landscape, emphasizing its historical, architectural, and cultural significance in the Mediterranean context. Rather than treating the Casbah solely as a preserved monument, the research conceptualizes it as a dynamic, resilient cultural system shaped by successive Amazigh, Arab-Islamic, Andalusian, Ottoman, and European influences. title: As geoestratégias formativas de Grandes Potências Regionais e o caso brasileiro recente (2003-2022)
abstract: The objective of this study is to contribute to the understanding of Brazilian geostrategy focused on extra-regional deterrence as it was shaped in the twenty-first century. To this end, the paper first defines some fundamental concepts of Geostrategy and Great Power status, following a Structural Realist approach. It then identifies key elements shared by the two successful trajectories of Regional Great Power formation in the last multipolar conjuncture of the interstate system, between 1815 and 1945. title: Institutional Transformation and Electoral Pragmatism in Indonesian Islamic Organisations
abstract: This article examines how Nahdlatul Wathan (NW), a pesantren-based Islamic organisation in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, has transformed from a religious educational institution into an electoral actor since 2004. It asks how this reflects tensions between religious authority and electoral pragmatism in post-1998 Indonesia, and what conditions enable or constrain pesantren-based organisations to maintain religious legitimacy while competing electorally. title: We Have Always Been Here: Xinka Resistance in the Face of Extractivist Projects
abstract: On October 22, 2017, a peaceful Xinka community protest against the Escobal extractivist mining project was met with brutal repression by the Guatemalan state, revealing enduring patterns of colonial governance and Indigenous dispossession. This article examines Indigenous Xinka resistance to extractivist megaprojects in the southeastern region of Guatemala as an expression of cosmological continuance, rather than merely a reaction to external violence. title: Pneumonia incidence, hospitalizations and mortality before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in Peru: An observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children and older adults. COVID-19 related disruptions in healthcare and surveillance may have altered incidence, hospitalizations, and deaths. We assessed pneumonia incidence, hospitalizations, and mortality rates in children under five and adults older than 60 years in Peru during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-22) versus the pre-pandemic period (2015-19). title: PHYSICOCHEMICAL QUALITY OF SOURCE WATER, PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SWIMMING POOLS ACROSS FIVE LOCAL GOVERNMENT AREAS OF DELTA STATE, NIGERIA.
abstract: Swimming pool water quality is critical to public health and tourism confidence, yet limited data exist comparing the physicochemical quality of the main water source, private (VIP), and public (VIP) swimming pools within the same locations in Nigeria. This study was therefore conducted across five locations in Delta State (Abraka, Warri, Ughelli, Agbor, and Asaba) to fill that gap. title: JWST MIRI Reveals a Potential Atmosphere on the Ultrahot Rocky Planet TOI-431b
abstract: Abstract An open question in exoplanet science is whether rocky exoplanets extremely close in to their host stars, “lava worlds,” can retain significant atmospheres. Thermal emission observations via secondary eclipse can be used to determine whether a rocky exoplanet possesses an atmosphere. It is expected that an atmosphere could increase the planet’s albedo and/or redistribute heat away from the dayside, reducing the secondary eclipse depth measured. title: The economic and environmental potential of sustainable food packaging: an empirical study using modified starch films with wasabi extract
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of starch-based biopolymers as innovative and sustainable food packaging materials, enabling the achievement of economic and environmental benefits. An empirical study was conducted to assess the effects of incorporating wasabi powder and paste into starch matrices, with the goal of improving antimicrobial properties and functional performance. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of these biopolymers as eco-friendly alternatives to conventional plastics, contributing to waste reduction and promoting circular economy models within the food industry. title: Extraction and Characterization of Bioactive Metabolites from an Axenically Cultured cyanobacteria Microcystis aeruginosa
abstract: Cyanobacteria are recognized as promising sources of diverse metabolites with potential applications in pharmaceutical, nutraceutical and biotechnological fields. The present study investigated the bioactive compound profile of an axenically cultured isolate Microcystis aeruginosa through solvent extraction, quantitative estimation and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis. abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor characterized by high metabolic plasticity and resistance to standard therapies. Targeting metabolic vulnerabilities has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy. 4-Methylumbelliferone (4MU), a known inhibitor of hyaluronan synthesis, has demonstrated antitumor effects beyond its canonical mechanism; however, its impact on tumor metabolism and associated pathways in GBM remains poorly understood. abstract: Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is prevalent in many developing countries like Nigeria mainly due to abuse of alcoholic beverages and excessive use of pain killer drugs. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of ethyl acetate fraction of Dialium guineense (DG) leaves on the stomach architecture of indomethacin intoxicated Wistar rats.
