title: Effects of pineapple waste-derived bromelain on digestive enzymes, nutrient utilization, and economics in Trichopodus pectoralis Regan, 1910
abstract: The use of agro-industrial by-products as functional feed additives represents a promising strategy to enhance sustainability and digestive efficiency in aquaculture. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of bromelain derived from pineapple processing waste on digestive physiology, nutrient utilization, and economic performance in snakeskin gourami, Trichopodus pectoralis Regan, 1910. abstract: The study aimed to develop an integrated ecological management action plan by analyzing the environmental behavior of residents in selected barangays of Concepcion, Tarlac. Using a quantitative survey approach, it examined attitudes, practices, and perceptions related to waste management, energy use, water conservation, and other green practices. title: Silenced Flesh, Sanctioned Hunger: The Predicament of Women in Prostitution in Jayanta Mahapatra’s Calcutta Poems
abstract: Between the lyric hush of the imagist poem and the clamour of a society that trades in hunger, Jayanta Mahapatra’s “Hunger” and “The Whorehouse in a Calcutta Street” stage some of the most disquieting encounters in Indian poetry in English. This paper investigates how the two poems render women ensnared in the sex trade, and whether their austere, image-driven art exposes the economic and patriarchal machinery of exploitation or quietly reproduces the silence it seeks to indict. title: Des musiques populaires enregistrées sur le terrain. Notes sur la prise directe et l’enregistrement de terrain dans la captation des voix populaires au début du xx e siècle
abstract: Cet article étudie les prémices de l’enregistrement de terrain dans le champ des musiques folk traditionnelles à la faveur de la mise en circulation des premiers phonographes (dès la fin du xix e siècle). Revenant sur les premières pratiques de captation permises par l’enregistrement sonore, puis suivant les collectes « équipées » de Bela Bartók en Europe, de Frances Densmore et de John et Alan Lomax aux États-Unis, l’analyse aboutit à discerner un « delta » entre documentation ethnographique des pratiques musicales folkloriques et création musicale.

title: Source node management in complex water network based on cascading failure and bidirectional risk transmission: The case of Henan Province
abstract: Water source nodes within water network are subject to dual pressures: the propagation of failure risks and reverse feedback from fluctuations in user demand. As the connectivity of water network and the relationship between water supply and consumption become increasingly complex, there is an urgent need to elucidate the patterns of bidirectional risk transmission in complex water network and to effectively manage water source nodes. title: Subestimar la investigación básica como error estratégico: una reflexión sobre política científica e innovación
abstract: La investigación básica constituye un componente fundamental de los sistemas científicos; sin embargo, los modelos de financiamiento y evaluación orientados hacia resultados de corto plazo pueden desfavorecer actividades cuyos beneficios son inciertos, acumulativos y diferidos. title: HOW WILL CHINA’S ADOPTION OF GENETICALLY MODIFIED SOYBEANS AFFECT GLOBAL SOYBEAN MARKETS?
abstract: China began commercial planting of genetically modified (GM) soybeans in 2024 after two decades of regulatory caution. Because China buys about two-thirds of the soybeans traded worldwide, exporters ask whether higher domestic yields will cut its imports and depress world prices. This paper works through three channels: yield gains on existing soybean land, land reallocation between corn and soybeans, and slower structural change in the countryside. abstract: The seemingly inescapable consequences of the climate crisis paint a grim vision of an impending apocalyptic end—one that could lead humankind to extinction through ecological catastrophe. The eschatological perspective and the ecological grief it generates are often articulated through terminology infused with religious connotations, thereby radicalizing the conflict between eco-activists and climate change deniers within competing belief systems. title: Production Risk and Productivity of Smallholder Onion Farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the production risks and productivity of smallholder onion farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria. The study specifically analyzed the production risk associated with onion production for each input, assessed the contribution of major production inputs to onion output, and estimated the returns to scale in onion production. A multistage sampling procedure was used to select 254 onion farmers from Jalingo, Ardo-Kola, and Wukari Local Government Areas of Taraba State. title: The Astronomical Language of James 1:17 Revisited
abstract: There is general agreement among scholars that παραλλαγὴ and τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα in James 1:17 refer to astronomical phenomena, but little agreement as to the nature of these phenomena. The present article returns to the writings of the Greek astronomers to gain a scientifically precise understanding of these terms, and argues that astronomical terms such as these diffused from the academy into everyday Greek and Jewish life, and were both meaningful to James’s readers and useful for James’s argument.

abstract: Abstract Shanidar Cave has long featured in debates concerning Neanderthal cognitive capacity and behaviour, including evidence for care and intentional burial. abstract: As part of a broader study, we gathered data on the natural history of carpet pythons (Morelia spilota) from the Lockerbie Scrub in Cape York. Between 2013 and 2016, we detected 37 carpet pythons during nocturnal road surveys across 28.8 km of woodland and rainforest. All specimens were in woodland, unlike rainforest-dwelling carpet pythons in the Atherton Tablelands. Our sample was dominated by small individuals. abstract: Direct UV–Vis spectrophotometric determination of Zn(II) is limited by the absence of a suitable intrinsic chromophore, necessitating complex formation to obtain an analytical absorption response. However, comprehensive optimization of the Zn(II)–diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) extraction system remains limited. This study optimized complex formation and chloroform extraction for Zn(II) determination and preliminarily examined Cr(III) interference. title: Savannah elephant family dynamics: short- and long-term responses to environmental and social changes
abstract: Multilevel societies offer flexibility in short-term association patterns for individual members while retaining valuable long-term relationships with conspecifics. Using a long-term data set on free-ranging African elephants, Loxodonta africana , in Amboseli, Kenya, we illustrate the complexity of decisions about associates in elephant multilevel societies on annual and longer-term timescales, spanning over 50 years. title: Experimentos Mentales y Racionalismo Modal: una evaluación crítica del enfoque de Chalmers
abstract: “Thought experiments” are common in many scientific disciplines and can have significant theoretical consequences. However, we know they can fail, which leads to the question of how to establish that a thought experiment legitimately achieves its result. Given the modal dimension of thought experiments, one plausible option is to address this question within the framework of a particular modal epistemology. title: The Kārṣāpaṇa and the King's Share: Currency, Taxation and Fiscal Administration in the Empire of Aśoka
abstract: Aśoka's empire rested on two fiscal instruments that the epigraphic and archaeological record allows us to see with unusual clarity: a silver punch-marked currency denominationed in kārṣāpaṇas and paṇas, and a land-based revenue system whose central levy, bali, is named by the emperor's own inscription at Lumbinī. abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ), an opportunistic bacterial pathogen, causes severe respiratory infections. Rapid detection of bacterial species is important for switching from broad-spectrum to narrow-spectrum antibiotics when antimicrobial resistance is present. Here, we designed paper-based hydrophilic-lipophilic balance/divinylbenzene/polydimethylsiloxane polymer-coated TF-SPME patches and integrated them into a bacterial culture to extract volatile emissions associated with the P. aeruginosa (ATCC 27853) strain. abstract: This study investigates the strategic role of cultural festivals in shaping destination image within the context of emerging tourism regions in Indonesia. Specifically, it examines the influence of the Radin Jambat Festival on the destination image of Way Kanan Regency, Lampung Province. Utilizing a quantitative approach, this research surveyed 95 respondents who attended the festival. Data were analyzed using Simple Linear Regression via SPSS. abstract: This article examines the transformation of marriage and wedding practices in Central Asia during the Soviet period, with particular attention to the interaction between Soviet state policy, Islamic institutions, customary law, and local traditions. Marriage represented one of the most important spheres in which Soviet modernization encountered deeply rooted social and cultural practices. abstract: Focussing on the period from 1970 to 1990, this article examines how gay men, many of whom moved from Ireland to London, adapted their activism in the face of evolving housing pressures. abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of rigid road pavements in Nepal, their lifecycle environmental impacts remain largely unquantified. abstract: Iodine is an essential micronutrient, and iodine deficiency remains an important public-health concern worldwide. title: Environmental Sanitation Management Techniques and the Politics of Filth in the Gold Coast (Colonial Ghana), c. 1878–1950
abstract: Between 1878 and 1950, the British administration in the Gold Coast repeatedly acknowledged the dangers posed by filth but struggled to provide effective sanitation. abstract: In his Roman History, Nikephoros Gregoras (c. 1295–1360) includes a curious aside about a “Scythian” woman who purchases an enslaved Byzantine man, marries him, and moves to Constantinople. abstract: Abstract Lightning activity is strongly concentrated in tropical continental “chimneys”, among which the African lightning chimney stands out as the most intense globally. title: The boundaries of global concern: How socioeconomic context shapes the link between global consciousness and environmental attitudes
abstract: Abstract Climate change requires unprecedented international cooperation; yet growing protectionist sentiment poses a significant barrier to collective action. Global Consciousness (GC), a psychological orientation characterized by a connection to humanity and the world as a whole, has been theorized as a key driver of benevolent behaviors, including pro‐environmental attitudes. However, empirical evidence linking GC to environmentalism remains largely confined to specific contexts, leaving the generalizability of this relationship across diverse societies unclear. title: Care through cultivation: Indigenous Swidden agriculture as forest care
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that the agricultural practices of Bunong swidden cultivators in northeastern Cambodia constitute relational care for forests that is fundamentally misunderstood, misrecognized, and marginalized by dominant state policies, conservation, and development paradigms. Bringing together care theory, long‐term ethnographic research, and foundational swidden scholarship, the paper reconceptualizes forest care through Indigenous ontologies and relationality, conceptualizing current conservation as a regime of anonymous care and Bunong swidden cultivation as relational care. title: Urbicidal planning: Managing risk in “dangerous” cities
abstract: The term “urbicide” has been used to describe the physical and material destruction of cities, specifically as a means to annihilate the material foundations of heterogeneity. Yet the act of physical destruction often works in tandem with parallel practices of construction that seek to create alternative urban futures. In this paper, we argue that “urbicidal planning” is a recurring logic of planning practice even in cases that do not involve the wholesale destruction of infrastructure. title: Graphs as focal interaction systems in higher-order dynamics
abstract: Abstract Graphs and hypergraphs are commonly distinguished by the order of the relations they represent, with graphs encoding pairwise relations and hypergraphs encoding interactions among arbitrary groups. We show that, for node-update dynamics, a more natural viewpoint is to regard a graph as a collection of focal neighbourhoods, each centred on a vertex and consisting of the vertex and its neighbours. title: Successful bark-beetle biocontrol. A review of the only case in history Releasing Rhizophagus grandis in Georgia, France, Britain and Türkiye against Dendroctonus micans
abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. abstract: ABSTRACT In the tropics, rapid urbanization, scarce research, and limited resources for studying bats constrain conservation efforts, positioning community science as a practical approach to address these challenges. This study presents the first integration of community science and passive acoustic monitoring for bat research in the Neotropics, implemented across urban and rural landscapes of the Peruvian Coast, Andes, and Amazon to investigate bat community structure and environmental responses. Materials and Methods: This sensory analysis study was conducted with 15 volunteer panelists. title: From the ‘City Upon a Hill’ to ‘American Carnage’: A Comparative Analysis of the Reagan and Trump Revolutions
abstract: ABSTRACT The elections of Ronald Reagan in 1980 and Donald Trump in 2016 were widely portrayed as transformative political moments. While some interpretations link them within a continuous conservative trajectory, this article argues that they represent distinct political paradigms. Using a qualitative comparative approach grounded in primary and secondary sources, the study examines ideological, policy, stylistic, and coalitional differences between the two presidencies. title: Essential oil from Piper aduncum L. leaves exhibits analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity in mice
abstract: Piper aduncum L. is a medicinal plant whose essential oil is rich in bioactive constituents, particularly dilapiol, and has attracted interest because of its diverse pharmacological properties. However, its anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and antinociceptive activities and the mechanisms potentially underlying these effects remain insufficiently characterized. Therefore, this study investigated the pharmacological effects of P. aduncum leaf essential oil (EO Pa ) and explored potential mechanisms involved in its antinociceptive activity. title: Comments on three invasive Rubus species: Rubus ellipticus Smith, Rubus rosifolius Smith and Rubus niveus Thunb., in Colombia
abstract: The occurrences of three invasive Rubus species, namely Rubus ellipticus Smith, Rubus rosifolius Smith and Rubus niveus Thunb. are analysed in three locations in Colombia. R. ellipticus and R. niveus are invasive species that form dense patches and threaten native vegetation. Due to their highly invasive nature, these two species should be given high priority in the development of an eradication programme. R. rosifolius was not seen to form thickets or to cause major environmental issues.

title: Drivers of Andean diversity: Phylogeographic structure and the evolution of hemipenial and dewlap morphology in a Neotropical lizard (Squamata: Anolidae: Anolis mariarum)
abstract: Abstract Phenotypic traits and genetic variation are fundamental for understanding biological diversity and evolutionary processes. In natural populations, phenotypic novelties are generally expected to align with genetic differentiation, establishing phenotype–genotype relationships. This pattern is evident in Neotropical lizards of the genus Anolis , where traits such as the dewlap and hemipenes play key roles in species recognition and sexual selection, and are often associated with reproductive isolation, genetic structure, and lineage divergence. abstract: Drawing from Lijiang Shen’s components of affective empathy, cognitive empathy and associative empathy, and considerations of the relationship between immersion and empathy, this article argues for a focus on embodied experience as a way of effectively developing digital empathic experiences through technologically augmented encounters using VR/XR/multisensory spaces. abstract: FUNDAMENTOS // La lesión medular (LM) representa un desafío global, pues este daño impacta profundamente en la funcionalidad y autonomía de la persona, afectando a su calidad de vida e influyendo significativamente en su imagen corporal (IC), generando procesos emocionales y alteraciones de la percepción complejos. title: Academic Burnout
abstract: Due to institutional pressures within neoliberal university environments, faculty are experiencing heightened burnout. Exploring ways to reduce burnout in accessible and creative communal ways is significant. To counter experiences of burnout, two professors and one emerging academic examined the three tenets of the self-compassion framework through arts-based inquiry. We created postcard images, mailed them to one another, and investigated our experiences using Maslach’s Burnout Inventory. title: BLOCKADE OF THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ: INFLATIONARY EFFECTS FOR OIL-IMPORTING ECONOMIES
abstract: The article examines the inflationary effects of a Hormuz blockade on oil-importing economies. It is proven that the war in the Middle East triggered the largest crisis in the history of the global oil market. Due to the fighting and the de facto blockade of the Strait of Hormuz – the main transit route for oil tankers – oil prices are rising to record levels. The immediate impact on hydrocarbon prices was significant. Oil prices surged by approximately 8%, while gas prices in Europe rose by about 20%. title: Effect of Accruals Quality on the Firm Value of Construction and Allied Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
abstract: Accruals quality is a dimension of financial reporting quality because reliable accrual information enables investors to assess reported earnings and firm performance. However, evidence on whether accruals quality translates into higher firm value remains limited among construction and allied firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The study examined the effect of accruals quality on firm value. title: Rethinking postcolonial mobilities through literature
abstract: Inspired by research that positions literary texts as capable of contributing to theoretical discussions on mobility, this article argues that literature can enable a deeper understanding of postcolonial mobilities than mainstream postcolonial literary scholarship. Although there are signs of increasing dialogue between postcolonial studies and mobilities theory, many analyses of ‘mobility’ within the field are not, strictly speaking, about mobility as such. title: Regeneration After Severe Wildfire: Hotter Microclimates Exceed Hydraulic and Thermal Tolerances in Sierra Nevada Conifer Seedlings
abstract: ABSTRACT Tree seedling regeneration after wildfire will determine the long‐term trajectory of forests under climate change, yet increasing drought and heat extremes can suppress regeneration and result in forest type conversion. We combined field observations and a controlled drought‐heat growth chamber experiment to investigate how these stressors independently and jointly affect drought‐ and heat‐tolerance physiology in seedlings of montane conifer species from drought‐ and wildfire‐prone regions in the southern Sierra Nevada. abstract: AbstractThis paper examines the conditions of possibility for semiotics to engage with the notion of participation and, through it, with participatory sciences. After tracing the genealogy of participation as a concept—from participant observation and action research to actor-network theory—the paper analyses the political requalification of this sociological notion into an institutional project for science. title: Amelioration on Mechanical Ventilated Patients in Response to Music Therapy: A Pilot Randomised Clinical Study
abstract: Introduction: Mechanical Ventilation (MV) is a crucial, lifesustaining treatment, but it frequently causes significant changes in physiological parameters and may challenge recovery. Research suggests music-based interventions to stabilise vital signs during MV. However, studies investigating specific music therapy techniques addressing physiological well-being in patients on MV are scarce. abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. abstract: Abstract Climate and energy issues continue to drive researchers to develop fossil-free energy technologies that are both sustainable and scalable. abstract: Abstract The guiding aim of the collection is to shift the focus of European studies from the institutional realities of European integration to the lived experience of it. However, it is not to separate the lived experience of Europe from the institutional and legal account of Europe but to show precisely how institutional and legal Europe is lived by individuals and social groups and, in the living, reflected and reproduced at the social level, generating various forms of injustices and indignities. abstract: This article examines the social –cultural relations between Iruekpen community and its neighbours in Esan society, Edo State, Nigeria. The study explores the social Cultural dynamics of Iruekpen community. Through a qualitative research approach, the study examines the historical, cultural, and geographical contexts of inter-village settlement, festivals, intermarriages, joint worship, and linguistic affinity between Iruekpen community’s relationships with its neighbours. The difficulty in removing all residual tumor cells during surgery contributes to the recurrence of osteosarcoma. abstract: ABSTRACT Although central Brazil hosts significant ion‐adsorption rare earth element (REE) deposits associated with A‐type granites, their coeval volcanic counterparts have been largely overlooked as exploration targets. This study demonstrates that acidic metavolcanic rocks of the Araí Group share strong radiometric, geochemical and mineralogical affinities with established REE‐enriched coeval granitic suites. title: La usura en el Islam: evolución histórica del interés en el mundo islámico
abstract: This article examines the historical evolution of usury in the Islamic world, with a particular focus on the concept of ribā, the Qur’anic term for any unjust increase in economic transactions, traditionally associated with interest. Challenging the Eurocentric perspective of economic historiography, the study shows that the rejection of usury was a shared phenomenon across civilizations, though developed with specific characteristics in Islam. title: Study on the possibility of optimizing technology for repairing aircraft skin using riveting according to strength criteria
abstract: Flight safety plays a decisive role in passenger comfort and security. It mostly depends on the reliability of the aircraft. During operation, this reliability is maintained by the effectiveness of repair technology and the quality of the repair. The implementation of new repair technologies and the optimization of existing ones is a key aspect of this process. For this reason, this study examines the possibility of optimizing a well-known technology for aircraft structural repair, namely the repair of the aircraft fuselage using riveting. title: Estimating isotopic turnover rates using DEB theory
abstract: The isotopic turnover rate (λ) quantifies the rate at which an organism’s tissues are renewed. It is a key parameter in dietary studies as it governs predator-prey dynamics and by extension the broader food web. However, λ has historically been difficult to estimate, typically requiring a combination of experiments, empirical data and modelling approaches. abstract: In this article, I propose a new category of autobiographical writing I call the ‘lyric sketchbook’. abstract: Over the past four decades, neoliberal reforms have reshaped education systems globally. Among these, school consolidation remains a popular policy instrument promising efficiency, consistency, and scale. In some urban contexts, however, consolidation has produced uneven impacts along racial and socioeconomic lines. title: Une synthèse des pelouses dunaires maritimes de l’Europe occidentale
abstract: Cet article concerne une tentative de synthèse sur les végétations de pelouses maritimes arrière-dunaires plus ou moins fixées de l’Europe occidentale, de la Norvège au Portugal. Outre une description synthétique des alliances et des associations, ces dernières sont placées dans deux schémas systémiques combinant l’ensemble des vingt géosigmetums des dunes sèches de la zone d’étude concernée.

title: Corrosion Control in Oil Pipeline Infrastructure Using Gmelina Arborea and Wire Croton Extracts
abstract: This research explores the sustainable application of Gmelina arborea and Wire Croton plant extracts as green corrosion inhibitors for oil pipeline infrastructure. Steel samples were exposed to different corrosive environment (acidic, alkaline, saline, and neutral) to simulate the diverse conditions faced by pipelines. Three different concentration ratios of the extract (50:50, 60:40, and 40:60) were applied into the corrosive environment to determine their efficacy in inhibiting pipeline corrosion. title: TENDINOPATÍAS: ACTUALIZACIÓN SOBRE MÉTODOS DE TRATAMIENTO Y PROTOCOLOS TERAPÉUTICOS ACTUALES
abstract: Las tendinopatías son trastornos musculoesqueléticos frecuentes que pueden ocasionar dolor, limitación funcional y disminución de la capacidad para realizar actividades cotidianas, laborales y deportivas. El objetivo fue analizar y actualizar la evidencia científica sobre los principales métodos terapéuticos utilizados actualmente en su tratamiento. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de actualización de la literatura científica, mediante la consulta de bases de datos biomédicas y especializadas, priorizando revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis, ensayos clínicos, guías de práctica clínica y doc

abstract: La sociedad en la actualidad se enfrenta a un cumulo de elementos centrados en que algunos permean los procesos educativos como lo es los avances tecnológicos y ante dicha realidad se hace necesario reconocer que dentro del hecho educativo se logran develar aspectos centrados en la convivencia escolar y es por ello que surge el siguiente propósito: reflexionar sobre los desafíos de la convivencia escolar en adolescentes con perspectiva y aportes desde el paradigma de la educación emocional, lo cual trajo como producto un ensayo científico abordado a través de la técnica de revisión bibliográfi

title: Computational Study of Gas-Phase Reactions to Produce Sulfite Esters: A New Class of Sulfur Containing Molecules in the Atmosphere?
abstract: Abstract We use computational quantum chemistry to study gas-phase reactions of aldehydes with water and sulfur dioxide. We find that a new reaction leading to the formation of previously nearly unstudied sulfite esters is possible with a comparatively low barrier. The reaction can be catalyzed by the presence of additional hydrogen bonding molecules, including water, nitric acid, and sulfuric acid. title: Validity of the comprehensive assessment of psychopathic personality–self‐report Korean version ( CAPP ‐ SR ) in a sample of Korean prison inmates
abstract: Given the theoretical and clinical importance of psychopathy, numerous assessment instruments have been developed, including the Comprehensive Assessment of Psychopathic Personality (CAPP). Although the CAPP has received increasing empirical support across cultures, research examining the validity of the Korean self-report version remains limited. The current study examined the validity of the Comprehensive Assessment of Psychopathic Personality-Self Report Korean Version (CAPP-SR) in Korea. title: The Contributions of Historian Mohamed-Seghir Ghanem to the Establishment of the Foundations of the Algerian Historical School
abstract: Following independence, historical studies in Algeria witnessed the emergence of a distinguished group of researchers and historians specialising in ancient, medieval, modern, and contemporary history. Among the most prominent scholars of the ancient history of the Maghreb was Dr Mohamed-Seghir Ghanem, who, despite his passing, left a rich scholarly legacy that helped reinterpret the region’s ancient history beyond the French colonial perspective that had long dominated most of its subjects. title: Inclusión financiera en Ecuador: Expansión del Acceso, Morosidad Sistémica y Presión sobre las Provisiones en la Banca Privada, Pública y el Sector Cooperativo
abstract: Existe una paradoja en la evolución reciente del sistema financiero ecuatoriano: el mismo proceso que permitió incorporar a millones de personas a productos y servicios financieros también contribuyó, en parte, al deterioro de la calidad de la cartera y a nuevas formas de exclusión. Personas que inicialmente accedieron al crédito hoy enfrentan restricciones para reingresar al sistema debido a historiales negativos, cartera castigada o bajas calificaciones crediticias, una realidad que preocupa a supervisores, entidades financieras y analistas. title: Vegetation cover dynamics across presidential terms in Brazil
abstract: Abstract National-level politics play important roles in shaping environmental policies. We provide a synthetic and integrative analysis of vegetation cover changes across presidential terms between 1990 and 2025 in Brazil, focusing on the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, and Cerrado. Our results show marked temporal differences in rates of habitat loss across biomes. title: Subnational spatial co-distribution of tuberculosis and diabetes mellitus across Ghana’s 16 regions following administrative reorganisation: An ecological analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: National administrative boundary reorganisations, increasingly common across sub-Saharan Africa, create discontinuities in surveillance data alignment that complicate subnational burden estimation for infectious and non-communicable diseases alike. Ghana's expansion from 10 to 16 administrative regions in 2019 provides a tractable case for demonstrating how publicly available surveillance and survey data can be used to characterise subnational co-distribution of tuberculosis and diabetes mellitus (DM) under a revised boundary structure. title: Importancia del control prenatal en la reducción de complicaciones obstétricas
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre el papel del control prenatal en la reducción de las complicaciones obstétricas. Método: revisión narrativa de literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: revisiones sistemáticas, ensayos clínicos, estudios de cohorte y transversales latinoamericanos. title: Soft Shell, Hard Core: Peach Culture and The Paradox of Immigrant Integration in Italy
abstract: To the international observer, Italy is the archetype of a Peach Culture, as a society characterized by a soft, approachable exterior where interpersonal warmth and informality facilitate initial social contact. This reputation for La Dolce Vita and warmth is often cited as a primary pull factor for newcomers. However, this commentary argues that this very cultural flexibility functions as a structural trap for economic migrants. title: Spontaneous mutation rate estimation in the large-genome unicellular eukaryote Euglena gracilis
abstract: The spontaneous mutation rate per nucleotide (µ) is a fundamental parameter shaping genome evolution, yet it remains unknown for many eukaryotic groups. Here, we estimated µ in the freshwater unicellular eukaryote Euglena gracilis, which possesses a 2.4 Gb genome, among the largest reported for unicellular species. We conducted a mutation accumulation experiment using 10 independent MA lines propagated through repeated single-cell bottlenecks and then identified 153 de novo nucleotide mutations. title: Low geochemical reactivity of cobalt and nickel in Swedish fine-textured soils
abstract: Fine-textured postglacial soils in Sweden commonly exhibit elevated total concentrations of cobalt (Co) and nickel (Ni), occasionally exceeding guideline values for sensitive land use. However, the environmental relevance of these exceedances remains uncertain. In this study, 26 soil samples from 23 sites were analysed to assess the mineralogical origin, geochemical reactivity, and solubility of Co and Ni. title: Vaginal formulations selectively target Lactobacillus iners and Candida spp. while preserving Lactobacillus crispatus
abstract: Vaginal eubiosis is associated with low bacterial diversity and Lactobacillus crispatus dominance, whereas Lactobacillus iners often persists after antibiotics. We evaluated complementary approaches to inhibit L. iners and Candida spp. while preserving L. crispatus. Carbohydrate screening of five strains per Lactobacillus species showed insufficient selectivity. Oleic acid showed the widest susceptibility differential: minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations were 0.4/0.8 mM for L. iners versus 1.6 to > 6.4 mM for L. crispatus. title: Navigating Bureaucratic Hurdles: Fostering an FTZ-minded Investment Climate in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand
abstract: Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand are reported to foster regional and international cooperation, as well as compete in attracting domestic and international investments, particularly within the context of FTZs. Bureaucratic hurdles remain the biggest issues responsible for stifling investment growth, which contrasts with the nature of FTZs and the designation as areas for rapid economic growth. title: Life cycle carbon emission accounting and emission reduction potential assessment of container and domestic glass industry in China
abstract: The container and domestic glass (CDG) industry is one of the most energy-intensive sectors in China. To analyse the life cycle carbon emissions and the potential for carbon reduction of the CDG industry in China, we developed a carbon-emission accounting model based on life cycle assessment (LCA) and conducted an empirical analysis using 2023 as the baseline year. title: War of Terrorism in West Africa and the Sahel: A Legal Analysis of Correlation Between Armed Conflicts and Global Terrorism
abstract: Terrorism in West Africa and the Sahel has evolved from isolated criminal acts into organised and sustained violence that increasingly resembles armed conflict. Groups such as Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM) and the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS) have established command structures, exercised territorial influence, conducted prolonged military operations and engaged state armed forces on a continuing basis. abstract: The biorenewable feedstock cardanol, a phenol compound substituted with an unsaturated C15 hydrocarbon chain, was selectively transformed into a cyclohexanone derivative through partial hydrogenation. Subsequent conversion via Baeyer-Villiger oxidation (BVO) gave a lactone product (pentadecylcaprolactone, PDCL), which is a mixture of two regioisomers. abstract: Emergency department visits are common among patients with advanced cancer and may increase during the final stages of disease. Although many visits are related to acute complications requiring urgent assessment, others may potentially be managed through anticipatory symptom control, outpatient care, or timely access to palliative care services. This systematic review aimed to determine the frequency of potentially avoidable emergency department visits among adults with advanced cancer receiving palliative care and to describe their clinical characteristics and associated factors. title: Bioengineered graphene–iron oxide nanocomposite and derived quantum dots as pro-angiogenic agents: potential therapeutic applications
abstract: The present study focuses on the conversion of a green-synthesized graphene–iron oxide nanocomposite into fluorescent quantum dots with enhanced optical properties. This was achieved by using Spirulina platensis crude extract to synthesize graphene-based quantum dots to enhance their biomedical performance. The synthesized quantum dots were biofunctionalized with naturally derived extracellular matrix proteins, namely collagen and fibrin. title: Development Strategy of E-Government in Village Governance in Banda Sub-District
abstract: Background: E-government is intended to improve transparency, accountability, efficiency, and public participation using information technology. However, its implementation in village governance in Banda Sub-district, Central Maluku Regency, remains uneven because of limitations in institutional readiness, human resources, infrastructure, and policy support. Objective: This study aims to examine the importance of e-government in Banda Sub-district and identify its benefits, barriers, implementation conditions, and development strategies in village governance. title: Estructura y dinámica poblacional de Prochilodus magdalenae (Characiformes: Prochilodontidae) durante migraciones, sector río Sogamoso (2014–2023)
abstract: Introduction: Prochilodus magdalenae (bocachico) is a key migratory species in the Magdalena River basin, with high ecological and fisheries relevance. However, its populations have declined due to overfishing and habitat degradation. This study analyzes the population dynamics of the bocachico in the Tienda Nueva - La Flor sector of the Sogamoso river during the period 2014-2023, evaluating its abundance, biomass and relationship with environmental variables. title: Obesity's Impact on Prognosis in Ph‐Like Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
abstract: Obesity is associated with chemotherapy resistance and poorer survival in pediatric high-risk B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). title: Integrating Meteorological Forecasts and Scenario Simulation to Support Smallholder Maize Farming Decisions in Kakamega County, Kenya
abstract: Seasonal rainfall outlooks can support advance planning in rainfed maize systems, but farm operations depend not only on seasonal rainfall totals but also on rainfall timing, continuity and short dry periods. This study examined Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) March-May seasonal outlooks for Kakamega County from 2021 to 2025 and used a transparent stochastic scenario model to explore rainfall indicators relevant to farm decision-making. title: El bloque en la frontera. El Edificio Vicente Suárez de Xosé Bar Bóo.
abstract: Entre 1972 y 1975 Xosé Bar Bóo proyectó y construyó un edificio de viviendas en una localización privilegiada del Ensanche de García Olloqui en Vigo. La naturaleza híbrida de esta pieza, su materialidad y la caracterización de sus espacios, responden a su condición fronteriza entre el Movimiento Moderno y su revisión crítica. title: Exact analytical solutions for the piston effect in supercritical fluids under post-acoustic approximation — Short-time asymptotics, thermal penetration depth and comparison with the Spacelab D-2 experiments
abstract: Near the liquid–vapor critical point, fluids become highly compressible, giving rise to a special, strongly coupled thermo-mechanical process: the piston effect. In this phenomenon, a thin thermal boundary layer develops near a heated wall; owing to strong thermal expansion, this layer acts like a piston, compressing the bulk fluid adiabatically and resulting in a seemingly accelerated thermal response. abstract: The main problem discussed in the paper is the existence of a causal relationship between certain criminal phenomena in the Republic of Serbia and the European Union, on the one hand, and the migrant crisis, on the other. A special problem is represented by certain criminal acts that can be classified as a direct consequence of migrant population movements. The time frame is the period of the past ten years, during which the migrant issue has been considered one of the most topical issues in the European Union. title: The fragmented green state: state capacity, green macrofinancial regimes, and political contestation in Thailand’s energy transition
abstract: This paper contributes to debates on green states and green macrofinancial regimes in the Global South. It analyses Thailand, an upper-middle-income country that, although subject to international financial subordination, has sufficient domestic finance to support renewable energy rollout. However, despite consensus on the need for green transition, renewable energy remains low in Thailand’s energy mix. We explain this using the concept of the fragmented green state. abstract: Desde tiempos antiguos se han consumido diversos alimentos fermentados entre ellos las bebidas fermentadas tradicionales preparadas a partir de cereales básicos que a nivel mundial constituye una de las principales fuentes de energía y nutrientes aportando carbohidratos, proteínas, fibra dietética, vitaminas, minerales y fitoquímicos tales como compuestos fenólicos y flavonoides. title: Microgastrinae parasitoid wasps (Hymenoptera: Braconidae) from Sakartvelo (Georgia), with new records and an updated checklist of species for the country
abstract: This study provides a revised checklist of Microgastrinae parasitoid wasps in Georgia. Accounting for the new information presented below, 69 species within 16 genera are here recognized for the country. We identified 26 species within 13 genera of Microgastrinae from Lagodekhi and some other localities from Georgia. Among the material we studied, two genera (Deuterixys and Rasivalva) and 22 species are recorded from Georgia and 10 species from Caucasus for the first time.

abstract: In a democratic society, the composition of the highest judicial authorities is a matter of great attention and scrutiny, especially when the focus is on constitutional courts, bodies of singular legal and political significance. abstract: BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a hypertensive complication of pregnancy characterized by dysfunction of the hemostatic system. title: ‘Think What They Have Meant to Me’: The War Poems of Roland Leighton
abstract: Scholarly discussion of Roland Leighton has previously been limited to his relationship to Vera Brittain and his role in her life as depicted in her memoir Testament of Youth. This article examines three of Leighton’s poems in the context of First World War poetry and thereby allows them to emerge from the shadow of Vera Brittain’s life and work. The study of Leighton’s poems widens our understanding of the early poetry of the war, which is often falsely depicted as dichotomous with the poetry of Brooke and Grenfell on one side and Charles Sorley on the other. abstract: Abstract Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for patients with severe respiratory failure, but current technology remains limited by hemocompatibility challenges. We previously developed microfluidic oxygenator prototypes utilizing rigid, flat-plate silicon membranes with etched micropores to improve blood flow dynamics and hemocompatibility. abstract: This study examined the ethno mathematics awareness and reported classroom practices of secondary mathematics teachers in the Division of San Fernando, Pampanga, and explored the challenges and enabling factors associated with ethno mathematics integration. title: Diel emergence and dispersal rhythms in the bamboo borer Dinoderus minutus (Coleoptera: Bostrichidae)
abstract: Biological rhythms regulate insect activity and represent a conserved adaptive trait across life forms. Understanding the behavioral rhythms of dispersive cryptic species is important for elucidating their ecological interactions and improving pest management strategies. In this study, we investigated the diel patterns of emergence and flight activity of the bamboo borer Dinoderus minutus under field and laboratory conditions using a chronobiological approach. abstract: A Caatinga apresenta expressiva diversidade vegetal e constitui uma fonte relevante de compostos bioativos com potencial farmacológico, incluindo substâncias capazes de atuar sobre alvos relacionados à neurobiologia da ansiedade. abstract: La edad corporal, estimada mediante bioimpedancia eléctrica, refleja el desgaste fisiológico acumulado del organismo y puede diferir considerablemente de la edad cronológica en función de los hábitos de vida, condición poco documentada en adultos mayores de entornos rurales andinos. title: Antibiotic production reduces the cost of resource exploitation in Streptomyces coelicolor
abstract: Soil is a competitive environment containing a variety of resources used for bacterial growth. Complex polysaccharides, like chitin or starch, require the secretion of enzymes that degrade these resources into smaller units before they can be consumed. However, exoenzymes and the products they create are public goods, meaning they can be used by competitors who consume and benefit from these public goods even if they do not produce enzymes themselves. abstract: Abstract Vegetation optical depth (VOD) is widely used to monitor vegetation water dynamics, yet its interpretation in dense tropical forests remains uncertain because independent observations of water partitioning among vegetation compartments are scarce. Here, we compare Global Navigation Satellite System transmissometry-derived VOD (GNSS-T VOD) with independent measurements of leaf, stem, and soil water in an old-growth Central Amazon rainforest. abstract: This study investigates how design-driven strategies enhance sustainability in food packaging within a circular economy framework. It identifies how design choices mediate environmental performance, usability and consumer behaviour, moving beyond material substitution as the sole sustainability strategy. abstract: Abstract River regulation alters environmental conditions and hydrological connectivity, yet these influences are embedded within natural longitudinal and seasonal variation. We examined fish and phytoplankton community structure across 15 sites along the Lower Niger River, regulated by two dams, during dry and rainy seasons. title: Cancer incidence in the Ecuadorian Amazon: A retrospective study (1990–2019)
abstract: BACKGROUND: There is a scarcity of cancer studies in the Amazon region. This study aimed to analyse trends in cancer incidence within the Ecuadorian Amazon between 1990 and 2019, identifying the most prevalent cancer types and assessing their provincial and temporal distribution. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from the Quito population-based cancer registry, focusing on patients whose habitual residence was in the Amazonian provinces of Sucumbíos, Orellana, Napo, and Pastaza. abstract: La encomienda de Añón fue una pequeña unidad administrativa de base de la Orden Militar del Hospital en el reino de Aragón. Nació en el siglo xii. El comendador hospitalario era el señor de las villas de Añón y Talamantes. El principal rival de la encomienda de Añón fue siempre el monasterio cisterciense de Veruela, ya que estaba situado muy cerca de la encomienda. title: 2026 Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report: Executive Summary and Key Changes
abstract: The Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report provides a comprehensive, annually updated evidence-based approach to asthma diagnosis, assessment, treatment, and prevention across the lifespan. Its central approach is personalized, iterative care based on the Assess-Adjust-Review cycle for both symptom control and reduction of future risk (including severe exacerbations, persistent airflow limitation, and treatment-related harm). abstract: Abstract There is increasing interest in adaptable building design as spatial needs, market conditions, and performance expectations evolve over time. Uncertainty in future demand requires designers to assess not only the financial implications of expansion strategies, but also their associated carbon impacts from an early stage. title: Reverse Logistics and Environmental Sustainability of Fast-Moving Consumer Goods Companies in Nigeria
abstract: Environmental sustainability is a major concern for Fast-Moving Consumer Goods Companies (FMCG) companies because their production and distribution processes significantly impact the environment. Various initiatives have been implemented to promote sustainability by minimizing waste and pollution. abstract: Forest degradation remains a critical driver of global biodiversity loss, necessitating robust frameworks for Sustainable Forest Management (SFM). abstract: Eschatological traditions in Islam, Christianity, and Judaism share recurring motifs of cosmic disruption, an adversary figure, an agent of final justice, resurrection, and divine judgment, yet these parallels are often asserted rather than tested against specified sources. This study compares how the signs and figures of the end times are presented in selected textual strands of the three traditions. title: Pilot scale, supercritical CO2 extraction of lipids and bioactive compounds from tiger nuts co-products: Green chemistry metrics and life-cycle assessment
abstract: Supercritical CO 2 (scCO 2 ) extraction of food wastes has emerged in the recent decades as a sustainable approach towards valorization and reduction of environmental footprint. We present for the first time an upcycling of tiger nuts co-products enabled by scCO 2 at a pilot level that paves the way for an industrial scale-up. The method demonstrated a great potential, with a noted 77% yield towards a good quality oil rich in oleic acid (71%), linoleic acid (10%), bioactive molecules (tocopherols, 0.114 g/100 g), or minerals (Fe, Mg, P). abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines a neglected aspect of industrial relations: workplace disputes in which workers are incidentally made idle because of strike actions of others. These spillover effects have received little systematic attention despite potentially accounting for a substantial share of the employment consequences of industrial conflict. abstract: Las enfermedades infecciosas conforman una carga persistente en Ecuador, sostenida por determinantes sociales, ambientales y conductuales que trascienden el origen biológico de cada patología. abstract: El artículo analiza el modo en que las cartas de Pedro de Valdivia convierten la adversidad, la fragilidad de la gobernación y la lealtad imperial en capital de autoridad. abstract: Poor air quality arising from landscape fire smoke (LFS) events presents a substantial health burden to at-risk individuals and communities. However, there are few dedicated health management resources available for priority populations, despite increasing climate-related landscape fire risks. We conducted a literature review to analyse health management plans and strategies available for at-risk individuals in Australia, Canada and the United States. abstract: Radiation dose to the heart is associated with various cardiac side effects. However, the specific cardiac and pulmonary structures that contribute to these toxicities remain incompletely understood. Moreover, although multiple factors contribute to reduced survival after radiotherapy, the role of radiation-induced cardiac toxicity remains underrecognized. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the associations between radiation dose to specific cardiac and pulmonary structures, cardiac side effects, and survival. title: The Function of Volcanic Stone Tools from Bed II at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania: A Case Study From the FC East and FC West Sites
abstract: Abstract This study presents the first micro-wear analysis of stone tools made from volcanic rocks from the Olduvai Bed II FC East (FCE) and FC West (FCW) sites at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania, dated to approximately 1.6–1.5 Ma. These sites form part of a key stratigraphic interval documenting major technological and biological transitions during the early Pleistocene. The analysed sample comprises 46 well-preserved artefacts selected from a larger assemblage of volcanic rocks. title: Christ’s Body, Affective Devotion and Female Spirituality in the Old English Descent into Hell
abstract: This article reads the Old English poem traditionally known as The Descent into Hell as an example of sophisticated, creative and speculative theology in the vernacular. In order to do so, it highlights the three most striking theological aspects of the poem’s content and structure: the depiction of Christ’s bodily descent into Sheol; the inclusion of devotions typically associated with later-medieval affective piety; and the distinctively female spirituality suggested by the poet’s adaptation of the Gospel. title: Analysis of KNVB Sports Diplomacy through Oranje Festival in Indonesia
abstract: This study analyzes the implementation of sports diplomacy conducted by the Koninklijke Nederlandse Voetbalbond (KNVB) through the Oranje Festival program in Indonesia. The research examines how football is utilized as an instrument of soft power and public diplomacy to strengthen relations between the Netherlands and Indonesia. Using a qualitative descriptive method and a case study approach, this research explores the role of football festivals in shaping public perception, cultural engagement, and transnational cooperation between football institutions and communities. title: Serving by choice: Motivations and determinants of voluntary military reservism in Spain
abstract: Military reserves are an essential component of any country's defence system. This study analyzes the Spanish model of voluntary reservists, involving over 3,000 citizens who temporarily join the Armed Forces to train and serve in areas related to their expertise. Using a territory-level dataset covering 2020-2024, the article integrates perspectives from rational choice theory, new institutionalism, public service motivation, and gender studies into a multi-layered explanatory framework. abstract: Soybean production in the Chugoku region is often limited by environmental stresses, including excessive soil moisture at sowing and typhoon-induced lodging. To improve productivity under these conditions, new cultivars have been developed. ‘Soratakaku’, a recently developed cultivar derived from Japanese and U.S. cultivar, is expected to exhibit high yield potential in southwestern Japan. abstract: Excoriation disorder (ED), recently recognized as a distinct diagnosis in the DSM-5, is characterized by recurrent compulsive skin picking behaviors that lead to skin lesions and significant emotional, functional, and social impairment. This comprehensive review addresses its pathophysiology, clinical assessment, comorbidities, and treatment, highlighting the importance of a multidisciplinary approach. abstract: Los materiales abiertos y no estructurados (loose parts) se utilizan en Educación Inicial porque pueden manipularse, combinarse y asumir funciones distintas durante el juego. abstract: Abstract Blood donation is a major cause of iron deficiency (ID). Eventually, hemoglobin concentration lower than reference limits leads to temporary deferral from blood donation eligibility. Multiple factors are associated with ID among blood donors. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of iron deficiency among southern Thai blood donors, evaluate their hematological profiles, and identify factors associated with ID. abstract: Water scarcity and increasing climatic variability have increased the need for reliable plant-based indicators for irrigation scheduling in semi-arid environments. This study was conducted during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons at the Batı Akdeniz Agricultural Research Institute (BATEM), Antalya, Türkiye, to evaluate the Crop Water Stress Index (CWSI) response of silage maize grown under subsurface drip irrigation (SDI) and to estimate CWSI values potentially useful for irrigation scheduling. abstract: Introducción: la cardiopatía isquémica representa el subgrupo más frecuente dentro de las enfermedades cardiovasculares y la mayor proporción de muertes atribuibles a este grupo. abstract: This article explores the potential of using parallel language corpora in the translation of Ukrainian culture-specific vocabulary into English. The relevance of this research stems from the active development of corpus linguistics, the expansion of Ukrainian-English parallel corpora, and the need to refine methods for analyzing the translation of linguistic units that represent national and cultural particularities. abstract: Religious practices through offerings (sesajen) in Indonesia and India reflect spiritual values, communal solidarity, and reverence for the sacred, yet simultaneously create ecological challenges when residues, such as flowers, leaves, incense, plastic containers, and holy water, are discarded without proper treatment. abstract: This research begins with the question of how the Sedekah Gunung Ngasa Gandoang ritual functions as a collective mechanism in maintaining ecological balance while strengthening the cultural identity of the community amidst the currents of modernization and ecological crisis. title: Universalism and parasitic injustice
abstract: Abstract A common criticism of supposedly Enlightenment ideals is that, in the light of racial, gendered, and colonial injustice, they have never actually been universal. This article proposes a novel set of methodologies for testing the universalizability of normative ideals by attending to patterns of parasitic injustice , or the ways in which normative ideals such as freedom and equality are premised upon access to the labor, bodies, or resources of others in ways that make them nonuniversalizable. abstract: El artículo examina la transformación demográfica de las Islas Malvinas tras la ocupación británica de 1833 y analiza cómo el Reino Unido implementó estrategias de colonización destinadas a consolidar y legitimar su dominio. title: Field Evaluation of Pavement Skid Resistance: A Case Study of Five Selected Roads in Ado-Ekiti Metropolis, Nigeria
abstract: Skid resistance is the force that is created when a tyre is prevented from rotating along the pavement and is one of the most critical safety features of road pavements. Poor skid resistance is associated with increased traffic accidents, especially when the pavement is wet. This paper presents a field evaluation of pavement skid resistance for five major roads in Ado-Ekiti metropolis, Ekiti State, Nigeria. abstract: The accumulation of single-use polyethylene waste presents a major challenge to the recovery of value from end of life plastic. abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) mediate plant–plant signalling and may contribute to phenotypic differentiation among populations. abstract: Abstract The article aims to explore the origins of far-right music in Italy and its contribution to the formation of a new and corresponding youth movement, which constitutes a phenomenon at least partly independent of the historical and political legacy of the Fascist regime. This study is conducted by analysing three key elements that contributed to the creation of a different background, more suited to the context of the 1960s and 1970s. title: Factors associated with protective behaviors against pesticide exposure: a study of rice farmers in Northern Iran
abstract: Rice farming in Mazandaran Province, Iran, relies heavily on chemical pesticides, posing significant health and environmental risks. Despite efforts to promote pro-environmental practices, farmers’ adoption of protective and sustainable behaviors remains limited. This study investigates factors associated with rice farmers’ preventive awareness and protective behaviors, focusing on the sequential progression from awareness to preparation and eventual recognition of the need for alternative pest management strategies within an enabling environment framework. abstract: This article focuses on translations and rewritings of classical Chinese poetry in a group of early twentieth-century modernist little magazines. abstract: Our duoethnographic inquiry, grounded in Intersectionality, addresses the following questions: How do intersectionality and internationalization complicate Black diasporic dynamics within the United States? What communal responsibilities do Black international/immigrant people hold toward Black American people within the U.S. academy? abstract: La construcción teórica del pensamiento numérico es objeto de controversia entre la didáctica de las matemáticas y las neurociencias cognitivas. abstract: The load capacity factor (LCF) is a preferred sustainability indicator due to its ability to measure the ecological footprint and the biocapacity to support both. abstract: PURPOSE: Although the Mediterranean diet has been widely studied in relation to depression, less is known about the associations between other diets, such as the Nordic Diet, and depressive symptoms and clinical depression. abstract: Postcolonial studies emerged as a critical-emancipatory tradition of criticism that analyzes historical forms of imperialism and colonial forms of knowledge and practice (such as racist exclusions) as constitutive of Western modernity. abstract: Applying Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) methods to the online output of climate change contesters, this article examines how their discursive strategies are accommodated within counter-disinformation frameworks. abstract: Las extradiciones de personas desde México hacia Estados Unidos se han intensificado en las últimas décadas como parte de la cooperación bilateral en materia de seguridad y persecución penal. abstract: Dry Afromontane forests are important carbon sinks, yet the influence of topographic gradients on their carbon stocks remains insufficiently understood. This study assessed aboveground carbon (AGC), belowground carbon (BGC), litter carbon (LC), soil organic carbon (SOC), and total carbon (TC) stocks along altitude, slope, and aspect gradients in Bela Mountain Forest, northern Ethiopia. abstract: Abstract Agricultural systems face the critical challenge of providing sufficient, healthy nutrition for a growing population while operating within planetary boundaries and conserving biodiversity. This study uses the biophysical model SOLm to evaluate the nutritional adequacy and biodiversity impacts of transforming the Swiss food system. abstract: The procurement of residential care facilities presents opportunities for design innovation, yet is challenged by various contextual factors, including country-specific policies, regulations, research, care models, organisational practices, and socioeconomic influences. abstract: This paper provides an insight to the world of transnational organised crime and drug trafficking. It examines transnational organised crime groups, their activities and the efforts made to stop them worldwide. abstract: This paper examines the challenges of Hungarian kin-state funding in Southern Slovakia through the lens of local governments, ethnic minority status, and prevailing allocation practices. abstract: Acne vulgaris is a widespread chronic inflammatory skin condition particularly affecting the pilosebaceous unit, with its pathogenesis intricately linked to excessive sebum production, abnormal follicular keratinization, overcolonization by Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes), and dysregulated host immune responses. Beyond its dermatological manifestations, the disorder is frequently associated with psychological comorbidities such as anxiety and depression, significantly impacting patients' quality of life. title: Enhancing chili (Capsicum annuum L.) growth through the combined effects of earthworms and indigo (Indigofera tinctoria L.) green manuring
abstract: A pot experiment was conducted from February to October 2023 in a net house at the Soil Science Field Laboratory, Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University (HSTU), Dinajpur, Bangladesh, to evaluate the response of earthworms to the application of indigo green manuring (IGM) and the growth and yield response of chili under the combined applications of IGM, earthworms, and cow dung.The experiment was designed using a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with nine treatments and four replications.The results showed that IGM significantly enhanced earthworm activity, which, in turn, le

title: Identifying intercalation electrodes for electrochemical ion recovery and desalination
abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). Among myriad ion capture techniques, we focus on electrochemical methods using intercalation electrodes, an energy-efficient approach capable of both selectively extracting specific ions or non-selectively ex

title: Irradiated Atmospheres VII. Effect of Mixing Energy Flux on Atmosphere-Interior Coupling
abstract: Highly irradiated, underdense rocky planets such as puffy Venuses may host strong coupling between their atmospheres and magma-ocean interiors. Previous studies have mainly treated this coupling through radiative transfer and chemical equilibrium, leaving the role of vertical mixing unclear. Here we quantify how energy transport associated with vertical mixing modifies the thermal structure, volatile chemistry, and emission spectra of puffy Venuses. title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

title: Building Macroeconomically Relevant Climate Indices via the Assemblage VAR
abstract: What should a macroeconomically relevant climate index contain? The composition is inherently ambiguous, and aggregation choices affect structural inference. We introduce the Assemblage VAR, which jointly estimates nonnegative aggregation weights and VAR parameters by maximizing the system likelihood-gain criterion, effectively outsourcing aggregation to observed macroeconomic dynamics. Two variants operate in component-space and rank-space, reweighting named subcomponents or emphasizing regions of the cross-sectional distribution. title: Changing Geographies of Violence in North and West Africa
abstract: This paper analyses spatial trends in armed conflicts in North and West Africa. It shows that all types of violence saw a significant increase in 2025. However, these violent incidents are distributed very unevenly across the region: while conflict is at its lowest in North Africa, the vast majority of violent incidents and victims are concentrated in five West African countries: Nigeria, Cameroon, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. Coastal countries are experiencing a very mixed picture: jihadism is not advancing as a front, from the Sahel toward the Gulf of Guinea, and most of the violence stems

title: Effects of Periodic Migration on Selection in Subdivided Populations
abstract: Migration and selection jointly shape evolutionary outcomes in spatially structured populations. Migration can vary over time as ecological shifts, such as changes in sea level, alter habitat connectivity. Here, we study the impact of periodic migration on selection within a geographically subdivided population. Using a two-deme Moran model with spatially heterogeneous selection, we analyze a scenario in which a mutant genotype is advantageous in one habitat and disadvantageous in the other. Keeping the time-averaged migration rate fixed, we vary the period, relative phase, and directional asy

title: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
abstract: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. The predicted momentum spectra at approximately 0 and 75 degrees are compared with experimental measurements of the atmospheric muon flux

title: Stochastic Snowball States in Planetary Climate
abstract: Motivated by the recent finding of Ji and Abbot (2025) that at moderate eccentricity (0.2--0.3) the planetary Snowball bistability vanishes, we have introduced stochasticity of the orbital eccentricity into a simplified version of the energy balance model of Eisenman and Wettlaufer (2009) to study a general Earth-like planet. The stochastic eccentricity is approximated by two dominant time scales, annual and daily, and is introduced through an analysis of the Kepler equation. title: Coronal Mass Ejections from the Young Sun: Deceleration-Powered Solar Energetic Particles as a Self-Extinguishing Forcing of the Early Earth
abstract: At $\sim$3.9~Ga (stellar age $\sim$0.6~Gyr), the young Sun was far more magnetically active than today. It launched $\sim$$10^2$ large, fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs) per year into a denser, more magnetized wind. We follow these eruptions to Earth's atmosphere with a semi-analytic model chain. We find that a CME launched at $v_0\sim3\text{--}4\e{3}\unit{km\,s^{-1}}$ dissipates $ΔE_k\sim6\e{25}\unit{J}$ as it decelerates, an amount set only by its launch and final speeds. title: Energy dissipation and free boundary stability of the Stefan problem
abstract: In this paper we prove the stability and the continuity of the free boundaries of two-phase and one-phase weak solutions to the Stefan problem in any dimension. Our proof has two main ingredients. The first one is an energy conservation principle for weak solutions that we derive for general domains in both the one-phase and the two-phase settings; this energy conservation principle provides the modulus of continuity for the displacement of the free boundary and is a flexible tool for analyzing long-time behavior of solutions. title: Nearly pristine gas in a galaxy 1 billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: Excitation of carbon and oxygen ions is the primary mechanism by which collapsing gas clouds dissipate heat to form new stars. At early cosmic times, in galaxies with chemically pristine gas, many stars are expected to have masses far larger than the mass of our sun due to the deficit in these elements. We searched for ultra-metal-poor galaxies using their spectroscopic absorption signatures in front of bright background quasars, employing the new GHOST high-resolution spectrograph. Here we report the discovery of the first galaxy containing a reservoir of neutral hydrogen gas with metallicity

title: Emission-Aware Optimization of Container Handling Vehicles: A HaminaKotka Port Case Study
abstract: Smart ports increasingly depend on IoT-enabled digitalization to turn heterogeneous operational processes into measurable, optimizable workflows. Accordingly, this paper first provides a concise review of IoT-enabler technologies for port digital transformation, emphasizing how sensing, connectivity, and data integration capabilities support real-time decision-making in port environments. Motivated by the growing emphasis on operational decarbonization reflected in the European Green Deal and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), we then present a data-driven fleet scheduling framework for

title: CreativeFlow: A One-to-Many Analogical Relation Transfer Method for 3D Asset Generation
abstract: Inspired by cognitive science, we present CREATIVEFLOW, an analogical generation framework that explicitly models analogical divergent thinking to mitigate creative homogenization in text-to-3D pipelines. Our method derives a series of meaningful yet relationally similar source-target asset pairs, each featuring distinct geometric configurations. Expert evaluations demonstrate that our framework substantially enhances creative novelty and visual fascination. This workflow and its resulting assets establish a foundational dataset and benchmark for future relation-aware 3D model training.

title: Radiation limits on amino acid preservation and chiral measurement at Oxia Planum
abstract: Amino acid enantiomeric excess (EE) is a potential biosignature, but its measurement requires sufficient surviving material as well as preserved chirality. We derive a criterion that separates abundance-limited from racemization-limited preservation and apply it to the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) on the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover. The model combines cosmic-ray and radiogenic doses with laboratory destruction kinetics and assumed ratios of interconversion to destruction rates. title: Personality Without Persons? A Psychometric Critique of Big Five Testing in Large Language Models
abstract: Human personality inventories are increasingly used to characterize large language models (LLMs), compare systems, and inform downstream governance claims. Yet, these inventories were developed and validated for humans, and it remains unclear whether they are valid for non-human systems. We present a systematic psychometric evaluation of Big Five personality measurement in LLMs. We ask three research questions: Do Big Five inventories a) appropriately describe LLMs, b) capture meaningful differences between models, and c) reflect internal factors consistent with human personality? title: An elementary approach to the Szegő theorems
abstract: The strong Szegő theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. In particular, Szegő's theorem states that, beyond the leading extensive contribution to such a determinant, there is a universal finite correction, $\sum_{r>0} rV_rV_{-r}$ where $V_r$ are the Fourier coefficients of the logarithm of the symbol. title: Beyond Equilibrium Raman Thermometry: Fermi-Level Control of the Anti-Stokes Response in Graphene
abstract: Non-equilibrium electron and phonon populations govern heat generation and dissipation in nanoscale devices, yet their direct characterization remains challenging. Anti-Stokes Raman scattering provides a sensitive probe of phonon populations and local temperatures, although its interpretation becomes more complex when electronic and phononic populations are driven out of equilibrium. Here, we investigate the gate-dependent anti-Stokes Raman response of monolayer graphene and find that the anti-Stokes response deviates from that expected from an equilibrium phonon population. title: Heuristics are Not Enough: Calibrated and Corrected Caching for Video Diffusion Acceleration
abstract: Feature caching has become a mainstream training-free strategy for accelerating video diffusion models by reusing intermediate outputs across denoising steps. However, existing adaptive methods rely on heuristic difference measures misaligned with actual generation quality, employ a single global threshold that ignores heterogeneous phase dynamics, and never validate their budget estimates against true approximation error, allowing systematic bias to propagate uncorrected. title: Universal relations for hybrid stars and their quark cores: a systematic scan of the quark-matter parameter space
abstract: Universal, equation-of-state (EOS) insensitive relations among the global properties of compact stars are well established for hadronic neutron stars and for self-bound strange stars. We ask whether analogous relations hold for the quark core of a hybrid star, and whether the core can be constrained from the surface. title: The Relation Before Lorenz: Kirchhoff, 1857, and the Symbols Lorenz Inherited
abstract: Abstract: A relation between the quantities now called the scalar potential and the vector potential, of the same form, up to a sign, as the one the literature attributes to Ludvig Lorenz in 1867, was written ten years earlier by Gustav Kirchhoff, with the same status: derived, unnumbered and unnamed. title: High-resolution Antarctic sea surface temperatures from Landsat enabled by cloud-native processing and novel seal-tag validation
abstract: Ocean heat transport drives approximately half of Antarctic ice mass loss, yet in situ ocean observations near glacier ice fronts remain exceedingly scarce given the challenges of data collection in this remote environment. Remotely sensed sea surface temperatures (SST) offer a powerful alternative, but no reliable product resolves the fine spatial resolution needed to observe partially ice-covered coastal Antarctic seas. title: A python‐based modeling package for underwater acoustic backscatter from individual gas bubbles
abstract: Abstract Acoustic backscatter from gas bubbles is key to detecting and quantifying marine seeps and related processes, yet practical tools for target strength (TS) prediction remain limited. We present seaEchoTSCalculator , an open‐source Python package that unifies established theories for individual gas bubbles from Rayleigh to geometric regimes (practically for 1–1250 kHz echosounders). title: Study of Waste Heat Recovery Systems in Marine Engines: Potential for Energy Savings and Emission Reduction
abstract: The shipping industry faces increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining operational efficiency. This study evaluates the energy-saving potential of an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system for waste heat recovery from a 21,840 kW MAN 8S65ME-C8.6 main marine diesel engine during a realistic 1,610.7-nautical-mile coastal voyage from Dalian to Qinzhou, China. R245fa was utilized as the working fluid, with the main engine operating at various loading conditions (50% and 90%) and seawater temperatures (10-30°C).
