title: Sediment plume evolution in the Black Sea after the Kakhovka Dam breach
abstract: The sediment plume resulting from the breach of the Kakhovka Dam on 06 June 2023 could lead to severe, long-term environmental pollution in the northwestern Black Sea (NWBS), as the floodwater transported contaminated sediments, chemicals, and polluted water from the reservoir and upstream sections of the Dnieper River. Although this event has raised significant concern among scientists and coastal managers, studies examining the plume's evolution and its environmental impact remain limited, posing a substantial challenge. title: In situ enhancement of coral larval settlement using acoustic enrichment, engineered habitats and living materials
abstract: Worldwide reef ecosystem degradation is inspiring efforts to enhance in-situ coral larvae settlement onto degraded or artificial reefs. Here we simultaneously test three approaches for enhancing settlement over two weeks in Kāne'ohe Bay, O'ahu, Hawai'i. Nineteen artificial structures, mimicking natural reef mesoscale roughness, were deployed along two transect lines at distances between 1 and 42 m from an "acoustic enrichment" underwater speaker broadcasting healthy reef sound. title: A unified numerical method based on added momentum source terms for hydrodynamic prediction of underwater vehicles
abstract: Classical numerical methods for predicting hydrodynamic coefficients of underwater vehicles typically rely on repeated grid generation, dynamic mesh techniques, and complex physical models, resulting in high computational cost and operational complexity. In this study, a unified numerical method combining added momentum source terms with the Wray-Agarwal 2018 Rotation/Curvature turbulence model (WA-2018 RC model) is developed to address these limitations. title: Energy-dependent underwater abrasion behavior of sustainable lightweight concrete incorporating agro-waste aggregates and natural fibers under rotational hydraulic conditions
abstract: Abstract Lightweight aggregate concrete has become a popular material in hydraulic engineering and coastal and offshore engineering, and understanding its durability under underwater rotational abrasion is critical. Comparative studies on the abrasion resistance of several agricultural waste aggregates under high-energy underwater conditions have been conducted for the production of sustainable concrete; however, such studies are still scarce, especially considering the combined effects of rotational speed, abrasion time, aggregate properties, and properties of the interfacial transition zone

title: The evolution of the Houthi weapons arsenal and its implications for maritime security and cargo shipping in the Red Sea
abstract: This article examines how the Yemeni Houthi movement transformed its missile, drone, and maritime capabilities into a source of regional instability and economic disruption in the Bab al-Mandab area. Rather than reconstructing the Yemeni war, it analyzes the development of the Houthi arsenal since the 2015 regionalization of the conflict and its intensified use following October 2023. title: Environmental and geographic predictors of seed plant diversity across South American terrestrial coastal lomas
abstract: Understanding the predictors of plant diversity gradients remains a major challenge in biogeography, particularly in understudied arid ecosystems where water availability is highly constrained. Coastal lomas—isolated, fog-fed vegetation oases distributed across the Peruvian and Chilean coastal deserts of South America–provide a unique system for examining how climate, topography, and geography shape plant diversity under extreme aridity. title: Numerical study of hydrodynamics and power performance of offshore floating photovoltaic: Effects of connector failure
abstract: As a core component of the offshore floating photovoltaic (OFPV) system, connectors exert a decisive influence on the stable operation of the entire multi-float structure. In this study, a coupled hydrodynamic-solar power generation model for the OFPV system is developed. First, a hydrodynamic model of a hinged dual-hexagonal OFPV system is built using the open-source DualSPHysics code, and the model is validated against available physical experimental data. title: Transcriptional Profiling and Co-expression Integration for the Filtering of Relevant Bacterial sRNA–mRNA Interactions: Application to Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm
abstract: Abstract Small regulatory ribonucleic acids coordinate bacterial gene expression and contribute to biofilm development, virulence, and stress adaptation. We characterized these regulators across six Staphylococcus aureus strains by integrating newly generated transcriptome data from strain Bmb9393 with public datasets from five additional strains. Sequence homology and covariance models supported annotation of candidate loci, whose expression and genomic context were characterized under biofilm and planktonic conditions. title: Numerical study of scattering and polarisation characteristics of marine spherical aerosol particles illuminated by non-diffracting Tricomi beams
abstract: Abstract Non-diffracting light beams have exceptional self-healing and propagation characteristics that make them unique for free-space optical communication, atmospheric optics, and remote sensing. Tricomi beams are a novel type of diffraction-free, structure-shaped beam whose scattering characteristics in humid maritime aerosol environments remain mostly unexplored. In this work, we present a comprehensive theoretical study of the scattering as well as the polarisation response of marine spherical aerosol particles illuminated by non-diffracting Tricomi beams. title: Late Pliocene–Quaternary Arc Volcanism at the Southern Limit of the Hikurangi Subduction Zone: Revised Chronology of the Taranaki Peninsula, New Zealand
abstract: Igneous centres across the Taranaki Peninsula represent the southwestern limit of arc volcanism associated with the Tonga–Kermadec–Hikurangi subduction system. Taranaki Maunga, the youngest and largest of three andesitic stratovolcanoes, dominates the geomorphology of the Taranaki Peninsula along with the eroded remnants of the Kaitake and Pouakai edifices. Beneath the peninsula, the ring plain built by Taranaki and its predecessors lies on an angular unconformity cut into Pliocene marine strata. title: Creativity Under Pressure: A Case Study of Drug Cartel Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. Building on creativity research applied to terrorist groups, we use a qualitative case study approach—drawing from news reports, official documents, open‐source materials, and academic work—to analyze 10 cases of cartel innovation across tactical, strategic, and organizational domains. title: The Impact of Planetary Phase Functions on Exo-Earth Detectability with EXOSIMS
abstract: Abstract The under-development NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to provide breakthroughs in exoplanet science, yet the most effective approaches to modeling the detection and characterization of potentially Earth-like worlds with HWO remain uncertain despite being essential considerations for mission design. In this work, we aim to better model and understand detection metrics through the use of Exoplanet Open-Source Imaging Mission Simulator (EXOSIMS), an exoplanet yield modeling tool. title: Arctic Grayling, scared to death: Are Brown Trout an impediment to Arctic Grayling reintroduction success in Michigan?
abstract: Abstract Introduction Arctic Grayling Thymallus arcticus were extirpated from Michigan in 1936. Their demise was likely caused by overfishing, habitat destruction from large-scale logging, and the introduction of Brook Trout Salvelinus fontinalis and Brown Trout Salmo trutta. Subsequently, Brook Trout and Brown Trout have become the dominant salmonid species in Michigan streams. Past attempts to restore Arctic Grayling to Michigan have been unsuccessful, perhaps due to competition with these now-resident salmonids. title: Position of the Lhasa Terrane and Two‐Stage Crustal Shortening During the India–Asia Collision
abstract: Abstract The paleolatitudinal change of the Lhasa Terrane is critical for estimating the timing of the India–Asia collision and associated syn‐to post‐collisional crustal shortening, but its paleoposition is highly debated. Here we present integrated geochronologic and paleomagnetic results from the Lower Eocene Nianbo Formation in the Linzhou Basin. Two SIMS U−Pb zircon ages of 54.59 ± 0.68 Ma and 53.97 ± 0.43 Ma were obtained from the strata. The magnetostratigraphy spans chrons C24r–C23r, estimating deposition from ∼55.37 to ∼52.54 Ma. title: Impact of control augmentation on pilot workload during shipboard helicopter hover operation
abstract: Abstract The integration of control augmentation techniques into helicopter systems aims to assist pilots during the critical phases of shipboard operations to mitigate the effects of ship motion, wind and other environmental factors that can compromise safety. The control augmentation presented in this paper involves the implementation of model following control laws featuring a combination of advanced response types with hold modes to improve helicopter handling qualities. title: Coupled U–Pb geochronology of inherited and detrital zircon in the Iberian Massif: insights into its deep structure and geodynamic evolution
abstract: Abstract The combined use of detrital and inherited zircon U-Pb age spectra provides new insights into the crustal evolution of the Iberian Massif as part of the North Gondwana margin. In the Ossa–Morena Zone (OMZ), Ediacaran detrital zircon populations are dominated by Pan‑African ages, whereas inherited zircons overwhelmingly record Cadomian signatures, implying that Cadomian crust remained largely unexposed during the Cadomian event itself. title: Design, synthesis, and evaluation of antifungal and antibacterial activities of novel quinazolinone–formononetin derivatives
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Plant pathogenic fungi and bacteria cause substantial losses in agricultural production worldwide, and escalating resistance to conventional agrochemicals necessitates the development of novel, environmentally benign pesticides. Formononetin, a naturally occurring isoflavone, exhibits promising bioactivities, while quinazolinone and piperidine moieties serve as privileged pharmacophores in agrochemical discovery. title: Compact low-frequency optomechanical triaxial inertial sensor
abstract: Triaxial optomechanical accelerometers offer a compact, ground-testable complement to free-fall electrostatic accelerometers used in satellite geodesy, alongside applications in seismometry and precision metrology. We demonstrate a compact triaxial inertial sensor using monolithic fused-silica resonators with dual heterodyne interferometric readout. title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
abstract: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. title: Decade-long data highlight medium-sized, fast-flowing cold-water streams as important recruitment habitats for European river and brook lampreys
abstract: European river lamprey Lampetra fluviatilis is a migratory (anadromous) species, spawning in freshwater rivers where it co-occurs with its non-migratory paired species, European brook lamprey L. planeri . Both species are listed under Annex II of the EU Habitats Directive, requiring habitat protection and sustainable management across their distribution ranges. title: Sulfide‐Ene Reactions by Visible‐Light‐Mediated Phosphine Redox Catalysis
abstract: Sulfur‐containing compounds play a crucial role in many biological processes. The important gasotransmitter hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) can be metabolized by cellular enzyme system for the biosynthesis of amino acids and regulatory effects related to diseases. Although the photocatalytic thiol‐ene reactions have been widely developed, a general H 2 S‐ene reaction by organic photocatalysis remains elusive. title: Resveratrol -Induced Demethylation of LATS1 and LATS2 Genes in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the potential of Resveratrol in reversing promoter hypermethylation of LATS1/2 genes, key components of the Hippo Signaling Pathway, in OSCC cell lines. title: Adakitic Permian magmatism along the eastern Gondwana margin: constraints on deep crustal processes and metallogenesis in northeastern Queensland
abstract: The Kennedy Igneous Association (KIA) of northeastern Queensland provides an opportunity to investigate links between granitoid magmatism, deep crustal processes and metallogenesis along the eastern Gondwana margin. This study integrates whole-rock geochemistry with new zircon U–Pb geochronology to constrain the timing, sources and tectonic significance of granitoids from the Georgetown region (Kidston subprovince). abstract: Linking X-ray variability to the underlying magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics of black hole X-ray binaries remains challenging. We systematically investigate the stochastic and oscillatory variability of the black hole X-ray binary candidate Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 outburst using Gaussian process (GP) regression applied to Insight-HXMT multi-band light curves. abstract: This research is aimed at Applying Bayesian decision model in Agribusiness value chain intervention project in Niger Delta. The objectives are: to determine Prior (Prototype) and Posterior (Model) Probability, Expected Monetary Value (EMV), Marginal Probability, Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI), Expected Profit in Perfect Information (EPPI), The problems the study solve were: inadequate funding of multipurpose scheme, inefficient economic benefits and losses. title: Magmatic controls on Cu-Pb-Zn mineralization at the Cunqian deposit, Qin-Hang Metallogenic Belt (China): insights from Hf isotopes and trace elements in zircon
abstract: The Cunqian Cu-Pb-Zn deposit is a significant skarn-porphyry deposit located at the junction of the eastern and central segments of the Qin-Hang metallogenic belt (QHMB) in China. However, ore prospecting in this area has been hindered by insufficient research on ore-related intrusions relative to adjacent areas. title: ASSESSMENT OF NATURALLY OCCURRING RADIOACTIVE MATERIALS AND RADIOLOGICAL RISKS IN SOILS AROUND THE KADUNA REFINING AND PETROCHEMICAL COMPANY, NIGERIA
abstract: Industrial activities, particularly petroleum refining, have been identified as significant contributors to the enrichment of Naturally Occurring Radioactive Materials (NORMs) in surrounding environments. This study assessed the radiological impact of the Kaduna Refining and Petrochemical Company (KRPC) on the local soil environment. Soil samples were collected from 10 sampling points within the refinery operational area and one control site located approximately 2 km away. abstract: This article reflects on the critical inquiry that shapes the Darkness Reframed issue and, from a decolonial perspective, problematizes the possible assumptions attached to the category of darkness. Unpacking coloniality not only as a historical legacy but as a living force that continues to shape ways of thinking, the reflection points to the plurality of futures to be reframed in order to embrace a multilayered understanding of darkness(es). title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. title: The Effect of i-PUBERS Implementation on Subsidized Fertilizer Distribution Effectiveness
abstract: The implementation of digital systems in public administration has become increasingly important in improving the effectiveness, transparency, and accountability of public service delivery. In the agricultural sector, digitalization is expected to support more accurate and efficient distribution of subsidized fertilizers to eligible farmers. This study aims to analyze the effect of i-PUBERS implementation on the effectiveness of subsidized fertilizer distribution at the Agricultural Office of Cirebon Regency, with a focus on the Agricultural Extension Center in Sedong District. title: Multiscale computational modeling of photoacoustic generation from micrometer-size polymeric bead suspensions in liquid media
abstract: Photoacoustic sensing has emerged as a promising technique for detecting polymeric particles suspended in liquids through the conversion of absorbed optical energy into acoustic signals. Here, we present a multiscale computational study of the photoacoustic response of polystyrene (PS) beads suspended in water under pulsed optical excitation. The framework combines particle-resolved simulations of individual beads with point-particle descriptions of randomly distributed multi-particle suspensions. abstract: O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar o inventário florístico das espécies de Piperaceae ocorrentes no município de Vitória da Conquista, Bahia. O trabalho foi desenvolvidocom base na análise de exsicatas provenientes de herbários, consultas a bases de dados virtuais e expedições de campo realizadas em fragmentos de floresta estacional decidual e floramentos rochosos. title: Numerical Solutions of Inelastic Compressible Fluid Flow in Two Dimensional Square Cavity
abstract: In this study, inelastic compressible flow within a two-dimensional square cavity is investigated using the Galerkin finite element method. The main goal is to investigate the effect of lid-driven boundary conditions on the flow characteristics. We apply two types of boundary conditions, a constant lid velocity and a given analytical velocity profile. title: HFIP-promoted Lewis acid-free one-pot synthesis of pyran derivatives under mild conditions
abstract: A one-pot, three-component reaction of aromatic aldehyde, malononitrile, dimedone or ethyl acetoacetate was developed in which the reaction medium and promoter was 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP). abstract: Abstract Polysaccharide-based materials, particularly dextran (Dex) derivatives, have emerged as versatile platforms for biomedical and materials science applications primarily due to their tunable chemical functionality and intrinsic biocompatibility. abstract: Soil is an essential and strategic resource for the sustainability of agricultural production on the planet; however, it faces progressive degradation derived from unsustainable management practices and the effects of climate change. Within this context, climate-smart agriculture emerges as an approach to try to increase productivity by strengthening the resilience of agricultural systems. title: Bio-inspired Open Ligamentous Knee Joint with Extended Pitch and Yaw Range of Motion
abstract: This study presents a bio-inspired open knee joint for biofidelic robots with an anatomically correct range of motion. Bio-inspired joints contribute to robot performance and understanding living organisms by providing dynamic motion data as the real-world physical twin. The proposed joint structure features the integration of the open joint and ligamentous constraint. title: Multiple stressor effects of hypoxia and metals on ventilation, activity, bioaccumulation, and loss of equilibrium in fathead minnows
abstract: Hypoxia is an increasing concern in freshwater ecosystems, driven by warming, stratification, and nutrient enrichment. Fish cope with hypoxia through behavioural and ventilatory adjustments, yet growing evidence suggests that certain metals can impair these critical compensatory mechanisms. It is currently unknown whether lead (Pb) and nickel (Ni), released in part through expanding mining operations, may alter these critical survival responses. title: Impact of Armed Banditry on Agricultural Productivity Among Rural Farm Households in North Central Nigeria: A Propensity Score Matching Approach
abstract: Armed banditry has emerged as a major threat to rural livelihoods and agricultural production in Nigeria, particularly in North Central Nigeria, a major food-producing region. Despite growing evidence linking insecurity to agricultural decline, empirical evidence on the causal effects of banditry on household’s farm productivity remains limited. This study examines the impact of banditry on agricultural productivity among rural farm households in Niger and Plateau States Nigeria. title: Life cycle toxicity analysis of engineered stone: a multi indicator comparison of polyester based and cement based product systems with regulatory implications
abstract: Abstract Production, sale, manufacturing and mounting of engineered stone kitchen countertops, tiles and sheets have been banned in Australia as at 2024. This type of change can be a point of concern with respect to other products which may also have reduced emissions throughout its life cycle, as well as decreasing the exposure of workers to respirable crystalline silica. title: Comparative efficacy of new-generation fungicides against major fungal diseases of rice
abstract: A field study was conducted during the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 at the Rice Research Unit, Agricultural Research Institute, Rajendranagar, using a randomised block design (RBD) with 8 treatments and 4 replications to evaluate the efficacy of seven multi-active combination fungicides against three predominant fungal diseases of rice in Telangana, namely sheath blight, blast and grain discolouration, which limit rice productivity and grain quality under intensive production systems. title: Weak and inconsistent associations between birch-feeding insects and pollution levels around two industrial towns during substantial emission decline (1988–2025)
abstract: Industrial emissions have historically altered terrestrial ecosystems, but their long-term effects on insect herbivores remain insufficiently understood, particularly during ecosystem recovery following emission decline. We analysed a dataset on the densities of 24 Recognisable Taxonomic Units (RTUs) of birch-feeding insects collected from 1988 to 2025 around two industrial towns in northwestern Russia previously identified as pollution hotspots. title: Functionalization of Peptides via Radical Arylation
abstract: Among the manifold methods for the functionalization of peptides known today, radical chemistry has so far only rarely been exploited to introduce structural modifications on this challenging type of substrate. In this short review, we give an overview showing that, especially, radical arylation reactions can represent attractive and powerful tools to access functionalized peptides under mild and biocompatible conditions where no protecting group strategy is required. title: A Cost-Illness Analysis of Economic Burden of Unimproved Water Use on Households: Empirical Evidence from Dhaka Urban Riparian Areas
abstract: The rapid urbanization and increasing industrial establishment near Dhaka’s rivers are creating environmental pressure on nearby communities. And people due to several factors are forced to use unimproved water from the nearby waterbodies. This study looks at how using unsafe water affects the health, health expenditure and poverty of 1,826 families living near the Turag River in Dhaka. title: Taking Value Constitutionalism Seriously: Migration and Values in EU Law and European Society
abstract: Abstract This article argues that taking Article 2 values seriously as a cornerstone of EU constitutional law requires analysing domains beyond the rule of law and judicial independence. It investigates the role of values in migration management by taking the EU–Turkey Statement and temporary reintroduction of border checks within Schengen as examples through which to tease out how values interact with non-values-based priorities, the indeterminacy of divergent interpretations of values, and the value of freedom. title: Seroprevalence and the determinants of lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV) in cattle reared under smallholder production systems in northwestern Bangladesh
abstract: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) is a vector-borne transboundary disease that causes substantial productivity losses in cattle. This study was undertaken to determine the seroprevalence of LSD and the associated determinants of non-vaccinated cattle reared in smallholder production systems of northwestern Bangladesh. A cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2024 to January 2025 covering ten districts where a total of 450 non-vaccinated cattle were sampled across 100 smallholder farms. This approach circumvents the need for Wilson lines, potentially enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of lattice calculations. title: Impact of weather parameters on the progression of bakanae disease (Fusarium moniliforme Sheldon) in aromatic rice (Oryza sativa L.) in the north-western region of Haryana, India
abstract: Various biotic constraints affect the cultivation of aromatic rice in India, especially in the North-West Plain Zone and bakanae disease is responsible for high economic losses ranging from 3.0–95.4 %. It occurs in Haryana and the adjoining states, particularly in early-transplanted rice crops. Weather influences all stages of the host and pathogen life cycle, as well as disease progression. To manage and forecast bakanae disease, it is important to understand the interaction between the host, pathogen and environment. abstract: The concept of vertical greening systems has gained considerable attention in recent years as an innovative approach to enhancing thermal comfort within various built environments. This growing interest is rooted in the recognition of the substantial influence that greenery can exert on the microclimate of structures. The design of student hostels in general faces a significant challenge on thermal discomfort, intensified by high solar gain in the tropical savannah climate. title: Recent advances and emerging mechanisms in graphene-based materials for cartilage tissue engineering
abstract: Graphene-based materials offer tunable mechanical, electrical, and biochemical properties that address longstanding challenges in cartilage tissue engineering. This review synthesizes recent advances in graphene derivatives, scaffold fabrication strategies, and emerging mechanisms governing cell-graphene interactions. We evaluate how graphene enhances mechanical reinforcement, bioactivity, and matrix production across hydrogels, polymer composites, and ECM-derived scaffolds. abstract: Probability theory has been applied to archaeological chronology since the advent of radiocarbon dating, but key chronological indicators, such as artifact typologies, continue to be dated in descriptive terms (e.g., “in the later 3rd c. BCE”). Moreover, the informational inter-dependency for how contexts and assemblages affect others’ dating can become opaque. title: Luxury hospitality meets sustainability: crafting impactful stories on social media
abstract: Purpose Luxury is synonymous with quality, exclusivity and rarity, characteristics which do not hold sustainability as a core consideration in service provision. This study aims to investigate how luxury service brands craft stories on social media around their sustainability practices. title: A deeper look into the diversity of suckermouth catfishes (Mochockidae: Chiloglanis Peters 1868) of southern Africa, with the description of four new species
abstract: Suckermouth catfishes of the genus Chiloglanis Peters 1868 are small and predominantly rheophilic fishes endemic to Africa. This genus is quite diverse, with over 70 species distributed across most river systems on the continent, except for the Cape Fold ecoregion and most of northern Africa. The present study undertook detailed genetic and morphological examination of suckermouth catfishes collected from multiple localities across the Zambezi River system. Results from this study support preliminary field observations that had identified considerable morphological and colour pattern variation

abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. title: Engineering properties of green chickpea plants and pods for machine design of a green pod stripper
abstract: Sustainable product development in agricultural mechanization increasingly relies on data-driven knowledge to design efficient technologies and improve the utilization of energy inputs. Physical and engineering properties of the green chickpea crop plants and pods are necessary for designing efficient stripping, handling, and storage equipment. Two varieties (PBG7 and PBG10) and two planting methods (Bed and Flat) were taken as independent parameters. title: Poking the cell surface: mechanics, remodeling, and what force reveals
abstract: Abstract What happens when you poke a living cell, applying a localized external force to its surface? The answer depends, in part, on how long you keep poking. The plasma membrane and the actomyosin cortex beneath it form a mechanically active interface that changes in disease and can itself be reshaped by force. This review explores how the cell surface responds to such force in two overlapping experimental regimes. title: Urban Environments Impact Parasite Diversity and an Antipredator Response in an Amphibian Model
abstract: Urbanization is a major driver of biodiversity loss by transforming ecosystems and imposing novel selective pressures that reshape not only species but also their interspecific interactions. In urban environments, predation pressure is often altered, leading to shifts in antipredator strategies, and parasitism varies with changes in environmental quality and the introduction of novel hosts or vectors. abstract: ABSTRACT Fruit‐associated insect communities in tropical citrus orchards are spatially heterogeneous; however, fine‐scale ecological relationships among tephritid emergence, parasitoid recruitment and associated insect guilds remain poorly resolved. This study quantified spatiotemporal variation and conditional co‐occurrence networks among insect assemblages across nine commercial citrus orchards in East Java, Indonesia. abstract: Stagnation in the summation of floating-point numbers occurs when the running sum, or the accumulator, does not change its value despite addends being greater than zero. abstract: We perform direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence to investigate the mechanisms responsible for the maintenance of large-scale geostrophic vortices. abstract: The 248 keV nuclear-recoil event observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment could potentially arise from dark matter (DM) interactions with nucleons. title: Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback
abstract: User simulators are gaining attention as environments to train LLM assistants that can better cope with the nuances of multi-turn conversations with real users. Prior work on user simulation has emphasized generating realistic user utterances, leaving unexplored their potential as a source of direct feedback on the assistant's responses. abstract: Crystallisation of calcium carbonate (CaCO$_3$) in aqueous solutions is essential for carbon dioxide sequestration and the sustainable production of calcium carbonate materials, which are widely used in industry and increasingly explored for novel applications. While crystallisation is often analysed within the framework of classical nucleation theory, CaCO$_3$ and other ionic crystals often form through amorphous precursor phases, motivating the need for alternative descriptions. abstract: Hurricanes severely impact coastal communities, disrupting social and economic systems and causing widespread physical damage. Rapid post-disaster assessment is essential for effective response, yet traditional on-site evaluations are slow and resource intensive. Advances in machine learning offer faster, automated alternatives by leveraging historical disaster data to predict damage in near real time. abstract: The current work seeks to identify the most critical wave properties that may influence the performance of Wave Energy Converters (WECs) operating near several European marine sites. abstract: Wide-area maritime monitoring of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference remains challenging because dedicated radio-frequency sensing infrastructure is often sparse, costly, or unavailable in open-sea environment. This paper explores Automatic Identification System (AIS) data as an infrastructure-light source for detecting regional interference effects. title: How Gaming Activities Shape Lower Secondary School Pupils' Understanding of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, there is a growing need to develop not only technical skills among lower secondary school pupils, but above all an understanding of how AI works and the ability to use it critically and effectively. abstract: Continuous monitoring of Mount Merapi's volcanic activity by the Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (BPPTKG) is frequently hindered by poor visual image quality caused by adverse weather, heavy cloud cover, dense fog, and insufficient nighttime illumination. These visual constraints impede accurate visibility assessment, which can delay disaster risk assessment and timely early warnings. title: An Analytical Model for Predicting Injectivity Decline During High-Rate Injection of Solid Suspension in Horizontal Well
abstract: Abstract Water injection is widely used for hydrocarbon production and reservoir pressure maintenance. Driven by environmental and economic considerations, produced water and filtered seawater are one of the main sources of the injected water. However, both may contain suspended solids that plug the formation, resulting in permeability damage and loss of injectivity. A horizontal injector, with its larger completion flow area and reduced injection flux, is well suited to maintaining high and sustained injection rates. abstract: Abstract The Bongor Basin in the Central African Rift System is a typical strongly inverted intracontinental rift that hosts unique "shallow-buried thick shale oil" resources. Previous studies, based only on limited data, underestimated its shale oil potential, and the controlling factors of movable oil and its enrichment mechanism remain unclear. title: From Regulation to Innovation: Mining High-Impact AI Patents Grounded in the EU AI Act and Korea’s AI Basic Act
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly operates in domains that impact human life, safety, and fundamental rights, and emerging regulation singles out such high-impact domains for binding obligations. Beyond legislative and use-case definitions, this study empirically maps and analyzes the high-impact AI landscape. A unified taxonomy of 15 high-impact AI domains is derived from the heightened-obligation categories of the EU AI Act and Korea's AI Basic Act. abstract: Gender inequality remains a persistent structural feature of the labour market, shaping women’s lifetime earnings and economic security. As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms organisational practices, there is growing concern that existing disparities may be unintentionally amplified through task automation, unequal access to upskilling opportunities, and differential returns obtained from technological change. title: Quantum Diplomacy: An Analytical Framework for the Disruptive Technology Era
abstract: The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence, big data, and global digital platforms has fundamentally altered diplomatic practice, shifting it from closed, state-centric negotiation to real-time, data-driven, and algorithmically mediated interaction. Existing international relations theory, built around linear and deterministic assumptions about state behavior, increasingly struggles to explain the non-linear, probabilistic dynamics of contemporary diplomatic practice. title: Supervised Reservoir Facies Classification for Pre-Paleogene Buried Hill Formation and Hydrocarbon Geological Significance, Offshore South China
abstract: Abstract The pre-Paleogene buried hills in the South China Sea are crucial succession of deep oil and gas reserves. Buried hill X, formed from a composite metamorphic sandstone and granite, is controlled by multiple phases of tectonic activity, exhibiting a well-developed fracture network but poor matrix properties. abstract: Sovereign AI has emerged as a major policy movement, with nearly 130 government-backed initiatives across more than 50 countries justified in part by the promise of cultural and linguistic self-determination. States seek national AI systems that reflect local languages, values, and knowledge traditions rather than importing the assumptions of foreign technology providers. title: From Maritime Regulations to Verifiable Properties with LLM Assistance
abstract: Abstract Maritime automation requires formal safety assurances that simulation alone cannot provide. The International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) are expressed in natural language, while Legata provides a structured domain-specific language for encoding these regulations. We propose a method for translating Legata specifications into logical properties that can be verified against an actor-based model using model checking. title: Explaining Time Series Classifications Counterfactually: A Human-Centered Evaluation
abstract: Counterfactual explanations can promote accountability, fairness, and transparency in AI-supported decision-making by demonstrating how changes in input data can alter outcomes, offering actionable feedback for users to revise unfavorable decisions. However, the majority of counterfactual algorithms focus on tabular and image data, ignoring many high-stakes scenarios that rely on time series data. title: Photoplethysmography and vital sign measurement using 3D-multispectral multimodal imaging
abstract: Contactless vital-sign monitoring can improve comfort and hygiene in long-term, sleep, home, and clinical monitoring, but robust estimation of heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), and oxygen saturation (SpO2) remains a coupled sensing and algorithmic problem. abstract: Current LLM-based vulnerability detection systems rely on static prompting strategies and fixed analysis pipelines, which fail to adapt to an evolving threat landscape. abstract: Market Basket Analysis (MBA) is a data mining technique that plays a key role in finding consumer purchasing patterns to aid in optimizing inventory management and marketing strategies. title: Ranking Cocoa Land Suitability Growth Requirements with Random Forest for a Spatial Decision-Support Platform
abstract: Cocoa-growing land in Indonesia has steadily declined, increasing import dependence. An earlier study developed a web-based geographic information system (GIS) platform using Spatial ID3 to classify cocoa land suitability in Bogor Regency from eight soil and topographic variables, but it could not identify which variables most strongly influenced the resulting classes. This study extends it by using Random Forest to rank the eight variables by their contribution to the suitability decision. title: Thermodynamic Screening of Solvents for Ternary Cellulose Acetate Blend Membranes Using Hansen Solubility Parameters
abstract: Solvent selection for phase inversion membranes still relies mostly on trial and error, even though the solvent governs how well a polymer blend forms into a stable, separation-capable structure. abstract: Iron sand deposits contain Fe-bearing oxide minerals with characteristic reflectance features, but field spectrometer and hyperspectral image measurements of these features do not always agree, owing to differences in sensor characteristics, observation scale, and surface conditions. This study evaluates the spectral consistency between ASD FieldSpec and EO-1 Hyperion reflectance over the Kulon Progo iron sand deposit, and examines how spectral processing and spatial representation affect that consistency. title: EnergyTrackr: A Modular Energy Regressions Detection Tool
abstract: Energy efficiency is increasingly recognized as an important dimension of software quality. As systems evolve rapidly, tracking how energy consumption changes across versions can provide valuable insights for developers and researchers. Although detecting energy regressions (i.e., unintended increases in energy consumption) remains challenging due to measurement variability and complex execution environments, recent advances now make systematic analysis practical. title: PCodeTrans: Translate Decompiled Pseudocode to Trace-Level Equivalent Source Code
abstract: Decompilation remains foundational for binary analysis, yet conventional tools prioritize human readability over compilation success and test-validated runtime consistency. While recent large language model approaches attempt refining decompiled pseudocode, they often introduce semantic hallucinations. title: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using GIS-Based Analytical Hierarchy Process in Pejawaran District, Banjarnegara
abstract: Landslide susceptibility mapping is an important tool for identifying relatively unstable zones and facilitating disaster mitigation and land-use planning. This study assesses landslide susceptibility in Pejawaran District, Banjarnegara, Central Java, Indonesia, using a GIS-based Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) in Question-Answering (QA) tasks. abstract: Due to complex, unstructured, and dynamic environmental conditions, the automation of forestry work processes is limited. The kinematic architecture, and typical industrial and forestry applications of commercially available walking robots, has been reviewed, and a catalog of requirements for use in forestry has been derived. title: A Model-Driven Formalization of Prompt Patterns
abstract: Prompt patterns provide reusable structures for designing prompts, but existing catalogs typically describe them through informal prose, examples, or loosely structured templates. This limits their systematic reuse, detection, comparison, and analysis. In this paper, we propose a model-driven formalization of prompt patterns based on a taxonomy.
